Chapter 95: Summer 1976 (part three: Peace Talks)

It wasn't easy for Remus to keep Sirius at a distance while he was staying with the Potters. The house was big enough, but that didn’t matter much in a family home; something Remus was only just learning. Mrs. Potter gave Remus his space during the first couple of days, but after that, it was clear that she had no idea of the rift between the marauders, and expected the three boys to spend all of their time together as usual.

Remus很難在Potter家時與Sirius保持距離。這房子足夠大，但在一個家庭中這並不重要；這是Remus剛剛學會的一件事。Potter夫人在最初的幾天里給了Remus一些空間，但之後她顯然不知道四個人之間的裂痕，期望三個男孩像往常一樣一直在一起。

As much as they were each uncomfortable with this arrangement, for their own reasons, none of them wanted to disappoint or worry Euphemia. So an uneasy truce was struck, and Remus spent most of his time reading his book, sitting close enough to James and Sirius that it did not look suspicious.

Remus, Sirius, 和 James各自都對這種安排感到不舒服，出於自己的原因，但他們都不想讓Euphemia失望或擔心。因此，達成了一個不安的休戰協議，Remus大部分時間都在閱讀他的書，坐在James和Sirius旁邊，這樣看起來不會可疑。

Grant had said that it wouldn't always hurt - and though he hadn’t had the full facts of the situation, Remus was starting to believe him. He still felt very angry towards Sirius - but it hurt less, as the final weeks of summer drained away in a flood of sunshine and blue skies. He was able, at least, to be civil, and Sirius seemed grateful. At any rate, he had stopped trying to corner Remus into a conversation every five minutes.

Grant曾說這不會一直痛——儘管他並不知道全部情況，Remus開始相信他。他仍然對Sirius感到非常生氣——但隨著夏季最後幾周在陽光和藍天中流逝，這種痛苦減少了。至少，他能夠保持禮貌，而Sirius似乎感激。不管怎樣，Sirius已經不再每五分鐘就試圖把Remus拉進談話中。

Besides, after his conversation with Moody, Remus had other things occupying his mind. For years now, he had been labouring under the assumption that Greyback did not know him, that he would have the element of surprise in his corner. But now it seemed that Greyback might be looking for him, too. He would not tell the marauders this, not until he knew more. No use getting them worried; if Moody said that Hogwarts was safe, then Remus was inclined to believe him for now. The Potters clearly trusted him, and that would have to be enough. What was more; he knew Ferox.

此外，與Moody談話後，Remus心中還有其他事情。多年来，他一直以為Greyback不認識他，他會有出其不意的優勢。但現在似乎Greyback也在找他。他不會告訴四個人這件事，直到他了解更多。沒有必要讓他們擔心；如果Moody說霍格沃茲是安全的，那麼Remus現在傾向於相信他。Potter一家顯然信任他，這必須足夠。此外，他還認識Ferox。

Remus had had Ferox on his mind too. Once again, his old professor seemed like the safest option when it came to asking questions. He understood Remus’s need to know more - even if he didn't know why, exactly. And Remus didn’t want to bother Mr. Potter, not when he seemed to have the weight of the world on his shoulders already. He would send an owl to Ferox as soon as he was back at school - and as soon as the dust had settled on this recent revelation.

Remus心中也一直記掛著Ferox。再一次，他的老教授似乎是提問的最安全選擇。他理解Remus需要知道更多——即使他不知道確切原因。而且Remus不想打擾Potter先生，因為他似乎已經肩負著世界的重擔。他會在回到學校後馬上給Ferox寄一隻貓頭鷹信——在最近的這個揭露塵埃落定後。

In the meantime, Peter came over every day, and they went out on their brooms, or else lounged about on the lawn, smoking, listening to Sirius’s record player and sunbathing. Remus turned a warm hazelnut brown all over, which made him look healthier than he ever had, and his hair bleached a shade fairer.

與此同時，Peter每天都過來，他們要麼出去騎掃帚，要麼就在草坪上閒逛，抽煙，聽Sirius的唱機，晒太陽。Remus曬成了一種溫暖的榛子棕色，這使他看起來比以往更健康，他的頭髮也漂白了一些。

On the penultimate day of the holidays, they were doing just this - it was too hot to move, and all four of them were lying on their backs baking in the sun. Remus had positioned himself a little further away from the others, just to show Sirius that he was not off the hook. (Also because Sirius had an annoying habit of taking his shirt off, and Remus was trying not to notice.)

在假期倒數第二天，他們正在做這些事情——天氣太熱了，無法動彈，四個人都仰躺在陽光下曬著。Remus故意讓自己離其他人遠一點，以示意Sirius他還沒被原諒。（也因為Sirius有個惱人的習慣，喜歡脫掉襯衫，而Remus試圖不去注意。）

“So tell me again,” Peter yawned up at the sun, arms behind his head, “What was the Knight Bus like? I’ve always wanted to go on it.”

“再告訴我一次，”Peter仰望著太陽，打著哈欠，雙臂放在腦後，“Knight Bus是什麼樣子的？我一直想坐它。”

“Dream big, Petey.” Sirius drawled.

“夢想大些，Petey。”Sirius慢吞吞地說。

“It wasn’t that great,” James replied, “Can’t wait until we can all apparate - lessons start in January.”

“其實沒那麼好，”James回答，“等不及我們都能幻影移形了——課程在一月開始。”

“I’m going to be rubbish at it.” Peter said, forlorn, “Dezzie has been reading the theory books, I can’t get my head around it.”

“我肯定會很糟糕。”Peter沮喪地說，“Dezzie一直在讀理論書，我搞不懂。”

“Well it's better than relying on that stupid bus.” James removed his glasses and rubbed his eyes, “It’s fine for magical locations, but the driver kept getting lost on the way to St Edmund’s.”

“總比依賴那愚蠢的巴士好。”James摘下眼鏡，揉了揉眼睛，“對於魔法地點還好，但司機在去St Edmund’s的路上一直迷路。”

Remus’s stomach flipped. He really, really hated the idea that James and Sirius had been there. He felt as though they’d seen some private part of him he would have preferred to keep hidden. Like the first time he’d transformed in front of them.

Remus的胃翻騰了。他真的，真的討厭James和Sirius去過那裡的想法。他覺得他們好像看到了他想要隱藏的一些私人部分。就像他第一次在他們面前變形時一樣。

“I can’t believe I missed that too.” Peter sighed. “Were there loads of muggles? What was it like?”

“我真不敢相信我也錯過了。”Peter嘆道。“有很多麻瓜嗎？那是什麼樣子的？”

“C’mon Pete,” James said, “That’s Moony’s home you’re talking about.”

“拜託，Pete，”James說，“那是Moony的家。”

“It’s fine.” Remus said.

“沒事。”Remus說。

“I bet it's great, living with loads of other people your age,” James said, encouragingly. It was James’s greatest sorrow that he had grown up an only child.

“我打賭和很多同齡人一起住很棒，”James鼓勵地說。他最大的遺憾就是他是獨生子。

“It’s…” Remus looked for the right word. “It’s noisy. Did you go inside?”

“那是……”Remus找著合適的詞。“很吵。你們進去了嗎？”

“Padfoot did, crawled under a hole in the back fence.”

“Padfoot進去了，從後院的洞爬進去的。”

“Didn’t go in the building, though.” Sirius said, rolling onto his front. The muscles in his back moved smoothly under his skin and Remus had to fight not to bite his lip. “Some bitch started throwing stones at me.”

“但沒進建築物。”Sirius說，翻身趴下。他背部的肌肉在皮膚下平滑地移動，Remus不得不忍住不咬嘴唇。“有個婊子開始向我扔石頭。”

“Matron.” Remus confirmed.

“宿舍管理員。”Remus確認。

“Must’ve been.” Sirius nodded, obviously pleased at the attention, “If she treats people the way she treats dogs then I don’t blame you for running away.”

“應該是。”Sirius點點頭，顯然對注意力很滿意，“如果她對待人就像對待狗一樣，我不怪你跑掉。”

“It wasn't really about her.” Remus said, pointedly.

“這不全是因為她。”Remus指責地說。

“It’s lucky Prongs and Padfoot found you though, eh Moony?” Peter smiled, blissfully ignorant, “Otherwise you’d be lost in muggle London!”

“幸好Prongs和Padfoot找到了你，對吧，Moony？”Peter笑著說，幸福地無知，“不然你會迷失在麻瓜的倫敦！”

“I wasn’t lost.” Remus said, icily, putting his book down finally. “I was with a friend.”

“我沒有迷路。”Remus冷冷地說，終於把書放下。“我和一個朋友在一起。”

“But James said--”

“但James說——”

“I said he was in a squat, Pete, not alone. He was with this muggle chap - sorry Remus, I’ve forgotten his name..?”

“我說他在一個臨時住處，Pete，不是獨自一人。他和這個麻瓜在一起——對不起Remus，我忘了他的名字..？”

“He didn't tell us his name.” Sirius said, out of nowhere. Remus sat up and squinted at him. Sirius was staring at him in a strange way, but it only brought Remus’s hackles up.

“他沒告訴我們他的名字。”Sirius突然說。Remus坐起來，瞇著眼看著他。Sirius用奇怪的眼神盯著他，但這只讓Remus更加警覺。

“No.” He replied, “I didn't.” He got to his feet. “I’m going in, it's too hot.”

“沒有。”他回答，“我沒說。”他站了起來。“我要進去了，太熱了。”

James, who seemed to have grasped that the conversation had taken an unpleasant turn, got up too.

James，似乎明白談話變得不愉快，也站了起來。

“Yeah, you’re right Moony. Shall we all go in for a bit? Have a drink and do that washing up mum wanted sorting. She’ll be back soon.”

“對，你說得對，Moony。我們都進去一會兒吧？喝點東西，做媽媽想讓我們做的洗碗。她很快就會回來。”

Mrs Potter had left for the afternoon on an errand, and Mr Potter was at work. Gully was in the house somewhere, of course, but he never made his presence known unless summoned. The boys were pretty much alone.

Potter夫人下午出去辦事了，Potter先生在上班。Gully當然在房子的某個地方，但除非被召喚，否則他從不露面。男孩們幾乎是獨自一人。

“I’ll go home if you’re going to do chores,” Peter grumbled, struggling to his own feet, “I can do housework at mine.”

“如果你們要做家務，我就回家，”Peter抱怨道，艱難地站起來，“我可以在自己家做家務。”

“Cheer up Wormy,” James slapped him on his sweaty shoulder, “There’re jam tarts in the kitchen, you can have the marmalade one if you want.”

“高興點Wormy，”James拍了拍他汗津津的肩膀，“廚房裡有果醬塔，如果你想要可以吃橘子醬的那個。”

The four of them strolled back across the crisp brittle lawn to the house, stopping at the shed so that Sirius and James could put their brooms away first. Pete went straight in for his tart, and Remus hung back on the patio, between them all, feeling very put out and agitated. He sat on the low brick wall again and listened to Sirius and James’s cheerful banter from inside the shed.

他們四個人漫步穿過乾脆的草坪回到房子，先在棚子停下，讓Sirius和James把掃帚收好。Peter直接進去拿他的塔，而Remus留在露台上，在他們之間，感到非常煩躁和不安。他再次坐在低矮的磚牆上，聽著棚子裡Sirius和James愉快的玩笑。

“I ought to polish the handle again before I pack it away…”

“在收起來之前我應該再擦一次把手……”

“Bloody hell Prongs, you polish it twice a day already.”

“該死的Prongs，你已經一天擦兩次了。”

“It’s called looking after your equipment, Black.”

“這叫保養你的裝備，Black。”

“I call it sexual frustration.”

“我叫它性挫折。”

“Piss off!”

“滾開！”

There was a scuffle, and Remus could hear Sirius’s gleeful cackling as the two boys wrestled. “Wait ‘til we’re back at school and I can curse your bollocks off!” James laughed,

有一陣爭鬥，Remus能聽到Sirius愉快的咯咯笑聲，兩個男孩摔跤。“等我們回到學校，我就能把你的睾丸詛咒掉！”James笑道，

“Don’t you dare - some of us use our bollocks!”

“你敢——我們有些人還用睾丸呢！”

“You tosser! I ought to - oh shit, watch out…”

“你這混蛋！我應該——哦，該死，小心……”

“Ah!” Sirius cried, “Bugger! That hurt.”

“啊！”Sirius喊道，“該死！好痛。”

They both staggered back out into the daylight, Sirius clutching his hand.

他們都搖搖晃晃地走回陽光下，Sirius捂著他的手。

“What did you do?” James asked, peering over. He paled, upon seeing Sirius’s hand, and backed away, “Sorry mate, you know how I am with blood…”

“你做了什麼？”James問道，探身過來。一看到Sirius的手，他就臉色蒼白，退後了一步，“對不起，老兄，你知道我對血有多敏感……”

“Eurgh, it’s really bleeding, too…”

“噁，它真的在流血……”

“Oi, get away from me!”

“喂，離我遠點！”

“What shall I do? Wait ‘til your mum gets home?”

“我該怎麼辦？等你媽媽回來？”

“No choice - I dunno any healing spells...”

“別無選擇——我不懂任何治療咒語……”

“Ow, it bloody hurts…”

“啊，好痛……”

“Oh, for god’s sake,” Remus stood up, squinting. “Let me see.” 「哦，天啊，」Remus站起來，瞇著眼。「讓我看看。」

Sirius and James both turned to look at him. Sirius’s eyes flickered to James, then back to Remus, before he walked over, hand outstretched. The cut was very deep, blood running in rivulets down Sirius’s long white wrists. Sirius和James都轉頭看著他。Sirius的眼睛在James和Remus之間閃爍，然後他走過來，伸出手。傷口很深，血沿著Sirius長長的白皙手腕流下。

Remus swallowed, “You need to clean that, it’ll get infected… hang on, I’ve got some stuff in my trunk.” Remus吞了吞口水，「你需要清理一下，否則會感染……等一下，我的箱子裡有些東西。」

He led Sirius through the kitchen, upstairs to the first floor bathroom and turned on the cold tap. He had some TCP in his trunk leftover from St Edmund’s, where he often had to look after his own scrapes when Madam Pomfrey wasn’t around. He brought it through, along with some cotton balls and gauze. 他帶著Sirius穿過廚房，上樓到一樓的浴室，打開冷水龍頭。他的箱子裡有一些TCP，這是從St Edmund’s留下來的，那裡他經常需要在Pomfrey夫人不在時自己處理擦傷。他帶了一些棉球和紗布過來。

“Come here.” He said, sitting on the edge if the bathtub and motioning that Sirius sit on the closed toilet seat. He obeyed, still holding his hand out warily. 「過來。」他說，坐在浴缸邊上，示意Sirius坐在蓋好的馬桶上。Sirius順從地坐下，依然小心翼翼地伸出手。

It was much cooler, in the bathroom, reassuringly sterile, like the hospital wing. Remus found that very calming. Sirius was placid and docile, trusting Remus completely with watchful eyes, like a pet. 浴室裡涼快多了，令人安心的無菌環境，像醫院病房。Remus覺得這非常平靜。Sirius安靜且溫順，完全信任Remus，目光警惕，像寵物一樣。

“What’s that?” He asked as Remus tipped some disinfectant onto the cotton. 「那是什麼？」當Remus把消毒液倒在棉球上時，他問道。

“TCP.” He said, “It’ll clean the wound.” 「TCP。」他說，「它會清潔傷口。」

“Is it muggle stuff?” 「是麻瓜的東西嗎？」

“I’m sure it will work just the same,” Remus raised an eyebrow. He took Sirius’s wrist, gripping it more roughly than he really needed to. His skin was hot from the sun. Remus could feel his pulse. “It’s going to sting.” He said, as he pressed down. Sirius flinched, and Remus was reminded of the time after Christmas they’d spent in the Potter’s bathroom, piercing Sirius’s ear. 「我相信它一樣有效，」Remus挑起一邊眉毛。他抓住Sirius的手腕，比實際需要的更粗暴。他的皮膚因陽光變得炙熱。Remus能感覺到他的脈搏。「這會刺痛，」他說，按了下去。Sirius顫抖了一下，Remus想起了聖誕節後他們在Potter家的浴室裡，給Sirius穿耳洞的情景。

“Will it hurt?” Sirius panicked at the last minute, as Remus was poised with the pin. 「會痛嗎？」當Remus拿著針準備時，Sirius在最後一刻驚慌地問道。

“Well we’ve numbed it a bit, but yeah, probably.” Remus said, matter-of-factly. “Don’t be such a girl.” 「我們已經稍微麻醉了一點，但可能會的。」Remus不以為然地說。「別這麼娘。」

“Be gentle with me, Moony!” 「對我溫柔點，Moony！」

They had both laughed, and Remus shook him fondly; 他們都笑了，Remus滿懷深情地搖了搖他；

“Stay still you big wuss.” 「別動，你這大膽小鬼。」

He finished cleaning the wound and then wrapped it in gauze, taping it neatly. 他清理完傷口後，用紗布包紮好，貼得整整齊齊。

“Probably throb a bit.” He explained. “Meant to be tight. Stops the bleeding.” 「可能會有點痛。」他解釋道。「要緊一點。止血。」

“Thanks, Moony.” 「謝謝，Moony。」

“Any time.” Remus went to get up, placing both hands on the cold porcelain of the tub. Sirius suddenly reached out and touched his arm. 「隨時。」Remus準備起身，雙手放在浴缸冷冰冰的瓷上。Sirius突然伸手碰了碰他的手臂。

“I’m sorry.” 「對不起。」

“I know.” Remus replied. “You’ve said.” 「我知道。」Remus回答。「你已經說了。」

“What I did…” Sirius licked his lips nervously, still grasping Remus’s arm as if that was the only thing keeping him in place. 「我做的……」Sirius緊張地舔了舔嘴唇，仍然抓著Remus的手臂，仿佛那是唯一能讓他穩住的東西。

“Don’t.” Remus frowned, his resolve weakening. 「別。」Remus皺起眉頭，他的決心開始動搖。

“But we ought to talk--” 「但我們應該談談——」

“We can’t.” Remus said, simply. “I can’t, anyway. There are no words for what you did to me.” 「我們不能。」Remus簡單地說。「反正我不能。對你做的事，我無言以對。」

“No.” Sirius hung his head. “You’re right.” He let go, but Remus didn’t walk away, though he knew he ought to. Sirius ran his uninjured hand through his hair in frustration. “I’m such an idiot.” He said. 「不。」Sirius低下頭。「你說得對。」他放開了，但Remus沒有走開，儘管他知道自己應該這麼做。Sirius懊惱地用未受傷的手撥了撥頭髮。「我真是個白痴。」他說。

Remus did not refute this. Sirius continued. “It was a really good year, wasn’t it, fifth year? Spending the moons together, and the parties… then I went and ballsed it all up.” Remus沒有反駁。Sirius繼續說。「那年真的很棒，不是嗎？第五年？一起度過月圓之夜，還有聚會……然後我把一切搞砸了。」

“Well.” Remus relented. “I made some mistakes too. I made things… things were different, after my birthday.” 「嗯。」Remus鬆口了。「我也犯了一些錯誤。我使事情……事情在我生日後變得不同。」

“What? Moony, no!” Sirius’s eyes widened. He looked so earnest and sincere that Remus wanted to forgive everything in an instant. “I know I wasn’t… you didn’t do anything wrong. That, what happened on your birthday, it was…” 「什麼？Moony，不！」Sirius瞪大了眼睛。他看起來如此真誠和誠懇，以至於Remus想立刻原諒一切。「我知道我不是……你沒有做錯任何事。那，發生在你生日的事情，是……」

Remus held his breath while Sirius searched for the word. “...it was really brave.” Sirius finished. Remus屏住呼吸，等待Sirius找詞。「……那真的很勇敢。」Sirius說完。

Remus blinked. Brave?! What on earth was that supposed to mean? Sirius saw his reaction, and tried to cover his tracks, Remus眨了眨眼。勇敢？！那到底是什麼意思？Sirius看到他的反應，試圖掩飾，

“I just mean that you shouldn't worry about it. It didn’t… that didn’t change anything, ok?” 「我只是想說你不應該為此擔心。那並沒有……那並沒有改變任何事情，好嗎？」

“Ok.” Remus looked down, then – feeling braver, looked up again. “We never talked about that.” 「好吧。」Remus低下頭，然後——感覺更勇敢了，再次抬起頭。「我們從未談過那件事。」

“You’re my best friend, Remus.” 「你是我最好的朋友，Remus。」

“Sirius, please….” 「Sirius，拜託……」

“And I know what I did. There aren’t words, no, so I’ll shut up and I’ll… I’ll do actions, instead, ok? I’ll prove I’m sorry, every day. I swear, I’ll never do another stupid thing without thinking again.” 「我知道我做了什麼。無言以對，所以我會閉嘴，我會……我會用行動代替，好嗎？我每天都會證明我很抱歉。我發誓，我再也不會在不經思考的情況下做愚蠢的事。」

Remus gave him a small smile, Remus對他微微一笑，

“Come on.” 「來吧。」

Sirius smiled too, looking relieved. Sirius也笑了，顯得鬆了一口氣。

“Yeah, ok, maybe a bit ambitious. I’ll never do anything to hurt any one of my friends, ever again, how’s that?” 「是的，好吧，也許有點雄心壯志。我再也不會做任何傷害我朋友的事，這樣如何？」

Remus breathed in deeply. Forgiveness would be such a blessed relief. Remus深吸一口氣。原諒真是莫大的安慰。

“It’s a start.” 「這是一個開始。」

 

 Chapter 96: Sixth Year: September

第96章：第六年：九月

 

Wednesday 1st September 1976
1976年9月1日，星期三

“This is the year, lads. This is the year it finally happens. Six years of waiting and it all pays off.”
“今年就是那一年，伙计们。今年终于会发生。六年的等待，全都值得了。”

“You can’t be talking about what I think you’re talking about,” Remus raised an eyebrow over to top of his book.
“你不会在说我想的那个吧，”雷穆斯抬起一只眉毛看着他的书。

“Oh yes,” James was beaming like a drunkard, “Lily Evans is definitely going to realise she’s mad about me. I can feel it.”
“哦，对，”詹姆斯像醉汉一样笑得灿烂，“莉莉·埃文斯一定会意识到她对我有多疯狂。我能感觉到。”

“你确定吗？”小天狼星笑道，“你以前也有过这样的感觉。”

“确实有过，”詹姆斯点了点头，表示尊重，“你说得对，皮足。但这次有些不同。我几乎能感受到。爱情弥漫在空气中。”

“谁在叫傻子，月亮？”小天狼星反驳道，“如果我让女人因欲望疯狂，我也没办法。”

“小天狼星该死的布莱克，我真想杀了你！”玛丽愤怒的尖叫声几乎能震碎玻璃。小天狼星几乎从座位上跳了起来。

Remus gave a satisfied nod.
雷穆斯满意地点了点头。

“Wild with something, anyway.”
“反正是被什么东西弄得很疯狂。”

James guffawed, nearly choking on the Bertie Botts every flavour bean he had been chewing.
詹姆斯哈哈大笑，差点呛到他咀嚼的博提·波特百味豆。

No one was happier about Remus and Sirius’s reconciliation than James. He didn’t say anything directly, but as soon as he recognised that his two best friends were no longer keeping each other at arm's length, he was grinning from ear to ear, back to his usual mischievous self. And therefore,
没有人比詹姆斯对雷穆斯和小天狼星和解更开心。他没有直接说什么，但一旦他意识到他最好的两个朋友不再互相保持距离，他就从耳到耳地笑了回去，恢复了他一贯的调皮。因此，
back to sighing over Lily Evans.
重新开始对莉莉·埃文斯叹气。

Lily entered the carriage at this point, just behind Mary who had burst in like a whirlwind. Lily smiled at Remus and took the spare seat beside him, he smiled back and they settled in to watch the show.
莉莉在此时进入了车厢，紧跟着像旋风般闯入的玛丽。莉莉对雷穆斯微笑，坐在他旁边的空位上，他也回以微笑，他们就这样安顿下来，准备观看接下来的戏码。

“我做了什么？！”小天狼星不满地问。

“You really don’t know, do you?!” Mary stood with her hands on her hips, a look of disgust on her face. She looked spectacular when she was angry, her gold hoop earrings jangled, her kohl rimmed eyes were wide and fiery. “Diagon Alley?!” She stamped her foot.
“你真的不知道吗？！”玛丽双手叉腰，脸上露出厌恶的表情。她生气的时候看起来很壮观，她的金色圆环耳环叮当作响，她的眼睛被眼线笔勾勒得又大又炯炯有神。“对角巷？！”她跺了跺脚。

Sirius’s eyes widened.
小天狼星的眼睛瞪大了。

“Bugger.”
“该死。”

“去你的，布莱克！”玛丽转身愤怒地离开了。小天狼星急忙跟在她身后走下走廊，火车刚开始动起来时，

雷穆斯转向莉莉，

“没有可能，”雷穆斯回答道，又翻了一页。

詹姆斯的褐色眼睛瞪大了，他盯着他们俩。莉莉咯咯笑了，她的眼睛充满挑逗，雷穆斯突然明白了她为什么让詹姆斯如此疯狂。

The compartment door slid open and Marlene entered. She’d had her hair cut into a neat bob over the summer, like Mia Farrow. It was very becoming. 雷穆斯真的很感动，他不得不抬起书本遮住脸。他希望莉莉知道詹姆斯是非常诚恳的，而不仅仅是为了赢得她的赞许。隔间的门滑开了，玛琳娜走了进来。她的头发在暑假剪成了整齐的波波头，像米亚·法罗一样，非常好看。她笑着对朋友们点头，坐在了詹姆斯旁边。

Mary forgave Sirius by the time they reached Hogwarts, on the promise that he would take her for a day in Hogsmeade to make up for it. Remus was pleased - he could honestly, truly say that, without bitterness. He felt that Sirius had drawn a line under their kiss, back in the Potter’s bathroom, and it was up to him, Remus, to honour and respect that line.
玛丽在他们到达霍格沃茨时原谅了西里斯，条件是他要带她去霍格梅德度过一天以弥补。雷穆斯对此感到高兴——他可以真心诚意地这样说，没有一丝苦涩。他觉得西里斯在波特家浴室里亲吻后的事情上画了一个句号，接下来就由他，雷穆斯，来尊重和履行这个界限。

西里斯喜欢玛丽。雷穆斯只能接受这个事实，仅此而已。是的，没错，有时雷穆斯会幻想亲吻西里斯的锁骨凹处，从他喉咙的深处一路抚摸到他的肚脐——那又怎么样？！这纯粹是雷穆斯自己的问题。他得把注意力集中在其他地方。也许克里斯托弗在暑假里变得光彩夺目了。

The feast and the sorting was as magnificent and reassuringly predictable as ever. The friends chatted about their new timetables (Lily was extremely disappointed to find out that Remus had chosen to drop Potions, but he promised to keep giving her a run for her money in Charms), their summers (tactfully avoiding Mary’s birthday) and the looming pressure of NEWTs. “发生了什么？”玛丽问道，双手叉腰，

“该死的穆尔西伯，”詹姆斯说，脸上带着滑稽的皱眉，他的腿在下面活跃地飞舞，

“Petrificus Totalus,” Sirius said, with a yawn. James froze still, and fell to the ground as stiff as a board.
“全身僵直咒，”西里斯打了个哈欠说道。詹姆斯立刻僵硬住，像木板一样摔倒在地。

“Black!” Lily sighed
“黑！”莉莉叹了口气

“What?!” Sirius grinned, “I was only trying to help!”
“怎么了？！”西里斯咧嘴一笑，“我只是想帮忙！”

Remus giggled, still stretching. It was probably time for bed. He got up slowly, as Sirius, Mary and Lily stood over James, arguing over which spell to break first - the dancing one or the petrifying one - and Sirius was in favour of simply levitating him up to bed as he was.
雷穆斯咯咯笑着，仍在伸展。差不多该睡觉了。他慢慢站起身来，看到西里斯、玛丽和莉莉站在詹姆斯身边，争论着先解除哪个咒语——跳舞的还是僵直的——西里斯倾向于直接把他悬浮到床上。

Just as Remus was heading in the direction of the boys dormitory, he caught sight of Christopher. The fifth year boy was coming down the stairs, with a shiny silver prefects badge pinned proudly to his chest. Unfortunately, Christopher had not become incredibly good looking over the summer - in fact, quite the opposite. He had obviously been somewhere very hot and sunny over the summer, and his pale English skin was scorched bright red and peeling grotesquely at his nose.
就在雷穆斯正朝男生宿舍方向走时，他看到了克里斯托弗。这个五年级的男孩正下楼，胸前别着一枚闪亮的银色学监徽章。不幸的是，克里斯托弗在暑假期间并没有变得非常好看——实际上，情况正好相反。他显然在非常炎热和阳光明媚的地方呆过，英俊的肤色被晒得通红，鼻子上的皮肤还在可怕地脱皮。

They stared at each other for a moment, before Christopher looked at his feet, then walked away without a word. Remus felt the sting of guilt. He’d have to apologise, at some point.
他们对视了一会儿，然后克里斯托弗低下头，默默地走开了。雷穆斯感到一阵内疚。他得找时间道个歉。

Wednesday 8th September 1976
1976年9月8日，星期三

“With your OWLs now behind you, and your NEWTs over a year away, do not fall into the trap of believing that this will be an easy year. Your sixth year lays the foundation for your advanced exams, and the work you do will be pivotal in determining the opportunities available to you once you leave school…”
“既然你的OWLs考试已经过去，你的NEWTs考试还在一年之外，不要陷入这种认为这一年会很容易的陷阱。你们的第六年为高级考试打下了基础，你们的努力将在确定你们离校后可用机会方面发挥关键作用……”

Remus fought not to yawn. He might have felt nervous, worried, spurred into action – and he had been. The first time he’d heard this speech. They were halfway through their first week of sixth year, and so far every teacher had performed some variation on this address. This morning, the lecture was being given by Professor Flitwick, and therefore made mildly more interesting because of his squeaky little voice.
雷穆斯努力抑制着哈欠。他本来可能会感到紧张、担忧，甚至激励自己——而且确实如此。这是他第一次听到这番话。他们已经进入了第六学年的第一周的一半，到目前为止，每个老师都在以不同的方式重复这段讲话。今天早上，教授弗利特维克在讲这段话，因此因为他的尖锐声音，讲座显得稍微有趣些。

Remus looked out of the window. It was the full moon tonight, and he was restless. He had a horrible feeling about it, as well as the usual early twinges and surges of adrenaline. It was the first full moon he would be spending with the marauders since that terrible night in June. It was the first full moon after the werewolf attack in August – since he had run away from St Edmund’s.
雷穆斯向窗外望去。今晚是满月，他感到不安。他对这次满月有一种可怕的预感，还有往常的早期抽搐和肾上腺素激增。这是他自六月份那可怕的夜晚以来，第一次和麻烦制造者们一起度过满月。这是八月份狼人袭击后的第一次满月——自从他从圣埃德蒙德逃走以来。

The murders played heavy on his mind. The family was called Munday – both parents had been muggle born. It had been in the papers, and Remus had read everything he could while he was at the Potters. He’d searched high and low for mention of Greyback, for a picture, a description – anything. If this… man was after him, then he needed to be armed with information. But there was nothing. The press wasn’t publishing anything more than Moody had already told him.
谋杀案件让他心情沉重。这个家庭叫穆恩迪——父母都是麻瓜出生的。这已经在报纸上报道了，雷穆斯在波特家时读了他能找到的一切。他拼命寻找有关格雷巴克的任何信息，包括图片、描述——任何东西。如果这个……人要找他，那他就需要掌握信息。但是没有任何线索。媒体没有比穆迪已经告诉他的更多的报道。

The letter to Ferox had been written for almost a week now. It was burning a hole in Remus’s back pocket. He’d been waiting to get a chance to sneak off to the owlery on his own.
写给费罗克斯的信已经写了快一个星期了。它在雷穆斯的后口袋里燃烧着一个洞。他一直在等待机会独自溜到信使塔去。

Dear Professor Ferox,
亲爱的费罗克斯教授，

[he knew that Ferox wasn’t a professor any more, but he didn’t know what else to call him, and couldn’t bring himself to address him as anything so familiar as ‘Leo’.]
[他知道费罗克斯不再是教授了，但他不知道该怎么称呼他，也不忍心用‘利奥’这样亲昵的称呼。]

I hope it’s ok for me to write to you. I had a few questions and I couldn’t think of anyone else who might know. I spoke to Alastor Moody while I was staying with the Potters this summer, and he said you’re well. I hope you aren’t anywhere too dangerous.
我希望写信给你没问题。我有一些问题，想不到还有谁能知道。我在这个夏天住在波特家时和阿拉斯托·穆迪谈过，他说你很好。我希望你现在不在任何危险的地方。

Moody told me that the Munday family were murdered by Greyback. He said that Greyback might try to find me, and get me to join him. I hope you know I would never join that side. I do want to be prepared if he comes after me, though. Can you tell me anything useful? I don’t even know what he looks like.
穆迪告诉我，穆恩迪一家被格雷巴克谋杀了。他说格雷巴克可能会试图找到我，让我加入他。我希望你知道我绝不会加入那一边。不过，我确实希望能有所准备，以防他来找我。你能告诉我一些有用的东西吗？我甚至不知道他长什么样子。

I’m sorry to bother you with this, but you are the only person I can ask, because you knew my dad, and you know me.
对不起打扰你了，但你是唯一一个我能问的人，因为你认识我的父亲，也了解我。

Thank you,
谢谢你，

Remus J. Lupin.
雷穆斯·J·卢平

He knew that you were supposed to end letters ‘yours sincerely’ or ‘yours faithfully’, or something like that, but it seemed so silly and formal. He worried that Ferox might think he was trying too hard to seem grown up.
他知道信的结尾应该用“此致敬礼”或“此致”之类的词，但这些看起来既傻又正式。他担心费罗克斯会觉得他在努力显得成熟。

“Moony? Wakey wakey!” Sirius shook his shoulder.
“穆尼？醒醒！”西里斯摇了摇他的肩膀。

“What?!” Remus looked up, blinking and dazed. Sirius was standing over him, and everyone else was packing up their things,
“什么？！”雷穆斯抬起头，眨了眨眼，感到迷茫。西里斯站在他身边，其他人则在收拾东西，

“Lesson’s over, dopey. Where did you wander off to?”
“课结束了，傻瓜。你去哪儿了？”

“Just distracted,” Remus replied. He stood up and scooped his own assortment of quills and parchment into his book back, getting up.
“只是有点分心，”雷穆斯回答道。他站起身，把一堆羽毛笔和羊皮纸放进书包里，然后起身。

Sirius’s face softened. He leaned in and said very low,
西里斯的脸色变得柔和了。他凑近，低声说道，

“Is it because of tonight? Are you nervous?”
“是因为今晚吗？你紧张吗？”

Remus gave a sort of half shrug, half reassuring smile,
雷穆斯半耸了耸肩，半带着安慰的微笑，

“No more than usual.”
“比平时多不了多少。”

“We’ve got a free now,” Sirius said, chirpily - he was very much enjoying his NEWT timetable, having dropped four subjects. “Want to pop round the greenhouses?”
“我们现在有空闲时间，”西里斯愉快地说——他很喜欢他的NEWT时间表，已经退选了四门课。“想去温室转转吗？”

“Nah,” Remus grinned, “S’ok. I actually… I have to go to the owlery. Got a letter to post.”
“没必要，”雷穆斯咧嘴一笑，“没事的。我实际上……我得去信使塔。有封信要寄。”

“Oh yeah? I’ll come with you, James has another poncey prefect meeting. I swear you never went to this many meetings,”
“哦？我跟你一起去，詹姆斯还有另一场虚伪的学监会议。我发誓你从来没有参加过这么多会议，”

“Nah, I sort of left it all up to Evans, to be honest,” Remus smirked, “Of course, I wasn’t trying to impress her.”
“嗯，我基本上都把一切留给了埃文斯，老实说，”雷穆斯咧嘴一笑，“当然，我不是为了打动她。”

Sirius laughed,
西里斯笑了，

“Too bloody right - at least you know where your priorities are, Moony. Who’s the letter for?”
“说得对——至少你知道你的优先事项在哪里，穆尼。那封信是给谁的？”

“Er… do you mind not asking?” Remus looked down, as they left the classroom, walking with a slightly longer stride than usual so that Sirius would have to walk faster to keep up. It was a cheap trick, but there had to be some benefits to being tall.
“呃……你介意别问吗？”雷穆斯低下头，他们离开教室时，走得比平时稍微快一点，以便西里斯得快点跟上。这是个小把戏，但作为高个子应该有一些好处。

“Oh, of course, mate.” Sirius nodded respectfully, “Don’t mind me, I’m just bored, y’know.”
“哦，当然，朋友。”西里斯尊敬地点了点头，“别介意我，我只是有点无聊，你知道的。”

He had been extremely pliant lately, eager to supply Remus with any allowances he requested. Remus thought he could probably get away with snogging Mary on the Gryffindor dinner table with Sirius’s blessing, the way things were.
他最近非常顺从，热衷于满足雷穆斯提出的任何要求。雷穆斯觉得他可能可以在格兰芬多的餐桌上和玛丽亲吻，只要得到西里斯的祝福，就没有问题了。

They tramped up to the owlery quickly - with the moon waxing Remus’s energy levels were through the roof - then going single file up the final narrow winding staircase.
他们迅速走到信使塔——随着月亮的盈满，雷穆斯的能量水平飙升——然后单列走上最后狭窄的盘旋楼梯。

The owlery was a beautiful place, by anyone’s standards (provided you ignored the smell of bird shit) with the very best view of anywhere else in the castle. It was a bright and airy space with high rafters, filled with the soft sounds of roosting owls. Sirius dutifully hung back a respectable distance as Remus selected the sturdiest looking owl (he had no idea where Ferox was, or how far away, and wanted a bird that was up to the job), attached his letter, and released it through the huge picture window.
信使塔是个美丽的地方，不管谁来看（只要你忽略鸟屎的味道），它提供了城堡中其他地方无法比拟的最佳视角。这里明亮通风，高高的椽子，充满了栖息的猫头鹰的柔和声音。西里斯恭敬地保持着一段可观的距离，雷穆斯挑选了一只看起来最结实的猫头鹰（他不知道费罗克斯在哪里，或者距离多远，他需要一只能胜任的鸟），将信件绑上，然后通过巨大的画窗释放了它。

Sirius was leaning out of the window on the opposite side, staring down at the forbidden forest.
西里斯正倚着对面的窗户，盯着禁忌森林。

“How far d’you reckon we got, last year?” He asked, “Couple of miles, at least…”
“你觉得我们去年飞了多远？”他问道，“至少几英里……”

“At least,” Remus agreed, joining him at the windowsill.
“至少，”雷穆斯同意道，走到窗台边和他一起站着。

“Think we could reach those mountains? There’re caves, I bet. I used to quite fancy living in a cave, when I was little. Me and Reggie were going to run away from home and become cave dwellers.”
“你觉得我们能到达那些山脉吗？那里一定有洞穴。我小时候挺喜欢住在洞穴里的。我和雷吉曾打算逃家成为洞穴居民。”

“Weirdo,” Remus shook his head. “It’d be freezing.”
“怪人，”雷穆斯摇了摇头。“会很冷的。”

“Yeah, well you don’t think about that stuff when you’re seven, do you?”
“是啊，不过你七岁的时候不考虑这些东西，对吧？”

“I s’pose. I never actually thought about running away, to be honest. Lots of boys actually did it, but the police normally brought them back. Matron used to say that if one of us went missing it was no skin off her nose - she still got paid, at the end of the week.”
“我想也是。老实说，我从来没有真正想过逃跑。很多男孩确实这样做了，但警察通常会把他们带回去。看护阿姨曾经说，如果我们其中一个失踪了，对她来说没什么损失——她到周末时还会拿到工资。”

“Moony, that’s…”
“穆尼，那是……”

Remus laughed, and moved away,
雷穆斯笑了笑，走开了，

“C’mon, let’s get out of here, I’m hungry.”
“走吧，我们出去，我饿了。”

They began a slightly slower descent down the spiral staircase, but had to stop halfway as they heard footsteps coming up. Remus’s stomach sank when he saw it was Christopher. He’d recovered a bit from his sunburn, but still had a bit of a hot glow around his cheeks and nose. He froze when he saw Sirius, with Remus just behind him.
他们开始缓慢下行的螺旋楼梯，但在听到脚步声上来时不得不在中途停下。雷穆斯的胃一沉，看到是克里斯托弗时。他的晒伤恢复了一些，但脸颊和鼻子周围仍然有些红热。他看到西里斯时立刻僵住了，雷穆斯就在他身后。

The two boys flattened themselves against the wall as best they could to let him past.
两个男孩尽量紧贴墙壁，让他过去。

“Hi, Chris,” Remus smiled, politely.
“嗨，克里斯，”雷穆斯礼貌地微笑道。

“Hi.” Christopher responded, not making eye contact. Ah. He was definitely still annoyed about the way Remus had spoken to him at the end of last term. Remus had been worried about that - but he supposed he deserved a bit of cold shoulder. The silver pin gleamed on Chris’s robes, and Remus tried not to wince. He could feel it in his teeth, a giddy, sick sensation.
“嗨。”克里斯托弗回应道，没有看眼睛。啊。他显然还对雷穆斯上学期末的态度感到生气。雷穆斯对这一点有些担忧——但他觉得自己确实应该受到些冷落。克里斯的袍子上的银色徽章在闪光，雷穆斯尽量不去皱眉。他在牙齿间感到一种晕眩的恶心感。

“Well done on getting prefect,” he said, trying to sound friendly and encouraging.
“恭喜你当上学监了，”他说，试图听起来友好和鼓励。

“Yeah… thanks.” Christopher nodded. he still didn’t look up, exactly, but he sort of looked at the space over Remus’s left shoulder, and gave a weak smile as he passed.
“嗯……谢谢。”克里斯托弗点了点头。他还是没完全抬头，但有点儿看了看雷穆斯左肩的上方，在路过时给了个虚弱的微笑。

The close proximity to the silver was extremely unpleasant, and Remus’s head swam, making him dizzy. As Christopher pushed past them both, Remus wobbled forward and had to grip Sirius’s shoulder to keep balanced. He had to concentrate on his breathing to avoid fainting altogether until Christopher had reached the owlery, and barely noticed that Sirius had slipped a strong arm around his back for support.
靠近银色徽章的地方非常不舒服，雷穆斯感到头晕目眩。克里斯托弗挤过他们时，雷穆斯前倾了一下，必须抓住西里斯的肩膀以保持平衡。他不得不集中精力呼吸，以免完全昏厥，直到克里斯托弗到达信使塔，几乎没有注意到西里斯在他背后搭上了一只强壮的手臂以支撑他。

When he opened his eyes, and the wooziness had passed, Remus thought it must only have been a few seconds that they had stood like that, clinging to each other in the shadowy stairway. (Must stop getting stuck in confined spaces with him, the logical part of Remus’s brain scolded.) He realised he had been gripping Sirius’s shoulder really quite hard, and let go quickly, stepping away and adjusting his robes.
当他睁开眼睛，头晕感消失时，雷穆斯觉得他们这样站着，大概只有几秒钟而已，在阴暗的楼梯间相互依偎着。（雷穆斯的理智部分训斥道：必须停止和他困在狭小的空间里。）他意识到自己抓着西里斯的肩膀很用力，迅速松手，退开一步，整理了一下袍子。

“Sorry,” he said, “Took me by surprise,”
“对不起，”他说，“把我吓了一跳。”

“S’ok,” Sirius smiled, turning and walking down the stairs again, “Another reason to hate prefects, eh?”
“没事，”西里斯笑了笑，转身再次下楼，“又一个讨厌学监的理由，对吧？”

 

 

 Chapter 97: Sixth Year: October Chapter Text Saturday 9th October 1976

 

“Ugh,” Remus staggered to his feet as the transformation completed and his body settled back into its human form.
“呃，”雷穆斯在变身完成后踉跄地站起身来，他的身体恢复成了人类的形态。

“That didn't seem too bad?” James said, having just transformed himself.
“这看起来不算太糟糕？”詹姆斯说道，刚刚完成了变身。

“Depends what you mean by bad,” Remus grimaced, pulling his trousers on quickly.
“这要看你说的‘糟糕’是什么意思，”雷穆斯做了个鬼脸，迅速穿上裤子。

James looked away, politely to preserve his modesty, and Sirius, still a dog, padded over with Remus’s shirt in his mouth, offering it up with a cocked head. “Cheers, Padfoot,” Remus smiled. He wanted to pat the dog on the head, and had to keep reminding himself that this was Sirius.
詹姆斯礼貌地转过身以保持他的体面，而西里斯仍然是一只狗，叼着雷穆斯的衬衫走过来，歪着头递给他。“谢谢，帕德弗特，”雷穆斯笑了。他想拍拍狗的头，却不断提醒自己这就是西里斯。

“Thank merlin it’s Saturday,” James yawned, taking a seat on the beaten-up couch. It sagged drearily beneath him, springs wheezing.
“谢天谢地今天是星期六，”詹姆斯打了个哈欠，坐在那张破旧的沙发上。沙发在他下面悲惨地塌陷，弹簧发出喘息声。

“Yeah, if Madam Pomfrey lets me off the hospital wing, I’ll probably go straight to bed anyway,” Remus replied, stifling his own yawn, and laying down on his cot.
“是啊，如果庞弗雷夫人让我离开医务室，我可能还是直接去床上休息，”雷穆斯回答道，抑制住自己的哈欠，躺在他的行军床上。

“You’re lucky,” Peter said, appearing as if from nowhere, in a far corner of the room, “S’posed to be taking Dezzie to Hogsmeade at eleven. Prongs, don’t you have to lead the third years down?”
“你运气真好，”彼得说道，仿佛从无处出现一样，在房间的一个角落，“我应该在十一点带德齐去霍格斯米德。詹姆斯，你不是要带第三年的学生下去吗？”

“Nah,” James yawned again, noisily, “Now Evans knows about Remus’s furry little problem she’s actually cutting me some slack. That fifth year kid with the sunburn is doing it instead.”
“没有，”詹姆斯再次打了个响亮的哈欠，“现在埃文斯知道了雷穆斯的毛茸茸的小问题，她实际上对我放了些水。那个有晒伤的五年级小子在替我做。”

“Evans doesn’t know anything else, does she?” Sirius finally reappeared, joining James on the couch.
“埃文斯不知道别的事吧？”西里斯终于重新出现，坐到詹姆斯旁边的沙发上。

James shook his head, leaning back on the couch and closing his eyes. “Oi,” Sirius nudged him, “We’ve got to go, soon, don’t sleep.”
詹姆斯摇了摇头，靠在沙发上闭上了眼睛。“喂，”西里斯推了推他，“我们快走吧，别睡。”

“You lot go,” Remus murmured, “Get some rest. Thanks for coming, and all that...”
“你们去吧，”雷穆斯低声说，“去休息一下。谢谢你们过来，还有其他的……”

“Coming to Hogsmeade, Moony?” Sirius asked, hauling James to his feet, “Three Broomsticks?”
“要去霍格斯米德吗，穆尼？”西里斯问道，拉着詹姆斯站起来，“三把扫帚酒吧？”

“Can’t,” Remus shook his head, “Didn’t I tell you? Had my permission revoked. After the attacks…”
“不能，”雷穆斯摇了摇头，“我没告诉过你们吗？我的许可被取消了。发生了袭击之后……”

“What?!” Sirius looked outraged, “They can’t punish YOU for something some other bastard’s done!”
“什么？！”西里斯看起来很愤怒，“他们不能因为别人干的事来惩罚你！”

“Shhh!” Remus flapped his hand, frowning. Madam Pomfrey could be on her way down the tunnel - and besides, he had a headache, “It’s not to punish me, it’s for my safety. Now get lost, the lot of you.”
“嘘！”雷穆斯挥了挥手，皱起了眉头。庞弗雷夫人可能在走下隧道的路上——而且，他还头痛，“这不是惩罚我，而是为了我的安全。现在你们都走吧。”

They were gone in just the nick of time, Madam Pomfrey entered the shack only minutes afterwards. She gave him a quick going over, and, satisfied, walked Remus back up to the castle. She prescribed him a few hours sleep in the hospital wing, which he was more than happy to accept. With all of his friends in Hogsmeade, there wasn’t much to miss out on.
他们刚好在最后一刻离开了，庞弗雷夫人几分钟后就进了小屋。她给他检查了一下，满意后，把雷穆斯送回了城堡。她建议他在医务室里睡几个小时，他非常乐意接受。既然所有的朋友都在霍格斯米德，他也不觉得错过了什么。

He woke at about lunch time, stomach rumbling as usual. Madam Pomfrey had evidently anticipated this; there was a plate of cold cuts and bread on his bedside table, along with a bowl of fruit and a large goblet of pumpkin juice, which he drained first.
他在午餐时间左右醒来，肚子像往常一样咕咕叫。庞弗雷夫人显然预料到了这一点；床头柜上有一盘冷切肉和面包，还有一碗水果和一个大酒杯的南瓜汁，他首先喝掉了南瓜汁。

Remus was so ravenous, in fact, that he did not notice the letter propped up in the fruit bowl between two apples until he was well into the construction of his second sandwich. When he saw that it was addressed to him in a script familiar from the hundreds of returned Care of Magical Creatures essays, he almost knocked his plate off the bed in his eagerness to open it.
雷穆斯实际上饿得非常厉害，以至于他直到制作第二个三明治时才注意到那封夹在两个苹果之间的信。当他看到信是写给他的，并且用的是熟悉的笔迹——那是从数百篇《神奇生物护理》论文中看到的，他几乎因急于打开它而把盘子从床上弄掉了。

Dear Remus,

It’s a pleasure to hear from you, I don’t mind in the least.

I cannot disclose my location at present, but rest assured that I am as safe as it is possible for me to be. I am glad to hear that you are well - Dumbledore told me about your OWL results. I’m incredibly proud of you, Remus, I know you must have worked very hard. Keep on like that and I promise that nothing can stop you.

亲爱的雷穆斯，

收到你的来信很高兴，我一点也不介意。

我目前不能透露我的位置，但请放心，我尽可能地安全。我很高兴听到你安好——邓布利多告诉我你的OWLs成绩。我为你感到非常骄傲，雷穆斯，我知道你一定付出了很多努力。继续这样下去，我保证没有什么能阻止你。

It is perfectly natural that you should want to know more about Greyback. I only wish I had more to tell you. I am afraid I have never worked on any werewolf-related cases for the ministry - and if you want my opinion, no one has done any useful research into lycanthropy since your father - and as you know, he was quite terribly wrong about a number of things.

I do know that Greyback was a dangerous wizard before he was bitten, and is one of the cruellest men I have ever heard of - save Voldemort himself. The council that freed him against your father’s wishes believed him to be a muggle tramp - I would take this to mean that he dresses shabbily, and is a skilled manipulator.

你想了解更多关于格雷巴克的事是完全自然的。我只希望我有更多可以告诉你的。我怕我从未为魔法部处理过任何与狼人有关的案件——如果你问我的意见，自从你父亲以来，没有人对狼人症进行过任何有用的研究——而且你知道，他在许多事情上都完全错误。

我确实知道格雷巴克在被咬之前就是一个危险的巫师，他是我听说过的最残忍的人之一——除了伏地魔自己。解救他的人认为他是一个麻瓜流浪汉——我认为这意味着他穿着邋遢，是个高明的操控者。

I’m sorry I can’t give you any more than this. I want to emphasise, however that the most important thing we know about Greyback is that he is dangerous. If you have even the slightest suspicion that he knows where you are, then must contact Dumbledore immediately. Only Dumbledore can be trusted.

Best of luck with your NEWTs.

Ferox.

很抱歉我不能给你更多的消息。不过，我想强调的是，我们知道的关于格雷巴克最重要的事情是他非常危险。如果你有任何怀疑他知道你在哪里，就必须立即联系邓布利多。只有邓布利多可以被信任。

祝你的NEWTS好运。

费罗克斯

Remus read this through twice, then read the first paragraph once more, just for the thrill of it. ‘I’m incredibly proud of you, Remus’. What a wonderful thing. There was no solid information in there, of course. Nothing Remus hadn’t already considered - of course Greyback must look homeless; that was the best way to avoid drawing attention to yourself. And Remus was the very last person who needed to hear how dangerous this man was. The letter felt precious, all the same. Only the marauders had ever written to him before.
雷穆斯读了两遍这封信，然后又读了一遍第一段，只是为了感受一下。“我对你感到非常骄傲，雷穆斯。”多么美好的话语。当然，里面没有确切的信息。雷穆斯已经考虑过这些——格雷巴克一定看起来像无家可归者；这是避免引起注意的最佳方法。而雷穆斯是最后一个需要听到这个人有多危险的。他还是觉得这封信很珍贵。之前只有marauders才写信给他。

“Good afternoon dear,” Madam Pomfrey emerged from behind the screen. She had a sixth sense for knowing when he was awake.
“下午好，亲爱的，”庞弗雷夫人从屏风后面出现。她似乎有一种第六感，知道他什么时候醒来。

“Hello,” he smiled at her, Ferox’s encouraging words still in his mind.
“你好，”他对她微笑，费罗克斯的鼓励话语仍在脑海中回荡。

“You’re in a good mood,” she smiled back, “Though I don’t blame you - nearly a perfect night! You’re free to go as soon as you like.”
“你心情很好，”她也笑着回应，“虽然我不怪你——几乎是一个完美的夜晚！你可以随时离开。”

“Thanks,” He swung his legs out of bed at once, then looked up, quickly, “Er… Madam Pomfrey? Can I ask you something?”
“谢谢，”他立刻把腿从床上垂下，然后迅速抬起头，“呃……庞弗雷夫人？我能问你一个问题吗？”

“Of course, Remus,” she replied, busying herself about stripping his bed now he had left it. She did it with a sweep of her wand, it was some of the most elegant and seamless magic Remus had ever seen.
“当然可以，雷穆斯，”她回答道，忙着给他整理床铺。她用一挥魔杖的方式完成了，这些是雷穆斯见过的最优雅无缝的魔法之一。

“I’d like to learn about healing spells. Just basic stuff - I’m no good at Potions - actually, I dropped it.”
“我想学习一些治疗魔法。只是基本的东西——我对药水没什么天赋——其实，我已经放弃了。”

“Mm, I was sorry to hear that,” she replied, tidying his bedside now, “Potion making is a useful skill.”
“嗯，我很遗憾听到这个，”她回答道，现在正在整理他的床头，“药水制造是一项有用的技能。”

“Right, but I just want to be able to sort myself out after a full moon - once school finishes, you know…”
“是的，但我只想在满月之后能自己处理一下——等学校结束后，你知道的……”

Madam Pomfrey stopped what she was doing and sat on the bed to look at him. When he was a little boy, they were eye to eye when she sat down. Now she had to look up as he towered over her, and he thought for the first time what a very small woman she was. He had never forgotten the morning she had rocked him in her arms, and how safe she made him feel then. He could probably pick her up now, if he wanted to, and somehow she still gave him that same sense of security.
庞弗雷夫人停下了手中的工作，坐在床上看着他。当他还是个小孩时，她坐下来时他们是平视的。现在她不得不仰视他，因为他比她高得多，他第一次意识到她是多么小的一个女人。他从未忘记那天早晨她抱着他，让他感到多么安全。他现在可能能抱起她，如果他愿意的话，但不知怎么的，她仍然给了他同样的安全感。

“All right, Remus,” she said, after surveying him, “I teach a small selection of students the basics of healing on Tuesday evenings. You’re welcome to join, if you wish, though there isn’t a qualification in it.”
“好吧，雷穆斯，”她说，检查了他之后，“我在星期二晚上教少数学生一些治疗基础知识。如果你愿意，可以加入，不过这没有资格认证。”

“I didn’t know you did that!”
“我不知道你做这个！”

She smiled fondly, getting up again and resuming her work,
她慈爱地笑了笑，又站起身来继续工作，

“It’s to prepare students wishing to begin their training as healers once they leave Hogwarts. I can only presume that healing was not your chosen career path when you spoke with Professor McGonagall last year,”
“这是为了准备那些希望在离开霍格沃茨后开始治疗师培训的学生。我只能推测，当你去年和麦格教授谈话时，治疗并不是你选择的职业道路。”

“Oh yeah, right…” He rubbed the back of his head, slightly embarrassed. He had never thought about healing - largely because he thought it probably involved a lot of potions, but also because he was quite certain that no one would want to hire a werewolf to look after vulnerable people.
“哦，对……”他摸了摸头后部，有些尴尬。他从未考虑过治疗——主要是因为他认为这可能涉及很多药水，但也因为他相当确定没人会雇佣狼人来照顾脆弱的人。

The common room was nearly empty, it being a nice sunny autumnal day and a Hogsmeade weekend. Remus entered the dorm room quite noisily, allowing the door to slam. James sat up in bed, startled,
公共休息室几乎空无一人，因为这是一个晴朗的秋日周末，又是霍格斯米德周末。雷穆斯很大声地进入了宿舍，让门重重地关上。詹姆斯惊讶地坐起身来，

“Bloody hell!”
“天哪！”

“Oh, sorry!” Remus cringed, “I thought you’d be in Hogsmeade!”
“哦，对不起！”雷穆斯缩了缩身，“我以为你们会在霍格斯米德！”

“We were going to,” Sirius rolled over in his own bed, yawning, “But our beds looked so comfortable…”
“我们本来要去的，”西里斯在自己的床上翻了个身，打着哈欠，“但我们的床看起来太舒服了……”

“Damn, I didn’t mean to sleep that long.” James got up, stretching. “I was going to slip Rosmerta a bit of cash for the Halloween firewhisky, too.”
“该死，我不是故意睡那么久的。”詹姆斯起身，伸了个懒腰。“我还打算给罗丝梅塔一点钱，买点万圣节的火焰威士忌。”

“Don’t worry, I got Peter to do it.” Sirius replied, lying on his back, making no sign that he planned to get up at all. “Is it lunch time?”
“别担心，我让彼得去做了。”西里斯回答道，躺在床上，丝毫没有要起床的迹象。“现在是午餐时间吗？”

“Yeah,” Remus grinned, pleased to have his friends for an afternoon which he had expected to be very dull and lonely. “Shall we go down?”
“是的，”雷穆斯笑了，他很高兴能在一个他本来预计会很乏味和孤独的下午有朋友陪伴。“我们下去吧？”

“Let me shower first,” James nodded, trailing sleepily towards the bathroom. “Ugh, and I really ought to start that Defence Against the Dark Arts essay on patronuses - have either of you done it?”
“让我先洗个澡，”詹姆斯点了点头，睡意朦胧地朝浴室走去。“啊，我真的应该开始写那篇关于护法神的黑魔法防御论文了——你们两个完成了吗？”

“Drafted,” Remus said, flicking through his own pile of homework, “You can take a look if you want, but I bet you know it better than me anyway.”
“草稿完成了，”雷穆斯说，一边翻看自己的一堆作业，“如果你想看的话可以看看，但我敢打赌你了解得比我多。”

“Hardly had time for the reading,” James shouted from inside the bathroom. He never shut the door, and treated everywhere like a quidditch locker room, “With the game coming up and these prefect patrols - not that I’m complaining about those… patronuses look really cool though, I wanted to be the first one to do it.”
“几乎没时间阅读，”詹姆斯在浴室里喊道。他从不关门，把每个地方都当作魁地奇更衣室，“比赛在即，还有这些巡逻任务——虽然我不抱怨这些……护法神看起来真的很酷，我想第一个做到。”

Remus didn’t respond to this, but he thought James probably would be the first to cast a patronus. Not only because he was the best in the year at DADA, but - according to the books Remus had read so far, anyway – it looked like you needed to be able to conjure up a happy thought at extremely short notice. James seemed the most likely to be able to do this. Remus thought he could probably manage it too – but maybe not very quickly. He made a mental note to give it some further thought before the practical lesson.
雷穆斯没有回应这个，但他认为詹姆斯可能会是第一个施展护法神的人。不仅因为他在黑魔法防御课上是年级中最优秀的，而且——根据雷穆斯到目前为止阅读的书籍——看来你需要能够在极短的时间内产生一个快乐的想法。詹姆斯似乎最有可能做到这一点。雷穆斯觉得他自己也能做到——但可能不够迅速。他在心里记下了要在实际课程前多想想这个问题。

“So, we’ve sorted the booze,” Sirius was saying – loudly, so that James could hear them over the water running, “Food is easy – and it’ll be right after the feast, anyway, so no one’ll be hungry except Moony.”
“所以，我们已经搞定了酒水，”西里斯大声说——这样詹姆斯就能听到他们的声音了，“食物很简单——而且这会在宴会之后，所以除了月亮，没人会饿。”

“Up yours.” Remus said, blithely, settling onto his own bed, still trying to come up with happy thoughts.
“去你的。”雷穆斯无所谓地说，安顿到自己的床上，仍在努力想些快乐的事。

“Decorations…” Sirius continued, smiling, “Well I’ve asked Avni in Hufflepuff to do something creative with pumpkins, so we’ll see how that goes… then all we need is music. You’ll do that again, won’t you, Moony?”
“装饰……”西里斯继续说道，微笑着，“嗯，我已经请赫夫帕夫的阿夫尼做些创意的南瓜装饰，我们看看效果怎么样……然后我们只需要音乐。你还会负责这个，对吧，月亮？”

Remus shrugged,
雷穆斯耸了耸肩，

“I could, but last time everyone just put on whatever they wanted anyway.” He didn’t want to admit that he wasn’t particularly looking forward to the Halloween party. Not that he didn’t love getting off his face on firewhisky and watching James make a prat of himself on the dancefloor. But he couldn’t shake the memory of the last Gryffindor common room party, and how that had ended for him.
“我可以，但上次大家只是随便放了些音乐。”他不想承认他并不特别期待万圣节派对。不是说他不喜欢喝火焰威士忌，看到詹姆斯在舞池上出洋相。但他无法摆脱对上次格兰芬多公共休息室派对的记忆，以及那次派对的结局。

“That’s fine,” Sirius was reassuring him, “Just get them going for the first few tracks. Er… something they can dance to, this time?”
“没关系，”西里斯在安慰他，“只要让他们在前几首曲子上跳舞就行。呃……这次能跳舞的音乐？”

Remus smirked and raised an eyebrow,
雷穆斯露出一丝微笑，扬起了眉毛，

“You can dance to Pink Floyd, if you try hard enough.”
“如果你努力的话，可以跳皮ンク·弗洛伊德的音乐。”

“I know you have standards, but er… Mary’s asked if you could stick on some ABBA, maybe?” Sirius asked this with a mild wince, as if it caused him physical pain.
“我知道你有标准，但呃……玛丽问你能不能放点ABBA的音乐？”西里斯问道，带着一丝轻微的痛苦表情，好像这让他感到身体上的痛苦。

“Oh, Jesus,” Remus flopped back on his bed, dramatically, throwing an arm over his face, “Spare me.”
“哦，天哪，”雷穆斯戏剧性地倒回到床上，把一只手臂搭在脸上，“饶了我吧。”

Sirius laughed, which made even ABBA seem worth it.
西里斯笑了，这让ABBA的音乐看起来都值了。

“Shit! Mary!” James shouted from the bathroom.
“糟糕！玛丽！”詹姆斯从浴室里喊道。

Sirius frowned,
西里斯皱起了眉头，

“What?” He yelled back.
“什么？”他大声回应道。

James came running out of the bathroom, soaking wet and dripping onto the floorboards, a towel around his waist.
詹姆斯跑出浴室，浑身湿透，水滴落在地板上，腰间围着一条毛巾。

“Mary!” He said, again, “You were supposed to treat her to a day out in Hogsmeade, to make up for her birthday!”
“玛丽！”他再次说道，“你应该请她去霍格斯米德玩一天，弥补她的生日！”

“Oh, buggering fuck.” Sirius slapped his head, annoyed, “How do I keep forgetting?!”
“哦，见鬼。”西里斯拍了拍自己的脑袋，恼怒地说，“我怎么总是忘记？！”

“Not your fault, mate,” James said grabbing another towel to dry his hair, making it extra messy in the process. “You’ve been busy.”
“不是你的错，伙计，”詹姆斯说，抓起另一条毛巾擦干头发，这样头发看起来更加凌乱。“你最近很忙。”

Remus thought this was extremely charitable of James, and actually a bit of a lie, really. Sirius was the least busy of the marauders – he hardly bothered with homework, he wasn’t on the quidditch team, did nothing at all extracurricular, and was taking less subjects even than Peter. Other than detentions and a dedicated commitment to practical jokes, Mary was Sirius’s only other real concern.
雷穆斯认为詹姆斯这句话非常宽宏大量，实际上有点虚伪。西里斯是marauders中最不忙的一个——他几乎不做作业，不参加魁地奇队，不做任何课外活动，而且选修的科目甚至比彼得还少。除了惩罚和对恶作剧的专注，玛丽是西里斯唯一真正关心的事。

“Ah, well, she’ll forgive me.” Sirius sighed, “I’ll take her out next time, and really go mad on Valentines day.”
“啊，好吧，她会原谅我的。”西里斯叹了口气，“我下次会带她出去，情人节那天我会好好犒劳她的。”

“That’s months away,” Remus reminded him.
“那还要几个月呢，”雷穆斯提醒道。

Sirius shrugged. James shook his head, putting his glasses on and rooting around in his dresser for clothes,
西里斯耸了耸肩。詹姆斯摇了摇头，戴上眼镜，翻找着衣柜里的衣物，

“Your funeral, mate,” he said, “You’re going to lose that girl if you’re not careful.”
“你自找的，伙计，”他说，“你要小心，不然会失去那个女孩的。”

Remus’s heart skipped a beat.
雷穆斯的心跳漏了一拍。

 

Chapter 98: Sixth Year: Halloween

 

Tuesday 26th October 1976Boarding the Hogwarts Express in September.9月登上霍格沃茨特快车。Listening to David Bowie听大卫·鲍伊的音乐Listening to T-Rex听T-Rex的音乐Christmas at the Potters在波特家的圣诞节Winning a game of chess赢得一局棋Starting a new book开始读一本新书Finishing a book读完一本书Grant’s voice on the phone格兰特的声音在电话里A perfectly executed prank一个完美执行的恶作剧Beating Sirius at History在历史课上战胜西里斯Beating Sirius at anything在任何事上战胜西里斯Running through the forest at full pelt with Padfoot和帕德弗特全速奔跑在森林中Sirius Black’s smile西里斯·布莱克的微笑Snogging Sirius…和西里斯亲吻…“Ugh, focus!” Remus muttered angrily to himself as he stalked through the corridors towards the hospital wing. A group of first year Slytherins who happened to be walking past jumped at his outburst, then scurried away, whispering. Oh great, Remus thought, bet Snape’s already told them all about Loony Lupin. Talking to yourself will really help…

“呃，专注！”雷穆斯愤怒地自言自语着，穿过走廊向医务室走去。几名正好路过的一年级斯莱特林学生被他的怒吼吓了一跳，然后慌忙跑开，低声窃窃私语。哦，太好了，雷穆斯想，肯定斯内普已经把疯癫的雷穆斯的事告诉他们了。自言自语真的会有帮助…

He was on his way to his first study session with Madam Pomfrey and the students putting themselves forward for healer training, and using the spare time to list all of his very happiest memories. Only one memory in particular kept interrupting. If my patronus is a black dog, he told himself, I’ll have to leave Hogwarts forever and never show my face again.

他正前往第一次和庞弗雷夫人的学习课，以及那些报名参加治疗师培训的学生，并利用空闲时间列出他所有最幸福的记忆。只有一个记忆特别频繁地打断他。如果我的护法神是一只黑狗，他对自己说，我将不得不永远离开霍格沃茨，再也不露面。

“Hello, Remus! What are you doing here?”

“你好，雷穆斯！你来这里干什么？”

He had reached the hospital wing now, and found Marlene waiting outside, smiling at him, clutching a large textbook to her chest.

他现在已经到达了医务室，发现玛琳在外面等着他，微笑着抱着一本大书。

“Hiya,” He smiled back, “I’m here for the healing lessons.”

“你好，”他也笑着说，“我来这里是为了上治疗课程。”

“Oh wow! I had no idea you wanted to be a healer!” She beamed.

“哇！我不知道你想成为治疗师！”她笑容满面地说。

“Er… well yeah, I mean I was just interested… how about you?”

“呃……嗯，是的，我只是感兴趣……你呢？”

“Oh yes, it’s all I’ve ever wanted to be!” She said, proudly.

“哦，是的，这就是我一直想成为的！”她自豪地说。

Remus tried not to look too taken aback. That felt like the sort of thing he ought to know about his friends – but then, Marlene had always been a bit more private than Lily or Mary.

雷穆斯尽量不显得过于惊讶。这感觉像是他应该知道的朋友间的事情——但玛琳总是比莉莉或玛丽更为隐私。

Secretly, Remus had always felt a special fondness for Marlene. She was quiet and shy, like he was, less abrasive than Mary and less bossy than Lily. He remembered once, in a moment of confusion at the age of thirteen, having decided to fancy her. That embarrassed him now, but he had a feeling that if he told her, she’d see the humour in it. Actually, now that he thought about it, Marlene had the inherent good nature and sensible attitude that probably suited a healer.

雷穆斯暗地里一直对玛琳有一种特别的喜爱。她安静而害羞，就像他一样，比玛丽少了一些尖锐，也比莉莉少了一些指挥。他记得在十三岁时曾一时糊涂地决定喜欢她。这现在让他感到尴尬，但他觉得如果告诉她，她会看到其中的幽默。实际上，现在他想起来，玛琳有着天生的善良和明智的态度，这可能很适合做治疗师。

Besides this, during Madam Pomfrey’s lesson Marlene was clearly the stand out student. She seemed to know half the spells already, and the medi-witch approvingly told her she had a natural gift. Marlene flushed with pride at this, and Remus realised that it was the first time he’d seen her so confident. She had always seemed to unsure of herself before.

此外，在庞弗雷夫人的课程中，玛琳显然是最突出的学生。她似乎已经掌握了一半的咒语，治疗师也赞许地告诉她她有天赋。玛琳为此感到自豪，雷穆斯意识到这是他第一次看到她如此自信。她以前总是显得对自己不太确定。

“Blimey, I should just start taking lessons from you!” He said, as they left the sick bay later that evening.

“天哪，我应该开始向你学习了！”他在晚上离开病房时说道。

“Oh, shut up,” she grinned, bashfully, “You’ll be running rings around me once you’ve had the chance to catch up.”

“哦，闭嘴，”她害羞地笑了笑，“等你赶上来后，你会让我无法招架的。”

“Doubt it,” he nudged her. “Don’t want to be a professional beater, then?”

“不敢说，”他轻轻碰了碰她。“那你不想成为职业击球手吗？”

“Ha, no chance!” She laughed, “You should see the state my brother’s in, and he’s only been professional for a few years. Wouldn’t mind being the healer for the Cannons, though. Or whatever team Potter gets drafted to – then I can still see you all after school finishes.”

“哈哈，没机会！”她笑道，“你该看看我哥哥的状况，他只做了几年职业球员。不过当坎农队的治疗师我倒不介意。或者波特被选到的任何球队——那样我还能在放学后见到你们。”

“We’ll see each other anyway!” Remus said, “You can’t get rid of us that easily.”

“反正我们还是会见面的！”雷穆斯说，“你不能这么轻易地甩掉我们。”

“You’re a sweetie, Remus,” she elbowed him. “Hey, I’m really looking forward to this party – are the rumours true?!”

“你真是个好人，雷穆斯，”她肘碰了他一下。“嘿，我真的很期待这个派对——那些传闻是真的吗？！”

“Er…”

“呃……”

Halloween 1976 was due to fall on a Sunday, and due to the nature of the evening, Hogwarts students were given Monday off. This, in Sirius’s mind, could not have been more perfect.

1976年的万圣节正好在星期天，而由于晚上的特殊性质，霍格沃茨的学生们星期一休息。对于西里斯来说，这简直再完美不过了。

The marauder’s parties had grown legendary in status, and there were whispers all over the castle speculating on what exactly the four boys might have in store. There was mention of copious amounts of alcohol, potential fireworks – Remus heard one Hufflepuff who swore blind they had smuggled in a real band, instruments and all.

马拉uders的派对已经变得声名显赫，整个城堡都在窃窃私语，猜测这四个男孩到底会有什么特别的安排。有提到大量的酒精，可能的烟花——雷穆斯听到一名赫夫帕夫发誓他们偷偷带进来了一个真正的乐队，还有乐器。

“What do they think?” Laughed James, “I’m hiding them under my bed? ...er… they might be right about the fireworks, though...”

“他们以为怎么样？”詹姆斯笑道，“我把它们藏在床下？……呃……他们可能对烟花说得对……”

“James!” Remus groaned, “You’re a prefect!”

“詹姆斯！”雷穆斯抱怨道，“你是级长！”

“Exactly,” he grinned, puffing out his chest, “And I have the authority to sanction any celebrations I see fit.”

“正是如此，”他得意地笑道，挺起胸膛，“我有权批准任何我认为合适的庆祝活动。”

Remus had tentatively prodded Lily on this statement – not wanting to get James into trouble, but equally not wanting to see her humiliated, either.

雷穆斯对莉莉的这一说法小心翼翼地试探了一下——既不想让詹姆斯惹麻烦，也不想看到她受辱。

“Look, Remus, after six years I’m learning to just go with the flow as far as you lot are concerned,” she said, not looking up from her Arithmancy charts, “If Potter and Black want a party, they’ll find a way – I’m just going to brush up on extinguishing spells and make sure no one gets hurt. Besides,” - and she did look up, now - “I think everyone needs a bit of cheering up. The war, you know…”

“听着，雷穆斯，经过六年的学习，我已经学会了顺其自然，面对你们这些人，”她说道，眼睛没离开她的算命图表，“如果波特和布莱克想要派对，他们会找到办法的——我只是打算复习一下灭火咒，确保没人受伤。此外，”——她这时抬起了头——“我觉得大家都需要一些振奋。你知道的，战争……”

So that was that, then. If Lily Evans was ok with a party, Remus supposed that he would have to be as well. Besides, it was partly to celebrate Sirius’s birthday, too, which fell on the following Wednesday. And you had to be capable of superhuman cruelty to deprive Sirius Black of a birthday celebration.

所以，就这样了。如果莉莉·埃万斯同意派对，雷穆斯想，他也必须同意。而且，这部分是为了庆祝西里斯的生日，生日正好在接下来的星期三。而你得有超人的残忍才能剥夺西里斯·布莱克的生日庆祝。

This was a sore spot with Mary, who had been forgotten about twice now and was rapidly losing patience with her flighty, easily distracted boyfriend. The problem was, she seemed to think that Remus was the best person to vent to about it.

这让玛丽非常不满，她已经两次被遗忘，对她那浮躁且容易分心的男朋友失去了耐心。问题是，她似乎认为雷穆斯是最适合倾诉的人。

“I’m not an idiot,” she sighed, a few days after forgiving Sirius for his latest slight (not after having charmed all of the goblets on the Gryffindor dining table to suddenly fling their contents into his face), “I knew what he was like before we started going out, and my auntie always says ‘you can’t change a man…’”

“我不是傻瓜，”她叹了口气，在原谅西里斯最新的冒犯（不久前她施了魔咒，让格兰芬多餐桌上的所有酒杯突然把酒泼到他脸上）几天后，“我早就知道他是什么样的人，我的阿姨总是说‘你不能改变一个男人…’”

“Mm.” Remus replied, hoping this sounded caring and supportive. Evidently it did, because she carried right on talking,

“嗯。”雷穆斯回答，希望这听起来关怀和支持。显然是这样，因为她继续说下去，

“And, y’know I like the fact that he doesn’t follow the rules, and he doesn’t care what anyone thinks. I do just sort of wish he cared what I think…”

“而且，你知道，我喜欢他不遵循规则，不在乎别人怎么看。我只是有点希望他能在乎我怎么想……”

“I’m sure he does.” Remus mumbled.

“我相信他是在乎的。”雷穆斯咕哝道。

“He doesn’t show it, though… and, actually, he’s not the only good-looking boy at Hogwarts.” She said this with a wry look on her face, as a tall Ravenclaw seventh year walked past them. Roman Rotherhide – Remus had heard a lot of girls whispering about him. He had curly fair hair as long as Sirius’s, and dark brown eyes.

“不过他没有表现出来……而且，实际上，霍格沃茨里并不是只有他一个帅哥。”她带着一丝讽刺的表情说，正好一位高大的拉文克劳七年级学生从他们身边走过。罗曼·罗瑟海德——雷穆斯听到很多女孩在低声谈论他。他有着和西里斯一样长的卷发，和深棕色的眼睛。

Mary licked her lips, her own eyes following the older boy as he left the library. Remus slammed his book shut,

玛丽舔了舔嘴唇，眼睛紧随那位年长的男孩离开图书馆。雷穆斯猛地合上了书，

“Shall we go?”

“我们走吧？” 

Sunday 31st October 1976

The afternoon of the party, Remus was lying on his bed with the curtains drawn, listening to Diamond Dogs for the hundredth time, trying to avoid all of the nonsense going on downstairs. 派对的下午，雷穆斯躺在床上，拉上窗帘，听着《钻石狗》已经是第百次了，试图避开楼下发生的所有混乱。 The girls seemed to have joined forces and turned the usually comfortable, slightly worn around the edges Gryffindor common room into a cross between a jumble sale and the Boots cosmetics counter. 女孩们似乎联合起来，把通常舒适、略显磨损的格兰芬多公共休息室变成了跳蚤市场和Boots化妆品柜台的结合体。 He could practically smell the perfume from his bed, and it made his nose itch. 他几乎能从床上闻到香水的味道，这让他的鼻子发痒。

They were ‘getting ready’, Mary and Marlene had told him, though Remus couldn’t see what that meant, exactly – except that it seemed to involve a lot of mirrors, a lot of giggling, and an ungodly amount of hairspray. 她们在‘准备’，玛丽和玛琳告诉他，虽然雷穆斯不太明白这到底是什么意思——除了看起来涉及了很多镜子、很多咯咯笑声，还有大量的发胶。

James was trying out new beaters for the quidditch team, and Remus assumed Sirius was with him. 詹姆斯正在为魁地奇队挑选新的击球手，雷穆斯猜测西里斯和他在一起。 Peter was helping Dezzie ‘choose a dress’ for the party (though Remus suspected this was just a cover story; a glance at the marauders map told him that Peter Pettigrew and Desdemona Lewis were alone in the prefect’s bathroom.) 彼得正在帮德茜‘挑选一件裙子’参加派对（虽然雷穆斯怀疑这只是掩饰故事；看一眼麻瓜地图告诉他彼得·佩蒂格鲁和德斯德蒙娜·路易斯独自在级长浴室里）。

Alone and exiled from the common room, Remus had considered the library – but Christopher was there, and it looked like he was sitting close to the entrance (a novice error – you got far better light near the back by the windows), which meant that Remus would have to say hello, and Christopher would make some cold, shrugging reply, and eventually Remus was going to have to sort all of that out, but just now he wasn’t in the bloody mood, ok?! 独自一人，流放在公共休息室之外，雷穆斯考虑过图书馆——但克里斯托弗在那里，而且看起来他坐得很靠近入口（这是个新手错误——你在窗户附近的后面区域会得到更好的光线），这意味着雷穆斯必须打招呼，而克里斯托弗会给出冷漠的、耸耸肩的回应，最终雷穆斯得解决这一切，但现在他实在没心情，明白吗？！

Feeling very sorry for himself, he reclined on the bed and raised his wand, lazily levitating the record out of its sleeve and onto the needle. 感到非常自怜，他躺在床上，举起魔杖，懒洋洋地将唱片从封面上漂浮到唱针上。 He’d lugged the record player up from its usual spot on Sirius’s shelf and sat it on the end of his bed, hoping that with the bedcurtains drawn he could play it loud enough to drown out the high-pitched chatter drifting up the stairs. 他把唱片机从西里斯的架子上搬到床尾，希望窗帘拉上的情况下，能把声音放大到足以淹没从楼梯上传来的尖细聊天声。

‘In the year of the scavenger, the season of the bitch
Sashay on the boardwalk, scurry to the ditch
Just another future song for lonely little kids…’
‘在清道夫的年代，婊子的季节
在长廊上漫步，跑到沟里
只不过是为孤独的小孩准备的未来歌曲…’

“Oh, hello.” Sirius poked his head through the curtains. “哦，你好。”西里斯把头探出窗帘。 Remus sat up. 雷穆斯坐了起来。

“Hi,” he replied, uneasily, slightly embarrassed, as if he’d been caught doing something he shouldn’t be, “Did you want your record player back?” “嗨，”他回答道，略显不安，稍微尴尬，就像他被抓到做了不该做的事情一样，“你要回你的唱片机吗？”

“Nah,” Sirius waved a hand. “不，”西里斯挥了挥手。 He opened the curtains further, and much to Remus’s horror, climbed inside, crawling onto the bed. 他进一步拉开窗帘，让雷穆斯感到震惊，爬进了床上。 He settled down on his back beside Remus and listened to the record with him. 他在雷穆斯旁边躺下，仰面朝上，和他一起听唱片。

They were quiet for a long while, both staring at the red canopy above them. 他们静静地躺了一会儿，两人都盯着头顶的红色帐篷。 Remus kept telling himself that Sirius was behaving perfectly normally. 雷穆斯不停地告诉自己，西里斯的行为完全正常。 He lounged about on James’s bed all the time; it meant nothing. 他经常懒散地躺在詹姆斯的床上；这并没有什么特别的意义。

Finally, much to his relief, Sirius spoke. 终于，让他松了一口气的是，西里斯开口了。

“Broke up with Mary.” “和玛丽分手了。”

Ah. So that was all. Remus raised his eyebrows, 啊，原来如此。雷穆斯扬起眉毛，

“Really? Sorry about that, mate.” “真的？抱歉，伙计。”

He felt Sirius shrug beside him, 他感觉到西里斯在他旁边耸了耸肩，

“Nah, it’s ok. Not like I was in love with her or anything.” “不，没事。不是说我爱上了她什么的。”

“Plenty more fish in the sea.” “海里还有很多鱼。”

“Yeah,” Sirius chuckled. “是啊，”西里斯笑道。 They both fell quiet again. Bowie’s thin, sharp voice rattled between them. 他们又一次陷入沉默。鲍伊那细腻而尖锐的声音在他们之间回荡。 The first song ended and the thunderous swell of Sweet Thing began. 第一首歌结束了，接着是《甜美的事物》的雷鸣般的乐曲。 “Love this track.” Sirius commented. “喜欢这首歌。”西里斯评论道。 Remus murmured in agreement. 雷穆斯低声表示同意。

‘If you want it, boys, get it here thing,
Cuz hope, boys, is a cheap thing, cheap thing’
‘如果你们想要，男孩们，就在这里拿，
因为希望，男孩们，是廉价的东西，廉价的东西’

“We did it.” Sirius said, suddenly. “我们做过这事。”西里斯突然说道。 “Me and Mary.” “我和玛丽。”

“You did… oh. When?” “你们做过……哦。什么时候？”

“Over the summer. Once or twice since we’ve been back at Hogwarts. “在暑假期间。自从我们回到霍格沃茨以来，有一两次。”

“Right. Is that… I mean, that’s not why she dumped you?” “对。那么……我的意思是，这不是她甩了你的原因吧？”

“No!” Sirius scowled at him, “不是！”西里斯对他皱起了眉头， “Thanks for the vote of confidence, but I don’t think I was that terrible. We just broke up, that’s all.” “谢谢你的信任，但我不认为我那么糟糕。我们只是分手了，仅此而已。”

“…How was it?” “……怎么样？”

“The break up?” “分手？”

“No! …How was… It?!” “不！……怎么……回事？！”

Sirius smiled enigmatically, 西里斯神秘地笑了笑，

“Oh yeah… it was good. Great. Not like I imagined, but… yeah, good.” “哦，对……感觉很好。很棒。不是像我想的那样，但……嗯，很好。”

“Well… good, then.” “那……很好。”

“She’s really gorgeous. Mary.” “她真的很美。玛丽。”

“Yeah, she is.” “是啊，她确实很美。”

‘Then let it be; it's all I ever wanted
It's a street with a deal, and a taste
It's got claws, it's got me, it's got you…’
‘那就让它成为它吧；这是我曾经想要的一切
这是条有交易和味道的街道
它有爪子，它有我，它有你……’

“Remember when we were kids, and we were convinced Bowie was a wizard?” Sirius said. “记得我们还是孩子的时候，我们确信鲍伊是个巫师？”西里斯说道。

Remus smiled fondly at the memory, 雷穆斯怀着深情的微笑回忆道，

“Yeah, I think I still sort of believe he is.” “是啊，我觉得我现在仍然有点相信他是。”

“One day, when we all live in London, we’ll go and find him, and then we can ask.” “总有一天，当我们都住在伦敦时，我们会去找他，然后我们可以问问。”

Remus burst out laughing. 雷穆斯突然笑了出来。

“What?!” Sirius grinned back at him. “什么？！”西里斯也咧嘴笑了。

“You can’t just meet someone like Bowie!” “你不能就这样见到像鲍伊这样的人！”

“Don’t see why not. We could go to one of his gigs, or find out where he lives. Have some imagination, Lupin – once we’re of age we can do anything.” “没看出为什么不行。我们可以去他的演唱会，或者找出他住在哪里。动动脑筋，卢平——等我们成年后，我们可以做任何事。”

Rebel Rebel started up next. It was practically Sirius’ theme song by now. 《反叛者》接着开始了。现在几乎成了西里斯的主题曲。

“Anything.” Remus smirked. “You already think you can do anything.” “任何事。”雷穆斯带着狞笑说，“你已经觉得自己可以做任何事了。”

“Calling me arrogant?” Sirius narrowed his eyes, sitting up. He was smiling. “在叫我自大？”西里斯眯起眼睛坐了起来。他在笑。 Remus smiled back, 雷穆斯也笑了，

“Going to deny it?” He replied, “要否认吗？”他回答道， “Your ego is so big it has its own orbit.” “你的自尊心太大了，甚至有了自己的轨道。”

“Harsh!” “真苛刻！”

“Your ego is so big,” Remus continued, slyly, “你的自尊心太大了，”雷穆斯继续狡黠地说， “When you were doing it with Mary you probably closed your eyes and imagined yourself!” “当你和玛丽做这事的时候，你可能闭上眼睛想象着自己！”

“You wound me, Lupin!” Sirius reached for a pillow and began to beat him with it. “你伤害了我，卢平！”西里斯伸手拿起一个枕头，开始用它打雷穆斯。 Remus kneed him in the shin, rolling over to try and stop Sirius’ onslaught, but Sirius was quicker. 雷穆斯用膝盖顶了他的小腿，翻身试图阻止西里斯的攻击，但西里斯更快。 Laughing, he clambered on top of Remus, forcing him down, holding his wrists over his head. 西里斯笑着，爬到雷穆斯身上，压住他，抓住他的手腕放在头顶。 “Ha!” He cheered, triumphant. “Apologise!” “哈！”他得意地欢呼，“道歉！”

“No.” Remus cocked an eyebrow, and struggled to get free. “不。”雷穆斯挑了挑眉，挣扎着想要挣脱。 Sirius was straddling him now, and braced himself against Remus’ movements, pushing back down. 西里斯现在正骑在他身上，抵住雷穆斯的动作，继续压下去。

“You can’t escape!” Sirius said, “你逃不掉！”西里斯说道， “I’ve got you, Moony!” “我抓住你了，月亮！”

Their eyes met and everything was different. 他们的目光交汇，一切都变了。 Remus became acutely aware of the lack of space between them, every shape and angle of Sirius’ body that was touching his own. 雷穆斯敏锐地意识到他们之间几乎没有空隙，西里斯的身体每一个形状和角度都贴在他身上。 He jerked upwards, deliberately, testing, and Sirius pushed back. 他故意向上扭动，试探一下，西里斯则向回推。

Remus blinked. 雷穆斯眨了眨眼。

“Right…” He swallowed, dryly. “对……”他干涩地吞咽了一下。

“Sorry.” “对不起。”

Remus snorted and shook his head. 雷穆斯哼了一声，摇了摇头。

“’s’if I would.” “像我会那样。”

Sirius nodded, and closed the curtain behind him. 西里斯点点头，拉上了帘子。

Remus flopped back on the bed, his mind still catching up. 雷穆斯无力地倒回床上，他的思绪还在追赶着。 If he wasn’t so confused, he’d be furious. 如果他没有这么困惑，他会非常生气。

Sunday 31st October 1976

The 1976 Hogwarts Halloween feast was so terrible that Remus’s first order of business immediately afterwards was to get as drunk as humanly possible.

It wasn’t terrible in any outward kind of way, of course. The food was delicious, as usual – a glorious golden hog roast with apple crumble covered in goopy yellow custard for pudding. It was just terrible for Remus. Sirius wasn’t rude, or cold – he wasn’t even trying to avoid Remus. It was exactly his dreadful dedication to normality that made it so awful. He smiled. He laughed. “1976年霍格沃茨的万圣节晚宴糟糕得让雷穆斯在之后的第一件事就是尽可能地喝醉。

这晚宴在外表上并没有什么糟糕的地方，当然。食物一如既往地美味——一顿金黄的烤猪肉，配上苹果酥皮和粘稠的黄色奶油布丁。只是对雷穆斯来说非常糟糕。西里斯没有粗鲁，也没有冷漠——他甚至没有试图避开雷穆斯。正是他对正常的可怕执着让一切变得如此糟糕。他微笑，他大笑，他开玩笑。他毫不羞耻地称呼雷穆斯为‘月亮’。雷穆斯别无选择，只能跟随他的脚步——毕竟，他承诺过不去告诉别人。”

Mind you, he hadn’t the first clue how you would tell somebody a thing like that.

Not that she’d have been upset. Wednesday 10th November 1976

In the week that followed, Remus was completely on edge whenever Sirius was around. They weren’t ever alone together – and it was hard to tell whether or not this had been engineered by Sirius, or whether it was just a consequence of being at boarding school. Certainly, Remus made no effort to catch him alone – who knew what might happen?!

“在接下来的一周里，每当西里斯在身边时，雷穆斯总是非常紧张。他们从未单独在一起——很难说这是否是西里斯刻意安排的，还是只是在寄宿学校的结果。雷穆斯当然没有努力试图单独见到他——谁知道会发生什么呢？！”

There were plenty of explanations, of this he was certain. He just had to think about it. Perhaps Sirius was just up for it – they were both teenage boys, after all. Remus had been readily available, and hadn’t put up any resistance. Perhaps this was the sort of thing rich boys did at boarding school. Find a bit of rough to rub up against. It could even be a bit of Sirius’ canine side coming out.

“有很多解释，这一点他很确定。他只需要考虑一下。也许西里斯只是想要这样的事情——毕竟他们都是青少年男孩。雷穆斯一直随时待命，也没有反抗。也许这就是富家男孩在寄宿学校里做的事情。找一个人来摩擦。甚至可能是西里斯犬类的一面在显现。”

The worst part was that Remus didn’t actually care what the reason had been. He just wanted it to happen again. As guilty as he knew he ought to feel, he spent every night lying in his bed and wishing, wishing that Sirius would come creeping over. Or that he, Remus, had the courage to get up and go to Sirius himself. But the courage never came, and after a week (which comprised Sirius’s birthday, a Hogsmeade weekend, Bonfire Night and a full moon) Remus simply had to try and give up on it.

“最糟糕的是雷穆斯其实不在乎原因是什么。他只希望这种事情能再发生一次。尽管他知道自己应该感到内疚，但他每晚都躺在床上，祈愿西里斯能悄悄地过来。或者他，雷穆斯，有勇气起来去找西里斯。但勇气从未出现，经过一周（包括西里斯的生日、霍格斯密周末、篝火之夜和满月），雷穆斯只是不得不尝试放弃它。”

As usual when facing a crisis, Remus had composed a trusty list to help even out his thinking. This one was titled: Reasons to forget the Sirius situation.

“像往常一样，在面临危机时，雷穆斯编写了一份可靠的清单来帮助整理思路。这份清单的标题是：忘记西里斯情况的理由。”

Sirius clearly wanted to pretend it had never happened. A good friend ought to respect his wishes. A contributing factor to Remus’s messy downfall at the Halloween party had been Sirius’s dogged attempts to flirt with every girl in the room over fifteen. Extremely successful attempts. “西里斯显然想要假装这一切从未发生过。一个好朋友应该尊重他的愿望。

西里斯毫不掩饰他对女孩的深厚和持久的吸引力。所有的女孩。每一个女孩。
最后一点是最重要的。雷穆斯在万圣节派对上糟糕表现的一个因素就是西里斯执着地试图调戏房间里每一个超过十五岁的女孩。极其成功的尝试。到下一个周末时，大家都知道西里斯现在随意地和霍夫波夫的阿夫尼·乔德里交往，她曾用魔法让南瓜在黑暗中发光。”

This was a familiar situation, by now, and Remus was at least glad that he wasn’t a prefect anymore, and ran no risk of stumbling upon Sirius and Avni snogging in the Astronomy tower. He did start avoiding the greenhouses, though.

“这种情况现在已经很熟悉了，雷穆斯至少很高兴自己不再是一个级长了，不必担心会在天文塔发现西里斯和阿夫尼亲吻。不过，他确实开始避免去温室了。”

Life plodded on. Remus’s study group slowly re-banded, sidling up to him one by one in the common room, or the library, to politely enquire whether the seat next to him was taken, and then – once he had confirmed its availability – settling in and asking if he would mind just checking something for them, or giving his opinion on some point or other. Remus didn’t mind. It was a good distraction, and much healthier than getting stoned, at least. Christopher did not join in, but Remus supposed he might just be busy with his OWLs.

“生活继续推进。雷穆斯的学习小组慢慢地重新聚集，逐个走近他，或是在公共休息室，或是在图书馆，礼貌地询问旁边的座位是否有人，然后——在他确认了空位之后——就坐下来，询问他是否介意帮忙检查一些东西，或者对某个观点发表意见。雷穆斯并不介意。这是一个很好的分散注意力的方法，至少比起变得麻木要健康得多。克里斯托弗没有参与，但雷穆斯猜测他可能只是忙于自己的OWLs。”

The third full moon of the year went just as well as the previous two – James swore he’d caught sight of a unicorn, really really, this time. And the lessons with Madam Pomfrey became an unexpected delight, to the point where Remus was now competent at healing minor abrasions and bruises. No more TCP for him.

“今年的第三次满月与前两次一样顺利——詹姆斯发誓这次他真的看见了一只独角兽。而与波姆弗雷夫人的课程变成了一种意外的愉快，甚至到达了雷穆斯现在能够治疗轻微的擦伤和淤伤的程度。不再需要TCP了。”

So really, he told himself repeatedly, he, Remus John Lupin, had no reason at all to be unhappy. Everything was as it should be - even James and Lily were getting along without any hexes or curses being thrown. The emptiness was only inside him – his outer life was fuller than ever.

“所以，他反复告诉自己，他，雷穆斯·约翰·卢平，根本没有理由不快乐。一切都如它应该的那样——即便詹姆斯和莉莉也和谐相处，没有任何咒语或诅咒。空虚只存在于他内心——他的外在生活比以往任何时候都要充实。”

In light of all of this, he was quite surprised to receive a letter one quiet afternoon in the library. Actually, ‘received a letter’ might be overstating it. A paper aeroplane stabbed him in the back of his head, while he was trying to concentrate on converting an Agrippan arithmetic equation into the Chaldean form. He hissed in pain and grabbed it, glaring around. He was alone, but he knew exactly who was to blame. James’s locomotor charms were legendary. He unfolded it, smoothed it out and began to read.

“鉴于这一切，他在图书馆的一个安静的下午收到了一封信，感到相当惊讶。实际上，‘收到一封信’可能有些夸张了。一个纸飞机在他专注于将一个Agrippan算术方程转换成Chaldean形式时戳到了他的后脑勺。他痛苦地嘶了一声，抓住它，四处瞪眼。他是一个人，但他知道究竟是谁的错。詹姆斯的移动咒语非常有名。他展开信纸，抚平它，开始阅读。”

Marauders assemble! We have lain dormant too long.

Tonight. Midnight. Garden tapestry. Mischief.

“流氓们集合！我们已经沉寂太久了。

今晚。午夜。花园挂毯。恶作剧。”

He couldn’t help but smile. They hadn’t done a proper prank in ages.

“他忍不住笑了。他们已经很久没做过真正的恶作剧了。”

“Who’s that?”

The ‘garden tapestry’ was on the ground floor, only a few yards away from the entrance to the dungeons. From this, Remus had surmised that the prank would be aimed at Slytherin. He was not wrong. James had a very large wooden box with him, which he was propelling along with his patented locomotion charm.

“‘花园挂毯’在一楼，离地牢入口只有几码的距离。由此，雷穆斯推测这次恶作剧将针对斯莱特林。他没有错。詹姆斯带着一个非常大的木箱，他用他专利的移动咒语推动着它。”

“Some of the bubotubers accidentally cross-bred with some puffball mushrooms,” he whispered, as they crept down the stairs to the dungeons. “Professor Sprout asked me to chuck them on the compost heap, but I thought that would be a waste…”

Once they had reached the dingy, cave-like lower levels of the castle, Peter transformed back into himself, and James set down his crate. He lifted the lid to present a bounty of at least one hundred large, yellowish, gently pulsating mushrooms.

They quickly and efficiently began squirrelling away the weird, pimpleish fungus – behind sconces, over doorways, under carpets and inside suits of armour. They had maybe half finished with the box, when Remus’s ears pricked – he had the strange sense he was being watched. Whirling around, he spotted the glowing yellow eyes of Mrs Norris, peering around the corner with that smug, spiteful look on her squashed face.

“当他们大约完成了半箱时，雷穆斯的耳朵竖起——他有一种奇怪的感觉，像是被监视了。转过身来，他发现了诺里斯夫人的发光黄色眼睛，她那张压扁的脸上带着那种自鸣得意、恶意的表情，从角落里窥视。”

“Who’s there?” Filch’s voice barked.

“‘谁在那里？’费尔奇的声音大声吼道。”

“‘快！’詹姆斯嘶声说，然后开始朝相反的方向跑去。”

Peter, Sirius and Remus looked at each other, before telepathically deciding to duck into the nearest open doorway – which just so happened to be the girl’s loos.

“彼得、西里斯和雷穆斯互相看了一眼，然后心灵感应地决定躲进最近的一个开门——刚好是女生厕所。”

“‘那只该死的猫对我有意见，’西里斯低声说，‘自从我成为Animagus之后就这样。’”

“‘你还能说话！’彼得不耐烦地回答，搓着手。雷穆斯把箱子拖到他们身后，绝望地寻找藏匿的地方。”

Sirius was not as good at this charm as James. He always put a bit too much force behind it. It was all Remus could do to duck down and cover his head, as the crate of delicate bubotuber-puffballs slammed loudly into the bathroom door, setting off every last pustule with a sickening squelch.

“西里斯这方面的魔咒没有詹姆斯那么熟练。他总是用力过猛。雷穆斯只能趴下，捂住头，当那箱脆弱的沸水怪菌-泡球混合体猛地撞上厕所门，发出令人作呕的挤压声，激活了每一个脓疱。”

Peter disappeared completely, shrinking down to rat-size at the very last moment, and scuttling down the nearest drain for refuge. Sirius, ever-confident in his abilities, simply stood there looking stupid as gallons and gallons of pus exploded in his face, coating the entire bathroom in the process.

“彼得完全消失了，最后一刻缩小到鼠子大小，急忙钻进最近的排水沟中避难。西里斯，永远对自己的能力充满自信，站在那里显得愚蠢，成吨的脓液爆炸在他的脸上，覆盖了整个厕所。”

It was sometimes very easy not to idolise Sirius Black.

“有时候，真的很容易不去崇拜西里斯·布莱克。”
