Friday 12th November 1976

They were caught, of course – just Sirius and Remus. Peter’s quick thinking had got him out of it, and James had run fast enough in time. He wanted to tell McGonagall that the whole thing had been his idea, but Sirius wouldn’t let him.
“他们被抓住了，当然——只有西里斯和雷穆斯。彼得的迅速反应让他脱身了，詹姆斯也跑得够快。他想告诉麦格教授整个事情是他的主意，但西里斯不让他这么做。”

Their head of house gave them one of the worst dressing downs they’d had in years – made all the worse by the fact that she was clad in her tartan nightie and dressing down, which was not amusing in the slightest, but extremely terrifying. They stood in her office, heads hung, dripping pus until she dismissed them to bed. Twenty house points lost, and detention until Christmas. Ah well.
“他们的年级主任给了他们多年来最严重的训斥——更糟的是，她穿着她的格子睡衣和睡袍，这一点一点都不好笑，反而非常可怕。他们站在她的办公室里，低着头，滴着脓液，直到她把他们赶去睡觉。失去了二十个院分，直到圣诞节的拘留。唉。”

“You both have an hour free before lunch tomorrow,” she said, as a parting barb, “I expect both of you to report to the dungeons in order to clean up your mess. Without magic.”
“‘你们明天午饭前有一个小时的空闲时间，’她说，作为告别的话，‘我希望你们两个人到地牢去清理你们的烂摊子。没有魔法。’”

Sirius was furious, and after he’d washed went to bed without another word. Pete sat on the end of his own bed, looking pale faced and worried.
“西里斯非常生气，洗完后就不再说话地上床睡觉。彼得坐在自己床的边缘，脸色苍白，神情忧虑。”

“I’m really sorry!” He whispered to Remus, desperately, “I panicked, sometimes I just lose control when I’m scared…”
“‘我真的很抱歉！’他绝望地对雷穆斯低声说，‘我慌了，有时候我在害怕时会失去控制……’”

“S’ok,” Remus replied, tiredly, “It’s only detention.”
“‘没关系，’雷穆斯疲倦地回答，‘不过是拘留罢了。’”

“Anyway,” James piped up from his bed, “They didn’t find any of the puffballs we hid, yet…”
“‘不过，’詹姆斯从他的床上插话道，‘他们还没有找到我们藏起来的那些泡球蘑菇……’”

James was quite right, and in a sublime twist of fate, the bubotuber-puffballs exploded early the next morning, just as most of the Slytherin students were on their way from the dungeons to the Great Hall for breakfast. So at least the evening had not been a complete waste of time.
“詹姆斯说得对，命运的奇妙转折是，那些沸水怪菌-泡球混合体在第二天早上爆炸了，正当大多数斯莱特林的学生正从地牢去往大厅吃早餐。所以至少晚上并没有完全浪费时间。”

“It was you two?!” Lily stared at Remus, amazed, when he told her why he couldn’t meet her in the library before lunch, “Not Black and Potter, Black and you?!”
“‘是你们两个？’莉莉惊讶地盯着雷穆斯，当他告诉她为什么不能在午餐前去图书馆见她时，‘不是布莱克和波特，是布莱克和你？’”

“Don’t have to act that surprised,” he frowned, “I’m capable of being an idiot as much as anyone else is.”
“‘没必要表现得那么惊讶，’他皱眉说，‘我也能像其他人一样愚蠢的。’”

“No, but I thought you and Sirius were on the outs.”
“‘不，我以为你和西里斯不合。’”

“Why would you think that?!”
“‘你为什么会这么认为？！’”

“Oh, something Mary said, I suppose…”
“‘哦，也许是玛丽说的什么……’”

“What did Mary say?” Remus felt a flare of heat shoot up his neck – had Sirius told Mary something? Some stupid slip of the tongue while they were cosying up together?
“‘玛丽说了什么？’雷穆斯感到脖子上泛起一阵热潮——西里斯告诉玛丽什么了吗？是否在他们亲密的时候说了什么愚蠢的话？”

“I don’t know,” Lily looked mildly surprised, “Ask her, I can’t really remember, I just thought she said something about the two of you not talking. Anyway, if you could please try not to destroy any more bathrooms this year? Gryffindor’s got the lowest house points already, and it’s not even Christmas.”
“‘我不知道，’莉莉看起来有点惊讶，‘问问她，我真的记不太清楚了，我只记得她说过你们两个没有说话的事。无论如何，你能不能尽量不要再破坏厕所了？格兰芬多的院分已经最低了，连圣诞节都还没到。’”

The surprise corridor attacks had lost twenty more house points from Gryffindor, and an extra night’s detention for Remus and Sirius. James was terribly guilty, but Sirius’s sense of chivalry and honour got in the way, and he still wouldn’t let him confess.
“意外的走廊袭击让格兰芬多又丢失了二十个院分，雷穆斯和西里斯又多了一晚的拘留。詹姆斯非常内疚，但西里斯的骑士精神和荣誉感阻碍了他，他仍然不让詹姆斯坦白。”

Of course, it was a very different story later that day, when he and Remus were standing outside the cordoned off bathroom, waiting for Filch to arrive with buckets and mops.
“当然，那天晚些时候的情况完全不同，当他和雷穆斯站在被封锁的厕所外，等待费尔奇带着桶和拖把来时。”

“Bloody Wormtail, this is all his fault.”
“‘该死的小虫子，这都是他的错。’”

“No it isn’t.” Remus yawned, leaning against the wall. He hadn’t had enough sleep.
“‘不是的。’雷穆斯打了个哈欠，靠在墙上。他没睡够。”

“The little twerp ran away like the vermin he is!”
“‘那小蠢货像他那样的害虫一样逃跑了！’”

“Hey, be nice,” Remus frowned, “He only did that because someone got over excited and blew up all those mushrooms.”
“‘喂，别这么说，’雷穆斯皱眉说，‘他只是因为有人过于兴奋而炸毁了那些蘑菇才这样做的。’”

“I was thinking on my feet.” Sirius raised his chin, defiantly.
“‘我当时是急中生智。’西里斯傲慢地抬起下巴。”

“You weren’t thinking at all.”
“‘你根本没有考虑。’”

“Well you weren’t doing anything!”
“‘而你什么也没做！’”

“I was trying to hide it! If we’d hidden the box and got under the cloak, no one would have got in trouble at all!”
“‘我在试着藏起来！如果我们把箱子藏好，躲在隐形斗篷下，没有人会有麻烦的！’”

“Well you didn’t say that at the time!” Sirius snapped.
“‘但你当时没有这么说！’西里斯怒吼道。”

“You didn’t give me a chance!”
“‘你没有给我机会！’”

“He still didn’t have to run away.” Sirius folded his arms, leaning against the opposite wall.
“‘他还是不应该跑掉。’西里斯抱着手臂，靠在对面的墙上。”

Tired and grumpy, Remus spat back,
“疲倦且烦躁，雷穆斯反驳道，”

“James ran away too. Don't see you cursing his name.”
“‘詹姆斯也跑了。没见你咒骂他的名字。’”

Sirius glared at him, furiously. How dare anyone speak against James Potter in the presence of Sirius Black. Remus rolled his eyes and stared at the ceiling until Filch arrived.
“西里斯愤怒地瞪着他。西里斯·布莱克怎么会允许任何人在他面前说詹姆斯·波特的坏话。雷穆斯翻了个白眼，盯着天花板，直到费尔奇到达。”

Argus Filch was one of the most unpleasant adults Remus had ever met. Matron would have liked him. A bitter, spiteful, creeping man on the wrong side of middle age, Filch was a caretaker and a sneak, who seemed to hate students more than anyone who worked in a school really ought to. This was never more evident than when he was permitted to administer detentions.
“阿格斯·费尔奇是雷穆斯遇到的最讨厌的成年人之一。保健员会喜欢他。他是一个尖刻、怨恨、鬼鬼祟祟的中年男人，费尔奇是一个看起来比任何在学校工作的人的学生都要讨厌的看护者和小偷。在他被允许执行拘留任务时，这一点表现得尤为明显。”

He dropped two large wooden buckets at their feet with a malicious grin on his face, and pushed the door open. Overnight, the pus seemed to have dried and left a thick yellowish crust over most of the surfaces it had hit. Remus wrinkled his nose. Filch handed them both mops and scrubbing brushes.
“他脸上带着恶意的笑容，将两个大木桶扔在他们的脚下，然后推开了门。过夜后，脓液似乎已经干了，留下了厚厚的黄色结痂覆盖在大部分受影响的表面上。雷穆斯皱起了鼻子。费尔奇递给他们两个拖把和刷子。”

“I’ll be back to check on you on two hours.” He said, “You ought to be done by then. No wands and no funny business.” He sneered as he left them to it.
“‘我两个小时后回来检查你们。’他说，‘到时候你们应该完成了。没有魔杖，没有搞怪。’他冷笑着离开了他们。”

Remus looked at Sirius, who was obviously still annoyed with him. He straightened his back,
“雷穆斯看着西里斯，明显还在对他不满。他挺直了背，”

“I’ll start over there,” he nodded to the far end of the bathroom, “You go over there.” He indicated the opposite end.
“‘我从那边开始，’他点了点厕所的另一头，‘你去那边。’他指了指相反的方向。”

“Fine.” Remus shrugged, lifting his bucket and filling it at the sink. Yes, actually, that was perfect. They’d keep to their own sides and just get this stupid thing over with.
“‘好吧。’雷穆斯耸了耸肩，提起他的桶在水槽里装满水。是的，实际上，这正合适。他们各自工作，把这件愚蠢的事尽快做完。”

Sirius still wasn’t talking to him, and turned his back, working in silence. Remus followed suit. Two could play at that game. Sirius was making it much easier.
“西里斯仍然不跟他说话，背过身去，默默地工作。雷穆斯也跟着做。两人都保持沉默。西里斯让事情变得容易了许多。”

Remus would never admit it, but he didn’t mind cleaning, and actually found it quite satisfying. As disgusting as the pus looked, it came away from the white tile easily with a bit of soap and water, so the work wasn’t too physically taxing, until it came to wiping down the walls. This was harder just because of all the reaching and stretching, which tired him out and made his shoulders ache.
“雷穆斯永远不会承认，但他并不介意清洁，实际上觉得这很有满足感。尽管脓液看起来很恶心，但用一点肥皂和水就能轻易清洁白色瓷砖，所以这项工作并不太费体力，直到需要擦拭墙壁时。这更难，因为要伸手去擦，感觉很累，肩膀也酸。”

Additionally, bubotuber pus wasn’t actually pus, according to the Herbology textbook Remus had skimmed in a hurry before turning up to clean it – in that it wasn’t dirty or toxic. In fact, it had several healing properties – and while this gunk was from an accidental cross-bred strain, it probably couldn’t do any more harm than pumpkin juice.
“此外，根据雷穆斯在急忙赶去清理之前匆匆浏览的植物学教科书，沸水怪菌的脓液实际上并不是脓液——它既不脏也不毒。实际上，它具有几种治愈属性——虽然这种污垢来自意外的杂交品系，但它可能不会比南瓜汁更有害。”

The little bathroom was eerily quiet, with the two boys silently working and only the occasional sloshing sound of them filling up their buckets or swabbing the floor. Remus didn’t mind the cold atmosphere, either – it actually helped him concentrate. He had known for a long time that his feelings for Sirius rarely got in the way of his ability to be irritated by Sirius.
“这个小厕所异常安静，两个人默默地工作，只有偶尔填满桶或擦地板时的水声。雷穆斯也不介意这种冷清的气氛——实际上，它帮助他集中注意力。他早已知道他对西里斯的感情很少妨碍他对西里斯的烦躁。”

By the time the first hour was up, they had managed to remove all trace of the mess, and all that was left to do was a final rinse down. Remus rinsed his bucket a few more times, and took the opportunity to wash his hands and his face, which had grown hot from exertion. Sirius joined him at the sink, but they didn’t speak.
“到第一个小时结束时，他们已经设法清除掉了所有的痕迹，只剩下最后的冲洗。雷穆斯再冲洗了几次桶，并趁机洗了手和脸，脸因为劳动而变热了。西里斯在水槽旁加入了他，但他们没有说话。”

“Nearly finished,” Remus tried, tentatively.

“我相信麦格教授很快会和你谈谈，但我想先联系你。我一直在和阿拉斯托·穆迪谈话，他对你的安全感到担忧。他告诉我你每年圣诞节都和波特一家在一起。波特一家是优秀的人，我知道詹姆斯是你的亲密朋友，但雷穆斯，他们不能指望来保护你。他们会尽一切努力——对此我毫无疑问，但我觉得如果格雷巴克试图追踪你，唯一找不到你的地方就是霍格沃茨。”

I am not telling you what to do, of course. But I am begging you to consider your own safety and the safety of those around you.
“我并不是在告诉你该做什么。当然。但是我恳请你考虑你自己的安全和你周围人的安全。”

Best wishes,
“祝好，”

L. Ferox
“L. 费罗克斯”

Well, Ferox was quite clearly telling him what to do, even if he was just passing on instructions from Moody. Remus’s heart sank when he finished reading this letter, but there was worse to come:
“嗯，费罗克斯显然是在告诉他该怎么做，即使他只是传达穆迪的指示。雷穆斯在读完这封信后，心情沉重，但更糟糕的事情还在后面。”

Mr Lupin,
“卢平先生，”

It has come to our attention that upon your seventeenth birthday next year, you will be of legal age as defined by your society.
“我们注意到，明年你满十七岁时，你将达到社会定义的法定年龄。”

While the law of the United Kingdom states that you are still a child, we have been informed that your circumstances override this legislation.
“虽然英国法律规定你仍然是一个孩子，但我们已经被告知你的情况超越了这项立法。”

As of 10th March 1977, you will no longer be under the care of St Edmund's Boys Reformatory. Any items or financial assets held in trust for you will be returned to you no later than thirty working days following this date. There should be no need for you to return to the premises.
“自1977年3月10日起，你将不再由圣埃德蒙男孩教养院照顾。任何为你保管的物品或财务资产将在此日期后的三十个工作日内归还给你。你不必再回到该机构。”

We wish you the very best in your future endeavours.
“祝你未来一切顺利。”

Sincerely,
“此致，”

Mrs. J. Orwell.
“J. 奥威尔女士。”

Fuck. Remus read this letter only once, then shoved it down into the very bottom of his trunk. He couldn’t think about that now.
“见鬼。雷穆斯只读了一遍这封信，然后把它塞进了行李箱的最底层。他现在不能考虑这个问题。”

He told the marauders about the first letter - omitting the Greyback details, of course. He had to; there was no other way to explain why he could not come to London for Christmas. More time for homework, he told himself. He mightn’t be the only student staying; the seventh years with NEWTs coming up might stick around to take advantage of an empty common room. He could probably enjoy quite a pleasant Christmas in the library, if he wanted to. Plus a Hogwarts Christmas dinner was nothing to turn your nose up at.
“他告诉了食死徒们第一封信的内容——当然省略了关于格雷巴克的细节。他必须这样做；没有其他办法解释他为什么不能去伦敦过圣诞节。他告诉自己这将是更多的家庭作业时间。他可能不是唯一留下的学生；即将参加新魔法考试的七年级学生可能会留在学校，利用空荡荡的公共休息室。如果他愿意的话，他可能会在图书馆享受一个相当愉快的圣诞节。此外，霍格沃茨的圣诞晚餐也是不错的。”

“It’s not bloody fair.” James ranted, when he heard, “You’re no danger to anyone, the full moon isn’t until the new year!”
“‘真不公平。’詹姆斯在听到后怒道，‘你对任何人都没有危险，满月还要等到新年呢！’”

“It’s the pack thing, though,” Remus replied, loosening his tie and flopping down on the bed. It had been a very long day of lessons, and he had at least three hours of homework ahead of him. “They’re worried I’ll get captured or join up or something.”
“‘不过是狼群的事。’雷穆斯回答道，解开领带，瘫倒在床上。今天的课非常长，他还有至少三小时的作业。‘他们担心我会被抓住或者加入他们什么的。’”

“I thought Ferox liked you,” Sirius frowned, dropping his book bag carelessly in the middle of the room, “He ought to know you’d never join them.”
“‘我以为费罗克斯喜欢你呢，’西里斯皱眉道，把书包随意扔在房间中央，‘他应该知道你绝不会加入他们的。’”

“He does know,” Remus said, “But he thinks they might force me or… well, none of us really know what might happen if I met another one…”
“‘他确实知道，’雷穆斯说，‘但他觉得他们可能会强迫我或者… 嗯，我们谁也不知道如果我遇到另一个会发生什么…’”

James, Peter and Sirius exchanged an uncomfortable look. Remus pulled off his itchy school jumper, to give them a moment to think about it. When he resurfaced, his hair fizzing with static, he gave them his biggest grin,
“詹姆斯、彼得和西里斯交换了一个不舒服的眼神。雷穆斯脱下了发痒的校服毛衣，给他们一点时间考虑。当他重新出现时，头发因静电而炸毛，他给了他们一个最灿烂的笑容，”

“It’s fine, anyway, I really don’t mind. It’ll be great to have some peace and quiet; I’m looking forward to a Christmas break from you lot.”
“‘没关系，我真的不介意。能有一段安静的时光太好了；我期待着从你们这些人身上获得一段圣诞假期。’”

James chuckled, and shook his head. He grabbed his maroon quidditch duffle bag,
“詹姆斯笑了，摇了摇头。他拿起了他的深红色魁地奇球袋，”

“None of us believe you, Moony. Right, I’ve got practice, then an hour for homework, then patrolling with Evans.” Anyone else might have reeled off this list of obligations with a weary air of martyrdom. But James looked as though he was having the best day of his life. “Fancy it, Black?”
“‘我们都不相信你，月亮。对了，我有练习，然后一个小时的作业，然后是和埃文斯一起巡逻。’其他人可能会以疲惫的受害者姿态列出这些义务。但詹姆斯看起来就像度过了人生中最美好的一天。‘西里斯，想要加入吗？’”

“Nah, you’re alright, Prongs,” Sirius shook his head. He hadn’t stopped looking at Remus since he’d unbuttoned his school shirt. “You go on, I’ll get a head start on that Charms homework…”
“‘不，没事，鹿角。’西里斯摇了摇头。他自从雷穆斯解开校服上衣的扣子后就没再看他。‘你去吧，我先开始做那个变形学作业…’”

“Yeah, right,” James smirked, “Who is it tonight, Florence again? See you.” He clattered down the stairs, whistling a chirpy tune.
“‘是啊，对了，’詹姆斯冷笑道，‘今晚是弗洛伦斯吗？再见。’他哐啷一声跑下楼梯，吹着愉快的曲调。”

Sirius turned to Peter.
“西里斯转向彼得。”

“You go and watch him then, Pete, if you fancy?”
“‘那你去看看他吧，彼得，如果你愿意的话？’”

“Nah,” Peter shook his head. He looked worryingly comfortable sitting on his bed, leaning against the headboard with his Charms notes scattered before him.
“‘不，’彼得摇了摇头。他看起来坐在床上非常舒适，靠在床头板上，变形学笔记散落在面前。”

“Oh right, you’re probably seeing Dezzie?”
“‘哦，对了，你可能要见德茜？’”

“Nope,” he shook his head, licking the end of his quill nib, “She’s got patrol tonight. And she says we need to get serious about our studies now we’re NEWT students… Can I do my homework with you two?”
“‘不，’他摇了摇头，舔了舔羽毛笔的笔尖，‘她今晚有巡逻任务。她说我们现在是新魔法考试学生了，需要认真对待学习… 我可以和你们一起做作业吗？’”

Remus and Sirius looked at each other. Sirius raised an eyebrow. Remus shrugged. Sirius got up.
“雷穆斯和西里斯互相看了看。西里斯扬起了眉毛。雷穆斯耸了耸肩。西里斯站了起来。”

“I tell you what - I forgot to return that book to the library. Better go and - oh, Moony, while I’m at it, wasn’t there another book you told me I should…”
“‘我告诉你，我忘了把那本书还到图书馆。最好去还了 - 哦，月亮，趁我在这儿，你不是告诉我还有一本书我应该…’”

“Oh, right, yeah!” Remus jumped up too, struggling into a clean woollen jumper, “Er… it’s a complicated title, I’d better help you find it.”
“‘哦，对，对了！’雷穆斯也跳了起来，挣扎着穿上干净的毛衣，‘呃… 这是个复杂的标题，我最好还是帮你找一下。’”

“Oh, do you want to re-locate to the library, then?” Peter asked, finally looking up from his notes.
“‘哦，你们要搬到图书馆去吗？’彼得问道，终于从笔记中抬起头来。”

“No point,” Sirius said, as they both bolted for the door, “Won’t take long…”
“‘没必要，’西里斯说，两人都冲向门口，‘不会花太久的…’”

“Won’t take long?!” Remus muttered, on the stairs.
“‘不会花太久？’雷穆斯在楼梯上嘟囔道。”

“I had to say something!”
“‘我不得不说点什么！’”

They made it through the common room without interference, but once they were outside in the halls, they were a bit lost.
“他们顺利穿过了公共休息室，但一旦到达走廊，他们有点迷失了。”

“What about the fourth floor girl’s--” Sirius started,
“‘四楼女孩的…’西里斯开口道，”

“No.” Remus snapped.
“‘不行。’雷穆斯打断道。”

“Fine. Er… Charms classroom is free, I think? On Fridays Flitwick finishes early and there aren’t any clubs.”
“‘好吧。呃… 我想变形学教室是空的？星期五弗立维克老师早早结束，没有任何社团活动。’”

“How do you know that?!”
“‘你怎么知道的？！’”

“Oh, shut up and follow me,” Sirius smirked.
“‘哦，闭嘴，跟我来，’西里斯笑道。”

They put a basic alarm spell on the door and shoved a desk in front of it for good measure - but Friday afternoons were typically pretty safe; everyone wanted to pretend the classrooms didn’t exist.
“他们在门上施了一个基本的警报咒语，并在门前推了一个桌子以作保险——但星期五下午通常是相当安全的；大家都想假装教室不存在。”

Afterwards, they redressed, smoothed their hair and sat on Flitwick’s desk smoking.
“之后，他们重新穿好衣服，整理好头发，坐在弗立维克的桌子上抽烟。”

“We’re going to actually have to go to the library now.” Remus said, blowing a chain of rings.
“‘我们现在真的要去图书馆了。’雷穆斯说道，吹出一串烟圈。”

“Nah,” Sirius shook his head, “We’re not going there now. We’ve got an hour before dinner and no-one’s around to interrupt us. Plus, I got us some nice butterbeer.” He waved the bottle he’d brought along.
“‘不，’西里斯摇了摇头，‘我们现在不去那里。我们还有一个小时的时间吃晚饭，周围没有人打扰我们。再说了，我还带了一瓶美味的黄油啤酒。’他挥了挥他带来的瓶子。”

“Just don’t get too comfortable,” Remus warned, “I don’t want any trouble if you start getting all…”
“‘只是不要太舒服，’雷穆斯警告道，‘我不想要任何麻烦如果你开始变得…’”

“Now, now, Moony,” Sirius cut him off, “We’re here to study. What else would we be doing?”
“‘好了，月亮，’西里斯打断了他，‘我们是来学习的。我们还能干什么？’”



““We’re going to actually have to go to the library now.” Remus said, blowing a chain of rings.“‘我们现在真的要去图书馆了。’雷穆斯说道，吹出一串烟圈。”

“Nah,” Sirius shook his head, “Just say they didn’t have it in.”
“‘不，’西里斯摇了摇头，‘就说他们没有这本书。’”

“Well that would be fine, except I was actually planning to do my Charms essay this evening…”
“‘那倒没问题，只是我今晚实际上计划写变形学论文…’”

Sirius rolled his beautiful eyes and tossed his beautiful hair. Remus fought the urge to sigh.
“西里斯翻了翻他那双美丽的眼睛，甩了甩他那头美丽的头发。雷穆斯忍住了叹气的冲动。”

The classroom was the same side of the castle as the quidditch pitch. They could hear the faint but shrill sound of James’s captain whistle somewhere below them. Sirius exhaled smoke, wistfully. Remus wondered how much he missed playing quidditch. He wondered if he ought to ask, or whether that would be too much.
“教室在城堡的同一侧，与魁地奇场相对。他们可以听到下面传来的詹姆斯的队长哨声的微弱而尖锐的声音。西里斯怀着怅然的心情吐出烟雾。雷穆斯想知道他有多么想念打魁地奇。他想知道自己是否该问，或者这样是否会太多。”

“Moony, are you definitely not coming for Christmas?”
“‘月亮，你真的不会来过圣诞节吗？’”

“Yeah. I’ve got to trust Ferox. He knows me, he knew my dad.”
“‘是的。我得信任费罗克斯。他认识我，也认识我的父亲。’”

“He knew your dad? You never told us.”
“‘他认识你的父亲？你从未告诉过我们。’”

“I don’t have to tell you lot everything,” Remus gave an irritated twitch, sucking hard on his cigarette. “He worked with him, we had a few chats about it, that’s all.”
“‘我不需要告诉你们一切，’雷穆斯有些烦躁地扭了扭，猛吸着香烟。‘他和我父亲一起工作过，我们聊过几次，仅此而已。’”

“Well, if you trust him then.”
“‘好吧，如果你信任他的话。’”

“I do.” Remus was aware of his tone, but did nothing to temper it.
“‘我信任。’雷穆斯意识到自己的语气，但没有做任何缓和的举动。”

“Ok! I was just going to say…” Sirius swallowed, “Well, I mean, I could stay too. Over Christmas. At Hogwarts. If it’s ok with you.”
“‘好吧！我只是想说…’西里斯咽了咽口水，‘我可以留下来。过圣诞节。留在霍格沃茨。如果你不介意的话。’”

“Oh.” Remus frowned, caught off guard, and turned to look at Sirius. “Do you want to?”
“‘哦。’雷穆斯皱起眉头，被这个意外的提议弄得有些措手不及，转过身来看着西里斯。‘你想这样做吗？’”

“You shouldn’t be stuck all by yourself, James has his family - and Pete, if he gets really desperate.”
“‘你不应该一个人待着，詹姆斯有他的家人——还有彼得，如果他真的非常急需的话。’”

“Yeah, but won’t they expect you? James’s parents? They’re mad about you.”
“‘是啊，但他们不会期望你吗？詹姆斯的父母？他们对你非常热衷。’”

He caught Sirius’s smile at that - a brilliant flash of elation, which made Remus’s heart beat faster.
“他看到西里斯的笑容——那是一种明亮的兴奋，让雷穆斯的心跳加速。”

“They can have a Christmas as a family, for once, without me crashing in. C’mon, Moony, don’t want to share the common room with me? I’ll be quiet and let you study if that’s what you really want.”
“‘他们可以有一次家庭圣诞节，不用让我打扰。来吧，月亮，你不想和我分享公共休息室吗？如果你真的想安静地学习，我会保持安静的。’”

He gave a coy smile, and Remus stubbed out his cigarette, leaned over and kissed him, hard. He still hadn’t really got used to being able to do that.
“他露出一个害羞的笑容，雷穆斯掐灭了香烟，倾身吻了他，吻得很用力。他还没真正习惯可以这样做。”

“As if.” He said, pulling away, revelling in the warm blush in Sirius’s cheeks.
“‘才不是呢。’他一边说着，一边抽身离开，享受着西里斯脸上温暖的红晕。”

 

Chapter 102: Sixth Year: Mince Pies Wednesday 15th December 1976

“Ok, so I probably won’t have time for another one of these until next term,” Remus told his study group, glancing at the nearby grandfather clock. It was almost nine o’clock in the evening. He looked up at their eager faces, and had to look down at his papers again - it was unnerving, commanding that much attention, “But I’m here almost every night anyway, so if you just had some quick questions…”

“‘好的，所以我可能要到下学期才能再开一次这样的课，’雷穆斯对他的学习小组说，一边瞥了一眼旁边的落地钟。现在差不多是晚上九点。他抬头看着他们急切的面孔，又不得不低头看着自己的文件——要求得到这么多的关注让人不安，‘但我几乎每晚都在这儿，所以如果你们有一些快速的问题…’”

“Thanks, Lupin,” the group chorused as they began to tidy up and disband.
“‘谢谢，卢平，’大家一齐说道，开始整理和散开。”

“Happy Christmas,” he nodded, as they dispersed off to their own corners of the common room, or else to bed.
“‘圣诞快乐，’他点头说道，看到他们各自散开到公共休息室的角落里，或者去睡觉。”

He fancied an early night himself. It was the last week of term and he’d pretty much completed all of his work, unless his professors were feeling cruel enough to assign more in the last days before Christmas. He yawned, and stretched, leaning back on his chair with his eyes closed.
“他自己也想早点休息。现在是学期的最后一周，他几乎完成了所有的工作，除非他的教授在圣诞节前的最后几天里觉得很残忍，布置更多的任务。他打了个哈欠，伸展了一下，靠在椅子上，闭上了眼睛。”

“Ahem.” Someone still sitting at the table cleared their throat awkwardly. Remus opened his eyes, embarrassed, and swung forward on his chair.
“‘咳。’一个还坐在桌子旁的人尴尬地清了清喉咙。雷穆斯睁开眼睛，感到尴尬，向前倾了下椅子。”

“Oh, sorry – I thought everyone had gone.”
“‘哦，抱歉——我以为大家都走了。’”

“Sorry,” Christopher replied, clutching a book, “I just wanted to say… Merry Christmas.”
“‘对不起，’克里斯托弗回答，紧握着一本书，‘我只是想说……圣诞快乐。’”

Remus felt an awkward twist of relief and guilt in his midsection. Poor Christopher.
“雷穆斯感到一种尴尬的解脱和内疚。可怜的克里斯托弗。”

“Thanks – Merry Christmas to you, too. Big plans?”
“‘谢谢——你也圣诞快乐。有什么大计划吗？’”

The younger boy shrugged,
“年轻的男孩耸了耸肩，”

“Just family. You?”
“‘只是和家人。你呢？’”

“Staying here.”
“‘留在这里。’”

“Oh. Not by yourself?”
“‘哦。不一个人吗？’”

“Um… Sirius Black is staying too.”
“‘嗯……西里斯·布莱克也会留在这里。’”

“Of course. I heard about the stuff with his family.”
“‘当然。我听说了他和家人的事情。’”

“Mm.” Remus did not want to talk about Sirius with Christopher at all, but least of all about the Black family. Christopher was pureblood too, and likely knew more than Sirius was comfortable with.
“‘嗯。’雷穆斯完全不想和克里斯托弗谈论西里斯，尤其是不想谈论布莱克家族。克里斯托弗也是纯血统的，可能知道的比西里斯更详细。”

“Well,” Christopher made to stand, “See you in January, I s’pose.”
“‘好吧，’克里斯托弗准备站起来，‘我想一月见吧。’”

“Wait!” Remus said, quickly, reaching out but not touching him. Christopher stood up, but looked down on Remus, his eyes hopeful, Remus looked down, “I’m sorry about the way I spoke to you before the summer. I was a right git.”
“‘等一下！’雷穆斯快速地说，一边伸出手却没有触碰到他。克里斯托弗站起身，但俯视着雷穆斯，眼中带着期盼，雷穆斯低下头，‘我为我在夏天之前对你说话的方式感到抱歉。我当时真是个混蛋。’”

Christopher did not dispute this. But he smiled,
“克里斯托弗没有反驳。但他笑了，”

“That’s all right. I hope it wasn’t something I… did?”
“‘没关系。我希望不是我……做了什么事？’”

“No!” Remus shook his head, vehemently. He wished Christopher would sit down. “No, I promise, it was just me being a moody tosser. I had some other stuff going on, I shouldn’t have taken it out on you.”
“‘不是！’雷穆斯坚决地摇头。他希望克里斯托弗能坐下来。‘不，我保证，那只是我情绪不好。我有些其他事情在发生，我不应该发泄到你身上。’”

“Ok. Well... thanks for saying so.”
“‘好的。嗯……谢谢你这么说。’”

Remus smiled, feeling a bit better. Christopher bit his lip, then said, “So… do you fancy a visit to Hogsmeade in the new year? The book shop has a January sale on, or we could just get a butterbeer.”
“雷穆斯微笑着，感觉好了一些。克里斯托弗咬了咬嘴唇，然后说，‘所以……你想在新年去霍格斯梅德吗？书店有一月的折扣，或者我们可以去喝黄油啤酒。’”

“Sorry, Chris, I can’t.” Remus felt horrible, and he saw Christopher’s face fall.
“‘抱歉，克里斯，我不能去。’雷穆斯感到很糟糕，他看到克里斯托弗的脸色黯淡下来。”

“Right. You’re probably going with Potter and Black and… what’s his face.”

“...Yeah.” Ok, that was a lie, but who was it hurting?

“‘我也是，’雷穆斯耸了耸肩，卷起袖子站起身，‘我来了，伙计们！’他在楼梯上高声喊道。”

Sunday 19th December 1976

It was a bitterly cold winter that year, and snow began to fall early over the castle. The marauders used this to great effect, and James perfected a spell which enabled the suits of armour which lined most of the classroom corridors to spit snowballs from their visors at various intervals. Remus liked the cold – or maybe he just liked wrapping up warm and sitting by the fire. In the winter at least no one asked why he wore long sleeves all the time.
“那年冬天非常寒冷，雪开始早早地落在城堡上。玛拉uders们充分利用了这一点，詹姆斯完善了一种咒语，使得大多数教室走廊上的盔甲套能够从面罩中发射雪块。雷穆斯喜欢寒冷——或者说他只是喜欢裹得暖暖的，坐在火炉旁。至少在冬天，没有人会问他为什么总是穿长袖。”

And he was excited – maybe more excited than he had ever been for a Christmas holiday. He loved seeing the Potters, and he loved their house and their village, and being witness to a proper family for once. But to be alone with Sirius for an entire week; that was something he could never have imagined happening, even two months earlier.
“而且他感到兴奋——也许比他以往任何圣诞节假期都更兴奋。他喜欢见到波特一家，他喜欢他们的房子和他们的村庄，还能见证一个真正的家庭。可是能和西里斯独处整整一周；那是他两个月前甚至无法想象的事情。”

They walked James and Peter down to the edge of the grounds – as far as Remus could go.
“他们把詹姆斯和彼得送到场地的边缘——这是雷穆斯能去的最远地方。”

“You sure?” James asked, one last time, “Ferox never said you weren’t allowed, and Mum and Dad honestly wouldn’t mind at all…”
“‘你确定吗？’詹姆斯最后一次问道，‘费罗克斯从未说过你不被允许，爸爸妈妈其实完全不会介意的……’”

“Next year, hopefully,” Remus shrugged, “It might all be over by then. And I couldn’t live with myself if anything happened to your family because of me.”
“‘希望明年吧，’雷穆斯耸耸肩，‘到时候可能一切都会过去。而且如果因为我而发生了什么事，我不能苟且安慰自己。’”

“Black? You’re really going to say no to mum’s mince pies?”
“‘布莱克？你真的要拒绝妈妈做的肉馅饼吗？’”

“Ah, but I’m not, my dear Prongs,” Sirius grinned from behind his red and gold scarf, “She sent some ahead, first thing this morning. I’ve got an entire tin full.”
“‘啊，但我不会，我亲爱的角鹿，’西里斯在红金色的围巾后面咧嘴笑道，‘她今天早上最早就寄来了一些。我有一整罐呢。’”

“Foiled again,” James smirked. He hugged Sirius, and then Remus, who was surprised by it. He couldn’t remember if they’d ever hugged before.
“‘又失败了，’詹姆斯嘴角上扬。他拥抱了西里斯，然后是雷穆斯，雷穆斯对此感到惊讶。他不记得他们以前是否曾经拥抱过。”

“Go on, get on the train, eh?” Sirius punched him in the shoulder, “You’ll have Evans all to yourself…”
“‘快点，赶快上火车，’西里斯拍了拍他的肩膀，‘你可以一个人和埃文斯在一起了……’”

James winked at him, then hurried away, Pete scurrying along behind him, waving to Remus and Sirius. The two boys staying behind stood there for a little while, watching the black cloaked students trudging through the pure white snow, all talking merrily about their plans for the break, the presents they looked forward to, and their eagerness to see their families.
“詹姆斯向他眨了眨眼，然后匆忙离开，彼得在他身后急忙跑来，向雷穆斯和西里斯挥手告别。留在这里的两个男孩站了一会儿，看着穿着黑色斗篷的学生们在纯白的雪地里艰难地行走，他们愉快地谈论着假期的计划、期待的礼物和对见到家人的渴望。”

“Seeya, Remus!” Christopher grinned at him, pink cheeked as he strolled past, “Have a good one!”
“‘再见，雷穆斯！’克里斯托弗笑着对他挥手，脸颊泛红地走过，‘祝你有个愉快的假期！’”

“You too,” Remus nodded, smiling back. He felt much better, now the air had been cleared.
“‘你也是，’雷穆斯点头回应，微笑着。他感觉好多了，现在气氛已经缓解。”

“That kid again.” Sirius murmured, “Who is he?!”
“‘那小子又来了。’西里斯喃喃道，‘他是谁？’”

“I’ve told you before, he’s a fifth year. In my study group.”
“‘我以前告诉过你，他是五年级的。在我的学习小组里。’”

“Right. He looks like a complete drip.”
“‘明白了。他看起来真像个彻底的傻瓜。’”

“He’s ok.” Remus smiled to himself, hoping Sirius didn’t notice.
“‘他还不错。’雷穆斯对自己微笑，希望西里斯没有注意到。”

A nasty voice came from behind them.
“一个讨厌的声音从他们身后传来。”

“What’s wrong, Potters kick you out too?”
“‘怎么了，波特一家也把你赶出来了吗？’”

Remus reached for his wand as they turned, and half expected to see Snape. He was surprised to find that is was Regulus Black standing there in the snow, face pinched with cold.
“雷穆斯在他们转身时伸手去摸他的魔杖，半期望看到斯内普。他惊讶地发现是雷古勒斯·布莱克站在雪地里，脸因寒冷而皱起。”

“No.” Sirius replied, hotly, “I’m just staying here this year.”
“‘没有。’西里斯愤怒地回答，‘我只是今年留在这里。’”

“Why?” Regulus asked, bluntly. He narrowed his eyes at his brother, as if waiting for the punchline.
“‘为什么？’雷古勒斯直接问道。他眯着眼睛看着他的哥哥，仿佛在等待笑料。”

“None of your business, that’s why. Now run along, little Reggie, I’m sure mummy’s waiting.”
“‘这关你什么事，就是这样。现在走吧，小雷吉，我相信妈妈在等你。’”

Regulus tutted, and raised an eyebrow, as if to show that he would not rise to Sirius’s bait. Remus hated it, and clenched his fists, which Regulus either saw, or sensed, because he gave Remus a sharp look, and Remus knew he was remembering their last altercation back in January. The younger boy visibly steeled himself, then spoke directly to Remus,
“雷古勒斯咂了咂嘴，挑起了一只眉毛，仿佛表明他不会上西里斯的当。雷穆斯厌恶这样的态度，紧握着拳头，雷古勒斯要么看见了，要么感觉到了，因为他给了雷穆斯一个锐利的眼神，雷穆斯知道他记得他们去年一月的冲突。年轻的男孩明显地使劲了劲，然后直接对雷穆斯说，”

“Not a prefect any more, Loony Lupin? I wonder why? Something to do with my delinquent brother, perhaps? Surely that greasy half-blood Severus wasn’t telling the truth..?”
“‘不再是级长了，疯疯癫癫的雷穆斯？我想知道为什么？和我那个流氓兄弟有关吗？难道那个油腻的混血斯内普说的是真的……？’”

Remus might have swung for him, if he wasn’t busy stopping Sirius from doing the same. They struggled together in the snow, Sirius snarling,
“如果雷穆斯不忙于阻止西里斯做同样的事情，他可能会挥拳打他。他们在雪地里挣扎，西里斯咆哮着，”

“Take that back you brown nosing little--”
“‘收回你的话，你这个拍马屁的小家伙——’”

Fortunately, Remus was stronger. Regulus walked off, cackling, towards Hogsmeade and the train.
“幸运的是，雷穆斯更强壮。雷古勒斯离开了，发出得意的笑声，朝霍格斯米德和火车方向走去。”

“I can curse him from here.” Sirius growled, once Remus let him go.
“‘我可以从这里咒骂他。’西里斯咆哮道，一旦雷穆斯放开了他。”

“I’d rather you didn’t,” Remus replied. He turned back to the snow-capped castle, “Look,” he encouraged, “We’ve got it practically to ourselves.”
“‘我希望你不要，’雷穆斯回答道。他转身看向雪山覆盖的城堡，‘看，’他鼓励道，‘我们几乎可以完全拥有这里。’”

“Yeah,” Sirius said, distracted, still shooting glanced back at his brother’s footsteps, “C’mon then, let’s go in. Freezing my bollocks off.”
“‘是的，’西里斯分神地说道，仍然回头看着他哥哥的脚印，‘那我们进去吧。冻得我睾丸都麻了。’”

His bad mood lasted until lunch time, when they went down to the Great Hall.
“他的坏心情持续到午餐时间，他们下到大礼堂时。”

“Blimey.” Sirius said, as they entered the room. It was almost completely empty, with only three students – a Slytherin seventh year and two Ravenclaw sixth years – seated at the same table, at the head of the room.
“‘天哪。’西里斯说道，当他们进入房间时。房间几乎完全空了，只有三个学生——一个斯莱特林七年级的和两个拉文克劳六年级的——坐在房间的同一张桌子上。”

“I reckon it’s the war,” Remus whispered, as they approached the table, “Parents want their kids home this Christmas.”
“‘我想是因为战争，’雷穆斯低声说道，当他们走近桌子时，‘父母希望他们的孩子在这个圣诞节回家。’”

“Just you and me, then, Moony,” Sirius grinned, “The orphans of Gryffindor tower.”
“‘那就只有你和我了，月亮，’西里斯咧嘴笑道，‘格兰芬多塔楼的孤儿。’”

Despite the small party, the hall had been decked out in silver and gold, with glistening streamers hanging like angel hair from every rafter, a dazzling tree that seemed to glow from somewhere within its branches, and a flock of jolly red-breasted robins enchanted to circle the room and whistle familiar Christmas tunes. Remus thought that Flitwick had really outdone himself, this year.
“尽管聚会人数很少，礼堂却被装饰得金光闪闪，银色和金色的彩带像天使的发丝一样悬挂在每根椽子上，一棵耀眼的圣诞树似乎从枝条内部发出光芒，还有一群快乐的红胸知更鸟被施了魔法，围绕房间飞翔并吹奏熟悉的圣诞旋律。雷穆斯觉得弗利特维克今年真的做得很出色。”

Sirius sat beside him, rather than across from him, as usual. They didn’t make much conversation with the rest of the party; the two Ravenclaws were obsessively quizzing each other on Arithmancy, and the Slytherin was deep in conversation with Professor Slughorn.
“西里斯坐在他旁边，而不是像往常一样坐在对面。他们和其他人几乎没怎么交谈；两个拉文克劳的学生对算术占卜的问题进行着强迫性的问答，而那个斯莱特林则和斯拉赫霍恩教授深谈。”

“Remember first year?” Sirius said, as the food appeared – the house elves clearly weren’t breaking for Christmas, “It was just you and me for Christmas then, too.”
“‘记得第一年吗？’西里斯说道，当食物出现时——显然，家庭小精灵们没有放假过圣诞节，‘那时也是你和我一起过圣诞节。’”

“Yeah,” Remus smiled at his Shepherd’s Pie, warmed by the memory. He had spent every Christmas with Sirius since he was eleven. “Electric Warrior.”
“‘是的，’雷穆斯对着他的牧羊人饼微笑，温暖的回忆涌上心头。他从十一岁起，每个圣诞节都和西里斯一起度过。‘电气战士。’”

“We’ll have to have a listen, later.”
“‘我们得等会儿听听。’”

They did, too. They stretched out on the rug in front of the fireplace and lay on their backs, playing the album at full volume. Sirius played Monolith twice because he knew it was Remus’s favourite, and Remus tolerated three replays of Jeepster for Sirius’s sake.
“他们确实这样做了。他们在壁炉前的地毯上伸展身体，仰面躺着，把专辑的声音开到最大。西里斯播放了《巨石阵》两次，因为他知道这是雷穆斯最喜欢的，而雷穆斯为了西里斯的 sake，容忍了《吉普车》播放了三遍。”

You slide so good,
With bones so fair,
You’ve got the universe reclining in your hair,
Cuz you’re my babe…
“你滑得这么好，
骨骼如此美丽，
你有整个宇宙在你头发中倾斜，
因为你是我的宝贝……”

Full, warm and content, Remus quietly drifted to sleep to the sound of Marc Bolan’s pretty voice and twanging guitar. He woke up a little later, with a sore back. He turned his head and found he was alone on the carpet, and the record had stopped playing. Sitting up stiffly, Remus looked around for Sirius, who was seated a little way away, curled up in an arm chair, whispering into his compact mirror.
“饱满、温暖而满足，雷穆斯在马克·博兰悦耳的声音和吉他的声音中安静地入睡。稍后他醒来，背部有些酸痛。他转过头，发现自己独自在地毯上，而唱片已经停止播放。僵硬地坐起身，雷穆斯四处寻找西里斯，他坐在离他有点距离的扶手椅上，蜷缩着，低声对着他的便携镜子。”

Remus relaxed, leaning back on his elbows and watched gently for a while, the firelight warming Sirius’s features with a fine glow, softening his sharper angles into supple grecian marble. He was so achingly beautiful. Obviously everybody knew that, Sirius’s beauty wasn't just for Remus, but sometimes it felt like it was. It had nothing to do with wanting Sirius, then, it was something much more. It drove Remus crazy.
“雷穆斯放松下来，靠在胳膊肘上，轻轻地看了一会儿，火光给西里斯的脸庞带来了微弱的光泽，把他的棱角变成了柔软的希腊大理石。他是如此令人心痛的美丽。显然，大家都知道这一点，西里斯的美丽不仅仅是为了雷穆斯，但有时感觉它确实如此。这与想要西里斯无关，而是更多的东西。这让雷穆斯发疯。”

Eventually, Sirius whispered a goodbye to the mirror and snapped it closed. He smiled at Remus, and slowly unfurled, stretching his long limbs out over the sides of the armchair. Remus watched, unmoving,
“最终，西里斯对着镜子低声说了声再见，然后合上了它。他对雷穆斯微笑，慢慢地展开，伸展出长长的四肢，横跨在扶手椅的两侧。雷穆斯看着他，未动。”

“How’s James?”

“Fine,” Sirius replied, that look growing in his eyes that Remus had come to recognise as a signal that something wonderful about to happen. Sirius got up from the chair and sauntered over to Remus. “Misses me, obviously.”

‘‘好极了，’西里斯回答道，他眼中的那种神情越来越明显，雷穆斯已经认识到这是某件美妙的事情即将发生的信号。西里斯从椅子上站起来，悠闲地走向雷穆斯。‘显然很想我。’”

“Obviously,” Remus said, repeating without listening, just watching Sirius’s approach. He towered over him, the fire light now blazing across him like a flare, streaks of gold flickering in his pupils. He sank to his knees astride Remus’s still prone body, and bent forward - not too far; not so far that Remus didn’t have to stretch a little to close that extra space between them. He didn’t mind. It was always worth the effort.
“‘显然，’雷穆斯说道，重复着没有听进，只是看着西里斯靠近。他俯身在雷穆斯仍然平躺的身体上，火光照在他身上像闪光灯一样，金色的光芒在他的瞳孔中闪烁。他跪在雷穆斯的身上，向前弯腰——不是太远；不是让雷穆斯不能稍微伸展一下以弥补他们之间的那段额外空间。他不介意。总是值得付出努力的。”

They were used to each other now – Remus had thought it had been good in the beginning, the very first time – but after a month of secretive exploration they had developed an intimate knowledge that Remus hadn’t known you could have with another person. He felt as attuned to the various movements and reactions of Sirius’s body as he was with his own. He knew the language in every gasp, or tightening, the code in his kisses, or the shapes Sirius traced on his own scarred skin.
“他们现在已经习惯了彼此——雷穆斯曾经认为刚开始时就很好，第一次——但经过一个月的秘密探索，他们已经发展出了雷穆斯从未知道可以与另一个人拥有的亲密知识。他感受到自己对西里斯身体的各种动作和反应的敏感，就像对自己身体一样。他了解每一个喘息声或收紧的语言，了解每一个吻中的密码，或者西里斯在他自己伤疤皮肤上勾勒出的形状。”

It made the moment they parted all the more difficult, though. Sirius would be quiet at first, and Remus would just listen to his breathing, the hitch in his chest, the sighs of overwhelming calm. And he would wait for it.
“然而，这使得他们分开时的时刻更加困难。西里斯一开始会安静，雷穆斯只是听着他的呼吸，胸口的轻微起伏，令人难以抗拒的平静叹息。然后他会等待。”

The laugh, the cheeky grin, the slap on the thigh that told Remus it was over, and they were back to normal.
“笑声，调皮的笑容，大腿上的一巴掌，告诉雷穆斯一切结束了，他们回到了正常。”

“Fancy a mince pie? I’m starving!”“‘想吃个肉饼吗？我饿得不行了！’

There it was. Sirius leapt up, grabbing his jeans and wriggling into them, before waving his wand,来了。’西里斯跳起来，抓住他的牛仔裤，扭动着穿上，然后挥舞他的魔杖

“Accio biscuit tin.” the big royal blue tin came flying down the stairs and came at Sirius so hard it nearly knocked him over. “Oof.”‘‘，‘‘取出饼干盒。’那个大皇家蓝色的罐子飞下来，撞击西里斯的力度大到差点把他撞倒。‘哎哟。’”

“Your wandwork is too broad,” Remus said, buttoning his own trousers and pulling on a t-shirt. Too warm for a jumper.
“‘你的魔杖动作太宽泛了，’雷穆斯说道，一边扣好自己的裤子，一边穿上T恤。太暖和了，不需要毛衣。”

Sirius tossed him a mince pie, sitting back in the armchair, then rubbed his knee, wincing.
“西里斯扔给他一个肉饼，坐回到扶手椅上，然后揉了揉自己的膝盖，微微痛苦。”

“Carpet burn.”
“‘地毯烧伤。’”

“You should see my back.” Remus replied, as if they were discussing the weather. He settled into the sofa opposite Sirius.
“‘你该看看我的背。’雷穆斯回答道，就像他们在讨论天气一样。他坐在西里斯对面的沙发上。”

They ate their pies quietly. When he finished, Sirius licked the sticky fruit off his fingers and brushed the crumbs from his torso.
“他们安静地吃着肉饼。当他吃完后，西里斯舔掉手指上的粘性水果，刷去他躯干上的面包屑。”

“Aren’t you going to put you shirt back on?” Remus enquired, folding the tin from his pie into neat triangular portions.
“‘你不打算穿上你的衬衫吗？’雷穆斯询问道，一边把肉饼的罐子折叠成整齐的三角形。”

“Nah. No one’s here.”
“‘不。这里没人。’”

“Yeah, but still…” Remus made a fruitless gesture. Sirius smirked.
“‘是的，但仍然……’雷穆斯做了个徒劳的手势。西里斯露出了得意的笑容。”

“Prude.”
“‘伪君子。’”

Remus laughed, flicking the folded up tin at him.
“雷穆斯笑了，向他扔去折叠好的罐子。”

“Tart.”
“‘小荡妇。’”

 

Chapter 103: Sixth Year: Twelve Nights 

I sing with impertinence, shading impermanent chords with my words

I borrowed your time, and I’m sorry I called, but the thought just occurred

That we’re nobody's children at all.

After all.

 

 

Thursday 20th December 1976

Sirius sang in the shower. Remus wasn’t sure if this was a new thing, or whether he had been doing it for ages and Remus simply hadn’t noticed – he’d typically been avoiding Sirius’s showering times. Anyway, as Remus dressed, he listened and smiled. He didn’t have a bad voice, really – nothing special, but in tune. He was obsessed with The Doors at the moment, and had perfected an imitation of Jim Morrison’s deep American holler,

“C’mon, c’mon, c’mon now TOUCH ME BAAABE,” he bellowed over the hissing of the taps. It might have been endearing, even alluring, if he didn’t spoil it by singing along with the trumpets, too, “BA-DAH Ba-daah…!”

He exited the bathroom in a fog of steam, his skin flushed, his shirt damp from his hair. “What?” he cocked an eyebrow at Remus, “No applause?”
“‘怎么了？’他挑了挑眉，看着雷穆斯，‘没有掌声吗？’”

Remus rolled his eyes, opening the dorm room door,

“Hurry up, I’m starving…”
“‘快点，我饿了……’”

It felt weird to leave the isolation of Gryffindor tower, where they had already made themselves at home, and to enter the rest of the castle, where everything was the same. They were early to breakfast, and the two Ravenclaws, a girl and a boy, sat closer to them this time.
“离开格兰芬多塔楼的隔离感，进入到整个城堡，感觉有些奇怪，在那里他们已经把自己当作了家。早餐时间他们来的很早，这次两个拉文克劳的学生——一个女孩和一个男孩——坐得离他们更近了。”

“Isn’t it ridiculous that they serve this much food when there are only five students?” The girl, who had large cat-eye glasses and a mass of freckles, remarked, “It seems so wasteful…”
“‘他们只招待五个学生，却提供这么多食物，不觉得很荒唐吗？’那女孩有着大大的猫眼眼镜和一脸的雀斑，她评论道，‘这似乎太浪费了……’”

The plates in front of them had filled with fried eggs, bacon, sausages, black pudding, baked beans, fried tomatoes and toast – not to mention cereal, porridge and fruit juices.
“他们面前的盘子里满是煎蛋、培根、香肠、黑布丁、烤豆、煎番茄和吐司——更别提还有麦片、粥和果汁了。”

“Nah,” Sirius replied, watching Remus pile up his plate, “You’ve clearly never seen Moony here eat.”
“‘不，’西里斯回答道，看着雷穆斯把盘子堆得越来越高，‘你显然从未见过月亮在这里吃东西。’”

“Shut up.” Remus replied, his mouth already full.
“‘闭嘴。’雷穆斯回答道，嘴里已经满满的。”

Still, the Ravenclaws watched, fascinated, until Remus was too embarrassed to eat any more. Fortunately, at that moment a distraction arrived in the form of the morning post owls. One landed in front of Remus. Three in front of Sirius.
“尽管如此，那两个拉文克劳的学生还是看得入迷，直到雷穆斯感到太尴尬而不再继续吃东西。幸运的是，此时早晨的邮递猫头鹰们带来了打扰。一只落在雷穆斯面前。三只在西里斯面前。”

“You’re popular.” The Ravenclaw boy leaned over. He was skinny and smallish, with a beaky nose.
“‘你真受欢迎。’拉文克劳的男孩靠过来。他瘦小，鼻子尖尖的。”

“Don’t encourage him.” Remus said. His own package was soft, and wrapped in lavender coloured paper. It was from Lily, he had no doubt. Sirius had five or six brightly coloured envelopes – none red, Remus noted with relief. No howlers from Walpurga this year.
“‘别鼓励他。’雷穆斯说。他的包裹很软，包裹在淡紫色的纸中。他毫无疑问这是莉莉的。西里斯有五六封鲜艳的信封——没有红色的，雷穆斯松了口气。今年没有沃尔普加的叫骂信。”

“We’re going ice skating before lunch,” the Ravenclaw girl smiled, brightly, “The lake’s frozen over. Want to come?”
“‘我们午饭前去滑冰，’拉文克劳的女孩明亮地笑道，‘湖面都冻上了。想来吗？’”

“Sounds good,” Sirius nodded, tossing his unopened post aside. Remus collected it up before they left the breakfast table, and took it up to the room with them.
“‘听起来不错，’西里斯点头道，把未拆开的信件丢到一边。雷穆斯在他们离开早餐桌前把它们收起来，带到房间里。”

“Are these all Christmas cards?!” He asked, flicking through.
“‘这些全是圣诞贺卡吗？’他问道，一边翻看着。”

“Oh, yeah, I think so.” Sirius shrugged, opening his wardrobe and rummaging through the bottom, pulling out drawers and old shoes he didn’t wear any more.
“‘哦，是的，我想是的。’西里斯耸耸肩，打开衣橱，翻找着底部，拿出抽屉和不再穿的旧鞋子。”

“Who are they from?”
“‘这些是谁寄来的？’”

“Whoever.”
“‘谁知道呢。’”

Remus frowned, then caught sight of something on Sirius’s bedside table. Another pile of unopened cards. He started opening them. Sirius clearly wasn’t interested.
“雷穆斯皱了皱眉，然后看到了西里斯床头柜上的另一堆未拆开的贺卡。他开始拆开它们。西里斯显然不感兴趣。”

‘Dear Sirius, have a wonderful Christmas, lots of kisses, Imelda.’
“‘亲爱的西里斯，祝你圣诞快乐，亲吻很多，伊梅尔达。’”

Hm.
“嗯。”

‘To the boy who holds my heart, merry Christmas and all my love, S.’
“‘给那个拥有我心的男孩，圣诞快乐，所有的爱，S。’”

…

‘Darling Sirius, please meet me in Hogsmeade under the mistletoe for a kiss… and maybe more? Emmeline.’
“‘亲爱的西里斯，请在霍格斯梅德的槲寄生下与我见面，亲吻一下……也许还有更多？艾梅琳’”

‘My raven haired prince, I cannot rest until I am in your arms…’
“‘我的乌发王子，直到我在你怀里我无法安宁……’”

“Sirius.”
“‘西里斯。’”

“What?” Came his muffled response. He was half buried in the back of his wardrobe now, on his hands and knees.
“‘什么？’他的声音从衣橱的后面传来。他现在正趴在地上，半埋在衣柜里。”

“These are all from girls…”
“‘这些全是女生寄来的……’”

“Aha!” He finally reappeared, leaning back on his ankles, holding a pair of ice skates aloft, “I knew I brought a pair during first year.”
“‘啊哈！’他终于露面了，倚靠在脚踝上，举着一双冰鞋，‘我知道我在第一年时带了一双。’”

“Are you telling me your feet haven’t grown since you were eleven?”
“‘你是在告诉我你的脚自十一岁以来没有长大吗？’”

“They have a growing charm on them,” Sirius explained, dusting them off, “They get bigger to fit me. Only the best for the Blacks!”
“‘它们有个成长魔咒，’西里斯解释道，一边擦去灰尘，‘它们会随着我的脚长大。只给布莱克家族最好的！’”

“Clever. These cards, though…”
“‘聪明。不过，这些贺卡……’”

“Oh, those? What’d you open them for? You want to be careful. One of them squirted perfume at me. Perfume.” He pulled a face.
“‘哦，那些？你为什么拆开它们？要小心。有一张向我喷了香水。香水。’他做了个鬼脸。”

“Are these all girls you’ve…?”
“‘这些都是你……’”

“Really, Moony, I’m flattered. As legendary as I’m sure my stamina is, no. They’re just girls. They send me nonsense all the time.”
“‘真的，月亮，我很受宠若惊。虽然我相信我的耐力很传奇，但不是的。她们只是女生。她们总是给我发些废话。’”

“All the time?”
“‘总是吗？’”

“Oh c’mon, what are you, jealous?” Sirius ruffled Remus’s hair, “They’re just cards.”
“‘哦，得了吧，你是吃醋了吗？’西里斯搔了搔雷穆斯的头发，‘他们只是贺卡。’”

“I suppose…”
“‘我想……’”

“Now, let’s get you some skates…”
“‘好了，咱们去找双冰鞋……’”

“I don’t want any, I’ll break my neck.”
“‘我不想要，我会摔断脖子的。’”

“You’ll be fine, I’ll show you how to do it.”
“‘你会没事的，我会教你怎么滑。’”

Remus picked up the pile again and flicked through it.
“雷穆斯再次拿起那堆卡片，翻看起来。”

“There must be twenty here, altogether…”
“‘这些加起来肯定有二十张……’”

“Look, Remus, why don’t we find you a girlfriend, then you won’t be so interested in my love life.”
“‘看，雷穆斯，为什么不找个女朋友呢，这样你就不会那么关心我的感情生活了。’”

“What?!” Remus stared at Sirius. He was being quite genuine, a look of mild concern on his face. Remus’s heart sank. Really?
“‘什么？！’雷穆斯盯着西里斯。他显得很真诚，脸上有一丝轻微的担忧。雷穆斯的心一下子沉了下来。真的？”

“Yeah, I reckon that freckly Ravenclaw likes you. Or Marlene! What about Marlene? She’s pretty, nice. Likes you.”
“‘是的，我觉得那个雀斑拉文克劳喜欢你。或者玛琳！玛琳怎么样？她很漂亮，很友善。喜欢你。’”

“She offered to snog me once,” Remus said, but shook his head, “It was a joke though – Marlene’s not interested in me. I don’t need a girlfriend.”
“‘她曾经主动吻我一次，’雷穆斯说，但摇了摇头，‘不过那是开玩笑——玛琳对我没有兴趣。我不需要女朋友。’”

“Don’t knock it ‘til you’ve tried it,” Sirius winked, “Right, let’s see what we can do about these skates…”
“‘没试过就别说不好，’西里斯眨眼道，‘好了，看看我们怎么处理这些冰鞋……’”

Ice-skating was marginally better than flying a broom, but not much. The lake was completely frozen, but Remus couldn’t shake the thought it might crack at any moment, and kept patting his pocket to check he could reach his wand. Sirius, obviously, was a natural. So was the Ravenclaw boy – Arnold – and the pair of them were soon racing each other up and down the length of the ice. Remus watched them, nervously, trying not to wobble.
“滑冰比骑扫帚稍微好一点，但也没好多少。湖面完全冻结，但雷穆斯无法摆脱它随时可能裂开的想法，不断拍打自己的口袋，确保能拿到魔杖。显然，西里斯天生就擅长滑冰。拉文克劳的那个男孩——阿诺德——也一样，他们俩很快就在冰面上相互竞速。雷穆斯紧张地看着他们，尽量不让自己摇晃。”

“Here,” the freckly girl – Tina – glided over to him, smiling kindly, “Put your hands on my shoulders if you want, and watch my feet,”
“‘在这，’那个有雀斑的女孩——蒂娜——滑到他身边，亲切地笑道，‘如果你愿意的话，把手放在我的肩膀上，看着我的脚。’”

He did so, gratefully, standing behind her as she dragged him steadily around in a small circle. He thought he was getting the hang of it.
“他感激地照做了，站在她身后，她稳稳地将他拖动在一个小圈子里。他觉得自己开始掌握了要领。”

“I wonder if the squid’s ok…” he said, after they’d been a bit too quiet for a while.
“‘我在想那个章鱼还好吗……’他说道，过了一会儿他们变得有点太安静了。”

“Ugh, I never even thought about that. Does it hibernate, do you think?” Tina peered down at the ice with some interest, “I don’t think I’ve actually ever read anything about the squid.”
“‘呃，我从没想过这个。你觉得它会冬眠吗？’蒂娜好奇地低头看着冰面，‘我好像从来没读过关于那个章鱼的任何东西。’”

“Me neither.” Remus replied, letting go of her shoulders and attempting to do a few meters unaided. “Professor Ferox liked it, though, I saw him feeding it once.”
“‘我也没有。’雷穆斯回答道，放开她的肩膀，试图自己滑几米。‘不过费罗教授喜欢它，我曾见过他喂它一次。’”

“Really?” She looked up at him, earnest and curious, “What did he feed it?”
“‘真的？’她抬头看着他，真诚而好奇，‘他喂它了什么？’”

Remus shrugged,
“雷穆斯耸了耸肩，”

“No idea. Something nasty looking.”
“‘不知道。看起来很恶心的东西。’”

“I miss Ferox,” she sighed, “He really brought his lessons to life. I ended up dropping Care of Magical Creatures. Taking an extra course in Goblin Finance, instead.”
“‘我想念费罗教授，’她叹息道，‘他真的让课程变得生动。我最后选择了放弃神奇生物护理，改修了一门额外的课程——高傲金融。’”

“Oh, that sounds… er… interesting.”
“‘哦，那听起来……呃……有趣。’”

“It is,” she nodded, without a trace of irony, “I can lend you a book, if you like?”
“‘确实有趣，’她点头道，没有一点讽刺的痕迹，‘如果你愿意的话，我可以借给你一本书？’”

“Er… thanks…”
“‘呃……谢谢……’”

After lunch, Remus and Sirius returned to the tower. Remus noticed that the pile of cards had disappeared, but he didn’t mention it. He lit the small bedroom fire and looked for a thicker jumper to wear,
“午饭后，雷穆斯和西里斯返回了塔楼。雷穆斯注意到那堆贺卡已经消失了，但他没有提及。他点燃了小卧室的火炉，找了一件厚一点的毛衣穿上，”

“Still cold?” Sirius asked, yawning.
“‘还冷吗？’西里斯问道，打了个哈欠。”

“Freezing.” Remus replied, pulling on a second pair of socks and raising his hands to the fire.
“‘冻得很。’雷穆斯回答道，一边穿上第二双袜子，一边将手伸向火炉。”

“Should have moved about a bit more, gets the blood pumping. Still,” his tone changed; turned sly and teasing, “You had a nice chat with freckles?”
“‘应该多活动活动，这样能让血液流动。话说回来，’他的语气变了，变得狡黠和戏弄，‘你和雀斑聊得不错吗？’”

“Tina. She’s interested in Goblin Finance.”
“‘蒂娜。她对高傲金融感兴趣。’”

“Excellent, you can marry rich.”
“‘太好了，你可以嫁得好。’”

Remus threw a slipper at him.
“雷穆斯扔了个拖鞋向他。”

“Oi!” Sirius barked with laughter, “I’m just trying to help you get out a bit, Moony, you ought to have other interests outside of that bloody study group.”
“‘哎！’西里斯笑着叫道，‘我只是想帮你多出去一下，月亮，你应该有其他的兴趣，而不仅仅是那个该死的学习小组。’”

“I think, if anything, I would be doing more studying if I started going out with Tina. Which I’m not going to.” Remus blew into his cupped hands, then held them up to the fire again. The cold just seemed to seep in and settle there.
“‘我觉得，如果真的这样的话，我会更专注于学习，而不是和蒂娜约会。我是不打算的。’雷穆斯对着双手吹气，然后再次伸手向火炉。寒冷似乎渗透进来，停留在那里。”

He turned to look at Sirius, who was leaning against his headboard, staring. His lips curled into a wicked smile.
“他转过身看着西里斯，西里斯靠在床头板上盯着他看。他的嘴角露出一个邪魅的笑容。”

“Bed’s warm…”
“‘床很暖和……’”

 

 

Friday 21st December 1976

“Bloody Regulus.”
“該死的雷古勒斯。”

“It was two days ago, get over it.”
“那是兩天前的事了，別再糾結了。”

“He’s such a prick.”
“他真是個混蛋。”

“I know. Left a bit!”
“我知道。稍微往左一點！”

“I can’t go any further left, there’s no room.”
“我不能再往左移了，沒地方了。”

“Careful! Not there…”
“小心！不是那裡…”

“Oops. Anyway, you should have let me hit him.”
“哎呀。不管了，你應該讓我打他一拳。”

“You weren’t going to hit him, you were going to break a knuckle. You can’t punch.”
“你根本不會打他，你只是要打斷你的指關節。你不能打架。”

“Yes I can!”
“我可以！”

“No, you can’t. Look, can you please concentrate? You keep missing.”
“不，你不行。看，你能不能專心點？你總是打不中。”

“I’ve punched loads of people – oops, sorry…”
“我打過很多人——哦，對不起……”

“You’ve play-fought with James. Not the same thing.”
“你和詹姆斯打過玩鬧，不一樣的。”

“Oh, and you know how to punch, do you Moony?”
“哦，你知道怎麼打拳，對嗎，月亮？”

“Yeah, I do, actually – aha, I win!”
“嗯，其實我知道——哈哈，我贏了！”

“It’s not fair. Can’t we get closer?”
“這不公平。我們不能靠近一點嗎？”

“No, that’s cheating.”
“不，那是作弊。”

“Oh fine, I forgot you were a stickler for rules, Prefect Lupin…”
“哦，算了，我忘了你是個死板的規則控，盧平長官……”

Remus folded his arms and let Sirius rant. He had won fair and square. They’d been playing this new game for about two hours now, and Remus was by far the best at it. He had never beaten Sirius at anything on the first go. It was an excellent feeling, and he was going to lord it over him.
雷木斯抱著手臂，讓小天狼星發牢騷。他贏得光明正大。他們已經玩這個新遊戲大約兩個小時了，而雷木斯顯然是最厲害的。他從未在第一次嘗試中擊敗過小天狼星。這種感覺非常棒，他打算好好炫耀一番。

The game involved levitating various items they’d found in the common room – gobstones, chocolate frogs, quills, slippers – and firing them at speed through the ‘goals’, constructed by cutting various sized holes in Peter and James’s bedsheets, which they had strung up across the common room, dividing it. (Remus had had reservations about cutting up his friend’s sheets out of boredom. But Sirius had reasoned that they couldn’t very well cut holes in their own bedsheets, which were in use.)
這個遊戲涉及到將他們在公共休息室找到的各種物品——如魔法石、巧克力青蛙、羽毛筆、拖鞋——懸浮起來，並以高速射穿‘目標’，這些目標是通過在彼得和詹姆斯的床單上剪開各種大小的洞來構建的，他們把床單掛在公共休息室裡，分隔開來。（雷木斯對於無聊而剪壞朋友的床單有些保留。但小天狼星認為，他們不可能在自己正在使用的床單上剪洞。）

The best part was that they never had to tidy up. Once they had got everything through the goals, all they needed to do was walk through the sheets and start again on the other side. This they began to do now, crossing to the half of the room with the fireplace in it. It was cosy.
最棒的部分是他們不必打掃。當他們把所有東西都通過目標後，他們只需要穿過床單，再從另一邊開始。現在他們開始這麼做，走向房間有壁爐的一半。那裡很溫暖舒適。

“I wonder if this is what camping is like,” Remus said, thoughtfully.
“我在想這是否就是露營的感覺，”雷木斯沉思地說。

“Never been.” Sirius replied. “James thought it was funny our family never did it.”
“從未去過。”小天狼星回答，“詹姆斯覺得我們家從來沒有露營很有趣。”

“I always wanted to.” Remus mused, beginning to levitate a crystal ball someone had carelessly let roll under the couch. “But I liked the idea of anywhere that wasn’t St. Edmund’s.”
“我一直想去。”雷木斯思索道，開始懸浮一個有人隨意滾到沙發下的水晶球。“但我喜歡任何不是聖埃德蒙德斯的地方。”

He frowned, slightly, having surprised himself. Why had he brought up St. Edmund's? He never talked about it in front of anyone at Hogwarts. Sirius didn’t seem fazed.
他稍微皺起眉頭，感到有些驚訝。為什麼他提起了聖埃德蒙德斯？他從未在霍格華茲的人面前談論過它。小天狼星似乎並不在意。

“Yeah, I don’t blame you.” He said, then, glancing at the floating crystal ball, “You’re going to smash that.”
“是啊，我不怪你。”他說道，然後瞥了一眼懸浮的水晶球，“你會把它弄碎的。”

“No I’m not, I'm aiming at the big settee.” Remus demonstrated, reeling back his wand and then flicking it, sending the crystal ball whizzing through the very smallest hole, landing with a quiet ‘thump’ on the other side. Remus smirked at Sirius, who, shook his head in disbelief.
“不，我不會，我瞄準的是那個大沙發。”雷木斯展示道，他將魔杖收回，然後輕輕一揮，讓水晶球穿過最小的洞，靜靜地落在另一邊。雷木斯對小天狼星露出得意的笑容，小天狼星則難以置信地搖頭。

“It’s scary how good at this you are. Get you on a broom and you’d make a bloody good chaser.”
“你在這方面的表現真是太驚人了。讓你騎上飛天掃帚，你會成為一個了不起的追球手。”

“No, thanks. Your go.”
“不用了。輪到你了。”

Sirius selected a gobstone. They were easier to levitate, but much harder to aim. He was terrible at understanding his own limits.
小天狼星選了一顆魔法石。它們更容易懸浮，但瞄準起來難度更大。他很難了解自己的極限。

“Did you play that muggle game, at St Edmund’s?” Sirius asked, casually, firing the gobstone too hard and missing the sheet altogether, sending it over the top.
“你在聖埃德蒙德斯時玩過那個麻瓜遊戲嗎？”小天狼星隨意地問，結果將魔法石射得太用力，完全錯過了床單，飛過了上面。

“Foul.” Remus said, “What muggle game?”
“犯規。”雷木斯說，“什麼麻瓜遊戲？”

“With all the running about and kicking. We saw them playing it when we… er, over the summer.”
“那些跑來跑去和踢球的。我們在……呃，暑假時看到他們玩。”

“Oh. Football. No, I never liked it. Had too many bruises already.”
“哦，足球。不，我從來不喜歡它。已經有太多瘀傷了。”

“Yeah, sorry, I didn’t think. Of course.” Sirius went a bit quiet after that. Remus knew him well enough to recognise that he was building up to something - a question, or a declaration. In the meantime, Remus started shooting quills like darts through each hole in the sheets. Finally, Sirius had gathered up whatever courage he needed, or prepared whichever words. “Is it really awful, living there?”
“是啊，對不起，我沒想到。當然。”小天狼星在那之後變得有些安靜。雷木斯對他了解得夠多，能夠認出他在為某事做準備——一個問題，或一個宣告。與此同時，雷木斯開始像射飛鏢一樣射羽毛筆穿過每個床單上的洞。最後，小天狼星鼓起了所需的勇氣，或準備了那些話。“那裡生活真的很糟糕嗎？”

Remus lowered his wand. He hadn’t ever complained about St Edmund’s - not in front of the marauders, or anyone, except for Grant, because Grant knew. He was about to say ‘Nah, it’s fine, really’, and shrug it off - but something stopped him. That was a lie, and there was no need to lie, just now.
雷木斯猶豫了一下，就像每次討論聖埃德蒙德斯時一樣。他從未明白為什麼人們覺得打探這種事是可以的。對他來說似乎是如此私人的事情。但他試圖誠實地回答。

“It’s… not awful, but it is… noisy. You always have to watch your back, and no one really cares about you, much. They have to make sure you don’t die, or get arrested, or starve or whatever, but they don’t actually care.”
“那裡……不是糟糕，但的確……很吵。你總是要提防，沒有人真的關心你。他們要確保你不會死掉，不會被逮捕，不會餓死什麼的，但他們實際上不在乎。”

He wasn’t in the mood to play any more. he reached into his back pocket and pulled out his cigarettes, lighting one with his wand tip, then tossing the box to Sirius. Sirius just held it, running his thumb over a loose bit of foil poking out from the join in the hinge.

“I know how that feels,” he murmured. That was all he said, and it was enough, at the time. He quickly looked up and grinned, “Look what I can do!”
“我知道那種感覺。”他低聲說道。這就是他當時要說的全部。他迅速抬起頭，笑道：“看看我能做什麼！”

He slid a cigarette out of the packer and placed it between his lips. A look of concentration flashed in his eyes for a moment, then he snapped his fingers, and the cigarette lit itself. His grin widened around the fag, and he looked at Remus for praise.

“Blimey,” Remus smiled, “Clever you.”
“哇，”雷穆斯微笑道，“你真聰明。”

 

Saturday 22nd December 1976

“What are you doing?”

“What’s it look like?” Remus replied sternly, over the top of his textbook. He’d spent a peaceful few hours all by himself in bed, until Sirius had marched in smelling of snow and hot chocolate. He’d gone ice skating again, and Remus had begged off this time, looking for some quiet.

“你在做什麼？”

“你看起來像在讀書。”雷木斯嚴厲地回答道，翻過書本的上面。他在床上獨自度過了幾個平靜的時光，直到小天狼星進來，身上帶著雪和熱巧克力的味道。他又去滑冰了，而雷木斯這次請假，想找些安靜的時光。

“You’re not studying at Christmas?!” Sirius flopped down beside him on the bed, looking scandalised.

“你在聖誕節不學習嗎？！”小天狼星在床邊一屁股坐下，表情驚訝。

“It’s not Christmas, it’s not even Christmas eve, it’s just a normal day. And I like reading, thank you very much.” Remus shifted away from him, rolling back and raising the book over his head to read.

“這不是聖誕節，甚至不是聖誕前夕，只是一個普通的日子。我喜歡閱讀，謝謝你。”雷木斯挪開了位置，翻回來，把書本高舉過頭來閱讀。

“How times have changed, eh Moony?” Sirius chortled, pulling off his socks and thick woollen jumper.

“時光如何變遷，嗯，月亮？”小天狼星咯咯笑著，脫下他的襪子和厚毛衣。

It was one the Potters had bought him - this year Sirius’s clothes had been much more practical and comfortable than before - hardly anything specially tailored or finely cut now. He was still very obviously an aristocrat, born and bred - that was clear in his bearing, in every enunciated phrase he spoke. But he was happier, and that showed just as much. “I remember a boy who hated reading, and homework, and--”

這是波特家族買給他的——今年小天狼星的衣服比以前實用多了，舒適多了——幾乎沒有什麼特別訂製或精緻裁剪的衣物。他仍然非常明顯是個貴族，從他的舉止、他所說的每一句話都可以看出。但他更幸福了，這也同樣明顯。“我記得有個小男孩討厭閱讀，討厭作業，還有——”

“Mm, and I remember someone who loved it, and came top in every subject…” Remus turned to him, finally. “What happened, didn’t like the competition?”

“嗯，我記得有個人喜歡這些，並且在每一門科目中名列前茅……”雷木斯終於轉向他。“怎麼了，不喜歡競爭了嗎？”

“Pfft. I could run rings around the lot of you, if I wanted to.” This wasn’t a boast. Sirius had always been exceptional when it came to intuitive magic, and intensely diligent at research - when it suited him.

“噗。我可以在你們所有人面前跑來跑去，如果我想的話。”這不是自誇。小天狼星在直覺魔法方面一直非常出色，而且在研究方面非常勤奮——當它適合他的時候。

“So why don’t you?”

“那為什麼不呢？”

“Rather do other stuff,” he shrugged.

“寧願做其他事情。”他聳了聳肩。

The conversation had hit a dead end - that hardly ever happened with Sirius, unless you brought up his family. And this certainly had something to do with the Blacks - or at least Sirius thought it did. They wanted him to be in Slytherin, so he ended up in Gryffindor. They wanted him to be a good pureblood heir, so he befriended the Potters and ran away. They wanted him to get the best marks in his exams to prove that purebloods were better than anyone else - so he used his talents exclusively in ways that would annoy them.

談話陷入了僵局——這種情況幾乎從未發生在小天狼星身上，除非你提到他的家人。這肯定與布萊克家族有關——至少小天狼星這麼認為。他們希望他進入斯萊特林，所以他最終進入了格蘭芬多。他們希望他成為一個好的純血繼承人，所以他結交了波特家族並逃跑了。他們希望他在考試中獲得最佳成績，以證明純血比其他人更優越——所以他將他的才華專門用於令他們不悅的方式。

Remus returned to his book. Two lines down, Sirius gave a long sigh.

雷木斯回到了他的書本上。兩行下，小天狼星長嘆了一口氣。

“I’m bored.”

“我無聊。”

“Go and play chess with the dynamic duo.” Remus replied, re-reading the second line.

“去和那對活力四射的雙胞胎下棋吧。”雷木斯回應道，再次閱讀第二行。

“Ugh, not that bored. Spent all morning with them. They’re ok, but merlin, everything’s so literal.”

“呃，沒那麼無聊。我和他們一起度過了整個早晨。他們還好，但天啊，一切都這麼字面。”

“Talk to James then.”

“那就找詹姆斯聊聊。”

“He’s got family visiting, or something. We’re talking after dinner. Anyway, not in the mood for talking.”

“他有家人來訪，還是什麼的。我們晚餐後再聊。無論如何，我不想聊天。”

Remus put down his book.

雷木斯放下了書本。

“Oh?”

“哦？”

“I don’t want to disturb you, though.” Sirius said, innocently, edging closer.

“我不想打擾你。”小天狼星說，無辜地靠近一些。

“It can wait.”

“可以等一下。”

Sunday 23rd December 1976

“Show me how to throw a punch, then?”

“那就教我怎麼揮拳吧？”

“Seriously?!” Remus sighed,

“真的？！”雷木斯嘆了口氣，

“Deadly Sirius.” The other boy waggled his eyebrows. Remus groaned. “Oh, go on,” Sirius laughed at his face, “Show me! Teach me something, Professor Lupin.”

“致命的小天狼星。”另一個男孩揚起了眉毛。雷木斯呻吟著。“哦，快點吧，”小天狼星對著他的臉笑，“教我！教我一些東西，盧平教授。”

They were lounging in their pyjamas, in the common room. Gryffindor tower was still being cleaned nightly by the house elves, but the funny little creatures had had the sense to leave up the ‘goal’ sheets, even if they’d tidied away all of the projectiles. The effect was that of a weird screen blocking out the windows on the other side, except for five pools of winter sunlight which streamed in through the cut out holes.

他們穿著睡衣，躺在公共休息室裡。格蘭芬多塔樓仍然在夜間由家養小精靈清理，但那些有趣的小生物有點智慧，留下了‘目標’的布單，即使他們已經清理了所有的投擲物。效果就像是一個奇怪的屏幕，擋住了另一邊的窗戶，除了五束冬日陽光從切口處射入。

“Ok, but you need something to hit that you won’t hurt yourself on.”

“好吧，但你需要一個打擊的東西，這樣你就不會傷到自己。”

They ended up finding an empty bit of wall and performing a softening charm on it. Sirius stood there, eagerly, awaiting instruction. “Make a fist.” Remus said. “No, ok, not like that… yeah, put your thumb there, unless you want it broken. Ok, now you want it at shoulder level… yeah, then… er…”

他們最終找到了一塊空曠的牆壁，對它施了柔化咒。小天狼星站在那裡，急切地等待指示。“握緊拳頭。”雷木斯說。“不，不是那樣……對，把你的拇指放在那裡，除非你想把它弄斷。好，現在把它保持在肩膀水平……對，然後……嗯……”

Remus eventually resorted to demonstrating a few times on the wall, before physically repositioning Sirius’s arms in order to get the angle right, “Legs apart, don’t lean forward so much… ok, try it now…”

雷木斯最終只好在牆上演示了幾次，然後實際上調整小天狼星的手臂位置，以便調整角度，“雙腿分開，不要前傾太多……好，現在試試看……”

It took about twenty minutes, but in the end Remus deemed Sirius at least competent enough to give a black eye.

“Where’d you learn this?” Sirius panted, elated with his success.

“St Edmund’s.”

“Oh, yeah…” He ducked his head.

“No, not like that,” Remus shook his head quickly, realising that Sirius was probably imagining him squaring off against a group of huge, tough muggles. “Some of the older boys taught me, a few summers ago. They were all a bit rough, liked a fight, but they were nice to me.”
“不是那樣的，”雷穆斯迅速搖頭，意識到小天狼星可能想像自己和一群巨大而強壯的麻瓜對峙。“幾個夏天前，一些高年級的男孩教過我。他們有點粗暴，喜歡打架，但對我很好。”

“Ah,” Sirius’s eyes gleamed with the light of understanding, “Was this the year you began your foray into organised crime?”

“My what?! Oh, yeah, the fags. Yep, that summer.”

“I’ll never forget you stomping onto the train in those boots.”

“Ugh, don’t,” Remus covered his eyes with his hands. He cringed every time he remembered the way he had acted, “I was so obnoxious.”
“啊，”小天狼星的眼睛閃爍著理解的光芒，“這是你開始涉足有組織犯罪的那一年嗎？”

“我什麼？！哦，對了，那些吸煙的。對，那個夏天。”

“我永遠不會忘記你穿著那些靴子踩上火車的樣子。”

“噫，別說了，”雷穆斯用手捂住了眼睛。他每次記起自己當時的行為都感到不安，“我當時太討厭了。”

“I didn’t think so. Anyway, you had good reason.” Sirius rubbed his knuckles. They looked red from hitting the wall so many times, and Remus fought the urge to take Sirius’s hand in his own and kiss every finger. “Did you, er… ever learn anymore about Greyback?” Sirius asked, tentatively, snapping Remus out of his daze.

“Yeah, bits and pieces.” He didn’t want to clam up, but he did anyway, sitting down again and picking up a newspaper, just to have something to hold.

“Moony, I know you hate talking about him. It.”
“我不這麼認為。反正，你有充分的理由。”小天狼星揉了揉他的關節。他們看起來很紅，因為打了那麼多次牆，雷穆斯努力抑制住把小天狼星的手握在自己手中的衝動，親吻每一根手指。“你，呃……有沒有了解更多關於格雷巴克的事？”小天狼星試探性地問道，把雷穆斯從恍惚中喚醒。

“是的，一些零碎的消息。”他不想閉口不言，但他還是這麼做了，重新坐下來，拿起一份報紙，只是為了有東西可以握著。

“You don’t think… the attacks over the last few months...”
“月，這幾個月的攻擊…”

Remus looked up at him, just to check his expression. He looked anxious, but not frightened. At least, not of Remus.

“Yeah,” he confirmed with a curt nod, “It was him. Moody told me.”

“Shit.”

“Yeah. Shit.”
雷穆斯抬頭看著他，只是為了檢查他的表情。他看起來焦慮，但不害怕。至少，對雷穆斯而言。

“是的，”他簡短地點頭確認，“是他。穆迪告訴我的。”

“該死。”

“是的。該死。”

“You don’t think he’d come after you?”

“Don’t see why he would.” The barefaced lie should have shocked him, or at least caused a pang of guilt. But this was justified, Remus told himself, this was to protect his friends. He touched the scar on his side over the top of his pyjamas. The fabric was thin, and if he pressed lightly he could feel the dimples and puckers in his flesh made by those dreadful teeth. “It’s not like he can do anything else to me now. The worst’s already happened.”
“你不認為他會來找你嗎？”

“我看不出為什麼他會。”這個厚顏無恥的謊言本該讓他感到震驚，或至少讓他感到一陣內疚。但這是合理的，雷穆斯告訴自己，這是為了保護他的朋友。他摸了摸自己睡衣上的傷疤。布料很薄，如果輕輕地按壓，他可以感覺到那些可怕的牙齒在肉體上留下的凹痕和皺紋。“他現在也不可能再對我做什麼。最糟糕的已經發生了。”

“Moony.”

It wasn’t a question or a request, and they both let it hang in the air.
“月。”

這不是問題或請求，他們都讓這句話懸在空中。

Monday 24th December 1976

“Do we have any weed?” Sirius asked as they walked back from breakfast on Christmas Eve. They’d dodged yet another chess tournament with the Ravenclaws. Remus didn’t actually mind the idea, but Sirius had decided they were intensely boring and not to be tolerated.

“When you say ‘we’,” Remus replied, dryly, “Do you mean me?”

“Fine, do you have any weed?”

“No.”

“But you know where some is.”

“Maybe.”

“That’s my little delinquent. C’mon then, show me.”

Remus sighed,

“We’d have to go outside, to the greenhouses - and probably smoke it there too, I don’t want the house elves getting a whiff. It’s too cold, I’d rather not.”
“我們有大麻嗎？”小天狼星在聖誕前夕從早餐回來的路上問道。他們又一次躲過了與拉文克勞的棋藝比賽。雷穆斯其實不介意這個主意，但小天狼星已經決定他們非常無聊，不能容忍。

“當你說‘我們’時，”雷穆斯乾巴巴地回答，“你是指我嗎？”

“好吧，那你有大麻嗎？”

“沒有。”

“但你知道在哪裡。”

“也許吧。”

“那是我的小流氓。來吧，帶我去找。”

雷穆斯嘆了口氣，

“我們得去外面，去溫室 - 可能還得在那裡抽，我不想讓家養小精靈嗅到。太冷了，我不想去。”

“Come on, Moony. You haven’t been outside in ages!”

“I know, that was deliberate.”

“Come on.” Sirius was dragging him by the sleeve now, and because there wasn’t much else to do, and he did quite fancy a spliff, Remus allowed it. They summoned their cloaks and left the castle, hurrying through the thinning sheet of snow down to the greenhouses. Behind them, buried in a tin box, Remus unearthed the illicit buds, wrapped up in twists of brown paper. He would have to pay back whoever it belonged to - if they found out, of course.
“來吧，月。你很久沒出去過了！”

“我知道，那是故意的。”

“來吧。”小天狼星現在拉著他的袖子，因為沒什麼其他事情可以做，而且他確實很想抽根煙，雷穆斯也就讓了。他們叫了披風，離開了城堡，急匆匆地穿過變薄的雪層，前往溫室。在他們身後，雷穆斯從一個鐵盒中挖出非法的大麻花苞，用棕色紙包裹著。他需要償還給任何擁有它的人——如果他們發現的話，當然。

The greenhouses themselves had no snow on the roofs; being warm enough inside.

“We could go in there?” Sirius suggested, shivering.

“Are you mental? Spout comes down here twice a day to check on the mandrakes. It has to be somewhere else.”

“The shack?”

“Fuck that.” Remus growled, without thinking. Sirius looked at him, surprised, and he shook his head, apologetically, “I hate it there. Please, somewhere else?”
溫室本身的屋頂上沒有雪；裡面足夠暖和。

“我們可以進去嗎？”小天狼星顫抖地建議。

“你瘋了嗎？斯普特一天來這裡兩次查看曼德拉草。必須找其他地方。”

“小屋？”

“去他媽的。”雷穆斯咆哮道，沒有思考。小天狼星看著他，驚訝地，他搖了搖頭，歉意地說：“我討厭那裡。拜託，找其他地方？”

“Ok, sorry… er… ooh, I know!” He grabbed Remus by the wrist this time, his ungloved hand still miraculously warm.

Remus worked out where they were going before they got there - and it was actually sort of brilliant. They were just approaching the statue of the hump-backed, one-eyed witch, when the seventh year Slytherin student turned a corner at the other end of the hallway. They stopped still, probably looking extremely guilty.

“What are you two doing?” He asked, tilting his head, weighing them up.

“Just going for a stroll.” Sirius replied, haughtily, “It’s a free castle.”

“Whatever.” The Slytherin rolled his eyes, bored. He kept walking past them, robes sweeping. Remus pulled out the map, as soon as he was out of sight, and watched the little dot with his name keep on towards the library. Perseus Flint.

“Bleugh,” Sirius pulled a face when he saw it, “I think he’s a relative…”

They entered the secret passage, cast an illuminating spell and rolled up their cloaks so that they could sit comfortably on the stone floor.

“Should have brought the record player,” Sirius said, “We could get quite comfy here, dunno why I never thought of it before.”

“You and your cave-dwelling fantasies,” Remus humoured him, laying out all of his paraphernalia. He liked rolling, it was a pleasant process. “We’re not spending the rest of Christmas in here.”
“好吧，對不起……呃……哦，我知道了！”這次他抓住雷穆斯的手腕，他沒有戴手套的手仍然奇跡般地溫暖。

雷穆斯在他們到達之前就猜到了他們要去哪裡——而且其實還蠻聰明的。他們正接近那座駝背獨眼女巫的雕像，當時一位七年級的斯萊特林學生在走廊的另一端轉了一個彎。他們停下來，可能看起來非常內疚。

“你們倆在做什麼？”他歪著頭問，打量著他們。

“只是散步。”小天狼星高傲地回答，“這是座自由的城堡。”

“隨便。”那斯萊特林翻了翻白眼，無聊地說。他繼續走過他們身邊，長袍掃過。他一離開視線，雷穆斯立刻拿出地圖，觀察著那個帶有自己名字的小點繼續向圖書館移動。珀修斯·弗林特。

“呸，”小天狼星看到它時做了個鬼臉，“我覺得他是親戚……”

“該帶上唱片機，”小天狼星說，“我們可以在這裡舒適地待著，不知道為什麼我以前沒想到。”

They did spend the next few hours there, though, minds drifting, murmuring stupid jokes to each other or humming half-remembered songs. He was just thankful Dumbledore wasn’t there; he’d see through them in an instant.

They were wrangled into a game of chess after lunch, once the table had been cleared, and Sirius actually became very competitive in his attempt to beat Tina, who must have been the reigning Ravenclaw champion. He was nudged awake about an hour later.

“You’re snoring, Moony.” Sirius chuckled.

“Are you all right?” Tina asked, her inquisitive face peering across the chess board. She had won, it seemed.

“You do look quite pale,” she continued. Her eyes raked over him analytically, “Perhaps you ought to go to bed for a bit? Sirius said you were busy all morning on Herbology, so I’m not surprised if you’re tired.”

Sirius bean to giggle, compulsively, and Remus elbowed him hard in the ribs.

He went back to the tower slowly, at first in case Sirius decided to follow him, and then because his hip hurt from sleeping in a stupid position. He took his Arithmancy textbook into the bathroom with him, hoping it would stop him from falling asleep again.

He’d only been in the water for ten minutes when Sirius’s voice broke into the dorm room,

“Moony?”

“I’m in the bath.” He called back. The door opened, Remus tutted, “Didn’t say you could come in…”

“Nothing I haven’t seen.” Sirius replied, archly. Remus blinked - was Sirius actually commenting on the recent turn their relationship had taken, or was this just another off handed remark? Perhaps he talked to James in the bath. Remus wouldn’t be surprised. Sirius leaned casually against the sink, “James gave me the password to the prefect’s baths, if you’d rather go there?”

“I’m fine here, thanks.”

“Ok. I’ve had an idea.”

“Does it involve smoking weed in a tunnel?”

“Yes.”

“Brilliant.”

“Not just that, though - I fancy an outing.”

“Do you?” Remus smirked, closing his eyes and leaning back. Here we go...

“How does the Hog’s Head sound?”

Remus opened his eyes.

“It sounds completely mad.”

“Excellent!” Sirius grinned, “We’ll go after dinner, then.”

Remus made half-hearted attempts to change Sirius’s mind, but when a plan had been concocted, it was generally pretty much set in stone. Particularly if it involved breaking school rules.

“I’m not allowed into Hogsmeade…”

“Moony, it’s Christmas Eve.”
“你看起來很蒼白，”她繼續說。她的眼睛仔細地掃視著他，“也許你應該去休息一下？小天狼星說你整個早上都忙於草藥學，所以我不驚訝你會累。”

小天狼星開始強迫性地咯咯笑，雷穆斯用力肘擊了他一下。

“好吧，我會去躺下的，謝謝。”

“我在這裡很好，謝謝。”

“好吧。我有一個主意。”

“這是否涉及在隧道裡抽煙？”

“是的。”

“太好了。”

“但不僅僅是這個——我想出去走走。”

“你想？”雷穆斯嘴角上揚，閉上眼睛靠在後面。來吧...

“霍格斯黑頭酒吧怎麼樣？”

雷穆斯睜開了眼睛。

“聽起來完全瘋狂。”

“太好了！”小天狼星露出笑容，“那我們晚餐後就去。”

雷穆斯嘗試著半心半意地改變小天狼星的主意，但一旦計劃制定出來，它通常就會石沉大海。特別是當它涉及違反校規的時候。

“我不被允許進入霍格斯密德……”

“小天狼星，今天是聖誕夜。”

 

 

So they went. After sharing a long joint in the tunnel (at the Honeyduke’s end, obviously - Remus didn’t fancy being stoned for the long walk through the passage), they crept up into the sweet shop (pocketing a few chocolate frogs on the way) and out into the dark, empty high street.
于是他们就去了。在隧道里共享了一根长长的麻醉卷（显然是在霍尼杜克的那一端——雷穆斯不想在穿过通道的长路上变得醉醺醺的），他们悄悄地进入了糖果店（一路上顺手拿了几只巧克力青蛙）并走上了黑暗空旷的街道。

The Three Broomsticks was the only place that looked at all welcoming - but Sirius reckoned Rosmerta might shop them to McGonagall if she saw them in there.
三把扫帚是唯一一个看起来有些欢迎的地方——但小天狼星认为罗斯梅塔可能会把他们报告给麦格教授，如果她看到他们在那里。

“Which would be total bollocks,” he huffed, “I’m seventeen, I should be allowed to do what I like.”
“这完全是胡说八道，”他喘息着说，“我已经十七岁了，我应该可以做我喜欢的事。”

The Hog’s Head was not nearly as inviting as the Three Broomsticks, but it still had a kind of atmosphere. The clientele were private, huddled in groups talking amongst themselves, and the barman surly, but he served Sirius and Remus without question, and they were able to find a table and stools without too much of a problem. There was an odd smell hanging about the place - something Remus liked a lot, but couldn’t quite place. It stirred a strange sort of wanting inside him, which he tried to drown in whisky.
霍格斯黑头酒吧的招待并不如三把扫帚那样热情，但它仍然有种氛围。顾客们私密地聚在一起谈话，酒保态度冷漠，但他没有质疑地服务了小天狼星和雷穆斯，他们很快找到了一张桌子和凳子。酒吧里弥漫着一种奇怪的气味——雷穆斯非常喜欢，但却无法确定那是什么。它在他心中激起了一种奇异的渴望，他试图用威士忌来淹没这种感觉。

They drank a lot, and quickly, caught up in each other’s overexcitement.
他们喝了很多，喝得很快，沉浸在彼此的兴奋中。

“I haven’t had a drink since Halloween.” Remus said, daringly.
“我从万圣节以来没喝过酒。”雷穆斯大胆地说。

“Ugh, I was so sick that night,” Sirius laughed, “I don’t even remember half of it.”
“呃，那晚我真的很醉，”小天狼星笑道，“我甚至不记得一半的事了。”

“I do.” Remus bristled. Sirius caught his look and the smile fell from his face. His brows knit and he looked down at his half empty goblet,
“我记得。”雷穆斯紧绷着。小天狼星捕捉到他的表情，笑容从他的脸上消失了。他皱起眉头，看着自己半满的酒杯，

“当然记得那部分，雷穆斯。”

He felt a bit guilty after that. A small part of him still wanted to punish Sirius for the hurt he’d caused, even if, on the whole, he wanted to forget it all and just be happy. Alcohol is fortunately the ideal solution for this particular problem. At least, Remus thought so. He smiled broadly,
之后他感到有点内疚。他内心的一小部分仍然想要惩罚小天狼星，尽管总体上他想要忘记这一切，只想要快乐。幸运的是，酒精对于这个问题是理想的解决方案。至少，雷穆斯是这么认为的。他面带笑容，

“我十三岁时在一个家庭宴会上醉过，”小天狼星回忆道，打了个响指再点了两杯，“但没有像我那年你生日那样醉过……不过，对母亲来说都是一样的，接着她就拿出了魔杖……”

He made a wide, slashing movement with his own wand hand, and imitated his mother’s sharp, precise voice, “A Black heir shows proper comportment at all times,” slash, slash.
他用自己的魔杖手做了一个宽大的劈砍动作，模仿他母亲尖锐而准确的声音，“黑家继承人应始终表现得体，”劈砍，劈砍。

雷穆斯皱了皱眉，想到小天狼星的腿肚子。小天狼星在劈砍中侧目看了他一眼，“对不起，”他说，双臂交叉，威士忌到达时，“这不好笑，我不知道为什么我表现得像是。”

“你现在已经出来了，”雷穆斯认真地说，“你再也不必回去了。”

How many times I stood between… he used to be a proper little crybaby, but Mother hates crying, she says it makes men sissies, it makes them - well, whatever, some bollocks, but anyway, Reg would cry, and I would do something worse to distract her, and then she’d do her thing,” slash, slash. His eyes were bright and his cheeks were pink, “Y’know if either of us had just learnt not to get upset, then maybe… but I s’pose Reg learnt, in the end, cold hearted fucker.”
“是啊，”小天狼星含糊不清地说，靠在椅子上，“现在都是雷吉的烂摊子了。那个可恶的小家伙——你知道我替他背了多少次锅吗？多少次我站在……他曾经是个真正的小哭包，但母亲讨厌哭泣，她说这会让男人变得娘娘腔，变得——好吧，无论如何，雷吉会哭，而我会做一些更糟糕的事来转移她的注意力，然后她会做她的事，”劈砍，劈砍。他的眼睛闪亮，脸颊红润，“你知道，如果我们其中一个学会了不生气，也许……但我想雷吉学会了，最终，冷酷的混蛋。”

“你不像雷吉。”小天狼星坚决地说，捏了捏雷穆斯的膝盖。雷穆斯傻傻地笑着看着他，小天狼星迅速收回了手，警惕地四处张望，生怕这个举动被注意到。

“陈旧的啤酒？体味？”小天狼星建议，自己笑了起来。

“No, it’s an animal or something…”
“不，是动物还是别的东西……”

“Sorry, mate,” he shrugged, “I could turn into a dog and have a sniff, but I think I’m too drunk to remember how to turn back…”
“抱歉，伙计，”他耸耸肩，“我可以变成狗去嗅嗅，但我觉得我太醉了，记不起怎么变回去了……”

“Hey,” he whispered, “Not here, someone’ll see... “
“嘿，”他低声说，“不是在这里，有人会看到的……”

They dragged each other back to Honeyduke’s, through the door and into the cellar - which Remus would have been more than happy with, but Sirius wouldn’t touch him again until they were inside the dark, dank tunnel. They hadn’t been together like this before after drinking - and neither of them had the presence of mind to light their wands, so it was pitch black, but Remus was hot with the whisky and Sirius was just as eager as him now they were alone, and it was the same as it had been, only better, more urgent and fluid and messy, and Remus felt a surge of courage, before pulling away and sinking to his knees, holding Sirius in place, and it was nerve-wracking, but god, so worth it to hear that surprised gasp,
他们互相拖回了霍尼杜克，通过门进入了地窖——雷穆斯对此很满意，但小天狼星直到他们进入黑暗潮湿的隧道才再次碰触他。他们之前在喝酒后从未这样在一起过——他们都没有点亮魔杖的意识，所以完全黑暗，但雷穆斯被威士忌烫得热乎乎的，小天狼星现在也和他一样迫不及待。感觉一样，只是更好，更紧迫，更流畅和混乱，雷穆斯感到一股勇气涌上心头，然后拉开距离，跪下来，固定住小天狼星，这让他感到紧张，但天哪，听到那惊讶的喘息声是如此值得，

“What are you...? – oh!”
“你在做什么……？——哦！”

Christmas Day 1976
1976年圣诞节

As was to be expected, both boys awoke on Christmas Day with thumping hangovers.
正如预期的那样，两人都在圣诞节醒来时有着严重的宿醉。

“Tell me there’s a cure, Moony,” Sirius wailed from his bed, “You’re the one taking healing lessons…”
“小天狼星，告诉我有解药吧，”小天狼星从床上哀号道，“你是唯一一个上了治疗课的人……”

“You’re the one taking Potions,” Remus grumbled from under his pillow. “Pain is a potion thing, I do cuts and abrasions.”
“你才上了药剂学，”雷穆斯从枕头下嘟囔道，“疼痛是药剂学的事，我处理割伤和擦伤。”

“Useless.”
“没用。”

“Shut up.”
“闭嘴。”

But it was no good, he was awake now, and there was nothing either of them could do about it. He clambered out from his bedsheets, head thudding at twice the tempo as he hobbled across the room to the bathroom. “Cold shower,” he mumbled at Sirius’s bed, “Then breakfast. Fried eggs, trust me.”
但没用，他现在已经醒了，两人都无能为力。他从床单中爬出来，头痛得像是加快了两倍的节奏，一拐一拐地走到浴室。“冷水澡，”他对着小天狼星的床喃喃道，“然后早餐。炒鸡蛋，相信我。”

They couldn't face opening presents and left it, instead stumbling down to eat, without combing their hair or making much effort to look smart at all. Dumbledore was there, and smiled at them benevolently as they took their seats at the table,
他们无法面对打开礼物，决定跳过，跌跌撞撞地去吃饭，头发也没梳理，完全没有努力打扮。邓布利多在那儿，看到他们坐到桌旁，慈祥地对他们微笑，

“Happy Christmas, one and all!” He boomed, cheerily, apparently oblivious to Sirius and Remus’s wincing.
“圣诞快乐，大家！”他愉快地大声说，显然没有察觉到小天狼星和雷穆斯的痛苦表情。

Breakfast did improve things, somewhat - at least it settled their stomachs, and they eagerly returned to the tower afterwards to open presents. Remus got the usual assortment of quills, chocolates, books and knitwear as usual, and was very pleased to receive them. Nothing from Matron this year - he supposed she’d decided to cut ties early, seeing as after his seventeenth birthday he would not be expected to return to St. Edmund’s. He pushed that thought down with a cigarette.
早餐确实有所改善——至少安抚了他们的胃，他们随后急切地回到塔楼拆礼物。雷穆斯像往常一样收到了各种笔、巧克力、书籍和针织品，对此非常满意。今年没有来自医务员的礼物——他想她可能决定早早断绝关系了，因为在他十七岁生日后，他不再被期望回到圣埃德蒙德学校。他用一根香烟将这个想法压了下去。

James got in touch shortly after that, through the compact mirrors, and they both wished him a merry Christmas,
詹姆斯随后通过紧凑的镜子联系了他们，他们都祝他圣诞快乐，

“Are you two ok?” He frowned up through the glass, “You look a bit peaky.”
“你们还好吗？”他通过玻璃皱着眉头问道，“你们看起来有点脸色苍白。”

“Hungover,” Sirius grunted.
“宿醉。”小天狼星咕哝道。

“Jealous.” James replied.
“真羡慕。”詹姆斯回答道。

“Weirdo.” Said Remus.
“怪人。”雷穆斯说道。

Afterwards, he took a nap, still worn out from the night before, and woke up in time for lunch - which, in Remus’s opinion, was basically a perfect Christmas Day.
之后，他小睡了一会儿，仍然感到昨晚的疲惫，醒来时正好是午餐时间——在雷穆斯看来，这基本上是一个完美的圣诞节。

Boxing Day 1976
1976年节礼日

“Why’s it called boxing day, anyway?”
“节礼日为什么叫节礼日呢？”

“Nobody knows,” Remus yawned over his porridge, “It’s one of the great mysteries of life.”
“没人知道，”雷穆斯在麦片上打了个哈欠，“这是生活中的一个伟大谜团。”

“Must be a muggle thing. I’ll ask my muggle studies professor.”
“一定是麻瓜的东西。我会问问我的麻瓜研究教授。”

“You do muggle studies?” The Slytherin, Flint, was staring down the table at him.
“你学麻瓜研究？”斯莱特林的弗林特盯着桌子上的雷穆斯问道。

Sirius threw two fingers up at him, then turned his back, ignoring him. Remus kept eating, the brown sugar melting on his tongue. Their knees were bumping under the table and it was delightful.
小天狼星朝他竖起两个手指，然后转过身，忽视他。雷穆斯继续吃着，棕糖在舌尖上融化。他们的膝盖在桌子下碰撞，感觉很愉快。

Suddenly, the owls arrived, screeching into the hall with an unusual urgency. There were more than usual, as well. Remus realised that Dumbledore and McGonagall were not at breakfast. Tina, sitting opposite, got her post first and opened it.
突然，猫头鹰们急促地飞进了大厅，发出尖锐的叫声。数量也比平时多。雷穆斯意识到邓布利多和麦格没有在早餐时出现。坐在对面的蒂娜首先收到了邮件，并打开了它。

“It’s from mum…” her eyes widened and she got up from the table at once, hurrying away out of the hall. Flint did the same, then Arnold.
“这是妈妈发来的……”她的眼睛睁大了，立刻从桌子上站起，匆匆离开大厅。弗林特也这样做了，然后是阿诺德。

“What’s going on?” Remus asked, as Flitwick sighed heavily, shaking his head. He passed the two remaining boys a copy of The Daily Prophet. They leaned in together to read it.
“发生了什么？”雷穆斯问道，此时弗利维克重重地叹了口气，摇了摇头。他递给剩下的两个男孩一份《预言家日报》。他们俩凑在一起阅读。

‘MUGGLES ATTACKED IN CHRISTMAS CRISIS’ blared the headline.
“麻瓜在圣诞危机中遭遇袭击”标题赫然醒目。

“Last night, while thousands slept safely in their beds on Christmas night, over one hundred muggles all over Britain were attacked in their homes. The Auror’s office confirmed this morning that the attacks were magical in nature, and intended to cause harm.
“昨晚，在成千上万的人在圣诞夜安然入睡时，英国各地的百余名麻瓜在家中遭到袭击。今天早晨，傲罗办公室确认这些袭击具有魔法性质，意在造成伤害。

The attacks took place in a number of locations, apparently targeting families with ties to the wizarding world - those with magical relatives or a history of muggle-magical relations. Offences range from minor jinxes to - in some cases - the use of unforgivable curses. There are no suspects at present. The minister for Magic is expected to make a statement later today.”
袭击发生在多个地点，显然以与巫师世界有联系的家庭为目标——那些有魔法亲属或有麻瓜与魔法关系历史的家庭。罪行从轻微的咒语到——在某些情况下——使用不可饶恕的诅咒不等。目前没有嫌疑犯。预计魔法部长今天晚些时候会发表声明。”

Professor McGonagall arrived while they were reading, with Flint, Tina and Arnold in toe. Tina looked as though she had been crying. Flint was scowling miserably.
麦格教授在他们阅读的时候到达了，弗林特、蒂娜和阿诺德跟在她身后。蒂娜看起来像是哭过。弗林特愁眉苦脸。

“You’ve all heard the news.” The professor said, her voice thinner than usual; strained and tired. “If your parents have requested that you return home, then we will make arrangements at once to ensure you arrive safely.”
“你们都听到消息了。”教授说，声音比平时要虚弱；疲惫和紧张。“如果你们的父母要求你们回家，我们会立即安排，确保你们安全到达。”
