“Livia,” Remus said, cigarette between his teeth, “Yeah, I think Ferox scared her off.”

“Too bloody right,” James nodded, much more comfortable talking action, “And I bet with Moody on the case she won’t be back any time soon, eh? So, are you in a lot of trouble? With Dumbledore?”

“I don’t think so.” Remus sighed. He rubbed his sore hip, “I think Dumbledore was more worried about me mucking up his spy ring, rather than breaking any rules.”

“He wouldn’t want to see you hurt. Any of us.” James said, sincerely. He eyed Remus’s awkward posture, “C’mon, there’s a bench down here, you can finish your toast.”

They made slow progress down towards the edge of the lake, where there were a few stone benches. It was too cold for anyone else to be out at this time on a Sunday, and Remus watched the late morning mist drift across the dark surface of the water as he chewed on the remains of his crusts. Sirius hadn’t spoken yet, since the owlery, and Remus was trying not to notice it. Sirius felt betrayed - Remus knew that as sure as he knew his own name. Betrayed even if he didn’t really have a right to feel it. This isn’t about you. Remus wanted to hiss at doleful, silent Sirius.
“那麼，”詹姆斯說，吞下去後，“她現在走了，對嗎？那隻狼人？”

“Can’t believe we all slept through the most exciting night of the year, eh.” James nudged Remus, trying to bring a bit of levity to the otherwise rather sombre atmosphere.

“It wasn’t that exciting,” Remus grinned back, giving him what he wanted, “I was crap. If Ferox hadn’t come… I dunno.”

“I dunno.” Remus replied, “I think… I got the impression, anyway, that she needed to me agree. Like it had to be me who made the decision – otherwise I s’pose they could all just gang up and snatch me.”

“No, of course not.” Remus said, quickly, “I’d never join Greyback.”

“Well then.” James repeated, satisfied.

Sirius sprang up, as if he had been wound up to breaking point. He glared at Remus as if he was about to start screaming at him. Then he walked away, at an impossible pace.
“真不敢相信我們全都錯過了今年最激動人心的夜晚。”詹姆斯輕推雷木斯，試圖為這個相當陰沉的氛圍帶來些許輕鬆。

“不，當然沒有。”雷木斯迅速說道，“我永遠不會加入格雷巴克。”

“那麼。”詹姆斯滿意地重複道。

雷木斯看著他那雙仍然沾滿吐司油脂的手。他把手擦在褲子上。當然不會。當然不會。除了。

“Moony?” James said, sensing the odd quiet.

“I’d never join him.” Remus said, carefully. “And Livia was… she was awful, but.” He breathed in, “Not everything she said was wrong.”

After all, as soon as he turned seventeen they would be all he had. “I’m really sorry, Wormtail.” He said, kindly, “Want to play chess instead, then?”

雷木斯只是半聽。 他伸展了一下，再次揉著他的臀部，看它是否能動一動。

Monday 16th January 1977

Remus was genuinely sorry to hear about Peter and Dezzie. She’d never really been part of their group, but she was a nice enough girl, and had made Peter happy – she had given him something that James and Sirius did not have, and that was special in itself. The breakup had ostensibly been simply down to a change in attitudes. They had been seeing each other since they were fourteen, and at sixteen it seemed that Desdemona wished to spread her wings a bit.

“她可能會改變主意嗎？”Remus 在第三局棋賽中對愁眉苦臉的 Peter 提議。

“She might change her mind?” Remus suggested to a glum faced Peter over their third chess game.

“Doubt it,” Peter huffed. “Reckon she’s got a crush on that Roman Rotherhide bloke. Wanker. Knight to F3.”

“我不太相信。”Peter 吹了口氣，“我覺得她對那個 Roman Rotherhide 小子有點意思。混蛋。騎士到 F3。”

“我以為 Mary 正在和他交往？”

“Mary sees everyone,” Peter sniggered, meanly. “She’s like the girl version of Padfoot.”

“Mary 看過每個人，”Peter 嘲弄地笑了，“她就像 Padfoot 的女孩版。”

Ferox’s reply arrived later that Sunday evening.

Ferox 的回信在那個星期天晚上晚些時候到達了。

Remus,

I’m afraid I can’t invite you into Hogsmeade, but I can meet you for supper on Monday evening at the castle. I’ll meet you outside the Great Hall at 6pm.

“Remus，

我恐怕不能邀請你進入霍格斯米德，但我可以在星期一晚上在城堡裡和你共進晚餐。我會在下午六點在大禮堂外面見你。”

That was ok. Good enough – he could ask what he needed to ask anywhere. Remus went to his lessons as usual on Monday, and told the marauders at lunch time. Sirius was speaking to him again, but not properly. For every small step forward, he and Remus seemed to take three enormous steps back again.

Remus had only been in the Care of Magical Creatures office once since Ferox had left – to request an extension on an essay after a full moon. “我明白了。Dumbledore 說過——”

“沒有，但我不是傻子。”Remus 不屑地說，“他沒有讓我做任何事情，因為他從不問。他只是確保你知道他想要什麼。但我也有一些想要的東西。”

“And what are those?”

“那些是什麼？”

“I’m not signing the register, on my birthday.” Remus said, steadily. “I’m not exposing myself to the ministry. I’ve looked into it – if I do, I have to report to them for three days every month. They’ll lock me up – I assume, it’s not very clear from the information they put out. I can’t keep a job, like that. If Dumbledore needs a spy, then he needs me to be untraceable, too.”

“我不會在我的生日那天簽署登記。”Remus 穩定地說，“我不會暴露自己給魔法部。我查過了——如果我這麼做，我每個月必須向他們報到三天。他們會把我鎖起來——我猜測，從他們公布的信息中並不太清楚。我不能那樣保持一份工作。如果 Dumbledore 需要一個間諜，那麼他需要我也不能被追蹤。”

“I see,” Ferox said again, “But—”

“我明白了，”Ferox 再次說道，“但——”

“I’m not finished.” Remus snapped. “Afterwards. If we win. I want amnesty for the werewolves. Even Greyback’s pack. Not Greyback, obviously, but his followers.”

“我還沒說完。”Remus 突然說，“之後。如果我們贏了。我想要狼人們的特赦。甚至是 Greyback 的包夥。不是 Greyback，顯然，但他的追隨者。”

“Remus, that’s completely—”

“Remus，這完全——”

“No it isn’t.” Remus folded his arms. “You don’t know. Livia might be batshit, but she’s not wrong. A choice between freedom under Greyback or imprisonment under the ministry is an easy one to make.”

“不是。”Remus 抱著雙臂。“你不知道。Livia 可能瘋了，但她並不錯。選擇在 Greyback 下的自由或在魔法部下的監禁是很容易的。”

Ferox looked at him, for a very long time. Remus drank his pumpkin juice, his throat very dry. His heart was beating so fast he thought that Ferox must be able to hear it.

“Ferox 盯著他看了很久。Remus 喝了他的南瓜汁，喉嚨非常乾。他的心跳得如此之快，他以為 Ferox 一定能聽到。”

“These aren’t necessarily things Dumbledore can do,” Ferox said, slowly.

“這些不一定是 Dumbledore 能做到的事情，”Ferox 慢慢地說。

“Bullshit.” Remus set down his goblet, a little too hard on the desk.

“胡說。”Remus 把酒杯放下，稍微用力了一些在桌子上。

“I can bring it to him.” Ferox sighed, sounding defeated, “But I can’t make promises.”

“我可以把它帶給他。”Ferox 嘆了口氣，聽起來很沮喪，“但我不能保證。”

“Well,” Remus replied, coolly, “I’m seventeen in two months. So there’s the deadline.”

“那麼，”Remus 冷冷地回應，“我兩個月後就滿十七歲了。所以這是最後期限。”

“Blimey.” Ferox scratched his head. He sounded impressed, rather than angry, “You don’t half remind me of Lyall, right now. What happened to the hot-headed kid always getting into scrapes?”

“哎呀。”Ferox 抓了抓頭。他的語氣聽起來更像是印象深刻，而不是生氣，“你現在真是讓我想起了 Lyall。那個總是惹麻煩的急躁小子去哪了？”

“I’m still hot-headed.” Remus said, simply, “I think Lyall probably was too. It’s not that I think Dumbledore can solve all my problems. But I wanted to lay all my cards on the table.”

“我仍然很急躁。”Remus 簡單地說，“我覺得 Lyall 也可能是這樣。我不是認為 Dumbledore 能解決我所有的問題。但我想把我的底牌都攤開。”

“Fair enough.” Ferox nodded. “All’s fair in love and war, eh?”

“公平。”Ferox 點點頭，“愛情和戰爭中一切都公平，對吧？”

“I wouldn’t know about that.” Remus replied.

“我不知道這些。”Remus 回答道。

Their plates vanished, suddenly, and then reappeared, bearing two big wedges of chocolate cake topped with fruit. They ate them quietly, both deep in thought, occasionally shooting looks at each other.

“他們的盤子突然消失了，然後再出現，擺著兩大塊上面有水果的巧克力蛋糕。他們靜靜地吃著，兩人都陷入了沉思，偶爾互相瞥了一眼。”

“How’s it going with Moody?” Remus asked, casually. “I s’pose you probably can’t tell me anything.”

“和 Moody 的情況怎麼樣？”Remus 隨口問道，“我想你可能不能告訴我什麼。”

“You suppose right,” Ferox nodded. “Moody’s well, though. Complete nutter, but glad he’s on our side.”

“你猜對了，”Ferox 點點頭，“Moody 還好。完全是個瘋子，但很高興他在我們這邊。”

“And Achilles?”

“Achilles 很好。”Ferox 微笑道，“和我一位朋友住在一起。說到這個——和 MacDonald 小姐的戀情進展怎麼樣，Lupin？”

“The what?!” Remus stared at him, wide eyed. Ferox laughed,

“什麼？！”Remus 眼睛瞪大地盯著他。Ferox 笑了，

“With Miss MacDonald, down there? I’d have matched you better with Marlene, but I s’pose the heart wants what it wants, eh?”

“和下面的 Miss MacDonald？我會更匹配你和 Marlene，但我想心想要的就是想要的，對吧？”

“Oh!” Remus relaxed, “No, Mary’s just a friend.”

“哦！”Remus 放鬆了，“不，Mary 只是朋友。”

“Hm,” Ferox said, obviously not quite believing him. “What’s brought on this personality switch, then?”

“嗯，”Ferox 說，顯然不太相信他。“那麼這種性格轉變是什麼原因呢？”

“Why does it have to be about a girl? Two years is a long time.” Remus said, annoyed. “It’s not like I’ve suddenly changed. Look, I first said I’d help Dumbledore fight when I was fourteen.” He tried to explain. “And then last year, James Potter told us all that he planned to join, as soon as he left school, and we all said we would too, and I… I was always going to, you know, but just because James and Sirius wanted to. I never had a reason myself, really.”

“為什麼一定要跟女孩有關？兩年是很長的時間。”Remus 生氣地說，“我並不是突然改變了。你看，我第一次說我要幫助 Dumbledore 作戰的時候我才十四歲。”他試著解釋，“然後去年，James Potter 告訴我們他打算在離開學校後立即參加，我們都說我們也會參加，而我……我一直都會，知道嗎，但只是因為 James 和 Sirius 想要。我自己其實並沒有真正的理由。”

“We’re all going to suffer, if you know who wins.” Ferox said.

“如果你知道誰贏了，我們都會遭受痛苦。”Ferox 說道。

“Yeah, I s’pose.” Remus nodded diplomatically. “I know that. But I meant… well I never really had much of a stake in it, before. Now I’ve met Livia, I don’t think anything’s going to be that great for me after school finishes, no matter who’s in power. I want a stake. If I live.”

“是的，我想。”Remus 外交性地點點頭，“我知道。但我的意思是……嗯，我以前真的沒有太多利害關係。現在我遇見了 Livia，我不認為在學校結束後，無論誰掌權，都會有什麼對我來說特別好的。我想要有一份利害關係。如果我活著。”

“You shouldn’t compare yourself to them, Remus. The pack.”

“Remus，你不應該拿自己和他們比較。那一群人。”

“I can’t really help it, can I? Everybody else will. You know my friend, Sirius Black?”

“我真的無法幫助自己，不是嗎？其他人會的。你知道我的朋友 Sirius Black 嗎？”

“Not well,” Ferox replied, “The Potters took him in, didn’t they? I thought it was a bit odd, knowing his family.”

“不太熟悉，”Ferox 回答，“Potters 收養了他，不是嗎？我覺得這有點奇怪，知道他的家庭。”

“Exactly!” Remus said, triumphantly, “Sirius is my best friend, and a Gryffindor, and the Potters love him – but to everyone else he’s still a Black. He’ll spend the rest of his life trying not to be, no matter how many good things he does. Because people never forget things like that – they think that what you are makes you who you are. It’s the same for me.”

“正是如此！”Remus 驕傲地說，“Sirius 是我最好的朋友，還是 Gryffindor，Potters 愛他——但對其他人來說，他仍然是個 Black。他會用餘生來試圖不成為 Black，不管他做多少好事。因為人們從不會忘記這樣的事情——他們認為你的身份決定了你是誰。對我來說也是一樣。”

Remus was struggling now to keep explaining. Ferox looked completely lost. He sighed, heavily, “I’m sorry it has to go through you. You’re the only person I know who has any weight with Dumbledore who I trust. Who trusts me.”

“Remus 現在努力著繼續解釋。Ferox 看起來完全迷失了。他重重地嘆了口氣，“對不起，這件事得由你來處理。你是我知道唯一一個在 Dumbledore 那裡有影響力且我信任的人。信任我的人。”

Ferox watched him again, with a steady expression.

“Ferox 再次用穩定的表情看著他。”

“I will try, Remus. You’re asking a lot.”

“我會試試的，Remus。你要求的太多了。”

Remus frowned. He thought about Livia – her bare feet, her ragged clothes; her terrible cough and the hollow look in her eyes. It was no way to live.

“Remus 皺著眉頭。他想到 Livia——她赤裸的腳，她破舊的衣服；她可怕的咳嗽和眼中的空洞目光。這不是一種活法。”

He might be asking for a lot. But Remus had never asked for anything before in his life. He hoped Dumbledore remembered that.

“他可能要求很多。但 Remus 在一生中從未要求過任何東西。他希望 Dumbledore 記得這一點。”

 

Chapter 108: Sixth Year: Mary, Mary

 

 Mary, Mary, where you goin' to?

Mary, Mary, can I go too?

This one thing I will vow ya,

I'd rather die than to live without ya,

Mary, Mary, where you goin' to?

 

 

 

Friday 5th February 1977

The rest of January seemed to whizz by in a blur, and Remus just tried to get back to normal. The full moon landed early in the month, and Remus threatened to lock the marauders out of the shack if they didn’t promise to stay inside this time. Eventually he knew he would weaken and allow them to begin letting him out again - but he felt that they ought to play it safe, at least for a while.
一月的剩餘時間似乎在朦朧中迅速過去，雷姆斯試圖回到正常的生活。月初的滿月來臨，雷姆斯威脅如果他們不保證這次待在小屋裡，就會把萬惡的巫師們鎖在外面。最終他知道自己會動搖，允許他們再次讓他出來——但他覺得他們應該先保持安全，至少一段時間。

The sudden distance between Remus and Sirius was painful, and made all the more difficult by the fact that their relationship (such that it was) had been a secret all along. Remus resorted to his usual tactic, burying himself in his studies, while Sirius absorbed himself in Emmeline. He was sulking, Remus knew. And for once, he didn’t blame him. The whole messy situation only proved to Remus that they had to put a stop to it as soon as they could. It was becoming impossible to stay friends, and they needed to be friends before anything else.
雷姆斯和天狼星之間突然的距離令人痛苦，更加困難的是，他們的關係（不管它是什麼）一直是秘密。雷姆斯採取了他一貫的策略，把自己埋在學業中，而天狼星則全心投入到艾蜜琳中。他在陰沉，雷姆斯知道。這次，他不責怪他。這整個混亂的局面只證明了雷姆斯，他們必須儘快停止這一切。保持朋友變得不可能了，他們需要先做朋友，然後才能做其他的。

The problem was, Sirius hadn’t come to him at all since that night they’d slept in the common room. Remus was terrified that this meant it was already over - that Sirius had come to the realisation on his own, and simply chosen to stop. And Remus would not allow that. It couldn’t just be finished , without either of them saying anything about it. Surely?
問題是，自從那晚他們在公共休息室睡覺後，天狼星根本沒有來找過他。雷姆斯害怕這意味著一切已經結束——天狼星自己意識到這一點，然後選擇停止。而雷姆斯不會允許這樣。這不能僅僅結束，沒有任何人談論這個問題。難道不是嗎？

You held my hand. He wanted to say. You saw me cry.
你牽過我的手。他想說。你看見我哭了。

The day after the February full moon, Remus lay in his usual hospital bed, pondering these things. He had a cut on his arm, which Madam Pomfrey had told him to practice his healing charms on. It was very basic, but he was so tired after his transformation,
滿月後的第二天，雷姆斯躺在他常用的醫院床上，思索著這些事情。他的手臂上有一道傷口，波芬夫人告訴他要在傷口上練習治療咒語。這很基本，但在變身後他已經很疲憊了，

“You have to try, dear,” the medi-witch said, unsympathetically, “You wanted to be able to take care of yourself after the moons, so you’ll just have to learn to find the strength.”
“你得嘗試一下，親愛的，”女醫師無情地說，“你想要在月亮過後能夠照顧自己，所以你得學會找到力量。”

He prodded the cut, already healing by itself anyway, making another half-hearted attempt to fix it. Nothing. The marks Livia had left were dulled to pale pink now, and Madam Pomfrey thought they would probably vanish, in time, as they weren’t inherently magical wounds.
他戳了戳那道已經自行癒合的傷口，再次心不在焉地嘗試修復它。什麼也沒有。莉維亞留下的痕跡現在變成了淡粉紅色，波芬夫人認為它們隨著時間的推移可能會消失，因為它們並不是固有的魔法傷口。

“You’re welcome to leave,” she called to him, now, from her office. “If you’re just going to sit there moping… Go and see your friends.”
“你可以離開了，”她現在從她的辦公室裡喊道，“如果你只是坐在那裡愁眉苦臉……去見你的朋友們吧。”

Remus didn’t bother telling her that it was his friends - or rather, one friend in particular - he was moping about. But he never thought twice when she gave permission for him to leave, so he got up and dressed quickly, hurrying out of the hospital wing,
雷姆斯沒有告訴她他所愁苦的其實是他的朋友——或者說，特定的一個朋友。但當她允許他離開時，他從未多想，所以他迅速起床穿衣，急忙走出醫院翼，

“See you Tuesday!” He called, on his way out.
“星期二見！”他在出去的時候叫道。

It was after lunch, and there was only one lesson left that day - Care of Magical Creatures - which Remus wasn’t much in the mood for. He was ahead of the rest of the class anyway, and no one would miss him. He sloped along the corridors aimlessly for a while, still thinking about Sirius and Emmeline, and how he was ever going to... wait a minute .
午餐後，只剩下一節課——魔法生物護理——雷姆斯對這門課沒有什麼興趣。他已經在班級中領先了，沒有人會錯過他。他漫無目的地沿著走廊走了一會兒，仍然在想天狼星和艾蜜琳，還有他怎麼辦……等等。

He stopped and frowned, looking at the nearest portrait. Something was very off about it. The painting depicted an elderly wizard with thinning hair and a neat little goatee peering through a large golden telescope. For some reason, he was wearing an enormous bright red curly wig. It didn’t seem to bother him - he just kept adjusting the sight on his contraption, murmuring quietly to himself. Remus snorted, and looked at the next picture along.
他停下來皺著眉頭，看著最近的一幅畫。畫中描繪了一位年老的巫師，頭髮稀疏，梳著整潔的小鬍子，透過一個大金色望遠鏡觀察。出於某種原因，他戴著一個巨大的鮮紅色捲髮假髮。這似乎不困擾他——他只是繼續調整他裝置上的視野，低聲自言自語。雷姆斯哼了一聲，接著看下一幅畫。

This one contained a group of pretty, buxom young shepherdesses tending to their flock - and they all had bright red wigs on too. The same with the next portrait - a witch carrying an overflowing basket of fruit, garish scarlet curls bouncing on her head. And the next - a sinister looking monk, whose red wig actually sat on top of his hood. None of the subjects of the paintings seemed at all perturbed, as Remus followed the trail of bizarre headwear to the third floor mezzanine.
這幅畫描繪了一群美麗的豐滿小牧女們照顧她們的羊群——她們都戴著鮮紅色的假髮。接著是下一幅畫——一位巫婆提著滿滿一籃的水果，鮮豔的猩紅色捲髮在她頭上跳動。再下一幅——一位看起來陰森的僧侶，他的紅色假髮實際上坐落在他的頭巾上。畫中的人物似乎都沒有受到困擾，雷姆斯跟隨著這些奇異的頭飾來到了第三層夾層。

“Padfoot!” Remus gasped, when he found the culprit.
“天狼星！”當他找到罪魁禍首時，雷姆斯驚呼道。

Sirius was at ease, hands in his pockets, chatting casually to a painting of a giggly sea nymph in a large golden frame. When she saw Remus she gave a shriek and dived into the waves below.
天狼星輕鬆地站著，雙手插在口袋裡，隨意地跟一幅大金框中的咯咯笑的海妖畫作聊天。當她看到雷姆斯時，她尖叫了一聲，然後跳進了下面的波浪中。

“Aw, Moony, what’d you scare her for?” Sirius tutted, “I was just about to cast the spell.”
“哦，月亮，你為什麼嚇到她了？”天狼星咂了咂嘴，“我正打算施咒。”

“This is brilliant!” Remus grinned, gesturing at all of the pictures he’d passed, “How come you never told me you were doing it? Is James in on it?”
“這太棒了！”雷姆斯笑著，指著他經過的所有畫，“你怎麼從來沒告訴我你在做這些？詹姆斯知道嗎？”

“Yeah, he’s taking the east wing,” Sirius nodded, moving on to the next painting. “We just had the idea walking back to bed this morning. Sorry, thought you’d be sleeping still.”
“是的，他在東翼，”天狼星點了點頭，繼續看下一幅畫。“我們只是早上回床上的時候想到的。抱歉，以為你還在睡覺。”

“Madam Pomfrey let me go…”
“波芬夫人讓我離開了……”

“Oh right. You’ll probably want to go to the library, or something? I’m nearly finished here, no need for you to stick around.”
“哦，對了。你可能想去圖書館，或者其他地方？我快完成了，你不需要留在這裡。”

“No, I--”
“不，我——”

“Oh shit!”
“哦，天啊！”

The big grandfather clock in the great hall had begun chiming - every classroom door was about to burst open, and students come pouring out for their next lesson. “They’ll know it’s us!” Sirius said, “Quick!” He pulled James’s invisibility cloak out from his robes and raised it up like a tent.
大禮堂裡的大掛鐘開始敲響——每個教室的門即將打開，學生們蜂擁而出，準備上他們的下一節課。“他們會知道是我們！”天狼星說，“快點！”他從袍子裡拿出詹姆斯的隱形斗篷，像帳篷一樣舉起來。

Remus hurried over to get under it, crouching slightly to compensate for their height difference. They both backed against the wall and waited. The doors began to slam open one at a time, and torrents of students filled the previously quiet space. Invisible and trapped, Remus realised that this was the best chance he’d had in days.
雷姆斯急忙走過去鑽進斗篷下，稍微蹲下以彌補他們的身高差異。他們倆靠在牆上等待。門開始一個接一個地砰然打開，學生們湧入之前安靜的空間。隱形並且被困住，雷姆斯意識到這是他幾天來最好的機會。

“Oi,” he whispered, directly into Sirius’s ear. He felt the other boy tense. “Are you still angry with me?”
“喂，”他低聲對天狼星的耳朵說。他感覺到另一個男孩緊張起來。“你還在生我的氣嗎？”

“What do you--”
“你說什麼——”

“You’re avoiding me.”
“你在避開我。”

“No I’m not.” Sirius pushed back, suddenly, as a third year girl came a bit too close. He backed straight into Remus’ chest, so that their whole bodies were now touching, practically. “James said to give you space.” He murmured, “ And you left me out of the Hog’s Head mission, even after we said we’d go together.”
“不，我沒有。”天狼星突然推開，當一名三年級的女孩靠得太近時。他直挺挺地撞到雷姆斯的胸口，使他們的整個身體幾乎接觸在一起。“詹姆斯說給你空間。”他低聲說，“而且你把我排除在豬頭酒吧的任務之外，即使我們說過要一起去。”

“It wasn’t a mission!” Remus whispered, struggling to keep his voice low. People were noticing the vandalised portraits now, pointing and laughing around them. “And I never agreed to go together!”
“那不是任務！”雷姆斯低聲說，努力保持聲音低沉。人們現在注意到那些被破壞的畫作，指指點點，圍繞著他們笑。“而且我從未同意一起去！”

她也笑了，他們一起離開了圖書館。他們一周的每個晚上都在那裡——除了莉莉有學監職責或瑪琳有魁地奇比賽的時候；那時只有雷姆斯和瑪麗。這出乎意料地還不錯——瑪麗對他們短暫的關係做了一些調侃，但沒有提到想要再做一次，看起來似乎再次與羅曼·羅瑟海德約會了。雷姆斯感到鬆了口氣。一次秘密的戀情已經足夠了。

It was early to be revising, but the four of them had decided to reconvene their study group this year in order to get through the first stage of their NEWTs. Final exams were still over a year away, but in Remus and Lily’s opinion, there was no such thing as being too prepared, particularly with the foundation year exams due in June.
雖然這時候還早，但他們四人已經決定今年重新召開學習小組，以便完成NEWTs的第一階段。期末考試還有一年多，但在雷姆斯和莉莉看來，沒有準備過頭的事，特別是基礎年考試將於六月到來。

“I’m knackered,” Mary said, as they approached the portrait of the fat lady (her wig had been removed by Professor Flitwick only a few days beforehand - she had apparently grown quite fond of it). “Day off, tomorrow?”
“我累壞了，”瑪麗說，當他們接近胖夫人的畫像（她的假髮在幾天前被弗立維克教授取下了——她顯然對那假髮頗有感情）。“明天休息一天？”

“If you want,” Remus said, catching her yawn, “I said I’d do a big study group on Sunday, so I’d be glad of the rest.”
“如果你想的話，”雷姆斯說，捕捉到她的哈欠，“我說過我會在週日做一個大的學習小組，所以我會很高興休息一下。”

“I don’t know how you do it, Lupin,” Mary shook her head in disbelief. “That’s perfect, though, leaves Saturday evening free.”
“我不知道你是怎麼做到的，盧平，”瑪麗搖頭表示不信。“不過這樣很好，星期六晚上可以空出來。”

“Got another date with Roman, have you?” Marlene asked, sounding a bit annoyed.
“又和羅曼約會了嗎？”瑪琳問，聽起來有點生氣。

“Yes, Marlene,” Mary rolled her eyes, “Despite your very apparent disapproval…”
“是的，瑪琳，”瑪麗翻了翻白眼，“儘管你非常明顯地不贊成……”

“I just think you ought to slow down, that’s all!” Marlene snapped, running her fingers through her hair again.
“我只是覺得你應該慢下來，就是這樣！”瑪琳咬牙切齒地說，再次把手指梳過頭髮。

“Well, as we’ve discussed before, it’s none of your business who I go out with, is it?!” Mary said, arching an eyebrow at her friend. Marlene had turned an uncharacteristic shade of hot pink, and was looking at the floor. Remus looked at both girls in surprise. He’d never seen them talk like that to each other before - usually they were the best of friends.
“好吧，正如我們之前討論過的，我和誰約會和你無關，不是嗎？！”瑪麗對她的朋友挑了挑眉。瑪琳的臉紅得異常，低頭看著地板。雷姆斯驚訝地看著兩個女孩。他從未見過她們這樣互相對話——通常她們是最好的朋友。

“Come on, we’re all tired,” Lily said, pushing forward, “ Blatherskite ,” she addressed the fat lady, who moved aside so they could all enter.
“來吧，我們都累了，”莉莉說，向前推，“胡說八道，”她對胖夫人說，胖夫人讓開了，他們都能進去。

“Evans!” James’s shout met them even before they were halfway through.
“埃文斯！”詹姆斯的叫聲在他們還沒走到一半時就迎接了他們。

“Yeah yeah, good evening, Potter,” Lily sighed, shaking her head. Remus caught her tiny smile, though she tried to cover it behind her long hair.
“是的，是的，晚上好，波特，”莉莉嘆了口氣，搖了搖頭。雷姆斯看到她微小的笑容，儘管她試圖用長髮遮掩。

“And Moony!” James continued, “Where are you been?”
“還有莫妮！”詹姆斯繼續說，“你去哪了？”

“Making furious love to us all, obviously,” Mary said, deadpan, pushing Sirius aside to sit nearest the fireplace.
“顯然是在和我們所有人激情做愛，”瑪麗冷冷地說，推開天狼星坐在離壁爐最近的位置。

“It’s true,” Lily grinned, sitting on the hearth rug, “He’s a stallion.”
“這是真的，”莉莉笑著說，坐在壁爐地毯上，“他是匹種馬。”

“It took all three of us to satisfy him!” Marlene piped up, looking a little bit happier.
“我們三個人都要一起才能滿足他！”瑪琳插話說，看起來有點高興。

“Oh my god, please shut up…” Remus groaned, taking his seat in his usual armchair. “We were in the library, as if you didn’t know.”
“哦，我的天啊，請閉嘴……”雷姆斯呻吟道，坐在他平常的扶手椅上。“我們在圖書館裡，難道你們不知道嗎。”

“Ah, of course,” James winked at him. “Say no more, Casanova.”
“啊，當然，”詹姆斯對他眨了眨眼。“別再說了，卡薩諾瓦。”

“Brr.” Mary held her hands up to the fire, “This castle is freezing.”
“哆嗦。”瑪麗把手伸向火爐，“這個城堡冷得要命。”

“ Scotland is freezing.” Sirius replied, monotonously. He was levitating a paper plane lazily about the room, slouched down in his chair.
“蘇格蘭很冷。”天狼星單調地回答。他懶洋洋地在房間裡懸浮著一架紙飛機，靠在椅子上。

“It’s only March,” Lily said, perkily, “It’ll start warming up soon enough. I can’t wait for the summer.”
“現在才三月，”莉莉愉快地說，“很快就會開始變暖了。我迫不及待想迎接夏天。”

“Nah, then I’ll be too hot,” Mary sighed, “Our flat is ridiculous, even if you open all the windows. S’pose I can do magic this year, though – am I allowed to if my family are muggles?”
“不，到了夏天我會太熱，”瑪麗嘆了口氣，“我們的公寓真是太糟糕了，即使你打開所有窗戶也是如此。不過我想今年我可以施魔法——如果我的家人是麻瓜，我允許這樣做嗎？”

“Oh, I do,” Lily said, biting her lip, “Are we not supposed to?”
“哦，我知道，”莉莉說，咬著嘴唇，“我們不是不應該這樣做嗎？”

“Why don’t you come and stay with me, Mary?” Marlene said, “More room at our house, it’s cooler.”
“為什麼不來我這裡住呢，瑪麗？”瑪琳說，“我們家有更多的空間，更涼爽。”

“Well I wouldn’t mind a holiday,” Mary mused, still rubbing her hands. “Haven’t had once since dad lost his job. We used to go to the seaside every year. Margate or Skegness.”
“嗯，我不介意休個假，”瑪麗沉思著，仍然擦著手。“自從爸爸失業以來就沒有度假過。我們以前每年都去海邊。馬格特或斯基根斯。”

“Ooh, I went to Cornwall last year,” Lily said, “It was lovely, we camped right near the beach.”
“哦，我去年去了康沃爾，”莉莉說，“那裡很美，我們就露營在海灘旁邊。”

“Camping again.” Sirius grumbled. “Don’t get Potter started…”
“又是露營。”天狼星嘟囔道。“別讓波特開始說了……”

“Evans, have I ever told you how much love camping?” James said, grinning madly from his position at the mantelpiece. He was fiddling with his golden snitch, tossing it from palm to palm, “It is one of my greatest pleasures in life.”
“埃文斯，我曾經告訴過你我多麼喜歡露營嗎？”詹姆斯說，從壁爐架上的位置瘋狂地笑著。他在玩弄他的金色飛賊，把它在手掌間擲來擲去，“這是我生活中最大的樂趣之一。”

“I’m talking about muggle camping, Potter,” Lily tutted, smoothing her skirt over her knees self-consciously, “In muggle tents – no fancy extension charms…”
“我說的是麻瓜露營，波特，”莉莉嘟囔道，自覺地把裙子抹平在膝蓋上，“在麻瓜帳篷裡——沒有華麗的擴展咒語……”

“Can’t be that different,” James replied, undeterred, “These two haven’t even been camping,” he nodded to Remus and Sirius.
“應該沒那麼不同，”詹姆斯回答道，毫不受阻，“這兩個人甚至都沒有露營過，”他對雷姆斯和天狼星點了點頭。

“We sort of did, over Christmas,” Remus said, throwing a daring glance at Sirius, who gave him a slow, conspiratorial smile.
“我們算是有過，聖誕節時，”雷姆斯說，向天狼星投去挑戰性的目光，天狼星給了他一個緩慢的陰謀微笑。

“Hey!” James said, suddenly, tossing the snitch high in the air, then reaching to snatch it back, “We should all go camping!”
“嘿！”詹姆斯突然說，將飛賊高高拋起，然後伸手去抓回來，“我們應該都去露營！”

“What?” Sirius said, sitting up.
“什麼？”天狼星說，坐直了身子。

“This summer!” James nodded, excited, “It’s our last summer before we all have to be grownups – and we’ll all be of age, we should do it!”
“這個夏天！”詹姆斯點頭，激動地說，“這是我們在成為成年人之前的最後一個夏天——而且我們都會成年，我們應該去！”

“All of us?” Marlene asked, eyeing Mary.
“我們所有人？”瑪琳問，瞄了一眼瑪麗。

“All of us,” James confirmed. “What’d you think, Evans?”
“我們所有人，”詹姆斯確認說。“你覺得怎麼樣，埃文斯？”

“Well…” Lily looked up at him, “Separate tents for boys and girls, right?”
“嗯……”莉莉抬頭看著他，“男孩和女孩要分開帳篷，對吧？”

“Pfft, you’re no fun.” Mary smirked. Lily kicked her from the floor, and continued,
“噗，你真沒趣。”瑪麗冷笑著。莉莉從地上踢了她一下，繼續說道，

“Ok, Potter – on one condition…”
“好吧，波特——有一個條件……”

“Anything!”
“任何事！”

“Muggle tents.”
“麻瓜帳篷。”

“Oh.”
“哦。”

 

 

Saturday 5th March 1977

If you are seventeen years of age, or will turn seventeen on or before the 31st of August 1977, you are eligible for a twelve-week course of Apparition Lessons from a Ministry of Magic Apparition instructor, beginning on Monday 4th April 1977.
如果你已經十七歲，或者在1977年8月31日之前將滿十七歲，你有資格參加一個由魔法部幻影移形講師授課的為期十二周的課程，將於1977年4月4日星期一開始。

Please sign below if you would like to participate.
如欲參加，請在下方簽名。

Cost: 12 Galleons.
費用：12加隆。

Remus stared up at the notice pinned to the Gryffindor notice board and sighed.
雷姆斯抬頭看著釘在格蘭芬多公告板上的通知，嘆了口氣。

“I’ll lend you the money,” Sirius said, at his shoulder.
“我會借錢給你，”天狼星在他肩膀上說。

“I’d rather you didn’t.”
“我希望你不要。”

“Remus, I’m ridiculously rich.”
“雷姆斯，我非常富有。”

“I’m quite aware of that.” He snapped, irritably. He looked at the board again. Remus had wanted to learn how to apparate for almost his entire time at Hogwarts. “Ok.” He nodded, “But I’ll pay you back. I really will.”
“我完全知道。”他不耐煩地說。他再次看了看公告板。雷姆斯在霍格華茲的幾乎整段時間裡都想學習幻影移形。“好吧。”他點了點頭，“但我會還你的。我真的會的。”

“I know,” Sirius nudged him with his hip, playfully. “You’re going to be making more money than any of us, one day, you big swot.”
“我知道，”天狼星用臀部輕輕撞了撞他，調皮地說，“總有一天你會賺比我們任何人都多的錢，你這個書呆子。”

“Ha.” Remus snorted. “Not likely, unless Dumbledore gets his act together.”
“哈。”雷姆斯嗤之以鼻。“不太可能，除非鄧不利多能振作起來。”

“Dumbledore? What’s he got to do with anything?”
“鄧不利多？他和這有什麼關係？”

Remus looked around, furtively. The common room wasn’t busy, but it wasn’t empty either.
雷姆斯四下張望，偷偷摸摸地。公共休息室不擁擠，但也不空曠。

“I can’t tell you here,” he said, “Upstairs?”
“我不能在這裡告訴你，”他說，“樓上？”

Sirius cocked his head, with a mock innocent expression that made Remus burst out laughing,
天狼星歪著頭，露出一副假裝無辜的表情，讓雷姆斯忍不住笑了出來，

“Not for that. Get your mind out of the gutter, Black.”
“不是那個。別想那些不正經的事，天狼星。”

They headed up to the bedroom. It was nice and quiet there – Peter was serving a detention somewhere with Filch and James was patrolling.
他們上了樓去到臥室。那裡安靜得很好——彼得在某處和費爾奇一起接受拘留，詹姆斯正在巡邏。

“So?” Sirius went straight for Remus’s bed, sitting cross-legged and alert, “What’s going on with Dumbledore?”
“那麼？”天狼星直奔雷姆斯的床，盤腿坐下，警覺地問道，“鄧不利多怎麼了？”

Remus sat down opposite him, not too close.
雷姆斯坐在他對面，保持著一定的距離。

“I… remember I had that dinner with Ferox? After I met Livia.”
“我……記得我和費羅克斯吃過晚餐？在我遇見莉維亞之後。”

“...yeah, of course.” Sirius sobered up at once. They hadn’t discussed it, since they’d made up.
“……是的，當然。”天狼星立刻變得嚴肅。他們自從和好後就沒有再討論這個問題。

“Ok, well don’t get angry with me, but… I sort of made some demands. On Dumbledore.”
“好吧，不要對我生氣，但……我有點提出了一些要求。對鄧不利多的要求。”

Sirius stared at him, blankly. Remus continued, with a hard swallow, “I told him that if they want me to help them, if they want me to be like an emissary to the werewolves, or whatever, then I wanted something in return. Protection, for the others in Greyback’s pack, first of all,”
天狼星呆呆地盯著他。雷姆斯吞了口唾沫，繼續說：“我告訴他，如果他們想讓我幫助他們，如果他們想讓我像一個使者一樣對待狼人，或者其他什麼，那麼我希望得到一些回報。首先是保護灰背狼群中的其他人。”

Sirius opened his mouth, then – apparently thinking better of it – closed it again, and waited. Remus carried on, watching him carefully for any sign of anger or disapproval, “And I’ve asked not to be forced to sign the register, on my birthday.”
天狼星張開嘴巴，然後——顯然覺得不妥——又關上了，等待著。雷姆斯繼續說，仔細觀察他的臉上是否有憤怒或不滿的跡象，“我還要求不要在我生日那天被迫簽名。”

“Well, that’s reasonable, at least,” Sirius breathed. “But, Moony… the other thing…”
“嗯，至少這是合理的，”天狼星喘了口氣。“但，莫妮……另一件事……”

“I know,” Remus nodded, “They’re murderers, some of them. I know that. But they’re… I don’t think they know any other way. I think that if we want to show them that there are other choices, better ways to live, then… that has to start with kindness.”
“我知道，”雷姆斯點了點頭，“他們是殺人犯，其中一些。我知道這一點。但他們……我不認為他們知道其他的生活方式。我認為如果我們想向他們展示其他的選擇，更好的生活方式，那麼……這必須從善意開始。”

“Kindness.” Sirius repeated.
“善意。”天狼星重複道。

“Not forgiveness,” Remus said, quickly, “I’m not saying they should go completely unpunished, but… I mean, you have to admit, the ministry has handled lycanthropy pretty poorly, so far. When we win this war, there’s a chance to make things better. For all wizards. Even half-breeds.”
“不是寬恕，”雷姆斯迅速說，“我不是說他們應該完全不受懲罰，但……我的意思是，你必須承認，到目前為止，魔法部對待狼人症的方式非常糟糕。當我們贏得這場戰爭時，有機會改善現狀。對所有巫師來說。甚至是混血種。”

天狼星看著他，眉頭微微皺起。他那深藍色的眼睛專注地凝視著，就像在尋找雷姆斯臉上的某些東西。然後他微微點了點頭。

“Yes.” Remus said, without missing a beat.
“是的。”雷姆斯說，毫不猶豫。

“You’ll have to convince a lot of people.”
“你得說服很多人。”

Remus nodded.
雷姆斯點了點頭。

“I know.”
“我知道。”

“We’ll help you, though.” Sirius said, not breaking eye contact. “Me and Peter and James – Evans too, probably, that girl worships you.”
“我們會幫助你的。”天狼星說，沒有打破眼神交流。“我、彼得和詹姆斯——還有埃文斯，可能，那女孩崇拜你。”

“You don’t need to,” Sirius shook his head. He leaned forward and kissed Remus so, so gently on the lips, barely a whisper. “Anything for our Moony.”
“你不需要，”天狼星搖了搖頭。他向前傾身，輕輕地吻了雷姆斯的嘴唇，幾乎是耳語般的親吻。“為我們的莫妮做任何事。”

Later that day, Remus was on his way to Flitwick’s classroom – the kindly Charms professor had allowed him to use it for his tutoring sessions, provided everything was tidied up afterwards. He had a map of the south coast in his bag, and was hoping to get there early enough to have the chance to study it. If they were all going on holiday that summer, then someone was going to have to organise it.
當天稍晚，雷姆斯正前往弗立維教授的教室——那位和藹的咒語教授允許他使用教室進行輔導，只要一切在之後整理好。他的包裡有一張南海岸的地圖，希望能夠早點到達，爭取時間研究它。如果他們這個夏天都去度假，那麼就需要有人來組織這件事。

The first full moon of the summer would fall on the first of July, and Remus was hoping to stay one extra night at Hogwarts for that. He had already asked James if he could stay with the Potters for the following week, and James, of course, had eagerly agreed. Then they would have the camping trip, and then… Remus didn’t have a clue what his next move would be. Back to Mile End, maybe; if Grant was still there. He couldn’t just stay at the Potters forever; not once he was seventeen.
夏天的第一次滿月會落在七月一日，雷姆斯希望能在霍格華茲多待一晚。他已經問過詹姆斯是否可以在接下來的一周住在波特家，詹姆斯當然欣然同意。然後他們將去露營旅行，然後……雷姆斯不知道自己的下一步會是什麼。也許回到邁爾恩德；如果格蘭特還在那裡。他不能永遠待在波特家；十七歲以後就不行了。

“Hiya Remus!” Christopher waved, already waiting outside the classroom. Remus’s heart sank, slightly. Of course Christopher was early. He never missed a chance to catch Remus alone.
“嗨，雷姆斯！”克里斯多夫揮手，已經在教室外面等著了。雷姆斯的心情稍微沉了下來。當然，克里斯多夫早到了。他從不會錯過單獨抓住雷姆斯的機會。

“Morning, Chris,” he smiled, politely. “Shall we go in?”
“早安，克里斯，”他禮貌地微笑著。“我們進去吧？”

They charmed the desks into a horseshoe shape, so that there would be plenty of room for practical demonstrations, then settled down, pulling out their books.
他們將桌子施了魔法，變成馬蹄形，這樣就有足夠的空間進行實踐演示，然後坐下來，拿出書籍。

“What are you doing after?” Christopher asked, over keen.
“你之後要做什麼？”克里斯多夫過於熱切地問道。

“Dinner.” Remus said, mildly, smoothing down his map and locating Cornwall. “Then detention, I’m afraid. ‘til late.” It was a full moon – though he’d be in detention even if it wasn’t. McGonagall never went back on a punishment.
“晚餐。”雷姆斯輕描淡寫地說，抹平他的地圖，找到康沃爾。“然後是拘留，我恐怕要待到很晚。”那天是滿月——即使不是，他也會被拘留。麥格教授從不會撤回懲罰。

“That’s a shame,” Christopher sighed, “You’re always in detention these days.”
“那真可惜，”克里斯多夫嘆了口氣，“你最近總是被拘留。”

“Yep,” Remus laughed, “I’m a no-good yob.”
“是的，”雷姆斯笑著說，“我是一個無用的混混。”

Christopher laughed, awkwardly. He meant well enough, but Remus had the impression that he was rarely comfortable with marauder style humour. It took getting used to.
克里斯多夫尷尬地笑了。他的好意很好，但雷姆斯覺得他很少能適應潑辣的幽默。這需要時間適應。

“Have you read this?” Christopher pushed a book across the desk, covering up the beach Remus had been inspecting. He sighed and looked at it. The Charioteer.
“你讀過這本書嗎？”克里斯多夫把一本書推到桌子上，遮住了雷姆斯剛才查看的海灘。他嘆了口氣，看了看它。《戰車手》。

“Nope,” Remus shook his head, picking it up and reading the blurb.
“沒有，”雷姆斯搖了搖頭，拿起書來閱讀封面介紹。

After an injury at Dunkirk, Laurie Odell is sent to a veterans' hospital to convalesce. There he befriends Andrew, a conscientious objector serving as an orderly. But when Ralph, a mentor from his school days, reappears in his life, Laurie is forced to choose between the sweet ideals of innocence and the distinct pleasures of experience.
在敦刻爾克受傷後，勞瑞·奧德爾被送到一個退伍軍人醫院康復。在那裡，他與安德魯——一名擔任醫務兵的良心拒絕者——成為朋友。然而，當他的學校時代的導師拉爾夫重新出現時，勞瑞被迫在純真的甜美理想和經驗的明確快感之間做出選擇。

“Oh,” Remus thought. It’s that sort of book.
“哦，”雷姆斯心想。原來是那種書。

“It’s a muggle book,” Christopher explained, excitedly, “It’s really good. You can borrow it, I’d love to know what you think!”
“這是一本麻瓜書，”克里斯多夫興奮地解釋道，“真的很好。你可以借來看，我很想知道你的看法！”

“Yeah, I’ll give it a go, cheers.” Remus nodded, quickly hiding it in the bottom of his bag before anyone else came in.
“好吧，我會試試看的，謝謝。”雷姆斯點了點頭，迅速將它藏在包底下，免得其他人進來。

At that moment, there was a knock at the door. Both boys turned around to see Emmeline Vance poke her head around the door. She was an immensely beautiful girl, with a tumble of golden curls and large apple green eyes. Another Ravenclaw, she was a seventh year too, and had previously gone out with Roman Rotherhide himself. She smiled, stepping in,
這時，門被敲了敲。兩個男孩轉過身來，只見艾梅琳·萬斯探頭進來。她是一位非常美麗的女孩，有著一頭金色的卷髮和一雙大大的蘋果綠眼睛。她也是一名七年級的拉文克勳，曾經和羅曼·羅瑟哈德約會過。她笑著走了進來，

“Hello, Remus,” she said, in her soft, girlish voice. He tried to be polite back, but he knew he sounded cold.
“你好，雷姆斯，”她用柔和的女孩聲音說。他試著禮貌地回應，但知道自己聽起來有些冷淡。

“Hello Emmeline. I didn’t expect you.”
“你好，艾梅琳。我沒想到你會來。”

“Oh, no, I’m not here for your little study club thing,” she smiled again, scrunching up her nose in a way that might have seemed cute or endearing to anyone but Remus and Christopher. “I was hoping Sirius would be here.”
“哦，不，我不是來參加你的學習小組的，”她再次微笑，皺起鼻子，這對任何人來說都可能顯得可愛或迷人，只是對雷姆斯和克里斯多夫來說不然。“我希望天狼星在這裡。”

“He isn’t.”
“他不在。”

“No, I see that!” She laughed, throatily, sweeping her hair over one shoulder. “But he said he’d meet me in the Astronomy tower half an hour ago…”
“哦，我知道！”她輕笑著，將頭髮撩到一邊。“但他說半小時前會在天文塔見我……”

Remus just shrugged at her, face blank. She tutted. “Well, if you see him, will you tell him to meet me tonight, after curfew?”
雷姆斯只是對她耸耸肩，面無表情。她噓了一聲。“如果你見到他，能告訴他今晚，宵禁後，來見我嗎？”

“He’s busy tonight.”
“他今晚很忙。”

“Doing what?! Ugh, he’s not seeing that MacDonald girl again, is he?”
“做什麼？！唉，他是不是又去見那個麥當勞女孩了？”

“You never know with Sirius,” Remus said, cruelly, trying not to smirk.
“你永遠不知道天狼星在幹什麼，”雷姆斯冷酷地說，試圖不露出笑意。

“Well. You tell him that if he’s not careful he’s going to lose me!”
“好吧。你告訴他，如果他不小心，他會失去我！”

“Oh, I definitely will.”
“哦，我一定會告訴他的。”

She closed the door, and Remus snorted, shaking his head.
她關上門，雷姆斯哼了一聲，搖了搖頭。

“Do you actually know where he is?” Christopher asked, with a small frown.
“你真的知道他在哪裡嗎？”克里斯多夫小皺著眉問。

“Nah,” Remus replied, “But I could guess. He’s probably with James somewhere.”
“嗯，”雷姆斯回答，“但我可以猜猜。他可能在某個地方和詹姆斯一起。”

“Those two.” Christopher sighed, “They’re funny, sometimes, but they cause so much trouble. How on earth Potter managed to end up a prefect I have no idea. And Black, he’s just…”
“那兩個。”克里斯多夫嘆了口氣，“他們有時候很有趣，但也帶來了很多麻煩。我真不知道波特是怎麼成為級長的。而天狼星，他只是……”

“He’s just what?!” Remus said, sharply.
“他只是什麼？！”雷姆斯尖銳地問道。

Christopher blinked, startled.
克里斯多夫眨了眨眼，驚訝地看著他。

“I know he’s your friend! Sorry, I just meant… he’s an arrogant tosser sometimes.”
“我知道他是你的朋友！對不起，我只是想說……他有時候是個傲慢的傢伙。”

“Yeah,” Remus nodded, loosening up. He thought about Sirius’s promise, made little more than an hour ago on Remus’s bed. If other people couldn’t see that Sirius, then it was their loss. Who were Emmeline and Christopher in the grand scheme of things?
“是的，”雷姆斯點了點頭，放鬆了些。他想起了天狼星在雷姆斯床上許下的承諾。如果其他人看不到那個天狼星，那是他們的損失。在宏觀的格局中，艾梅琳和克里斯多夫算什麼？

Not marauders; not important.
不是麻瓜，不重要。

“You’re not wrong." Remus shrugged. "Right, where do you want to start?”
“你說得沒錯。”雷姆斯耸了耸肩。“好了，你想從哪裡開始？”

 

Chapter 110: Sixth Year: Seventeen 

Thursday 10th March 1977

1977年3月10日，星期四

“HAPPY BIRTHDAY, REMU!”

“生日快樂，雷姆！”

Three gangly, noisy, highly excitable teenage boys jumped onto Remus’s bed at the crack of dawn. It was not the same as when they were eleven. For one thing, Remus’s legs were a lot longer; for another, they were all much heavier.

黎明時分，三個瘦高、吵鬧、非常興奮的少年跳上了雷姆斯的床。這與他們十一歲時不同。首先，雷姆斯的腿長了很多；其次，他們都重了很多。

“Gerroff you wankers,” Remus grumbled, “What time is it?”

“你們這些混蛋滾開，”雷姆斯咕噥道，“現在幾點了？”

“Time is immaterial,” James said, wearing a brightly coloured pointed party hat, “It’s your birthday.”

“時間不重要，”詹姆斯戴著一頂色彩鮮艷的尖頂派對帽說道，“今天是你的生日。”

“Your seventeenth birthday!” Sirius added, wearing a polka dot party hat at a rakish angle on his head.

“你的十七歲生日！”天狼星補充道，他戴著一頂斜斜的波點派對帽。

“You’re of age!” Peter said, lunging at Remus with a fourth hat, snapping the elastic under his chin.

“你成年了！”彼得說著，猛撲向雷姆斯，給他戴上第四頂帽子，彈性帶卡在下巴下。

Remus glared at them all, stony faced.

雷姆斯怒視著他們，面無表情。

“You’re going to make me wear this all day, aren’t you?”

“你們打算讓我戴這個一整天，是嗎？”

They nodded, all three, in perfect unison, the streamers on their conical headwear bobbing and flashing in the dull morning light.

他們三個齊刷刷地點頭，錐形帽上的彩帶在昏暗的晨光中搖曳閃爍。

“It’s impervious to water,” Sirius explained cheerfully, “So you can even shower with it on.” He winked, and Remus hoped he wasn’t blushing. Sirius had been in his bed only hours before, for a very different reason, and Remus was finding the quick transitions harder and harder to deal with.

“它防水，”天狼星快活地解釋道，“所以你甚至可以戴著它洗澡。”他眨了眨眼，雷姆斯希望自己沒有臉紅。天狼星幾個小時前還在他的床上，出於完全不同的原因，而雷姆斯發現這種快速轉換越來越難以應付。

Only half an hour later, and Remus had showered (hat still firmly on his head), opened about fifty birthday cards wishing him many happy returns (“I didn’t think I knew fifty people!”) and eaten a generous slice of Mrs Potter’s chocolate cake.

僅僅半小時後，雷姆斯就洗完了澡（帽子依然牢牢戴在頭上），打開了大約五十張生日賀卡，祝他幸福多多（“我都沒想到我認識五十個人！”），並吃了一大塊波特夫人的巧克力蛋糕。

“And you’ll get your proper present later,” James said, cryptically, “At the party.”

“你會在晚些時候得到你的正式禮物，”詹姆斯神秘地說，“在派對上。”

“You lot are mad,” Remus said, as they filed down into the common room, “You shouldn’t go to all this trouble.”

“你們這些人真瘋了，”雷姆斯說，當他們排隊走進休息室時，“你們不應該這麼費心。”

“Shut up, Moony.” Peter said, good naturedly.

“閉嘴，莫妮。”彼得善意地說。

“Happy birthday Remus!” The girls chorused in the dining hall. They were all wearing party hats too, apparently thanks to Lily’s persuasiveness.

“生日快樂，雷姆斯！”女孩們在餐廳裡齊聲說道。她們也都戴著派對帽，顯然是由於莉莉的說服力。

“Nice one, Evans,” James winked at her, giving her a sly nod with his elbow, “New you wouldn’t let the side down.”

“幹得好，埃文斯，”詹姆斯向她眨了眨眼，用肘部狡黠地點了點頭，“知道你不會讓我們失望。”

“Oh, bugger off, Potter,” she elbowed him back, looking very pleased and a bit flushed.

“哦，滾開，波特，”她用肘部回擊他，看起來很高興，有點臉紅。

The usual three round rendition of ‘Happy Birthday’ accompanied Remus’s birthday breakfast, and he was so used to it by now that he even stood up and gave a shy bow once they’d finally finished. Then the owls arrived.

三輪慣例的《生日快樂》伴隨著雷姆斯的生日早餐，他現在已經習慣了，甚至在他們最終唱完後站起來害羞地鞠了一躬。然後貓頭鷹們到了。

There was a card from Ferox, which was unexpected - Remus hadn’t been sure if they were still on speaking terms after their last meeting. There was also a note from Dumbledore.

有一張來自Ferox的賀卡，這很意外——雷姆斯不確定他們在上次見面後是否還能說上話。還有一張來自鄧布利多的便條。

He cracked the cherry red seal quickly under the table, and read it as fast as possible.

他迅速在桌下打開鮮紅色的封印，盡快讀了起來。

 

Mr Lupin,

盧平先生，

Many happy returns for the day.

祝你今天幸福多多。

I understand we have a few things to discuss. Please present yourself at the headmaster’s office at 4pm this afternoon.

我知道我們有幾件事要討論。請在今天下午四點到校長辦公室。

Sincerely,

此致

Albus Dumbledore.

阿不思·鄧布利多

 

 

“Here we go.” He sighed, under his breath. Sirius, who had an annoying habit of reading over his shoulder, leaned in,

“來了。”他低聲嘆道。天狼星有個惹人厭的習慣，就是在他肩膀上讀信，這時也靠了過來，

“Do you want someone to go with you?”

“你想要有人陪你去嗎？”

Remus shook his head, but smiled at Sirius, trying to be kind,

雷姆斯搖了搖頭，但對天狼星笑了笑，試圖友善一些，

“Nah. Thanks for offering, but I think it’s better if I do it alone.”

“不用了。謝謝你的提議，但我覺得我一個人去更好。”

Sirius nodded, looking troubled all the same.

天狼星點了點頭，依然顯得有些擔心。

The day passed slowly, the meeting with Dumbledore lurking at the end of it like some malevolent spider. Remus tried imagining the scenario over in his head – coming up with a script, or at least something coherent to say in defence of his wild demands. Nothing came to him, and at 3.45pm that afternoon he found himself walking to the headmaster's office very slowly indeed.

這一天過得很慢，與鄧布利多的會面像一隻惡毒的蜘蛛一樣潛伏在一天的結尾。雷姆斯試圖在腦海中想像那個場景——編寫一個劇本，或者至少說出一些連貫的話來為他的狂野要求辯護。但什麼也沒想到，當天下午3:45，他發現自己確實非常緩慢地走向校長辦公室。

He’d been mad to even suggest this in the first place. No one else needed as reason to help in the war effort – James would never do it. But then, Remus supposed, there was nothing James wanted that Dumbledore could give him. Unless Dumbledore held the key to Lily Evans’s undying love.

他當初提出這個建議真是瘋了。沒有人需要這個理由來幫助戰爭努力——詹姆斯永遠不會這樣做。但雷姆斯想，鄧布利多沒有什麼可以給詹姆斯的東西。除非鄧布利多掌握了莉莉·埃文斯不朽愛情的鑰匙。

He found the staircase already open, and ascended just as slowly, remembering only at the very last minute to rip the party hat from his head.

他發現樓梯已經開了，於是也同樣緩慢地上去，直到最後一刻才想起把派對帽從頭上摘下來。

“Good afternoon, Mr Lupin. Happy birthday.”

“下午好，盧平先生。生日快樂。”

Dumbledore was sitting at his desk, as usual. This time he wasn’t writing letters; he was waiting patiently, a benign smile on his face.

鄧布利多像往常一樣坐在他的桌子旁。這次他沒有寫信；他耐心地等待著，臉上帶著仁慈的微笑。

“Thanks,” Remus replied, warily, sitting down in the chair opposite. He thought for a moment before saying, “D’you mind just calling me Remus?”

“謝謝，”雷姆斯警惕地回答，坐在對面的椅子上。他想了一會兒，然後說：“你介意只叫我雷姆斯嗎？”

“As you wish,” Dumbledore nodded. He seemed to be in good humour. “How does it feel, coming of age?”

“如你所願，”鄧布利多點了點頭。他似乎心情很好。“成年感覺如何？”

“It’s ok.”

“還好。”

“I have a few things for you, sent on to me from Mrs Orwell.”

“我有一些東西要給你，奧威爾夫人寄給我的。”

“Matron?!”

“護士長？！”

“Indeed.” Dumbledore gestured at a shoebox, which seemed to have appeared on the large mahogany desk out on thin air. “I believe there are a few items in there which belong to you, which were held in trust at St Edmund’s.”

“的確。”鄧布利多指著一個鞋盒，它似乎憑空出現在大紅木桌上。“我相信裡面有幾件屬於你的東西，這些東西在聖埃德蒙德托管。”

“Oh, wow…” Remus touched the lid of the box, tentatively, but didn’t open it. He wanted to be alone for that.

“哦，哇……”雷姆斯試探性地觸摸著盒子的蓋子，但沒有打開。他想一個人看。

“There is also that matter of your inheritance.”

“還有你的遺產問題。”

“My what?!”

“我的什麼？！”

“Your father left a will. He left some provisions for your mother, and the rest to you. He was not a wealthy man, I should say, but nevertheless, his vault in Gringott’s now belongs to you.” Dumbledore pulled a key from his pocket and passed it across the desk.

“你父親留下了遺囑。他為你的母親留下了一些物資，剩下的給你。他不是一個富有的人，我應該說，但無論如何，他在古靈閣的金庫現在屬於你。”鄧布利多從口袋裡掏出一把鑰匙，遞過桌子。

Remus held it in his hand, and thought about Lyall – who had not been on his mind in some months.

雷姆斯把它握在手中，想起了萊爾——他已經有幾個月沒想到他了。

“Thank you.” He said, remembering his manners.

“謝謝。”他說，記起了禮貌。

“And there are other legal matters, as well you know.” Dumbledore clasped his hands in front of him, long slender fingers intertwined. He was waiting for a response.

“還有其他法律問題，你也知道的。”鄧布利多把雙手握在胸前，細長的手指交叉。他在等待回應。

“The register.” Remus said.

“登記簿。”雷姆斯說。

“The register.” The headmaster agreed. He pulled out a piece of parchment and pushed that across the desk too. It was a form.

“登記簿。”校長同意。他抽出一張羊皮紙，也推過桌子。那是一張表格。

 

Ministry of Magic: Declaration of Lycanthropic Infection.

魔法部：狼人的感染聲明。

 

Remus felt queasy. There was a dotted line at the bottom, awaiting his signature. He sat on his hands and looked at Dumbledore.

雷姆斯感到噁心。底部有一條虛線，等待他的簽名。他坐在手上，看著鄧布利多。

“What do you want me to do with it?”

“你想讓我怎麼處理這個？”

“Leo Ferox led me to believe that you already had a very good idea of what to do with it, Remus.” The old man replied, his eyes serious. “You are an adult, I leave it in your hands.”

“Leo Ferox讓我相信你已經有很好的想法如何處理它，雷姆斯。”老人回答，眼神嚴肅。“你已經是個成年人了，我把它交到你手裡。”

Remus picked up the parchment immediately, held it up to eye level and tore it clean in two. Dumbledore smiled again. “Admirably done.”

雷姆斯立刻拿起羊皮紙，舉到眼前，撕成兩半。鄧布利多再次微笑。“做得很好。”

“Ferox told you something else, though.” Remus said, trying to maintain eye contact but finding it extremely difficult. Dumbledore was not like anyone else - he smelled just as strongly of magic as every other witch or wizard, but nothing else. He had no unique signifier at all.

“但是Ferox還告訴了你其他事情。”雷姆斯說，試圖保持眼神接觸，但發現極其困難。鄧布利多不像其他人——他和其他巫師一樣散發著強烈的魔法氣息，但除此之外什麼也沒有。他根本沒有任何獨特的標誌。

“He did. I think, perhaps, you can anticipate my response.”

“他確實告訴我了。我想，也許你能預料到我的回應。”

Remus felt something deflate inside of him, making room for the coming rage.

雷姆斯感覺內心有什麼東西泄氣了，為即將到來的憤怒騰出空間。

“So it’s a no.” He said, flatly.

“所以是拒絕。”他平淡地說。

Dumbledore inclined his head, gently,

鄧布利多輕輕地點了點頭，

“Not entirely. A request for patience, perhaps.”

“不完全是。也許是要求耐心。”

“With respect,” Remus heard the hardness in his own voice, and it surprised him, but made him braver, “There isn’t time for patience.”

“恕我直言，”雷姆斯聽到了自己聲音中的硬度，這讓他感到驚訝，但也讓他更勇敢，“沒有時間耐心等待。”

“There never is, when one is young.” Dumbledore replied, softly. “Remus, I know how things must seem to you, believe me.”

“年輕時從來沒有時間。”鄧布利多輕聲回應。“雷姆斯，我知道事情在你眼裡是什麼樣的，相信我。”

“You didn’t see her. They’re suffering. Right now.”

“你沒見過她。他們正在受苦。現在就受苦。”

“Many people are suffering, Remus. You have spent precious little time in the wizarding world yet-“

“很多人都在受苦，雷姆斯。你在巫師界花的時間還很少——”

“Whose fault is that?!” Remus muttered fiercely. Dumbledore gave him a silencing glance,

He was going to have a good time if it killed him. Fuck Dumbledore. Fuck Greyback, Ferox, Livia, Emmeline and Sirius fucking Black. “你什麼時候開始在意了？”天狼星輕聲說，再次靠近。雷木斯迅速後退，把手按在天狼星的胸口，讓他保持距離。

“No, Sirius. What about Emmeline?”
“不，天狼星。那艾梅琳呢？”

Sirius shook his head dizzily, frowning.
天狼星暈頭轉向地搖頭，皺起眉頭。

“Fuck Emmeline!” He grunted. Remus rolled his eyes,
“去他的艾梅琳！”他咕噥著。雷木斯翻了個白眼，

“But you already do, don’t you, Black? That’s the problem.”
“但你已經這麼做了，不是嗎，布萊克？這就是問題所在。”

“So…” Sirius spoke slowly, mind foggy with drink, “We have to stop our… thing, just because of her?”
“所以…”天狼星慢慢說，因為喝酒腦子昏昏沉沉，“我們要因為她而停止我們的…事情嗎？”

“Our ‘thing’!? God, Sirius, you’re unbelievable.”
“我們的‘事情’！？天啊，天狼星，你真是不可思議。”

“What?!”
“什麼？！”

“Siiiiiiiriuuuuuuuus…” Emmeline’s tipsy voice echoed up the staircase, “Where are youuuuuu?”
“天狼星...”艾梅琳醉醺醺的聲音在樓梯上迴響，“你在哪兒啊？”

They both turned, looking down into the shadows.
他們都轉過身，看向陰影中的樓下。

“You’d better go to her.” Remus said, walking over to his bed. Sirius followed him like a lost puppy, pulling at the waistband of his pyjama bottoms needily.
“你最好去找她。”雷木斯說，走向他的床。天狼星像迷路的小狗一樣跟著他，需求地拉著他的睡褲腰帶。

“C’mon, just…”
“拜託，只是…”

“No!”
“不！”

“Siiiiriuuuuuuus…. I’m coming to get you!”
“天狼星...我來找你了！”

Remus pushed him away one last time,
雷木斯最後一次把他推開，

“Go on, I don’t want her up here!”
“快去，我不想她上來！”

Sirius stared at him for a bit longer, drink still blurring his reactions, making him slow and stupid.
天狼星盯著他看了一會兒，酒精仍然模糊著他的反應，讓他變得遲鈍而愚蠢。

“Ok, but I’ll come back… we can talk…”
“好吧，但我會回來的...我們可以談談…”

“No.” Remus said, again. “We’ve talked. It’s over. Goodnight, Sirius.”
“不。”雷木斯再次說。“我們已經談過了。結束了。晚安，天狼星。”

Chapter 111: Sixth Year: Separation 

Remus woke up the next morning with a hangover and an enormous sense of relief. He’d had to be drunk to do it, but it was done. No more jealousy, no more worrying, no more anxious questioning. The key now, he decided, was maintaining a distance, and building barriers.
雷木斯第二天早上醒來時，宿醉和巨大的解脫感一起襲來。他必須醉醺醺的才能做到，但終於完成了。不再有嫉妒、不再擔心、不再焦慮。現在的關鍵，他決定，是保持距離，並建立屏障。

By the time he had finished his shower on the morning after his seventeenth birthday, Remus had a plan of action. He would close the door on whatever his relationship with Sirius had been - it was fine to look upon Christmas as a fond memory, or to feel a little bit lonelier, a little less whole - but this was entirely necessary, both for his health and his sanity.
在他十七歲生日的第二天早晨，洗完澡後，雷木斯已經制定了一個行動計劃。他會關上與天狼星之間關係的大門——可以把聖誕節當作美好的回憶，或者感到有點孤單，有點不完整——但這是完全必要的，為了他的健康和理智。

Sirius was not the whole world, as much as he might seem it sometimes.
天狼星並不是整個世界，儘管有時候看起來像。

Remus had demonstrated this almost immediately. Upon exiting the bathroom, he bumped into James - who looked as though he hadn’t touched a drop of liquor the night before, despite having had just as much as everyone else. That infuriating Potter good fortune apparently applied to hangovers, too.
雷木斯幾乎立刻證明了這一點。走出浴室後，他撞見了詹姆斯——看起來他昨晚一滴酒都沒碰，儘管喝得和其他人一樣多。那令人惱火的波特好運顯然也適用於宿醉。

“Morning, Moony!” He grinned, rosy cheeked in his quidditch robes. Today was not a practice day, but why should that stop James? He raised his broom, “Fancy a spin around the pitch?” This was an old joke - he always asked, and Remus always pulled a face.
“早上好，月亮臉！”他咧嘴笑了笑，穿著魁地奇長袍，臉頰紅潤。今天不是訓練日，但這為什麼要阻止詹姆斯呢？他舉起掃帚，“想在球場上轉一圈嗎？”這是一個老笑話——他總是問，而雷木斯總是做鬼臉。

Remus glanced at the two made beds, and the two with the curtains still closed, where (presumably) Peter and Sirius were still fast asleep.
雷木斯瞥了一眼那兩張已經整理好的床，以及另外兩張床帷還拉著的床，彼得和天狼星還在熟睡。

“Yeah.” Remus said. “Go on, then.”
“好。”雷木斯說。“那就去吧。”

“Eh?!” James stopped in his tracks.
“啊？！”詹姆斯停下腳步。

Remus nodded, casually,
雷木斯隨意地點了點頭，

“I’ll go with you. I ought to get better at flying, might be useful when we finish school. I’ve got your old broom somewhere, let me dig it out…”
“我和你一起去。我應該學會更好地飛行，這在我們畢業後可能會有用。我有你的舊掃帚，讓我找找看...”

Credit to James, after his initial surprise he was all for the idea, and even held his tongue when he saw the state of Remus’s dusty, neglected broomstick. He simply offered to polish it, then led Remus down to the quidditch pitch jabbering about simple, basic exercises to ‘get your confidence up’.
詹姆斯值得稱讚，儘管他最初感到驚訝，但他完全贊成這個主意，甚至在看到雷木斯那把布滿灰塵、被忽視的掃帚狀態時也沒說什麼。他只是提出幫忙擦亮它，然後帶著雷木斯到魁地奇球場，喋喋不休地講述一些簡單的基本練習來“增強信心”。

And it wasn’t awful. James was a very patient teacher, and Remus felt in safe hands - the bespectacled boy didn’t even laugh after the third time he fell off. Afterwards, Remus felt he even understood James a little better. It was a very wholesome feeling, walking back to breakfast, hungry and aching and full of energy. This first experiment had gone so well, in fact, that Remus decided he would say yes to anything his friends asked of him from now on. In this way, he would keep himself busy until Sirius went back to being whatever he’d been before.
並沒有那麼糟糕。詹姆斯是一位非常耐心的老師，雷木斯感到很安全——這個戴眼鏡的男孩即使在他第三次摔下來之後也沒有笑。之後，雷木斯感覺他甚至更了解詹姆斯了一點。這是一種非常健康的感覺，走回去吃早餐時，飢餓、酸痛且充滿活力。事實上，這次初次嘗試進展得如此順利，雷木斯決定從現在起對朋友們的任何要求都說“好”。以這種方式，他會讓自己忙碌起來，直到天狼星恢復到之前的樣子。

At breakfast they were greeted by a row of red eyed, sickly-faced Gryffindors, all leaning sleepily on their elbows, Mary and Marlene sitting back to back, propping each other up.
在早餐時，他們遇到了一排眼睛紅紅、面色病態的格蘭芬多學生，個個睡眼惺忪地靠在桌上，瑪麗和瑪琳背靠背坐著，互相支撐著。

“Christ,” Mary squinted at James and Remus, “You’ve not been exercising?! Bloody lunatics.”
“天啊，”瑪麗瞇著眼看著詹姆斯和雷木斯，“你們沒有在運動吧？！瘋了吧。”

“You went, Moony?!” Sirius looked up, wincing and rubbing his apparently sore neck.
“你去了，月亮臉？！”天狼星抬起頭，皺著眉頭揉著顯然酸痛的脖子。

Remus just gave him a small shrug, then looked away. Sirius didn’t try to talk to him again.
雷木斯只是輕輕聳了聳肩，然後轉過頭去。天狼星再也沒有試圖和他說話。

They were halfway through the meal - Remus as usual eating half his bodyweight in fried bread, eggs, baked beans and bacon; everyone else picking at their own plate with faintly nauseous expressions or else nursing a large mug of black coffee - when Lily straightened up, eyes wide suddenly, as if electrified.
他們吃到一半——雷木斯像往常一樣吃著相當於自己體重一半的油炸麵包、雞蛋、烤豆和培根；其他人則帶著輕微的惡心表情撥弄著自己的盤子，或者端著一大杯黑咖啡——這時莉莉突然挺直了腰，眼睛睜大，好像被電擊了一樣。

“Oh shit!” she said, then kicked James under the table, “Potter!” She hissed, “We never gave Remus his present!”
“哦，糟了！”她說，然後踢了詹姆斯一腳，“波特！”她低聲說，“我們還沒給雷木斯他的禮物！”

James smirked at her, and Remus raised an eyebrow,
詹姆斯對她露出得意的笑容，雷木斯挑了挑眉，

“You and James got me a present? Together?”
“你和詹姆斯一起給我買了禮物？”

“We all did,” James laughed, “And there’s no need to beat me up, Evans, I’ve got it right here,” he withdrew a brown leather box from his robes. It was about the size of his hand, smooth and expensive looking, with a gold embossed border. It looked like the sort of thing girls kept their pricier jewellery in.
“我們所有人一起買的，”詹姆斯笑道，“不用打我，埃文斯，我這裡就有，”他從長袍裡取出一個棕色的皮革盒子。盒子大約有他的手掌大小，看起來光滑且昂貴，邊緣有金色的壓花。看起來像是女生用來裝貴重首飾的那種東西。

“You all…?” Remus accepted the box, curiously. “I hope you didn’t spend too much, you know I can’t--”
“你們所有人...？”雷木斯好奇地接過盒子。“希望你們沒花太多錢，你知道我不能——”

“Oh, shut yer face, Moony,” Peter yawned, prodding his porridge dazedly, “We had a whip-round for you - almost everyone in Gryffindor wanted to put in.”
“哦，閉嘴吧，月亮臉，”彼得打了個哈欠，迷迷糊糊地戳著粥，“我們為你湊了份子——幾乎所有的格蘭芬多人都想參與。”

“Not just Gryffindor, either,” Marlene grinned, “Nearly everyone we asked, even some teachers!”
“不只是格蘭芬多，”瑪琳笑道，“幾乎我們問過的每個人，甚至還有一些老師！”

Remus was just looking down at the box, now, because he knew he had probably gone red. Some hot, sickly bubble of emotion was burning his throat, so he swallowed, hard, which didn’t help.
雷木斯只是低頭看著那個盒子，因為他知道自己可能已經臉紅了。一股火熱、難受的情感泡泡正在燒灼他的喉嚨，所以他努力吞嚥，但沒有用。

“Open it, Remus!” He heard Lily’s voice. He pried it apart, and the box sprang open in a pleasingly neat motion. The interior was midnight blue velvet, and nestled among the folds was the most beautiful piece of treasure Remus had ever seen.
“打開它，雷木斯！”他聽到莉莉的聲音。他把盒子撬開，盒子以一種令人愉悅的整齊動作打開了。內部是午夜藍色的天鵝絨，折痕間嵌著雷木斯見過的最美麗的寶物。

It was a golden pocket watch, on a long, fine chain, polished to a high shine so that it was practically glowing. The case was decorated with intricate, vine-like swirls and patterns surrounding a shield at the centre which had been engraved in elaborate script with his initials: R. J. L.
那是一個金色的懷錶，掛在一條細長的鏈子上，拋光得非常光亮，幾乎在發光。錶殼上裝飾著複雜的藤蔓狀漩渦和圖案，中心是一個盾牌，上面刻著他名字的首字母：R. J. L.

He snapped it open with the lightest touch, and saw inside that the clock face was mother of pearl, and shimmered gorgeously beneath the golden hands which ticked away reassuringly. The other half seemed to contain a compass.
他輕輕一觸就打開了它，看到裡面的錶盤是珍珠母做的，在金色指針下閃閃發光，令人放心地滴答作響。另一半似乎裝有一個指南針。

“I didn’t think they worked at Hogwarts?” He murmured,
“我以為它們在霍格沃茲不起作用？”他喃喃道，

“It’s special!” Mary said, eagerly, “It doesn’t point north, or wherever normal ones do. If you say the name of somebody you love, it points you in their direction!”
“它很特別！”瑪麗急切地說，“它不指向北方，也不指向其他正常的方向。如果你說出你愛的人的名字，它會指向他們的方向！”

“Try it out, Moony!” James encouraged.
“試試看，月亮臉！”詹姆斯鼓勵道。

Remus looked up at his friends, nervously, then quickly raised the watch to his mouth and whispered,
雷木斯緊張地看著他的朋友們，然後迅速將懷錶舉到嘴邊，低聲說，

“Lily Evans.”
“莉莉·伊萬斯。”

At once, the needle spun into place, pointing directly across the table. Lily grinned bashfully. James kicked him under the table,
針馬上旋轉到位，指向桌子的另一邊。莉莉害羞地笑了。詹姆斯在桌下踢了他一腳，

“Bloody ladies man.”
“真是個花花公子。”

“You’re all amazing.” Remus said, hoping he didn’t sound too choked up. “Bloody amazing.”
“你們都太棒了。”雷木斯說，希望自己的聲音不會太哽咽。“真是太棒了。”

For the first week, Remus’s new regime seemed pretty effective. It certainly kept him busy. He said yes to everything; happily dropping whatever he was doing at a minute’s notice to help a younger student with their homework, or call a group study session when the Care of Magical Creatures NEWTs class panicked over sphinxes. He accompanied Lily on patrols, he discussed literature with Chris, talked quidditch tactics with Marlene and played endless games of chess with Peter (and lost every time). He was the angel of Gryffindor tower.
在第一周，雷木斯的新制度似乎相當有效。這確實讓他忙碌起來。他對所有事情都說“好”；高興地在一分鐘的通知下放下手頭的事情去幫助低年級學生做作業，或者當神奇生物護理課的N.E.W.T.s班級因斯芬克斯而恐慌時召集小組學習會。他陪莉莉巡邏，與克里斯討論文學，與瑪琳討論魁地奇戰術，並與彼得玩無數局象棋（每次都輸）。他成為了格蘭芬多塔的天使。

Because Sirius was not the only thing Remus was ignoring.
因為天狼星並不是雷木斯唯一忽視的事情。

The old shoebox Dumbledore had given him sat underneath his bed still, gathering dust and unopened, as it probably had been for many years – perhaps on some shelf in Matron’s office. Why was it a shoebox? Remus wondered, as he tossed and turned in his bed every night. Something so mundane, so every day. It made whatever was inside seem all the more terrifying. Trust Matron to be so heartlessly practical. It wasn’t even from a good shoe shop, like Clarks or Johnson’s. It was an economy brand, like everything else he’d ever received at St Edmund’s.
鄧布利多給他的那個舊鞋盒仍然放在他床下，積著灰塵，沒有打開，可能已經很多年了——也許在醫務室的一個架子上。為什麼是鞋盒？雷木斯每晚在床上翻來覆去地想著。這麼平凡、這麼日常的東西。這讓裡面的東西顯得更加可怕。相信醫務室阿姨是這麼無情實際的。甚至不是來自好的鞋店，比如Clarks或Johnson's。這是一個經濟品牌，像他在聖愛德蒙學院收到的所有東西一樣。

The box might have contained any number of things; and it wasn’t that Remus wasn’t curious. It wasn’t as if he didn’t try to imagine what was in there. Deeds to a house he could go and live in, that would be pretty brilliant. Maybe some old money. Photographs. A letter from his father, an explanation - it might contain answers to questions he hadn’t even known to ask.
這個盒子裡可能裝著各種各樣的東西；而且不是說雷木斯不感興趣。他並不是沒有試圖想像裡面有什麼。可以住進去的房子的契約，那會非常棒。也許一些舊錢。照片。父親的一封信，一個解釋——可能包含他甚至不知道該問的問題的答案。

But he didn’t open it. He knew that once he opened the box, all of the mystery would disappear, and he would be left with something disappointing. Because there could be nothing inside that could truly satisfy him.
但他沒有打開它。他知道一旦打開盒子，所有的神秘感都會消失，他會失望地發現裡面沒有什麼真正能滿足他的東西。因為裡面不可能有任何東西能真正滿足他。

So, keeping busy helped; making sure he exhausted himself each day so that he fell straight to sleep each night, even when the other boys stayed up chatting, plotting pranks. But Sirius himself helped, too. By some incredible twist of fate, he appeared to be giving Remus space.
所以，保持忙碌有幫助；確保每天讓自己筋疲力盡，這樣每晚可以直接入睡，即使其他男孩熬夜聊天，策劃惡作劇。但天狼星自己也幫了忙。命運的一個驚人轉折，他似乎在給雷木斯空間。

If Sirius remembered Remus’s harsh words from the night of the party, then he didn’t mention it. But he didn’t try to get him alone, or treat him with any kind of resentment or disdain. Remus surmised that Sirius had either:
如果天狼星記得雷木斯在聚會之夜的嚴厲話語，那麼他沒有提及。但他也沒有試圖單獨找到他，或以任何形式對待他懷有怨恨或鄙視。雷木斯猜想天狼星要麼：

been too drunk to take anything in, or;
喝得太醉而什麼都沒聽進去，或者；

taken Remus at his word, and chosen to back away quietly.
接受雷木斯的話，並選擇悄悄退後。

For Remus, with exams on the horizon, option 2 was by far the most preferable, so he decided to believe it.
對於雷木斯來說，隨著考試的臨近，第二個選項是最可取的，所以他決定相信它。

Their separation was so smooth, and so complete, that soon even Remus had a hard time believing they’d ever been close at all. Surely, to everyone else, it must seem that nothing had changed at all. Sirius was still Sirius - outgoing, girl-loving, cheeky, rebellious, devastating. And Remus was just Remus - quiet, private, studious and long-suffering secondary marauder.
他們的分離是如此順利和徹底，以至於很快連雷木斯自己都很難相信他們曾經親密無間。當然，對其他人來說，這似乎一點都沒有變化。天狼星仍然是天狼星——外向、愛女孩子、厚臉皮、叛逆、令人心碎。而雷木斯只是雷木斯——安靜、內向、好學和長期受苦的次要惡作劇者。

As March drew to a close, the birthday party now weeks behind them, there was only one moment when the situation very nearly came to a head, but was quickly deflated, with help from an unexpected quarter.
隨著三月接近尾聲，生日聚會已經過去幾周，只有一次情況差點達到高潮，但在意想不到的幫助下迅速化解了。

It was late one Friday afternoon, and Remus was hosting an introductory duelling workshop. Christopher was there – Christopher was never far away, these days – but most of the class were beginners, and much younger. They were just grasping some basic disarming and diversionary spells, when the door to the Charms classroom opened, but no one walked in. Everyone turned to look, and muttered ‘Peeves’, before returning to their attack stances. Remus knew better.
那是某個星期五的下午，雷木斯正在主持一個基礎決鬥工作坊。克里斯托弗也在場——這些天來，克里斯托弗從未遠離——但大多數學生都是初學者，而且年紀較小。他們剛剛掌握了一些基本的繳械和轉移咒語，這時魔咒課教室的門開了，但沒有人進來。大家轉頭看了一眼，喃喃道“皮皮鬼”，然後繼續他們的攻擊姿勢。雷木斯心裡清楚。

He followed the scent about the room, and watched the open door of Flitwick’s office moved only very slightly, as if someone had brushed the handle on their way inside. Flitwick trusted Remus, and left his office open in case they needed any equipment from inside - he kept a number of large mattresses which were good for duelling, as well as an emergency healing kit in there. Remus cleared his throat,

他們離開了教室——只有他們兩個——雷木斯靜靜地關上了門，以避免引起懷疑。

“也許你應該放輕鬆，”雷木斯嘆了口氣，“聽起來確實有點有趣。上天知道我們都需要笑一笑。”

“Prefects are supposed to uphold all of the rules,” Christopher replied, an echo of McGonagall in his voice, “Not just the boring ones. Anyway, if that’s how you feel, I don’t know why I bother.”
“學監應該維護所有規則，”克里斯托弗回答，語氣中帶著麥格教授的回音，“不僅僅是那些無聊的規則。無論如何，如果你是這麼覺得，我不知道我為什麼要再費心。”

He started to get up,
他開始站起來，

“Chris,” Remus looked up at him, “C’mon, don’t be like that. I’ll quiz you on Runes if you like.”
“克里斯，”雷木斯抬頭看著他，“來吧，不要這樣。如果你願意，我可以考考你符文。”

“I don’t feel like it.” Christopher replied, snippily, “I’m going to bed.” He walked off, towards the dorms. Remus sighed again, and rubbed his eyes. He’d give it a few minutes then go up himself. It had been a trying sort of day.
“我不想。”克里斯托弗脾氣暴躁地回答，“我要去睡覺了。”他走向宿舍。雷木斯再次嘆了口氣，揉了揉眼睛。他會等幾分鐘再上去。今天真是令人疲憊的一天。

But of course, it wasn’t over. No sooner had Remus brushed his teeth and changed into his pyjamas, than Sirius had taken his opportunity. He was standing in the middle of the dorm room with a face like thunder, arms folded. Remus felt at a bit of a disadvantage, in his night things and bare feet, but he tried to remain stoic and nodded.
但當然，這一切還沒有結束。雷木斯剛刷完牙，換上睡衣，天狼星就抓住了機會。他站在宿舍的中央，臉色陰沉，雙臂抱胸。雷木斯感覺有些處於不利地位，穿著睡衣和赤腳，但他試圖保持冷靜，點了點頭。

“Hello, Sirius. I’m just going to bed.” He tried to walk towards his side of the room, but Sirius blocked him.
“你好，天狼星。我只是要去睡覺。”他試圖走向房間的一側，但天狼星擋住了他。

“You really pissed me off, you know that?” He said, furiously.
“你真的惹惱我了，你知道嗎？”他憤怒地說。

“Excuse me?” Remus reeled back, frowning. Sirius carried on, practically ranting.
“什麼？”雷木斯退縮，皺起了眉頭。天狼星繼續說，幾乎在咆哮。

“If you were trying to make me jealous, then I think it’s really bloody low of you, Remus.”
“如果你是想讓我嫉妒，那我覺得你真的太卑鄙了，雷木斯。”

Remus rolled his eyes, which he knew would rile Sirius up even more.
雷木斯翻了個白眼，他知道這會更加惹怒天狼星。

“Oh, of course .” He said, sarcastically, “Everything’s about you , isn’t it? For god’s sake, you weren’t even supposed to be there! Why didn’t you just leave with the rest of the group?!”
“哦，當然。”他諷刺地說，“一切都圍繞著你，是不是？天哪，你根本不應該在那裡！你為什麼不和其他人一起離開呢？！“

“I thought you’d want to go down to dinner together! How was I supposed to know you’ve been having secret trysts with that… that...”
“我以為你會想一起去吃晚餐！我怎麼知道你和那個……那個……”

“I haven’t been having ‘secret trysts’ with anyone but you , you idiot.” Remus spat, “And you’ve already made me regret that. Christopher is my friend, and either way it’s none of your bloody business, so keep your nose out!”
“我除了和你之外，根本沒和任何人有‘秘密私會’，你這個白痴。”雷木斯噴出來，“而且你已經讓我後悔了。克里斯托弗是我的朋友，無論如何這都是你的狗屁事，所以別再插手了！”

“Fine!” Sirius shouted, “If that’s what you want!”
“好！”天狼星大聲說，“如果這就是你想要的！”

“I said so, didn’t I?!”
“我不是說了嗎？！”

Remus was furious, so angry that he knew if he stayed much longer he’d say something he regretted. They both liked the last word in an argument, it was one of the only ways they were similar. As he had nowhere to go, he pushed past Sirius to his bed, and shut the curtains so vigorously that he almost ripped the rings from the frame.
雷木斯憤怒至極，他知道如果再待一會兒，他會說出後悔的話。他們倆都喜歡爭論中的最後一句話，這是他們唯一的相似之處。因為他無處可去，他推開了天狼星，走向自己的床，拉上窗簾的動作如此激烈，幾乎把窗簾環從框架上撕下來了。

In a few moments, he heard Sirius’s angry footsteps stomping back down the stairs. Well, Remus thought. If he didn’t get the message before, he’s got it now.
幾分鐘後，他聽到天狼星憤怒的腳步聲重重地踩下樓梯。好吧，雷木斯想。如果他之前沒明白，現在應該明白了。

Monday 4th April 1977

Inconveniently enough, the very first Apparition lesson of the year happened to fall on the April full moon. Remus was already intensely nervous - in that shaky, sweaty sort of way - about these lessons; add to that the challenge he usually had keeping his magic under control in the days preceding the moon, and he was sure it was a recipe for disaster.
1977年4月4日，星期一

非常不巧的是，這學年第一次幻影移動課恰好在四月滿月的那天。雷木斯已經對這些課程感到非常緊張——以那種顫抖、汗水淋漓的方式——再加上他通常在月亮來臨的幾天內控制魔力的挑戰，他確信這將是一場災難的配方。

“I might end up on the other side of the country!” He said in a low voice to Lily as they queued up outside the Great Hall.
“我可能會出現在全國另一端！”他低聲對莉莉說，當他們在大廳外排隊時。

“You can’t,” she assured him. “I asked Professor McGonagall; they’ve only lifted the anti-apparition measures on the hall, so I don’t think you can get outside it.”
“你不會的，”她向他保證。“我問了麥格教授；他們只解除了一些防幻影移動的措施，所以我覺得你不會出到外面去。”

“Really? Ok, that’s good.” He nodded, trying to calm himself. It had been unendingly useful, having Lily aware of the furry little problem. She was much better at common sense than James or Sirius.
“真的嗎？好的，那很好。”他點了點頭，試著讓自己平靜下來。有莉莉知道那個毛茸茸的小問題，真的非常有用。她比詹姆斯或天狼星更有常識。

“Anyway,” she whispered, “You should stop acting like it’s a bad thing, being extra strong sometimes. I’d have thought it was an advantage, especially for someone as clever as you.”
“無論如何，”她低聲說，“你應該停止把偶爾變得特別強大當成壞事。我會認為這是一種優勢，尤其是對於像你這樣聰明的人。”

That struck him in a funny way. No one had ever suggested he try to be positive about his problem before. Well, except for Livia. You don’t know half of the power you hold, Remus Lupin.
這讓他感到有點奇怪。沒有人曾經建議他對自己的問題保持積極。嗯，除了莉維亞。你不知道你擁有一半的力量，雷木斯·盧平。

Inside the hall, Professor McGonagall introduced the eager sixth and seventh years to the tall, spindly ministry official who was there to teach them apparition. Remus had, of course, done a fair bit of reading on the subject, and already knew about the ‘three d’s’, but he had rather hoped there would be more to it than that.
在大廳內，麥格教授向渴望學習的六年級和七年級學生介紹了那位高瘦的部委官員，他來這裡教他們幻影移動。雷木斯當然對這個主題做過相當多的閱讀，已經知道了“三個D”的概念，但他倒是希望能有更多的內容。

After much too little instruction, in Remus’s opinion, the students were given wooden hoops, asked to simply ‘have a go’. He caught Mary’s eye, as they carried their hoops to a free space. She pulled a bug-eyed face and he laughed, which earned a stern look from the instructor. Not wanting to make a bad impression, Remus re-focussed his attention on the hoop.
在雷木斯看來，指導的時間過於短暫，學生們被給了木圈，要求他們“試一試”。他與瑪莉對視，當他們把圈子帶到一個空位時。她做了個瞪眼的表情，他笑了，這讓指導者投來了嚴厲的目光。不想留下壞印象，雷木斯重新將注意力集中在木圈上。

It was very difficult to concentrate, when everyone around you was twirling on the spot, tripping and stumbling, like puppies being trained to roll over. Still, Remus closed his eyes and tried.
當你周圍的人都在原地旋轉，跌跌撞撞，就像小狗被訓練翻滾一樣，很難集中注意力。儘管如此，雷木斯閉上了眼睛，嘗試著。

Deliberation. Best not to take it too fast; like flying a broom. Slow and steady wins the race.
深思熟慮。最好不要太快；就像飛掃帚一樣。慢而穩贏得比賽。

Determination . He really, really wanted to beat Sirius.
決心。他真的很想超越天狼星。

Destination . The hoop wasn’t even that far away. He’d side-alonged further, that time with Mr Potter.
目的地。那個圈子離得並不遠。他那次與波特先生一起側面轉移過去。

Remus tried to recall how that had felt. The magic, pulling him forward - no, more like… more like following a channel, like water swirling down a bathtub drain; if you pressed your fingertips against the holes you could feel the vacuum sucking… it was a bit like that.
雷木斯試著回憶那種感覺。魔法把他向前拉——不，更多的是……更像是跟隨一個渠道，就像水在浴缸排水口旋轉；如果你用指尖按壓那些孔，你能感覺到真空在吸……就是這樣的感覺。

“BOLLOCKS!” A shout went up, causing a lapse in Remus’s concentration. He opened his eyes in time to see James and Sirius sitting dazed on floor, staring at each other confused, rubbing their heads. Oh no, Remus thought, did they do it, already?
“該死！”一聲呼喊打斷了雷木斯的專注。他及時睜開眼睛，看到詹姆斯和天狼星茫然地坐在地上，互相困惑地盯著對方，揉著頭。哦不，雷木斯想，他們已經成功了嗎？

“Idiots.” Mary laughed. Everyone else was laughing too, and Sirius was looking extremely put out, as he climbed to his feet and dusted off his robes with a dignified sniff.
“蠢貨。”瑪莉笑了。其他人也在笑，天狼星看起來非常不高興，他站起來，輕輕拍了拍他的袍子，帶著優雅的嗅聲。

“What happened?” Remus asked.
“發生了什麼事？”雷木斯問。

“They both jumped at the same time and hit each other.” She snorted. “Silly buggers. I’m not feeling anything, are you?”
“他們倆同時跳起來撞到了一起。”她哼了一聲。“傻子。我沒感覺到任何東西，你呢？”

Remus shook his head. He closed his eyes again and concentrated as hard as he could, feeling for whatever it was that would pull him in the right way. He thought he had it, tried twirling, but got nowhere. At least he didn’t fall over.
雷木斯搖了搖頭。他再次閉上眼睛，盡力集中精力，感受能把他拉到正確方向的東西。他覺得自己找到了，試著旋轉，但沒有任何進展。至少他沒有摔倒。

Something wasn’t right. This was like the stupid patronus thing all over again (he still hadn’t managed one; he was one of the only ones who hadn’t. Even Peter had produced a wispy bit of silver.) Only the trick to that was having a happy thought - and Remus accepted that happy thoughts were not his forte. This , however, this required determination. And wasn’t he determined?
有些地方不對勁。這就像是那愚蠢的護法問題一樣（他仍然沒能成功；他是少數未能做到的之一。甚至彼得都產生了一絲銀光。）只是那個技巧是要有一個快樂的想法——而雷木斯接受快樂的想法並不是他的長處。然而，這需要決心。難道他不決心嗎？

Just then, the ministry sanctioned apparition instructor wafted past, and Remus caught a whiff of his magic. It was peculiar and strong - buzzing. It reminded him of the way that the old TV in the rec room at St Edmund’s gathered a fuzz of static on the screen. As a child, Remus had held his hands up to it in wonder, and stroked the bizarre, otherworldly energy, as if he could absorb it
就在這時，經部批准的幻影移動指導者輕輕走過，雷木斯嗅到他的魔法氣息。那種氣息奇特而強烈——嗡嗡作響。這讓他想起了聖埃德蒙德的休息室裡的老電視屏幕上的靜電。作為一個孩子，雷木斯曾經好奇地把手伸向它，撫摸那種奇異的、來自異世界的能量，好像他能夠吸收它。

There was a snap in Remus’s mind, like ice cracking. That was it! Remus relaxed his body. He didn’t have to look for the right channel, or try to feel it out - he could already feel it. The room was full of magic, thick and iron-like and hot-cold against his teeth. He could always sense it, he just learnt to tune it out over the years. That was harder to do on a full moon, but in this scenario, that might not be a disadvantage, as Lily had said…
雷木斯的心靈中發出了一聲脆響，就像冰裂開了一樣。就是這樣！雷木斯放鬆了身體。他不需要尋找正確的頻道，或試圖感受它——他已經能感覺到它了。房間裡充滿了魔法，濃厚而像鐵一樣，冷熱交替地碰觸著他的牙齒。他總是能感覺到它，只是多年的經驗讓他學會了忽視它。在滿月時，這會更難做到，但在這種情況下，這可能不是劣勢，正如莉莉所說……

He closed his eyes, breathed in, and moved - it felt like only the slightest twitch, a wand flick, or the quirk of an eyebrow. He let the magic do all the work, and when he opened his eyes with a gasp, he was inside the hoop.
他閉上眼睛，吸了一口氣，然後移動——感覺就像是最輕微的抽搐、手杖的一揮，或是眉毛的一挑。他讓魔法做所有的工作，當他驚呼著睜開眼睛時，他已經在圈子內了。

“Bravo!” The instructor was clapping his spindly hands together delicately, noiselessly.
“好極了！”指導者輕柔地拍著瘦長的手。

“Nice one, Moony!” James called across the room, a large, egg shaped bruised growing on his forehead.
“做得好，月亮！”詹姆斯在房間的另一邊叫道，他的額頭上長了一個大大的、蛋形的瘀傷。

“Well done , Remus!” The girls cheered.
“做得好，雷木斯！”女孩們歡呼道。

Remus looked at his feet, embarrassed, but thrilled.
雷木斯低頭看著自己的腳，感到尷尬，但也很興奮。

 

 

Friday 15th April 1977

By mid-April, there seemed to be no limits to Remus’s newfound confidence. He was cautious about it, of course - he didn’t tell anybody (perish the thought!) in case they might think him arrogant, or even worse - dangerous. But he knew that something had changed. For many years now, Remus had considered his lycanthropy, and the uncontrollable feelings and senses which arose from it, as a limitation on his magic. If the past few weeks were anything to go by - this had been incorrect.
到四月中旬，雷木斯的新信心似乎沒有界限。當然，他對此非常謹慎——他沒有告訴任何人（真是可怕的想法！），以防他們會認為他傲慢，甚至更糟——危險。但他知道某些東西已經改變了。多年間，雷木斯一直把他的狼人症和由此產生的無法控制的情感和感官視為魔法的限制。如果過去幾周有任何參考價值，那就是這種看法是錯誤的。

Perhaps this misunderstanding was simply due to the fact that too little study had been done on werewolves in the wizarding world. Or perhaps Livia had been right - Remus had been instructed by the wrong people all along.
也許這種誤解只是因為在魔法世界中對狼人研究得太少。或者也許莉維亞是對的——雷木斯一直受到錯誤人士的指導。

Now, in private, he carried out various experiments, from simple, basic spells, to much more complex transfiguration and transmutation. All of them came much easier when he relaxed, when he harnessed whatever magic was already there in the space around him. Before, casting a spell had felt like drawing water up from a well inside him, a heavy bucket on a winch. After the apparition discovery, he felt as though he had been standing in a lake all along - and all he needed to do was drink. He had even begun to make steps towards wordless magic.
現在，私下裡，他進行了各種實驗，從簡單的基本咒語，到更複雜的變形和變質。當他放鬆身心，利用周圍空間中已經存在的魔法時，一切變得容易多了。以前，施展咒語就像是從他體內的井裡抽水，沉重的桶在滑輪上。發現幻影移動後，他感覺就像是一直站在湖中——他所需要做的只是喝水。他甚至開始朝著無言魔法邁進了一步。

In the meantime, he had exams to prepare for, and while his newfound strength would certainly be useful in his practical exams, Remus still had to complete several written papers. On this particular afternoon, he had convinced James (and by extension, Peter) to revise along with him. It was a bright spring day, and the last chills of winter had eked out enough that they all agreed it would be nice to sit outside for a change.
與此同時，他還有考試要準備，雖然他新發現的力量在實際考試中肯定會有用，但雷木斯仍然需要完成幾篇書面報告。在這個特定的下午，他說服了詹姆斯（以及彼得）一起複習。這是一個明亮的春天，冬天的最後寒意已經消退，他們都同意換個環境坐在外面會很好。

They sprawled on the grass, books open, James reading with his tongue between his teeth and a quill behind his ear, Peter half-heartedly jotting down notes on hinkypunks.
他們攤開在草地上，書本攤開著，詹姆斯在閱讀時把舌頭夾在牙齒之間，耳朵後面夾著一支羽毛筆，彼得心不在焉地在hinkypunks上記筆記。

“It’s not fair,” he whinged, “It’s not NEWTs or OWLs this year, why’ve we got to do exams at all?”
“這不公平，”他抱怨道，“今年不是NEWTS或OWLs，為什麼我們還要考試？”

“Wouldn’t want you to lose your edge, Wormy,” James replied, still engrossed in his book. “Think of it as practice for NEWTs.”
“可不想讓你失去你的鋒芒，蟲子，”詹姆斯回答，仍然專注於他的書。“把它當作NEWTs的練習吧。”

“Rather not.” Peter pulled a face. “Moony, do you have the notes for--”
“我才不想呢。”彼得做了個鬼臉。“月亮，你有——”

“Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays.” Remus said, promptly, not looking up from his DADA essay.
“星期二、星期四和星期日。”雷木斯迅速說道，沒有抬起頭來看他的DADA論文。

“What?” Peter scratched his head.
“什麼？”彼得抓了抓頭。

“Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays.” Remus repeated. “Those are the days I hold my study groups, and those are the days I help other people with their work. I need the rest of the time to catch up with my own stuff.”
“星期二、星期四和星期日。”雷木斯重複道。“那些是我召開學習小組的日子，也是我幫助其他人完成工作的日子。我需要其他時間來趕上自己的進度。”

“Oh, but I’m your best friend,” Peter moaned, “Pleeease, Moony?”
“哦，但我是你最好的朋友，”彼得哀求道，“拜託，月亮？”

“Less time snogging Dorcas, more time organising your notes.” Remus smirked. It was very easy to be pious when you weren’t allowed to snog the people you wanted to snog. Speaking of which.
“少花點時間親吻多卡斯，多花點時間整理你的筆記。”雷木斯冷笑道。當你不被允許親吻你想親吻的人時，很容易變得虔誠。說到這個。

“All right, lads?” Sirius came sauntering across the lawn towards them, Emmeline trotting along behind him. James looked up and grinned, Peter moved to make a space.
“好吧，小夥子們？”天狼星一邊走向他們，一邊悠閒地穿過草地，艾梅琳在他身後跟著。詹姆斯抬起頭來，露出了笑容，彼得則移動到一邊騰出空間。

“Where’ve you been?” James asked, “Never see you these days.”
“你去哪了？”詹姆斯問，“這些日子從未見過你。”

“Not my fault you’ve become one of them, prefect Potter.” Sirius replied, coolly, “I had detention.”
“這不是我的錯，你變成了他們中的一員，學監波特。”天狼星冷冷地回道，“我有留校察看。”

“You’re in detention more often than I’m doing anything prefect-ish,” James countered, no longer reading his book, now back in marauder mode. He nodded at Emmeline, who sat primly beside Sirius, smoothing her skirt down, “All right, Em?”
“你留校察看的頻率比我做任何學監的事情還要高，”詹姆斯反駁道，不再讀書，現在回到了土匪模式。他點了點坐在天狼星旁邊、端莊地撫平裙子的艾梅琳，“好吧，艾？”

“Hi James,” she smiled back at him, “Peter, Remus. Are you all revising?”
“嗨，詹姆斯，”她對他微笑道，“彼得，雷木斯。你們都在複習嗎？”

“Unfortunately,” Peter groaned. “Moony’s not helping me, though.”
“不幸的是，”彼得抱怨道，“月亮不幫我。”

“Oh, help yourself, for once,” Remus snapped, no longer lightly teasing.
“哦，自己動手吧，”雷木斯斥道，不再輕鬆地取笑。

“是吧。”

“說到這個，”她繼續說，忽略了他的敷衍，“你想在霍格斯密德做什麼？我會在那裡遇見你，還是你會在我的公共休息室外接我？”

“唉，我不知道。為什麼這一定要是一件大事？”

Peter, despite his earlier despair, suddenly became fascinated by his DADA notes, head bowed over the parchment.
儘管彼得之前很絕望，但他突然對他的DADA筆記產生了興趣，低頭看著羊皮紙。

“是的。”他回答道，露出天狼星·布萊克的笑容。

“嗯？”

“帕德富特有感情嗎？”

“肯定沒有。”

天狼星一言不發地站起來，離開了。

雷木斯瞪了他一眼。

“Ask him!”
“去問他！”

“I did. He won’t say anything.”
“我問了。他什麼都不說。”
