“……真的嗎？”雷木斯真心感到驚訝。他曾半信半疑地以為天狼星已經告訴他每一個骯髒的細節。他一定真的很羞愧。

“Really.” James was looking at him very intensely now, “What’s going on?”
“真的。”詹姆斯現在非常認真地看著他，“發生了什麼事？”

“I… I slept with Mary.” At least it was true. Peter made an odd sort gasp, beside him, but Remus ignored it. “He found out, that’s all.”
“我……我和瑪麗上了床。”至少這是真的。彼得在他身旁發出了一種奇怪的喘息聲，但雷木斯忽略了它。“他知道了，就這樣。”

“You… what?!” James eyebrows shot up in unmasked surprise. He quickly rearranged his features, clearing his throat, “Oh, well good on you, mate. I had no idea you and she…”
“你……什麼？！”詹姆斯的眉毛驚訝地挑了起來。他迅速整理了一下神情，清了清喉嚨，“哦，嗯，你做得好，伙計。我完全不知道你和她……”

“Just a one off thing.” Remus said, quickly.
“只是一次性的事情。”雷木斯迅速地說。

“Ok. Right, well. Why’s Sirius in a mood about it? He and Mary broke up ages ago.”
“好吧。那麼，為什麼天狼星對此情緒不好？他和瑪麗很早就分手了。”

“Yeah.” Remus replied, glumly. He sighed, “Oh, go on then, Pete, borrow my notes. Which bit are you stuck on?”
“是的。”雷木斯沮喪地回答。他嘆了口氣，“哦，那就拿去吧，彼得，借我的筆記。你卡在了哪一部分？”

 

Chapter 113: Sixth Year: The Box 

The quidditch stands on a Sunday were one of the only places you were guaranteed some peace and quiet at Hogwarts. Remus had been going there every week since his birthday to catch the tail end of James’s spartan training sessions, and to have a flying lesson of his own, afterwards.
魁地奇看台在星期天是霍格沃茨唯一能保證安靜的地方之一。自從他的生日以來，雷木斯每週都會去那裡，抓住詹姆斯艱苦訓練課程的尾聲，然後自己上飛行課。

This morning, however, as he limped into the stands, he found that he was not alone.
然而，今天早上，當他一瘸一拐地走進看台時，他發現自己並不孤單。

“Hiya, Lily,” Remus beamed, surprised, “What are you doing here?”
“嗨，莉莉，”雷木斯驚訝地笑道，“你怎麼在這裡？”

Lily spun around and blinked at him, mouth open in a small pink ‘O’, as if she had not expected anyone else. Her eyes darted to the pitch, then back to Remus nervously, and she gave a sheepish grin,
莉莉轉過身來，瞪著他，嘴巴張成一個小小的粉紅色‘O’，彷彿她沒有預料到其他人。她的目光在場地和雷木斯之間來回跳動，神色緊張地露出一個害羞的微笑，

“Hi! Er… just watching Marls practice. Moral support and all that.”
“嗨！嗯……只是來看瑪琳的練習。道義上的支持和那些。”

“Oh, right. Mind if I join you?”
“哦，對了。我可以加入你嗎？”

She smiled and shifted her bag, as if to make room for him, though the stands were completely empty. They sat quietly and watched the practice for a bit. James was drilling the chasers and the keeper, so only half the team was there today. Remus vaguely remembered James’s ‘focus sessions’ initiative, which had come as a relief to the rest of the Gryffindor team, as it meant they didn’t actually have to practice every day, even if James did.
她微笑著，移動了一下她的包，好像要給他騰出空間，儘管看台上完全空無一人。他們靜靜地坐著，看了一會兒練習。詹姆斯在訓練追球手和守門員，所以今天只有一半的隊伍在那裡。雷木斯模糊地記得詹姆斯的‘專注訓練’倡議，這讓格蘭芬多的其他隊員鬆了一口氣，因為這意味著他們不必每天都練習，即使詹姆斯需要。

“Er… Lily?” Remus said, after a while, “Did you know that Marlene isn’t practicing today?”
“嗯……莉莉？”雷木斯過了一會兒說，“你知道瑪琳今天不練習嗎？”

She looked down at her knees, her hair falling in a coppery sheet in front of her face.
她低頭看著她的膝蓋，頭髮垂落在她的臉前，如銅色的布料一般。

“Yes.” She whispered.
“是的。”她輕聲說。

“So you’re here to watch…?”
“所以你來這裡是為了看……？”

“Don’t make me say it , Remus,” she sounded defeated. She raised her head, pushing her hair behind her ear, “Go on then, let me have it.”
“別讓我說出來，雷木斯，”她聽起來很沮喪。她抬起頭，將頭髮推到耳朵後面，“那就說吧，讓我聽聽。”

“What?!” Remus was amused. Prefect Lily Evans, all come undone. Sirius would love it.
“什麼？！”雷木斯感到好笑。學生會長莉莉·艾文斯，完全崩潰了。天狼星會喜歡這樣的。

“Tease me, make fun of me, tell me I’m a complete idiot…” she sighed, looking out at the pitch, “I already know.”
“嘲笑我，取笑我，告訴我我是個完全的傻瓜……”她嘆了口氣，望向場地，“我已經知道了。”

“I don’t think you’re an idiot just for fancying James.” Remus laughed, nudging her jovially, “But… I mean, it is a bit funny, after all this time.”
“我不認為你只是因為喜歡詹姆斯而成為傻瓜。”雷木斯笑了，愉快地碰了碰她，“但是……我的意思是，畢竟這麼長時間，確實有點好笑。”

“Ugh, I know.” She groaned, “I can’t bloody believe it.”
“唉，我知道。”她抱怨道，“我真不敢相信。”

“Does he know?”
“他知道嗎？”

“No!” She stared at him in disbelief, “I’d absolutely die !”
“沒有！”她瞪著他，難以置信，“我一定會死的！”

“Why?!” Remus laughed again, “You don’t honestly think he’ll turn you down? He’s been hoping for this exact thing for five years!”
“為什麼？！”雷木斯再次笑了，“你真的不覺得他會拒絕你嗎？他已經期待這個準確的事情五年了！”

“Exactly!” She said, gesturing wildly with her hands, spreading out her fingers in a show of exasperation. “He’s wanted it forever, and I’ve only wanted it for… er… well maybe a little while, actually… but nowhere near as long. If I give in now, he’s so intense . I might break his heart.”
“正是如此！”她說，揮舞著手，手指張開表現出沮喪。“他永遠想要這個，而我只想要……嗯……其實可能也只是一小段時間……但遠不及那麼久。如果我現在讓步，他那麼強烈。我可能會傷他的心。”

She bit her lip, still watching him flying, blowing his whistle and pointing emphatically at the goal rings.
她咬了咬嘴唇，仍然看著他飛行，吹著口哨，強調地指著球門圈。

“You might.” Remus agreed, “But I think James Potter would consider it an honour to have his heart broken by you.”
“你可能會。”雷木斯同意道，“但我覺得詹姆斯·波特會把被你傷心當作一種榮譽。”

She snorted,
她嗤之以鼻，

“Remus, honestly, you sound as bad as he does. I’m not this… I dunno, perfect ‘dream girl’ who’s going breeze into his life and make all the crap stuff wonderful. It’s not a fairytale. I’m not a fairytale. I’m really annoying. I’m a complete mess in the mornings - ask Mary - and I hate losing arguments, and I shout when I’m angry, and my nose runs when I cry. I don’t know anything about quidditch and I don’t really want to learn, either.”
“雷木斯，說真的，你聽起來跟他一樣糟。我不是那種……我也不知道，完美的‘夢中女孩’，會輕鬆地進入他的生活，讓一切變得美好。這不是童話故事。我不是童話故事。我真的很煩人。我早晨完全是一團糟——問瑪麗——我討厭輸掉爭論，生氣時會吼叫，哭的時候鼻子會流鼻涕。我對魁地奇一無所知，也不想學。”

“So?” Remus smiled. “I’m pretty sure he knows most of that. If he doesn’t then I don’t think it’ll hurt for him to find out. Anyway, it’s not as if James is perfect. I’ve smelled his socks.”
“那又怎麼樣？”雷木斯微笑道，“我很確定他知道大部分這些。如果他不知道，那我覺得他知道也無妨。反正詹姆斯也不是完美的。我聞過他的襪子。”

Lily laughed.
莉莉笑了。

“Thanks, Remus.”
“謝謝你，雷木斯。”

“Going to tell him?”
“打算告訴他嗎？”

She wrinkled her freckled nose.
她皺了皺帶雀斑的鼻子。

“Nah. Want to think about it a bit more first.”
“嗯。不過想再考慮一下。”

“Just going to stare at him riding his broom for hours on end?”
“就這樣盯著他騎著掃帚幾個小時？”

She shoved him, laughing,
她推了推他，笑著，

“If I want to! He’s easy on the eye, what can I say?” She poked out her tongue and returned to gawping. Remus smiled, and dredged up the only real piece of advice he had.
“如果我想的話！他看起來很不錯，我還能說什麼？”她伸出舌頭，繼續盯著看。雷木斯微笑著，提出了他唯一真正的建議。

“Don’t leave it too long. It gets harder, the longer you wait.”
“不要拖得太久。等待越久，就越困難。”

Lily looked at him, curiously, and Remus instantly regretted saying anything.
莉莉好奇地看著他，雷木斯立刻後悔說了什麼。

“Oh yeah?” She said, “You seem very wise in the ways of love, all of a sudden.”
“哦，是嗎？”她說，“你突然變得非常懂得戀愛的智慧。”

“Nah.” He laughed, he hoped convincingly, “I just read lots.”
“沒有。”他笑道，希望顯得說服力十足，“我只是讀了很多書。”

“I could have given you all of my heart,
But there’s someone who’s torn it apart.
And he’s taken nearly all that I have got,
But if you want I’ll try to love again…”

“Black, next time you decide to break someone’s heart, can you do it outside of the exam period?” Lily groaned as Sirius entered the common room and every radio, turntable and gramophone within twenty metres began blaring PP Arnold’s tragedy stricken voice.
“布萊克，下次你決定傷害別人的心時，可以在考試期間外做嗎？”當天狼星進入公共休息室時，每個收音機、唱片機和留聲機在二十米內都開始大聲播放PP·阿諾德悲劇性的聲音，莉莉抱怨道。

“Baby I’ll try to love again, but I know…
The first cut is the deepest…”

“What d’you want me to do about it?!” Sirius raged, storming about the room, trying to mute every speaker in sight.
“我能怎麼辦？！”天狼星怒火中燒，怒氣沖沖地在房間裡奔波，試圖靜音所有能見到的喇叭。

It had been a painful, drawn out melodrama, but Emmeline and Sirius had finally split. And apparently nobody treated Emmeline Vance like that, so in retaliation, she had placed a very advanced hex on him, which meant that every time he entered a room breakup songs began to play. This was usually limited to music players, but occasionally, when there was nothing else about, the portraits had begun to burst into song too.
這是一場痛苦而漫長的情感劇，但艾蜜琳和天狼星終於分手了。顯然沒有人會像那樣對待艾蜜琳·范斯，因此作為報復，她對他施下了一個非常高級的詛咒，每次他進入房間時，分手歌曲就會開始播放。這通常僅限於音樂播放器，但偶爾當周圍沒有其他設備時，畫作也會開始歌唱。

“只要向她道歉，解除那該死的咒語！”莉莉回應道。

“Cuz when it comes to being lucky, he’s cursed,
when it comes to lovin’ me, he’s worst…”

“我沒什麼好道歉的！”他激烈地反駁，“沉默！沉默，沉默，沉默！”

音樂終於停止了。不知道會持續多久。雷木斯沒有插手，他只能讓事情變得更糟，天狼星整周都心情不好。

Every time she got to the end, she would unravel it all, comb it out gently, and begin again. Sometimes Remus didn’t think he’d ever understand girls. Still, Marlene, who usually hated being fussed over, seemed to be quite enjoying it, she looked very peaceful.

“哦，是啊，繼續支持她，你們這些人。該死的女人。”天狼星把自己扔進莉莉對面的扶手椅，懶散地靠在椅子上，瞪著火焰。“有人有煙嗎？”

Remus did, but he didn’t say anything.
雷木斯有，但他沒有說什麼。

“她把你甩了我一點也不驚訝，”瑪麗笑著說，“你最近真是個令人厭煩的傢伙。我已經徹底厭倦了你。”她給了他一個調皮的眨眼，他的皺眉減少了。

“你其實愛我，”他嘟囔道。

“一切都整理好了——你們只需要來就行了，”詹姆斯笑著說，“當然，要帶上你們的帳篷。”

“Dad says I can borrow the family ones, as long as I take care of them,” Lily said, “Two two-sleepers.”
“爸爸說我可以借用家裡的帳篷，只要我好好照顧它們，”莉莉說，“兩個雙人帳篷。”

“Cosy.” Sirius said, sarcastically, “With seven of us going.”
“溫馨。”天狼星諷刺地說，“我們有七個人去。”

“Eight,” Peter piped up, “James said I could bring Dorcas.”
“八個人，”彼得插話道，“詹姆斯說我可以帶多卡斯。”

Remus groaned inwardly at that. Not that he didn’t like Dorcas; Dorcas was fine. But he had been looking forward to a summer holiday with all of his closest friends, not tag-alongs. Thank goodness Mary wasn’t bringing her latest boyfriend. Though, with Mary, the turnover was too fast to make any kind of long term plans.
雷木斯在心裡抱怨。不是他不喜歡多卡斯；多卡斯很好。但他一直期待著與所有親密朋友一起度過暑假，而不是帶上其他人。謝天謝地瑪麗沒有帶她最新的男朋友。儘管如此，瑪麗的男朋友更替太快，無法做任何長期計劃。

“Well I was rather hoping that you boys would bring your own tent, actually.” Lily replied, giving Sirius a frosty look.
“其實我還是希望你們這些男孩能帶上自己的帳篷。”莉莉回應道，給了天狼星一個冷漠的眼神。

“Mum said in her last letter that there’s a muggle camping supply shop in our village,” James said, quickly, ever the peacemaker, “So we’ll all go at get ours as soon as we’re home. You’re definitely coming to stay, this summer, right Moony?”
“媽媽在她的最後一封信中說我們村裡有一家麻瓜露營用品商店，”詹姆斯迅速說道，作為調解者，“所以我們回家後會去那裡買。你今年夏天一定會來住，對吧，月亮？”

“If it’s still ok?” Remus asked, anxiously. He still didn’t have a plan b. Maybe James would let him keep one of the tents afterwards. Ugh, what a depressing thought.
“如果還可以的話？”雷木斯焦急地問。他仍然沒有備選計劃。也許詹姆斯會讓他之後保留其中一個帳篷。唉，多麼令人沮喪的想法。

“Of course,” James grinned magnanimously, rubbing his hands together, “This summer is going to be great .”
“當然，”詹姆斯大方地笑道，搓著手，“這個夏天會很棒的。”

“How are we getting to Cornwall?” Marlene asked. “Apparating?”
“我們怎麼去康沃爾？”瑪琳問道。“使用瞬間移動？”

“If we’ve all passed, yeah.”
“如果我們都通過了，是的。”

They looked at Peter, guiltily. He’d still not quite managed to get anywhere without splinching himself, yet.
他們愧疚地看著彼得。他仍然沒能成功地瞬移到任何地方，經常會出現瞬間分裂的情況。

“I’m really trying,” he said, embarrassed. “I could get the Knight Bus?”
“我真的在努力，”他尷尬地說，“我可以搭乘騎士巴士嗎？”

“It’ll be fine,” James said, cheerily. “I promise. Best summer ever.”
“會沒事的，”詹姆斯愉快地說，“我保證。會是最棒的夏天。”

 

Mother

You had me

But I never had you

I wanted you

You didn’t want me.

 

Friday 24th June 1977And really, Remus thought to himself, as he left his last exam of the term - Care of Magical Creatures, written - thank goodness for James’s eternal optimism. It was one of the only things that kept any of them going, these days.
真的，雷木斯在離開學期的最後一門考試——《魔法生物護理》，筆試時對自己說——多虧了詹姆斯那永不熄滅的樂觀精神。這是目前唯一能讓他們堅持下去的東西之一。

Exams were the same as they ever had been - easier, maybe, at least when it came to practical magic. Fortunately no one expected a patronus this year. There was something reassuring about a timetable, though, and deadlines and timed exercises. It all made good common sense, and didn’t encourage too much independent thought. Remus was always grateful for an opportunity to switch off his brain. Especially as he had set himself a very personal deadline of his own.
考試和以往一樣——也許在實踐魔法方面更簡單了。幸好今年沒有人期待護法咒。儘管如此，時間表、截止日期和限時練習還是有種安慰感。這一切都很符合常識，也不會鼓勵太多的獨立思考。雷木斯總是感激能有機會讓大腦放空。尤其是他自己給自己設定了一個非常個人的截止日期。

Once his final exam was over (and today was the day), he would open the shoebox. It had been sitting under his bed for the better part of three months now. He had not so much as glanced at it. Whatever was in it would be disruptive, he knew that. Even if it was nothing more than some boring notes from Matron, old school work or something, he knew that just thinking about the whole St Edmund’s problem was going to drag him down eventually. He told himself that it was very sensible and mature; he needed a clear head for exams.
一旦最後的考試結束（而今天就是那一天），他會打開那個鞋盒。它已經在他的床下放了差不多三個月了。他甚至沒看過它一眼。他知道裡面會有一些擾人的東西。即使只是一些來自院長的無聊筆記，舊的學校作業或其他什麼，他也知道僅僅是想到整個聖埃德蒙德的問題最終會把他拖下來。他告訴自己這是非常明智和成熟的；他需要清晰的頭腦來應對考試。

But it was late June now, and he had nothing left to do. Of course, there was always something to do - NEWTs would begin in earnest next year; he ought to get a head start. There was talk about an end of year party, and he could start preparing for that. He really ought to catch up on his reading for Madam Pomfrey’s healing classes, too; he was woefully behind on bruises.
但現在已經是六月底了，他沒有其他事情可做。當然，總有事情要做——NEWTS將在明年正式開始；他應該提前準備。還有關於年終派對的討論，他可以開始準備這個。他真的應該趕上對波姆弗雷夫人的療愈課程的閱讀；他在瘀傷方面明顯落後了。

He ate lunch first. Unpleasant experiences were generally better faced on a full stomach. There were exams scheduled that afternoon for Muggle Studies and Divination - both of which James and Sirius were taking.
他先吃了午餐。一般來說，面對不愉快的經歷時，肚子飽了會更好。那天下午安排了麻瓜研究和占卜的考試——詹姆斯和天狼星都要參加。

“Moony, what are hot air balloons for? I still don’t get it…” James pleaded, looking very frazzled.
“月亮，熱氣球是幹什麼用的？我還是不明白……”詹姆斯懇求道，顯得非常焦躁。

“You’ll be fine,” Lily said, pouring herself some pumpkin juice, “Muggle Studies should be easy for you, after advanced Transfiguration.”
“你會沒事的，”莉莉說，給自己倒了一些南瓜汁，“在高級變形術之後，麻瓜研究對你來說應該很簡單。”

“Wow, thanks Evans,” James beamed. Everyone looked at Lily, who blushed and returned to her food.
“哇，謝謝埃文斯，”詹姆斯笑著說。大家看著莉莉，她臉紅了，回到了她的食物上。

“I’ve still never seen anything in a crystal ball.” Peter sighed deeply.
“我還是從來沒在水晶球裡看到過什麼。”彼得深深地嘆了口氣。

“Tell her you see a grim,” Sirius said, cheerfully, “That’s what I’m doing.”
“告訴她你看到了一隻預兆，”天狼星愉快地說，“這就是我在做的事。”

“Why a grim?”
“為什麼是預兆？”

“I just have a feeling she might actually see one, tomorrow afternoon, at about two o’clock.” Sirius smirked. James and Peter began to laugh, much to the girls’ confusion.
“我只是有一種感覺，她明天下午兩點左右可能真的會看到一隻預兆。”天狼星邪魅地笑道。詹姆斯和彼得開始笑了，讓女孩們感到困惑。

Remus loitered outside the Great Hall for as long as he could with his friends, until they all had to go in for the exam. Putting it off a few minutes won’t hurt...
雷木斯和他的朋友們在大禮堂外徘徊了很長時間，直到他們都必須進去考試。拖延幾分鐘也無妨……

But eventually, it was time to face the music. After all, the sooner he did it, the longer he’d have by himself to actually process it. Even if it was nothing; even if he only had to cope with another disappointment. He had a good book on hand, and full access to Sirius’s record collection, so the afternoon didn’t have to be completely unpleasant.
但最終，還是要面對現實。畢竟，越早面對，就能有更多的時間自己來處理這些事情。即使什麼都沒有；即使他只需要應對另一個失望。他手頭有一本好書，還能隨意使用天狼星的唱片收藏，所以這個下午不必完全令人不快。

He drew the curtains around his bed, even though he was alone in the dorm room. He blew the dust from the cardboard lid, and it made him cough.
他拉上了床邊的窗簾，儘管他在宿舍房間裡是獨自一人。他吹走了紙板蓋上的灰塵，結果讓他咳嗽起來。

“Scourgify,” he choked, aiming his wand at his sheets to rid them of the nasty grey matter. No going back now. As quickly as ripping off a plaster, he lifted the lid.
“清潔咒，”他呛聲著說，用魔杖對準床單，清除那該死的灰色物質。現在已經沒有回頭路了。像撕掉膠布一樣迅速，他打開了蓋子。

At first, it all looked completely harmless. Everything inside was flat - papers, presumably, sorted into neat brown envelopes of varying sizes, varying ages.
起初，一切看起來完全無害。裡面的東西都是平的——大概是一些紙張，分門別類地放在整齊的棕色信封中，大小和年齡各異。

His admission papers to St Edmund’s - Remus John Lupin, 5 years 3 months, arrival date 12/07/1965. Reports written by his primary school teachers - all of the marks were ‘poor’. ‘Shows very little aptitude for academia’, one read, ‘Incapable of learning. May suit unskilled work.’ Fucking bitches.
他進入聖埃德蒙德的入學文件——雷木斯·約翰·盧平，5歲3個月，入學日期1965年12月7日。由他的小學老師寫的報告——所有的分數都是‘差’。其中一份寫著‘顯示出對學術的興趣很少’，‘無法學習。可能適合不需要技能的工作。’該死的臭女人們。

His birth certificate. It was a muggle one - he supposed his mother had not been admitted to St. Mungo’s. Remus learnt that he had been born at home, in Bristol, of all places. His mother’s name was Hope, and his father was listed as ‘Unemployed’. All of this, Remus worked through with impassive patience, like an archivist sifting through documents relating to some ancient history, not his own life. But then came the photographs.
他的出生證明。這是一份麻瓜的證明——他猜他的母親沒有被送進聖芒戈醫院。雷木斯了解到他是在布里斯托出生的，真是不可思議。他母親的名字是Hope，而他的父親則列為‘失業’。雷木斯以無動於衷的耐心處理這一切，就像一位檔案館員在篩選與古老歷史相關的文件，而不是他自己的人生。但接下來是那些照片。

They were black and white. Muggle; unmoving. One of a chubby baby dressed in some white knitted affair, with buttons shaped like bunny rabbits. Remus supposed it was him, there was nothing written on the back, only the stamp from Boots. There was another, which must have been taken when he arrived at St Edmund’s. In it, he was able to recognise some features - the dark, cautious stare, the mouth set in a determined grimace. He was looking up - at whoever was taking the photo, presumably - and he looked frightened.
這些照片是黑白的。麻瓜的；沒有動作。其中一張是胖乎乎的嬰兒穿著白色編織的衣物，上面有像兔子一樣的鈕扣。雷木斯猜那是他，背面什麼也沒有寫，只有Boots的印章。還有另一張，應該是在他到達聖埃德蒙德時拍的。在這張照片中，他能認出一些特徵——黑暗而謹慎的凝視，嘴巴緊抿成堅定的表情。他在仰望——可能是看著拍照的人——看起來很害怕。

The last picture was the worst. It was of a family he did not remember.
最後一張照片是最糟糕的。那是一個他不記得的家庭。

There was Lyall, tall and slim and gangly, tousled hair and small, wire framed spectacles. He was smiling - Remus never pictured him smiling. Sitting in a floral armchair beside him was a small, very young looking woman. She had immaculate platinum blonde hair in a proper sixties beehive, and she was wearing a neat shirtwaister which showed off her pretty figure. Her nose was a bit long and beakish, but she had a nice face. On her lap was a little boy, giggling, his face all creased up with joy. She was looking at him, her mouth was open - what had she been saying?
那裡有萊爾，高挑、纖瘦且瘦長，亂蓬蓬的頭髮和小巧的金屬眼鏡。他在微笑——雷木斯從未想像過他會微笑。坐在他旁邊的是一位看起來非常年輕的小女人。她擁有完美的鉑金金髮，梳成了標準的60年代蜂窩頭，穿著整潔的連衣裙，展現了她漂亮的身材。她的鼻子有點長，像鳥嘴，但她的臉很美。在她的膝蓋上是一個小男孩，咯咯地笑著，臉上滿是喜悅的皺紋。她在看著他，嘴巴張開——她在說什麼呢？

Remus put it down, feeling light headed. He realised he’d been holding his breath for a long time, and exhaled. There was one envelope left. The handwriting on it was not Matron’s. It hadn’t been sealed, though, so maybe she’d read it before. Maybe that’s why she hadn’t given it to him. Steeling himself once more, Remus pulled out a letter, folded neatly in thirds. It was written on pretty note paper with a floral design at the borders. The handwriting was pretty, too.
雷木斯放下它，感覺頭暈。他意識到自己已經屏住了很長時間的呼吸，於是呼氣了。還剩下一個信封。上面的字跡不是院長的。它沒有封口，也許她之前已經讀過了。也許這就是為什麼她沒有給他。雷木斯再次鼓起勇氣，拿出一封信，整齊地對折成三份。信紙上有漂亮的花卉設計邊框。字跡也很漂亮。

My darling boy,

I know I’ve no right to leave you this letter. It may be a good few years before you receive it - if you receive it at all. I hope that you do, and I hope that when you do, you’ll be old enough. Still, I don’t expect forgiveness.

I can’t think what to tell you. How can I explain? You were my beautiful, precious boy from the moment you were born. No - from the moment I felt you move inside me. Your father and I loved each other very much, and having you tripled our happiness a thousand times over. You were loved, my little Remus, I pray you haven’t forgotten it. But you’re very young, and they tell me that sometimes forgetting is kindest.

When the accident happened, I promised you I would do everything I could to make it right again. I had some stupid idea that just loving you would be enough.

Then when Lyall left us both, I tried for you. I swear tried. But I was never a very clever girl, and never as strong or practical as your father. You needed so much, and I had so little. I had no family once I married him, you see, they told me to make a choice. My parents didn’t approve, and even after he’d gone, I knew they wouldn’t approve of you.

I can’t say how sorry I am, to let you go. In my heart I know it’s the safest thing, and the best for you, in the end. I know I will never forget you, and I know I will always long to see you again. I pray that when the time comes, I shall not be difficult for you to find.

All my love,

Hope Jenkins.
親愛的寶貝，

我知道我沒有權利給你留這封信。也許你要過幾年才能收到它——如果你能收到的話。我希望你能收到，我希望當你收到的時候，你已經夠大了。不過，我不指望得到你的原諒。

我不知道該告訴你什麼。我怎麼解釋呢？從你出生的那一刻起，你就是我美麗而珍貴的寶貝。不，從我感受到你在我體內移動的那一刻起。你父親和我非常相愛，擁有你讓我們的幸福倍增。你是被愛的，我的小雷木斯，我祈禱你沒有忘記這一點。但你還很年輕，他們告訴我，有時候忘記是最仁慈的。

當事故發生時，我向你承諾，我會盡一切努力使一切恢復正常。我曾經有個愚蠢的想法，就是僅僅愛你就足夠了。

然後，當萊爾離開了我們兩個人，我為你努力。我發誓我真的努力了。但我從來不是一個很聰明的女孩，也從來不像你的父親那樣堅強或實際。你需要那麼多，而我擁有那麼少。你看，當我嫁給他後我沒有了家人，他們告訴我必須做出選擇。我父母不贊成，即使在他去世後，我知道他們也不會贊成你。

我無法說我有多麼抱歉，讓你離開。我的內心知道這是最安全的，也是對你最好的選擇。我知道我永遠不會忘記你，我知道我將永遠渴望再次見到你。我祈禱當那時來臨時，我不會讓你難以找到。

滿滿的愛，

Hope Jenkins.

Remus put the letter back in the envelope and closed the box. He threw the box under the bed. He climbed underneath his heavy covers and curled up small, like he used to at St Edmund’s. He felt as if a hole had been opened up inside of him, a big, gaping emptiness. Tears picked his eyes, and because he was alone, he let them come.
雷木斯把信放回信封裡，然後合上了盒子。他把盒子扔到床下。他爬到沉重的被子下面，蜷縮成一團，就像他在聖埃德蒙德時一樣。他感覺內心好像被打開了一個洞，一個巨大的、張嘴的空洞。眼淚湧上了他的眼眶，因為他是獨自一人，他讓它們流下來。

Saturday 2nd July 1977

He’d never given his mother much thought. At least, not since he’d been at Hogwarts, which seemed so full of Lyall and all his achievements and mistakes. Obviously it would have been better to have a mother than not, but he wasn’t sure what he’d been missing all that time. Matron hadn’t been very maternal, but she wasn’t paid to love the boys she looked after.
他從未多想過他的母親。至少，自從他進了霍格華茲以來，似乎萊爾以及他所有的成就和錯誤占據了他的思緒。顯然，有一個母親會比沒有母親要好，但他不確定自己一直以來缺少的是什麼。院長並不太具母性，但她不是為了愛護她照顧的男孩而被聘用的。

This window into Hope’s life - into his own life - was terrifying to Remus, and he wished he’d never read the stupid letter. Still, he read it more than once. He read it every night, for the rest of the term, as if reading the word ‘loved’ could make him feel it. It couldn’t.
這扇窗戶打開了對Hope生活的了解——也就是對他自己生活的了解——對雷木斯來說是令人恐懼的，他希望自己從未讀過那封愚蠢的信。儘管如此，他還是讀了不止一次。他每晚都讀，直到學期結束，就像讀到‘被愛’這個詞能讓他感受到一樣。但它不能。

The marauders stayed an extra two nights at Hogwarts, for Remus’s sake. The first full moon of the summer fell on the 1st July, and it was more convenient (not to mention safer for the Potters) if Remus spent it in the Shrieking Shack. Well, he was supposed to be in the Shrieking Shack, but of course Wormtail, Padfoot and Prongs had other ideas. Free of exams and excited about the summer, they had one of the best full moon nights they’d had in ages.
麻瓜四人組多留在霍格華茲兩晚，是為了雷木斯的緣故。夏季的第一次滿月落在了7月1日，如果雷木斯在嚎叫屋度過，那會更方便（更安全，尤其對波特夫婦來說）。嗯，他本應在嚎叫屋，但當然，蟲尾、獵犬和角鹿有其他的想法。沒有了考試，對夏天充滿期待，他們度過了多年来最好的滿月之夜之一。

Still, Madam Pomfrey insisted on the usual course of aftercare, and knocked Remus out with a strong sleeping draught to ensure he rested through the next morning,
儘管如此，Pomfrey夫人還是堅持了通常的護理程序，給雷木斯喝下了強效的安眠藥，以確保他能夠好好休息到第二天早晨。

“Travelling by floo powder can make you queasy at the best of times,” she cautioned, “Better safe than sorry.”
“搭乘火爐粉旅行在最佳情況下也可能讓你感到不適，”她警告道，“謹慎一點總比後悔好。”

They were due to travel that evening, using the fireplace in McGonagall's office. Remus woke up just after lunch, and found he was not alone.
他們計劃在那天晚上通過麥格教授的辦公室的壁爐旅行。雷木斯在午餐後不久醒來，發現自己並不孤單。

“Hiya, Moony,” Sirius said, softly, sitting in the chair by his bed. His eyes were dark, he looked as though he had been dozing, too.
“嗨，Moony，”小天狼星輕聲說，坐在他床邊的椅子上。他的眼睛很暗，看起來像是也在打盹。

“Hiya,” Remus echoed, sitting up, stretching, “You ought to be in bed, you look knackered.”
“嗨，”雷木斯回應道，坐起來伸展身體，“你應該在床上休息，你看起來很疲憊。”

“Shut up, I look gorgeous,” Sirius replied, yawning. “Anyway, James is tearing the bedroom apart trying to pack, I wouldn’t get any sleep. Hungry?”
“閉嘴，我看起來很迷人，”小天狼星回應，打了個哈欠。“不過，詹姆斯正在把臥室弄得一片狼藉試圖打包，我根本無法入睡。餓了嗎？”

“Always.”
“總是。”

“Good, I’m supposed to make sure you eat,” he motioned to a plate sitting on the bedside table, loaded with fruit and sandwiches. Remus picked up an apple and bit into it, ravenous.
“很好，我應該確保你吃東西，”他指著床頭櫃上的盤子，上面擺滿了水果和三明治。雷木斯拿起一個蘋果咬了一口，餓極了。

Neither of them said much for a while, but Sirius ate a few grapes. Since March, they had perfected the art of making small talk with as little detail or eye contact as possible. You could call it a friendship, if you didn’t know what had come before.
他們一會兒都沒有說太多話，但小天狼星吃了幾顆葡萄。自從三月以來，他們已經將閒聊的藝術完善到了盡量少涉及細節或眼神接觸的程度。如果你不知道之前的事情，你可以稱之為友情。

“I feel a bit bad.” Sirius said, out of the blue, looking at his shoelaces.
“我覺得有點愧疚。”小天狼星突然說，看著自己的鞋帶。

“Hm?”
“嗯？”

“I feel a bit bad about the way I spoke to you, a while ago. About your friend er… Christopher?”
“我對之前跟你談話的方式有點愧疚。關於你的朋友呃…克里斯托弗？”

“Yeah.” Remus finished his apple core, down the the stem, which he put down, reaching for a sandwich next. Cheese and pickle. “You were a bit rude, but it’s ok. I haven’t thought about it much.”
“嗯。”雷木斯吃完了蘋果的果核，放下來，伸手拿了一個三明治。奶酪和醃菜。“你有點粗魯，但沒關係。我沒有多想。”

“Oh, that’s good.” Sirius nodded. He looked at Remus, then quickly diverted his gaze out of the window. “I thought maybe… I thought he might be the reason you decided to stop.”
“哦，那就好。”小天狼星點頭。他看了看雷木斯，然後迅速轉移視線望向窗外。“我想也許…我以為他可能是你決定停止的原因。”

Remus didn’t need to ask what he meant. Sirius was being very clear.
雷木斯不需要問他指的是什麼。小天狼星非常明確。

“No.” Remus said, choosing his words carefully. “It wasn’t to do with him. I told you, he’s my friend, that’s all.”
“不。”雷木斯說，仔細選擇著詞語。“這和他無關。我告訴過你，他只是我的朋友，就這樣。”

Sirius nodded, bravely.
小天狼星勇敢地點點頭。

“Yeah, I believe you. I do.”
“是的，我相信你。我相信。”

He still didn’t understand, Remus realised, sadly. He still didn’t know why they couldn’t just carry on the way they were. Stupid, beautiful, impossible boy.
他仍然不理解，雷木斯悲傷地意識到。他仍然不知道為什麼他們不能繼續像以前那樣。愚蠢、漂亮、不可思議的男孩。

“Look, Sirius,” he said, still cautious, “I just… I’ve had a bit of a shit year, to be honest. Maybe I’m having a shit life, I dunno. There’s a lot of stuff going on at the moment that I can’t really control. So the way I see it... if something’s making me miserable that I can control, then…”
“看，天狼星，”他說，仍然小心翼翼，“老實說，我今年過得有點糟糕。也許我過得很糟，我也不知道。現在有很多我無法控制的事情。所以我覺得…如果有什麼讓我痛苦而我能夠控制，那麼…”

“Oh, right. I get it.”
“哦，我明白了。”

“Yeah?”
“是嗎？”

“I would never want to make you miserable, Moony,” Sirius said, “I just want you to be happy.”
“我絕對不想讓你痛苦，Moony，”小天狼星說，“我只希望你能幸福。”

Remus gave a small smile. He reached out, putting his hand over Sirius’s. It was warm, and the touch was gentle. Sirius looked down at their hands, surprised.
雷木斯露出了一個小微笑。他伸出手，放在小天狼星的手上。那是溫暖的，觸感很輕柔。小天狼星低頭看著他們的手，感到驚訝。

“Thanks,” Remus said. “It means a lot.”
“謝謝，”雷木斯說。“這對我來說意義重大。”

 

Sirius didn’t say anything, but he squeezed Remus’s hand gently, and the two of them sat in silence, sharing a moment of quiet understanding. The afternoon sun filtered through the window, casting a warm, golden glow over the room.
小天狼星沒有說什麼，但他輕輕地握住雷木斯的手，他們兩人靜靜地坐著，共享一刻靜謐的理解。午後的陽光透過窗戶灑進房間，給房間覆上了一層溫暖的金色光輝。

 

Chapter 114: Summer 1977: Part 1Television man is crazy, saying we’re juvenile delinquent wrecks,

Oh man! I need TV, when I got T.Rex!

 

Saturday 2nd July 1977

Remus felt strangely untethered, arriving at the Potter’s with all of his earthly possessions, moving them into a temporary room. He was going to have to tell somebody what had happened – and soon. If he could just get Mr Potter on his own, maybe… but both of James’s parents were busier than ever this year, running in and out of the house on errands, or holding secretive meetings which the boys weren’t allowed to attend.
雷木斯感覺有些不知所措，帶著他所有的世俗財物來到波特家，將它們搬進了一個臨時的房間。他得告訴某人發生了什麼事——而且要快。如果他能單獨找到波特先生，也許…但是詹姆斯的父母今年比以往更忙碌，頻繁地出入於家中辦事，或者舉行秘密會議，男孩們不被允許參加。

“But we’re all of age,” James protested.
“但我們都成年了，”詹姆斯抗議道。

“You’re still my little boy, though,” Mrs Potter kissed his head, patronisingly, as she cleared their breakfast plates.
“但你仍然是我的小男孩，”波特夫人親吻了他的頭，帶著一絲居高臨下的語氣，一邊收拾他們的早餐盤子。

James looked highly insulted by this babying, but Remus’s eyes pricked with tears and he had to excuse himself.
詹姆斯對這種溺愛的態度顯得非常不滿，但雷木斯的眼睛紅了，眼淚在眼眶中打轉，他不得不找藉口離開了。

They had a week to prepare for the camping trip, and on the very first day set off into the village to purchase a tent. Remus had never been camping in his life, but still found himself better equipped than James, Sirius or Peter, who were in turns distracted, terrified and fascinated by every single item in the shop. It fell to Remus to talk to the shopkeeper about boring things like ground sheets and pegs and rigging. In the end, he settled for two sensible brown and orange two-man tents, ignoring Sirius’s pleading that he consider a blue and green psychedelic number.
他們有一周的時間來準備露營旅行，第一天就出發到村子裡去買帳篷。雷木斯一生中從未露營過，但他發現自己比詹姆斯、小天狼星或彼得更具備準備的能力，後三者在商店中的每一個物品上輪流分心、恐懼和著迷。雷木斯負責與店主討論那些無聊的事情，比如地布、帳篷釘和繩索。最後，他選擇了兩個實用的棕色和橙色的雙人帳篷，無視了小天狼星請求他考慮一個藍綠色迷幻風格的帳篷。

The next day, Remus had to check they all had appropriate muggle clothes, seeing as they would be using a muggle campsite, then they got a crash course in cooking from Gully the house elf.
第二天，雷木斯不得不檢查他們是否都有合適的麻瓜衣物，因為他們將使用一個麻瓜露營地，接著他們還從家養小精靈Gully那裡獲得了速成烹飪課程。

“Can’t the girls do the cooking?” James whinged, as the foul smell of burnt eggs filled the air. Mrs Potter, who had been watching with amusement came up and slapped him lightly around the head,
“難道女孩們不能做飯嗎？”詹姆斯抱怨道，當空氣中彌漫著焦蛋的難聞氣味時。波特夫人看到這一幕，輕輕拍了拍他的頭，帶著一絲娛樂的表情，

“Some man I’ve raised here,” she sniffed, “If you can’t cook a young lady breakfast, don’t expect her to spend the night.”
“我養出了什麼樣的男人，”她嗤之以鼻，“如果你不能為一位女士煮早餐，就不要指望她過夜。”

“噁心，媽媽！”詹姆斯皺起眉頭，厭惡地說，而小天狼星和雷木斯則彎著腰大笑。

They filled the rest of the time planning all of the things they would do with their holiday freedom, watching the matinee at the local cinema (there was a Bond film playing, and Airport ‘77, which was Remus’s personal favourite) and of course, flying their brooms. Sirius was very impressed by Remus’s recent improvement, and they actually managed to organise a very small scale quidditch game (without the snitch, Peter as Keeper).
他們利用剩下的時間計劃假期自由時要做的所有事情，看了當地電影院的下午場（那裡正在放映一部邦德片和《機場77》，這是雷木斯的最愛），當然，還有飛掃帚。小天狼星對雷木斯最近的進步感到非常滿意，他們還成功地組織了一場非常小規模的魁地奇比賽（沒有金探子，由彼得擔任守門員）。

There was no sign of Moody, this summer. Mr Potter explained over dinner one night that security measures on their house had been increased, and Moody was back in the Auror’s office, managing things there. Remus was relieved - he’d tied Moody and Ferox together in his mind, muddled them all up with the Livia encounter and Dumbledore’s cruel single mindedness. All in all, after the year he’d had, Remus was looking forward to a few weeks away from anyone older than him.
今年夏天沒有摩迪的身影。波特先生在某晚的晚餐中解釋說，他們家中的安全措施已經加強，摩迪回到了奧羅的辦公室，負責那裡的事務。雷木斯感到如釋重負——他將摩迪和費羅克斯混為一談，把它們與利維亞的遭遇和鄧布利多的殘酷單一思想混在一起。總的來說，在度過了這樣的一年後，雷木斯期待著遠離比他年長的幾週時間。

It was decided that they would all apparate to Cornwall, except for Peter, who had failed his test. Mrs Potter had kindly offered to take him as a side-along, before disapparating back home, but Peter insisted on taking the Knight bus. This way, he decided, he could collect Dorcas along the way.
他們決定所有人都將傳送到康沃爾，除了彼得，他未能通過測試。波特夫人好心地提議在返回家之前帶他一起，但彼得堅持搭乘騎士巴士。他決定這樣做，可以在路上接上多卡斯。

在他們準備離開的前夕，詹姆斯、小天狼星和雷木斯擠進了波特街盡頭的紅色電話亭，與小天狼星所說的“女性代表”進行協調。

“我可以按按鈕嗎，Moony？”詹姆斯問道，手指在銀色鍵盤上劃過。

“哪一部分是你說話的地方？”小天狼星說，將話筒舉到眼前檢查。

“Oh, for goodness sake, you two, calm down…” Remus dialled Lily’s home number, snatching the black plastic receiver back. It rang for a bit, and he hoped that Lily would pick up the phone, and not one of her parents.
“哦，天哪，你們倆，冷靜點…”雷木斯撥通了莉莉的家號，奪回了黑色塑料話筒。電話響了片刻，他希望莉莉能接電話，而不是她的父母中的任何一個。

“Good evening, Evans household?” A young woman answered.
“晚上好，埃文斯家？”一位年輕的女子回答道。

“Lily?”
“莉莉？”

“Who’s speaking, please?”
“請問是誰在說話？”

“Er… Remus Lupin.”
“呃… 雷木斯·盧平。”

There was a very rude snorting laugh, then the person on the other end shouted away from the receiver;
那邊傳來了一聲非常粗魯的哼聲，然後那人朝話筒外面大喊道；

“LILY! It’s for YOU!”
“莉莉！是你的電話！”

Remus waited, shifting from foot to foot, Sirius and James watching him eagerly.
雷木斯等待著，不停地換腳，小天狼星和詹姆斯熱切地看著他。

“Thanks, Pet,” Lily’s voice said on the other end.
“謝謝，Pet，”莉莉的聲音在另一端說道。

“別等太久，我在等弗農打來。”

“Hello?” Lily’s voice came louder, directly into the phone.
“你好？”莉莉的聲音變得更大，直接傳到電話中。

“Hi Lily, it’s Remus.”
“嗨莉莉，我是雷木斯。”

“Hiya Remus! Sorry, that was my sister. Are you all ready?”
“嗨雷木斯！抱歉，那是我妹妹。你準備好了嗎？”

“Yep, I think so. Pete’s left already I think. You lot?”
“嗯，我想是的。我想彼得已經出發了。你們呢？”

“Mary and Marlene got here just before tea. We agreed one o’clock in the afternoon, didn’t we?”
“瑪麗和馬琳在茶點前來到這裡。我們說好下午一點見，不是嗎？”

“Yeah, one o’clock, just outside the campsite. I made James get a map.”
“對，下午一點，就在露營地外面。我讓詹姆斯拿了一張地圖。”

“Oh good. I think mum’s letting me borrow the A to Z.”
“太好了。我覺得媽媽讓我借了A到Z地圖。”

“Cool.”
“太棒了。”

James was tugging on Remus’s sleeve. He sighed, “Er, Lily? James and Sirius have never used a phone before, can you talk to them for a minute so they leave me alone?”
詹姆斯在拉著雷木斯的袖子。他嘆了口氣，“呃，莉莉？詹姆斯和小天狼星從未用過電話，你能跟他們聊一會兒，讓他們離開我嗎？”

Lily laughed,
莉莉笑了，

“Go on then, it’ll wind Pet up.”
“那就去吧，這會讓Pet惱火的。”

Remus leaned back against the glass panes and watched James and Sirius fight over the phone, taking turns to shout something at Lily and then press the receiver to their ears and listen with wonder. Night began to fall around them, and if anyone had walked past they would just have seen three village boys mucking about in a phone box, without a care in the world.
雷木斯靠在玻璃窗上，看著詹姆斯和小天狼星爭奪電話，輪流對莉莉大喊什麼，然後把話筒貼在耳朵上，驚奇地聽著。夜色開始降臨，如果有人路過，他們只會看到三個村子裡的男孩在電話亭裡嬉戲，無憂無慮。

Saturday 9th July 1977Remus’s first time apparating outside of Hogwarts could have gone a bit better, but at least he didn’t end up in a tree, like James did. He ended up, in fact, about half a mile south of the campsite, on the beach.
雷木斯第一次在霍格華茲以外的地方瞬移本來可以更順利些，但至少他沒有像詹姆斯那樣掉進樹裡。實際上，他最終出現在了露營地南方約半英里處的海灘上。

He’d been to the seaside before, on summer trips at St Edmund’s – three times to Margate, once to Southend. He couldn’t say he’d particularly enjoyed these outings – or at least he didn’t enjoy them any more than he would have enjoyed sitting in the back garden at St Edmund’s. They were busy, noisy places, full of crying children and barking dogs and strange sugary smells and brightly coloured fairground rides.
他以前去過海邊，在聖埃德蒙德的夏季旅行中——三次去瑪格特，一次去索森德。他不能說他特別喜歡這些出遊——至少他不比坐在聖埃德蒙德的後花園中更喜歡這些地方。那裡是繁忙而嘈雜的地方，充滿了哭鬧的孩子、吠叫的狗、奇怪的糖果氣味和色彩鮮艷的遊樂場設施。

This beach was almost deserted, except for a few kids – dots in the distance, really – flying a pink and blue kite. The day was warm enough, the sky was blue and the sand soft and yellow. He knew he ought to start walking towards the campsite, to find the others, but instead he sat down for a few minutes, just to look. The sea wasn’t green, or bright blue, like in picture books – it was more of a concrete kind of grey. Still pretty, glimmering under the midday sun. In the very far distance, Remus could just about make out a long dark shape on the horizon. Was that France? Might be. He could pretend it was.
這片海灘幾乎是空無一人的，只有幾個孩子——實際上是遠處的小點——在放一隻粉紅色和藍色的風箏。天氣足夠暖和，天空湛藍，沙灘柔軟而金黃。他知道他應該開始朝露營地走去，去找其他人，但他卻坐下來幾分鐘，只是看一看。大海不像圖畫書中那樣綠色或明亮的藍色——它更像是一種混凝土般的灰色。仍然很漂亮，在正午的陽光下閃閃發光。在遙遠的地平線上，雷木斯勉強能辨認出一個長長的黑色形狀。那是法國嗎？也許是。他可以假裝是。

Remus hadn’t been able to relax, at the Potters. He’d felt like a visitor there; someone who didn’t belong. He didn’t know where he did belong. 雷木斯在波特家中無法放鬆。他覺得自己像是一個訪客；一個不屬於那裡的人。他不知道自己屬於哪裡。既然他已經十七歲了，他可以去任何他想去的地方。住在這裡，康沃爾會很好嗎？他最近發現自己出生在布里斯托，並想知道那裡是什麼樣的；那裡也在海邊。雷木斯從未想過自己會住在倫敦以外的地方。曾經，他以為自己可能永遠不會離開艾塞克斯。

Eventually, he felt too guilty and had to go and look for the others. The walk was bracing, and after a year of being confined to Hogwarts, it was a thrill just to be able to go somewhere alone. The campsite itself was halfway up the beach, on a long stretch of flat, neatly trimmed grass. A few families had already pitched tents, and the mothers and fathers were sitting outside them in deck chairs, soaking up the rare English summer sun with cups of tea and newspapers standing by.
最終，他感到太內疚了，必須去尋找其他人。步行讓人感到神清氣爽，經過了一年的霍格華茲生活，能夠獨自去某個地方真是一種激動。露營地本身位於海灘的中途，長長的平坦草地上已經有幾個家庭搭起了帳篷，父母們坐在帳篷外面的躺椅上，享受著難得的英國夏日陽光，旁邊放著茶杯和報紙。

Mary, Marlene, James and Sirius were sitting on a picnic bench outside the site office, which was little more than a breezeblock hut. Mary and Marlene jumped up when they saw him,
瑪麗、馬琳、詹姆斯和小天狼星正坐在露營地辦公室外的野餐桌上，辦公室只是個簡單的磚塊小屋。當瑪麗和馬琳看到他時跳了起來，

“We thought we’d lost you!”
“我們以為我們把你弄丟了！”

“Overshot,” he explained, “Landed on the beach - not in the water, luckily.”
“我超過了，”他解釋道，“降落在了海灘上——幸運的是，不是在水裡。”

“We all ballsed it up, a bit,” Mary laughed, and they each recounted the strange places they’d ended up. Except for Lily, who had arrived in precisely the place she’d meant to. She was inside the office, booking them in.
“我們都有點搞砸了，”瑪麗笑道，他們每個人都講述了自己最終到達的奇怪地方。除了莉莉，她準確地到達了她打算去的地方。她在辦公室裡，正在為他們辦理登記。

This done, the party set about finding the perfect place to pitch their tents. James and Sirius decided this needed to be as close to the beach as possible. Then there was the matter of actually erecting the tents, which was endlessly fascinating to the two pureblood boys.
辦完這些，大家開始尋找搭帳篷的完美地點。詹姆斯和小天狼星決定這需要盡可能靠近海灘。然後就是實際搭建帳篷的問題，這對兩個純血男孩來說是無窮的魅力所在。

Lily took charge, channelling her prefect persona, reading out directions and barking out orders.
莉莉掌握了主導，發揮了她的學監角色，讀出指示並發號施令。

“No not that hook, I said the one in the corner… bloody hell, Black, use the flipping mallet, not your boot! Come on, chop chop, we haven’t got all day…”
“不是那個鉤子，我說的是角落裡的那個……該死的，布萊克，使用那把該死的錘子，不是你的靴子！來，快點，我們沒有整天的時間……”

“Blimey, Evans,” James grinned, standing with his arms up, holding one of the poles in place while Mary and Marlene tried to get the canvas over it, “Have you ever considered quidditch coaching? You’d be incredible.”
“天啊，埃文斯，”詹姆斯咧嘴一笑，雙臂舉起，保持一根支柱的位置，而瑪麗和馬琳試圖把帆布套在上面，“你考慮過魔法飛球教練嗎？你會很棒的。”

“Please, no,” Marlene called out, muffled under the heavy fabric. “I’ll leave the team if I have to put up with both of you blowing whistles at me.”
“拜託，不要，”馬琳在厚重的布料下喊道。“如果我必須忍受你們兩個對我吹口哨，我會離開隊伍的。”

It took almost two hours, but it was a huge amount of fun, and everyone was very pleased with themselves once all four tents were up in a neat row, facing out to sea.
花了差不多兩個小時，但這非常有趣，當四頂帳篷整齊地排成一行，面對著大海時，每個人都對自己感到非常滿意。

“Well done, lads,” Lily smiled, sitting cross legged on the grass they waited for the kettle to boil, “And no magic at all. You’ll make muggles yet.”
“做得好，夥計們，”莉莉微笑道，雙腿交叉坐在草地上，他們等著水壺煮開，“而且完全沒有魔法。你們還會成為麻瓜的。”

Peter and Dorcas arrived shortly after that, looking very rumpled and tired from their long journey on the Knight bus.
彼得和多卡斯不久後到達，看起來很疲憊，因為他們在騎士巴士上長途旅行後非常凌亂。

“It stopped at Guernsey twice before we even started south…” Dorcas explained, looking vaguely disturbed. Peter accepted a cup of tea and sat in silence, yawning.
“它在我們開始南行之前在根西停了兩次……”多卡斯解釋道，看起來有點擔憂。彼得接過一杯茶，靜靜地坐著，打了個哈欠。

Once they’d woken up a bit, Mary decided it was time to go to the beach. It was about three o’clock by then, but still very warm, and they had hours of daylight left. The girls disappeared into their tents to get into swimming costumes. Sirius and James had been so excited by the prospect of muggle swimming trunks that they’d been wearing them all day anyway, and Remus – still in jeans and long sleeves – wasn’t planning to take off his clothes under any circumstances.
等他們稍微清醒了一些，瑪麗決定是時候去海灘了。當時大約是三點鐘，但仍然很暖和，他們還有幾個小時的日光。女孩們消失進帳篷裡換上游泳衣。小天狼星和詹姆斯對麻瓜泳褲的前景感到如此興奮，以至於他們整天都穿著它們，而雷木斯——仍然穿著牛仔褲和長袖——則不打算在任何情況下脫下衣服。

He did remove his trainers and socks, when they reached the sand, but ignored the other’s pleas to join them in the sea. He was happy enough to sit on the bank, enjoying the warm sun on his back and listening to the seagulls screaming overhead. The girls shrieked too, as they dipped their toes in the icy cold water, and they made a game of running back and forth with the tide, daring each other to get in. James was knocked over by a wave when he wasn’t looking – too busy staring at Lily’s long bare legs. Mind you, Remus caught her throwing a few longing glances at him too. Those muscles were pretty hard to ignore.
當他們到達沙灘時，他確實脫下了運動鞋和襪子，但忽略了其他人邀請他一起去海裡。他很高興能坐在岸邊，享受背上的暖陽，聽著頭上的海鷗尖叫。女孩們也尖叫著，把腳趾浸入冰冷的水中，並玩著隨著潮水來回跑的遊戲，相互挑戰著去海裡。詹姆斯在不注意時被一個波浪打翻了——他太忙於盯著莉莉修長的裸腿。說實話，雷木斯也看到她對他投來了幾個渴望的目光。那些肌肉真的很難忽視。

Sirius, as usual was in a league of his own. He strode out into the surf as if it was as warm as bathwater, and as soon as he was waist deep, dived right under, sleek and graceful as a fish. He swam long, languid strokes, and came back looking happier than Remus had seen him in a long time.
小天狼星，像往常一樣，獨具一格。他大步走進海浪中，彷彿水溫和浴缸一樣溫暖，一到腰深，他就迅速潛入水中，像魚一樣光滑優雅。他游了很長的悠閒的泳姿，回來時看起來比雷木斯很長一段時間看到的要快樂多了。

Afterwards, wrapped in towels, the girls showed the pureblood boys how to build a sandcastle without any magic, and James and Peter became extremely invested in creating a complicated irrigation system to ensure that the moat was properly supplied at all times.
之後，裹著毛巾的女孩們向純血男孩們展示了如何在沒有魔法的情況下建造沙堡，詹姆斯和彼得對建立一個複雜的灌溉系統變得非常投入，以確保護城河隨時得到適當的供應。

Back at the tents they cooked dinner – thankfully Marlene and Dorcas offered to supervise this, frying bacon over a little gas burner Lily’s father had donated. James and Lily went off to the shop – ostensibly for milk – and returned with a case of cider.
回到帳篷裡，他們煮晚餐——幸運的是，馬琳和多卡斯提供了監督，使用莉莉父親捐贈的小燃氣爐煎培根。詹姆斯和莉莉去了商店——表面上是為了買牛奶——然後帶回了一箱蘋果酒。

“Muggle drinks, too?!” Sirius exclaimed.
“麻瓜飲料，也有？！”小天狼星驚叫道。

“We’re getting a fully rounded experience, apparently,” James laughed. Lily giggled then blushed and looked away.
“顯然，我們在獲得完整的體驗，”詹姆斯笑道。莉莉咯咯笑著，然後臉紅了，轉過頭去。

Remus could already see where the evening was heading, and sat himself as far away from Sirius as possible. They’d already agreed that Sirius and James would share one tent, with Peter and Remus in the other, so at least there would be no awkwardness there. He just had to watch his drinking.
雷木斯已經能夠看出晚上的走向，於是坐得離小天狼星盡可能遠。他們已經同意了小天狼星和詹姆斯共用一個帳篷，彼得和雷木斯在另一個帳篷裡，所以至少那裡不會有尷尬。他只需要注意他的飲酒。

Mary had lit a fire using magic while Lily had been gone (“no one tell her, all right? I’m not about to sit here freezing my snatch off while Potter and Black piss about rubbing sticks together.”), and Marlene had brought a wireless radio, so once the cans of cider had been passed around it was a very cosy scene indeed.
瑪麗用魔法點燃了火，而莉莉不在時（“沒人告訴她，好嗎？我不想在這裡坐著，讓自己冷得快凍僵了，而波特和布萊克卻在那裡用木棍摩擦。”），馬琳帶來了一台無線電，所以當蘋果酒的罐子傳來傳去時，這確實是一個非常舒適的場景。

“How long have you two been going out?” Dorcas asked James and Lily. They leapt apart, looking at each other guiltily.
“你們倆在一起多久了？”多卡斯問詹姆斯和莉莉。他們分開，彼此愧疚地看著對方。

“We’re not!” Lily squeaked, moving to sit next to Remus, as if to prove it. Mary and Marlene exchanged a look, and Sirius shot a confused glance at James.
“我們沒有！”莉莉尖叫道，移到雷木斯旁邊坐著，彷彿要證明什麼。瑪麗和馬琳交換了眼色，小天狼星對詹姆斯投去困惑的目光。

“Oh, sorry!” Dorcas smiled, oblivious, “I just thought… but Sirius and Mary, you used to go out, right?”
“哦，對不起！”多卡斯笑道，毫無察覺，“我只是以為……但小天狼星和瑪麗，你們以前交往過，對吧？”

“For my sins,” Mary squawked, laughing. Sirius poked his tongue out at her.
“作為我的罪過，”瑪麗尖叫著，笑了。小天狼星對她吐了吐舌頭。

Marlene, who had been reading a guidebook she’d bought in the visitor’s information centre, cleared her throat loudly,
“馬琳，之前在遊客資訊中心買了一本指南的，清了清嗓子，

“There’s a castle ruin not far from here, we could go tomorrow?” Which swiftly changed the subject to plans for the rest of the week. Camping holidays seemed to involve a lot of walking, Remus realised. He hoped his hip would be up to it.
“這裡不遠處有一座城堡遺址，我們可以明天去看看？”話題迅速轉向了接下來一週的計劃。雷木斯意識到露營假期似乎涉及大量的步行。他希望他的臀部能夠承受。

A few tins in and they were all in a very silly mood. The drink was flat and clear, which Remus knew was a dangerous sign when it came to cider. They’d all have skull-splitting headaches in the morning if they weren’t careful. He didn’t bring it up, though - everyone was so happy, why spoil it worrying about consequences?
喝了幾罐之後，他們都變得非常愚蠢。飲料是平的且清澈的，雷木斯知道這在蘋果酒中是一個危險的跡象。如果他們不小心的話，早晨都會有令人頭痛欲裂的頭痛。他沒有提起這點——大家都這麼開心，為什麼要擔心後果來破壞這種感覺呢？

Dorcas was lying back on Peter’s chest, using him as an armchair, humming softly to the music. He was trying to get his hand under her shirt, and thought he was being discreet. Mary and Marlene were whispering to each other, bursting into giggles every now and then. James and Sirius were throwing stones into the fire – it was obviously a competition of sorts, but Remus couldn’t figure out what the rules were supposed to be.
多卡斯躺在彼得的胸膛上，當作扶手椅，輕聲哼著音樂。他試圖把手伸進她的襯衫下，認為自己很隱蔽。瑪麗和馬琳互相低語著，時不時地爆發出笑聲。詹姆斯和小天狼星在往火裡扔石頭——顯然是一種比賽，但雷木斯無法弄清楚規則是什麼。

A familiar tune began to play on the radio – Mott the Hoople. It was a few years old now, but it had been a favourite at Gryffindor parties,
無線電上開始播放一首熟悉的曲調——Mott the Hoople。現在已經有幾年了，但這一直是格蘭芬多派對上的最愛，

“Billy rapped all night about his suicide,
“比利整晚都在談論他的自殺，

How he’d kick it in the head when he was twenty-five,
他二十五歲時會一腳踢到頭，

Speed jive, don’t wanna stay alive, when you’re twenty five…”
迅速搖擺，不想活到二十五歲……”

“Turn it up!” Mary nudged Marlene, who flicked her wand at the wireless, lazily, then cracked open another can. They all hushed to listen, nodding along and tapping their feet softly on the grass. When the chorus came, the girls all sang along in that soft, under the breath way that girls were so good at,
“把音量調高！”瑪麗輕推馬琳，馬琳懶洋洋地對著無線電揮了揮魔杖，然後又打開了一罐。他們都靜靜地聽著，點頭附和，輕輕地在草地上打拍子。當副歌來臨時，女孩們以她們擅長的那種輕聲、低語的方式一起唱，

“All the young dudes, carry the news…”
“所有年輕的傢伙，傳播消息……”

When the song finished they cheered drunkenly, laughing amongst themselves.
當歌曲結束時，他們醉醺醺地歡呼，彼此間笑著。

“I bloody love you lot,” Marlene slurred, “You’re all my best friends,”
“我他媽地愛你們，”馬琳含糊地說，“你們都是我最好的朋友，”

“Same to you, McKinnon,” Sirius grinned across the flames, raising his can.
“我也是，麥金農，”小天狼星笑著舉起罐子，穿過火焰。

“Shhh!” She waggled a drunken finger at him, dopily, “I know your game, Black. I’ll have you know, you’re not my type.”
“嘘！”她迷迷糊糊地對他揮了揮醉酒的手指，“我知道你的把戲，布萊克。我告訴你，你不是我的類型。”

Everybody laughed at that, even Sirius.
大家都笑了出來，連小天狼星也不例外。

“When are we going to find you a nice girl, hm Remus?” Lily said, thoughtfully, squeezing up to him for warmth and laying her head on his shoulder.
“我們什麼時候才能給你找個好女孩，嗯，雷木斯？”莉莉若有所思地說，靠在他身上取暖，把頭靠在他的肩膀上。

He smiled wanly, putting an affectionate arm around her.
他微笑著，親切地把手臂搭在她身上。

“Yeah, you deserve a bit of fun, Moony,” James winked at him.
“是啊，你應該享受點樂趣，月亮狼，”詹姆斯對他眨了眨眼。

Remus avoided Sirius sudden glare by taking another swig from his can.
雷木斯通過再次啜飲罐中的飲料來避開小天狼星突然的怒視。

“I have plenty of fun with you lot.” He said.
“我和你們在一起很開心。”他說。

“Have you ever had a girlfriend, Remus?” Dorcas asked. She didn’t mean anything by it; she didn’t know them very well. But there was an awkward hush all the same. Or maybe Remus was the only one who noticed. He glanced up at Mary coyly and smiled.
“你曾經有過女朋友嗎，雷木斯？”多卡斯問道。她並沒有什麼其他意思；她不太了解他們。但無論如何，氣氛變得尷尬。或者也許只有雷木斯注意到了。他害羞地看了一眼瑪麗，然後微笑著。

“Nah,” he said.
“沒有，”他說。

“Aww,” Dorcas said, very tipsy, “How come?”
“哦，”多卡斯說，已經很醉了，“為什麼呢？”

Suddenly, it dawned on Remus. Marlene was right – he loved these people, every one of them. What was the point, keeping secrets from them? This wasn’t up to Sirius, this wasn’t up to anyone but him. He breathed in and looked at the fire again.
突然，雷木斯領悟到了。馬琳是對的——他愛這些人，每一個。他隱瞞秘密又有什麼意義呢？這不是小天狼星的事，也不是任何人的事，只有他自己。他深吸一口氣，再次看向火焰。

“I’m gay.” He said.
“我喜歡男人。”他說。

Peter choked on his drink. Out of the corner of his eye, Remus saw James run his hands through his hair, sit up straighter. He saw Mary’s mouth fall open, and heard Marlene give out a surprised hiccup. He dared not look at Sirius. His stomach turned and he prepared to get up, to walk away and apparate somewhere. Anywhere.
彼得被他的飲料呛到了。雷木斯從眼角瞥見詹姆斯把手伸進頭髮中，坐得更直。他看到瑪麗的嘴巴張開了，聽到馬琳發出了驚訝的嗝聲。他不敢看小天狼星。他的胃翻江倒海，他準備站起來，離開並瞬移到某個地方。隨便哪裡。

But then Lily raised her head. She kissed his cheek and hugged him tighter, before settling back down against his shoulder.
但隨後莉莉抬起頭來。她吻了他的臉頰，緊緊擁抱了他，然後再次靠在他的肩膀上。

“You still deserve some fun.” She said, decisively.
“你仍然應該享受點樂趣。”她斷然地說。

 

Chapter 115: Summer 1977: Part 2 

Sweet handsome friend, I can tell you truly

that I've never been without desire

since it pleased you that I have you as my lover;

nor did a time ever arrive, sweet handsome friend,

when I didn't want to see you often;

nor did I ever feel regret,

nor did it ever come to pass, if you went off angry,

that I felt joy until you had come back;

nor [ever].

- Tibors de Sarenom

 

Two hours later...

 

Peter and Dorcas were snogging, rolling backwards onto the grass. Everyone was drunk, but they were probably the drunkest.
彼得和多卡斯在接吻，向後滾到草地上。每個人都醉了，但他們可能是最醉的。

“Go back to your tent, if you’re going to do that!” James threw an empty cider can at them.
“要是你們要這麼做，就回你們的帳篷去吧！”詹姆斯向他們扔了一個空的蘋果酒罐。

“D’you mind, Moony?” Peter surfaced, red in the face and bleary eyed, “If we go back to ours? You can bunk in with Prongs and Padfoot, can’t you?”
“你介意嗎，月亮狼？”彼得浮出水面，臉紅而迷糊地問，“我們要是回到我們那個帳篷，你可以和詹姆斯和小天狼星挤在一起，不是嗎？”

“Oh, don’t worry,” Remus waved a hand, “I’ll find somewhere.” Sirius still hadn’t looked at him, and he had a feeling that after the evening’s revelations he would not be particularly welcome.
“哦，別擔心，”雷木斯揮了揮手，“我會找地方的。”小天狼星仍然沒有看他，他覺得在今晚的揭示後，他可能不會受到特別的歡迎。

Peter and Dorcas disappeared, there was muffled giggling from within the tent, then the ghostly, hollow quiet of a silencing charm.
彼得和多卡斯消失了，帳篷裡傳來了悶悶的笑聲，接著是靜音咒語所帶來的幽靈般的寂靜。

“Share with us if you want, Remus?” Mary said, getting up to leave for her own tent. Lily nodded,
“要是你願意的話，和我們一起睡吧，雷木斯？”瑪麗說，起身要回自己的帳篷。莉莉點了點頭，

“Yeah, our tent’s much bigger – come in with us.”
“是啊，我們的帳篷大得多——來和我們一起吧。”

“Thanks girls,” He smiled – he really was grateful. “You go on – I’m not tired yet. Think I’ll just go for a walk.”
“謝謝你們，女孩們，”他微笑著——他真的很感激。“你們先走吧——我還不累。我想我會去散散步。”

He got up, limbs stiff and aching, and headed for the sea. It was properly dark now, away from the fire, but Remus had always been able to see in the dark. The tide was in, and louder than ever. A cold breeze flew forth, and he fumbled in his back pocket for a cigarette. He lit up and inhaled deeply, closing his eyes, feeling that now he could really think.
他站起來，四肢僵硬而疼痛，朝海邊走去。現在遠離火光，已經完全黑了，但雷木斯總是能在黑暗中看得清楚。潮水已經漲上來，比以往更大聲。一陣冷風吹來，他在後口袋裡摸索著找煙。他點燃了煙，深吸了一口氣，閉上眼睛，感覺到自己現在可以真正思考。

He was glad he’d said it, no matter what the reaction, but he still considered leaving. Ok, so they weren’t all about to kick his head in, but who knew how they’d all act in the cold light of morning, stark and sober. Was it better or worse than being a werewolf?
他很高興自己說出來了，不管反應如何，但他仍然考慮離開。好吧，他們不是都要揍他一頓，但誰知道他們在清晨的冷光中會怎麼反應，醒來後會怎麼樣。這比做狼人好還是壞呢？

He could still apparate, if he wanted to; go and look for Grant, maybe. Remus felt a surge of guilt. He hadn’t thought about Grant in a while – maybe not all year. The other boy had been so kind to him; taken him in and been willing to put him up indefinitely. He’d given Remus some excellent advice too, if only Remus had taken it. Stay away from posh boys.
如果他想的話，他仍然可以瞬移；去找格蘭特，或許。他感到一陣內疚。他已經有一段時間沒有想到格蘭特了——可能整年都沒有。那個男孩對他非常友善；接納了他並願意無限期地容納他。他還給了雷木斯一些很好的建議，如果雷木斯能接受的話。遠離高貴的男孩。

Chapter 116: Summer 1977: Part 3 

Remus woke up and stretched beneath bright canvas, Sirius breathing lightly beside him. It was a little bit too warm and sticky, but he wouldn’t have moved for anything. Lying peacefully under the blankets, he could still taste the salt on Sirius’s skin, feel his heartbeat. At the bottom of the sleeping bag, their feet were tangled together. Remus在明亮的帆布下醒來並伸了個懶腰，Sirius在他身旁輕輕地呼吸著。天氣有點太熱和黏膩，但他什麼也不願意動。安靜地躺在毯子下，他仍然能夠品嚐到Sirius皮膚上的鹽味，感受到他的心跳。在睡袋的底部，他們的腳纏在一起。

Sirius stirred, screwing up his face before he opened his eyes. Sirius動了一下，皺著臉然後睜開眼睛。

“Morning.” 「早安。」

“Morning.” 「早安。」

“Fuck me, my mouth is dry.” 「見鬼，我的嘴巴好乾。」

“Yeah, mine too,” Remus agreed, running his tongue over his teeth. All that cider. “I could go and get some water from the pump?” 「是啊，我也是，」Remus同意道，舌頭在牙齒上滑過。都是那該死的蘋果酒。「我可以去泵那邊取點水嗎？」

Remus listened carefully, then shook his head. He hoped Sirius wasn’t worried about getting caught - surely no one could question their sharing a tent? What else could they have done? It was probably a bit early to start interrogating Sirius, so Remus held his tongue as they dressed quietly and quickly, fishing about in the bottom of the bed for their clothes, which seemed to have scattered in the night. Clambering out and blinking hard against the bright daylight, Remus thought that everything seemed to look different. The same; but not quite as he’d remembered it before. More realistic; solid and anchored down. 爬出帳篷並對抗明亮的日光眨著眼睛，Remus覺得一切看起來都不一樣了。相同的，但並不像他之前記得的那樣。更真實；堅實且穩定。

They sauntered off in the direction of the water pump with their canteens, and as they walked, they fell into step, and Remus felt as though his heart would burst with joy. Stupid, really, such a small thing. The campsite was lovely and peaceful, sparrows darting between the trees overhead, and the occasional camper popping their head out and wishing a polite ‘good morning’ to the boys as they passed. 他們拿著水壺朝水泵的方向漫步走去，走著走著，他們步調一致，Remus覺得自己的心幾乎要因為喜悅而爆炸。真的很愚蠢，這麼小的事情。營地非常可愛和平靜，麻雀在樹上飛來飛去，偶爾有露營者探出頭來，經過時禮貌地對男孩們說「早安」。

The water pump was by the shower block, and they both ducked in to wash their faces quickly, before filling their canteens, as well as the others they’d brought. 水泵在淋浴間旁邊，他們都迅速低頭洗了臉，然後填滿他們的水壺，以及其他他們帶來的水壺。

“Shop sells pasties,” Sirius said, thoughtfully, nodding in the direction of a little wooden hut with a blue and white striped awning, “Shall we get some for breakfast, return to the camp as heroes?” 「小店賣餡餅，」Sirius若有所思地說，點頭指著一個有藍白條紋遮陽篷的小木屋，「我們買些當早餐，回營地當英雄？」

“Good idea,” Remus smiled, shyly. 「好主意，」Remus害羞地笑了笑。

They bought far too many Cornish pasties, but they were fresh out of the oven, flaky and buttery and warm, and Sirius had no impulse control. 他們買了太多康沃爾餡餅，但它們是剛出爐的，酥脆、奶油味濃且溫暖，而Sirius無法控制衝動。

Remus held his breath, not sure what was coming, but somehow knowing he needed to hear it. “You have so many secrets, and it must be so shit, keeping things back,” Sirius began, gaining momentum the more he spoke, “And I made it all worse, I just gave you more things to hide…” 「但是，這真的不是沒事，」他的眉頭微微皺起，搜尋著他需要的詞語。Remus屏住呼吸，不確定接下來會發生什麼，但他知道自己需要聽到這些。「你有那麼多秘密，保持這些秘密一定很糟糕，」Sirius開始說，隨著他說得越多，動力越大，「而我讓一切變得更糟糕，我只是讓你有更多的東西要隱藏……」

I’ve loved keeping your secret, Remus wanted to say, I’d keep a thousand more, for you. He knew that this line of thinking could only make things worse, so he said nothing. Sirius risked reaching out, grasping Remus’s hand and holding it. Remus squeezed back. Remus想說，我喜歡保守你的秘密，我願意為你保守千萬個秘密。他知道這種想法只會讓事情變得更糟，所以他什麼也沒說。Sirius冒險伸出手，握住了Remus的手。Remus回握。

Sirius looked at him, full of pleading. Remus forgave him wholeheartedly. It wasn’t difficult to meet his eyes any more. Sirius看著他，滿是懇求。Remus全心全意地原諒了他。再也不難與他的眼神相遇。

“James seemed… pretty ok with me being queer.” Remus prompted, quietly. He felt a bit underhanded, bringing up James - James belonged to Sirius, it wasn’t Remus’s business to interfere. 「James看起來……對我同性戀這件事還挺好的。」Remus輕聲提到。他覺得這有點卑鄙，提起James——James屬於Sirius，這不是Remus該干涉的事。
