“Ok,” Remus said. He was agreeing to everything, he knew it was stupid. But it was so easy now. 「好吧，」Remus說。他同意了所有的事情，他知道這很愚蠢。但現在這樣真的很容易。

“Morning, lads!” Mary yelled from the campsite, Sirius pulled his hand back, quickly, giving Remus an apologetic glance, “Cheers for the pasties!” 「早安，伙計們！」Mary從營地喊道，Sirius迅速把手收回來，歉意地看了Remus一眼，「謝謝你們的餡餅！」

They both turned around and waved at her. Sirius got up, extending an arm to help Remus to his feet. 他們都轉過身來，朝她揮手。Sirius站起來，伸出手臂幫助Remus起身。

“C’mon,” he said, eyes twinkling, “I can’t wait to rip the shit out of Prongs for finally getting his leg over.” 「來吧，」他說，眼睛閃閃發光，「我迫不及待地想取笑Prongs終於得手了。」

“Not in front of Lily!” Remus cautioned, “She’ll curse your knob off.” 「不要在Lily面前！」Remus警告道，「她會詛咒你的。」

“Well, can’t have that, I’m very attached to my knob.” 「那可不行，我很喜歡我的。」

“Sirius?” 「Sirius？」

“Remus?” 「Remus？」

“This isn’t just for the summer, is it?” 「這不僅僅是夏天的事，對吧？」

Sirius looked at him and grinned. Sirius看著他，笑了。

“I bloody hope not.” 「我真的希望不是。」

 

 

Fortunately, no one was much interested in whatever Sirius and Remus had been up to the night before, because everybody else's night had been just as eventful. Peter gave him a bit of a wary look, but that might have been the hangover. Mary was grinning at everyone like the cat who’d got the cream, picking at her pasty and trying to catch Lily’s eye. 「幸運的是，沒有人太在意Sirius和Remus昨晚做了什麼，因為每個人的夜晚都同樣充滿了事件。Peter有點警惕地看著他，但那可能是宿醉的緣故。Mary笑得像隻得了奶油的貓，吃著餡餅，試圖引起Lily的注意。」

Marlene was bundled up in blankets, looking very green around the gills and giving out the occasional moan. 「Marlene裹在毯子裡，臉色蒼白，不時發出呻吟。」

“Alright, Marls?” Remus asked, gently. 「還好嗎，Marls？」Remus輕聲問道。

“Mmmmph.” 「嗯嗯。」

“Poor love,” Mary tutted, patting her friend’s blonde head gently, “Went a bit hard on the Old Rosie, didn’t you? Still, could be worse. Dorcas hasn’t come back from the loo’s, yet.” 「可憐的愛人，」Mary咂嘴，輕輕拍著朋友的金髮頭，「你喝Old Rosie喝得太多了，不是嗎？不過，還好，Dorcas還沒從廁所回來呢。」

James and Lily were sitting next to each other, but not too close. Lily had scraped her hair back in a pigtail, and was consciously staring at the ground, eating her pasty with a kind of quiet resignation. James looked absolutely chuffed, but was trying not to show it too much. 「James和Lily坐在一起，但不是很近。Lily把頭髮紮成馬尾辮，有意識地盯著地面，帶著一種安靜的無奈吃著餡餅。James看起來非常高興，但試圖不表現得太明顯。」

“So…” Mary grinned, widely, looking around at everyone, “We’ll stick with the new sleeping arrangements for the rest of the week, then, shall we?” 「那麼……」Mary大笑著，看著大家，「我們這週就繼續用新的睡覺安排，是嗎？」

“Suits me.” Sirius said, casually. 「對我來說沒問題。」Sirius隨意地說。

“And me,” Peter nodded, mouth full of mince. 「我也是，」Peter點頭，嘴裡塞滿了肉餡。

Marlene gave a silent, queasy thumbs up. James and Lily looked at each other, then looked away. 「Marlene默默地舉起了一個噁心的拇指。James和Lily互相看了一眼，然後轉開目光。」

Once everyone had finished eating, the girls arranged an expedition to the shower block. The boys followed after, towels under their arms and Sirius teased James mercilessly. 「大家吃完後，女孩們安排了一次去淋浴間的探險。男孩們跟在後面，胳膊下夾著毛巾，Sirius無情地戲弄James。」

“No, go away, I’m not telling you anything.” James laughed. 「不，走開，我不會告訴你任何事情。」James笑著說。

“This is purely for academic purposes,” Sirius chided, “It’s going to be a matter of historical interest, future generations will need to know what miraculous feats you had to perform in order to finally convince Evans to--” 「這純粹是為了學術目的，」Sirius責備道，「這將是一個歷史興趣的問題，未來的世代需要知道你必須做出什麼奇蹟般的壯舉才能最終說服Evans——」

“We just talked!” 「我們只是聊天！」

“Oh, so the silencing spell was for…?” 「哦，那麼消音咒是為了……？」

James turned bright red and disappeared inside a shower cubicle. Sirius chucked triumphantly. 「James臉紅了，消失在淋浴間裡。Sirius得意地笑了。」

“Doesn’t anyone want to know about me and Dorcas?” Peter asked, innocently. 「沒人想知道我和Dorcas的事嗎？」Peter天真地問道。

The castle ruins were about five miles walk, which nobody seemed to think was too far at all. Marlene had perked up a bit after showering and eating, and everyone decided that fresh air was probably the best cure for a hangover. They zipped up their tents, stuffing valuables into rucksacks - along with some leftover pasties and bottles of water - and set off around eleven. 「城堡遺址大約有五英里的步行路程，似乎沒有人覺得這太遠了。Marlene在洗澡和吃飯後精神好多了，大家決定新鮮空氣可能是宿醉最好的解藥。他們拉上帳篷的拉鍊，把貴重物品塞進背包——還有一些剩下的餡餅和瓶裝水——大約在十一點出發。」

They followed a footpath along the shoreline, which curled around and gradually steepened into a cliff. The view at the top was breath-taking, but Remus was struggling to enjoy it much - his eyes watered and his legs burned with the effort of clambering uphill. Sirius, Marlene and Mary had raced to the top; Marlene coming first despite her queasiness. James surprised Remus by slowing down to match his own shambling crawl. 「他們沿著海岸線的小路走，小路繞著彎逐漸變成陡峭的懸崖。山頂的景色令人嘆為觀止，但Remus很難享受——他眼睛流淚，腿因爬山的努力而灼熱。Sirius、Marlene和Mary已經賽跑到了頂端；儘管感到噁心，Marlene還是第一個到達。James放慢腳步以配合他自己的蹣跚爬行，這讓Remus感到驚訝。」

“Alright there, Moony?” He asked, cheerfully. 「還好嗎，Moony？」他愉快地問道。

“Brilliant,” Remus panted, not sure if he was pulling off sarcasm or just sounded like a terrible liar. 「太棒了，」Remus喘著氣，不確定自己是在諷刺還是聽起來像個糟糕的騙子。」

“We’re in no rush, take it easy.” 「我們不著急，慢慢來。」

“Hmmph.” 「哼。」

“Padfoot wasn’t too much of a tosser last night, was he? About the whole… er… about the stuff you told us?” 「Padfoot昨晚沒有太過分吧，關於整個……呃……關於你告訴我們的事情？」

Remus shook his head, focussing on breathing, and the horrible grind-click noise that hard started happening in his hip every time he stepped forward. 「Remus搖了搖頭，專注於呼吸，以及每次向前走時他臀部發出的可怕的磨擦聲。」

“Good,” James nodded, relieved, “I just worried he might be, y’know what his family was like about that kind of thing. Was in two minds about leaving him alone with you to be honest, but I thought you’d just give him a thump if he got out of order.” 「很好，」James點頭，鬆了口氣，「我只是擔心他可能會，你知道他的家庭對那種事情的看法。老實說，我對讓他和你單獨在一起有點猶豫，但我想如果他失控了，你會給他一拳。」

“Everything’s fine,” Remus wheezed, “Don’t worry.” 「一切都好，」Remus喘著氣說，「別擔心。」

“Good.” James said again, and stopped, because Remus had. Just for a moment. 「很好。」James再次說，然後停下來，因為Remus停下來了。只是片刻。

The other six had crested the hill now, and were disappearing down the other side. They’d only been walking for twenty minutes, Remus thought grimly. He wondered if he could apparate ahead - but the ‘deliberation’ part would be difficult, without a map, or having seen the place before. He was embarrassed, having James stay back with him, but at least it wasn’t one of the girls. 「其他六個人已經登上了山頂，並消失在另一邊。他們只走了二十分鐘，Remus陰鬱地想。他想知道自己是否可以先幻影移形——但沒有地圖或以前見過這個地方的話，‘慎思’部分會很困難。他對James留在他身邊感到尷尬，但至少不是其中一個女孩。」

“Sorry,” he said, wiping sweat from his brow, “Usually not as bad this far away from the moon.” 「對不起，」他擦著額頭上的汗說，「通常離月亮這麼遠不會這麼糟。」

“S’fine,” James shrugged, “We’re on holiday, not a route march.” 「沒事，」James耸肩，「我們在度假，不是行軍。」

“Don’t you want to catch up with Lily? I’ll be fine.” 「你不想追上Lily嗎？我會沒事的。」

“Giving her a bit of space. I think she’s embarrassed.” 「給她點空間。我覺得她有點尷尬。」

“She really likes you, though,” Remus said, encouragingly, “She told me.” 「她真的很喜歡你，」Remus鼓勵地說，「她告訴我的。」

“I know,” James smiled, getting that dopey, dreamy look as he stared over the clifftop, “Can’t believe my bloody luck.” He cleared his throat, “But it was just talking, all right? that’s the party line, don’t say anything to Black.”
「我知道，」James笑著，凝視懸崖頂部，露出那種愚笨的夢幻神情，「真不敢相信我的好運。」他清了清喉嚨，「但只是聊天，好嗎？這是官方說法，別告訴Black。」

Remus laughed, straightening up, 「Remus笑了，挺直身體，」

“I won’t.” They began to walk again, steadily. The sun was reaching its highest point, blazing above them so that they had to squint, or look at their feet. 「我不會的。」他們又開始穩步行走。太陽正到達最高點，在他們上方炙烤，使他們不得不瞇起眼睛，或者看著腳下。」

“We talked about you, actually,” James said. “Well, Lily did. I listened.” 「其實我們談到了你，」James說。「嗯，Lily說的。我在聽。」

“Oh?” 「哦？」

“Yeah - nothing horrible, I promise! I think it was probably just the cider and we were both rambling about how you were such a good mate, and then she said something about being brave and making your feelings known and living honestly, or… oh, I dunno, I was too busy being amazed she was even talking to me.” 「是的——沒有什麼可怕的，我保證！我想可能只是蘋果酒，我們都在胡亂說你是多麼好的朋友，然後她說了一些關於勇敢地表達感情和誠實生活的話，或者……哦，我不知道，我太忙於驚訝她竟然在和我說話。」

Remus smiled at James, and wanted to hug him on Lily’s behalf. 「Remus對James微笑，想代Lily擁抱他。」

They reached the castle two hours later, a good half an hour behind the rest of the group, who had waited for them. 「他們在兩個小時後到達了城堡，比其他人晚了半小時，其他人已經在等他們。」

“Sorry,” Sirius said, once they were out of earshot of the others, “I didn’t think.” 「對不起，」Sirius說，等他們走到其他人聽不見的地方，「我沒想那麼多。」

“I’m fine,” Remus smiled, trying to hide his exhaustion, “I had Prongs.” 「我沒事，」Remus微笑，試圖掩飾他的疲憊，「我有Prongs。」

“There’s a local bus that goes back past the campsite, I checked,” Sirius said, gallantly, “We can get that back, if you want?” 「有一輛當地的巴士會經過露營地，我查過了，」Sirius紳士地說，「如果你想，我們可以坐那輛回去？」

“I’m fine.” 「我沒事。」

The castle was a ruin, beautiful grey stone in the summer sunshine, cast against the glistening sea, hundreds of feet below. Remus could barely believe anyone had really lived there - the narrow spiral staircases had crumbled and led nowhere, long grass and bright yellow dandelions had invaded what might once have been a great feasting hall. There were arrow slits in the remaining walls, and graffiti carved into the parapets, where no doubt some bored soldier had waited once, a thousand years ago. Perhaps he hadn’t been much older than they were. War never changed. 「這座城堡是一片廢墟，夏日陽光下的美麗灰色石頭，映襯著數百英尺下閃閃發光的海洋。Remus幾乎無法相信曾經有人真的住在這裡——狹窄的螺旋樓梯已經崩塌，通向無處，長草和明亮的黃色蒲公英侵佔了曾經可能是一個偉大宴會廳的地方。剩下的牆上有箭孔，雉堞上刻有塗鴉，無疑一千年前一些無聊的士兵曾在那裡等待。也許他們並不比他們年長多少。戰爭從未改變。」

James, Peter and Sirius began a very enthusiastic sword fight with some stray sticks they’d found, while Remus sat rolling up cigarettes on a pile of rocks, watching them. 「James, Peter和Sirius開始用他們找到的一些樹枝進行非常熱情的劍鬥，而Remus坐在一堆石頭上捲煙，觀看他們。」

“You’d feel a lot fitter if you didn’t fill your lungs up with that shit,” Marlene tutted. 「如果你不讓你的肺裝滿那些垃圾，你會覺得健康很多，」Marlene咂嘴說。」

“Here for a good time, not a long time, Marls,” he replied, dryly, licking the adhesive strip on his paper and sticking it down carefully. 「來這裡是為了享受，不是長時間，Marls，」他乾巴巴地回答，舔著紙上的粘條，小心地粘好。」

He made four or five, just to pass the time, tucking them neatly into an old matchbox he’d saved for the purpose. He watched Sirius, playing the knight against Peter’s dragon, and laughed as James captured Lily - apparently now a princess - hoisting her effortlessly over his shoulder and running for the castle gates. She laughed and beat her fits against his back playfully, and when he put her down she looked so happy in his arms. 「他做了四五個，只是為了消磨時間，將它們整齊地放進他為此保留的一個舊火柴盒裡。他看著Sirius扮演騎士對抗Peter的龍，並且當James抓住Lily——顯然現在是公主——輕鬆地將她扛在肩上跑向城堡大門時，他笑了。她笑著玩笑地打著他的背，當他把她放下時，她在他懷裡顯得那麼快樂。」

Eventually, some of the other tourists started to get a bit annoyed with the eight teenagers mucking about, so they decided it was time to go back down to the beach and spend the rest of the afternoon cooling off in the sea. 「最終，一些其他遊客開始對這八個少年胡鬧感到有些惱火，所以他們決定是時候回到海灘，度過剩下的下午在海裡涼快。」

Lily and James led the group this time, hand in hand, chattering happily as if they had been this intimate for years. A pang of envy shot through Remus. Not that he wanted to hold Sirius’s hand. For one thing, it was much too hot, for another, you couldn’t keep Sirius still long enough. 「這次是Lily和James手牽手領著大家，快樂地聊天，仿佛他們已經這麼親密多年。Remus感到一陣嫉妒。並不是說他想牽著Sirius的手。一方面，天氣太熱了，另一方面，你無法讓Sirius靜止足夠長的時間。」

“You lot go ahead,” Sirius called, “Me and Moony are having a fag break.” 「你們先走，」Sirius喊道，「我和Moony要休息一下抽根煙。」

Marlene tutted once more, but hurried to catch up with the others. 「Marlene再次咂嘴，但急忙趕上其他人。」

Remus and Sirius sat on a stone wall for a bit, smoking. 「Remus和Sirius坐在石牆上抽煙。」

“There’s a pub down there,” Sirius nodded further up the lane. “Saw it on the way up, it’s got a garden. Want to go and waste some time?” 「那邊有家酒吧，」Sirius點頭向車道上方，「上來的時候看到的，有個花園。想去那裡浪費點時間嗎？」

“Yeah,” Remus said, surprised. That sounded ideal. “But don’t you want to catch up with James?” 「好啊，」Remus驚訝地說。這聽起來很理想。「但你不想趕上James嗎？」

“James doesn’t love me anymore,” Sirius sighed, dramatically, holding his wrist against his forehead like an old woman about to faint, “His heart has been claimed by another.” 「James不再愛我了，」Sirius戲劇性地嘆息，像一個即將昏倒的老太太一樣將手腕放在額頭上，「他的心已經被別人佔據了。」

Remus laughed, then dared to say, 「Remus笑了，然後大膽地說，」

“Oh well. you’ve got me.” 「哦，好吧。你還有我。」

“I’ve got you,” Sirius nodded with a grin, hopping down from the wall. “C’mon, then. Could murder a pint.” 「我有你，」Sirius微笑著點頭，從牆上跳下來。「來吧。想喝杯啤酒。」

The pub was a small whitewashed cottage with mustard yellow shutters, a red tile roof and a neat row of red geraniums planted in pots outside. Inside was dark, musty and cavernous; Remus had to duck under the low ceiling. The gruff working men propping up the bar all turned to look as they entered, and for a moment Remus wondered if it had been a bad idea after all. 「這家酒吧是一個小小的粉刷過的平房，有芥末黃的百葉窗，紅色的瓷磚屋頂，外面整齊地種著一排紅色的天竺葵。裡面昏暗、霉臭且空曠；Remus不得不低頭走過低矮的天花板。那些支撐在吧台上的粗魯工人都轉過頭來看他們，有一刻Remus懷疑這是否真的是個壞主意。」

Still, Sirius ordered two pints of lager, and they took them outside to the garden, sitting on a table underneath a beech tree for shade. As they headed out, the surly barman and unfriendly locals turned back to their own drinks, obviously deciding to ignore the two boys. Remus was sure he heard one of them mutter ‘bloody toffs,’ which he took as a personal slight, though of course it could have been much worse. Still, they were alone in the garden, and had the privacy they’d been seeking. 「儘管如此，Sirius還是點了兩品脫啤酒，他們把啤酒拿到外面的花園，在一棵山毛櫸樹下的一張桌子上坐下乘涼。當他們走出去時，那個陰沉的酒保和不友好的當地人轉回他們自己的飲料上，顯然決定忽略這兩個男孩。Remus確信他聽到其中一個人嘀咕「該死的貴族」，他把這當作個人侮辱，儘管當然可能會更糟。不過，他們在花園裡是獨自一人，擁有他們尋求的隱私。」

Sirius was impervious to the attitudes of others - maybe he didn’t notice; maybe he just didn’t think muggles were worth worrying about. 「Sirius對他人的態度無動於衷——也許他沒有注意到；也許他只是覺得麻瓜不值得擔心。」

“It’s great here,” he said, gulping down his foggy, warm beer, “D’you think we could live here, when it’s all over?” 「這裡真不錯，」他說，一口喝下他的濁熱啤酒，「你覺得當一切結束後我們可以住在這裡嗎？」

“I like London,” Remus replied, “It’s what I’m used to.” 「我喜歡倫敦，」Remus回答，「這是我習慣的。」

“Remember you promised we could go to Carnaby Street,” Sirius said, playing with Remus’s matchbox, “This summer. I’m holding you to it.” 「記得你答應我們可以去Carnaby街，」Sirius說，玩著Remus的火柴盒，「這個夏天。我可記住你說的。」

“When did I say that?” 「我什麼時候說過？」

“Christmas.” 「聖誕節。」

“Oh, right. Ok, we’ll go.” 「哦，好吧。我們會去的。」

“I can’t believe you forgot.” 「真不敢相信你忘了。」

“Well you also spent half of Christmas trying to convince me to get a girlfriend, so…” 「嗯，你也花了半個聖誕節試圖說服我找個女朋友，所以……」

“Uggh,” Sirius groaned, apparently in shame, “Sorry. I thought it might help me er… feel less attached to you. Sounds a bit bonkers now I think about it...” 「唉，」Sirius呻吟道，顯然感到羞愧，「對不起。我以為這可能會幫助我……不那麼依賴你。現在想起來有點瘋狂……」

“Now it sounds bonkers,” Remus kicked him gently under the table. 「現在聽起來很瘋狂，」Remus在桌下輕輕踢了他一腳。」

“Logical thought processes are not my forte, Mr Moony,” Sirius laughed, with an aristocratic turn of his head, “You ought to make your peace with it if we’re going to… um… if we’re going to…” 「邏輯思維不是我的強項，Moony先生，」Sirius笑著，貴族般地轉過頭，「如果我們要……嗯……如果我們要……」

“Start going out…” Remus prompted, gently. Sirius gave him an apologetic smile, 「開始約會……」Remus輕聲提示。Sirius給了他一個抱歉的微笑，

“Going out, yeah.” He agreed. “Sorry.” 「約會，是的。」他同意了。「對不起。」

“You’ll get there,” Remus said, casually, gulping his pint. 「你會做到的，」Remus隨口說道，喝著他的啤酒。」

And with that, the ice was broken, and they began to talk. And talk, and talk. It was that easy; after months of failure to communicate, it seemed that the gates had now been flung open wide. They found that once they had begun, they couldn’t stop. Remus would relate some assumption he had made; some belief he had held about an interaction long ago, and what he thought it had meant at the time. And Sirius would shake his head with wide, earnest eyes and say; 「就這樣，冰被打破了，他們開始交談。聊啊聊。就這麼簡單；在幾個月的溝通失敗之後，似乎大門現在已經大開。他們發現，一旦開始，就停不下來。Remus會講述他所做的一些假設；他曾經對很久以前的一次互動抱有的某些信念，以及當時他認為它的意義。而Sirius會睜大認真的眼睛搖頭說，」

“But Moony, it wasn’t like that at all.” 「但是Moony，根本不是那樣的。」

When it came down to brass tacks, Remus discovered that much of his misery was his own making; that most of the time Sirius had never meant harm, and often hadn’t even known he was causing Remus any pain at all - it was just his own bungled idea of what was going on. They even talked about Mary. 「說到底，Remus發現他的許多痛苦都是他自己造成的；大多數時候，Sirius從未有意傷害，而且通常甚至不知道他在給Remus帶來任何痛苦——這只是他自己對正在發生的事情的拙劣理解。他們甚至談到了Mary。」

“I really did like her,” he said, “I think that’s what threw me off, in the beginning. Y’know, it wasn’t like girls weren’t doing it for me, in that department… and she was so confident.” 「我真的很喜歡她，」他說，「我想這就是一開始讓我困惑的原因。你知道，並不是說在那方面女孩對我沒有吸引力……而且她是那麼自信。」

“I thought you were just with her because you didn’t want to be with me.” 「我以為你和她在一起只是因為你不想和我在一起。」

“No.” Sirius said, firmly, “That’s a horrible thought. It was for her, not for you.” He looked at him, “Sorry.” 「不是的。」Sirius堅定地說，「這是個可怕的想法。那是為了她，不是為了你。」他看著他，「對不起。」

“Ha, don’t be. That makes me feel better, actually.” 「哈，不用。其實這讓我感覺好些了。」

“Anyway,” Sirius smirked, “What about you and Mary?” 「無論如何，」Sirius笑了笑，「你和Mary呢？」

“Oh god,” Remus buried his face in his hands, “Don’t. I’m so embarrassed.” 「哦天哪，」Remus把臉埋在手裡，「別提了。我太尷尬了。」

“It’s fine. I liked it.” Sirius raised an eyebrow, giving Remus a look so sultry it would probably get him arrested in some parts of the country. 「沒關係。我喜歡。」Sirius挑了挑眉，給了Remus一個如此性感的眼神，以至於在國內某些地方可能會因此被捕。」

“I noticed.” He blushed, “Didn’t help you feel less attached, then?” 「我注意到了。」他臉紅了，「那也沒幫助你減少依戀，是嗎？」

“Apparently not.” 「顯然不是。」

“I couldn’t believe you didn’t mind that. And yet, when you found out about Chris…” 「我無法相信你不介意那個。而當你發現Chris的時候……」

Sirius straightened up, looking annoyed, 「Sirius挺直身體，顯得很惱火，」

“Him.” He grumbled. 「他。」他抱怨道。

“There’s nothing between us. We’re just friends.” 「我們之間沒什麼。我們只是朋友。」

“And… this other bloke… Grant? Was he...” Sirius shifted, obviously uncomfortable as he struggled to get the word out, “Your boyfriend?” 「還有……這個叫Grant的傢伙？他是……」Sirius轉了轉身，顯然不舒服，努力說出這個詞，「你的男朋友？」

“Not really,” Remus replied, easily, “It’s hard to explain. He’s… a friend. I care about him as much as I do you, and James, and Peter, and the girls.” 「不是的，」Remus輕鬆地回答，「這很難解釋。他是……一個朋友。我對他的關心程度和我對你、James、Peter和女孩們一樣。」

“More secrets, Remus.” Sirius ran his hands through his hair, frustrated, “I can’t keep track, I dunno how you do it. Can you stop hiding stuff? From me, at least?” 「更多的秘密，Remus。」Sirius沮喪地用手梳理著頭髮，「我跟不上，不知道你怎麼做到的。你能停止隱瞞東西嗎？至少對我？」

“I don’t know.” Remus said, quietly, “It’ll be hard.” 「我不知道。」Remus輕聲說，「這很難。」

“But you can try.” Sirius smiled. Remus chuckled, and nodded. 「但你可以試試。」Sirius微笑著說。Remus笑了笑，點了點頭。」

They finished their drinks, and decided to head back to the campsite. 「他們喝完了酒，決定回到露營地。」

“I’ll teach you to swim.” Sirius offered. 「我會教你游泳。」Sirius提議。」

“Fuck off, will you.” Remus snorted. 「去你的吧。」Remus哼了一聲。」

“Is there anything else you’ve been keeping secret, eh, Remu?” Sirius nudged him, as they meandered slowly downhill. It was much easier, the way back, but they were going very slowly anyway. 「還有什麼你一直隱瞞的秘密嗎，Remu？」Sirius推了推他，他們慢慢地走下坡路。回去的路要容易得多，但無論如何他們走得很慢。」

“Nope,” Remus laughed. He felt light as air - it was like being high; having nothing to hide at all, “Queer, illiterate, homeless, werewolf…” he ticked them off on his fingers, “I think that’s it. Oh, and my mother.” 「沒有，」Remus笑了。他感覺輕如鴻毛——就像嗑藥一樣；完全沒有什麼需要隱藏的，「同性戀，文盲，無家可歸，狼人……」他用手指數著，「我想就這些了。哦，還有我母親。」

“Your mother?!” 「你母親？！」

“I got a letter, in that box of depressing stuff from Dumbledore. Photos, and a letter - an apology.” 「我收到了信，在Dumbledore那箱令人沮喪的東西裡。照片，還有一封信——一封道歉信。」

“Oh, blimey, ok. What did it--” 「哦，天哪，好吧。那上面寫了什麼——」

“No, I don’t want to talk about it yet. Sorry.” 「不，我還不想談這個。對不起。」

“Fine,” Sirius shrugged, “Let’s say we can talk about anything at all, except our mothers.” 「好吧，」Sirius聳了聳肩，「我們可以談任何事情，除了我們的母親。」

“Perfect.” Remus nodded. 「完美。」Remus點了點頭。

 

- Old Rosie is cider, and if you drink too much of it you will regret it.
- Cornish pasties are the pinnacle of British cuisine.
- The incident Sirius is referring to (which triggered his interest in Remus) happened in Chapter 51.

 

Chapter 117: Summer 1977: Part 4 

The rest of the week in Cornwall passed in complete bliss, as far as Remus and Sirius were concerned. They spent long hot days on the beach and hillsides, wandering through quaint little villages, exploring caves and getting tipsy in pub gardens. They dined exclusively on pasties, fish and chips and ice cream, and at night - oh, the nights were best of all. 康沃爾的剩餘一周對Remus和Sirius來說簡直是極樂。他們在海灘和山坡上度過了漫長而炎熱的日子，漫遊在古樸的小村莊裡，探索洞穴並在酒吧花園裡微醺。他們的飲食僅限於餡餅、魚和薯條以及冰淇淋，而夜晚——哦，夜晚是最美好的。

During the day, if the others were around, they would toss a ball back and forth across the sand, or Remus would consent to paddle in the sea a little - jeans rolled up and long sleeved shirt still firmly on. If it was just the two of them, then he might roll the sleeves up to his elbows, exposing old scars, and Sirius would become Padfoot and chase sticks or his own tail. And they often got to be alone, because everyone else seemed to want to keep sneaking off. 白天，如果其他人在身邊，他們會在沙灘上來回拋球，或者Remus會同意在海裡踩踩水——捲起牛仔褲，仍然堅持穿著長袖襯衫。如果只有他們兩個，那麼他可能會把袖子捲到肘部，露出舊傷疤，而Sirius會變成Padfoot追逐棍子或自己的尾巴。而且他們經常能獨處，因為其他人似乎都想偷偷溜走。

Lily and James were the worst - when they weren’t bickering they were snogging; gratuitously, and at length. Lily和James是最糟糕的——他們不吵架的時候就在親熱；毫無節制，而且時間很長。

“You’re supposed to be prefects!” Mary yelled at them, after the third night, finding them practically horizontal in front of the campfire. 「你們應該是級長！」Mary在第三個晚上對他們大喊，發現他們幾乎橫躺在營火前。

“Oh, as if I haven’t caught you a hundred times on my rounds!” Lily laughed, getting up and straightening her clothes nonetheless. “And you, Black, so you can stop leering.” 「哦，好像我沒在巡邏時抓到你們一百次一樣！」Lily笑著站起來，整理著衣服。「還有你，Black，你可以停止色瞇瞇地看了。」

“What?” Sirius blinked, innocently. 「什麼？」Sirius天真地眨了眨眼。

He was carrying back the bowl of washing up from the shower block. Remus had been pretty amazed by that - Sirius had volunteered to do the dishes every night so far (“I quite like doing it, the muggle way,” he had confided, secretively, “Mother used to make us do the house elf’s work as a punishment sometimes, but I just found it relaxing, to be honest.”) 他正從淋浴區端回洗好的碗。Remus對此感到非常驚訝——Sirius自願每晚洗碗（「我挺喜歡用麻瓜的方式洗碗，」他偷偷告訴Remus，「母親有時會讓我們做家養小精靈的工作作為懲罰，但說實話，我覺得這很放鬆。」）

“Don’t draw me into your sordid escapades,” Sirius was saying, prudishly, setting down the tub. “I’ve been a perfect gentleman all holiday.” 「別把我牽扯到你們骯髒的冒險中去，」Sirius說，裝模作樣地放下了桶。「整個假期我都是一個完美的紳士。」

“I’m not convinced you haven’t been sneaking off with some muggle girl in the village.” Marlene said. She was lying stretched out on a towel in her underwear, sunbathing. Her body was very long and very pale. 「我不相信你沒跟村裡的某個麻瓜女孩偷偷溜走。」Marlene說。她只穿著內衣躺在毛巾上曬太陽。她的身體很長，很白。

“How dare you,” Sirius flicked her with the damp tea towel, making her yelp and crease up, “I’ve been tucked up in bed early every night, haven’t I, Moony?” 「你怎麼敢，」Sirius用濕毛巾輕輕打了她一下，讓她尖叫並皺起眉頭，「我每晚都早早上床，不是嗎，Moony？」

Remus choked on the crackers he’d been nibbling on, and had to be slapped on the back by James a few times before he recovered. You’ll pay for that later, Black, he glared at Sirius, eyes watering. Remus被他正在啃的餅乾噎住了，不得不被James拍了幾下背才恢復過來。你等著瞧，Black，他瞪著Sirius，眼睛都流淚了。

Once James had calmed down about the ‘Lily Evans Event’ (as Sirius was calling it, behind his back) enough to think straight, he’d been surprised that Sirius and Remus were now sharing a tent, and suspicious, for all the wrong reasons. 一旦James對「Lily Evans事件」（Sirius在背後這樣稱呼它）冷靜下來，足以理清思緒，他對Sirius和Remus現在共用一個帳篷感到驚訝，並因為所有錯誤的理由而感到懷疑。

“You’re not going to start fighting again, you two? You know you only wind each other up in close proximity...” 「你們倆不會又開始打架吧？你知道你們在近距離時只會互相挑釁……」

“Right you are, Prong,” Sirius said, brightly, “You bunk in with Moony and I’ll share with Evans.” 「你說得對，Prong，」Sirius愉快地說，「你和Moony住一起，我和Evans住。」

That put an end to that line of questioning, but not to James’s sudden overprotectiveness of Remus. It was nice - certainly nothing to whinge about - but a bit uncomfortable. Remus had never had any kind of big brother figure - unless you counted Ste or Craig, who had taught him to steal and drink and throw a proper punch - but James now seemed determined to do his clumsy, kind-hearted best. Midway through the week, Remus was a little surprised that no one had so much as mentioned the confession he had made on the first night. Not that he wanted anyone to make a fuss, or say anything sly or backhanded, but… still. Nothing at all? He brought it up with Sirius in a quiet moment, and he’d laughed, 這結束了那條問題線索，但沒有結束James對Remus的突然過度保護。這很好——當然沒什麼可抱怨的——但有點不舒服。Remus從來沒有任何大哥般的人物——除非你算上Ste或Craig，他們教他偷竊、喝酒和打出合適的一拳——但James現在似乎決心盡他笨拙、善良的最大努力。到了這周中期，Remus有點驚訝，沒有人提到他在第一個晚上所做的告白。並不是他希望有人大驚小怪，或者說什麼狡猾或隱晦的話，但……還是。什麼都沒有？他在一個安靜的時刻向Sirius提起這件事，Sirius笑了，

“Well if Prongs gave everyone else that bloody speech I’m not surprised.” 「嗯，如果Prongs對其他所有人都做了那該死的演講，我就不驚訝了。」

“Speech?” 「演講？」

“Yeah he pulled me aside and told me if I started treating you any differently he’d thump me. Probably didn’t say that to the girls - maybe Lily did them.” Sirius stretched out, doggishly, lying on his front. 「是啊，他把我拉到一邊，告訴我如果我開始對你有任何不同的對待，他會揍我。可能沒對女孩們說這些——也許是Lily說的。」Sirius像狗一樣伸展著，趴在前面。

They were lounging on the beach, alone, on a quiet stretch of sand which so far no one else had discovered. Sirius was in his swimming trunks and Remus was taking the opportunity to stare at him as much as he liked, and as brazenly as he liked. Every now and then he gathered a handful of silky yellow sand and poured it over Sirius’s skin, just to watch the grains slide like water over the muscles of his back. 他們正獨自在海灘上閒散地躺著，這片寧靜的沙灘目前還沒有人發現。Sirius穿著泳褲，Remus正抓住機會肆無忌憚地盯著他看。時不時地，他會抓一把絲滑的黃沙，倒在Sirius的皮膚上，只為了看著沙粒像水一樣滑過他背部的肌肉。

“You’re having me on.” Remus said, lazily, not believing Sirius. 「你在耍我吧。」Remus懶洋洋地說，不相信Sirius。

“Wish I was. I swear, it was so hard not to laugh in his face and just tell him everything.” He rolled over, brushing the sand away carelessly, “I’m going to have to go and wash off in a minute, if you keep doing that.” 「希望我是。我發誓，要不是忍住不在他臉上笑出來，然後告訴他一切，真是太難了。」他翻過身，漫不經心地刷掉沙子，「如果你繼續這樣，我得馬上去洗掉。」

“That’s the idea,” Remus smirked. Sirius in the sea was his new favourite thing to look at. 「這就是我的想法，」Remus得意地笑了。Sirius在海里是他的新寵。

Remus still didn’t really believe him, until the very last day of the holiday. They were all trying to pack up the tents - which didn’t seem to want to fit back into the bags they’d arrived in - and Remus had ended up taking over, because Peter, Sirius and James didn’t seem to understand the concept of instructions. The girls had deconstructed their own camp in less than an hour, and it was getting a bit shameful. Remus直到假期的最後一天仍然不太相信他。他們都在試圖收拾帳篷——這些帳篷似乎不想再回到他們到達時的袋子裡——最後由Remus接手，因為Peter、Sirius和James似乎不明白指示的概念。女孩們在不到一個小時內就拆除了自己的營地，這變得有點丟人。

“Right, that peg needs to come out first, and there’s a sort of top sheet we need to remove, otherwise everything gets tangled up…” Remus said, scratching his head. James and Sirius did this successfully and began folding up the brown canvas. 「好吧，先把那個帳篷釘拔出來，然後我們需要移除一個頂板，否則一切都會糾纏在一起……」Remus說，抓了抓頭。James和Sirius成功地做到了這一點，開始折疊棕色的帆布。

“What would we do without you, Moony,” James chuckled. 「沒有你我們該怎麼辦，Moony，」James輕笑道。

“Yeah,” Peter said from the ground, where he was collecting pegs, “Who’d have thought you’d be good at all this stuff.” 「是啊，」Peter從地上說道，他正在收集帳篷釘，「誰會想到你對這些事情這麼在行。」

“Well, I have always been the sensible one,” Remus murmured, not really paying it any mind, skimming the next few steps in the leaflet. Then he realised it had gone quiet, and James was standing over Peter. 「嗯，我一直是那個理智的人，」Remus喃喃道，並沒有真的在意，只是略讀了小冊子上的幾個步驟。然後他意識到周圍變得安靜了，James站在Peter上方。

“What do you mean, ‘this stuff’?” 「你說的‘這些事情’是什麼意思？」

Peter looked up, confused, and rubbed his hands together, Peter抬頭，困惑地揉了揉手，

“Y’know, outdoorsy stuff - blokey stuff. I didn’t mean--” 「你知道的，戶外的事情——男人的事情。我不是故意的——」

“Pete. A word.” James said, his voice weirdly hard and flat; channeling Euphemia Potter in a stern mood. He marched off, towards the beach, Peter following nervously behind, still wringing his hands. 「Pete，說句話。」James說，他的聲音奇怪地硬而平；在嚴厲的情緒中傳達Euphemia Potter的風格。他朝海灘走去，Peter緊張地跟在後面，仍在絞著手。

“Blokey stuff.” Sirius muttered, though he looked anxious and pale too. 「男人的事情。」Sirius喃喃道，雖然他也看起來焦慮且蒼白。

“What was that all about?!” Remus asked, going over to pick up the pegs Peter had put down. 「這到底是怎麼回事？！」Remus問道，走過去撿起Peter放下的帳篷釘。

Sirius shook his head, and didn’t speak again until Peter and James returned, Peter looking very shaken. Remus wished he could have said something, but he felt like he might only make the problem worse. Sirius搖了搖頭，直到Peter和James回來，Peter看起來非常震驚，Sirius才再次開口。Remus希望他能說點什麼，但他覺得這只會讓問題變得更糟。

When it came time to say goodbye, nobody wanted to leave. Remus found himself staring glumly down at the four yellow squares of grass where their tents had been, while James and Lily clung to each other, saying their goodbyes. 當到了告別的時候，沒有人想離開。Remus發現自己沮喪地盯著他們帳篷所在的四個黃色草地，而James和Lily緊緊抱在一起，說著告別的話。

“You going back to Essex, Remus?” Mary asked, cheerfully. 「你要回埃塞克斯嗎，Remus？」Mary高興地問道。

“Staying with the Potters for a bit.” Remus replied, trying to perk up. 「在Potter家住一段時間。」Remus回答，試圖振作起來。

“Lucky!” Mary said, “I’ve got to go back to Croydon - Marlene invited me to stay, but Mum says she doesn’t see enough of me as it is.” 「真幸運！」Mary說，「我要回克羅伊登——Marlene邀請我住，但媽媽說她已經不常見到我了。」

“That’s nice,” Remus smiled, “It’s nice to be missed.” 「那很好，」Remus笑道，「被思念是件好事。」

Peter and Dorcas left first, heading up to the main road to find a secluded spot to hail the Knight Bus. Remus waved them off, and everything seemed fine, but that might just have been James’s presence. The girls apparated - once Lily finally let go of James, promising to visit before the summer was over, promising to write, making James promise to telephone. She hugged Remus, and then - perhaps just in a moment of blind happiness, Sirius too. Peter和Dorcas最先離開，前往主路尋找一個隱蔽的地方召喚騎士公共汽車。Remus揮手送別他們，一切看起來都很好，但這可能只是因為James的存在。女孩們幻影移形——當Lily最終放開James時，承諾在夏天結束前來訪，承諾寫信，讓James承諾打電話。她擁抱了Remus，然後——也許只是在盲目快樂的時刻，擁抱了Sirius。

James, Remus and Sirius apparated back to the Potter’s with somewhat more success than the first time. Remus ended up in the back garden, somehow, Sirius somewhere in the village, but Mrs Potter was thrilled to see them all the same, and decided they all needed some proper food, at once. James、Remus和Sirius比第一次更成功地幻影移形回到Potter家。Remus最後在後花園，不知怎的，Sirius在村裡某處，但Potter夫人見到他們依然非常高興，決定立刻給他們準備一些正餐。

“Should we get in touch with the home for you, Remus?” Mr Potter asked, casually over dinner, “You’re not pulling another vanishing act, are you? Can’t have the muggle police called again.” 「我們應該和你的家人聯繫嗎，Remus？」Potter先生隨意地在晚餐時問道，「你不會再玩消失了吧？不能再讓麻瓜警察來了。」

“Oh - er, no, I… um…” Remus stammered over his boiled potatoes - what could he say, to stop them asking? What would buy a bit more time? Sirius kicked him underneath the table, and gave him a look. Go on, Moony, it said; tell the truth. Remus looked at Mr Potter, “Actually, now I’m seventeen, there isn’t a place for me at St Edmund’s.” 「哦——呃，不，我……嗯……」Remus在他煮的土豆上結結巴巴地說——他能說什麼來阻止他們問呢？什麼能多爭取點時間？Sirius在桌子下踢了他一腳，給了他一個眼神。繼續，Moony，它說；說實話。Remus看向Potter先生，「其實，現在我已經十七歲了，聖埃德蒙茲不再有我的位置。」

“Oh good,” Mrs Potter smiled benignly, “We’ve got you all summer then, wonderful!” 「哦，太好了，」Potter夫人慈祥地笑著，「那麼我們整個夏天都能有你了，太棒了！」

As easy as that. 就是這麼簡單。

“I told you,” Sirius whispered, as he slid into Remus’s bed, after midnight. “The Potters love taking in strays.” 「我告訴過你，」午夜過後，Sirius悄聲說，滑進了Remus的床。「Potter家喜歡收留流浪者。」

“Should you be here?” Remus whispered back, anxiously, “What about James?” 「你應該在這裡嗎？」Remus焦慮地回聲問道，「那James呢？」

“Snoring his head off, I could hear him through the wall.” 「打呼嚕打得厲害，我能聽到穿過牆壁的聲音。」

Remus didn’t press it further - after all, he wanted Sirius there. It felt funny, lying alone in a big double bed after a week spent squished up in a tent. Having another body close by was comforting. Having Sirius’s body close by was even better. Remus沒有再追問——畢竟，他希望Sirius在那裡。經過一周擠在帳篷裡後，獨自躺在一張大雙人床上感覺很奇怪。身邊有另一個人的存在令人感到安慰。身邊有Sirius的存在更好。

“Well done for telling them.” Sirius said, quietly, holding Remus’s hand under the covers. He did that often, and only in bed, in the dark. Remus didn’t mind. 「告訴他們做得很好。」Sirius輕聲說，握著Remus的手在被子下。他經常這樣做，只在床上，在黑暗中。Remus不介意。

“Yeah, I’m just telling everyone everything, this week,” Remus laughed. 「是啊，我這周就是在告訴每個人一切，」Remus笑道。

“Nothing wrong with asking for help, Moony. People like helping their friends.” 「尋求幫助沒什麼錯，Moony。人們喜歡幫助他們的朋友。」

“I know.” Remus kissed the top of Sirius's head - one of the many privileges now permitted to him. Sirius liked to sleep hidden under the covers, like a hibernating creature. It made him seem smaller than he was, and made Remus feel protective. Another thing that was ok to feel, now. “Sirius?” 「我知道。」Remus親吻了Sirius的頭頂——這是他現在被允許的許多特權之一。Sirius喜歡藏在被子下睡覺，像冬眠的生物。這讓他看起來比實際上小，讓Remus感到保護欲。這也是現在可以感覺的另一件事。「Sirius？」

“Mm?” 「嗯？」

“That thing Wormtail said, did it really upset you?” 「Wormtail說的那件事，真的讓你不安嗎？」

He felt Sirius tense against him, and instantly wished he hadn’t brought it up. He tried to cover his tracks, “Just... you know Pete, he’s a bit of an idiot sometimes, but he’s just thick, not spiteful. He’ll get used to it. Get used to me. Next time he needs his homework done, it won’t matter.” 他感覺到Sirius緊貼著他，立刻後悔提起這件事。他試圖掩蓋自己的行蹤，「只是……你知道Pete，他有時候有點傻，但他只是笨，不是惡意的。他會習慣的。習慣我。下次他需要做作業時，這不會有關係。」

“I’ve heard stuff like that before, that’s all.” Sirius said, very low, so that Remus, who usually had perfect hearing - better than perfect - had to listen closely. “About being a man. You know the sort of thing.” 「我以前聽過類似的話，就這樣。」Sirius非常低聲地說，讓通常有著完美聽力——比完美更好的Remus也不得不仔細聆聽。「關於做男人的事。你知道那種事。」

“From your mother?” 「來自你母親？」

Sirius didn’t speak, but his head moved slightly and Remus took it for a nod. Sirius沒有說話，但他的頭微微移動，Remus將其視為點頭。

We aren’t talking about mothers. Remus had to remind himself. He just squeezed Sirius’s hand, and said the only thing he could think of. 我們不談母親。Remus不得不提醒自己。他只是握緊Sirius的手，說出了他唯一能想到的話。

“Well then, you know it was all bollocks.” 「那麼，你知道那全是胡說八道。」

 

Saturday 30th July 1977

James Potter was not as clever as Remus had given him credit for. They had been back from Cornwall for a fortnight. James had telephoned Lily from the phonebox at the end of the road exactly fourteen times. And exactly fourteen times, Remus had had to accompany James to the phonebox, put the coins in the slot, dial the number for him, and show him how to hang up, at the end. 詹姆斯·波特並不像雷木斯想像的那麼聰明。他們從康沃爾回來已經兩個星期了。詹姆斯從路邊的電話亭打了十四次電話給莉莉。而這十四次，雷木斯都要陪詹姆斯去電話亭，把硬幣放進槽裡，幫他撥號，並在最後教他如何掛斷電話。

The phonecalls lasted about an hour, usually, leaving Sirius and Remus to sit outside on the brick wall, smoking. Occasionally they walked up and down the high street, but mostly they just waited for James to finish. 這些電話通常持續約一個小時，讓小天狼星和雷木斯坐在外面的磚牆上抽煙。他們偶爾會在高街上來回走動，但大多數時候他們只是等著詹姆斯結束通話。

“Bloody idiot.” Remus sighed, as he exited the booth the fourteenth time. “How hard is it to remember a few simple steps? He did muggle studies, don’t they explain this stuff?” 「真是個笨蛋。」雷木斯在第十四次離開電話亭時嘆道。「記住幾個簡單的步驟有那麼難嗎？他學過麻瓜研究，他們不是應該解釋這些東西嗎？」

“Aww, he gets too excited to remember anything.” Sirius laughed, “Have some sympathy for the lovesick fool.” 「哦，他太興奮了，什麼都記不住。」小天狼星笑道，「對這個愛情中的傻瓜多點同情吧。」

“No. I will be joyless and miserable forever.” Remus grumbled, fumbling with his cigarette lighter. 「不。我將永遠不快樂和痛苦。」雷木斯嘟囔著，摸索著打火機。

“Oh good, I love it when you’re all dark and moody.” 「哦，太好了，我喜歡你陰鬱的樣子。」

“Fuck off.” 「滾開。」

“Mm, oooh yeah, now call me a stupid prat, that really gets me going…” Sirius teased, cigarette between his teeth, embers glowing in his eyes. Remus shoved him so that he stumbled off the wall, laughing. 「嗯，哦，是的，現在叫我蠢貨，這真的讓我興奮起來了……」小天狼星調侃道，香煙叼在牙齒間，火星在他眼中閃爍。雷木斯推了他一下，他跌跌撞撞地從牆上掉下來，笑了起來。

“You are being a stupid prat.” 「你就是個蠢貨。」

“Only for you.” Sirius stubbed out his cigarette. There was a low, dark rumbling in the far distance, and Sirius’s whole face lit up. He grabbed Remus’s arm, “Look! here it comes, right on time!” 「只為了你。」小天狼星掐滅了香煙。遠處傳來低沉的隆隆聲，小天狼星整張臉都亮了起來。他抓住雷木斯的手臂，「看！它來了，正好趕上！」

Remus rolled his eyes. Sirius had another reason to indulge James. Every evening, while they waited for the lovebirds to finish their phone call, a miraculous thing happened - in Sirius’s eyes, anyway. A motorbike drove through the village - probably some aging hippie on his way home from his boring commuter job, Remus thought, petulantly. 雷木斯翻了個白眼。小天狼星有另一個縱容詹姆斯的理由。每個晚上，當他們等著這對愛侶結束通話時，一件奇蹟般的事情發生了——至少在小天狼星眼裡。一輛摩托車駛過村莊——可能是某個年老的嬉皮士下班回家的路上，雷木斯不耐煩地想。

It was a Triumph Bonneville T120 (Remus hated that he knew this, but after they’d seen it the first time Sirius had dragged them to the newsagent’s to buy every motorcyclist magazine he could find, until they had identified the model), with a cherry red tank, every inch of chrome polished to a gleaming silver. Sirius was madly in love, Remus was madly jealous. 那是一輛Triumph Bonneville T120（雷木斯討厭自己知道這些，但在他們第一次看到它後，小天狼星拉著他們去報刊亭買了所有能找到的摩托車雜誌，直到他們認出這個型號），有一個櫻桃紅的油箱，每一寸鍍鉻都被打磨得閃閃發亮。小天狼星瘋狂地愛上了它，而雷木斯則瘋狂地嫉妒。

Once the bike had passed, Sirius gave a sigh of satisfaction, then climbed back onto the wall, and watched Remus for a while. He did that a lot, now. Remus had to learn not to mind too much; being scrutinised. Sirius cocked his head, “Is it the moon? Making you grumpy?” 摩托車過去後，小天狼星滿意地嘆了口氣，然後爬回牆上，看了一會兒雷木斯。他現在經常這樣做。雷木斯不得不學會不要太在意；被仔細打量。小天狼星歪著頭，「是月亮嗎？讓你煩躁？」

“Probably.” Remus shrugged. “Usually makes me restless.” 「可能吧。」雷木斯聳了聳肩。「通常會讓我坐立不安。」

“Yeah, I noticed, last night.” Sirius winked. 「是啊，我注意到了，昨晚。」小天狼星眨了眨眼。

“Oh my god, shut up, obnoxious prick.” 「天啊，閉嘴，討厭的傢伙。」

Sirius grinned and poked out his sharp pink tongue. 小天狼星咧嘴笑了，伸出他尖尖的粉紅色舌頭。

Remus was nervous about the moon. It would be his first full moon not spent at either Hogwarts or St Edmund’s. (Though presumably there had been another full moon, once, long ago, with his mother.) Mr Potter had taken him aside, after it was agreed Remus would be staying for the rest of the summer, and explained their plan of action. 雷木斯對月亮感到緊張。這將是他第一次不在霍格沃茲或聖埃德蒙茲度過的滿月夜。（儘管可以推測，很久以前，他和母親一起度過了一次滿月。）在決定雷木斯將在夏天剩下的時間裡住下來後，波特先生把他拉到一旁，解釋了他們的行動計劃。

Not that it mattered much to Remus; a locked room was a locked room. This time it was the attic, and Moody had offered to stand guard outside, ensuring that the family would be safe. Mr and Mrs Potter (not to mention James and Sirius) had repeatedly reassured Remus that they weren’t concerned in the slightest, and that he oughtn’t to worry either. But of course he did, anyway. 對雷木斯來說，這並不重要；一個鎖著的房間就是一個鎖著的房間。這次是閣樓，而穆迪主動提出在外面守衛，確保家人的安全。波特先生和波特夫人（更不用說詹姆斯和小天狼星）反覆向雷木斯保證，他們一點都不擔心，他也不應該擔心。但他當然還是擔心了。

Sirius wanted to go in with him - so did James, but James at least had enough common sense to realise it wouldn’t be possible. No one was going to get anything past Moody - who had a new, creepy eye, electric blue and horribly enchanted. 小天狼星想和他一起進去——詹姆斯也是，但詹姆斯至少有足夠的常識知道這不可能。沒有人能瞞過穆迪——他有一隻新的、詭異的眼睛，電藍色，恐怖地被施了魔法。

“Tackled werewolves before,” he said, gruffly, as Remus was led up the ladder to the attic, “Always got a good result, minimal casualties.” 「以前對付過狼人，」當雷木斯被帶上梯子到閣樓時，他粗聲說道，「總是有好結果，傷亡最少。」

This did not make Remus feel better, but he wasn’t sure if it was supposed to. 這並沒有讓雷木斯感覺好些，但他不確定這是否本來就應該如此。

It was a bad night. Maybe it was Moody’s presence. Maybe the wolf didn’t like heights. Maybe it could smell its usual playmates, Prongs and Padfoot, and felt lonely. Maybe the wolf just hated Remus, who knew. Either way, when he woke he found he’d ripped the room apart; torn at the blinds and scratched the floorboards. In the end, the wolf had chewed its own paws out of frustration. 這是一個糟糕的夜晚。也許是因為穆迪的存在。也許狼不喜歡高處。也許它能聞到平時的玩伴，叉子和尖頭，感到孤獨。也許狼只是恨雷木斯，誰知道呢。無論如何，當他醒來時，他發現自己把房間撕成了碎片；撕破了窗簾，刮傷了地板。最終，狼因為沮喪而咬傷了自己的爪子。

Hands bleeding, the skin all grazed away, Remus lay in the dark, his heart pounding, waiting for the pain to subside, or for someone to come and help him; whichever came first. 雙手流血，皮膚都擦傷了，雷木斯躺在黑暗中，心臟怦怦跳著，等待疼痛消退，或者等待有人來幫助他；無論哪個先到。

Mrs Potter patched him up, and did a good job, but he still struggled to hold his wand for a few days, while the skin grew back. He couldn’t hold a broomhandle, either, so had to just watch while Peter, Sirius and James practiced, like old times. 波特夫人給他包紮傷口，做得很好，但在皮膚長回來的幾天裡，他仍然難以握住魔杖。他也不能握住掃帚柄，所以只能像以前一樣看著彼得、小天狼星和詹姆斯練習。

Remus found other ways to occupy himself. He’d got hold of a copy of the telephone book and spent more time than was probably healthy looking up every ‘Jenkins’ in Bristol. There were lots of them, but no Hopes. Hopeless . It didn’t matter, he tried to tell himself. He’d got on all right for twelve years without her. 雷木斯找到了其他方法來打發時間。他拿到了一本電話簿，花了比健康狀況允許的更多時間查找布里斯托爾的每一個「詹金斯」。有很多，但沒有霍普斯。沒希望了。他試圖告訴自己，這沒關係。沒有她，他已經過了十二年了。

“Tell me a secret,” Sirius would whisper, late at night - every night, he came to Remus, “Tell me something no one knows.” 「告訴我一個秘密，」小天狼星會在深夜輕聲說——每個晚上，他都來找雷木斯，「告訴我一些沒人知道的事。」

And Remus would tell him - because it made Sirius happy, and that was a very worthwhile pursuit - in fact, Remus was realising, making Sirius happy might be the only thing worth doing, for the rest of his life. 雷木斯會告訴他——因為這讓小天狼星高興，而這是一個非常值得的追求——事實上，雷木斯意識到，讓小天狼星高興可能是他餘生唯一值得做的事。

“I’m the one who told Philomena Pettigrew to go to America.” 「是我告訴菲洛梅娜·佩蒂魯去美國的。」

“You never!” 「你不會吧！」

“Yep, in the bathroom on Christmas eve.” 「是的，在平安夜的浴室裡。」

“Sly bastard. How’d you get girls falling all over each other to talk to you, eh? what’s your secret?” 「狡猾的混蛋。你怎麼讓女孩們爭相和你說話的，嗯？你的秘密是什麼？」

“Maybe they trust me because they know I’m not trying to get off with them.” 「也許她們信任我，因為她們知道我不是想和她們調情。」

“An intriguing thought. Tell me another secret.” 「一個有趣的想法。再告訴我一個秘密。」

“Um… I don’t know, I’ve told you everything.” Everything that wouldn’t hurt you, he added, silently. 「嗯……我不知道，我已經告訴你一切了。」他默默地補充道，「一切不會傷害你的事。」

“You haven’t,” Sirius said, his lips now against Remus’s, as he crawled on top of him, hands sliding up under Remus’s night shirt. He flicked his tongue along Remus’s bottom lip, “I’m going to know everything about you, one day, I promise.” 「你沒有，」小天狼星說，他的嘴唇貼在雷木斯的嘴唇上，爬到他身上，雙手滑到雷木斯的睡衣下面。他的舌頭輕舔雷木斯的下唇，「我會知道你的一切，有一天，我保證。」

Remus kissed him deeply, believing every word. 雷木斯深深地吻了他，相信每一個字。

 

Chapter 118: Summer 1977: Part 5 

1977 and we are going mad

It's 1977 and we've seen too many ads

1977 and we're gonna show them all

Apathy's a drag.

 

Monday 29th August 1977

Remus awoke from his second full moon slightly better off than his last, but unable to move. Moody had bound him to the bed (kept in the attic specifically for this purpose) using some kind of advanced magic. It didn’t hurt, but it was pretty humiliating, having to lie there and wait to be released, without any clothes on. Sirius had been vehemently against the idea, but it didn’t hurt, and it was better than the alternative. Remus didn’t care how the wolf felt about it. 雷木斯從第二次滿月中醒來，比上次稍微好些，但無法動彈。穆迪用某種先進的魔法把他綁在床上（這個床專門放在閣樓上，用於這個目的）。這不疼，但非常羞辱，必須躺在那裡等著被解放，身上什麼都沒穿。小天狼星強烈反對這個主意，但這不疼，比另一種選擇要好。雷木斯不在乎狼對此有什麼感覺。

“Made a lot of noise,” Moody said, as he released him, “But that’s to be expected.” 「發出了很多噪音，」穆迪在解開他時說，「但這是意料之中的。」

“What do the others do?” Remus asked, pulling on his jeans quickly, wishing Moody would leave, or at least turn his back, “The werewolves the ministry knows about?” 「其他人怎麼做？」雷木斯一邊快速穿上牛仔褲，一邊問，希望穆迪能離開，或者至少轉過身，「那些魔法部知道的狼人？」

“Either deal with it at home like this - with an Auror checking in before and after - or report to the ministry holding cells. I’ll get you a leaflet, if you want.” 「要麼像這樣在家裡處理——有一名奧羅在前後檢查——要麼報到魔法部的拘留室。如果你想，我可以給你一份傳單。」

“No thanks.” 「不用了。」

Remus had the distinct impression that Moody did not approve of Remus’s decision not to register himself. 雷木斯有明顯的感覺穆迪不贊成雷木斯決定不登記自己。

Downstairs, in his normal bedroom, Mrs Potter had laid out a set of robes on the bed for him - not uniform robes, but normal, everyday ones. The sort that James and Sirius wore out of school. He hoped they were hand-me-downs; he didn’t know how he’d ever repay them if they started buying him clothes. 樓下，在他的普通臥室裡，波特夫人為他準備了一套長袍——不是制服長袍，而是普通的日常長袍。是詹姆斯和小天狼星放學後穿的那種。他希望這些是二手的；如果他們開始給他買衣服，他不知道自己該怎麼報答他們。

“They’re for going out in,” James explained, when Remus asked about it, “Diagon Alley today!” 「這些是用來出去穿的，」詹姆斯解釋說，當雷木斯詢問時，「今天去對角巷！」

With the first day of school not far off, it had been agreed that the boys would stay in Diagon Alley for the last few days of the summer holiday. Mr and Mrs Potter would be leaving for a few weeks - on business for Dumbledore, apparently, though they neither confirmed nor denied this. Even Moody could not argue with Remus going to Diagon Alley this time, 隨著開學的第一天不遠了，大家一致決定男孩們在暑假的最後幾天留在對角巷。波特夫婦將離開幾週——顯然是為了鄧布利多的工作，儘管他們既未確認也未否認這一點。即便是穆迪也無法反對雷木斯這次去對角巷，

“Crawling with Aurors, these days - under cover, you wouldn’t even know it.” 「現在到處都是奧羅——藏得很深，你甚至不會知道。」

“And I’m seventeen,” Remus said, curtly, “So I’m free to go where I please.” 「而且我已經十七歲了，」雷木斯簡短地說，「所以我可以自由地去我想去的地方。」

“Quite,” Euphemia said, tiredly. 「的確，」尤菲米婭疲倦地說。

Their Hogwarts letters had arrived only a week ago, and to everyone’s surprise James had been named Head Boy, as evidenced by a brand new gold pin tucked inside his envelope. 他們的霍格沃茲信件僅在一週前到達，令所有人驚訝的是，詹姆斯被任命為男生組長，信封裡裝著一個全新的金色徽章。

“Bloody hell!” James gasped, 「天哪！」詹姆斯驚呼道，

“What the fuck?!” Sirius frowned. 「什麼鬼？！」小天狼星皺起了眉頭。

“Language!” Mrs Potter scolded them both. 「語言！」波特夫人責罵了他們倆。

She’d been very proud, of course, but James was only interested in telling Lily, and rushed to owl her at once - in less than half an hour, they learned that she had been made Head Girl. 她當然非常驕傲，但詹姆斯只關心告訴莉莉，並立刻去寫信給她——不到半小時，他們得知她被任命為女生組長。

“It’s fate!” James declared, “Destiny!” 「這是命運！」詹姆斯宣布，「命運！」

They used Floo powder to get to The Leaky Cauldron, a homely, old fashioned wizard pub which doubled-up as a B&B, meeting place and general community centre, as far as Remus could tell. James had booked two twin rooms, and after being greeted by the odd looking, hunchbacked publican, the four marauders hauled their school trunks up the stairs to settle in. Remus was sharing with Peter, because neither Remus nor Sirius could come up with an excuse for sharing together. The rooms were adjoining, which was some small comfort, but not much. 他們用佛羅粉來到破釜酒吧，一個古樸、老式的巫師酒吧，按雷木斯的說法，這裡還兼作B&B、會議場所和一般的社區中心。詹姆斯預訂了兩間雙人房，在遇到那位外貌奇特、駝背的酒保後，四位搶奪者把他們的書包搬上樓安頓下來。雷木斯和彼得共用一間房，因為雷木斯和小天狼星都無法編造出共用的理由。房間是連通的，這有些安慰，但不多。

Diagon Alley was not like Hogsmeade, as Remus had thought it might be; it was more packed in, bustling, noisy - the wizarding equivalent of cosmopolitan. The streets were busy with throngs of students, and every shop was packed to the rafters. 對角巷並不像雷木斯以為的霍格斯密德那樣；這裡更擁擠、熙熙攘攘、嘈雜——是巫師界的繁華大都市。街上擠滿了成群的學生，每家商店都擠得滿滿當當。

Gringotts was the first port of call for everyone, and Remus followed James and Sirius around the palatial bank, struck dumb by the complete alienness of everything. Remus had never even been in a muggle bank before, but nothing could have prepared him for Gringotts; goblins and secret passageways and mountains and mountains of gold. James and Sirius swanned about like VIP members - mind you, they probably were. The goblins grovelled at their feet, which Remus found hugely distasteful, but couldn’t really say anything about. He wished Lily was there, or Marlene and Mary - anyone a bit more down to earth. 格林戈茨是大家的第一站，雷木斯跟著詹姆斯和小天狼星在這座宏偉的銀行裡，對一切的陌生感到目瞪口呆。雷木斯甚至從未進入過麻瓜銀行，但什麼也無法準備他面對格林戈茨；那裡有妖精和秘密通道，以及成山的黃金。詹姆斯和小天狼星像貴賓一樣翩翩而行——說實話，他們可能真的這樣。妖精們在他們腳下低頭行禮，這讓雷木斯感到極其厭惡，但他無法說什麼。他希望莉莉在那裡，或是瑪琳和瑪麗——任何一個更接地氣的人。

Remus found he had been left just under four hundred galleons in the vault which had once belonged to Lyall Lupin. This sounded like an enormous amount to Remus - until he saw the pitying look on Sirius’s face. He quietly took out enough for his books and some new robes, as well as a bit of spending cash to convert to muggle money. 雷木斯發現他在曾經屬於萊爾·雷木斯的保險庫中剩下了不到四百個加隆。對雷木斯來說，這聽起來是一個巨大的數字——直到他看到小天狼星臉上的憐憫神情。他靜靜地拿出了足夠購買書籍和一些新長袍的錢，以及一些花費現金以便兌換成麻瓜貨幣。

Remus was so shattered after the full moon and the floo powder and the bank, that once he’d withdrawn his money he had to go back to the room at the Leaky Cauldron to collapse. The others promised him they’d leave off shopping until the next day, and would spend the rest of their afternoon looking at brooms and quidditch supplies. Remus was too tired to care, and crashed out on his little single bed, dead to the world for at least fifteen hours. He didn’t even wake when the others came clattering in at midnight, smelling strongly of whisky, loudly shushing each other and giggling. 雷木斯在滿月、佛羅粉和銀行之後感到筋疲力盡，一旦取出錢後，他不得不回到破釜酒吧的房間裡倒下。其他人承諾將購物推遲到第二天，並將剩下的下午時間用來查看掃帚和魁地奇用品。雷木斯太累了，無心關心，倒在他的小單人床上，至少睡了十五個小時。他甚至沒有在其他人午夜闖入時醒來，他們帶著濃烈的威士忌氣味，大聲地互相嘘寒問暖和笑鬧。

The next day, Lily arrived, and their school shopping began in earnest. She and Remus had similarly methodical minds when it came to completing tasks, and conferred privately on a plan of action, before ordering the other three boys about for the rest of the morning. Remus wished he could have more time in Flourish and Blotts, but as they had done books last (being the heaviest items on the list), James, Sirius and Peter were seriously flagging by this point, and on the verge of mutiny if they didn’t get some ice cream. 第二天，莉莉到了，他們的學校購物正式開始。她和雷木斯在完成任務時有著類似的方法性思維，並私下商量了一個行動計劃，然後指揮其他三個男孩度過了上午的時間。雷木斯希望他能在弗盧里什和布羅茨書店多待一些時間，但由於他們最後才買書（因為它們是清單上最重的物品），詹姆斯、小天狼星和彼得在這個時候已經非常疲憊，快要叛變了，如果他們得不到一些冰淇淋的話。

So; back to The Leaky Cauldron to dump their goods and have some lunch, (“For god’s sake, James, you can’t have ice cream before you’ve had any real food, that’s ridiculous!”), then to Florean Fortescue’s, where Sirius tried to buy Remus a scoop of every single flavour (“C’mon, Moony, it’s only fair, you’ve never tried them before; how will you know which is your favourite?!”) 於是；回到破釜酒吧把他們的物品放下，吃午餐（「該死的詹姆斯，你不能在吃正餐之前吃冰淇淋，這太荒謬了！」），然後去弗洛里安·福特斯居斯的店，那裡小天狼星試圖給雷木斯每種口味的冰淇淋都來一勺（「來吧，小月亮，這是公平的，你從未嘗試過；你怎麼知道你最喜歡的是哪一種？」）

Once all of this had been completed, Remus found his energy almost completely depleted once again, and it was only two in the afternoon. He considered taking a quick nap, but it was their last night in London, and he had one thing he really needed to do before leaving. 完成所有這些後，雷木斯發現他的精力幾乎再次耗盡，而現在才下午兩點。他考慮過稍微打個盹，但這是他們在倫敦的最後一晚，他有一件事真的需要在離開之前做。

It took a little while to get a quiet moment to himself, but in the gent’s at Florean Fortescue’s, Remus took the opportunity to pull out his pocket watch. He clicked it upen - the mechanism every bit as satisfying as it had been the first time he’d used it - and whispered, “Grant Chapman,” at the compass half. 花了一點時間才得到一個安靜的時刻，但在弗洛里安·福特斯居斯的男廁所裡，雷木斯抓住了機會掏出他的懷錶。他打開了它——機械裝置的感覺和他第一次使用時一樣令人滿意——並在指南針的一半輕聲說：「格蘭特·查普曼。」

He expected the arrow to start pointing east, but much to his alarm, it began to spin uncontrollably around and around, faster and faster. The compass had not come with instructions, but Remus had a sinking feeling that something he’d known all along was finally being confirmed. Grant was not safe. Grant needed help. 他預期指針會開始指向東方，但令他驚慌的是，它開始不受控制地旋轉起來，越轉越快。指南針沒有說明書，但雷木斯有一種揪心的感覺，他一直知道的事情終於得到了確認。格蘭特不安全了。格蘭特需要幫助。

I live off you!

And you live off me!

And the whole world lives off of everybody

See we gotta be exploited!

See we gotta be exploited!

By somebody by somebody by somebody… 我依賴於你！

而你依賴於我！

整個世界都依賴於每一個人

看看我們得被利用！

看看我們得被利用！

被某人，被某人，被某人…

Remus hurried back to the little table outside the parlour, where his four friends were sitting, making a lot of raucous noise over something Peter had just done with his milkshake. 雷木斯匆匆回到客廳外的小桌子旁，他的四個朋友正在那裡坐著，因為彼得剛剛用他的奶昔做了些事情而發出很多喧鬧的聲音。

“Alright, Moony,” Sirius grinned as Remus hovered nearby, “This lot want to go and do some sightseeing stuff, but it sounds boring, want to bunk off down Carnaby street, finally?” 「好吧，小月亮，」小天狼星一邊笑著說，一邊看著雷木斯在旁邊徘徊，「這些人想去做些觀光的事情，但聽起來很無聊，要不要最後逃到卡納比街去？」

“Yeah, great!” Remus said, forcing a grin. He widened his eyes at Sirius, hoping he got the message. Thankfully, Sirius was very skilled at following secret signals, and came over at once, 「好啊，太好了！」雷木斯說，強行露出笑容。他向小天狼星擴大眼睛，希望他能明白。幸運的是，小天狼星非常擅長跟隨秘密信號，立刻過來了，

“What’s up?” He whispered, “You look a right state.” 「怎麼了？」他低聲問，「你看起來很慘。」

“I have to go and find Grant.” Remus said, agitated. “Look!” He showed Sirius the compass’ mad spinning. 「我得去找格蘭特。」雷木斯焦躁地說。「看看！」他給小天狼星看指南針瘋狂的旋轉。

“Right now?” Sirius frowned, “But we were going to--” 「現在？」小天狼星皺起了眉頭，「但我們要去——」

“Now.” Remus said. “I can’t explain it, I just have to, I know I have to. Could you tell James and Peter something? I don’t know what - just if they ask.” 「現在。」雷木斯說。「我無法解釋，我只是必須這麼做，我知道我必須這麼做。你能告訴詹姆斯和彼得些什麼嗎？我不知道說什麼——只是如果他們問的話。」

“What? No, I’m coming with you!” 「什麼？不，我要跟你一起去！」

“Sirius…” 「小天狼星……」

“Remus.” Sirius mocked his stern tone and quirked an eyebrow. 「雷木斯。」小天狼星模仿了他的嚴厲語氣，挑了挑眉毛。

Remus sighed. This was probably one of those things he was supposed to include Sirius in. He swallowed his temper and relented. 雷木斯嘆了口氣。這可能是他應該讓小天狼星參與的事情之一。他壓抑住脾氣，讓步了。

“Ok, fine.” 「好吧，沒問題。」

“Shall we just tell the others where we’re going?” 「我們就告訴其他人我們要去哪裡嗎？」

“No. Don’t argue with me on this.” He didn’t want anyone else knowing about Grant. 「不。不要在這上面和我爭論。」他不想讓其他人知道關於格蘭特的事。

Sirius, apparently recognising that Remus would only go so far, nodded, and didn’t push his luck. They told the others they were going to Carnaby Street, to look at the shops, paid and hurried away, without looking back. 小天狼星顯然意識到雷木斯的底線，點了點頭，沒有再推進。他們告訴其他人他們要去卡納比街看商店，付了錢，匆忙離開，沒有回頭。

They had to go and change into muggle clothes first, and once they had left Diagon Alley they headed for Charing Cross station and caught two tubes to the squat in Mile End, which Remus thought was probably the best starting point. By the time they got there it was almost four in the afternoon. 他們首先需要換上麻瓜的衣服，一旦離開對角巷，他們便前往查令十字車站，搭乘兩輛地鐵到達米爾恩德的臨時住處，雷木斯認為這可能是最好的起點。當他們到達那裡時，已經接近下午四點。

Remus wasn’t sure if it was a year of neglect or just hindsight that made the rundown block of tenements look much less welcoming than they had last summer. The smell of damp was stronger, part of the linoleum seemed to have been ripped up, exposing dirty, cracked cream tile. It was a warm day, but it still felt cold inside. Adz, the man Remus had met the year before, was the only one of the original crowd still living there. 雷木斯不確定是因為一年的忽視還是僅僅是事後的回顧，使得這片破舊的公寓樓比去年夏天看起來更不友好。潮濕的氣味更強烈，一部分油膠地板似乎被撕裂，暴露出髒亂、破裂的奶油色瓷磚。這是一個溫暖的日子，但室內仍然感覺寒冷。阿茲，雷木斯去年遇到的那個人，是仍然住在那裡的原始人群中的唯一一位。

“Grant?” He scratched his head, looking dazed, “Yeah, I fink ‘e went out west, when it got too rough round ‘ere. ‘ammersmiff, maybe. Knocking this place down next week, I’m goin’ Brixton.” 「格蘭特？」他抓了抓頭，看起來很茫然，「嗯，我想他在這裡變得太艱難時去了西部。也許是哈默史密斯。下週要拆掉這個地方，我要去布里克斯頓。」

“Hammersmith?!” Remus said, “That’s the other side of town!” 「哈默史密斯？！」雷木斯說，「那是城鎮的另一邊！」

“Yeah ‘e made some friends out there I reckon. Grant’s always good at making friends , when it suits him.” 「是的，我想他在那裡交了一些朋友。格蘭特總是擅長交朋友，當他需要的時候。」

He said that a bit sharply, Remus didn’t like it, and automatically made himself taller, squaring his shoulders. Adz looked him up and down irritably and snapped, “Look, if ‘e don’t wanna be found, ‘e won’t be.” 他有點尖銳地說這話，雷木斯不喜歡這樣，立刻挺直了身子，擴展了肩膀。阿茲不耐煩地打量了他一眼，厲聲說：「看，如果他不想被找到，他就不會被找到。」

So, back on the Central line, and across the city they went. As they passed Tottenham Court Road, Remus felt guilty for ruining Sirius’s day in muggle London, and secretly promised to make it up to him when he next had the chance. Still, Sirius was having a surprisingly good time; as enthralled by the escalators and ticket barriers as Remus had been by Gringotts. 於是，他們又回到中央線，穿越城市。當他們經過托特納姆法院路時，雷木斯感到內疚，因為他破壞了小天狼星在麻瓜倫敦的一天，並暗自承諾下次有機會時會彌補。儘管如此，小天狼星似乎意外地過得很愉快；對電扶梯和票務閘機的著迷就像雷木斯對格林戈茨的著迷一樣。

They changed at Notting Hill, then walked, because Remus didn’t have a clue where he was going, except for his nose, and the compass, which was spinning less erratically now, and seemed to be trying to lead in in a vague direction. 他們在諾丁丘換乘，然後步行，因為雷木斯不知道自己要去哪裡，只有他的鼻子和指南針，指南針現在旋轉得不那麼無序了，看起來在試圖引導他去一個模糊的方向。

“It’s amazing,” Sirius said, staring up at the houses as they walked, peering into shop windows and stopping to watch double decker buses shunt past. “I’ve lived in London most of my life, and I’ve never seen it like this .” 「這真是太神奇了，」小天狼星說，一邊走一邊仰望房屋，窺視商店的窗戶，停下來看雙層巴士穿梭而過。「我在倫敦生活了大部分時間，但我從未見過這樣的景象。」

“Glad you’re having fun,” Remus said, distracted. They were in Shepherd’s Bush now, he was pretty sure. It was past six in the evening, and he was slowing down. His hip hurt from rattling about on the underground; his shins were sore from the walking, and his back hurt because of Moody’s awful binding spell. 「很高興你玩得開心，」雷木斯分心地說。他們現在在謝泼德布什，他很確定。已經過了晚上六點，他正在減速。他的臀部因為在地鐵上搖晃而疼痛；小腿因為走路而疼痛，背部因為穆迪的可怕束縛咒語而疼痛。

“Let’s sit down a minute, shall we?” Sirius asked, with a look of deep concern. “Look, there’s a park over there.” 「我們坐下來休息一下，好嗎？」小天狼星擔心地問道。「看看，那裡有個公園。」

It was Shepherd’s Bush green - at least Remus knew where they were. He consented to rest only for a short while - he was mostly worried that once he’d sat down it would be impossible to get up again. 那是謝泼德布什綠地——至少雷木斯知道他們在哪裡。他同意休息片刻——他主要擔心一旦坐下來，就很難再起身。

“Then I’ll carry you.” Sirius said. 「那我抱你。」小天狼星說。

“Piss off, will you.” Remus snorted, resting his elbows on his knees and leaning forward. He pulled out the compass to check it once more. “Ugh, it’s going mental again!” He groaned, “I thought I was getting somewhere…” 「滾開，好嗎。」雷木斯哼了一聲，把肘部靠在膝蓋上，向前傾身。他拿出指南針再次檢查。「噢，它又瘋狂了！」他呻吟道，「我以為我快找到地方了……」

 

“It might be because you’re agitated” Sirius suggested, delicately. “Er… you know, because it feeds off your emotion towards the person you’re looking for. So maybe if you…” 「這可能是因為你很激動。」小天狼星細心地建議道。「呃……你知道，因為它會受到你對尋找的人情緒的影響。所以也許如果你……」

 

“Are you telling me to calm down?” Remus frowned.

 

“It might help.” Sirius replied, evenly. “How about you tell me something about Grant? Something nice?”

 

“If you think it will help…” They didn’t have time for this, Grant needed him right now … But at this point, Remus was willing to try anything. 「他長什麼樣子？」

「你見過他。」

「我沒看清楚，我當時是一隻狗。不管怎麼說，重點是讓你想起他。」

「繼續，」小天狼星鼓勵道，「你們喜歡相同的音樂？所以是鮑伊？T.Rex？」

“Yeah, and he likes, um… Deep Purple.”
「是的，他還喜歡，嗯……深紫。」

Then one day he er… well he just kissed me, and that’s how I knew…” Remus glanced at Sirius quickly to check that it was ok to keep going. He never makes me feel odd, or different.”

「他聽起來真是一個很棒的朋友。」小天狼星禮貌地說。

「謝菲德布什區」沒有比「邁爾恩德」好多少，並且似乎有著熱鬧的夜生活。酒吧和俱樂部周圍填滿了來自各種亞文化的青少年和年輕人；穿著亮色緞面和亮片的迪斯科孩子、穿著吊帶褲和靴子的髒兮兮的皮膚頭，蓬亂的髮型的老式搖滾樂迷和穿著鉚釘夾克、滿臉金屬的朋克。最後，當他們來到拉蒂默路時，雷木斯停住了腳步。

“There.” He said, pointing across the darkening street to a building with blacked out windows, and steps leading down into a basement. The compass confirmed this, pointing straight ahead.
「那裡。」他說，指著逐漸變暗的街道對面的一棟窗戶被黑色遮擋、樓梯通向地下室的建築。大聲的音樂震撼著街道——無論那支樂隊是誰，他們對自己的樂器毫不在意，對觀眾的耳膜更是毫無顧忌。「他在那裡。」雷木斯堅定地說。指南針確認了這一點，指向前方。

The basement - looked a bit livelier than Remus was comfortable with. As well as the ‘music’, loud shouts and screams were blaring from inside, east end accents, teenage rage. Skinny, yellow-toothed punks stood outside in packs, green spikey hair and heavy bike chains. Remus felt horribly vulnerable in his worn out brown corduroys and oversized grandad shirt, but Sirius was even more out of place, with his long hippie hair and unmistakably well-bred posture.
地下室——看起來比雷木斯能夠接受的要活躍一些。除了‘音樂’之外，裡面還傳來了大聲的吼叫和尖叫，東區口音，青春期的憤怒。瘦弱、黃牙的朋克們成群結隊地站在外面，綠色的尖髮和沉重的摩托車鏈。雷木斯穿著磨損的棕色燈芯絨褲和過大的爺爺襯衫，感覺非常脆弱，但小天狼星的情況更為格格不入，他那長長的嬉皮士頭髮和顯而易見的優雅姿態。

“Should we go in?” Sirius asked, without a trace of nerves.
「我們應該進去嗎？」小天狼星問道，臉上沒有一絲緊張。

“Um.” Remus said. He was about to suggest that he go alone, when fate intervened.
「嗯。」雷木斯說。他正打算提議他自己去的時候，命運介入了。

 

 

“Sling yer ‘ook ya fucking nancy boy,” the bouncer was yelling at a young man, who was staggering out onto the street, head bent, hands in pockets. He had a mess of dirty blond hair, and a scent that Remus would know anywhere on earth.
「把你的手拿開，你這個混蛋嬲娃。」保安對一名年輕人喊道，那人踉蹌地走上街道，低著頭，雙手插在口袋裡。他有一頭亂糟糟的髒金色頭髮，散發著雷木斯在地球上任何地方都能識別的氣味。

“Grant!” Remus bolted towards him, running across the road without even looking.
「格蘭特！」雷木斯朝他跑去，甚至沒有看路就衝過了馬路。

Grant didn’t hear, and was making his way slowly down the street, hunched over. There was something wrong with the way he was walking; his gait twisted and skewed. He reeked of cheap gin, even standing meters away. The punks were leering at him, yelling vile obscenities to chase him off. Grant turned and sneered back, throwing up two fingers and warbling incoherently.
格蘭特沒有聽到，慢慢地走在街上，佝僂著身子。他的步伐有些異樣，扭曲而歪斜。他身上散發著廉價杜松子酒的味道，即使相隔幾米也能聞到。那些朋克盯著他看，喊著粗鄙的話語驅逐他。格蘭特轉過身來，對他們冷笑，豎起兩根手指，語無倫次地嘮叨。

「格蘭特！」雷木斯再次喊道，追上他，站在一盞黃色街燈下。格蘭特終於停下來，轉過身來，眯著眼睛。身後的牆上被噴上了各種不同的標語：

‘EAT THE RICH’,

‘BUZZ KIDS AND THE GIRL NEXT DOOR/DON’T WANNA PLAY IN YOUR COLD WAR’,

‘FUCK NATIONAL SERVICE’.

「我的天啊。你在這裡做什麼？」格蘭特搖搖晃晃地站立，喝醉了，靠在牆上，捂著側身，好像那裡有什麼地方在痛。

“Looking for you!” Remus walked up to him, trying to see his face, obscured by shadow.
「找你來的！」雷木斯走近他，試圖看清他的臉，但被陰影遮擋。

“Right, obviously… bloody hell, how do you manage it every time?!” Grant shook his head.
「對，顯然……真是該死，你每次都怎麼辦到的？！」格蘭特搖了搖頭。

He didn’t look good. He looked dreadful. He was thin; thinner than he should be, thinner than was really healthy. His hair was lank and looked like it hadn’t been washed in a while, and he had a patchwork of bruises down one side of his face, disappearing under his t-shirt, purple and ugly.
他看起來很糟糕。他非常瘦，瘦得比應該的還要多，瘦得不健康。他的頭髮垂直無光，看起來有一段時間沒洗了，他的臉頰一側滿是瘀傷，延續到他的T恤下，紫色又醜陋。

“What happened to you?”
「你發生了什麼事？」

“Fucking punk happened, didn’t it?” Grant laughed, a horrid choking sound, then staggered again and sat on the pavement. “Sorry mate, bit dizzy.” He retched a few times, but nothing came up, so he spat.
「是他們這些該死的朋克。」格蘭特笑著，發出可怕的窒息聲，然後再次踉蹌地坐在了人行道上。「對不起，朋友，有點頭暈。」他嘔吐了幾次，但什麼也吐不出來，所以他吐了口水。

Remus squatted beside him, hands trembling.
雷木斯蹲在他旁邊，雙手顫抖。

“Who did this? Did it happen in there?!” He leaned over, trying to get a proper look at Grant’s poor battered face.
「誰幹的？是在那裡發生的嗎？！」他俯身，試圖仔細看一下格蘭特那張受傷的臉。

It was definitely Grant, but he was changed almost beyond recognition. Gone was the bright blue denim and cheeky grin Remus remembered. Replaced by torn black drainpipes, haunted sallow eyes, nasty looking piercings in his nose, eyebrow, lip that were definitely infected.
這無疑是格蘭特，但他已經變得幾乎無法辨認了。消失的是雷木斯記得的明亮藍色牛仔布和顽皮的笑容。取而代之的是撕裂的黑色窄褲，幽靈般的蒼白眼睛，令人作嘔的穿孔在他的鼻子、眉毛、嘴唇上，顯然已經感染了。

「滾開，」格蘭特搖搖晃晃地揮動。他不會打到雷木斯，即使打了也不會很痛，但小天狼星瞬間向前跳了過來，

「喂，退後，朋友，」

格蘭特眨了眨眼，看向小天狼星，舉起手來遮擋街燈的光亮。他皺了皺眉頭，然後冷笑，

「我覺得你不需要再喝酒了……怎麼樣，吃點晚餐？」

A flash of sobriety returned to Grant’s features,
格蘭特的臉上閃過一絲清醒，

“Got cash?”
「有錢嗎？」

“Yes, of course,” Remus nodded, trying to guide him away from the horrible street they were on, “Come on, I’ll buy you dinner, what would you like?”
「是的，當然，」雷木斯點點頭，試圖引導他離開他們所處的可怕街道，「來吧，我請你吃晚餐，你想吃什麼？」

「哦，你知道我，我很隨便，」格蘭特咯咯笑道，沉重地靠在他身上，但至少讓自己被引導著。

小天狼星跟著，看起來非常不舒服。格蘭特直到他們到達一家咖啡館時才注意到，這家咖啡館在路上稍遠的地方。到那時他已經稍微清醒了一些，但仍然依賴著雷木斯，雷木斯能聽到他呼吸中的奇怪喘息聲，告訴他格蘭特在痛苦。

「這裡可能是我們能找到的最好的地方了。」

「又是你！」格蘭特嘟囔道，「我以為我告訴過你們離開。」

「格蘭特，」雷木斯輕聲說，「這位是小天狼星，我學校的朋友。」

格蘭特瞪大了眼睛，眯起眼睛（或者說眼睛，反正只有一隻眼睛真正睜開），

“Well fuck me.” He murmured, still swaying, “Proper stunner.”

小天狼星看起來很尷尬，於是雷木斯把格蘭特推進咖啡館坐下，點了三杯茶，一份餡餅和薯條。雞肉和蘑菇口味的。

“I don’t want no trouble from you.” The burly man behind the counter said, as he set the mugs of greyish tea down. “I know your types.”
「我不想從你這裡惹麻煩。」櫃檯後面那個魁梧的男人說，放下灰色的茶杯。「我知道你們這些人。」

「滾開，你這個髒老頭，」格蘭特口齒不清地說，「我敢打賭你會付錢的，如果你能的話。」

「我說了什麼？！」

「看，」雷木斯迅速站起來說，「他在清醒過來，我會讓他安靜下來，我發誓。我會先付錢，他吃了東西就會好的……」

那位大漢打量著他，目光掃過仍坐著的小天狼星，再看向格蘭特，然後又回到雷木斯身上，

“What are you, Christian Outreach?”
「你們是基督教外展組織嗎？」

“Sort of.” Remus nodded, trying to look religious. Whatever religious looked like. Anyway, it satisfied the cafe owner, who lumbered back behind his counter, presumably to heat up their food.
「算是吧。」雷木斯點點頭，試圖看起來像個宗教人士。無論宗教人士看起來怎樣。反正這樣讓咖啡館老板滿意了，他回到櫃檯後面，大概是去加熱他們的食物。

「哇，」格蘭特笑著喝茶，「你變得越來越高尚了，我老朋友雷木斯。」

“Just please stop trying to fight everyone for five minutes, will you?”
「請你至少五分鐘不要再和人打架，好嗎？」

Grant blew a raspberry, then giggled.
格蘭特噗噗地吹了個口哨，然後咯咯笑了起來。

食物來了，格蘭特像是幾周沒吃飯一樣狼吞虎嚥。雷木斯希望這不是真的，但根據他那副骨瘦如柴的模樣，情況看起來並不好。餡餅和薯條在幾分鐘內被吞噬了，雷木斯又點了一個Bakewell tart作為甜點，以及一些茶。

「你住在哪裡？」他問，希望自己聽起來是善意的，而不是指責的。「你在那個俱樂部做什麼？」

「喝得爛醉。」格蘭特低聲說。他現在吃過東西後變得更冷靜了，動作緩慢，變得更柔順。

「好吧，你達到了。那些瘀傷……」
