“那你呢？”Amos突然轉向Remus，Remus眨了眨眼。有時他忘記了Potters把他也包括在他們的責任之內。

“R-Remus.” He said, trying to be brave, but failing miserably. What if this man knows something? What if he knows I’m a werewolf? “Lupin.”
“R-Remus。”他說，試圖表現得勇敢，但失敗得很慘。如果這個人知道什麼？如果他知道我是狼人怎麼辦？“Lupin。”

“Hmph.” Amos made a note, but asked no further questions. “You’re all to wait here while I speak with Dumbledore.” He said, pompously.
“哼。”Amos做了個筆記，但沒有再問問題。“你們都在這裡等著，我去跟Dumbledore談。”他自負地說。

 

“Like hell we will.” Fleamont snorted, “If you want to go and interrupt Albus Dumbledore while he assists in the investigation of a terrorist attack for the sake of a few frightened teenagers, then—” “我們才不會這樣做。”Fleamont哼了一聲，“如果你想去打擾Albus Dumbledore在調查恐怖襲擊時僅僅是為了幾個受驚的青少年，那麼——”

“Amos!” Someone – was it really Frank? – shouted from the distance, “Where the hell are you, we need you up here – it’s Leo!” “Amos！”有人——真的是Frank嗎？——從遠處喊道，“你到底在哪裡，我們需要你上來——是Leo！”

The official turned, sharply, and with a reluctant final glance at Sirius, he ran towards the voice. Mr Potter leapt into action, taking no chances, 那位官員猛地轉身，最後不情願地看了Sirius一眼，然後朝聲音的方向跑去。Potter先生立刻行動起來，不敢冒任何風險，

“Quick, boys – are you all ok to apparate? Miss Evans, probably best you come with us for now?” “快，孩子們——你們都可以幻影移形嗎？Evans小姐，你現在最好跟我們一起走？”

Lily nodded, and James kissed her, before they both disapparated together, hand in hand. Fleamont nodded at Sirius and Remus, before vanishing with a loud CRACK himself. Remus looked at Sirius. Sirius looked at him too, still angry, still full of a hot desire for revenge. Lily點了點頭，James吻了她一下，然後他們兩人手牽手一起幻影移形。Fleamont對Sirius和Remus點了點頭，然後自己也發出一聲響亮的噼啪聲消失了。Remus看著Sirius。Sirius也看著他，仍然憤怒，仍然充滿了復仇的熱望。

“Oh no.” Remus said, firmly, then, barely even thinking about it, grabbed Sirius’s elbow, hard, and prepared to apparate with him. “哦不。”Remus堅定地說，然後幾乎沒有考慮就緊緊抓住了Sirius的肘部，準備和他一起幻影移形。

Sirius fought it, mid-turn – the stupid fool could easily have splinched them, as he strained against Remus’s spell, wanting only to stay where the fight was. But Remus was stronger – the air was full of fizzing, roaring leftover magic, and Remus drank from it, overpowering Sirius with the sheer weight of his own determination. Sirius在中途掙扎——這個愚蠢的傢伙很容易把他們劈開，他用力抵抗著Remus的咒語，只想留在戰鬥的地方。但Remus更強壯——空氣中充滿了嘶嘶作響、咆哮的剩餘魔法，Remus從中吸取力量，用自己決心的巨大力量壓倒了Sirius。

They arrived on the Potter’s front porch with such force their heads banged together, and they wrenched apart, panting, feeling scorched. 他們以如此大的力量到達Potter家的前廊，以至於他們的頭撞在一起，然後分開，喘著氣，感覺燒灼。

“Fucking hell, Moony!” Sirius gasped, rubbing his elbow where Remus had grabbed him. “該死的，Moony！”Sirius喘著氣，揉著被Remus抓過的肘部。

“Had to… stop you… idiot…” Remus bent forward, hands on his knees. He felt completely drained, but buzzing with it; nerves alight with static. “不得不…阻止你…笨蛋…”Remus彎腰，雙手扶著膝蓋。他感到完全筋疲力盡，但仍充滿能量；神經因靜電而興奮。

James opened the door, James打開了門，

“Get inside,” he said, “Quickly.” “進來，”他說，“快點。”

Sirius pushed past Remus without looking at him. Sirius沒看他一眼就推開了Remus。

Lily stayed for another hour or so, drinking cup after cup of tea, as Gully scuttled back and forth from the kitchen, wringing his little wizened hands and shaking his head woefully. Mr Potter apologised profusely to Lily, and hoped they would meet again soon under better circumstances – before locking himself away in his study. After that they sat in silence for most of the time; with only the occasional outburst from James or Sirius. Lily又待了一個多小時，一杯接一杯地喝茶，Gully在廚房裡來回跑，擰著他那雙小小的乾癟的手，悲傷地搖著頭。Potter先生對Lily連連道歉，希望他們能在更好的情況下再次見面——然後把自己鎖在書房裡。之後大部分時間他們都默默坐著；只有James或Sirius偶爾爆發。

“Snape!” Sirius ranted, pacing back and forth, “We saw him in the bookshop, he threatened Moony – he must have had something to do with it!” “Snape！”Sirius咆哮道，來回踱步，“我們在書店裡見過他，他威脅過Moony——他肯定和這事有關！”

“You don’t know that.” Lily said, shakily, staring at the pattern of her teacup. “你不知道。”Lily顫抖地說，盯著她茶杯上的圖案。

“Did anyone see any of them, though?!” “但有人看到他們中的任何人嗎？！”

“No.” James shook his head. “Too busy trying to take cover.” “沒有。”James搖了搖頭。“忙著躲避。”

“No.” Lily shook her head. “沒有。”Lily搖了搖頭。

“No…” Remus said. Sirius looked up at him, “沒有…”Remus說。Sirius看著他，

“Moony. You smelled something. You told me, remember? Do you know who—” “Moony。你聞到了什麼。你告訴過我，記得嗎？你知道是誰——”

“Remus you can smell people?!” Lily looked up, half shocked, half curious. “Like a scent?” “Remus你能聞到人嗎？！”Lily抬起頭，有些震驚，有些好奇。“像氣味一樣？”

“Not like… it’s just a… a wolf thing. Instinct. But I didn’t. I don’t…” Remus wished the ground would swallow him up. “不像…只是…一種狼的事情。本能。但我沒有。我不知道…”Remus希望地面能把他吞沒。

He could tell them. But he didn’t want to break it to Sirius like this; not while they were furious at each other, and frightened, and Lily and James were sitting right there. 他可以告訴他們。但他不想在這種情況下對Sirius說出來；不想在他們互相憤怒、害怕的時候，Lily和James就在那裡的時候。

“Moony.” Sirius said, in a very low, dark voice that none of them had ever heard before. “Tell me. Who?” “Moony。”Sirius用一種非常低沉、黑暗的聲音說，他們都從未聽過。“告訴我。是誰？”

Remus looked at James, desperately for help, but he was just staring back, waiting. Lily too, her mouth slightly open. He looked at Sirius again, and tried to hold his stare. Remus絕望地看向James尋求幫助，但他只是回望著，等待著。Lily也是，嘴微微張開。他再次看向Sirius，試圖堅持住他的目光。

“I think Regulus was there. But lots of people were there Sirius—” “我想Regulus在那裡。但很多人都在那裡Sirius——”

Sirius threw his hands up and left the room in utter silence. Lily gave a very tired sigh. Sirius舉起雙手，靜默地離開了房間。Lily疲憊地嘆了一口氣。

“James,” she said, “I think I had better go home. Mum and Dad will wonder.” “James，”她說，“我覺得我最好回家。爸爸媽媽會擔心。”

James insisted on apparating back with Lily, then returning by himself. Remus wished he hadn’t. He didn’t want to be left alone. Alone, it all came flooding back into his mind, as vivid as a cinema screen. The noise, the smoke, the utter terror. And shame. He had not acted. His first chance to prove to Dumbledore, and Moody, and even Snivellus, that he was on the right side, and willing to fight for it. But he had never expected it to be like that. Had never considered that when the time came, and you were on a battlefield with the only people you love in the world – all he’d wanted to do was find them, and run away. James堅持和Lily一起幻影移形回去，然後自己再回來。Remus希望他沒這麼做。他不想被留下來。獨自一人，所有事情都湧回他的腦海，像電影屏幕一樣生動。噪音，煙霧，完全的恐怖。還有羞愧。他沒有行動。他第一次有機會向Dumbledore，Moody，甚至Snivellus證明他站在正確的一邊，並且願意為此而戰。但他從未預料到會是這樣。從未想過當時刻來臨時，當你在戰場上和你世上唯一愛的人在一起時——他只想找到他們，然後逃跑。

When James returned, he found Remus pacing, treading the same stretch of carpet Sirius had been earlier. 當James回來時，他發現Remus在踱步，走在Sirius之前走過的同一塊地毯上。

“Are you ok, Moony?” He asked, nervously, taking slow steps forward, arms up, as if Remus was an untamed beast. “你還好嗎，Moony？”他緊張地問道，慢慢向前走，雙手抬起，好像Remus是一隻未馴服的野獸。

“I didn’t do anything.” Remus muttered, still pacing. “I just… I couldn’t move. I couldn’t think.” “我什麼都沒做。”Remus喃喃道，仍在踱步。“我只是…我無法動彈。我無法思考。”

“Remus…” James kept speaking in that steady, friendly tone. It was more soothing than Remus wanted to admit. “Nobody could. It was horrible; it’s the scariest thing that ever happened.” “Remus…”James繼續用那種穩定、友好的語調說話。這比Remus願意承認的還要安慰人。“沒有人能做到。那是可怕的；那是發生過的最可怕的事情。”

Remus stopped dead, and stared at James. He gave a half smile and shrugged, “None of us knew what to do.” Remus停下來，盯著James。他露出一個淡淡的微笑，聳了聳肩，“我們誰都不知道該怎麼辦。”

“Sirius did.” Remus challenged. “He was the one who got up. He wanted to help…” “Sirius知道。”Remus挑戰道。“他是那個站起來的人。他想幫忙…”

“Sirius never thinks though, Moony, you know that.” “Sirius從來不思考，Moony，你知道的。”

“Oi, up yours, Potter.” Sirius suddenly appeared in the doorway, arms folded. His eyes were a bit pink, but he didn’t look angry any more. Remus smiled at him, hopefully, behind James’s back. Sirius smiled back, reassuringly. “喂，去你的，Potter。”Sirius突然出現在門口，雙臂交叉。他的眼睛有點紅，但他看起來不再生氣了。Remus在James的背後對他微笑，希望地。Sirius回以微笑，安慰地。

“I was going to say,” James laughed, “That’s what makes you so brave, you wanker. You just want to rush in and help, even if it’s the worst idea in the world.” “我正要說呢，”James笑道，“這就是讓你如此勇敢的原因，你這個傻瓜。你只是想衝進去幫忙，即使那是世界上最糟糕的主意。”

“Yes, ok, it was not a good idea.” Sirius said, sitting down on the sofa, beside James. “是的，好吧，那不是個好主意。”Sirius說，坐在沙發上，坐在James旁邊。

“At least you did something.” Remus said, “At least you got up.” “至少你做了點什麼。”Remus說，“至少你站起來了。”

“You got up, too, Remus.” Sirius said, softly. “你也站起來了，Remus。”Sirius輕聲說。

“After you did!” Remus shot back, “I was pathetic, I was… how are we ever going to win this war if it’s going to be like that?! If I’m too scared to…” “在你之後！”Remus反擊道，“我太可悲了，我是…如果這樣下去我們怎麼可能贏得這場戰爭？！如果我太害怕…”

“I was scared too.” Sirius said, looking up. “I’m not that bonkers. I was still bricking it, I mean. Fucking hell.” “我也害怕。”Sirius抬頭說。“我不是那麼瘋狂。我還是嚇壞了，我是說。該死的。”

“Don’t.” James said, running his hand through his hair, still gritty with rubble. “It took me so long to even figure out what happened – and all I could think about was getting Lily somewhere safe. I thought I would just do anything to make sure she was safe.” “別這樣。”James說，用手撥過頭髮，頭髮上還沾滿了碎石。“我花了很長時間才弄清楚發生了什麼——我唯一能想到的就是把Lily帶到安全的地方。我以為我會做任何事情來確保她安全。”

“There you are then.” Sirius said, firmly. “That’s how we win it.” “那就對了。”Sirius堅定地說。“這就是我們贏的方式。”

Mrs Potter did not come back from St Mungo’s all night, but Fleamont stepped out of his office to tell the boys he had spoken to her, and that she was all right, before asking Gully to make him a sandwich and closing the door again. Potter夫人整晚都沒有從聖Mungo醫院回來，但Fleamont走出辦公室告訴男孩們他和她談過了，她沒事，然後讓Gully給他做個三明治，然後又關上了門。

Peter came over, white and shaking – he had heard the news, apparently he had a cousin working for The Daily Prophet. There was no useful information though. No death count yet, it hadn’t been finalised. Peter stayed for supper, but James was the only one really able to keep up a proper conversation, and eventually Peter left. When Remus announced he wanted an early night, the other two shrugged and agreed to go up too. Peter過來了，臉色蒼白，顫抖著——他聽到了消息，顯然他有個在《預言家日報》工作的表兄。沒有有用的信息。還沒有死亡人數，還沒有最終確定。Peter留下來吃晚飯，但James是唯一一個能夠正常交談的人，最終Peter離開了。當Remus說他想早點休息時，其他兩人聳了聳肩，也同意上樓。

After showering and washing the dust and smoke out of his hair, he brushed his teeth in the cold quiet bathroom and tried not to think about how odd it felt to be doing such normal things on such an abnormal day. He could hear Sirius and James murmuring quietly in the next room, solemn, tense tones. He decided to leave them to it. 洗完澡，把頭髮上的灰塵和煙霧洗掉後，他在寒冷安靜的浴室裡刷牙，試圖不去想在這樣一個異常的日子裡做這些正常事情的感覺。他能聽到Sirius和James在隔壁房間低聲說話，語調莊重而緊張。他決定讓他們自己去處理。

Hours later, Remus was seriously regretting that decision. He couldn’t sleep. He waited and waited for Sirius to come, until he realised that he must still be in with James, and might not come at all. Remus lay on his back and tried to keep his thoughts from getting too loud. This is war, he kept thinking. This is what you agreed to do. You promised Dumbledore. You promised your friends. 幾個小時後，Remus對那個決定深感後悔。他睡不著。他等啊等，等Sirius來，直到他意識到Sirius一定還在James那裡，可能根本不會來。Remus仰躺著，試圖讓自己的思緒不那麼吵鬧。這就是戰爭，他一直在想。這是你同意要做的事。你向Dumbledore承諾了。你向你的朋友承諾了。

Finally, in the small hours, when he was sick from tiredness and the first pink rays of sunrise were peeking around the curtains, his door opened. Sirius crept across the room with the stealth of a cat. 最後，在凌晨時分，當他因疲倦而感到不適，第一縷粉紅色的日出光線透過窗簾時，他的門開了。Sirius像貓一樣悄悄穿過房間。

“Remus?” He whispered from the foot of the bed. Remus rolled over. “Remus？”他從床尾低聲問道。Remus翻身過來。

“I’m here.” “我在這裡。”

Sirius practically flew at him, sliding in under the covers and burying his head under the duvet. They clung to each other, and everything steadied itself. Remus felt was calm at last. In a moment, Sirius moved slightly and whispered, Sirius幾乎是飛撲過來，滑進被子下，把頭埋在被子下。他們緊緊抱著對方，一切都穩定了下來。Remus終於感到平靜。片刻後，Sirius微微動了動，低聲說，

“Tell me a secret? A nice one?” “告訴我一個秘密？一個好的？”

Remus paused. He kissed Sirius’s hair. Remus停頓了一下。他親吻了Sirius的頭髮。

“I’m mental about you, too.” “我也瘋狂地愛著你。”

 

 

Chapter 126: Sevenths Year: Christmas Part 3 

Monday 2nd January 1978

星期一，1978年1月2日

The next week and a half was one of the darkest Remus could remember. When Mrs Potter finally arrived home the day after the attack, she was white and drawn, and hugged her family so tight, as if she had thought she would never see them again.

接下來的一個半星期是Remus所能記得的最黑暗的時期之一。當Potter夫人在襲擊發生後的第二天終於回到家時，她臉色蒼白，神情憔悴，緊緊擁抱著她的家人，好像她以為再也見不到他們了一樣。

“About fifty dead, so I’ve heard.” She said, solemnly. “I was mostly triage, though. Hundreds wounded.”

“據我聽說，大約有五十人死亡。”她莊重地說。“我主要負責分類救治，有數百人受傷。”

“Any… any of us?” Mr Potter asked. He looked as though he hadn’t slept in hours – and indeed, as far as Remus knew, he had not been to bed either.

“有……我們的人嗎？”Potter先生問道。他看起來好像幾個小時沒睡——事實上，據Remus所知，他也沒上床睡覺。

Euphemia nodded, closing her eyes.

Euphemia點了點頭，閉上眼睛。

“Later.” She said, casting a glance at the boys. James looked indignant.

“晚點再說。”她說，瞥了一眼男孩們。James看起來很氣憤。

“We can hear it.” He said. “We’re all of age, and we were there when it happened!”

“我們可以聽。”他說。“我們都成年了，而且事情發生時我們就在那裡！”

“Yes, I know you were!” Mrs Potter shouted, her voice shrill. James’s mouth snapped shut and he looked down, ashamed. Mrs Potter got up. “I’m going for a lie down.”

“是的，我知道你們在！”Potter夫人大聲喊道，聲音尖銳。James閉上了嘴，看起來很羞愧。Potter夫人站起來。“我要去躺一會兒。”

She left the room, and the men sat in silence.

她離開了房間，男人們坐在那裡，沉默不語。

“Sorry, dad.” James mumbled.

“對不起，爸爸。”James喃喃道。

“It’s all right.” Fleamont removed his glasses and rubbed the bridge of his nose. “We’re all upset. Your mother and I need you boys to listen, and do as you’re told until it’s time to go back to school, do you understand?”

“沒關係。”Fleamont摘下眼鏡，揉了揉鼻樑。“我們都很難過。你母親和我需要你們這些男孩聽話，按照吩咐行事，直到回到學校的時候，你明白嗎？”

They all nodded, reluctantly, and Remus saw the muscles in Sirius’s jaw tighten. It was a mark of his respect for Mr Potter that he did not protest. “Now,” Fleamont continued, “This house is going to be very busy for the next few days, and you’re going to see a lot of very important people doing very important work. Do not ask too many questions, and do not make nuisances of yourselves.”

他們都不情願地點了點頭，Remus看到Sirius的下巴肌肉緊繃。這表明他對Potter先生的尊敬，以至於他沒有抗議。“現在，”Fleamont繼續說道，“接下來的幾天這個房子會非常忙碌，你們會看到很多非常重要的人在做非常重要的工作。不要問太多問題，也不要惹麻煩。”

“Can’t we help?” James asked, earnestly.

“我們不能幫忙嗎？”James認真地問道。

“Yes.” Fleamont nodded. “By being gracious hosts and minding your mother.”

“可以。”Fleamont點了點頭。“通過做個殷勤的主人，照顧你們的母親。”

“Yes, dad.” James sighed, looking down again, obviously disappointed.

“好的，爸爸。”James嘆了口氣，又低下頭，顯然很失望。

“James…” Fleamont began, reaching over to touch his son’s arm.

“James…”Fleamont開始說，伸手去碰他兒子的手臂。

Remus and Sirius took that as their cue to clear the table, and waited around in the kitchen, half-heartedly helping Gully do the washing up.

Remus和Sirius把這當作清理桌子的暗示，然後在廚房裡等著，心不在焉地幫Gully洗碗。

“I don’t see what the fuss is about.” Sirius grumbled, elbow deep in soap suds. “If they knew half of the things we were capable of – we can actually help.”

“我不明白這有什麼大驚小怪的。”Sirius抱怨道，手肘深陷在肥皂泡裡。“如果他們知道我們能做的一半事情——我們實際上可以幫忙。”

“We’ll have our chance.” Remus replied, staring out of the window as he dried the plates. The garden was very dark, and a chill mist hung in the air, making it difficult to see much beyond the patio wall. He could just make out James’s quidditch hoops on the lawn, and the dim waning moon. He didn’t like not being able to see very far, it made him uneasy.

“我們會有機會的。”Remus回答道，擦乾盤子，望向窗外。花園非常黑暗，空氣中彌漫著寒冷的霧氣，使得看不清露台牆外的東西。他剛好能看到草坪上的James的魁地奇球門，還有暗淡的殘月。他不喜歡看不遠的感覺，這讓他感到不安。

“That’s all right for you to say.” Sirius was still complaining, “You’ve already proved yourself.”

“這對你來說無所謂。”Sirius仍在抱怨，“你已經證明了自己。”

”What?!” Remus glanced up at him, confused, and momentarily distracted from the window.

“什麼？！”Remus抬頭看了他一眼，困惑不解，暫時從窗外分心。

“With that werewolf you met, last year. You’ve already faced the enemy and shown Dumbledore he can trust you.”

“去年你遇到的那個狼人。你已經面對了敵人，並向Dumbledore證明了他可以信任你。”

“I don’t think I explained that properly, if that’s what you think…” Remus said. “Livia wasn’t… it wasn’t about the war.”

“我不認為我解釋清楚了，如果你是這麼想的話…”Remus說。“Livia不是…那不是關於戰爭的。”

“Dumbledore thinks it was. Moody does. They talk about the werewolves all the time – how useful you’ll be trying to convince the dark creatures not to join you know who.”

“Dumbledore認為是。Moody也是。他們總是在談論狼人——你試圖說服黑暗生物不加入你知道誰的行列，這有多麼有用。”

“Can we talk about something else?”

“我們可以談點別的嗎？”

“Fine.”

“好吧。”

They talked about nothing. They did the dishes in complete silence. Remus stared out of the window into the blackness of the Potter grounds and looked for… something.

他們什麼也沒說。他們在完全的沉默中洗碗。Remus凝視著窗外Potter家的黑暗，看著……某些東西。

Finally, James came in, just as they finished putting away the last of the china.

最後，James進來了，正好他們把最後一個瓷器放好。

“All right, mate?” Sirius asked, cheerily.

“還好嗎，夥計？”Sirius高興地問道。

“Yeah,” James shrugged, looking somehow wiser; older. “Just dad stuff, y’know.”

“是的，”James聳了聳肩，看起來更聰明；更成熟。“只是爸爸的事情，你知道的。”

Sirius and Remus glanced at each other, and Remus knew they were both experiencing the same sour envy. What did it mean to have a father like Fleamont Potter? To have one at all?

Sirius和Remus互相看了一眼，Remus知道他們都在經歷同樣的酸溜溜的嫉妒。擁有像Fleamont Potter這樣的父親意味著什麼？擁有一個父親意味著什麼？

“I said I’d give Lily a ring, if you two fancied a walk into the village?”

“我說過我會給Lily打電話，如果你們兩個想去村子裡走走的話？”

“Why not.” Sirius said, leaving the dish rag over the tap.

“為什麼不呢。”Sirius說，把抹布放在水龍頭上。

“Oh, Moony, dad said to give you this?” James handed over a small scroll of paper. Remus opened it quickly, glancing over the neat name and address written there. James cocked his head, curious,

“哦，Moony，爸爸說給你這個？”James遞過來一張小紙卷。Remus迅速打開它，瞥了一眼上面寫著的整潔的名字和地址。James歪著頭，好奇地問，

“What is it?”

“這是什麼？”

“Oh nothing. Book I was asking about.” Remus stuffed it in his pocket. “C’mon. Calls are cheaper after six.”

“哦，沒什麼。我問的一本書。”Remus把它塞進口袋裡。“走吧。六點後打電話便宜些。”

James had finally learnt how to use the phone box unaided, so there was nothing for Remus to do but lean against the fence next to Sirius, waiting. He rolled cigarettes to pass the time; he’d cut the fingers off his gloves back in November for explicitly this purpose.

James終於學會了獨立使用電話亭，所以Remus無事可做，只能靠在Sirius旁邊的柵欄上等待。他捲香煙消磨時間；他在11月份為了這個目的剪掉了手套的指頭。

“I didn’t mean you.” Sirius said, quietly. “When I said dark creatures.”

“我不是指你。”Sirius輕聲說。“當我說黑暗生物時。”

“I know you didn’t.” Remus licked the rizla then smoothed it down. He handed the completed cigarette to Sirius, who took it and put it behind his ear. Remus began another one.

“我知道你不是。”Remus舔了舔捲紙，然後撫平它。他把完成的香煙遞給Sirius，Sirius接過來放在耳後。Remus開始捲另一根。

“Got to teach me how to do that one day.” Sirius murmured, watching him appreciatively. “I bet we could work out a spell to do it instantly.”

“總有一天你得教我怎麼做這個。”Sirius喃喃道，欣賞地看著他。“我打賭我們可以研究出一個瞬間完成它的咒語。”

“Probably,” Remus sighed, lining up tobacco. “But I like doing it this way.”

“可能吧，”Remus嘆了口氣，排好煙草。“但我喜歡這樣做。”

“Fair enough.”

“合理。”

They were quiet again. Remus finished his second one and held it between his thumb and forefinger, wondering whether or not to smoke it. Mrs Potter didn’t like the smell on them, and he hated to add to her troubles. But on the other hand, he could really use something to calm his nerves. Sirius could too, if the constant tapping of his leg was anything to go by. He was chewing his fingernails, too.

他們又沉默了。Remus完成了第二根煙，拿在拇指和食指之間，猶豫是否要抽。Potter夫人不喜歡他們身上的味道，他也不想增加她的麻煩。但另一方面，他真的需要點東西來平靜神經。如果根據他腿部不斷的敲擊來判斷，Sirius也需要。他還在咬指甲。

Remus lit the cigarette with a snap of his fingers, and inhaled. Sirius followed suit. His leg stilled.

Remus打了個響指點燃香煙，吸了一口。Sirius也跟著點燃。他的腿靜止了。

“I am, though.” Remus said, on an exhale.

“但我是。”Remus呼出一口氣說。

“What?”

“什麼？”

“A dark creature, like you said.”

“像你說的那樣，是個黑暗生物。”

“Moony, no…”

“Moony，不是…”

“Yep,” Remus nodded, gazing out at the fields before them, and the motorway behind that. “So when you talk about wanting to prove yourself, I do understand what you mean. People trust werewolves just about as much as they trust the disgraced sons of dark wizards.”

“是的，”Remus點點頭，凝視著前方的田野，和背後的高速公路。“所以當你說想要證明自己的時候，我確實理解你的意思。人們對狼人的信任程度和對黑巫師的恥辱之子的信任程度差不多。”

“I do know. I didn’t mean to act like…”

“我知道。我不是想表現得好像…”

“Like you’re the only one with a stake in this war?”

“好像你是這場戰爭中唯一有利害關係的人？”

“Yeah, like that. I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to.”

“是的，像那樣。我很抱歉。我不是故意的。”

“I know,” Remus smiled, looking at him, finally. “I’m sorry about Regulus.”

“我知道，”Remus微笑著，終於看著他。“我為Regulus感到抱歉。”

“Well.” Sirius scuffed his feet in the gravel, “I already knew, pretty much. Of course he was there.”

“嗯。”Sirius在礫石上磨蹭著腳，“我早就知道了，當然他會在那裡。”

“I’m going to work so hard on this Slytherin prank when we get back to school. It’ll be my best work.”

“我們回到學校後，我會非常努力地做這個斯萊特林惡作劇。這將是我最好的作品。”

Sirius laughed, an honest, abandoned noise, throwing his head back.

Sirius大笑起來，發出真誠的聲音，仰起頭。

“Godric, Moony.” He grinned broadly, “When you say things like that it makes me want to snog your face off.”

“Godric，Moony。”他咧嘴笑著說，“當你說這些話的時候，讓我想要親你。”

“Ha,” Remus snorted. He shot a look at James, inside the red phone box, jabbering away with a huge smile on his face, “Maybe not just yet…”

“哈，”Remus哼了一聲。他瞥了一眼在紅色電話亭裡，滿臉笑容地喋喋不休的James，“也許還不到時候…”

Sirius looked mournful again,

Sirius又看起來悲傷了，

“I’m going to tell him, just not with all this bad stuff going on, you know?”

“我要告訴他，只是不想在所有這些壞事發生的時候，你知道嗎？”

“I know.” Remus nodded. He did. He didn’t want Sirius to know it, but the idea of James finally finding out about them was much scarier than he had prepared himself for. Why shake everyone up again?

“我知道。”Remus點點頭。他明白。他不想讓Sirius知道，但James終於發現他們的事情這個想法比他準備的更可怕。為什麼要再一次攪亂所有人？

“Remus? If I ask you something, will you tell me the truth?”

“Remus？如果我問你一件事，你會告訴我真相嗎？”

“Ok.” His stomach clenched involuntary, but he steeled himself.

“好吧。”他的胃不由自主地抽搐了一下，但他堅定了自己。

“What was the note from James’s dad? It wasn’t a book title, was it?”

“James的爸爸給的那張紙條是什麼？那不是書名，是嗎？”

“No.” Remus agreed, “It wasn’t.” He reached inside his pocket and pulled it out, thumbing the soft, thick parchment for a moment before handing it over to Sirius.

“不是。”Remus同意道，“不是。”他伸手進口袋裡拿出來，揉了揉那張柔軟厚實的羊皮紙片片刻，然後遞給Sirius。

Sirius unfolded it quickly and looked down.

Sirius迅速展開它，低頭看了看。

“Hope Jenkins?” He read, a crease in his brow, “What does that mean?”

“Hope Jenkins？”他念道，眉頭皺了皺，“這是什麼意思？”

“It’s a name.” Remus said, quickly, “My mother’s name. And address.”

“這是一個名字。”Remus迅速說道，“我母親的名字和地址。”

“Oh!” Sirius breathed, re-reading it, still frowning. “Your mother.” He said the word as if he had never even considered the possibility that Remus had such a thing.

“哦！”Sirius呼吸著，又讀了一遍，仍然皺著眉。“你的母親。”他說這個詞彷彿他從未考慮過Remus有這樣一個人。

“Yeah,” Remus took the parchment back, shoving it back into his pocket. “I know we said we would talk about anything but mothers, but. Well. Dumbledore gave me a letter she’d written me, back after Lyall died. She said I could try to find her, when I was of age, so… Mr Potter found her, I s’pose.”

“是的，”Remus把羊皮紙拿回來，塞回口袋裡。“我知道我們說過不談論母親，但……Dumbledore給了我一封她在Lyall死後寫給我的信。她說我成年後可以試著去找她，所以……Potter先生找到了她，我猜。”

“What are you going to do with it? Write to her?”

“你打算怎麼做？寫信給她？”

“Yeah I think I will.”

“是的，我想我會。”

Sirius moved his hand on the fence, subtly brushing Remus’s fingers.

Sirius把手移到柵欄上，輕輕地刷過Remus的手指。

“Well. I hope you find her.”

“嗯。我希望你找到她。”

 

 

Mr Potter had been right – for the next few days, the house was busier than Remus had seen it since the Christmas party of ’73. Except, of course, there was very little cheer. These were the people closest to Dumbledore – many of them were working for the ministry, but all of them were loyal to him before anything else. They were the front line in the war effort.
Potter先生說得對——接下來的幾天，房子比Remus自73年聖誕派對以來見過的任何時候都要忙碌得多。當然，幾乎沒有什麼歡樂。這些人是最親近Dumbledore的人——他們中許多人在為部門工作，但所有人首先忠於他。他們是戰爭努力的前線。

Some of them were familiar faces – Moody, of course, who usually spared the time to cast a gruff nod at the three teenaged boys who were now spending their days watching the fireplace for new arrivals. Then there was Frank Longbottom himself, just as pleasant and good natured as Remus remembered. He came through most often with his girlfriend, Alice, the young woman who had ushered Sirius and Remus back on the day of the attack.
其中一些是熟悉的面孔——當然包括Moody，他通常會抽空向這三個整天盯著壁爐等候新來者的少年們粗魯地點頭。還有Frank Longbottom，他依然像Remus記憶中那樣愉快和善良。他通常和女友Alice一起來，Alice就是襲擊當天帶Sirius和Remus回來的年輕女子。

The Prewett twins were another surprise – James and Sirius were falling over themselves to catch up with them, and share every nefarious act they had committed at Hogwarts since the older boys’ departure. They had both grown very handsome, broad shouldered and rougher round the edges from a few adventures – but they still had their same easy tempers and wicked sense of humour. Often they brought their red-haired sister, and her equally flame-haired husband.
Prewett雙胞胎是另一個驚喜——James和Sirius爭先恐後地跟他們敘舊，分享他們在學校畢業後在霍格沃茨所做的每一件壞事。他們都變得非常英俊，寬肩膀，經歷了幾次冒險後變得更加粗獷——但他們依然保持著那種輕鬆的脾氣和惡作劇般的幽默感。他們經常帶著他們紅髮的妹妹和同樣火紅頭髮的丈夫來。

All of these guests only stopped to chat a few moments to James, Remus and Sirius, before vanishing into Mr Potter’s study, or else heading out into the garden to apparate (apparently Moody had placed a charm over the Potters’ house making it not only unplottable, but impossible to place an apparition trace on). As a consequence, the living room and entrance hall began to feel very much like platform 9 ¾.
這些客人只停下來和James、Remus和Sirius聊幾句，然後消失在Potter先生的書房裡，或者走到花園裡去幻影移形（顯然Moody給Potter家的房子施了一個咒語，使其不僅無法定位，還無法在上面放置幻影移形的痕跡）。因此，客廳和入口大廳開始感覺像9 ¾站台一樣。

In the evening’s, Mrs Potter would come home, looking worn out and determined. She would still have a smile for everyone, and be ready to host whoever was in the house for supper. She was nothing sort of spectacular.
晚上，Potter夫人回到家，看起來疲憊而堅定。她依然會對每個人微笑，並準備好招待家裡的任何人吃晚餐。她真是非凡極了。

The night before the boys were expected to return to Hogwarts, Moody, Frank and Alice were joining them for dinner – beef stew with dumplings. They were having a very pleasant evening, Frank and Remus were having a very intense discussion about defensive charms, and Alice and the boys (including Fleamont) were arguing over which quidditch team was going to win the league.
在男孩們預計返回霍格沃茨的前一晚，Moody、Frank和Alice與他們一起吃晚餐——牛肉燉餃子。他們度過了一個非常愉快的晚上，Frank和Remus進行了一場關於防禦咒語的激烈討論，而Alice和男孩們（包括Fleamont）則在爭論哪支魁地奇隊伍會贏得聯賽。

To Remus’s left, Moody leaned over to address Mrs Potter, and whispered,
在Remus的左邊，Moody俯身對Potter夫人說，

“I hear Ferox is getting out, tomorrow?”
“我聽說Ferox明天要出來了？”

“Getting out?!” Remus spun around, cutting frank off mid-flow, “Getting out of where?”
“出來？！" Remus轉過身來，打斷了Frank的話，“從哪裡出來？”

Moody raised an eyebrow, making his eerie magical eye bulge grotesquely,
Moody揚起眉毛，他那隻詭異的魔法眼睛怪異地凸起，

“Bloody good hearing you’ve got, lad. Make a good auror.”
“你聽力真好，孩子。會成為一個好傲羅。”

Remus shook his head impatiently,
Remus不耐煩地搖了搖頭，

“Professor Ferox?”
“Ferox教授？”

“Yes, dear,” Euphemia explained, calmly, “Leo Ferox was injured in the attack on Diagon Alley. He’s now stable, and will be going to stay with his grandmother for a while to recuperate fully. I’m sorry, I quite forgot he taught at Hogwarts, did you know him well?”
“是的，親愛的，”Euphemia冷靜地解釋，“Leo Ferox在對角巷的襲擊中受傷。他現在穩定了，將去和他的祖母住一段時間以完全康復。對不起，我完全忘了他在霍格沃茨教過書，你認識他嗎？”

“Sort of. He was my favourite teacher,” Remus said, his insides churning. “Is he… what happened? Was he in one of the shops?”
“算是吧。他是我最喜歡的老師，”Remus說，他的內心翻滾著。“他……發生了什麼？他在其中一家店裡嗎？”

“He was on the ground, in the battle with us,” Frank said, “He was in the thick of it, you couldn’t fault his technique, he was firing spells better than anyone, but we all get unlucky sometimes.”
“他在地面上，和我們一起戰鬥，”Frank說，“他在戰鬥的最前線，你無法挑剔他的技術，他施展咒語比任何人都好，但我們有時候運氣不好。”

“But he’ll be all right?” Remus put down his fork now, he wasn’t going to eat any more.
“但他會沒事嗎？”Remus現在放下了叉子，他不打算再吃了。

“With proper rest.” Mrs Potter nodded, smiling wanly.
“好好休息就會。”Potter夫人點點頭，微笑著說。

All of the terror Remus had been trying to ignore for the past few days came crashing back. He gripped the seat of his chair and stared at his plate and thought about Ferox, lying unconscious in the rubble. A good, strong man like that, shot down. Remus felt a stab of angry defiance in his gut, sharpening his focus. He was going to do better, no matter what it took. He was going to be quicker; braver. The next time the battle came to him, he would be ready.
過去幾天裡，Remus試圖忽視的所有恐懼都湧了上來。他緊握椅子的座位，盯著盤子，想著Ferox躺在瓦礫中的樣子。像那樣一個好人，強壯的人，被擊倒。Remus感到一陣憤怒的反抗，集中注意力。他無論如何都要做得更好。他要更快；更勇敢。下次戰鬥來臨時，他會準備好。

 

Chapter 127: Seventh Year: Responsibilities 

Monday 9th January 1978

Remus wrote three letters on his last night before school that Christmas break. Two would need a muggle stamp, and were to be posted into the red Royal Mail pillar box at the end of the road before they left for King’s Cross. The second could wait until he got to Hogwarts, and could use one of the school owls.
Remus在聖誕假期的最後一晚寫了三封信。兩封需要貼上麻瓜郵票，並在前往國王十字車站前投遞到路盡頭的紅色皇家郵筒中。第三封信可以等他到霍格沃茨後，用學校的貓頭鷹寄出。

The first was to Hope:

Dear Ms. Jenkins,

My name is Remus Lupin. My father was Lyall Lupin, and I believe I am your son.

I am now seventeen years old. I was given a letter written by you in 1965. I hope that you do not mind my writing to you. If you would like to write back, I would like that very much.

Yours Sincerely,

Remus John Lupin.

(He thought he had better sign off with his full name, though he would be very surprised if there was another Remus Lupin living in Britain. He also thought it best to keep it short and to the point. She would appreciate that, maybe, if she chose to ignore the letter.)
第一封信是給Hope的：
親愛的Jenkins女士：
我的名字是Remus Lupin。我的父親是Lyall Lupin，我相信我是您的兒子。
我現在十七歲了。我收到了一封您在1965年寫的信。希望您不介意我給您寫信。如果您願意回信，我會非常高興。
謹啟
Remus John Lupin
（他認為最好用全名簽署，雖然他會非常驚訝如果英國還有另一個叫Remus Lupin的人。他還認為最好簡明扼要。也許，如果她選擇忽視這封信，她會感激這樣的措辭。）

The second letter was to Grant:

Dear Grant,

I hope you had a nice Christmas. I wish I could have come to visit, but I stayed with my friend’s family and it’s hard to get away.

I hope you’re all right. How’s the job going? Have you saved up for a flat, yet? I’ll have to start thinking about that soon. It’s my last term of school, ever, and by June I will be living in the real world. I hope I can see you then.

Please write back as soon as you can, and let me know how you are doing.

Yours,

Remus.

(He didn’t want to put ‘yours sincerely’, because it seemed silly and over-formal. He didn’t want to put ‘love’, because that seemed very extreme. So in the end, ‘yours’, seemed the simplest, and most honest way to put it.)
第二封信是給Grant的：
親愛的Grant：
希望你有個愉快的聖誕節。我希望能去看你，但我和朋友的家人在一起，很難抽身。
希望你一切都好。工作進展如何？你攢夠錢買房子了嗎？我很快也要考慮這個問題了。這是我最後一個學期，到六月我就要進入現實世界了。希望到時能見到你。
請儘快回信，讓我知道你過得怎麼樣。
謹啟
Remus
（他不想寫“謹啟”，因為這看起來很傻，過於正式。他不想寫“愛”，因為這顯得非常極端。所以最後，“謹啟”似乎是最簡單、最誠實的方式。）

“So it’s just the Ferox letter still to post, then?” Sirius asked, as they took their seat in their usual carriage on the Hogwarts Express. They were completely alone – Peter had gone in search of Dorcas, who had apparently written him a very steamy letter over the Christmas break, while James and Lily had made a beeline for the prefect’s carriage.
“所以只剩下給Ferox的信還沒寄了，是嗎？”Sirius問道，當他們在霍格沃茨特快列車上找到他們常坐的車廂時。他們完全是獨處——Peter去找Dorcas了，聽說她在聖誕假期寫了一封非常火辣的信給他，而James和Lily則直接去了級長車廂。

“Just the Ferox one.” Remus nodded, patting his pocket. Sirius sat on the same bench as him, reclining back and stretching his legs out in Remus’s lap, arms folded behind his head. Remus snorted indulgently, “Make yourself comfortable, why don’t you.”
“只有Ferox的那封。”Remus點點頭，拍了拍口袋。Sirius坐在同一條長椅上，靠在背上，伸展雙腿放在Remus的腿上，雙臂交叉在頭後。Remus寵溺地哼了一聲，“隨便坐吧，你真是不客氣。”

“Don’t mind if I do.” Sirius grinned wickedly. “So.” He said, “Which letter are you most looking forward to getting a reply from?”
“那我就不客氣了。”Sirius狡猾地笑了笑。“那麼。”他說，“你最期待哪封信的回覆？”

“Which reply am I most looking forward to?” Remus quirked an eyebrow dryly, “You mean between my battle-wounded ex-teacher, my young-offender ex-boyfriend or the mother who abandoned me?”
“我最期待哪封回信？”Remus乾巴巴地挑了挑眉毛，“你是說在我受傷的前老師、我年少犯錯的前男友和拋棄我的母親之間？”

“Well, when you put it like that ,” Sirius tutted. “Honestly, the amount of stuff you keep back.”
“嗯，當你這麼說的時候，”Sirius咂咂嘴。“說真的，你藏了這麼多事情。”

“Would you rather I was whinging all the time?” Remus sighed, opening the book he’d brought for the journey on top of Sirius’s legs.
“你寧願我一直在抱怨嗎？”Remus嘆了口氣，打開了旅途中帶來的書，放在Sirius的腿上。

“No,” Sirius mused, staring up at the carriage ceiling thoughtfully. “But, I mean. If you didn’t have me to talk to about this stuff, I’d be worried your head would explode.”
“不，”Sirius若有所思地盯著車廂的天花板。“但我是說，如果你沒有我來談這些事情，我會擔心你的腦袋會爆炸。”

“It would not explode , thank you very much,” Remus slapped his knee lightly with the orange-covered penguin paperback. “You’re so dramatic. I coped perfectly well before you decided to involve yourself.”
“它不會爆炸，謝謝你，”Remus用橙色封面的企鵝平裝書輕輕拍了拍他的膝蓋。“你太戲劇化了。在你決定插手之前，我處理得很好。”

“How?!”
“怎麼處理？”

“Well.” Remus chewed his lip, “I er… you’ll think it’s stupid.”
“嗯。”Remus咬了咬嘴唇，“我……你會覺得這很愚蠢。”

“What?”
“什麼？”

“I… make lists, in my head. Benefits and losses. And sometimes I have pretend conversations, you know, to help me work through a problem…”
“我……在腦子裡列清單。優點和缺點。有時候我會假裝對話，你知道，幫助我解決問題……”

“Bloody hell, Moony,” Sirius sat up, spluttering. “You complete nutter.”
“我的天啊，Moony，”Sirius坐起來，噴笑道。“你真是個瘋子。”

Remus laughed,
Remus笑了起來，

“Yeah, ok. Maybe a bit mental.”
“是的，好吧。也許有點瘋狂。”

Sirius slid his feet off Remus’s lap and sidled up to him on the seat,
Sirius將腳從Remus的腿上滑下來，靠到他身邊的座位上，

“Ever had an imaginary conversation with me?”
“有過和我假裝的對話嗎？”

“No!” Remus replied, closing his eyes as he felt Sirius’ s breath on his neck. “I only have imaginary conversations with sensible people.”
“沒有！”Remus閉上眼睛，感受到Sirius的呼吸在他脖子上。“我只和理智的人假裝對話。”

“Well maybe that's where you’re going wrong…” Sirius began to kiss Remus, very lightly just behind his earlobe. Remus squirmed, the book dropped to the carriage floor.
“也許這就是你出錯的地方……”Sirius開始親吻Remus，非常輕輕地在他的耳垂後面。Remus扭動了一下，書掉到了車廂地板上。

Suddenly, the door began to rattle open, and giggles could be heard in the corridor. Sirius and Remus leapt apart just as Marlene and another girl stumbled inside,
突然，門開始嘎吱作響地打開，走廊裡傳來笑聲。Sirius和Remus猛地分開，正好Marlene和另一個女孩跌跌撞撞地進來，

“Oh!” Marlene’s eyes widened in surprise, cheeks turning pink, “Thought this car was empty…”
“哦！”Marlene的眼睛驚訝地睜大了，臉頰變紅，“以為這個車廂是空的……”

“Nope,” Sirius leaned back, looking amused. He was eyeing Marlene with a very wicked glint in his eye. He winked at the girl coming in behind her, a tall, dark haired sixth year Remus thought he vaguely recognised. “Patel.” Sirius nodded.
“不是，”Sirius靠了回去，看起來很有趣。他用非常狡黠的眼神盯著Marlene，對她身後進來的那個高大的黑髮六年級女生眨了眨眼。Remus覺得他模糊地認出了她。“Patel。”Sirius點點頭。

Oh god, Remus thought to himself, could Sirius possibly have old conquests I don’t even know about?!
哦天啊，Remus心想，Sirius可能有我不知道的舊情人嗎？！

“Remus, have you met Yasmin?” Marlene asked, taking a seat opposite him, “She's the new Keeper.”
“Remus，你見過Yasmin嗎？”Marlene問道，坐在他對面，“她是新的守門員。”

“Oh, right, hiya.” Remus nodded, giving an awkward wave.
“哦，對，嗨。”Remus點點頭，尷尬地揮了揮手。

“No Mary?” Sirius was raising an eyebrow at Marlene, as if he knew something. Remus was just confused and a bit flustered.
“沒有Mary嗎？”Sirius挑起眉毛看著Marlene，似乎知道些什麼。Remus只是困惑和有點慌亂。

“No Mary.” Yasmin answered, with a similar smirk.
“沒有Mary。”Yasmin回答，帶著類似的笑容。

“She’s talking to one of the Ravenclaw prefects,” Marlene said, quickly, “It’s not as if we’re deliberately avoiding her or anything!” Marlene looked… was she blushing ?! Why was everybody acting so oddly? Remus shifted in his seat, noting the weird atmosphere.
“她在和一個拉文克勞的級長說話，”Marlene迅速說道，“這並不是說我們故意躲著她或什麼的！”Marlene看起來……她在臉紅嗎？！為什麼每個人都表現得這麼奇怪？Remus在座位上移動了一下，注意到了奇怪的氣氛。

“Hm.” Sirius said, still smiling at Marlene smugly, “What were you two up to, then?”
“嗯。”Sirius說，仍然得意地對Marlene微笑，“那麼你們兩個在做什麼？”

Yasmin tutted, and looked him dead in the eye with a wry smile of her own.
Yasmin咂咂嘴，帶著自己的苦笑直視他的眼睛。

“Nothing. What were you two up to?” She raised a suggestive eyebrow and Remus nearly leapt up with shock. She knew ?! Just who was this Yasmin person, then?
“沒什麼。你們兩個在做什麼？”她挑起一條暗示性的眉毛，Remus差點驚跳起來。她知道？！那麼這個Yasmin到底是誰？

“Nothing!” Sirius sat up straight.
“沒什麼！”Sirius坐直了身子。

“Well then.” Marlene shrugged, her face clearing as she settled back in her seat looking like she had just won a particularly rewarding game of chess. “We’ll leave it at that, then, shall we?”
“那好吧。”Marlene聳聳肩，她的臉色變得清晰，像是剛贏了一局特別有趣的棋局一樣回到座位上。“那我們就這樣吧，好嗎？”

“Fine.” Sirius leaned back too, folding his arms. Yasmin giggled, and Remus just scratched his head.
“好吧。”Sirius也靠了回去，雙臂交叉。Yasmin咯咯笑了起來，Remus只是抓了抓頭。

“What are we leaving where?” He asked Sirius, later that evening. They were making their way slowly up to the owlery before curfew. He’d eaten a lot at dinner, and was somewhat regretting it, now.
“我們在什麼地方留下了什麼？”他那天晚上問Sirius。他們在宵禁前慢慢走向貓頭鷹棚。他在晚餐時吃了很多，現在有點後悔了。

“Moony, really.” Sirius laughed, “Someone as observant as you hasn’t noticed anything different about Marlene, lately?”
“Moony，真的。”Sirius笑道，“像你這麼觀察入微的人最近沒注意到Marlene有什麼不同嗎？”

“I don’t know what you’re talking about.” He panted, struggling as always with the spiral staircase.
“我不知道你在說什麼。”他喘著氣，一如既往地在螺旋樓梯上掙扎。

Remus didn’t want to admit that if he was observant, it was only Sirius he was observing. He typically regarded the girls as a complete mystery, and rarely had any idea what was going on with them unless they explicitly told him. Lily and Mary did this more often than Marlene, who had always been as private as he was.
Remus不想承認，如果他很觀察入微，那也是他只在觀察Sirius。他通常認為女生是一個完全的謎團，除非她們明確告訴他，否則他很少知道她們在做什麼。Lily和Mary比Marlene更常這麼做，後者一直和他一樣保守。

“Oh come on, Moony,” Sirius laughed, “Marlene and Yaz? Don’t tell me you didn’t see - they were all over each other before they realised the carriage wasn’t empty.”
“哦，拜託，Moony，”Sirius笑道，“Marlene和Yaz？別告訴我你沒看出來——在她們發現車廂不是空的之前，她們都纏在一起了。”

Remus stopped - partly because he needed a moment to catch his breath, partly because he couldn’t believe what Sirius was saying.
Remus停了下來——部分是因為他需要喘口氣，部分是因為他不敢相信Sirius在說什麼。

“You mean, Marlene is…?”
“你是說，Marlene是……？”

“Yep.”
“是的。”

“And Yasmin…”
“還有Yasmin……”

“Yep.”
“是的。”

“Bloody hell.”
“我的天啊。”

“Yep.” Sirius’s eyes were glittering mischievously. “Can’t believe you hadn’t figured it out already!”
“是的。”Sirius的眼睛閃爍著淘氣的光芒。“真不敢相信你還沒看出來！”

“Well.” Remus huffed. They were nearly at the top, now. “I’m pretty impressed that you did. Seeing as you apparently had no idea about me, after we’d been shagging for a year.”
“嗯。”Remus哼了一聲。他們快到頂樓了。“我對你能看出來很佩服。看起來你對我卻毫無頭緒，儘管我們已經搞了一年了。”

“It wasn’t a whole year.” Sirius replied, defensively, reaching the top and looking around furtively, before continuing into the empty room.
“不是整整一年。”Sirius辯解道，到達頂樓，四處張望了一下，然後走進了空房間。

Remus came in behind him, and looked for an appropriate owl. It wasn’t a long journey, he didn’t think. He seemed to remember Ferox telling him that his grandmother lived in Liverpool. It had been a difficult letter to write, but necessary, considering they had last parted on difficult terms. He simply hoped Ferox was well, and added in a few inconsequential details about his NEWT preparation.
Remus跟在他後面進來，尋找合適的貓頭鷹。他認為這不是一次長途旅行。他似乎記得Ferox告訴他，他的祖母住在利物浦。這封信很難寫，但很有必要，考慮到他們最後是在困難的情況下分開的。他只是希望Ferox一切都好，並添加了一些關於他NEWT準備的無關緊要的細節。

“So if Marlene knows…” Remus said, thoughtfully, tying the letter to his chosen owl’s leg.
“那麼如果Marlene知道……”Remus若有所思地說，將信綁在他選中的貓頭鷹的腿上。

“Yeah, I know. James next.” Sirius sighed.
“是的，我知道。下一個是James。”Sirius嘆了口氣。

“I don’t mean to keep bringing it up...” Remus said, apologetically, setting the owl free to fly out of the nearest window. He watched it go.
“我不是想一直提起這件事……”Remus抱歉地說，讓貓頭鷹飛出最近的窗戶。他看著它飛走。

“No, I promised I would do it.” Sirius threw up his hands. “Anyway, this term’s going to be enough of a nightmare what with NEWTs and the war… rather not have anything else to worry about.”
“不，我答應了會做。”Sirius揮了揮手。“無論如何，這個學期因為NEWTs和戰爭已經夠噩夢了……不想再有其他事情操心了。”

“Are you nervous?”
“你緊張嗎？”

“Shitting myself.”
“緊張死了。”

“Lovely.” Remus rolled his eyes, “Can I help?”
“真可愛。”Remus翻了個白眼，“我能幫忙嗎？”

“Not if you’re going to suggest me having an imaginary conversation with Prongs…”
“如果你打算建議我和Prongs進行想像中的對話，那就不行……”

“Don’t see why not,” Remus shrugged. “Prongs is easy to do. Nice and predictable.”
“我不明白為什麼不行，”Remus聳了聳肩。“Prongs很好模仿。友好且可預測。”

“Mm, unlike some.” Sirius murmured. “Anyway, it’s not what he’ll say that I’m worried about. I know what he’ll say. It’ll be like it was when you… um…”
“嗯，不像某些人。”Sirius咕噥道。“無論如何，我擔心的不是他會說什麼。我知道他會說什麼。就像當你……呃……”

“...came out…” Remus prompted, helpfully. Sirius nodded, bashfully.
“……出櫃……”Remus幫忙提醒。Sirius害羞地點點頭。

“I know he’ll be his usual righteous self. I’m more worried about the stuff he doesn’t say...”
“我知道他會像往常一樣正義。我更擔心的是他不說的那些……”

“Well.” Remus said, turning away from the window, “There’s nothing you can do about that.”
“嗯。”Remus說，轉身離開窗戶，“你對此無能為力。”

“Black?! Bla-aaack? Oi, Padfoot!” Sirius's pocket began shouting at him. Sirius grinned, fishing out his compact mirror and opening it,
“Black？！Bla-aaack？喂，Padfoot！”Sirius的口袋開始對他喊叫。Sirius笑了，掏出他的化妝鏡並打開它，

“Speak of the devil.”
“說曹操曹操到。”

“Where are you, tosser?” James’s voice boomed out of the mirror.
“你在哪裡，白痴？”James的聲音從鏡子裡傳出來。

“Owlery.”
“貓頭鷹棚。”

“Moony with you?”
“Moony在你那裡嗎？”

“Yep.”
“是的。”

“Dumbledore wants him.”
“Dumbledore要找他。”

“Right now?!” Sirius glanced up at Remus, whose stomach sank. This was never good.
“現在？！”Sirius抬頭看了看Remus，後者的胃沉了下去。這從來都不是好兆頭。\

 

One hour later

一小時後

Remus was not surprised to find all three marauders (and Lily - who by this point may as well have her own nickname and access to the map, anyway) waiting outside of Dumbledore’s office for him. He was grateful - he was in such a state that if he’d had to walk back to the tower alone he’d probably have got lost.

Remus 發現三個掠奪者（還有 Lily——到了這個時候，她也差不多該有個自己的綽號並且能使用地圖了）在鄧不利多的辦公室外面等他時並不驚訝。他很感激——他現在這種狀態，如果要自己走回塔樓，他可能會迷路。

“Well?” Sirius asked, eager as always to be the first to know.

“那麼？”Sirius 像往常一樣急切地想要第一個知道。

“Um.” Said Remus.

“嗯。”Remus 說。

“Come on,” Lily said, taking his arm gently, “You don’t have to tell us, we just wanted to know you’re ok.”

“來吧，”Lily 輕輕地抓住他的手臂說，“你不必告訴我們，我們只想知道你還好嗎。”

“Of course he has to tell us.” Sirius frowned. Remus gave him a warning glance.

“當然他得告訴我們。”Sirius 皺眉道。Remus 給了他一個警告的眼神。

“Can we go somewhere a bit more private? Not the common room…”

“我們能去個更私密的地方嗎？不是公共休息室……”

“Dorm room?” Peter suggested.

“宿舍？”Peter 建議。

“Yeah.” Remus nodded.

“對。”Remus 點點頭。

He wouldn’t speak to them until they got there, and used the time to work out exactly how he was going to explain without hurting at least Sirius’s feelings, never mind wounding James’s pride. Dumbledore hadn’t said he couldn’t tell anyone. Only to exercise caution with who he told. For your safety, and theirs, the old man had cautioned ominously. Remus still had serious doubts about whether or not Dumbledore was all that concerned for his safety, personally, but kept his mouth shut. You had to be careful what you said, in Remus’s position.

在到達之前，他不會對他們說話，並利用這段時間思考該如何解釋才能不傷害至少 Sirius 的感情，更不用說傷害 James 的自尊。鄧不利多並沒有說他不能告訴任何人，只是要謹慎告訴誰。為了你的安全，還有他們的安全，那老人陰沉地警告。Remus 仍然非常懷疑鄧不利多是否真的那麼關心他的安全，但他保持了沉默。在 Remus 的立場上，你必須謹慎言行。

Finally, they all piled into the marauder’s dorm room - even Lily, which was a bit weird, especially when she sat herself down on James’s bed, as if she had done it a hundred times before. Remus sat on the lid of his trunk. Hadn’t even had time to unpack, yet.

最後，他們全都擠進了掠奪者的宿舍——甚至連 Lily 也來了，這有點奇怪，尤其是當她坐在 James 的床上時，就像她已經這樣做了一百次一樣。Remus 坐在他的箱子蓋上。還沒有時間解開行李。

“So?!” Sirius asked again, impatient, leaning against his bedpost, “What did Dumbledore want?”

“那麼？！”Sirius 不耐煩地再次問道，靠在床柱上，“鄧不利多要什麼？”

“He gave me an assignment.” Remus stared at the worn out rug as he said this, not meeting anyone’s eyes. He still couldn’t quite believe it himself.

“他給了我一個任務。”Remus 盯著破舊的地毯說，沒有看任何人的眼睛。他自己也還無法完全相信。

“He what?!” James surprised Remus by speaking first. “He gave you … not any of us?”

“他什麼？！”James 搶先說話，讓 Remus 感到驚訝。“他給了你……不是我們中的任何一個？”

“James,” Lily said, sharply, touching her boyfriend’s arm, “It’s obviously something Remus is best suited for.”

“James，”Lily 尖銳地說，碰了碰男朋友的手臂，“這顯然是 Remus 最適合的事情。”

“Werewolves.” Sirius said. Remus looked up and met his eye. He looked upset, so Remus smiled.

“狼人。”Sirius 說。Remus 抬頭看著他的眼睛。他看起來很不高興，所以 Remus 笑了。

“Yeah. Done it before, haven’t I?”

“是啊。我以前做過，不是嗎？”

“You’ve done…” Lily started, then shook her head, as if thinking better of it. “What does he need from you? Why now?”

“你做過……”Lily 開始說，然後搖了搖頭，似乎改變了主意。“他需要你做什麼？為什麼是現在？”

“They think there’s one in Hogsmeade,” Remus explained, slowly, “The centaurs told him, or something.” (He was foggy on those details, because when Dumbledore had been explaining it Remus had been trying very hard not to throw up from nerves), “Dumbledore wants me to um… ‘make my presence known,’ next time I’m in town. See if it… er… takes the bait.”

“他們認為霍格莫德有一個，”Remus 慢慢解釋道，“是半人馬告訴他的，或者什麼的。”（他對那些細節有些模糊，因為當鄧不利多解釋的時候，Remus 一直在努力不讓自己因為緊張而嘔吐）， “鄧不利多希望我，下次我在鎮上時，呃……‘表明我的存在’。看看它是否……呃……上鉤。”

“Bait?!” Sirius practically shouted.

“餌？！”Sirius 幾乎大喊。

“...It’s just an expression.” Remus replied.

“……這只是一種表達方式。”Remus 回答。

“Not a great one,” Peter said, nervously, chewing his nails.

“不是很好的表達方式，”Peter 緊張地說，啃著指甲。

“Sorry.” Remus shrugged. “Don’t worry about me. If there is a werewolf, and it’s one of Greyback’s, then I don’t think I’m in any danger. He wants me to join him, remember?”

“對不起。”Remus 耸了耸肩。“不要擔心我。如果有一個狼人，而且是 Greyback 的手下，那麼我認為我沒有危險。他希望我加入他，記得嗎？”

“Yeah, I remember getting my own invitation to join that side.” Sirius said, with a shiver. Remus wished he hadn’t brought that up. The last image he needed in his head right now was Sirius’s unconscious body falling out of the Potters’ fireplace on that horrible night.

“是的，我記得自己收到過邀請，加入那一邊。”Sirius 顫抖著說。Remus 希望他沒有提到這個。他現在最不需要的畫面就是那個可怕的夜晚，Sirius 昏迷的身體從 Potters 家的壁爐中掉出來。

“It’s not going to be like that.” He said, stiffly. “Nothing might happen at all, they might not even be here for me. And I was ok, last time, wasn’t I?”

“事情不會那樣的。”他僵硬地說。“可能什麼都不會發生，他們可能根本不是為了我來的。上次我不也是沒事嗎？”

“Only because Ferox showed up!” Sirius had forgotten that they weren’t alone, he was gearing up for a proper row.

“只是因為 Ferox 出現了！”Sirius 忘記了他們不是單獨在一起，他準備好了一場正經的爭吵。

“I know, but I’m of age, now… I’ll know what to expect.” Remus tried to keep his own voice placid, hoping it would remind Sirius to keep himself in check.

“我知道，但我已經成年了……我會知道該期待什麼。”Remus 試圖保持自己的聲音平靜，希望這能提醒 Sirius 控制自己。

“It’s so dangerous, Remus!” Lily started.

“太危險了，Remus！”Lily 開始說。

“I know that too, but I wasn’t exactly given a choice!” He snapped. She lowered her head and pursed her lips. He hadn’t meant to raise his voice to her, but he’d have to feel bad about it later. Just now it was too much to ask.

“我也知道，但我並沒有選擇的餘地！”他嚴厲地說。她低下頭，緊閉雙唇。他並不想對她提高嗓門，但他得以後再為此感到內疚。現在這要求太高了。

“When?” Sirius asked, calmer than before.

“什麼時候？”Sirius 問，比之前冷靜了。

“Next Hogsmeade weekend.”

“下個霍格莫德週末。”

“That’s in two weeks.” James said, “After the next moon…”

“那就是兩週後。”James 說，“在下一次月圓之後……”

“They’re going to increase security in the village, obviously.” Remus said. “After last time.”

“顯然，他們會增加村莊的安全。”Remus 說。“上次之後。”

“Ok, I’m going to need a few things explained, here…” Lily said, a deep crease in her forehead.

“好的，我需要一些解釋……”Lily 說，眉頭緊鎖。

“James, would you?” Remus pleaded, “I think I just want to go to bed…”

“James，可以嗎？”Remus 懇求道，“我想我只想上床睡覺……”

“Yeah, of course.” James nodded, springing into action at once. “We can talk about this tomorrow, when everyone’s had some time.”

“是的，當然。”James 點點頭，立刻行動起來。“我們可以明天再談這個，等大家都有些時間。”

“Thanks.” Remus smiled, weakly, getting up, thinking to go and brush his teeth, looking forward to being alone in the bathroom for a few minutes to collect himself.

“謝謝。”Remus 虛弱地笑了笑，站起來，打算去刷牙，期待能在浴室裡獨處幾分鐘來整理自己。

“Moony?” James said quickly, as the others got up, “I didn’t mean that you shouldn’t get an assignment, or that you can’t do it, or anything--”

“Moony？”James 很快地說，當其他人起身時，“我不是說你不應該得到任務，或者你不能完成，或者什麼的——”

“I know,” Remus nodded, patting him on the shoulder. “Believe me, if you or Sirius could do it instead, I wouldn't be Dumbledore’s first pick. S’pose I just got lucky, eh?”

“我知道，”Remus 點點頭，拍了拍他的肩膀。“相信我，如果你或 Sirius 能代替做這件事，我不會是鄧不利多的首選。假設我只是運氣好，嗯？”

Inside the locked bathroom, he pressed his back against the door, and tried to regulate his breathing. Now that his friends knew, it all became much more real to him. The thought that had been gnawing away at him since Dumbledore had first described the task finally sank in. You never actually thought he would ask this. Remus chastised himself, you never really believed you would be useful. Be careful what you wish for, Loony Lupin.

在鎖上的浴室裡，他背靠著門，試圖調節自己的呼吸。現在他的朋友們知道了，這一切變得更加真實。自從鄧不利多第一次描述這個任務以來一直困擾他的想法終於沉澱下來。你從沒想過他會要求這個。Remus 自責道，你從未真正相信你會有用。小心你所願望的，Loony Lupin。

Dizzy and trembling, he now pressed his ear to the bathroom door. They had all left the room. All but one. He wrenched the door open without a second thought, and stood face to face with Sirius.

頭昏眼花，渾身顫抖，他現在將耳朵貼在浴室門上。他們全都離開了房間。除了其中一人。他毫不猶豫地打開門，與 Sirius 面對面站著。

“You ok?” Sirius asked, his cool blue eyes full of concern. Remus shook his head.

“你還好嗎？”Sirius 問，他那雙冷靜的藍眼睛充滿了關切。Remus 搖了搖頭。

“No.”

“不好。”

Sirius reached out, and Remus clung to him.

Sirius 伸出手，Remus 緊緊抱住他。

1978年1月9日星期二

“Right, Moony,” James marched into the great hall the next morning carrying a pile of books he could barely see over. He slammed them all down on the breakfast table in front of Remus, disrupting the porridge he had been picking at. He didn’t have much of an appetite, somehow.

“Moony，”第二天早上James帶著一堆書走進大禮堂，他幾乎看不見前方。他把書全都砸在Remus面前的早餐桌上，打亂了他正在挑來挑去的粥。他不知為什麼沒有什麼食欲。

“What are these?” He reached over to pick up the nearest book. Advanced Defensive Spells.

“這些是什麼？”他伸手拿起最近的一本書。《高級防禦咒語》。

“Potter,” Lily straightened her back, staring over the pile with a look of bemusement, “Have you been in the library?! In the morning?! Instead of flying?!”

“Potter，”Lily挺直了背，看著那堆書，滿臉困惑，“你去圖書館了？！早上？！而不是去飛行？！"

“我們需要讓Moony做好準備，Lily！”

“但是…你說早上對你來說是神聖的！”Sirius說。

“你說你必須向魁地奇場的神靈致敬！”Peter咧嘴笑道。

“我可以錯過一個早上。”James漫不經心地說。

“Prongs！”Remus抓住他的手，戲劇性地對他說，“我感動了。”

“Gerrof,” James snatched his hand back, ears turning bright red. “You can all stop making fun of me. Am I the only one taking this seriously?!”

“放開，”James把手抽回來，耳朵變得通紅。“你們都別再取笑我了。難道只有我在認真對待這件事嗎？！”

“嘿！”Sirius得意地笑了。Remus和Peter因為預感到接下來的事而哼哼起來，“我永遠是Sirius。”

Peter and Remus covered their eyes in embarrassment, but it must have been the first time Lily had ever heard that joke because she snorted with laughter so suddenly that her tea shot out of her nose. This was the funniest thing that even the marauders had seen in ages, and they were all hysterical for a good five minutes - each time any of them managed to stop, Lily would snort again, or James would waggle his eyebrows and they would be helpless with laughter once more.

Peter和Remus尷尬地遮住了眼睛，但這可能是Lily第一次聽到這個笑話，因為她突然大笑起來，茶水從她鼻子裡噴了出來。即使是掠奪者們也很久沒見過這麼好笑的事了，他們都狂笑了好幾分鐘——每次他們中的任何一個人好不容易停止笑，Lily又會哼笑起來，或者James會擺動他的眉毛，他們又會無助地再次笑得前仰後合。

When they’d finally calmed down, Remus opened the first book eagerly and decided that he would eat his porridge after all.

當他們終於平靜下來時，Remus急切地打開了第一本書，決定還是要吃他的粥。

They went to their lessons with a new sense of purpose, and James suggested that they all meet in the library after the last bell to begin work on preparing Remus for whatever was ahead. They did this every day for a whole week, commandeering a block of six desks behind some stacks in a corner, where they could have complete privacy, pushed them all together and covered the thing in textbooks on battle theory, duelling techniques, defensive incantations and hexes. Peter even made a threatening sign which read Marauder’s War Council: Do Not Disturb, which worked like a charm (possibly because it had been literally charmed by Lily) and meant they could leave their work there and return to it whenever they liked.

他們懷著新的目標去上課，James建議他們在最後一節課後在圖書館見面，開始為Remus準備即將面臨的挑戰。他們整整一週每天都這樣做，佔據了一角堆放書堆後的六張桌子，在那裡他們可以完全隱私，將桌子推到一起，堆滿了戰鬥理論、決鬥技巧、防禦咒語和詛咒的教科書。Peter甚至製作了一個威脅性的標誌，上面寫著“掠奪者戰爭委員會：請勿打擾”，效果奇佳（可能是因為Lily施了咒語），這意味著他們可以隨時離開並回來繼續工作。

Remus abandoned his study groups, asking Christopher to take over, James nominated Marlene to take over two of his quidditch sessions, and even Lily stopped going to Slug Club meetings that week. (Though she did try to break into Slughorn’s study to get her hands on some Felix Felicis for Remus, but had no luck and was almost caught). In short, all five of them spent as much time as possible working towards the same cause; preparing Remus for his mission.

Remus放棄了他的學習小組，請Christopher接管，James提名Marlene接管他的兩節魁地奇訓練，甚至Lily那週也停止參加Slug Club會議。（雖然她試圖闖入Slughorn的書房為Remus拿到一些福靈劑，但沒有成功，差點被抓到）。總之，他們五個人盡可能多地花時間為同一個目標努力；為Remus的任務做準備。

He had been teasing James before, but Remus really was touched - only there was hardly any time to dwell on it, as they all knuckled down to study harder than any of them ever had before. Remus just thanked his lucky stars that James was so good at defense against the dark arts; they’d never had a teacher stay longer than a year in that subject, so Remus’s own knowledge was patchy. James and Lily’s combined efforts helped him cover more ground in a week than he had since his OWLs.

他之前一直在取笑James，但Remus真的感動了——只是他們幾乎沒有時間去思考這個問題，因為他們都比以往任何時候都更加努力地學習。Remus只能感謝他的幸運星，James在黑魔法防禦術上如此出色；他們從未有過一個老師在這門課程上停留超過一年的，所以Remus自己的知識是零散的。James和Lily的共同努力幫助他在一週內覆蓋了自OWLs以來更多的知識。

“You’re good at charms, and that’s half the battle.” James said, appraisingly, as they stood in the empty common room one evening, “The rest is really just quick thinking and determination.”

“你擅長咒語，這就是一半的戰鬥。”James評價道，當他們有一天晚上站在空蕩的公共休息室裡，“剩下的就是快速思考和決心。”

“And we know you can do those.” Lily encouraged, tidying up the mess they’d made trying to freeze sofa cushions mid-air.

“我們知道你能做到這些。”Lily鼓勵道，收拾他們試圖在空中凍結沙發靠墊時弄亂的場地。

“It won’t be like Diagon Alley,” Sirius reassured him, slapping him on the back, “Because you’ll know what’s coming. You’ve got time to get ready.”

“這不會像對角巷那樣，”Sirius安慰他，拍了拍他的背，“因為你會知道接下來會發生什麼。你有時間準備。”

“Easy enough to say…” Remus bit his lip. “I’m ok at most of this, here, with you lot, but if I was actually defending myself… and I still can’t do a patronus.”

“說起來容易……”Remus咬了咬嘴唇。“在這裡，和你們在一起，我大部分都還可以，但如果我要真正保護自己……我還是不能施展護法。”

“Don’t worry about that, now, just focus on the simpler stuff.” James advised, rubbing his chin, “The patronus will come - it’s not as if you’re not strong enough; you apparate like it’s nothing.”

“現在不要擔心那個，只專注於簡單的東西。”James建議道，摸著下巴，“護法咒會來的——並不是說你不夠強大；你幻影移形就像不費吹灰之力。”

“That’s easy.” Remus sighed. “That’s just thinking. Patronuses are feeling.”

“那很容易。”Remus嘆了口氣。“那只是思考。護法咒是感覺。”

“Could somebody please let me down, now?” Peter called from above their heads, where he had been paralysed mid-air.

“現在能有人讓我下來嗎？”Peter從他們頭頂上方叫道，他在空中被定住了。

Sunday 15th January 1978

1978年1月15日，星期天

By the following weekend, they had definitely hit their stride, and Remus was feeling more confident than ever - as long as he didn’t think too much about Livia’s incredible ability with wandless magic. He tried to convince himself that he was over-prepared, if anything. Dumbledore had merely required him to show his face in Hogsmeade, to see if this other wolf (if there even was another wolf) sniffed him out. He might never use anything James had taught him at all. 到了下週末，他們確實找到了狀態，而Remus比以往任何時候都更有信心——只要他不去想Livia那令人難以置信的無杖魔法能力。他試圖說服自己，他過度準備了。Dumbledore只是要求他在Hogsmeade露面，看看這只狼（如果真的有另一只狼）是否會嗅出他。他可能永遠不會用上James教他的任何東西。

Yeah, right - that nasty voice in the back of his head spoke; always late at night, when everyone else was asleep and he was most alone - as if you’ve ever been that lucky. 是啊，對——那討厭的聲音在他腦海中響起；總是在深夜，當其他人都睡著而他最孤單的時候——好像你曾經那麼幸運過。

They spent all day Saturday in the library, all five of them, but on Sunday Lily was required to mediate a prefect dispute and Peter had an afternoon detention for poor uniform, so for a good portion of the day it was just Remus, James and Sirius working in their quiet little study nook. 他們整個星期六都在圖書館度過，五個人都在，但週日Lily需要調解一個級長的爭端，而Peter因為穿著不整而在下午被罰留校，所以大部分時間只有Remus、James和Sirius在他們安靜的小書房裡學習。

Sirius and James were on the blacklist for the restricted section, so Remus went in alone, and came back with the biggest book on curses he could find. Sirius和James被限制進入限制區，所以Remus獨自進去，帶回了他能找到的最大的一本咒語書。

“There are some second years on the other side of the hall taking bets on whether we’re really behind studying for NEWTs or just planning the most amazing prank Hogwarts has ever seen.” He said, setting the huge tome down on top of three more. “有些二年級的學生在大廳的另一邊打賭我們是否真的在為NEWTs考試而學習，還是只是計劃霍格沃茲有史以來最驚人的惡作劇。”他說，把那本巨大的書放在另外三本書上。

“I’m so proud of our legacy, aren’t you, Mr Prongs?” Sirius smirked over the book he was taking notes from. “我為我們的遺產感到如此自豪，不是嗎，Mr Prongs？”Sirius在他做筆記的書上得意地笑著說。

“Quite so, Mr Padfoot, quite so.” James replied, scanning a glossary. “Ah ha!” He grabbed a book triumphantly, and began flipping pages. “確實如此，Mr Padfoot，確實如此。”James回答道，掃視著一本術語表。“啊哈！”他得意地抓起一本書，開始翻頁。

Sirius looked up. Sirius抬起頭來。

“Found something good?” “找到什麼好東西了嗎？”

“Maybe…” James murmured, reading fast. “也許吧……”James低聲說，快速閱讀著。

Remus began to look at the contents of the book of curses. The chapter titles were truly horrible, and he hoped he’d never actually have to use any of this stuff. Remus開始查看那本咒語書的內容。章節標題真的很可怕，他希望自己永遠不會真的需要用到這些東西。

“Ok,” James said, “Look at this.” He had finished reading, and flipped the book to show Remus and Sirius, who were on the other side of the table. “I really think this sort of thing plays to your strengths, Moony. It's all intuitive stuff with a lot of punch behind it, the way you do pranks.” “好了，”James說，“看看這個。”他讀完了，把書翻過來給桌子另一邊的Remus和Sirius看。“我真的認為這種東西發揮了你的特長，Moony。這都是一些直觀的東西，背後有很多力量，就像你做惡作劇的方式。”

Sirius and Remus both stood to pore over the book, leaning forward on the desk. Remus's shoulders were still so sore from the last moon - the pain-free days between moons seemed to be getting shorter the older he got; his tendons felt like hard knotted rope rubbing against the bone. He stretched to rub a particularly sore spot while he read, pressing down with his fingertips and breathing in slightly at the pain. Sirius和Remus都站起來仔細閱讀那本書，向桌子上靠近。Remus的肩膀仍然因為上次的滿月而疼痛——在滿月之間沒有痛苦的日子似乎隨著年齡的增長而變得越來越短；他的肌腱感覺像硬繩子結在骨頭上摩擦。他伸展身體揉了揉一個特別疼的地方，用指尖按壓，稍微吸氣以緩解疼痛。

Sirius moved closer, and - perhaps without thinking - reached out to rub the sore spot with his own long fingers. He was much better at it than Remus, who felt a wave of relief as Sirius worked small, soothing circles into his muscle. He sighed, tiredly. Sirius靠近了，或許是無意識地，用他自己的長手指伸手揉了揉那個疼痛的地方。他比Remus做得好得多，當Sirius在他的肌肉上畫著小而舒緩的圈時，Remus感到一陣放鬆。他疲憊地嘆了口氣。

Remus was the first to finish reading, and looked up at James. The bespectacled young man was not looking at the text, though. He was staring at them, across the table. Specifically at the point where Sirius's hand was touching Remus's neck. James’s mouth had fallen slightly open, and there was a question in his eyes. Remus是第一個讀完的，他抬頭看著James。然而這個戴眼鏡的年輕人並沒有看著書本。他在桌子對面盯著他們。特別是Sirius的手碰到Remus脖子的地方。James的嘴微微張開，眼中有一個疑問。

Remus moved to alert Sirius, who finally looked up at his friend. Seeing immediately what he had done, he just stared back, still for a moment. Remus half expected him to step away, withdraw his hand. But he didn’t. Instead, Sirius wrapped his arm around Remus's shoulders, and squeezed him, very deliberately, all the while holding James's gaze. Remus動了動提醒Sirius，Sirius終於抬頭看著他的朋友。馬上看到他做了什麼，他只是回望著，靜止了一會兒。Remus半期待他會退後，收回他的手。但他沒有。相反，Sirius把手臂繞過Remus的肩膀，非常刻意地擠了擠他，同時注視著James。

James closed his mouth, looked at them both again, and nodded, wordlessly. Remus straightened up, letting Sirius’s arm drop. James閉上了嘴，又看了看他們倆，無言地點了點頭。Remus直起身子，讓Sirius的手臂放下。

He had to leave them alone, that much was obvious. He cleared his throat, 他必須讓他們單獨相處，這一點顯而易見。他清了清喉嚨，

“Er. I’m sure there’s a book I’ve read which goes into more depth than this. I think I’ve got a copy upstairs, I’ll er… just go and get it… see you in an hour or so, maybe?” “呃。我確信我讀過一本書，比這本書深入得多。我想我樓上有一本副本，我呃……就去拿……可能一個小時左右見？”

“虫尾巴，我們有事情要告訴你。”

Friday 20th January 1978

1978年1月20日星期五

Peter took a little while to get used to it, but then they all did, really - even Remus and Sirius. They kept forgetting that the marauders knew, and they’d grown so used to consciously avoiding each other that they were oddly shy to show any sort of affection in front of the others. Of course, Remus kept reminding himself, it was better to keep a low profile anyway; they still had the rest of the school to worry about.

彼得花了一點時間來適應，但他們都真的適應了——甚至雷木斯和天狼星。他們總是忘記了掠奪者知道了，並且他們已經習慣於有意識地避開彼此，以至於在其他人面前表現出任何形式的愛意時都感到奇怪的害羞。當然，雷木斯不斷提醒自己，保持低調總是好的；他們還有整個學校需要擔心。

“You could tell Christopher, though.” Sirius said, as they left the library for the last time before the Hogsmeade trip. It was almost midnight and they’d had to be chased out by Madam Pince, who wouldn’t let them stay any longer, even when Lily and James had flashed their Head Girl and Boy badges.

“你可以告訴克里斯多弗。”天狼星說，當他們在去活米村旅行前最後一次離開圖書館時。已經快午夜了，他們不得不被平斯夫人趕走，平斯夫人不允許他們再待下去，即使莉莉和詹姆斯亮出了他們的級長徽章。

“Oh, now you remember his name,” Remus yawned, clutching his books to his chest - really just for something to hold on to.

“哦，現在你記得他的名字了，”雷木斯打著哈欠，抱著書到胸前——真的只是為了有東西可以抱著。

“I’m just saying ,” Sirius caught the yawn and covered his mouth, but continued speaking, “He already knows half of it, no harm telling him the rest. Not really fair to let him keep pining away for you when there’s not a chance in--”

“我只是說，”天狼星接住哈欠並捂住嘴，但繼續說道，“他已經知道一半了，告訴他剩下的也沒什麼壞處。不讓他繼續為你心碎而沒有任何機會，這不公平--”

“Sirius Black, are you jealous?!” Lily cackled, giggly with overtiredness.

“天狼星布萊克，你嫉妒了？！”莉莉咯咯笑著，因為過度疲勞而發笑。

“No.” Sirius sniffed, nose in the air, “I just don’t want any misunderstandings.”

“沒有。”天狼星吸了吸鼻子，抬起頭，“我只是不想有任何誤會。”

“Well if I survive tomorrow then I’ll think about it.” Remus yawned again.

“如果我明天能活下來，我會考慮的。”雷木斯再次打著哈欠。

That made everyone go quiet and he regretted saying it. They walked back to the common room in solemn silence. Gryffindor tower was peaceful and mostly empty - a few stray second years up past their curfew fled to their dorms as soon as they saw James and Lily, and the marauders took their usual seats by the fireplace. Remus settled into his armchair and immediately returned to the book he had been reading before Pince had so rudely interrupted.

這讓大家都安靜下來，他後悔說了這句話。他們在莊嚴的沉默中走回公共休息室。格蘭芬多塔平靜且大多是空的——幾個違反宵禁的二年級學生一看到詹姆斯和莉莉就逃回了宿舍，掠奪者們在壁爐旁找到了他們的常坐之處。雷木斯坐進了他的扶手椅，立刻回到了他之前被平斯夫人粗魯打斷的書中。

Sirius flicked his wand at the kettle hanging over the fireplace and Lily summoned some clean tea cups from the cupboard, but still no one spoke until the water was boiled and the tea brewing in its pot.

天狼星揮動他的魔杖對著掛在壁爐上的水壺，莉莉從櫥櫃裡召喚出一些乾淨的茶杯，但直到水煮沸並且茶在壺裡沖泡好後，仍然沒有人說話。

“Moony,” Sirius said, softly, “Put down the book, eh? We’ve done so much already.”

“月亮臉，”天狼星輕聲說，“放下書，好嗎？我們已經做了很多了。”

“Doesn’t feel like enough.” Remus replied, feeling prickly and irritable. “I know I’m missing something.”

“感覺還不夠。”雷木斯回答，感到刺痛和煩躁。“我知道我漏掉了什麼。”

Everyone kept staring at him, and by now he didn’t know whether it was because they were amazed (or repulsed) about the whole Sirius thing, or whether they were convinced he was about to run away and join the werewolves.

大家一直盯著他，到現在他不知道是因為他們對整個天狼星的事情感到驚訝（或者厭惡），還是因為他們相信他即將逃跑並加入狼人。

“It’s loads.” James said, now pouring the tea and handing Remus a saucer, “Honestly, you know enough now to walk any Defence Against the Dark Arts exam. Might as well bunk off the rest of the year.”

“已經很多了。”詹姆斯說，現在倒茶並遞給雷木斯一個茶碟，“說真的，你現在知道的已經足夠通過任何黑魔法防禦術考試了。不如把剩下的學年翹掉。”

“This isn't an exam.” Remus snapped. The cup and saucer shook in his hands, so he set it down on the arm of the chair. He had a feeling Sirius had noticed that, but hopefully no one else.

“這不是考試。”雷木斯厲聲說。杯子和茶碟在他手中顫抖，所以他把它放在椅子的扶手上。他感覺天狼星注意到了這點，但希望其他人沒有。

“But Moony,” Peter slurped his own tea noisily, “You’ve done this before. Last year.”

“但是月亮臉，”彼得大聲地喝著自己的茶，“你以前做過這個。去年。”

“Exactly,” James nodded, encouragingly.

“沒錯，”詹姆斯點頭，鼓勵道。

Remus sighed, and said no more. What was the point; whinging wasn’t going to get him anywhere. He sipped his tea, willing his hand to stay steady. This was potentially the worst time of the month for a mission, he couldn’t help thinking. Only four nights away from the full moon and his magic felt stronger than usual, but also less predictable. He was restless, his skin crawling, his senses bare and his mood hot. He knew he was forgetting something. He just knew . A dark feeling of foreboding that told him all the curses in the world would be no good.

雷木斯嘆了口氣，沒再說什麼。有什麼意義呢？抱怨不會讓他有任何進展。他啜飲著茶，強迫自己的手保持穩定。他忍不住想，這可能是這個月執行任務最糟糕的時候。離滿月只有四個晚上，他的魔力感覺比平時更強，但也更難預測。他焦躁不安，皮膚爬行，感官裸露，情緒激動。他知道他忘了什麼。他就是知道。一種陰暗的預感告訴他，世界上所有的詛咒都無濟於事。

He stood up, sharply, knocking the teacup off the armchair. Sirius was quick, and stopped it mid-air with a flick of his wand. Remus ignored this.

他猛然站起來，把茶杯從扶手椅上撞掉。天狼星動作迅速，用魔杖一揮在空中停住了茶杯。雷木斯無視了這一點。

“Going to bed.” He said, cracking his knuckles.

“去睡覺了。”他說，指節作響。

“Ok, Moony,” James nodded, brightly. He glanced at Lily, “Think we’ll stay down here for a bit.”

“好吧，月亮臉，”詹姆斯明亮地點點頭。他看了一眼莉莉，“我們會在這裡待一會兒。”

Peter looked at Sirius, and then Remus with an expression of faint terror. Remus tutted.

彼得看著天狼星，然後看著雷木斯，臉上帶著淡淡的恐懼。雷木斯咂嘴。

“It’s ok, Wormtail, I really am just going to sleep. See you all tomorrow.”

“沒事，虫尾巴，我真的只是去睡覺。明天見。”

He didn’t sleep. His brain wouldn’t let him. He hated Dumbledore, and he hated Greyback, he hated the war, and as the hours got smaller and smaller, he hated Peter too.

他沒有睡。他的大腦不讓他睡。他恨鄧布利多，他恨格雷伯克，他恨戰爭，隨著時間越來越少，他也恨彼得。

He did not hate the other werewolf, though; the one who was not Greyback. Just as he had not hated Livia, though she frightened him. The more Remus thought about what was ahead of him, the less sure he was about his preparedness.

但他不恨另一個狼人；那個不是格雷伯克的。就像他沒有恨過莉維亞一樣，雖然她讓他害怕。雷木斯越想越不確定自己是否準備好了。

Yes, he knew more curses and hexes now than Regulus and Severus combined (probably), but the more he thought back to his encounter with Livia, the less useful these things seemed. Hadn’t she said it herself? “You can wear that uniform and wave your silly stick, but you know that you have more in common with me than anyone in that castle.” He knew she was stronger than him; she could hurt him if she wanted to - but she hadn’t, not really. Instead, he remembered the pity he had felt, immediately after their meeting. He remembered the desire to help her, and his conversations with both Ferox and Dumbledore.

是的，他現在知道的詛咒和咒語比雷古勒斯和賽弗勒斯加起來還多（可能），但他越想起與莉維亞的相遇，這些東西似乎越沒用。她不是自己說過嗎？“你可以穿那套制服，揮動你那愚蠢的魔杖，但你知道你和我比這城堡裡的任何人都有更多的共同點。”他知道她比他強；如果她想傷害他，她可以——但她沒有，並不是那樣。相反，他記得他們見面後立即感到的憐憫。他記得想要幫助她的渴望，還有他與費羅克斯和鄧布利多的對話。

As dawn broke, Remus lay wide awake, thinking at a million miles an hour, his heart hammering and his stomach fizzing with excited anticipation. If he had to go to war, then fine. But this was his battle, and it would be on his terms.

黎明破曉時，雷木斯清醒地躺著，每小時思緒飛速，心跳如雷，胃部因興奮的期待而發麻。如果他不得不參戰，那也好。但這是他的戰鬥，他將按照自己的方式進行。

* * *

It was an April morning when they told us we should go

As I turned to you, you smiled at me

How could we say no?

 

Oh, the fun to have

To live the dreams we always had

Oh, the songs to sing

When we at last return again

Slipping off a glancing kiss

To those who claim they know

Below the streets that steam and hiss

The devil's in his hole

 

--

Saturday 21st January 1978

1978年1月21日，星期六

Breakfast that morning was a bleak affair. Remus was ravenously hungry, but no one else seemed to be eating. Sirius was on black coffee, and it was already making him jittery; he kept bobbing up and down in his seat. Mary and Marlene were the only ones acting halfway normal, because neither of them knew about the assignment.

那天早上的早餐氣氛非常沉悶。Remus非常餓，但其他人似乎都沒有胃口。Sirius只喝黑咖啡，這已經讓他變得緊張不安；他不停地在座位上上下晃動。Mary和Marlene是唯一表現正常的人，因為她們都不知道這次任務。

“Three Broomsticks, later?” Mary asked, brightly.

“一會兒去三把掃帚？”Mary明亮地問道。

Lily and James nodded, trying to smile, and succeeding only in looking slightly deranged. They were holding hands under the table again, and Remus was trying not to think about it, instead reaching for the plate of bacon for another helping.

Lily和James點點頭，努力微笑，但結果只讓他們看起來有點瘋狂。他們又在桌子下牽著手，Remus努力不去想這件事，轉而伸手拿盤子裡的培根再來一份。

“Can I bring Yaz?” Marlene was asking Mary. Mary raised an eyebrow,

“我可以帶Yaz來嗎？”Marlene問Mary。Mary揚起一眉。

“I mean, I suppose …”

“嗯，我想可以……”

“Great.” Marlene grinned. Mary’s mouth twisted, but she didn’t say anything.

“太好了。”Marlene咧嘴笑了。Mary嘴角扭曲，但她什麼也沒說。

The walk into Hogsmeade seemed longer than ever. Fortunately Lily and James had duties to perform, so at least they weren’t following Remus about, just waiting. Unfortunately, Sirius had enough nervous energy for three people, and Remus could feel it coming off him in waves.

走到霍格莫德的路似乎比以往任何時候都長。幸運的是，Lily和James有任務要執行，所以至少他們沒有跟著Remus，只是等著。不幸的是，Sirius有足夠的緊張能量可以供三個人使用，Remus能感受到這股能量一波波從他身上散發出來。

“Where shall we go?” He murmured, low enough so only Peter and Remus could hear.

“我們去哪裡？”他低聲咕噥，聲音低到只有Peter和Remus能聽到。

“Everywhere, I s’pose.”

“哪裡都去，我想。”

“Would it help if I was Padfoot?”

“如果我變成Padfoot會有幫助嗎？”

“If you like.”

“如果你願意。”

“Shall I change too?” Peter asked.

“我也要變嗎？”Peter問道。

“If you like.”

“如果你願意。”

Remus was unable to summon up very much interest. He was too busy trying to work out whether or not Hogsmeade smelled genuinely different, or whether it was because he usually tried to ignore scents as a human.

Remus提不起太多興趣。他正忙著想弄清楚霍格莫德是否真的有不同的氣味，還是因為他通常作為人類時會忽略氣味。

They ducked into a shop alleyway and Peter and Sirius transformed behind some bins. Wormtail crawled onto Remus’s palm, and he sat him on his shoulder. The weight was a small comfort, even if his whiskers tickled Remus’s neck. Nice to have Padfoot too, big and black and excitable, trotting alongside like a loyal companion. Yes. Much better when your friends aren’t human, in Remus’s opinion. At least, right now.

他們躲進一條商店的小巷裡，Peter和Sirius在一些垃圾箱後面變形。Wormtail爬上Remus的手掌，然後他把Wormtail放在肩上。這重量帶來了一點安慰，即使他的鬍鬚讓Remus的脖子發癢。Padfoot也很好，大而黑，興奮不已，像忠實的同伴一樣在旁邊小跑。是的，當你的朋友不是人類時會好很多，至少現在是這樣。

They walked. Remus deliberately avoided the high street, instead wandering around the backs of the houses. How many people lived in Hogsmeade? How many were potentially in danger, without even knowing it? He tried sniffing the air, and it was like exercising a muscle he had allowed to atrophy.

他們走著。Remus故意避開大街，而是在房屋後面漫步。霍格莫德有多少人居住？有多少人可能處於危險之中，卻渾然不知？他試著嗅嗅空氣，就像鍛煉一塊他已經讓其萎縮的肌肉。

Some scents came through stronger than others. Padfoot, obviously, and Wormtail. Household waste from the bins, compost from back gardens, and magic - that heavy, iron taste which settled on his tongue like treacle when he was this close to the moon. Other students, the sickly sweet aroma of Honeyduke’s and the comforting smell of parchment emanating from Scrivenshaft's.

有些氣味比其他氣味更強烈。顯然是Padfoot和Wormtail。垃圾箱裡的家庭廢物，後院的堆肥，還有魔法——那種沉重的鐵味，當他離滿月這麼近時，這種味道就像糖漿一樣落在他的舌頭上。還有其他學生，蜂蜜公爵的甜膩香氣，以及來自Scrivenshaft's的羊皮紙散發出的安慰氣味。

The forest. He could smell the forest, if he really tried. He closed his eyes briefly and inhaled. Green, lush, dense, teeming with life… and magic. At first it seemed like an indulgent whim, just an idea that he rather liked the smell, and wanted to get closer. But the further they walked, and the closer they got, the more important it felt. Remus had the impression that something had been drawing him in this direction for some time now.

森林。他可以聞到森林的味道，如果他真的試一試的話。他短暫地閉上眼睛，吸了一口氣。綠色，茂盛，濃密，充滿生命……還有魔法。起初這似乎是一個放縱的念頭，只是一個他相當喜歡這種氣味，並想靠近一點的想法。但他們走得越遠，越接近，這種感覺就越重要。Remus有一種印象，這段時間以來有什麼東西一直在吸引他向這個方向前進。

The Forbidden Forest loomed large over the little village, miles and miles of darkness and danger, against a backdrop of blue-grey snow-capped mountains. For the first time (as a human, anyway) Remus had the urge to go in - to explore.

禁林在這個小村莊上空隱約可見，無邊無際的黑暗和危險，以藍灰色積雪覆蓋的山脈為背景。這是第一次（至少作為人類）Remus有了進去探索的衝動。

Padfoot whined beside him as they left Hogsmeade and the road behind them. He wondered if Sirius could smell it too, but it was impossible to get any kind of sense out of him in dog-form. Remus tried to switch off his rational mind for a moment - was there anything there at all, or was he just overthinking?

當他們離開霍格莫德和身後的道路時，Padfoot在他旁邊呻吟。他想知道Sirius是否也能聞到這氣味，但在狗形態下是不可能得到任何感覺的。Remus試圖關掉理智的大腦片刻——那裡到底有什麼，還是他只是想得太多了？

The magic in the forest wasn’t the same as at Hogwarts; it wasn’t human, it didn’t have that metallic, gunpowder smell Remus had come to associate with most witches and wizards he knew. It was more organic; less precise; a heady, mulchy smell of soil and decay. There was power, in there. He knew this instinctively - dizzying, huge, earth-moving power. It would have been frightening, once. But the closer Remus grew, the surer he was - the power was his, if he wanted it. All he needed to do was let it in. Another scent revealed itself; an animal; blood. Remus felt the wolf inside stir, and his desire to enter the forest grew almost impossible to resist.

森林中的魔法與霍格沃茲的不一樣；它不是人類的，它沒有那種金屬的火藥味，Remus已經把這種味道與他所認識的大多數巫師和巫師聯繫在一起。它更有機；不那麼精確；一種泥土和腐爛的濃烈氣味。那裡有力量。他本能地知道——令人頭暈目眩的，巨大的，地動山搖的力量。曾經這是可怕的。但Remus越接近，他就越確信——這力量是他的，如果他想要的話。他所需要做的就是讓它進來。另一種氣味顯現出來；一種動物的；血。Remus感覺到內心的狼在蠢蠢欲動，他進入森林的渴望變得幾乎無法抗拒。

Padfoot barked, sharply, and ran in front of him. The great black dog turned on Remus, raising its hackles and emitting a low growl. Remus blinked, snapping back into himself. Wormtail was speaking and quivering on his shoulder - maybe had been for a few minutes, now.

Padfoot尖聲吠叫，跑到他前面。大黑狗轉向Remus，豎起鬃毛，發出低沉的咆哮聲。Remus眨了眨眼，恢復了正常。Wormtail在他肩上說話並顫抖著——可能已經有幾分鐘了。

“Sirius.” Remus frowned. “Move.”

“Sirius。”Remus皺眉。“讓開。”

Padfoot continued to growl. Wormtail gave another squeak, before scuttling down Remus’s robes into his left pocket. Remus felt hot and angry - as if something had been snatched from him that he wanted. That he needed. He made to move forward, and Sirius transformed back into himself.

Padfoot繼續咆哮。Wormtail又發出一聲尖叫，然後爬下Remus的長袍進入他的左口袋。Remus感到熱和憤怒——就像有人從他手中奪走了他想要的東西。他需要的東西。他向前走，Sirius變回了自己。

“Where are you going?!” He said, still blocking Remus’s way. “Can’t you smell it?!”

“你要去哪裡？！”他說，仍然擋在Remus的路上。“你聞不到嗎？！”

Remus stopped trying to get past and caught Sirius’s eye,

Remus停止了嘗試超越，抓住了Sirius的目光，

“Can you?” He whispered, not quite believing it.

“你能嗎？”他低聲問道，有點不敢相信。

“There’s something bad in there. It must be the wolf.”

“裡面有不好的東西。一定是狼。”

“It is.” Remus nodded, eagerly. Surely that was obvious?!

“是的。”Remus急切地點點頭。當然這是顯而易見的？！

“I can’t be sure, though.” Sirius frowned.

“但我不能確定。”Sirius皺眉。

“I can.” Remus replied. “Let me past.”

“我能。”Remus回應。“讓我過去。”

Sirius moved again, blocking him.

Sirius再次移動，擋住他。

“No.” He said. “You’ve done what you said you’d do. We know it’s there. Let’s go back, now.”

“不。”他說。“你已經做了你說要做的事。我們知道它在那裡。現在我們回去吧。”

“I…” Remus stared over Sirius’s shoulder, into the dark, wintry wilds beyond. He wanted this so badly. More than he’d ever wanted anything; except - maybe - the boy standing before him. “I have to.” He finished. It was an insufficient explanation, but it was all he had.

“我……”Remus盯著Sirius的肩膀，望向外面的黑暗冬季荒野。他非常渴望這一切。比他曾經想要的任何東西都要多；除了——也許——站在他面前的男孩。“我必須。”他補充道。這是一個不足的解釋，但這是他唯一的解釋。

“There you lot are! Where’s Pete?”

“你們都在這裡！Pete在哪裡？”

Sirius and Remus’s deadlock was interrupted by James’s cheerful shout. They both turned to see him striding towards them from the village, Lily at his side. “What are you doing all the way out here? Thought you were supposed to be trailing your scent all over town or something.”

Sirius和Remus的僵局被James的愉快叫聲打斷。他們都轉過身來，看見他從村莊向他們大步走來，Lily在他身邊。“你們在這裡幹什麼？我以為你們應該在整個鎮上拖著你們的氣味或什麼的。”

“是的，我們現在正要回來。”Sirius說——Remus認為這相當厚顏無恥，更不用說自以為是了。

“你們可以。”Remus說。“我不回去。”

“Not what?” Lily asked, confused. “Where is Peter?”

“不什麼？”Lily困惑地問道。“Peter在哪裡？”

Remus could feel the warm weight of Wormtail’s furry little body in his pocket, but said nothing. James had been agonising for months over when to break the animagus thing to his girlfriend, and now was definitely not the right time.

Remus能感受到口袋裡Wormtail毛茸茸的小身體的溫暖重量，但什麼也沒說。James幾個月來一直在為何時向他女朋友透露變形師的事而痛苦，而現在絕對不是合適的時候。

“狼在裡面。”Sirius解釋道，“而Moony完全瘋了，決定他必須現在就進去面對它。”

Remus’s head snapped back to Sirius, outraged and betrayed.

Remus的頭猛然轉向Sirius，憤怒而被背叛。

“幫助我們理解，Remus，”Lily溫柔地走上前，“這不像你，衝進戰鬥……”

Remus nearly laughed in her face. Did no one remember who he was? What he was?

Remus差點對著她笑出聲來。沒有人記得他是誰嗎？他是什麼？

They were all staring at him, unconvinced. His anger flared again, and he had a very unpleasant thought - that he could very easily get past them, if he wanted to. The magic in the forest was more than enough; it made him feel strong. He could force his friends to stay in place, and it wouldn’t even tire him out, he probably wouldn’t even need his wand. 他們都盯著他，不相信。他的怒火再次燃起，他有一個非常不愉快的想法——如果他願意，他可以很容易地超越他們。森林中的魔法已經足夠多；它讓他感覺很強壯。他可以強迫他的朋友們留在原地，這甚至不會讓他感到疲倦，他可能甚至不需要他的魔杖。這個想法燃燒得如此明亮，讓他感到害怕。
