- AC-DC (Alternate current/direct current) is '70s slang for bisexuality.

 

 

Chapter 132: Seventh Year: Victims 

Howling. Whining. Scents - animals, magic, mould. He had to get out. Hunt. Pack. Pack. The big one tried to stop him. The black one tackled him. But he had to get out. He was so hungry. So hungry...
狼嚎。哀鳴。氣味——動物、魔法、霉味。他必須出去。狩獵。群體。群體。那隻大的一直試圖阻止他。那隻黑色的撞上了他。但他必須出去。他太餓了。太餓了……

“Remus?! Remus?? Wake up!”
“Remus？！Remus？？醒來！”

His eyes snapped open as Sirius shook him roughly by the shoulders.
Sirius 用力抓住他的肩膀，讓他的眼睛猛地睜開。

“Wha??”
“什麼？？？”

“Are you ok?”
“你還好嗎？”

He was lying on his back, on the dusty shack floor. He was bleeding, but he didn’t know where from. Sirius was bleeding too. Remus tried to sit up, and winced as his head rattled and his back creaked.
他躺在背上，臉朝上，躺在滿是灰塵的小屋地板上。他在流血，但不知道從哪裡來。Sirius 也在流血。Remus 試著坐起來，卻因為頭部的震動和背部的咔嚓聲而疼痛。

“What happened?” He gasped, throat raw from howling - or screaming.
“發生了什麼？”他喘息著問，喉嚨因狼嚎——或是尖叫而沙啞。

“Here,” Sirius helped him up, and over to the bed. He pulled out a goblet - Remus didn’t know where he’d got it - and whispered, “Auguamenti.” Sirius’s hands were shaking as water poured from his wand, and he handed it to Remus, who drank greedily, spilling it down his front. He knew something was wrong; he could smell the blood and the fear and the sunrise, but it was taking longer than usual for his human thoughts to come back to him; like waking up still drunk with a hangover to boot.
“在這裡，”Sirius 幫助他站起來，帶到床邊。他拿出一個高腳杯——Remus 不知道他從哪裡弄來的——輕聲說道，“Auguamenti。”Sirius 的手在搖晃，水從他的魔杖中流出，他把杯子遞給 Remus，Remus 貪婪地喝著，水灑了一身。他知道有些不對勁；他能聞到血腥氣和恐懼和日出的味道，但他的人的思維回到他身上的時間比平時更長，就像醒來時還是醉著加上宿醉一樣。

“What happened?” he asked again, frowning, “Are you hurt?”
“發生了什麼？”他再次問，皺著眉頭，“你受傷了嗎？”

“It’s fine,” Sirius shook his head. He looked very pale - not his usual aristocratic alabaster, but sickly, worried, yellowish with sweat. “You just nipped me a few times - you kept trying to get out.”
“沒事，”Sirius 搖了搖頭。他看起來非常蒼白——不是他平時那種貴族般的白皙，而是病恹恹的、擔心的，帶有汗水的黃色。“你只是咬了我幾次——你一直在試圖出去。”

“Did I--?!” Remus grabbed him, suddenly, pulling his shirt. Sirius pushed him down, gently, reaching for blankets to cover him with. He shook his head,
“我——？！”Remus 突然抓住他，拉扯著他的襯衫。Sirius 輕輕地把他推下去，拿起毯子給他蓋上。他搖了搖頭，

“No, we kept you here. You never left, I promise you.”
“不，我們一直留在這裡。你從未離開，我向你保證。”

“Where are the others?”
“其他人呢？”

“They had to go - Madam Pomfrey’ll be here soon. When you turned back it was different - harder than normal, I think. You wouldn’t wake up properly, so James left me the cloak. I didn’t want to leave you here.”
“他們得走了——Madam Pomfrey 很快就會來的。當你變回人的時候不一樣了——比平常更困難，我覺得。你無法正常醒來，所以 James 留給我了斗篷。我不想把你留在這裡。”

Remus lay back, his mind racing. He tried to remember, but it was all scrambled up. He only knew one thing for sure.
Remus 躺回去，腦海中一片混亂。他試著回憶，但一切都亂成一團。他只知道一件事。

“Something really bad happened.” He whispered. His own voice was trembling now, and cold dread settled in his stomach like a sickness. Sirius didn’t say anything. He just squeezed his hand.
“發生了真的很糟糕的事。”他低聲說道。他的聲音現在在顫抖，寒冷的恐懼像病一樣在胃裡安定下來。Sirius 沒有說話。他只是握住了他的手。

He hid under the cloak as soon as Madam Pomfrey arrived, and she hurried in, with a terrible grey look on her own face. He sat up, every muscle screaming at him,
他在 Madam Pomfrey 到達的時候立刻藏在斗篷下，她匆匆進來，臉上帶著可怕的灰色神情。他坐起來，每一塊肌肉都在尖叫，

“Poppy!” He rasped, “What happened? Please tell me!”
“Poppy！”他嘶啞地說，“發生了什麼？請告訴我！”

“How are you, first?” She asked, coming over to feel his forehead, “You’re running very high.”
“你怎麼樣，首先？”她問道，過來摸他的額頭，“你發燒很高。”

“I feel fine,” he lied, batting her hand away impatiently, “There was an attack, wasn’t there?”
“我覺得很好，”他撒謊道，不耐煩地拍開她的手，“發生了攻擊，是不是？”

She nodded, wordlessly. His heart thumped, “Who? How many?”
她無言點頭。他的心跳加速，“誰？多少人？”

“I don’t know.” She said, very quietly. He had never heard that voice come out of her before. For a moment, she wouldn’t even meet his eyes. She had always looked him in the eye.
“我不知道。”她非常輕聲說道。他從未聽到過她發出那種聲音。她有一會兒甚至不願意看他的眼睛。她總是直視著他的眼睛。

“Please.” He said again. She shook her head, very slightly.
“請。”他再次說道。她輕輕搖了搖頭。

“There’s nothing I can tell you. It’ll be in the morning news.”
“我不能告訴你什麼。這會在早晨的新聞中報導。”

“I have to see Dumbledore!”
“我得去見 Dumbledore！”

“He’s not here.” She stood up, “Now, can you walk? Professor McGonagall says you’re to go to your lessons as usual, if you’re fit enough? We don’t want anyone asking where you are. I’ll give you something for the pain.”
“他不在這裡。”她站起來說，“現在，你能走嗎？Professor McGonagall 說如果你能夠適應的話，應該照常去上課。我們不想讓任何人問你在哪裡。我會給你一些止痛藥。”

They walked through the tunnel in silence, with Sirius behind them, still invisible. Madam Pomfrey dealt with the worst of his scratches - mostly from Padfoot, though fortunately she assumed he’d done them to himself - and told him to carry on about his day. He took the potion she gave him, but his head still throbbed and his body ached. As soon as she had turned a corner, Sirius revealed himself, and slid an arm around Remus’s back.
他們靜靜地穿過隧道，Sirius 在他們身後，仍然隱形。Madam Pomfrey 處理了他最糟糕的刮痕——主要來自 Padfoot，幸好她以為這些傷是他自己造成的——並告訴他繼續過他的日子。他喝下她給他的藥水，但頭部仍然劇烈疼痛，身體也在疼痛。她一轉角，Sirius 就顯形，將手臂搭在 Remus 的背上。

“Why are you pretending you’re ok?” He hissed, supporting Remus up the stairs back to their dorm, “You can barely walk!”
“你為什麼假裝你沒事？”他咝咝地說，扶著 Remus 上樓回到宿舍，“你幾乎走不動！”

“I’ll be fine in a minute.” Remus replied, gritting his teeth, “She’s got enough to worry about. Ugh, fucking stairs.”
“我馬上就會好的。”Remus 回答道，咬牙切齒，“她有足夠的事要擔心。唉，該死的樓梯。”

“James said he’d send an owl to his dad right away,” Sirius said, as they slowly traversed the marble staircase, “If anyone knows what’s happened, the Potters will.”
“James 說他會馬上給他爸爸發一封貓頭鷹信，”Sirius 說道，他們慢慢走過大理石樓梯，“如果有人知道發生了什麼，Potters 會知道。”

“Yeah,” Remus nodded, wheezing, “Good…” But he knew that it was all no good. Whatever had happened, had happened, and it had been just as awful as Castor promised. It was the end of any chance of civility for the werewolves.
“是的，”Remus 點了點頭，喘著氣，“很好……”但他知道這一切都沒有用。無論發生了什麼，都已經發生了，而且就像 Castor 承諾的那樣糟糕。這意味著狼人失去了任何文明的機會。

Back in the dorm room, James was still waiting for a reply from his parents. Remus sat down on his bed, heavily, chest heaving, every part of him aching, his skin on fire.
回到宿舍，James 還在等待他父母的回覆。Remus 重重地坐在床上，胸口起伏不定，身體的每一部分都在疼痛，皮膚燒灼著。

“You could just bunk off,” Sirius said, awkwardly, glancing at the others, “We do it all the time.”
“你可以不去上課，”Sirius 尷尬地說，看了看其他人，“我們經常這樣做。”

Remus shook his head. He hauled himself up, clutching the bed frame.
Remus 搖了搖頭。他掙扎著站起來，緊緊抓住床架。

“Can’t risk it. We’ve got Arithmancy first, Snape’s in that - if the papers are full of werewolf attacks and I’m not there, what d’you want to bet he’ll be the first to start stirring? I’m going for a shower, just a minute.”
“不能冒這個險。我們第一節課是算術，Snape 在那裡——如果報紙上滿是狼人攻擊而我不在，那你怎麼看他會不會是第一個開始炒作的人？我去洗個澡，馬上就來。”

He could hear the other three marauders whispering loudly through the bathroom door, but he hadn’t the energy to focus on anything except getting through the next six hours. He turned on the taps and let the hissing water drown them out.
他能聽到另外三個調皮捣蛋者在浴室門外大聲低語，但他沒力氣去關注任何事情，只想度過接下來的六個小時。他打開水龍頭，讓嘶嘶的水聲淹沒他們的聲音。

WEREWOLF ATTACKS - MAGICAL COMMUNITY DEMANDS ACTION!
狼人攻擊 - 魔法界要求採取行動！

Hundreds were affected by a string of brutal werewolf attacks during last nights full moon which left fifteen wizards dead and at least five missing - presumed kidnapped. None of the creatures responsible have been identified as yet, and the Auror’s office has advised everyone to be on high alert, and to consult the published ministry guidelines on identifying and approaching werewolves, which are classified XXXXX and considered highly dangerous.
數百人受到昨晚滿月期間一系列殘暴狼人攻擊的影響，造成十五名巫師死亡，至少五人失踪——被認為是被綁架了。負責的生物至今尚未被確認，奧羅部門已經建議大家保持高度警惕，並參考已發布的部門指南，以識別和接近狼人，這些指南被列為 XXXXX，並被認為極其危險。

The interim minister for magic has been criticised for failure to maintain the Werewolf Register, established by Newt Scamander in 1947. Speaking for the opposition, Abraxas Malfoy released a statement in the early hours of this morning:
臨時魔法部長因未能維護1947年由 Newt Scamander 設立的狼人登記冊而受到批評。反對派發言人 Abraxas Malfoy 在今天清晨發表了一份聲明：

“Last night’s attacks are further proof that the ministry is in dire need of reform, and on behalf of the ancient and law abiding magical families of Great Britain we demand stricter sanctions on half humans and other undesirable and potentially dangerous elements.”
“昨晚的攻擊進一步證明了魔法部迫切需要改革，代表大不列顛的古老且守法的魔法家庭，我們要求對半人類和其他不受歡迎的、潛在危險的元素實施更嚴格的制裁。”

This statement has provoked outrage in what insiders are describing as an increasingly divided ministry…”
這份聲明在內部人士描述的越來越分裂的魔法部中引發了憤怒……”

---

 

“No names.” James muttered darkly. “That’s not good.”
“没有名字。”James 黑暗地嘟囔道，“这不好。”

“Protecting the victims’ families?” Sirius suggested.
“保护受害者的家人？”Sirius 提议道。

“Since when has the Daily Prophet cared about that?” Lily hissed, venomously. “Since when has the ministry?!”
“《预言家日报》什么时候关心这些事了？”Lily 恶毒地说道，“魔法部又什么时候关心过？！”

“Careful what you say!” Peter whispered, his eyes wide, “My cousin who works at the Prophet said they’re being sent really strict guidelines on what they can write - about the ministry, the war, anything - and there are spies everywhere checking on them, making sure no one’s being too critical.”
“说话小心点！”Peter 低声说，眼睛睁得大大的，“我表哥在《预言家日报》工作，说他们收到了一些非常严格的写作指南——关于魔法部、战争、任何事情——而且到处都有间谍监视他们，确保没有人过于批评。”

This made everyone go quiet, and Lily looked around nervously, glancing over her shoulder. It didn’t matter; everyone in the Great Hall seemed to be talking about the same thing, huddled in groups over newspapers, whispering amongst themselves.
这让大家都安静了下来，Lily 紧张地四处张望，回头看了看。没关系；大礼堂里的每个人似乎都在讨论同一件事，成群结队地围绕着报纸，低声窃窃私语。

“It’s not as if we’re disagreeing with what the paper says,” Marlene whispered, leaning forward, “I hate Malfoy’s politics as much as the next half-blood, but he’s right about the failures of the register. The werewolves need to be contained, or stuff like this will happen, dark lord or not!”
“这不是说我们不同意报纸上的内容，”Marlene 低声说，向前倾身，“我对 Malfoy 的政治厌恶不亚于下一个混血巫师，但他关于登记册失败的说法是对的。狼人需要被控制，否则这种事情会发生，无论是否有黑魔头！”

“That’s ridiculous!” Sirius scoffed, “An organised attack like this only happens when there’s someone behind it, this would never happen without Voldemort goading them.”
“这真荒谬！”Sirius 讥讽道，“像这样的有组织的攻击只有在背后有某人操控时才会发生，没有伏地魔的煽动，这绝对不会发生。”

Everyone winced as he said the name. Remus had noticed that happening more and more, as the list of missing grew and people trusted each other less.
他提到那个名字时，大家都畏缩了一下。Remus 注意到这种情况越来越频繁，失踪人员的名单不断增加，人们之间的信任也越来越少。

“They’re still dangerous.” Marlene replied. “I don’t see why we’re pretending they aren’t - it says right here,” she jabbed the black and white print, “Classified XXXXX. I know it’s unfortunate for them, they might have been perfectly normal otherwise, but facts are facts.”
“他们仍然很危险。”Marlene 回复道，“我不明白我们为什么要假装他们不是——这里写着，”她戳了戳黑白印刷的文字，“分类 XXXXX。我知道这对他们来说不幸，他们可能本来是完全正常的，但事实就是事实。”

No one said anything to that.
对此没有人说什么。

Remus doing his best to ignore all of them. He was busy writing a letter to Professor Ferox, who was the only person he could think of who had been in potential danger last night. Livia knew him; he had attacked her once, and Remus thought she seemed like the sort of person to hold a grudge. Besides, writing gave him something to distract himself from how dreadful he felt; aching and shivery all over. He knew he looked awful too, and thought it best to keep his head down.
Remus 竭尽全力忽略他们。他忙于给 Ferox 教授写信，Ferox 教授是他唯一能想到的昨晚可能处于危险中的人。Livia 认识他；他曾经攻击过她，Remus 觉得她似乎是那种会怀恨在心的人。此外，写信让他有事可做，以分散他感到糟糕的情绪；全身疼痛和发抖。他也知道自己看起来很糟糕，觉得还是低头比较好。

“She doesn’t know what she’s talking about.” Lily whispered to him, on their way out of the Hall. “Marls just sees everything as black and white. Don’t take it personally,”
“她不知道自己在说什么。”Lily 低声对他说，正准备离开礼堂，“Marls 只是把一切都看成是非黑即白。不要放在心上。”

“I don’t.” Remus replied, tiredly, “I’m fine, don’t worry about me.”
“我不会的。”Remus 疲倦地回答道，“我没事，别担心我。”

Still, he was dreading Care of Magical Creatures later that morning, when he’d have to sit next to Marlene. He’d cast a glamour to cover up his newer scars, and was sipping on a Pepper Up potion as if it was keeping him alive, but he couldn’t hide the fact that he was utterly exhausted. Not to mention the bone crushing guilt he felt over the attacks. He’d known they were going to happen. He’d told Dumbledore, but it hadn’t been enough, he ought to have done more.
尽管如此，他还是很害怕上午晚些时候的神奇生物护理课，因为他不得不坐在 Marlene 旁边。他施了一个魅影咒来掩盖他新的伤疤，并像喝了 Pepper Up 药水一样，仿佛它能让他活下去，但他无法掩饰自己完全疲惫的事实。更不用说他对这些袭击感到的沉重内疚。他早就知道这些事会发生。他已经告诉了邓布利多，但这还不够，他应该做得更多。

Arithmancy wasn’t too bad; he had Sirius, James and Lily in that, and they formed a protective huddle around him, taking their seats at the back of the class. The exercises were almost impossible to do, Remus found his mind oddly fractured; unable to hold down a thought for very long. James and Sirius fell into their usual clownish mischief, creating a satisfactory distraction any time the teacher glanced up at Remus. He was so grateful, especially as they had both been up all night too.
算术课还算不错；他有 Sirius、James 和 Lily 在其中，他们围成了一个保护性的小圈子，坐在教室的后面。作业几乎不可能完成，Remus 发现自己的思维异常碎片化，无法长时间集中注意力。James 和 Sirius 进入了他们惯有的滑稽恶作剧，任何时候老师瞥向 Remus 时，他们都制造了令人满意的分心。他非常感激，尤其是他们两个整晚也没休息。

Afterwards, Sirius walked him to Care of Magical Creatures, as he had a free hour, and Remus hadn’t the energy to refuse. The hallways were too busy for him to risk leaning on the other boy for support, so they just went slowly.
之后，Sirius 带着他去上神奇生物护理课，因为他有一个空闲的小时，而 Remus 没有精力拒绝。走廊太拥挤，他不敢依靠其他男孩的支持，只能慢慢走。

“Just bunk off?” Sirius pleaded, watching him struggle down the third flight of stairs, “You’ve shown your face, Snivellus has seen you…”
“干脆逃课？”Sirius 恳求道，看着他艰难地走下第三段楼梯，“你已经露面了，Snivellus 已经看见你了……”

Remus just shook his head, carrying on doggedly. As he reached the bottom, a couple of third year boys rushed past, shouting at each other and laughing. One of them bumped into Remus with his bag, which would have been nothing on a good day, but at that moment was exactly the wrong thing, and knocked Remus sideways into the bannister. He bit his lip as the left side of his body hit the hard stone, but couldn’t help letting out a gasp of pain.
Remus 只是摇了摇头，执着地继续前行。当他到达楼梯底部时，几个三年级的男孩冲过来，相互喊叫着笑。一个男孩用他的包撞到了 Remus，这在平时没什么，但在那个时刻正好是错误的举动，将 Remus 撞到了一侧的扶手上。他咬住嘴唇，感到身体的左侧撞上了坚硬的石头，但忍不住发出了一声痛苦的喘息。

“Syrtis-corpius!” Sirius yelled, pulling his wand out and firing the hex at all three boys. They yelped as the marble staircases turned to quicksand beneath them, and began to swallow them up. Sirius only stopped it when their legs were dangling through the bottom and they were both trapped halfway. “Watch where you’re going!” He said, menacingly, before helping Remus down the last few steps.
“Syrtis-corpius！”Sirius 大喊，抽出魔杖，对三个男孩施了咒语。他们尖叫着，因为大理石楼梯变成了流沙，开始吞噬他们。Sirius 直到他们的腿悬在底部，被困在中途才停止了咒语。“小心点！”他说，带着威胁，随后帮助 Remus 下完最后几步台阶。

No one intervened - no one ever did when it was Sirius - and Remus was too focussed on getting to his lesson on time.
没有人插手——当是 Sirius 时，没人会插手——而 Remus 只专注于准时到达他的课程。

“Promise me you’ll go back and free them?” He asked, as they neared the classroom, “I don’t need you getting a detention on top of everything…”
“答应我你会回去解救他们？”他问道，随着他们接近教室，“我不希望你再因为这事被拘留……”

“If someone else hasn’t found them,” Sirius shrugged. “I only taught them a lesson, any prefect would have done the same.”
“如果其他人还没有发现他们，”Sirius 轻描淡写地说，“我只是给他们上了一课，任何一个监考员都会这么做。”

Remus usually would have found that funny, but he felt as though he was wading through quicksand too, his limbs heavy and slow, everything around him foggy and blurred. “Right,” Sirius was saying, “I’ll be back here in an hour to get you.”
Remus 通常会觉得这很有趣，但他感觉自己也像在流沙中一样，四肢沉重缓慢，周围的一切都模糊不清。“好，”Sirius 说，“我会在一个小时后回来接你。”

“I don’t need collecting, I’m not a child.” Remus muttered.
“我不需要接送，我不是小孩子。”Remus 嘟囔道。

“No,” Sirius squeezed his hand, very quickly, “You’re my Moony.”
“不，”Sirius 很快地握了握他的手，“你是我的 Moony。”

He made a mental note to save that up for later, when he was alone, and could bask in the thought of being Sirius’s anything. Just now he hated himself too much to allow anyone to be kind.
他在心里记下了稍后独自一人时保存那个想法的决定，那时他可以沉浸在成为 Sirius 的任何人的念头中。此刻，他太讨厌自己了，无法允许任何人对他表示友善。

Care of Magical Creatures was worse than he could have imagined. His temperature was running even higher from the exertion, and he had to keep wiping sweat from his eyes, hair sticking to his forehead. Despite breakfast having been only an hour earlier, his stomach felt like an empty cavern, growling intermittently. His head ached and his vision swam, but he sat bolt upright, staring fixedly at the blackboard.
神奇生物护理课比他想象的还要糟糕。他的体温因劳累而更高，他不得不不断擦拭汗水，头发黏在额头上。尽管早餐才一个小时前，但他的胃感觉像个空洞，不时发出咕咕声。头痛，视线模糊，但他坐得笔直，目不转睛地盯着黑板。

They were supposed to be doing dragons - identifying the various species and their individual properties. Kettleburn began the lesson as he always did, with a terrifying and usually harrowing story of an encounter he’d had with whichever creature they were discussing. Today was no different, and the battle-scarred professor was in his element today - he had lost two limbs to dragons.
他们应该在学习龙——识别各种龙的种类及其特性。Kettleburn 像往常一样开始了课程，用一个恐怖且通常令人痛苦的故事讲述他与他们讨论的生物的遭遇。今天也没有例外，这位满身伤痕的教授今天表现得非常得心应手——他曾因龙而失去了两条肢体。

Despite this animated tale, only half of the class was actually paying attention (you could tell by the look of faint horror on their faces as they scribbled down notes). The other half - Marlene and Mary included - was busy reading the chapter in their textbooks which concerned werewolves.
尽管有这个生动的故事，只有一半的班级实际上在注意（你可以从他们边写笔记边露出的微弱恐惧中看出来）。另一半——包括 Marlene 和 Mary——则忙于阅读教科书中有关狼人的章节。

“There’s something a bit sexy about the whole beast-man thing, though,” Mary whispered across Remus, who began to feel light-headed.
“不过，整个野兽人之类的东西还是有点性感的，”Mary 低声对 Remus 说道，Remus 开始感到头晕。

“Mary!” Marlene hissed, angrily, “That’s completely insensitive, people died!”
“Mary！”Marlene 生气地低声斥责，“这完全是没心没肺，人们死了！”

“I’m just saying!”
“我只是说说而已！”

“You wouldn’t think that, anyway, if you met a real one! I spoke to Sian Bolsh over the summer; she left last year for healer training, and she’s been shadowing a healer on the lycanthropy ward at St. Mungo’s. They have awful hygiene, most of them, because they can’t live near normal wizards, and they basically live off hand-outs and charity--”
“如果你见到真正的狼人，你不会这么想！我在暑假时和 Sian Bolsh 说过；她去年离开去接受治疗师培训，她一直在 St. Mungo’s 的狼人病房跟随一位治疗师。他们中的大多数人卫生条件极差，因为他们不能住在正常巫师附近，他们基本上依靠施舍和慈善——”

“Well then I feel sorry for them!” Mary snapped back, “That sounds horrible, wizards are so heartless.”
“那我就为他们感到难过！”Mary 回嘴道，“这听起来太可怕了，巫师们真是无情。”

“You’re being deliberately dense! They’re not safe --”
“你故意无知！他们不安全——”

“Excuse me, Professor Kettleburn,” the whole class turned to see McGonagall standing in the doorway. Remus’s stomach dropped - had she come for him? Had the ministry finally come for him?!
“打扰了，Kettleburn 教授，”全班转头看到 McGonagall 站在门口。Remus 的胃一下子沉了下来——她是来找他的吗？难道魔法部终于来找他了吗？！

The head of Gryffindor house looked very grave, and was holding a letter in her hand, but she did not look at Remus. “I am sorry to interrupt. Marlene McKinnon, may I speak to you?”
格兰芬多学院院长看起来非常严肃，手里拿着一封信，但她没有看 Remus。“抱歉打扰了。我能和 Marlene McKinnon 谈谈吗？”

Marlene frowned and stood up, setting her quill back into the inkwell. She threw a confused glance back at Mary and Remus before following Professor McGonagall out of the room. The door closed and everyone stared at it in silence.
Marlene 皱了皱眉，站起身，把羽毛笔放回墨水瓶里。她困惑地看了一眼 Mary 和 Remus，然后跟着 McGonagall 教授离开了房间。门关上了，大家默默地盯着门看。

“She can’t be in trouble,” Mary whispered to Remus, “She’s too goody-goody.”
“她不可能惹上麻烦，”Mary 低声对 Remus 说，“她太乖了。”

Remus mumbled something, but his hunger had turned into queasiness and he didn’t want to open his mouth. He wished he could take off his cloak, the room was so stuffy and hot; he was getting uncomfortably damp under his armpits and across his back. “Are you all right, sweetheart?” Mary asked, her face concerned. “You look like you’re going to puke, is it Kettleburn’s horrid stories?”
Remus 嘟囔了几句，但饥饿变成了恶心，他不想张嘴。他希望自己能脱下外套，这个房间太闷热了；他的腋下和背部感到不舒服地潮湿。“你还好吗，亲爱的？”Mary 问道，脸上带着担忧。“你看起来要吐了，是 Kettleburn 的可怕故事吗？”

“Mmmph.” Remus nodded very slightly, shooting pains firsting up his neck as he did so. He rested his forehead in his hands, hoping he just looked like he was really interested in his notes.
“Mmmph。”Remus 微微点了点头，脖子上先是一阵刺痛。他将额头靠在手上，希望自己看起来只是对笔记非常感兴趣。

There was no room for Mary to probe him anymore, though. A horrible shriek sounded outside the classroom, followed by a chilling moan of absolute despair. Mary was on her feet at once, and flew out of the room to see her friend. Remus caught only a glimpse as the door swung open and shut, of Marlene on her knees, sobbing, and McGonagall bent over her, patting her shoulders.
不过，Mary 再也没有机会探问他了。教室外传来一声可怕的尖叫，随后是一声彻底绝望的寒冷呻吟。Mary 立刻站起身，飞快地跑出房间去找她的朋友。Remus 只在门开合时瞥见了一眼，看到 Marlene 跪在地上抽泣，McGonagall 弯下身，拍着她的肩膀。

Even Kettleburn was rendered mute for a few minutes, before regaining his composure, and clearing his throat.
连 Kettleburn 也沉默了几分钟，然后才恢复镇定，清了清喉咙。

“We’re living in difficult times,” he said, quite out of character, “I urge you all to be kind to each other, especially as you prepare to leave Hogwarts.”
“我们生活在艰难的时期，”他说，完全不像平时，“我敦促你们彼此善待，尤其是在你们准备离开霍格沃茨的时候。”

The lesson continued after that, much subdued, and it took all of Remus’s concentration to stay conscious in his seat, now that he was alone on his desk. About fifteen minutes before the class was due to end, there was a second knock at the door.
课程在那之后继续进行，变得更加沉寂，Remus 需要集中全部注意力才能保持清醒。就在课程结束前大约十五分钟，门上又响起了第二声敲门声。

“Enter!” Kettleburn barked. The door opened, and Lily walked in,
“进来！”Kettleburn 吼道。门开了，Lily 走了进来，

“Good morning, professor, I’ve just come to collect Marlene’s things for her.”
“早上好，教授，我来给 Marlene 收拾东西。”

Kettleburn nodded and gestured at Marlene’s desk, where her work was still spread out, her book bag hanging off the back of her chair. Lily went over and quickly started gathering things together. She took one look at Remus and raised her head, “Sorry, professor - could I ask Remus to come with me? I didn’t realise Mary left all of her bits too…”
Kettleburn 点了点头，示意 Marlene 的桌子，那里她的工作还散落着，她的书包挂在椅子背上。Lily 过去，迅速开始收拾东西。她看了一眼 Remus，抬起头，“抱歉，教授——我能让 Remus 跟我一起走吗？我没意识到 Mary 也把所有东西都忘了……”

“Of course, of course,” Kettleburn nodded, distractedly, labelling a diagram of a dragon’s lair on the board. “Chapters eighteen to twenty five for next lesson, please, Mr Lupin.”
“当然，当然，”Kettleburn 心不在焉地点了点头，给黑板上的龙穴图标上标签。“下一节课请看第十八章到第二十五章，Lupin 先生。”

“Yes sir,” Remus croaked, picking up Mary’s bag. Thank god it wasn’t heavy. And thank god for Lily Evans.
“是的，先生，”Remus 嘶哑地答道，拿起 Mary 的书包。谢天谢地，它不重。也谢天谢地有 Lily Evans。

As soon as they were outside in the corridor, Remus leaned heavily against the wall and closed his eyes.
一出到走廊，Remus 就重重地靠在墙上，闭上了眼睛。

“Oh, Remus,” Lily said, anxiously, raising a cool hand to his forehead, “You look dreadful!”
“哦，Remus，”Lily 焦急地说，伸出凉爽的手摸了摸他的额头，“你看起来很糟糕！”

“I’m fine.” He mumbled, uselessly, eyes still shut, “Just give me a second… is Marlene…?”
“我没事。”他无力地嘟囔，眼睛仍然闭着，“给我一点时间……Marlene……”

“She’s gone home.” Lily lowered her voice, though they were quite alone, “Her brother, Danny, was attacked last night. St. Mungo’s started realising names.”
“她回家了。”Lily 降低了声音，尽管他们很孤独，“她的哥哥 Danny 昨晚遭到了袭击。St. Mungo’s 开始确认名字。”

Remus’s head swam; he opened his eyes only to see black spots, and closed them again, in case he fainted,
Remus 的头晕了；他睁开眼睛只看到黑点，又闭上了，以防他昏倒。

“Is he…”
“他怎么样了……”

“He’s alive. But… it doesn’t sound very good.”
“他还活着。但是……听起来不是很好。”

The guilt was overwhelming, roaring in Remus’s ears. How would he ever look Marlene in the eye again? “Come on,” Lily took his arm and draped it over her shoulders. 内疚感压倒了一切，在 Remus 的耳边轰鸣。他怎么能再直视 Marlene 的眼睛？ “走吧，”Lily 扶着他的胳膊，搭在她的肩膀上。她的体型非常贴合，但他不敢过多依靠她，“我带你去塔楼，你现在没有状态上学。我会说你在帮我为 Marlene 收拾东西。”

“Someone ought to tell--” He was about to say Yasmin, but realised that it was still a secret. “...Madam Pomfrey.” He finished, lamely, “Marlene’s going to miss healing lessons.”
“有人应该告诉——”他正要提 Yasmin，却意识到那还是个秘密。“……Madam Pomfrey。”他无力地补充道，“Marlene 会错过治疗课。”

“I’m sure she already knows,” Lily replied, briskly, “Come along, now.”
“我相信她已经知道了，”Lily 迅速回答，“我们走吧。”

She was a lot harder to refuse than Sirius.
她比 Sirius 更难拒绝。

 

Chapter 133: Seventh Year: Sunday Afternoon 

Sunday 29th January 1978

“Moony?”

“Mmm?”

“It’s after midday…”

“So?”

“Thought you might fancy getting up?”

“...no thanks.”

“Can I come in?”

“...no.”

“...ok, then.” Sirius began to walk away, and Remus’s stomach flipped.
“...好吧。”天狼星开始走开，雷木斯的胃翻了个跟头。

“I’m sorry.” He said, loud enough for Sirius to hear, and stop. Remus finally crawled out of the covers. “I do want you here, I just don’t know what to say.”
“对不起。”他大声说道，让天狼星听到并停下。雷木斯终于从被子里爬了出来。“我确实希望你在这里，只是我不知道该说什么。”

He could hear Sirius fidgeting, his hands in his pockets, then running through his hair. Finally,
他能听到天狼星在扭动，手插在口袋里，然后用手揉着头发。最后，

“We don’t have to talk?”
“我们不需要谈话吗？”

Remus sighed. He was a mess; he hadn’t washed properly since Wednesday, and had only got out of bed to use the bathroom. The other boys had been feeding him by passing food through the crack in his curtains, and if they hadn’t Remus wasn’t sure if he’d have eaten at all. He was in the worst state he’d ever been in. But he missed Sirius.
雷木斯叹了口气。他一团糟；自从星期三以来他没有好好洗过澡，只是为了上厕所才离开床铺。其他男孩通过帘缝给他送食物，如果没有他们，雷木斯不确定自己是否会吃东西。他处于他有史以来最糟糕的状态。但他很想天狼星。

“...好吧。”

“谢谢，”他低声对雷木斯的头发说，“谢谢你让我进来。”

“我觉得我一定很臭。”

天狼星深吸了一口气，挠了挠雷木斯的额头，让他扭动身体。

“不，闻起来只是像月狼一样。”

“滚开，狗头。”雷木斯从他身边挪开了。

Remus chuckled, and it felt strange, but good. Still, he had a melancholic episode to maintain.
雷木斯轻笑了一声，这感觉很奇怪，但也很好。不过，他还是要维持那种忧郁的情绪。

“你在流血吗？我能闻到血腥味。”

“可能是你，来自满月的伤口。”

“No, I’ve healed already, I never have open wounds longer than a day.”
“不，我已经愈合了，我从来不会有超过一天的开放伤口。”

“天呐，”天狼星轻轻地笑了，“你怎么可能变得更酷呢？！”

“And it's your blood, I can tell.”
“而且是你的血，我可以分辨出来。”

“There you go again! You’re basically a superhero.”
“你又来了！你简直是个超级英雄。”

“ Sirius!”
“天狼星！”

“Ok, ok,” he sat up, running his hands through his hair. “You swiped at me a few times over the moon, I told you that, we did it to each other. And you can’t turn me when I’m a dog, we’ve tested that enough times.”
“好，好，”他坐起来，跑过手发。 “你在满月时挠了我几次，我告诉过你，我们互相做过。你不能在我变成狗的时候变回我，我们已经测试了很多次。”

“But you’re still bleeding?! It was almost a week ago! You need to go to Madam Pomfrey!”
“但你还在流血？！已经快一周了！你需要去找庞弗雷夫人！”

“Oh yeah, and say my werewolf boyfriend scratched me while I was in dog form as an illegal animagus?!”
“哦，对了，还要说我变成狗的时候被我的狼人男朋友抓伤了，作为一个非法的动画形态？！”

“天啊。”雷木斯呻吟着，拉起自己从床上起来，抓住天狼星的手腕，拉着他往外走。

“Where are we going?!”
“我们要去哪儿？！”

“I need better light!”
“我需要更好的光线！”

他猛地打开了浴室的门，狠狠地拍下了马桶盖。“坐下。”他指示道。天狼星顺从地坐下，半笑着。

Remus opened the little mirror cabinet above the sink, digging out murtlap essence and disinfectant and gauze and cotton balls. (He had found over years of trial and error that a combination of magical and muggle things worked best. As with almost everything else.) He pulled his wand out of his pyjama bottoms and stood in front of Sirius.
雷木斯打开了洗手池上方的小镜柜，挖出了墨特拉普精华、消毒剂、纱布和棉球。（他发现经过多年的尝试和错误，魔法和麻瓜的结合效果最佳。就像几乎所有其他事情一样。）他从睡裤里抽出他的魔杖，站在天狼星面前。

“Ok. Show me.”
“好吧。给我看看。”

Sirius dropped his head, no longer enjoying Remus’s newfound motivation. He sighed heavily and lifted his shirt, saying, “It's not that bad…”
“也不是那么糟糕……”

It wasn’t as bad as Remus had feared, but it still made his stomach clench when he saw. Three dark red stripes, across Sirius’s ribs. They were starting to heal, but he knew he could fix it fairly easily. He took a deep breath, met Sirius’s eye, and then reached for the disinfectant. Then his wand. Remus was pretty good at healing cuts now, and the scab and the redness were gone in an instant. Now they were white stripes.
“没有 Remus 想象中的那么糟糕，但看到它时他仍感到肚子一阵绞痛。Sirius 的肋骨上有三道深红色的伤痕。伤痕开始愈合了，但他知道自己可以很容易地处理好它。他深吸了一口气，与 Sirius 对视，然后拿起消毒剂和魔杖。Remus 现在对治疗伤口相当擅长，伤疤和红肿瞬间消失。现在只剩下白色的伤痕。”

“I’m so sorry,” he said, mournfully. “It was a magical wound. You’ll have a scar there for the rest of your life, now.”
“对不起，”他忧伤地说，“这是一个魔法伤口。你现在会在那里留下一个伤疤，余生都带着它。”

Sirius looked down at the mark, then up again.
“Sirius 低头看了看伤痕，然后又抬起头来。”

“That's fine, Remus.” He said, quietly.
“没关系，Remus。”他静静地说道。

So, Remus rejoined the group, at Sirius’s goading, and they were all kind enough to pretend he had merely been unwell, and not avoiding them. The news over the past few days had been particularly grim. First the Prophet had published a list of the dead, and their photographs. Then they had published a list of those ‘presumed bitten’, along with their photographs, which had provoked outcry among some of the more liberal commentators, and ignited a debate on mandatory registration for all werewolves.
“所以，在 Sirius 的刺激下，Remus 重新加入了团队，他们都好心地假装他只是生病了，而不是在躲避他们。过去几天的新闻特别令人沮丧。首先，《预言家日报》发布了死者名单和他们的照片。然后，他们发布了‘疑似被咬’者的名单和他们的照片，这在一些更自由派的评论员中引发了抗议，并引发了关于所有狼人强制登记的辩论。”

Greyback’s name had not been mentioned, nor any other werewolf that Remus was aware of. It was as if the horrific crimes simply happened one night, and the assailants had vanished into thin air. No one had heard from Marlene, either, though Danny McKinnon was one of those named in the papers.
“Greyback 的名字没有被提到，也没有提到其他 Remus 知道的狼人。仿佛那些可怕的罪行只是发生在某个夜晚，而袭击者就这样消失在空气中。Marlene 也没有消息，虽然 Danny McKinnon 是报纸上提到的其中一个人。”

He’d been given a full four inches of text, by virtue of his celebrity as beater for the Chudley Cannons. The team’s manager was interviewed and quoted saying that while he had not yet been briefed on the details Danny’s condition, the Cannons operated a ‘zero-tolerance’ policy to ‘half-breeds and dangerous creatures’, and would deal with any allegations of infection accordingly. James vowed that he would never see a Chudley Cannons game again, but Remus mostly felt sorry for Danny.
“由于他是 Chudley Cannons 的击球手，他获得了整整四英寸的报道。球队经理接受了采访，并引用了他的话，表示虽然他尚未获得 Danny 病情的详细情况，但 Cannons 执行对‘半血和危险生物’的‘零容忍’政策，并将根据任何感染指控采取措施。James 发誓再也不看 Chudley Cannons 的比赛了，但 Remus 对 Danny 感到更为遗憾。”

They tried to put all of this misery behind them, and went down for Sunday lunch (and thank goodness; it was generally Remus’s favourite meal of the week, and he’d have been even more blue if he’d missed it), then spent the rest of the evening cosied up in the common room in front of the fire. “他们尽力将所有这些痛苦抛在脑后，去享用周日午餐（谢天谢地；这通常是 Remus 一周中最喜欢的餐点，如果错过了他会更沮丧），然后在火炉前的公共休息室里度过了余下的晚上。Remus 甚至同意和 Peter 下了一盘棋，Peter 高兴得很。”

“‘你知道我们该开始认真对待什么了，”Sirius 一边整理他的唱片收藏，一边沉思道。”

“‘NEWts（普通巫师文凭考试）？’Remus 希望地问道，当 Peter 捕捉到他的骑士时。”

“Job applications?” Lily said, from the arm chair, where she sat in James’s lap, reading a magazine.
“‘工作申请？’Lily 说，从扶手椅上，她坐在 James 的腿上，看着一本杂志。”

“The quidditch cup?” James suggested.
“‘魁地奇杯？’James 提议道。”

“For goodness sake,” Sirius tiutted, “I’m ashamed to call you all marauders.”
“‘真是的，’Sirius 不满地嘟囔道，‘我都不好意思叫你们这些人作恶作剧者了。’”

“What?!” All three of them frowned, offended. Peter chuckled,
“‘什么？！’他们三个人都皱起了眉头，感到被冒犯了。Peter 笑了起来，”

“He’s talking about the big prank on Slytherin. You know, we started planning it before Christmas.”
“‘他说的是对 Slytherin 的大恶作剧。你知道的，我们在圣诞节前就开始策划了。”

“Wormy-boy, you are without a doubt my very favourite person.” Sirius grinned broadly. Peter snorted,
“‘Wormy-boy，你无疑是我最喜欢的人。’Sirius 露出了灿烂的笑容。Peter 哼了一声，”

“Bugger off,” and promptly captured Remus’s queen.
“‘滚开，’然后迅速捕捉到 Remus 的皇后。”

“‘唉。我不知道我为什么要费心，自从我十三岁以来就没有赢过你。’Remus 叹了口气，双肘撑在地毯上。他抬头看着 Sirius，‘那？有计划吗？’”

“‘也许吧。不管我们做什么，我认为我们应该把攻击重点放在地下室。’”

“Let’s not throw around words like ‘attack’,” Lily said, hurriedly, “This is just a practical joke, right? In the wholesome spirit of harmless house rivalry?”
“‘别用‘攻击’这种词语，’Lily 急忙说，‘这只是个恶作剧，对吧？以一种无害的宿舍竞争的健康精神？’”

“‘天哪，最后一次了，他们不是我的‘小喽啰’！’Remus 翻了个白眼。‘反正，我们这学期还没有召开过一次正式的学习小组。我最近有点忙。’”

“Well, as none of us are scheduled to be in mortal peril for the next month or so,” Sirius replied, “I think we ought to get cracking. Everyone could do with a laugh, eh? Assemble the troops, we’ll meet sometime next week.”
“‘好吧，由于我们这一个月左右都没有预定要面临生死危险，’Sirius 回答道，‘我认为我们应该开始行动了。大家都需要笑一笑，对吧？召集部队，我们下周某个时候见。’”

“其他人都看了看钟表，或者开始打哈欠，并同意跟着一起去。公共休息室现在也在清理，他们是最后几个离开的。”

Remus had just got his pyjamas on and brushed his teeth, when he remembered that he’d left his book downstairs. While that didn’t usually matter, this particular book was Maurice, by E.M. Forster, and though the cover was nondescript, he was a bit concerned that if someone picked it up and read the blurb there would be raised eyebrows.
“Remus 刚换上睡衣刷好牙，就想起他把书落在了楼下。虽然这通常没什么关系，但这本书是 E.M. Forster 的《Maurice》，尽管封面不显眼，他还是有点担心如果有人拿起它看到书摘会引起怀疑。”

“叹了口气，他离开浴室，急匆匆下楼，一边对排在队里的 Sirius 嘟囔着‘去拿我的书’。”
