“他刚拿到书，正准备上楼时，听到肖像洞滑开了。他转身看到 Mary 进来了。她穿着一条短短的闪闪发光的银色裙子，进门时摔了一下，但她自己稳住了，咯咯地笑了起来。”

“All right?” He called to her.
“‘一切还好吗？’他对她喊道。”

She looked up, squinting a bit in the dim light.
“她抬头看了看，在昏暗的光线中微微眯眼。”

“Hiya, sexy,” she grinned, wandering in a bit unsteady on her feet. Might have been the four inch heels she was wearing. Or it might have been the Witches Brew Remus could smell wafting off her.
“‘嗨，性感的家伙，’她咧嘴笑道，脚步有些不稳地走了进来。可能是她穿的四英寸高跟鞋。也可能是 Remus 可以闻到的那股 Witches Brew 酒味。”

“Hello, been somewhere?” He walked back towards the couches, wanting to make sure she was all right before leaving.
“‘你好，去哪儿了？’他走回沙发旁，想确保她没事才离开。”

“Pfffff.” She waved a hand, collapsing into the nearest armchair, spreading her legs out. Her short dress rode up her thighs, but she didn’t seem bothered, “Just a few drinks in the Ravenclaw common room.”
“‘哼哼。’她挥了挥手，倒在最近的扶手椅上，腿分开。她的短裙滑到大腿上，但她似乎不在意，‘只是 Ravenclaw 休息室喝了几杯酒。’”

“Thought you were seeing a Hufflepuff?”
“‘我以为你去见一个 Hufflepuff 呢？’”

“Mm, he was there.” She exhaled, smiling, tilted her head back and closed her eyes. The lids were painted gold, finely rimmed with kohl. She looked like an Egyptian queen in a party frock. “But a lot of people were there, I s’pose.”
“‘嗯，他在那里。’她呼气，微笑着，把头向后仰，闭上了眼睛。眼睑涂成金色，精细地用 kohl 修饰。她看起来像一位穿着派对礼服的埃及女王。‘但我想很多人都在那里。’”

She sounded sad. Remus sat down in the armchair opposite her, clutching the book in his lap.
“她听起来很伤心。Remus 坐在她对面的扶手椅上，抱着膝上的书。”

“Are you ok, Mary?”
“‘Mary，你还好吗？’”

“Oh. Fine.” She opened her eyes, slowly, and smiled at him. She wasn’t that drunk, he realised, but she looked tired, and deeply unhappy. “Just stuff on my mind. Boys being wankers. Poor Marlene.”
“‘哦，还好。’她慢慢地睁开眼睛，对他微笑。她并没有那么醉，Remus 发现，但她看起来很疲倦，也非常不开心。‘只是脑子里有些事。男孩们太讨厌了。可怜的 Marlene。’”

“Have you heard from her?”
“‘你有她的消息吗？’”

Mary shook her head, then sat up, blinking.
“Mary 摇了摇头，然后坐直了，眨了眨眼睛。”

“Haven’t got a fag, have you sweetheart? I don’t usually, but I just really fancy one.”
“‘你有烟吗，亲爱的？我平时不抽，但现在特别想要一根。’”

“Yeah,” Remus reached in his pockets for his matchbox, where he kept the cigarettes he had rolled himself. He slid it open, “Normal or fun?”
“‘有，’Remus 从口袋里拿出他用来存放自己卷的香烟的火柴盒。他打开了它，‘普通的还是有趣的？’”

“Oooh, fun, please,” she purred, reaching over, “Might help me sleep.”
“‘哦，趣味的，谢谢，’她咕哝道，伸手过来，‘也许会帮我睡觉。’”

“Um, about Marlene,” Remus said, lighting his own, “I just had a thought, er… you know her friend Yaz? Have you seen her about? I wasn’t sure if anyone told her--”
“‘嗯，关于 Marlene，’Remus 说，点燃自己的烟，‘我刚有个想法，呃……你知道她的朋友 Yaz 吗？你见过她吗？我不确定是否有人告诉她——’”

“I did.” Mary said, exhaling, watching Remus through the smoke beneath her heavy golden eyelids. “I told her.”
“‘我告诉过她。’Mary 说，呼气，透过烟雾看着 Remus，眼睑沉重且金光闪闪。‘我告诉她了。’”

“Oh!” Remus blinked, surprised. “That’s good, then.”
“‘哦！’Remus 眨了眨眼睛，感到惊讶。‘那就好。’”

“Mmm, I thought she had better know,” Mary mused, pulling a strand of her hair and winding it coyly around her little finger. “Didn’t want her to think Marls had gone cold on her.”
“‘嗯，我觉得她最好知道，’Mary 思索道，把一缕头发绕在小指上。‘不想让她觉得 Marls 对她冷淡了。’”

Remus took a quick, sharp puff on his cigarette, frowning very slightly.
“Remus 吸了一口烟，微微皱了皱眉。”

“What do you mean?”
“‘你什么意思？’”

Mary laughed, arching back in the chair, showing her pearly white teeth. She let the curl of hair spring back into place like a corkscrew.
“Mary 笑了，向椅子后靠，露出一口白牙。她让那缕卷发像螺旋一样回到原位。”

“Oh come on, Remus,” she shook her head, “I know.”
“‘哦，别这样，Remus，’她摇摇头，‘我知道的。’”

“You… she told you?”
“‘你……她告诉你了？’”

“No,” Mary conceded, settling back down with a sigh, “But I’m not thick, despite rumours to the contrary. At least, I know what romance looks like.” She arched her eyebrow, “I’m not as dense as James, for example. How long did he take to figure it out?”
“‘没有，’Mary 承认，叹了口气，‘但我并不愚蠢，尽管有相反的传闻。至少，我知道什么是浪漫。’她挑了挑眉，‘我不像 James 那么迟钝，比如他花了多长时间才弄明白？’”

“He doesn’t know about Marlene,” Remus replied, “They must keep it quiet during quidditch stuff.”
“‘他不知道 Marlene 的事，’Remus 说道，‘他们肯定在魁地奇的时候保持安静。’”

“I’m not talking about Marlene, now. I’m talking about you.”
“‘我现在不是说 Marlene 的事。我说的是你。’”

“Me?!”

“He’s a good kisser, isn’t he?” She winked at him. “But then, you were too, I seem to remember.”
“‘我？!’”

“他亲吻得很好，不是吗？”她对他眨了眨眼。“但我记得你也很棒。”**

“How…?!”

“Mm, I’ve suspected for a little while now. Just little things. All the time you spend together. His being single for more than five minutes. I wasn’t a hundred percent sure, but you’ve just confirmed it for me.”
“‘嗯，我有点怀疑了一段时间了。只是一些小细节。你们一直在一起的时间。他单身超过五分钟。我不是百分之百确定，但你刚刚证实了。’”

“Bugger.”“‘真讨厌。’

She laughed again, a friendly, trilling sound.她又笑了一下，声音亲切而清脆。

“Silly boy.” She smiled affectionately, playing with her hair again as she smoked. She looked at him again, her eyes more focussed. When she spoke, her voice was more serious than normal. “It’s fine if you want to keep it quiet. I was going to wait, to see if you told me yourself - like I’m doing with Marls. But. I just wanted to let you know… I know I’ve got this reputation for being a bit of a big mouth, but I can keep a secret, ok? Especially for my friends. And if…” She bit her lip, “If there’s anything else you’re keeping secret, Remus, then you can trust me, ok? It doesn’t change anything.”

“‘傻孩子。’她亲切地笑着，一边玩弄自己的头发。一边吸烟。她再次看着他，眼神更加专注。她说话时，语气比平时更严肃。‘如果你想保密是没关系的。我原本打算等你自己告诉我——就像我对 Marls 做的那样。但是。我只是想让你知道……我知道我有点爱说话的名声，但我可以保守秘密，好吗？尤其是对我的朋友们。如果……’她咬了咬嘴唇，‘如果你还有其他秘密，Remus，你可以相信我，好吗？这不会改变什么。’”**

This was almost too many revelations for one evening. Remus sucked hard on his cigarette, and half wished he’d opted for a spliff too.
“这几乎是一个晚上太多的揭示了。Remus 使劲吸了一口烟，半希望自己也抽了个大麻卷。”

“What are you saying?” He asked, very carefully. “Do you think you know something… else?”
“‘你在说什么？’他小心翼翼地问。‘你觉得你知道其他的东西吗？’”

“Remus.” She sat up. “The scars? Being ill every full moon? We do the same Care of Magical Creatures class.”
“‘Remus。’她坐直了。‘那些伤疤？每次满月生病？我们上同一门神奇生物学课的。’”

“You can’t tell anyone.” Remus said, his voice very low, even though they were completely alone. “Please, Mary… me and Sirius, that’s one thing, but this… I could get kicked out of school. I could get arrested!”
“‘你不能告诉任何人。’Remus 说，声音非常低，尽管他们完全是独处的。‘拜托，Mary……我和 Sirius 的事是一码事，但这……我可能会被开除。我可能会被逮捕！’”

“Hey!” Mary stood up, quickly, and came over to sit on the arm of the chair, “I’m not going to tell! That’s what I’m trying to explain.” She wound an arm around his shoulder. “Makes no difference to me, I swear.”
“‘嘿！’Mary 快速站起，坐到椅子的扶手上，‘我不会告诉的！这就是我想解释的。’她把手臂绕到他的肩膀上。‘对我来说没什么区别，我发誓。’”

“Really?”
“‘真的？’”

“Honestly.” She kissed his cheek and gave him a squeeze. “So don’t take what happened to Marlene’s brother so hard, eh? It was nothing to do with you.”
“‘真的。’她亲吻了他的脸颊，给了他一个拥抱。‘所以不要把 Marlene 的兄弟发生的事看得那么严重，好吗？这和你无关。’”

“She’d never forgive me, if she knew…” Remus said, sadly. Mary handed him what was left of the joint and he puffed on it gratefully.
“‘如果她知道的话，她永远不会原谅我……’Remus 伤心地说。Mary 把剩下的烟递给他，他感激地吸了一口。”

“Don’t worry about that,” She said, flippantly, “She’ll come around. She knows who you really are. And maybe you could help? You could write to Danny, even - I bet he could do with a friend.”
“‘别担心，’她轻描淡写地说，‘她会明白的。她知道你真正的样子。也许你可以帮忙？你可以写信给 Danny，甚至——我敢打赌他需要一个朋友。’”

“That’s--” Remus was about to say that while it was a really nice idea, it was almost impossible, considering the fact that he was unregistered, and it would be a bad idea to draw attention to himself.
“‘那是——’Remus 正要说虽然这是个很好的主意，但考虑到他没有登记，这几乎是不可能的，而且引起注意也不好。”

“Mooony, where are you?” Sirius’s plaintive voice came clattering down the stairs, “I can smell the pot all the way from here, you’re not being subtle-- oh! Hiya MacDonald.”
“‘Moony，你在哪儿？’Sirius 的哀怨声音从楼梯上传来，‘我能从这里闻到大麻的味道，你不够隐蔽——哦！嗨，MacDonald。’”

“Black,” Mary nodded, still perched on the arm of Remus’s chair, “Sorry, I’m trying to seduce your boyfriend.”
“‘Black，’Mary 点了点头，仍然坐在 Remus 椅子的扶手上，‘抱歉，我在试图勾引你的男朋友。’”

“Oh yeah, I’d like to see you -- wait, my what ?!”
“‘哦，我倒想看看你——等等，我的什么？！’”

She just poked out her tongue at him. He looked at Remus, “Are we just telling everyone, now?!”
“她只是向他吐了吐舌头。他看着 Remus，‘我们现在就告诉大家了吗？！’”

“Oi!” Mary hopped off the seat, “I’m not ‘everyone’! Arrogant tosser. Don’t forget I had you both first.”
“‘哎！’Mary 跳下座位，‘我不是‘大家’！自以为是的家伙。别忘了我先拥有了你们两个。’”

Remus couldn’t help laughing at the look on Sirius’s face, and got out of the chair, sheepishly, still clutching Maurice,
“Remus 忍不住笑了，看着 Sirius 的表情，他羞怯地起身，仍然抱着《Maurice》，”

“Sorry, I’ll come up now, we were just chatting.” He looked back at Mary, “Will you be ok?”

“‘抱歉，我现在上去，我们只是聊了一会儿。’他回头看向 Mary，‘你没事吧？’”

“Fine,” She nodded, smiling, “I’m off to bed too. Night lads!”
“‘没事，’她点头，笑着说，‘我也要去睡觉了。晚安，大家！’”

“Good night!”
“‘晚安！’”

Back upstairs in the warm glow of their dorm room, Peter was already snoring softly behind his curtains, and James was sitting cross-legged on his bed, flipping through his quidditch notebook.
“回到他们宿舍楼上的温暖灯光中，Peter 已经在窗帘后面轻轻打鼾，而 James 坐在床上盘腿坐着，翻阅他的魁地奇笔记本。”

“Thought we’d lost you, Moony,” he whispered cheerily, as the two boys entered.
“‘以为我们要丢失你了，Moony，’他高兴地低声说，当两个男孩进来的时候。”

“Bumped into Mary, she’s been at some party with the Ravenclaws.”
“‘碰见了 Mary，她在和 Ravenclaw 的人一起参加聚会。’”

“See, this is what happens when you get stuck with the Head Boy and the Head Girl in your house,” Sirius sighed, leaning back on his own bed, “All the fun happens elsewhere.”
“‘你看，这就是当你被困在你们宿舍的学长和学姐身边时会发生的事，’Sirius 叹了口气，靠在自己的床上，‘所有的乐趣都发生在别的地方。’”

“Oh, stop whinging,” James grinned, closing his book, “We’ll have more parties and you know it. Now go to bed like a good boy.”
“‘哦，别抱怨了，’James 露出笑容，合上书，‘我们还会有更多的聚会，你知道的。现在乖乖去睡觉吧。’”

“Fine,” Sirius yawned, falling backwards dramatically, so that he disappeared through the heavy velvet hangings.
“‘好吧，’Sirius 打了个哈欠，戏剧性地向后倒去，消失在厚重的天鹅绒帷幕后面。”

“G’night then,” Remus started, making for his own bed, but Sirius’s hand shot out and grabbed his wrist.
“‘那晚安了，’Remus 开始朝自己的床走去，但 Sirius 的手突然伸出抓住了他的手腕。”

“Moony…” he whispered softly, from the shadows behind the veil. Remus bit his lip and glanced over at James, who looked away awkwardly, and began to draw his own bed curtains across. Oh well. Fuck it.
“‘Moony……’他从帷幕后的阴影中轻声说道。Remus 咬了咬嘴唇，瞥了一眼 James，后者尴尬地移开视线，开始拉上自己的床帘。算了。去他妈的。”

“Mmm… ok…” Remus let Sirius pull him inside.
“‘嗯……好吧……’Remus 让 Sirius 拉他进去。”

 

Chapter 134: Seventh Year: Valentine's Day 1978 

You think I'm a lame duck

But I don't give a blue fuck

So you leave me like crazy

Drive me to be lazy.

I love you, you big dummy!

I love you you big dummy!

 

Monday 13th February 1978

“You know,” Lily yawned, “Other boyfriends might take the night before Valentine’s day to plan something nice for their girlfriends, rather than an assault on other students.”

“‘你知道，’Lily 打了个哈欠，‘其他男朋友可能会在情人节前夜计划一些漂亮的惊喜给他们的女朋友，而不是袭击其他学生。’”

“Thought we were calling it a practical joke, Evans,” Sirius winked. “Anyway, how do you know what other boys are doing? We’re the only boys you know, and we’re doing this.”
“‘以为我们叫它恶作剧呢，Evans，’Sirius 眨眨眼。‘不过，你怎么知道其他男孩在做什么？我们是你认识的唯一男孩，而我们正在做这个。’”

“Touchè.” Lily poked her tongue out at him from where she sat cross-legged on James’s bed.
“‘中肯。’Lily 坐在 James 的床上，盘腿坐着，伸出舌头对着他。”

“And,” James said, sitting on the floor beside Remus, folding envelopes as fast as Remus could stuff them, “How do you know I haven’t already planned something nice?!”
“‘而且，’James 说，坐在地板上，快速折叠信封，‘你怎么知道我还没计划好什么漂亮的东西？！’”

“When do you have the time?” She shrugged, “Whenever you’re not with me you’re playing quidditch.”
“‘你什么时候有时间？’她耸耸肩，‘每当你不和我在一起时，你都在打魁地奇。’”

“I can multi-task,” he said, haughtily, a mischievous twinkle in his eye.
“‘我可以多任务处理，’他说，傲慢地，眼中带着顽皮的光芒。”

Remus gave James a sideways glance. He couldn’t account for any of James’s free time either, but it was best never to underestimate James Potter.
“Remus 侧眼看了看 James。他也无法解释 James 的任何闲暇时间，但最好不要低估 James Potter。”

“How about you, Pete?” Mary asked, sitting on James’s other side, neatly stacking the envelopes he handed her and ticking names off the list, “Big plans for tomorrow?”
“‘你呢，Pete？’Mary 问道，坐在 James 的另一边，把他递给她的信封整齐地堆放起来，勾选名单上的名字，‘明天有大计划吗？’”

“Nope.” Peter replied, glumly. He was lying on his stomach on his bed, frantically completing the Charms notes due for the next day. He’d dropped a few hints to Remus about copying them, but Remus had pretended not to understand and eventually poor Wormtail had dropped it and just resigned himself to doing a poor job.
“‘没有。’Peter 沮丧地回答。他趴在床上，疯狂地完成第二天要交的咒语笔记。他向 Remus 透露了一些复制它们的暗示，但 Remus 假装不明白，最后可怜的 Wormtail 放弃了，只好接受做得不好。”

“What about Dorcas?” Mary pressed.
“‘Dorcas 怎么样？’Mary 继续追问。”

“Dumped me.”
“‘甩了我。’”

“Aw, poor love.” She cooed, “At least I won’t be the only single one.”
“‘哦，可怜的爱人。’她轻声说道，‘至少我不会是唯一的单身者。’”

“Really?” Pete looked up, hopefully.
“‘真的吗？’Pete 抬起头来，希望地问道。”

“Yep, dumped that stupid Hufflepuff.” Mary nodded, bent over her work.
“‘是的，甩了那个愚蠢的 Hufflepuff。’Mary 点了点头，弯腰继续她的工作。”

“Oh well, if you fancied dinner, maybe…” Peter started. Mary shook her head,
“‘哦，那样的话，如果你想吃晚饭，也许……’Peter 开始说。Mary 摇了摇头，”

“Oh no, sorry Pete, I’m triple booked as it is; it’ll be a miracle if none of them bump into each other.”
“‘哦，不，抱歉 Pete，我已经排满了；如果他们都不碰到彼此，那将是个奇迹。’”

“Oh.” Peter returned to his homework, looking even more depressed than before. Lily stifled a giggle, but Mary seemed oblivious.
“‘哦。’Peter 继续做作业，看起来比之前更沮丧了。Lily 压抑住笑声，但 Mary 似乎没有察觉。”

“Cheer up Pete, we still love you.” Remus offered, stuffing his very last envelope and handing it to James. “Me and Padfoot’ll have dinner with you.”
“‘振作起来 Pete，我们还是爱你的。’Remus 提议，把他最后一个信封塞好，递给 James。‘我和 Padfoot 会和你一起吃晚饭的。’”

“So basically exactly the same as every other night of the year.” Sirius teased.
“‘所以基本上和一年中的其他每个晚上一模一样。’Sirius 调侃道。”

“You two not doing anything, then?” Mary asked, casually. It felt like a loaded question, all the same, and Remus found it hard to ignore the glances his friends were now shooting at each other. He looked up at Sirius and said, very firmly,
“‘你们两个就不做什么了吗？’Mary 随意地问道。感觉像是个有内涵的问题，Remus 发现很难忽视朋友们现在互相投来的目光。他抬头看着 Sirius，非常坚定地说，”

“Don’t even think about it.”
“‘别想了。’”

Sirius’s face cracked into a smile,
“Sirius 的脸上露出了笑容，”

“I think Valentine’s Day is Moony’s idea of hell.”
“‘我觉得情人节是 Moony 的地狱。’”

“Exactly.” Remus nodded, solemnly. Let the girls have flowers and hearts. He had plenty else going on, thank you very much.
“‘正是。’Remus solemnly 点了点头。让女孩们去享受花朵和心形吧。他还有很多其他的事情要做，谢谢。”

“Aww, I think that’s a shame,” Mary said, crossing the last name off her list and stretching her legs out on the rug, lying back on her elbows. “Valentine’s Day can be nice, if you do it right.”
“‘哦，我觉得这很可惜，’Mary 说，划掉最后一个名字，伸展双腿躺在地毯上，撑着手肘仰卧。‘情人节可以很美好，只要你做得对。’”

Remus smirked at her. ‘Doing it right’ to Mary meant receiving votive offerings from her various acolytes; a fantasy in which she was Aphrodite, and all would pay homage.
“Remus 对她露出了笑容。对 Mary 来说，‘做得对’意味着收到她的各种追随者的奉献；她幻想自己是 Aphrodite，所有人都会敬奉她。”

“Nope, not interested.” He said, stretching his own stiff legs. “Just a normal day.”
“‘不，不感兴趣。’他说，伸展自己僵硬的腿。‘只是普通的一天。’”

“Sirius likes it.” Mary said, slyly, “He was always dead romantic.”
“‘Sirius 喜欢这个。’Mary 狡黠地说，‘他总是很浪漫。’”

“When we weren’t fighting.” Sirius interjected. Remus looked at him, and realised he had never actually considered whether or not the other boy was interested in celebrating the day. He’d just assumed they were on the same page.
“‘当我们没在吵架的时候。’Sirius 插话道。Remus 看了看他，意识到他从未真正考虑过其他男孩是否有兴趣庆祝这个节日。他只是认为他们在同一页上。”

“Anyway, that was different.” Peter mused, sucking the nib of his quill and getting ink on his lip.
“‘无论如何，那是不同的。’Peter 沉思道，吮吸着他的羽毛笔尖，弄得嘴唇上沾满了墨水。”

“What was?” Mary asked.
“‘什么不同了？’Mary 问道。”

“When Padfoot was going out with you.” Peter replied. “Obviously he did all the mushy stuff then.”
“‘当 Padfoot 和你约会的时候。’Peter 说。‘显然他当时做了所有那些浪漫的事情。’”

“Obviously?” Lily spoke up. Remus cringed. He could see where this was going. The redhead had her hackles up; it didn’t happen often, but when it did it always ended in a scolding. “What do you mean, Peter?”
“‘显而易见？’Lily 说。Remus 感到不安。他能看出接下来要发生什么。红发女孩情绪激动；这种情况不常发生，但每当发生时总是以训斥告终。‘你是什么意思，Peter？’”

Peter saw it coming too, but bless him, he tried to explain himself.
“Peter 也看出来了，但他还是试图解释自己。”

“I wasn’t being nasty,” he said, “It’s just… well it’s not the same thing, is it?”
“‘我不是在恶意中伤，’他说，‘只是……嗯，这不一样，不是吗？’”

“Yes it is!” Mary frowned.
“‘是的，确实是！’Mary 皱眉说。”

James was clearly annoyed too. Remus sighed, inwardly. He looked up at Sirius, who shrugged at him. Remus held out his hand, and Sirius hopped off the bed to take it, pulling Remus to his feet. Remus cleared his throat.
“James 显然也很恼火。Remus 内心叹了口气。他抬头看着 Sirius，Sirius 对他耸耸肩。Remus 伸出手，Sirius 从床上跳下来接过手，拉起 Remus 站起来。Remus 清了清嗓子。”

“If you’ve all finished discussing our relationship amongst yourselves?”
“‘如果你们都讨论完了我们的关系？’”

They all looked up, sheepishly.
“他们都羞愧地抬起头来看。”

“Sorry, Moony,
“‘抱歉，Moony，’”

“Sorry Remus.”
“‘抱歉，Remus。’”

“Let’s move on, shall we?” Remus raised an eyebrow, and leaned against his bedpost with his hands in his pockets. He nodded at the pile of sealed envelopes, “We need to pass those around tomorrow, as soon as. I think probably best to do it at breakfast, so it gets mixed in with the regular post and doesn’t look suspicious.”
“‘我们继续吧，好吗？’Remus 皱起眉头，双手插在口袋里，靠在床头。他点了点那些封好的信封，‘我们需要在明天尽快分发这些。我觉得最好在早餐时发，这样可以和正常的邮件混在一起，不容易引起怀疑。’”

This was met with a murmur of general agreement.
“大家普遍同意，表示了赞同。”

“Don’t forget, the ink only becomes legible when the right person gives their name.” Remus continued. He went over to his bedside table for his matchbox of cigarettes and slid one out.
“‘别忘了，墨水只有在正确的人写下名字时才会变得清晰。’Remus 继续说道。他走到床头柜那儿拿了一盒火柴烟，并抽出一根。”

“That was such a good idea, I can’t believe you did it so quickly.” Mary said. She didn’t know that the spell they’d used was exactly the same as the one on the Marauder’s Map, and they weren’t going to tell her.
“‘真是个好主意，我简直不敢相信你们这么快就做出来了。’Mary 说。她不知道他们使用的魔咒和 Marauder’s Map 上的魔咒完全一样，他们不打算告诉她。”

“You are in the presence of greatness, MacDonald.” Sirius said, taking Remus’s cigarette the second he’d lit it. Remus sighed and pulled out another.
“‘你身处伟大的存在之中，MacDonald。’Sirius 说，刚点燃 Remus 的烟时就拿走了。Remus 叹了口气，又拿出一根。”

“At least open a window if you have to smoke in here,” James sighed.
“‘如果你们非得在这里抽烟，至少开个窗，’James 叹了口气。”

“We have to smoke in here,” Sirius said, flicking his wand at the windows so that they flung wide open. “Because our poxy Head Boy banned smoking in the common room.”
“‘我们必须在这里抽烟，’Sirius 说，挥动魔杖把窗户打开。‘因为我们讨厌的学长禁止了在公共休息室抽烟。’”

“All the prefects voted on that, actually.” Lily said, wryly.
“‘其实，所有的级长都投了票。’Lily 讽刺地说道。”

“See, Moony,” Sirius nudged him with his hip, “This is why you should have stayed a prefect, you could have been the voice of dissent.”
“‘看，Moony，’Sirius 用臀部碰了碰他，‘这就是你应该继续做级长的原因，你本可以成为异议的声音。’”

“Truly tragic.” Remus exhaled smoke.
“‘真是悲剧。’Remus 吐出一口烟。”

“Right, I’m off to bed, then.” Mary said, getting up, lifting the pile of invitations and setting them down on James’s trunk. “I’m looking forward to this, be nice to have something else to think about.”
“‘好了，我去睡觉了。’Mary 说，站起身，把一堆邀请函拿起来，放在 James 的箱子上。‘我很期待这次，能有别的事情去想真是太好了。’”

“I’ll come with you.” Lily said, getting up too.
“‘我也和你一起去。’Lily 说，站起身。”

“Shall I walk you back?” James leapt to his feet. Both girls giggled, as if he had said something charming, rather than ridiculous,
“‘我送你们回去吗？’James 跳了起来。两个女孩咯咯笑着，好像他说了什么迷人的话，而不是荒谬的话，”

“I’ll keep her safe on the arduous journey across the common room, Potter.” Mary teased.
“‘我会在艰难的穿越公共休息室的旅程中保护她，Potter。’Mary 调侃道。”

Still Lily and James spent the next five minutes bidding each other goodbye, which involved a lot of snogging. When Mary finally managed to drag her friend away, Lily was pink and grinning,
“尽管如此，Lily 和 James 花了接下来的五分钟时间互相告别，期间有很多亲吻。当 Mary 最终设法拖走她的朋友时，Lily 脸红而笑着，”

“Love you!” She called on her way down the stairs,
“‘爱你！’她在下楼时喊道，”

“Love you too!” James called back.
“‘我也爱你！’James 回喊道。”

Sirius began to make sick noises, which made Peter start laughing, but Remus just watched James’s dopey expression. He hadn’t heard them say ‘I love you’ before. He didn’t think he’d ever heard anyone say it, actually; not anyone he cared about, at least. He’d seen it written down. In books, and in the letter from Hope. But neither of those things had felt as tangible as this. How long had they been saying that? As long as they’d been feeling it? Was it hard to say the first time? Remus thought it must be. Like casting a patronus.
“Sirius 开始发出恶心的声音，让 Peter 开始笑起来，但 Remus 只是看着 James 那呆呆的表情。他以前没有听到他们说‘我爱你’。他实际上不认为他听到过任何人说过这个，至少不是他关心的人。他见过这个词写下来。在书里，还有 Hope 的信中。但是这些东西都没有像现在这样真实。他们已经说了多久？和他们有的感觉一样久吗？第一次说难吗？Remus 认为一定很难。就像施展守护神一样。”

He finished his cigarette in a contemplative mood while the others moved around him, finishing homework and changing for bed. He supposed he could ask Sirius about the whole ‘love’ thing, but he wasn’t sure he wanted to open that can of worms. They were happy as they were, weren’t they? It was just getting comfortable, now that their friends knew. Plus, after two years of pining and almost a year of secrecy, Remus wanted to just enjoy what they had, without all of that prescriptive stuff hanging over them.
“他在沉思中完成了他的香烟，而其他人则在他周围活动，完成作业和换衣服上床。他想他可以问 Sirius 关于‘爱’的事情，但他不确定是否想打开这个话题。他们现在的幸福不是很完美吗？现在他们的朋友都知道了，他们只是变得更舒服了。再加上，两年的思慕和近一年的秘密，Remus 只想享受他们拥有的，而不必让那些规定性的东西悬在他们头上。”

Remus knew from experience that it was best to resist the temptation to pick things like that apart. Especially something as precious and hard won as he and Sirius had. The problem was; once you started, you might never remember how it worked in the first place.
“Remus 从经验中知道，最好还是抵制将这些东西拆解的诱惑。特别是像他和 Sirius 之间那样珍贵且来之不易的东西。问题是；一旦开始，你可能永远也不会记得最初是怎么运作的。”

He brushed his teeth still thinking, and wandered towards Sirius’s bed to sit and wait for him.
“他边刷牙边思考，然后走向 Sirius 的床，坐下等待他。”

“Finished!” Peter cried, raising his quill with a flourish. “Finally.”
“‘完成了！’Peter 高呼，扬起他的羽毛笔。‘终于。’”

“Well done, Pete.” James yawned, climbing into bed.
“‘干得好，Pete。’James 打了个哈欠，上床睡觉。”

“I didn’t get to help you lot, though.” Peter said, looking at the pile of envelopes wistfully.
“‘不过，我没能帮你们。’Peter 说，怀着惆怅的目光看着那堆信封。”

“That’s ok, this is only preliminary work.” Remus offered, “The real planning starts on Wednesday.”
“‘没关系，这只是初步工作。’Remus 说，‘真正的计划从星期三开始。’”

“Exactly.” James nodded encouragingly, “Anyway, don’t feel bad, Padfoot didn’t help either.”
“‘确切的。’James 鼓励地点了点头，‘总之，别难过，Padfoot 也没有帮忙。’”

“Oi!” Sirius came out of the bathroom at that moment, “I wrote the damn things! Where would you lot be without my beautiful penmanship? And I don’t recall Mrs Prongs doing anything either.”
“‘喂！’Sirius 这时从浴室出来，‘我写了那些该死的东西！要是没有我美丽的字迹，你们会在哪里？我也不记得 Mrs Prongs 做了什么。’”

He had taken to calling Lily this in private (he wouldn’t dare to her face) with the full knowledge that it annoyed James. The messy-haired boy just rolled over in bed, flicking his middle finger in Sirius’s direction. Sirius chuckled and got into his own bed. Remus got in too, still deep in thought.
“他私下里开始这样称呼 Lily（他不会当面这样叫她），完全知道这让 James 恼火。那位乱发的男孩只是翻了个身，用中指朝 Sirius 的方向挥了挥。Sirius 笑了笑，躺回到自己的床上。Remus 也躺下了，仍然深思熟虑。”

“Night lads!” Sirius called, drawing the curtains shut.
“‘晚安，各位！’Sirius 叫道，拉上窗帘。”

“Night!” Peter and James echoed back.
“‘晚安！’Peter 和 James 回应道。”

In the dark, Sirius held Remus’s hand, and they smiled at each other sleepily.
“在黑暗中，Sirius 握着 Remus 的手，他们疲惫地对视而笑。”

“You’re very quiet.” Sirius whispered. “Everything ok?”
“‘你很安静。’Sirius 低声说，‘一切都好吗？’”

“Yeah.” Remus whispered back. “Just thinking. Prank stuff.”
“‘嗯。’Remus 低声回答，‘只是想着，恶作剧的事。’”

“Good.”

“...Sirius?”

“Remus.”

“You know Valentine’s Day?”

“Heard of it.”

“Did you want to… er. What Mary said…”

 

 

“I knew that would get you wound up. I could practically see your brain start to overheat.”
“我就知道这会让你激动起来。我几乎能看到你的大脑开始过热。”

“Piss off.” Remus kicked his shin. “I’m just asking .”
“别烦我。”雷木斯踢了踢他的胫骨。“我只是问一下。”

“Mary loved all that stuff - presents and flowers and cards and shit. I liked doing it for her, because it made her happy. You’d hate it, so I won’t.”
“玛丽喜欢那些东西——礼物、花朵和卡片什么的。我喜欢为她做这些，因为它让她开心。你会讨厌这些，所以我不做了。”

“It’s just so public,” Remus said.
“这就是太公开了，”雷木斯说。

“I know. Don’t worry about it.”
“我知道。别担心。”

“Ok.”
“好。”

“...”
“...”

“Remus.”
“雷木斯。”

“What?”
“什么？”

“Stop worrying!”
“别担心了！”

“Fine, fine, I believe you!”
“好吧，好吧，我相信你！”

“Anyway, it’s not even a real thing.” Sirius said, thoughtfully. “Valentine’s day. I looked it up.”
“反正这根本不是什么真实的事。”天狼星沉思地说。“情人节。我查过了。”

“It’s real to muggles, isn’t it?” Remus frowned. He couldn’t say he’d given it much thought.
“对麻瓜来说是真的，对吧？”雷木斯皱眉道。他不能说自己考虑过这个问题。

“There was a bloke called Valentine, but there’s nothing especially romantic about it. But I did find out some other stuff, about the Romans.”
“有个叫瓦伦丁的家伙，但这并没有什么特别浪漫的东西。不过我确实发现了一些其他的东西，关于罗马人的。”

“Why can’t you apply this thirst for knowledge to your actual schoolwork?!”
“你为什么不能把这渴望知识的精神用到你的学业上？！”

“Ugh, don’t be so boring. Anyway, have you heard of the Lupercalia?”
“唉，别这么无聊。反正，你听说过卢佩卡利亚节吗？”

Remus felt a sinking feeling in his stomach and let go of Sirius’s hand.
雷木斯感到胃里一阵沉重的感觉，放开了天狼星的手。

“I don’t want to talk about wolf stuff right now.”
“我现在不想谈论狼人相关的事。”

“You have heard of it!” Sirius sounded pleased.
“你听说过！”天狼星听起来很高兴。

“No. I just know the latin for wolf because it’s my bloody name.”
“没有。我只知道‘狼’的拉丁语，因为这就是我该死的名字。”

“Oh right… It’s not what you think, it’s a festival!”
“哦，对… 这不是你想的那样，这是一个节日！”

“Ok.”
“好。”

“And it’s really cool, there are blood sacrifices, and running around naked, and--”
“而且真的很酷，有血祭，还有裸体跑来跑去，还有——”

“I’m going to sleep.”
“我要去睡觉了。”

“But you like history.”
“但你喜欢历史。”

“Shut up, Padfoot, he wants to go to sleep.” James shouted from across the room. “And so do I!”
“闭嘴，帕德弗特，他想去睡觉。”詹姆斯从房间那边喊道。“我也是！”

“Yeah!” Peter echoed.
“是的！”彼得附和道。

“Mind your own business.” Sirius shouted back.
“管好你自己的事。”天狼星回喊道。

“Sonoro Quiesces.” Remus muttered, creating a dry bubble of silence inside the bed. He still whispered when he spoke, though, because it was weird to talk an normal volume in the dark. “I said I didn’t want to talk about wolf stuff, god.”
“安静的魔音。”雷木斯低声咕哝，创造了一个干燥的安静泡泡在床上。不过他说话时仍然是低声的，因为在黑暗中用正常音量说话很奇怪。“我说了我不想谈论狼人相关的事，上帝。”

“I was only trying to make you feel better about Valentine’s Day.”
“我只是想让你对情人节感觉好一点。”

“I didn’t feel badly about it in the first place!”
“我本来就没觉得它不好！”

“Ok, sorry, I misread you.” Sirius was whispering too, but loudly, obviously annoyed. “You were all quiet about it and I wanted to cheer you up. I thought you were jealous of Lily and James.”
“好吧，对不起，我误解了你。”天狼星也在低声说话，但声音很大，显然有些烦恼。“你对这事儿都很安静，我想让你高兴一点。我以为你是嫉妒莉莉和詹姆斯。”

“Jealous?!”
“嫉妒？！”

“That’s the wrong word. You were just… I saw you watching them, kissing and stuff, and being all mushy. And I know you hate public displays of affection, but I dunno. It’s not like we have a choice either way...”
“那不是正确的词。你只是… 我看到你看着他们，接吻什么的，变得很黏腻。我知道你讨厌公开的亲密表现，但我不知道。无论如何，我们也没有选择…”

Remus blinked in the dark, rolling back over to see Sirius’s face.
雷木斯在黑暗中眨了眨眼，翻身回去看天狼星的脸。

“It bothers you, doesn’t it?” It had to, because it had never bothered Remus before. Suddenly he realized what it had all been about.
“这让你烦恼，对吧？”它一定让你烦恼，因为雷木斯以前从未为此烦恼。突然他意识到这到底是什么回事。

“A bit, maybe.” Sirius replied, honestly. Remus fumbled under the duvet for his hand again.
“也许有一点。”天狼星诚实地回答。雷木斯再次在被子下摸索他的手。

Tuesday 14th February 1978
1978年2月14日，星期二

The next morning, James and Sirius were nowhere to be found - Remus presumed they had left early for quidditch practice; it was a bright, sunny day, despite a chill in the air. After a few minutes of deep thought, Remus rifled in his bedside drawer for his very last chocolate frog and bunged it in his pocket before heading downstairs.
第二天早上，詹姆斯和天狼星都不见了——雷木斯猜他们早早地去参加魁地奇训练了；尽管空气中有些凉意，但阳光明媚。经过几分钟的深思，雷木斯在床头柜抽屉里翻找他的最后一只巧克力青蛙，把它塞进口袋，然后下楼。

The rest of the Gryffindors awoke to find that in the night the house elves had decorated their common room with garlands of red and pink paper hearts - something which seemed to divide all of the students.
其余的格兰芬多醒来发现，夜里家养小精灵们用红色和粉色的纸心装饰了他们的公共休息室——这似乎让所有的学生产生了分歧。

“It’s hardly appropriate in a school.” Christopher grumbled, meeting Remus and Mary on their way out of the portrait hole.
“在学校里这不太合适。”克里斯托弗抱怨道，遇到雷木斯和玛丽正要离开画框洞口。

“Aww, I think it’s lovely.” Mary sighed, cheerily. She was subtly dressed for the occasion, wearing a red ribbon in her hair, and red enamel studs in each earlobe. Christopher shook his head, grimly at her.
“哦，我觉得这很可爱。”玛丽愉快地叹了口气。她为这个场合稍微打扮了一下，头发上绑着红色丝带，每只耳垂上都有红色的珐琅耳钉。克里斯托弗对她摇了摇头，神情严肃。

“If it were a proper holiday, like Christmas, or Easter or something--”
“如果这是一个真正的节日，比如圣诞节，或者复活节什么的——”

“But why do wizards celebrate those things?” Remus cut in, thoughtfully, as they progressed towards the dining hall. Every corridor was also decked out in pink and red crepe paper, and there seemed to be music coming from somewhere, “None of the purebloods I’ve met are Christians, or even know anything about Jesus, or the Easter bunny, or--”
“但巫师为什么要庆祝这些东西呢？”雷木斯插话道，若有所思地走向餐厅。每条走廊也装饰着粉色和红色的纸绸，还有音乐从某处传来，“我遇到的纯血巫师都不是基督徒，甚至不知道耶稣，或复活节兔子，或者——”

“The Easter what?!” Christopher was staring at him as if he was mad.
“复活节什么？！”克里斯托弗盯着他，仿佛他疯了。

“Don’t bother, Remus,” Mary laughed, “Lily and I tried back in first year. We’re not supposed to ask.”
“别费心了，雷木斯，”玛丽笑道，“莉莉和我在第一年时也试过。我们不该问。”

Christopher’s mood did not improve as they entered the Great Hall, which was bathed in a rosey pink glow by a collection of candles floating inside red glass lanterns. Fresh flowers had been placed in vases on every table, and pink envelopes flew back and forth over the heads of the students - valentine’s cards looking for their recipient.
当他们进入宏伟的大厅时，克里斯托弗的情绪没有好转。大厅里被一群漂浮在红色玻璃灯笼中的蜡烛映照成玫瑰粉色的光辉。每张桌子上都放着新鲜的花朵，粉色的信封在学生们的头顶上飞来飞去——情人节卡片在寻找它们的收件人。

“For goodness’ sake.” Christopher muttered, taking his seat and pouring himself a very black coffee.
“看在上帝的份上。”克里斯托弗嘟囔着，坐下并给自己倒了一杯非常黑的咖啡。

“It’s only one day.” Remus said, lifting the teapot, which was also pink.
“这只是一天。”雷木斯说，提起了同样是粉色的茶壶。

No sooner had they sat down, than a pile of pink envelopes fluttered into Mary’s lap, making her squeal with delight. Remus grinned too. He pulled out his own envelopes and whispered an incantation, tossing them into the air so that they mingled with the others flying above them.
他们刚坐下，一堆粉色的信封就飘到了玛丽的腿上，让她兴奋地尖叫。雷木斯也咧嘴笑了。他拿出自己的信封，低声念了个咒语，把它们扔到空中，让它们和其他在空中飞来的信封混在一起。

“Here you go, Chris,” Remus tossed one across the table, “It’s not a valentine, promise.”
“给你，克里斯，”雷木斯把一个扔到桌子那边，“这不是情人节卡，保证。”

“Oh. Er… what is it?” Christopher held the blank envelope warily.
“哦。呃… 这是什么？”克里斯托弗小心翼翼地拿着空白的信封。

“An invitation.” Remus winked. “Give it your name, but don’t share it, ok?”
“一个邀请函。”雷木斯眨眨眼。“写上你的名字，但不要分享，行吗？”

“Er… ok…”
“呃… 好…”

“Good morning!” Lily appeared, looking cheerful as usual, clutching a book on advanced potions. “Anyone seen Potter?”
“早上好！”莉莉出现了，像往常一样愉快，手里捧着一本高级魔药书。“有人看到波特了吗？”

“Quidditch pitch?” Remus raised his head.
“魁地奇场地？”雷木斯抬起头。

“Nope,” Lily shrugged, “I thought so too, but Ravenclaw booked it this morning.”
“没有，”莉莉耸耸肩，“我也这么想，但拉文克劳今天早上预定了。”

“He and Padfoot were gone when I woke up.” Remus said.
“他和帕德弗特早上我醒来时就不在了。”雷木斯说。

“That’s exactly what I was afraid of…” Lily replied, taking her seat.
“这正是我担心的…”莉莉回答道，坐下。

No sooner than she had sugared her porridge, than a loud pop echoed over their heads, and everyone looked up. Those students who hadn’t immediately dived for cover beneath their breakfast tables began ‘oohing’ and ‘ahhing’, as a rather spectacular fireworks display began over their heads. The bursts of colour took the form of gigantic glittering love hearts, and the embers which rained down turned out to be pink and white flowerheads,
莉莉刚刚给她的粥加了糖，就响起了一个响亮的“啪”声，回荡在他们头顶上，所有人都抬头看了过去。那些没有立刻躲到早餐桌下的学生们开始发出“哦”和“啊”的声音，因为一场相当壮观的烟火表演在他们头顶上开始了。彩色的烟火呈现出巨大的闪光心形，落下的余烬原来是粉色和白色的花朵，

“Lilies!” Mary said gleefully, as one settled on her pile of cards.
“百合花！”玛丽高兴地说，一朵落在她的卡片堆上。

“Oh no!” Christopher wailed, “I’m allergic!” He sneezed, before aiming his wand upwards and gasping, “Protego!” to defend himself against the fluttering blooms.
“哦不！”克里斯托弗尖叫道，“我过敏！”他打了个喷嚏，然后指着上面喊道，“护盾咒！”以保护自己免受飞舞的花朵的袭击。

“I don’t believe this…” Lily was blushing harder than Remus had ever seen her. He grinned,
“我不敢相信这…”莉莉的脸红得比雷木斯见过的还要厉害。他咧嘴笑了，

“You were asking for it, I’m afraid.”
“我怕是你自找的。”

“I’d have been happy with a card!” She hissed, as the final fireworks died out, and the last of the lilies sailed to the floor like great pink snowflakes, filling the room with their lovely scent.
“我本来就会对一张卡片感到开心！”她低声说，最后的烟火熄灭时，最后一朵百合花像巨大的粉色雪花一样飘落在地上，房间里充满了它们可爱的香味。

“Oh shut up, Evans,” Mary tutted, “It’s bloody gorgeous of him.”
“闭嘴，埃文斯，”玛丽啐道，“他真是太漂亮了。”

“Cheers, MacDonald,” James appeared at Lily’s shoulder, with Sirius.
“谢谢，麦克唐纳，”詹姆斯在莉莉的肩膀上出现了，身边还有天狼星。

“You utter idiot!” Lily stood up and wound her arms around James’s neck, kissing him. Remus wasn’t watching this display, though; he was watching Sirius, who flicked his wand behind James’s back.
“你真是个愚蠢的家伙！”莉莉站起身，搂住詹姆斯的脖子，亲吻了他。不过雷木斯并没有看这个场景；他在看天狼星，天狼星在詹姆斯背后挥了挥魔杖。

The flowers which had gathered on the table (those which Chris had not tried to clear, anyway) began to move again, and gathered together in front of Lily’s plate. With another soft little pop, the pile had transformed into a large box, emblazoned with even more lilies.
那些在桌子上聚集的花朵（克里斯没有尝试清除的那些）开始再次移动，并在莉莉的盘子前聚集在一起。随着另一声轻微的“啪”声，这些花朵变成了一个大盒子，上面还装饰着更多的百合花。

“What’s that?” Lily turned, leaning over to get a closer look.
“那是什么？”莉莉转过身，俯身去看得更清楚一些。

“Open it and see!” James was grinning ear to ear, clearly utterly chuffed with himself.
“打开看看！”詹姆斯笑得合不拢嘴，显然对自己非常得意。

Christopher sneezed again, and blew his nose, but was roundly ignored as Mary and Remus stood up to get a better look. Lily, still pink and smiling, carefully lifted the lid of the box, and everyone leaned in. On a red velvet pillow, with a bow around its neck, was a tiny little charcoal grey kitten with huge yellow eyes.
克里斯托弗再次打了个喷嚏，擤了擤鼻子，但玛丽和雷木斯站起来看得更清楚时，他被完全忽视了。莉莉，脸色依然红润而微笑，轻轻地揭开了盒子的盖子，所有人都倾身过去。在一个红色天鹅绒的枕头上，系着蝴蝶结的是一只小巧的深灰色小猫，拥有一双巨大的黄色眼睛。

“Ohhh!” Lily gasped, reaching in immediately to pick up the mewing creature and cuddle it close, “Really, Potter?! You got me a cat?! I love him! Or… her?”
“哦哦！”莉莉惊呼道，立刻伸手去抱起那只叫着的小猫，紧紧搂在怀里，“真的，波特？！你给我买了一只猫？！我喜欢它！还是… 她？”

“Him,” James nodded, “I know your old family one died last Christmas, and Hagrid told me a litter was born in the village last week, so…”
“它是男猫，”詹姆斯点点头，“我知道你家里那只猫去年圣诞节死了，海格告诉我上周村子里出生了一窝小猫，所以…”

“Oh he’s so sweet!” Mary reached over to stroke the kitten’s head.
“哦，它真可爱！”玛丽伸手抚摸小猫的头。

“Oh for Merlin’s sake…” Christopher stood up, clutching his handkerchief to his nose. “I’m allergic to cats, too! Bloody stupid day…” with that, he got up and stormed away, further up the table.
“看在梅林的份上…”克里斯托弗站起身，捂着鼻子。“我对猫也过敏！该死的愚蠢的一天…”说完，他起身愤怒地离开了，走向桌子的另一端。

“Such a shame.” Sirius smirked, taking his empty seat. “Morning, Moony.”
“真可惜。”天狼星冷笑着，坐回他的空座位。“早上好，月亮。”

“Morning, Padfoot.” Remus smiled.
“早上好，帕德弗特。”雷木斯笑了。

The rest of breakfast was spent cooing over Lily’s new kitten, and trying to choose a name. Remus kept a polite distance; just in case. He’d had bad experiences with cats in the past, and didn’t fancy any new scratches today, no matter how tiny its claws were.
早餐的剩余时间都用来对莉莉的新猫发出咯咯的声音，试图给它起个名字。雷木斯保持了一定的距离；以防万一。他过去与猫有过不愉快的经历，不愿意今天再被划伤，不管它的爪子有多小。

Soon, everyone was getting up to go to their various lessons (while arguing over who ought to look after the kitten that morning), and Sirius fell into step with Remus,
很快，大家都开始起身去上各自的课（同时争论谁应该照看小猫），天狼星和雷木斯并肩走着，

“Walk you to history?” He offered,
“我陪你去历史课？”他提议道，

“Oh, I don’t need to go,” Remus replied, slyly, “It’s a drop-in lesson, for NEWTs.”
“哦，我不需要去，”雷木斯狡黠地回答，“这是个自选课程，为新魔法学位课程的。”

“But you always go to your lessons,” Sirius replied, “Even the optional ones.”
“但你总是去上你的课，”天狼星回答，“即使是自选的课。”

“I know, but you’re always telling me to relax, so…” Remus covertly pulled his little matchbox out of his robe pocket and tapped it. Sirius raised an eyebrow,
“我知道，但你总是告诉我要放松，所以…”雷木斯偷偷从袍子口袋里拿出一个小火柴盒并敲了敲。天狼星扬起一眉，

“As much as I really love stoned Moony - what’s brought on the rebelliousness?”
“虽然我真的很喜欢醉醺醺的月亮——是什么让你变得如此叛逆？”

“Does there have to be a reason?” Remus shrugged. He glanced around quickly to check that no one was listening too intently - but they were all pretty absorbed in their various cards and gifts. He slipped the chocolate frog into Sirius’s pocket. “Happy Valentine’s Day, wanker.”
“非得有个理由吗？”雷木斯耸耸肩。他迅速扫视四周，确认没有人过于专注地听他们谈话——但大家都忙于各种卡片和礼物。他把巧克力蛙塞进了天狼星的口袋里。“情人节快乐，混蛋。”

He had never seen Sirius Black blush like that.
他从未见过天狼星·布莱克脸红成那样。

 

Chapter 135: Seventh Year: The Marauder’s Inter-house Prank Planning Co-operativeWednesday 15th February 1978

“I can’t believe you’re holding this thing here.” Christopher said, agitatedly, as Remus unlocked the Charms classroom.  

“我真不敢相信你把这个东西放在这里。”克里斯托弗激动地说，雷木斯正在解锁魔咒教室。

 

“Best way to avoid detection. Flitwick always lets me use it.” Remus replied.  

“这是最好的避免被发现的办法。弗立维克总是让我使用它。”雷木斯回答道。

 

“Exactly! It’s so brazen!” Christopher chided, as they entered.  

“正是如此！这太厚颜无耻了！”克里斯托弗责备道，当他们进入时。

 

“Brazen is our middle name!” James declared excitedly, following them.  

“厚颜无耻是我们的中间名！”詹姆斯兴奋地宣称，跟在他们后面。

 

“Your middle name is Fleamont, you prat.” Sirius scoffed. “And this place is genius , no one will ever suspect anything. I knew your swot lessons would come in useful one day, Moony.”  

“你的中间名是弗利蒙特，你这个傻瓜。”天狼星嗤笑道。“而且这个地方真是天才之作，没人会怀疑任何事情。我早知道你的死记硬背课程会有用的，月亮。”

 

“A lot of people find Remus’s study group very helpful, actually .” Christopher said primly, folding his arms and leaning against the wall.  

“其实很多人觉得雷木斯的学习小组非常有帮助。”克里斯托弗一本正经地说，双臂交叉，靠在墙上。

 

“Oh Chris, he’s just teasing,” Remus chuckled, setting his book bag down. He glanced at his pocket watch. “We’re all nice and early, James, have you got an agenda?”  

“哦，克里斯，他只是开玩笑的，”雷木斯笑着说，放下了书包。他瞥了一眼他的怀表。“我们都很早到了，詹姆斯，你有安排吗？”

 

“A what?” James turned around from the blackboard, where he was directing the chalk to draw a gigantic lion with ‘ Gryffindor Rulez OK ’ beneath it.  

“什么？”詹姆斯从黑板转过身，他正在用粉笔画一个巨大的狮子，下面写着“格兰芬多万岁”。

 

“Never mind.” Remus sighed.  

“没关系。”雷木斯叹了口气。

 

“So who else got an invitation?” Christopher asked, over the top of his book (which seemed to have materialised from nowhere - Christopher was the only other person Remus knew who could go from 0 to reading in less than three seconds flat).  

“那还有谁收到了邀请函？”克里斯托弗在书的上方问道（书似乎凭空出现了——克里斯托弗是雷木斯唯一知道的，可以在不到三秒的时间内从零到阅读的人）。

 

“About twenty or thirty people, maybe.” Remus said, “Anyone who expressed an interested before Christmas who seemed trustworthy.”  

“可能有二三十个人。”雷木斯说，“任何在圣诞节前表示过兴趣且看起来值得信赖的人。”

 

“It was an extremely rigorous vetting process, actually,” James said, now standing on Flitwick’s desk and trying to touch the ceiling with his fingertips.  

“实际上，这是一个非常严格的审查过程，”詹姆斯说，现在站在弗立维克的桌子上，试图用指尖碰到天花板。

 

“Yeah, we almost didn’t let Wormtail in.” Sirius barked with laughter from the window, where he was leaning half out of it, smoking. Remus dearly wanted to go over there and wrap his arms around Sirius, steal the cigarette (which was probably one of his anyway, the thief) and kiss his neck. But the others would be arriving soon, and it was a completely mental line of thinking, that.  

“是啊，我们差点没让彼得进去。”天狼星从窗户那边大笑道，他半身探出窗外，抽着烟。雷木斯非常想过去拥抱天狼星，偷走那根香烟（可能本来就是他的，那个小偷）并亲吻他的脖子。但其他人很快就会到达，这种思维真是完全疯狂。

 

“Why do you all call Peter that?” Christopher asked.  

“你们为什么都叫彼得那个名字？”克里斯托弗问道。

 

“Just a nickname.” They all said, in unison.  

“只是个昵称。”他们齐声说。

 

Peter arrived shortly after that, followed in by Mary, Lily and Yasmin. Next were the sixth and seventh years from Remus’s study group, and Dorcas - who was still on friendly terms with Peter, apparently. Mary’s latest squeeze, a Ravenclaw boy called Jonty Simmons, who looked like he couldn’t believe his luck. And finally, much to Remus’s distaste, Emmeline Vance sauntered in (two minutes late) with Roman Rotherhide.  

彼得随后不久就到了，接着是玛丽、莉莉和雅斯敏。然后是雷木斯学习小组的六年级和七年级学生，以及多卡斯——显然她与彼得仍然保持友好关系。玛丽最近的新欢，一个叫乔恩提·西蒙斯的拉文克劳男孩，看起来似乎不敢相信自己的运气。最后，令雷木斯不满的是，艾梅琳·范斯（迟到两分钟）与罗曼·罗瑟海德一同走进了房间。

 

The room was pretty crowded after that, and noisy with the buzz of excitement. Most of the group had some idea why they were there, but others were curious, and all of them were fascinated by the marauders.  

之后房间里相当拥挤，兴奋的嗡嗡声也很吵。大多数人知道他们为什么在这里，但其他人则感到好奇，他们都对掠夺者充满了兴趣。

 

Sirius and James adored the attention, of course, and immediately took centre stage.  

天狼星和詹姆斯当然喜欢这种关注，立即成为了中心人物。

 

“Now, we all know why we’re here,” James started, using his quidditch captain voice.  

“现在，我们都知道我们为什么在这里，”詹姆斯开始说道，用他魁地奇队长的声音。

 

Immediately, Emmeline Vance’s arm shot up.  

艾梅琳·范斯立刻举起了手臂。

 

“Sorry, but I don’t…”  

“抱歉，我不…”

 

Remus gave an impatient snort and Christopher, sitting next to him, shot him a strange look.  

雷木斯不耐烦地哼了一声，坐在他旁边的克里斯托弗投来了一道奇怪的目光。

 

“Nor do I!” Dorcas raised her hand too, along with one or two sixth years from Remus’s study group.  

“我也没有！”多卡斯也举起了手，还有一两个雷木斯学习小组的六年级学生。

 

“Why did all of you come, then?!” Sirius asked, eyebrows raised. A group of girls sitting at the back of the room giggled. Remus made a mental note. He’d tried to avoid inviting too many members of the Sirius Black fanclub, but it was pretty unavoidable when that applied to half the school.  

“那你们都来干什么？！”天狼星问道，挑起了眉毛。坐在房间后面的一个女孩们咯咯地笑了。雷木斯在心里记下了这一点。他曾试图避免邀请太多天狼星·布莱克的粉丝，但当这涉及到学校的一半时，很难避免。

 

“We’re here to plan a… an organised protest,” Christopher said, blushing a bit, because he wasn’t used to speaking in front of lots of people. “Against Slytherin.”  

“我们来这里是为了策划一个… 组织性的抗议，”克里斯托弗说道，有点脸红，因为他不习惯在很多人面前讲话。“针对斯莱特林。”

 

“Yeah!” Another sixth year shouted, “I heard you lot were planning your biggest prank yet!”  

“是的！”另一个六年级学生喊道，“我听说你们计划了你们最大的一次恶作剧！”

 

“ I heard one of you knows how to get to the monster out of the chamber of secrets!”  

“我听说你们中的一个知道怎么把怪物从密室里弄出来！”

 

“I heard you were planning to blow up the dungeons!” One Hufflepuff boy squeaked.  

“我听说你们打算炸毁地牢！”一个赫奇帕奇男孩尖叫道。

 

“Woah woah woah,” James held up his hands, “Bit less dramatic than that…”  

“哇哇哇，”詹姆斯举起双手，“比那个稍微少一点戏剧性…”

 

“Well, if it’s about getting the Slytherins back for all the nonsense they’ve pulled, I’m in.” Emmeline

 

 said, decisively, tossing her luxuriant blonde curls. Remus tutted, loudly, and Chris shot him another look.  

“好吧，如果是为了报复斯莱特林搞的一切荒唐事，我愿意参加。”艾梅琳决定性地说，甩了甩她那丰盈的金发。雷木斯发出 loud 的声音，克里斯托弗又给了他一个看。

 

“That’s exactly what it’s about. And exactly why we need all of you to keep quiet about it.” James said, getting into his flow, now. “This is our last year, and we’re inviting all of you to help us plan our final prank.”  

“这正是我们所要做的。这也是我们需要你们所有人保持沉默的原因。”詹姆斯现在进入了状态。“这是我们最后一年，我们邀请你们所有人来帮助我们计划最后的恶作剧。”

 

“Does that make us marauders?” The Hufflepuff boy squeaked again. There was an excited murmur.  

“那这是否意味着我们成了掠夺者？”赫奇帕奇的男孩再次尖叫道。大家激动地低声议论起来。

 

“ No .” Peter said, indignantly, though no one really paid him any attention.  

“没有。”彼得愤慨地说道，不过没有人真的注意到他。

 

“I like to think of it as more of a collaboration.” James said, thoughtfully.  

“我更愿意把它看作是一种合作。”詹姆斯若有所思地说。

 

“An inter-house co-operative!” Sirius added.  

“跨学院合作！”天狼星补充道。

 

Everyone seemed pretty pleased with that. At least, it sounded impressive, and official enough.  

大家似乎对此感到非常满意。至少，这听起来很令人印象深刻，而且足够正式。

 

“Right.” James clapped his hands together and rubbed them, smiling round at everyone. “Now that’s out of the way, who’s got some ideas?!”  

“好。”詹姆斯拍了拍手，搓了搓手，笑着看着每个人。“既然这件事已经解决了，谁有一些主意？！ ”  

 

Twenty hands shot up.  

二十只手齐刷刷地举了起来。

 

“Err,” Lily spoke up, “I think before we get into that it might be good to have some ground rules?”  

“呃，”莉莉开口说，“我觉得在我们开始之前，制定一些基本规则可能会更好？”

 

“Like what?” Sirius folded his arms, grumpily.  

“像什么？”天狼星不高兴地抱着手臂。

 

“Like not actually hurting anyone? This is just fun, ok? Not revenge for everything Slytherin’s ever done.” She was using her Head Girl voice, now, and a few people lowered their hands.  

“比如说不伤害任何人？这只是好玩的，明白吗？不是为了报复斯莱特林所做的一切。”她现在用的是她的女生主席声音，一些人低下了手。

 

“Fair enough,” James said, holding up his hands amicably, coming between Sirius and Lily. “No physical harm intended. And as I said before, no talking about it outside of this room. On pain of death. Joking , Evans!” He ducked as she went to slap the back of his head.  

“公平，”詹姆斯说，友好地举起双手，站在天狼星和莉莉之间。“不打算造成身体伤害。正如我之前所说的，不要在这个房间之外谈论此事。否则后果自负。开玩笑的，埃文斯！”他躲开了她去拍他脑袋的手。

 

After these initial teething problems, everyone seemed to enter into the spirit of the thing. Lots of people had ideas - from the extreme (Lily vetoed summoning a banshee to haunt the dungeons), to the subtle (Emmeline knew of a spell which would transfigure everyone’s right shoe into a left shoe - she said she’d done it to her sister over the summer and it had taken her three days to realise what had been bothering her).  

经过这些初步的问题后，大家似乎都融入了这个氛围。许多人有主意——从极端的（莉莉否决了召唤女妖来困扰地牢）到微妙的（艾梅琳知道一个咒语可以把每个人的右脚鞋子变成左脚鞋子——她说她在暑假时对她的妹妹做过这个，她花了三天才意识到是什么困扰了她）。

 

Eventually, time ran short, so James set everyone ‘homework’ - requiring them to come back next week with an idea.  

最终，时间不够了，所以詹姆斯给大家布置了“作业”——要求他们下周带着主意回来。

 

“Then we can decide on the best one.” Sirius declared.  

“然后我们可以决定最好的方案。”天狼星宣布道。

 

“Who decides?” Mary narrowed her eyes.  

“谁来决定？”玛丽眯起了眼睛。

 

“Me, James, Pete and Moony, obviously.” Sirius raised his chin.  

“我，詹姆斯，彼得和月亮，显然。”天狼星昂起下巴。

 

“Can’t we vote?” One of the sixth years asked.  

“我们不能投票吗？”一个六年级学生问道。

 

“Yeah, that seems fairer.” Mary nodded. “If we’re all putting ourselves at risk of expulsion for you.”  

“是的，这样更公平。”玛丽点头道。“如果我们都要冒着被开除的风险的话。”

 

“Expulsion?!” Christopher bit his lip, “Surely not… surely we won’t go that far…?”  

“开除？！”克里斯托弗咬着嘴唇，“肯定不会……我们不会走到那一步吧……？”

 

“ Will we get in trouble, though?” The hufflepuff boy raised his hand again. Everyone looked at him.  

“那我们会不会惹上麻烦？”赫奇帕奇的男孩再次举起手。大家都看着他。

 

“Not much.” Sirius shrugged. “Bit of detention never hurt anyone.”  

“不多。”天狼星耸耸肩。“一点留校察看从来不会伤害任何人。”

 

“No, sorry, I don’t mean detention.” The boy shook his head, nervously. “I mean with… you know the Slytherins. They won’t… tell the death eaters to get us, will they?”  

“不，对不起，我不是说留校察看。”那男孩紧张地摇头。“我是说……你知道斯莱特林。他们不会……告诉食死徒来抓我们吧？”

 

Sirius looked about to laugh, when he realised that the atmosphere in the room had changed. A few people looked very awkward, some of them were whispering amongst themselves. Remus could even smell a whiff of real fear creeping into the room; everybody seemed to have tensed up a bit.  

天狼星本来想笑，但他意识到房间里的气氛发生了变化。一些人看起来很尴尬，有些人在低声耳语。雷木斯甚至闻到了一丝真正的恐惧弥漫在房间里；每个人似乎都紧张了一些。

 

Of course, Sirius and James did not worry about that sort of thing. This was all part of the crusade of chaos they’d been on since they were eleven. Even Remus had been pretty flippant about the magnitude of the prank. But he saw now that it meant a lot more to those gathered in the room. James, Sirius and Peter were the only purebloods in attendance. Unless you counted Christopher, who had his own axe to grind with the Slytherins.  

当然，天狼星和詹姆斯并不担心这种事。这一切都是他们从十一岁开始的混乱 crusade 的一部分。即使雷木斯对恶作剧的规模也相当轻率。但他现在明白这对房间里的人意义重大。詹姆斯、天狼星和彼得是唯一出席的纯血巫师。除非你算上克里斯托弗，他对斯莱特林也有自己的怨气。

 

James stood up again, pushing off Flitwick’s desk and drawing himself to full height.  

詹姆斯再次站起身，推开弗立维克的桌子，挺直了身体。

 

“Absolutely not. No one in this room is getting hurt because of this prank.”  

“绝对不行。这个恶作剧不会让房间里的人受到伤害。”

A few people relaxed - after all, James Potter, heir to the Sleek-ezy fortune, head boy, quidditch captain and leading mischief maker was somebody that most people trusted. Remus believed him whole-heartedly - even if the issue had not been raised, it would have been a point of honour for James to protect anyone smaller than him. Lily was beaming at him too, and Sirius looked very pleased, as if that had settled everything.
几个人放松了——毕竟詹姆斯·波特，Sleek-ezy 财富的继承人，学生会主席，魁地奇队长和首席捣蛋鬼，是大多数人信任的人。雷木斯全心全意地相信他——即使问题没有被提出来，这也是詹姆斯保护比他小的人的一种荣誉。莉莉也在微笑着看着他，天狼星看起来很满意，仿佛一切都解决了。

“Right,” Lily clapped her hands together now, taking the floor again, “See you all again next week, I suppose. I think we’d all better leave in small groups, don’t want to draw attention to ourselves…”
“好，”莉莉现在拍了拍手，重新站到大家面前，“我想我们下周再见。我觉得我们最好分小组离开，不想引起别人的注意……”

With that, the room slowly returned to normal, groups of students now chattering excitedly about ideas they’d had, or curses they’d like to try out. Lily assumed her Head Girl voice and started directing people out of the room in groups of three or four, at short intervals. The marauders turned inwards, to confer.
随即，房间慢慢恢复了正常，学生们开始兴奋地讨论他们想到的主意，或者他们想尝试的咒语。莉莉以学生会主席的口吻，开始将人们分成三到四人的小组，有间隔地引导他们离开房间。掠夺者们转向内部，开始商讨。

“Bloody hell.” James muttered, so that he wouldn’t be overheard, “That was intense.”
“真是的。”詹姆斯咕哝道，避免被听到，“真是紧张。”

“What did you expect?” Mary tutted, hoisting herself up onto the desk and swinging her legs. “This isn’t a game to everyone - some people are out for revenge.”
“你期望什么？”玛丽发出声响，坐到桌子上摆弄着腿。“这对每个人来说都不是游戏——有些人是为了报复。”

“Then that’s what we’ll give them.” Sirius said, fiercely. He had that brightness in his eyes that told Remus he would be utterly unbearable for the next few hours. A plan was afoot, and nothing could bring Sirius down from that kind of excitement.
“那我们就给他们这个。”天狼星坚定地说。他眼中的光芒让雷木斯知道，他在接下来的几个小时里会变得非常难以忍受。一个计划正在进行中，没有什么能让天狼星从这种兴奋中退缩。

“Calm down, Black,” Mary teased, “You’re schoolkids, not generals.”
“冷静点，布莱克，”玛丽调侃道，“你们是学生，不是将军。”

“For now.” He replied, darkly.
“暂时是这样。”他阴沉地回答。

“Ok you lot,” Lily turned back into the room. It was only the seven of them left. “We’ll go back in two groups, because no one is going to believe you four weren’t up to something…”
“好了，你们这些人，”莉莉转回房间。只剩下他们七个人了。“我们分成两组回去，因为没有人会相信你们四个没有搞什么鬼……”

Mary, James, Lily and Peter left first, with instructions for Remus, Sirius and Christopher to give them a ten minute head start. Remus was a bit reluctant about this, but there was no way to bring it up. He couldn’t help remembering what had happened the last time he and Christopher were alone in that classroom with Sirius. Though, of course, Christopher hadn’t known Sirius was there at the time, and nor would Remus ever tell him.
玛丽、詹姆斯、莉莉和彼得首先离开，指示雷木斯、天狼星和克里斯托弗给他们十分钟的领先时间。雷木斯对此有些不情愿，但没法提出。他忍不住回忆起上次他和克里斯托弗在教室里和天狼星独处时发生的事。当然，克里斯托弗当时并不知道天狼星在场，雷木斯也不会告诉他。

They tidied up the desks, cleared the chalkboard of James’s lion, then stood about awkwardly for a little bit.
他们整理了桌子，擦掉了黑板上的詹姆斯的狮子，然后尴尬地站了一会儿。

“Let’s play truth or dare.” Sirius grinned.
“我们来玩真心话大冒险吧。”天狼星咧嘴一笑。

“Why?” Remus sighed, leaning on the desk. Here we go...
“为什么？”雷木斯叹了口气，靠在桌子上。开始了……

“Pass the time.”
“打发时间。”

“Or we could just have a normal conversation…”
“或者我们可以聊聊……”

“Christopher wants to, don’t you, Christopher?”
“克里斯托弗想玩，不是吗，克里斯托弗？”

“Err…”
“呃……”

“Great, you can go first. Truth or dare, what do you fancy?”
“很好，你可以先来。真心话还是大冒险，你想要哪个？”

“Um.” Chris’s eyes flicked between Remus and Sirius nervously. “I don’t… um… truth?”
“嗯。”克里斯的眼睛在雷木斯和天狼星之间紧张地闪烁。“我不……嗯……真心话？”

“Excellent! Start off easy, if it’s your first time playing,” Sirius nodded encouragingly. “Hmmm, let me see… ah! Ok, why did you want to get involved with the prank?”
“太棒了！如果这是你第一次玩，最好从简单的开始，”天狼星鼓励地点头。“嗯，让我看看……啊！好的，你为什么想参与这个恶作剧？”

“What?”
“什么？”

“Y’know. How come you came today?”
“你知道的。你怎么会来呢？”

“Chris has been involved since the beginning, Padfoot, you know that.” Remus tutted.
“克里斯从一开始就参与了，天狼星，你知道的。”雷木斯发出声响。

“Right, right - so what made you get involved in the first place, then?”
“对，对——那是什么让你最初参与的呢？”

“If you have to know.” Christopher said, rather icily, “It was your brother.”
“如果你非要知道的话。”克里斯托弗有些冷淡地说，“是你哥哥。”

Sirius, to his credit, did not flinch.
天狼星值得称赞的是，他没有退缩。

“Fair enough, he’s a right little prick.” He nodded. He licked his lips, and glanced at Remus, then back at Chris. “Sure there was no other reason?”
“说得对，他确实是个小混蛋。”他点了点头。他舔了舔嘴唇，瞥了雷木斯一眼，然后又看向克里斯。“确定没有其他原因？”

“No.”
“没有。”

“I’ll go next,” Remus said, quickly. “Chris, you can ask me to do a dare.” He never picked ‘truth’, it was far too dangerous.
“那我来，”雷木斯迅速地说。“克里斯，你可以让我要做一个大冒险。”他从不选择“真心话”，这太危险了。

“Umm…” Christopher bit his lip, still a bit thrown by this whole thing. “Oh, I don’t know, I’m crap at this sort of thing.”
“嗯……”克里斯托弗咬着嘴唇，仍然有些被这整个事情弄得措手不及。“哦，我不知道，我这方面很糟糕。”

“I’ve got a good one!” Sirius said at once. He winked at Remus, then leaned over and whispered in Chris’s ear. Christopher’s eyes widened and he laughed, covering his mouth.
“我有一个好主意！”天狼星立刻说。他对雷木斯眨了眨眼，然后靠过来在克里斯托弗耳边低声耳语。克里斯托弗的眼睛瞪大了，笑了起来，捂住了嘴巴。

“Ok, Remus,” Chris was still blushing, but he was having fun now. “Ok, you have to write something rude on the blackboard and leave it there.”
“好的，雷木斯，”克里斯托弗仍在脸红，但现在他很开心。“好吧，你得在黑板上写些粗鲁的东西，然后把它留在那里。”

“I gave you specifics.” Sirius complained.
“我给了你具体要求。”天狼星抱怨道。

“I’m not saying that out loud!” Christopher laughed, turning even redder. Remus could easily guess the tone of Sirius’s suggestion. He raised an eyebrow wryly, as if under duress,
“我不想大声说出来！”克里斯托弗笑着，脸红得更厉害了。雷木斯可以轻松猜到天狼星建议的语气。他挑了挑眉，仿佛受到了压力，

“Ok, fine, I’ll do it…”
“好吧，算了，我来做……”

He went up to the board and picked up some chalk. He considered it for a moment, “How rude?” He asked the other two, casually.
他走到黑板前，拿起一些粉笔。他考虑了一下，“多粗鲁？”他随意地问另外两个人。

“Very.” Christopher said, smirking shyly.
“非常。”克里斯托弗脸红地说道，带着狡黠的笑容。

“Well, it’s the rules of the game, I s’pose…” Remus began to draw, enjoying the snickering over his shoulder as he deftly traced out the first rude thing that popped into his head.
“嗯，规则就是这样，我想……”雷木斯开始画画，享受着肩膀上的窃笑，因为他灵巧地勾勒出第一个出现在脑海中的粗鲁词汇。

He stepped back, an artist admiring his work. The other two boys stood either side of him, grinning madly. “Well?” He asked.
他退后一步，像艺术家一样欣赏自己的作品。其他两个男孩站在他身旁，狂笑着。“怎么样？”他问道。

Sirius slapped him on the back,
天狼星拍了拍他的背，

“Moony, me old pal, it’s the biggest knob I’ve ever seen.”
“月亮，我的老朋友，这是我见过最大的那玩意儿。”

“Well, that’s a relief.” Remus smirked, forgetting Christopher was there. He didn’t seem to notice - or else just assumed that it was marauder humour (which it sort of was).
“嗯，那就放心了。”雷木斯笑道，忘记了克里斯托弗还在场。他似乎没注意到——或者只是认为这是掠夺者的幽默（虽然确实是）。

“Glorious.” The younger boy nodded, still very pink about the cheeks.
“太棒了。”年轻的克里斯托弗点了点头，脸颊仍然非常红。

“Come on then,” Remus set down the chalk, “That’s enough of a gap, we can go now. Common room?”
“那么，走吧，”雷木斯放下粉笔，“已经留了足够的时间，我们可以走了。回公共休息室？”

“Oi, I’ve not had my turn, yet!” Sirius folded his arms.
“喂，我还没轮到我呢！”天狼星抱起了胳膊。

“What’s the point,” Remus shook his head, “You always choose a dare, and there’s nothing I can think of that you’d even think twice about doing.”
“有什么意义，”雷木斯摇了摇头，“你总是选择大冒险，我想不出你会考虑的事情。”

“Are you saying I’m the bravest --”
“你是在说我最勇敢——”

“Stupidest, maybe,” Remus teased, elbowing him in the ribs. “Come on, let’s go.”
“也许是最愚蠢的，”雷木斯调侃道，用肘部碰了碰他。“走吧，我们走吧。”

They left the classroom and set off through the quiet hallways back to Gryffindor tower. It was fairly late in the evening now, and curfew was only a couple of hours off, so they were alone most of the way, other than the portraits, who were enjoying the peace and quiet.
他们离开了教室，沿着安静的走廊前往格兰芬多塔楼。现在已经是傍晚了，禁足时间只有几个小时，所以他们大部分时间都独自一人，除了挂在墙上的画像们，他们正享受着宁静。

“Did you finish Maurice, Remus?” Chris asked. Always back to books.
“你读完《莫里斯》了吗，雷木斯？”克里斯托弗问道。总是回到书本上。

“Nearly,” Remus replied. “Just a chapter or two to go. Do you promise me it’s a happy ending?”
“差不多了，”雷木斯回答。“就剩一两章了。你能保证这是个快乐的结局吗？”

“Definitely,” Chris nodded. “You’ll love it. I was thinking… if you’re free on Saturday we could have a chat about it in the Three Broomsticks? I’d really like to know what you think.”
“当然了，”克里斯托弗点了点头。“你会喜欢的。我在想……如果你周六有空，我们可以在三把扫帚酒吧聊聊吗？我很想知道你怎么想。”

“Yeah, maybe…” Remus was torn between his desire not to disappoint Christopher (which he always seemed to be doing) and his keen awareness of Sirius’s very mercurial mood. “Don’t see why not.”
“嗯，也许……”雷木斯在不想让克里斯托弗失望（他总是觉得自己在做这个）和对天狼星非常善变的情绪的敏锐感知之间挣扎。“没理由不行。”

“Is that the muggle book you’ve been reading?” Sirius asked, “Is it good then?”
“那是你一直在读的麻瓜书吗？”天狼星问道，“那么好吗？”

“Yeah, quite good.” Remus nodded, cautiously.
“是的，相当不错。”雷木斯小心翼翼地点头。

“Great. Maybe I’ll read it then. I can get it done by Saturday, I read faster than you.”
“太好了。也许我会读这本书。我可以在周六之前读完，我读得比你快。”

“You do not!” Remus scowled, scandalised.
“你才没有呢！”雷木斯皱起眉头，愤愤不平。

“Well I have more time to read, anyway.”
“嗯，我有更多时间阅读。”

“Only because you hardly go to half your lessons.” Remus shot back.
“只因为你几乎不上半数的课。”雷木斯回击道。

“I doubt it’s your sort of thing, Sirius.” Christopher spoke up. They both looked at him. He shrugged, “Well, it’s not! Tell him what it’s about, Remus.”
“我怀疑这是不是你喜欢的书，天狼星。”克里斯托弗说道。他们俩都看向他。他耸了耸肩，“好吧，确实不是！雷木斯，告诉他这本书讲的是什么。”

“Er…”
“呃……”

But it was too late, Sirius was already rummaging in the book bag at Remus’s hip as they walked, and at once withdrew the text. Remus fought the urge to snatch it back, only because he’d underlined some parts of it, just because he’d liked them so much, and he was embarrassed about it now.
但为时已晚，天狼星已经在雷木斯的书包里翻找，并立刻抽出了那本书。雷木斯拼命克制住抢回书的冲动，只是因为他在书中划了几处，只是因为他非常喜欢这些地方，现在对此感到尴尬。

(I think you’re beautiful, the only beautiful person I’ve ever seen. I love your voice and everything to do with you, down to your clothes or the room you are sitting in. I adore you.)
（我觉得你很美丽，是我见过的唯一美丽的人。我爱你的声音和与你有关的一切，甚至是你的衣服或你坐着的房间。我崇拜你。）

Fortunately, Sirius didn’t flip through the pages, only looked at the back cover, frowning slightly.
幸运的是，天狼星没有翻动书页，只是看了看封底，微微皱起了眉头。

“Isn’t this one of my uncle’s?” He asked.
“这不是我叔叔的一本书吗？”他问道。

“Yeah, you said I could borrow it…” Remus rubbed the back of his head.
“是的，你说我可以借的……”雷木斯摸了摸头后。

“Is it dirty?”
“这本书有色情内容吗？”

“No.”
“没有。”

“Oh well. I’ll read it anyway.” Sirius poked out his tongue. “That can be my dare.”
“哦，好吧。我还是读读吧。”天狼星伸出舌头。“这可以成为我的大冒险。”

“Very brave.” Remus grabbed back the book and shoved it in his bag.
“非常勇敢。”雷木斯抢回书本，把它塞进了包里。

“But it’s about…” Christopher frowned. They were almost at the portrait hole now, and Sirius stopped, making all three of them stop too. Sirius looked at Remus, raising an eyebrow, he nodded to Chris.
“但这本书讲的是……”克里斯托弗皱起眉头。他们快到画像洞口了，天狼星停了下来，使得三人都停了下来。天狼星看着雷木斯，挑了挑眉，向克里斯托弗点了点头。

“He makes a lot of assumptions, this one.”
“这个人做了很多假设。”

Remus was surprised to find that his own cheeks were heating up, too. He shrugged,
雷木斯惊讶地发现自己的脸颊也在发热。他耸了耸肩，

“He doesn’t know you very well.”
“他对你了解不多。”

“Oi, Christopher?” Sirius shot him a very wicked look. “Dare me to snog Moony?”
“喂，克里斯托弗？”天狼星向他投以了一个非常邪恶的目光。“大冒险我亲吻月亮怎么样？”

“Wha-- I--?!” Christopher looked stricken, as if he knew there was a笑话 somewhere, but he couldn’t figure out the punchline.
“什么——我——？！”克里斯托弗看上去非常震惊，仿佛知道这里面有个笑话，但他无法找到笑点。

Sirius wasted no time. He took Remus’s head, roughly, and pulled him in for a kiss. Remus gave in. It was a bit mean, but he could hardly refuse. If it was a test of loyalty, or simply something Sirius thought would be funny, he had to go along with it.
天狼星没有浪费时间。他粗暴地抓住雷木斯的头，将他拉近，亲吻了他。雷木斯屈服了。这有点刻薄，但他几乎无法拒绝。如果这是对忠诚的考验，或者只是天狼星认为有趣的事，他必须配合。

“Oh for Merlin’s sake!” A voice came from further up the corridor, causing Sirius and Remus to spring apart. “I’m away for a week and the castle turns into an orgy!”
“真是的，梅林的圣名！”一个声音从走廊深处传来，导致天狼星和雷木斯分开。“我离开一周，城堡就变成了一个纵欲的场所！”

All three boys spun around to see Marlene standing there in her travelling cloak, duffle bag at her side. She gave them a knowing smirk, “What a load of queers.”
三个人转过身，看到玛琳站在那儿，穿着旅行斗篷，旁边放着一个大包。她露出会意的微笑，“真是一群同性恋者。”

Chapter 136: Seventh Year: Mind GamesEveryone was thrilled to see Marlene, of course. Sirius ushered her through the fat lady portrait as fast as he could, and practically trumpeted her arrival to the whole common room, as though he had conjured her from thin air.
当然，大家都很高兴看到玛琳。天狼星尽快把她带过胖夫人画像，几乎是向整个公共休息室宣布她的到来，就好像他从空气中召唤了她一样。

Lily and James rushed over, hugging her and taking her bag, and cloak and leading her to the couch by the fireplace, where Mary hugged her so fiercely Marlene almost squeaked.
莉莉和詹姆斯急忙跑过来，拥抱她，拿过她的包和斗篷，带她到壁炉旁的沙发上，玛丽抱得如此紧，玛琳差点尖叫出声。

“We’ve missed you!” Mary exclaimed, finally letting her friend go.
“我们好想你！”玛丽惊呼道，终于放开了她的朋友。

“I can see that!” Marlene gasped, pink cheeked. “Have you all been that bored without me?”
“我能看出来！”玛琳喘息着，脸颊泛红。“你们没有我真的那么无聊吗？”

Remus hung back a little. He and Marlene didn’t hug much, anyway, so he didn’t think it would be noticed. He watched her warily, and chose to sit in the armchair furthest away from her, trying not to draw attention to himself. Christopher had slipped away too, at some point, maybe up to his dorm room. In the back of his mind, Remus hoped Chris wasn’t angry with him, but he filed that away for another time. He had too much to worry about with Marlene’s return.
雷木斯稍微退后了一点。他和玛琳不太拥抱，所以他觉得不会被注意到。他警惕地看着她，选择坐在离她最远的扶手椅上，尽量不引起注意。克里斯托弗也在某个时候悄悄离开了，也许是上他的宿舍。在他心底，雷木斯希望克里斯没有生他的气，但他把这个问题留到以后再处理。他现在有太多关于玛琳回来的事情需要担心。

“How’s Danny?” Mary was asking now, lowering her voice.
“丹尼怎么样了？”玛丽现在问道，声音压得很低。

“He’s… recovering.” Marlene nodded, her eyes serious. “He’s at home now, mum’s driving him crazy as usual. He won’t… he won’t be going back to the Cannons.” She swallowed and looked down at her hands.
“他在……康复中。”玛琳点头，她的眼神很严肃。“他现在在家里，妈妈像往常一样把他搞疯了。他不会……不会再回到加农队了。”她吞了吞口水，低头看着自己的手。

“It’s a bloody disgrace.” James banged his fist on the arm of the couch, “If I was their manager, I’d--”
“这真是个可耻的事。”詹姆斯重重地拍了一下沙发的扶手，“如果我是他们的经理，我会——”

“He’s too badly injured, anyway.” Marlene shook her head, wiping quickly under her eyes, “He’d have been off for the rest of the season either way; it’ll be months before he’s back on a broom. So. Just as well.”
“反正他的伤也很严重。”玛琳摇摇头，迅速擦拭了眼下，“不管怎么说，他都会休息整个赛季；要等几个月才能再次骑上扫帚。所以。也好。”

“Still bollocks.” James muttered.
“还是很糟糕。”詹姆斯喃喃道。

“Yeah, well.” Marlene looked up, stonily. “Can hardly blame them. I know I would have… anyway. Not worth thinking about.”
“嗯，好吧。”玛琳抬起头，面无表情。“很难怪他们。我知道我会……反正。不值得再想了。”

Remus felt sick with tension. Everyone else sitting in the group knew what he was - everyone except Marlene. 即将到来的满月前的那个周末，他们从霍格莫德回学校，雷木斯因为他那该死的髋关节不得不再次放慢脚步。天狼星和詹姆斯在前面聊天，而克里斯托弗则落后一步陪着雷木斯。

他们去了三把扫帚，但那是一大群人，克里斯托弗总是太害羞，在那种情况下不太说话。所以他现在抓住了机会。

“我很高兴你喜欢那本书，”他说，双手插在口袋里走着，“结局不错吧？”

“是的，很好。”雷木斯喘着气，揉着他的髋关节试图让它动起来。

“什么？不。”尽管二月的天气很冷，他还是因为用力开始出汗。他擦了擦额头，眯着眼睛往山上看。天狼星和詹姆斯在前面大步走着，一起笑着什么。克里斯托弗跟随着他的视线。他抿紧了嘴唇。

“你和他...？”他找不到合适的词语，而雷木斯知道那是什么感觉，所以他直接回答了。不需要含糊其辞。

“是的。我们是。”

“哦。”克里斯托弗听起来很泄气，好像他还以为这一切都是在开他的玩笑。“那是什么感觉？”

“我不知道。很好。非常好。”

“我希望...”他听起来很伤心，但没有说完这句话。过了很久，雷木斯努力跟上，他轻轻地拍了拍克里斯托弗的肩膀。

“There's someone for everyone, Chris.”
“每个人都有适合的人，克里斯。”

“Maybe.”
“也许吧。”

“Oi Moony! Come on!” Sirius was yelling. They were almost at school now, Sirius had stopped under the stone arch gateway to wait.
“喂，月亮脸！快点！”天狼星在喊。他们快到学校了，天狼星停在石拱门下等他。

“待会见，好吗，雷木斯？”克里斯托弗嘟囔着，匆匆跑开了。雷木斯继续前行，终于到达了校门。他的髋关节现在在尖叫，关节燃烧着，疼痛在腿上来回穿梭。他向天狼星点了点头，作为问候，喘不过气来说话。他用一只手靠在石头上，希望天狼星不介意再等一会儿，让他恢复一下。

“对不起。”他终于喘着气说道。“讨厌那该死的山坡。”

“你还好吗？”天狼星问道，给了他一个奇怪的眼神。“对不起，不是故意把你落在后面的。”

“没事。”雷木斯回答，“你知道我，只是有点不对劲。”他挺直了身子，皱了皱眉，又揉了揉侧面。

“是你的髋关节吗？”天狼星现在双手叉腰，像庞弗雷夫人在糟糕的满月后那样上下打量着他。

“是的，”雷木斯耸了耸肩。“一直有点不对劲。”

“当你说‘有点不对劲’时，你是说你在痛吗？”

“只是有点酸痛。”雷木斯愤愤地说道。

“所以，是疼痛。”天狼星挑起眉毛。雷木斯讨厌那种居高临下的表情。“疼了多久了？”

“哦，我不知道，”雷木斯举起双手，气恼地说道——这有什么意义呢？！“从我十三岁开始。”

“Are you joking?!”
“你在开玩笑吗？！”

“Just off and on.”
“只是时不时地。”

“What does Madam Pomfrey say?”
“庞弗雷夫人怎么说？”

“Oh for god’s sake, I don't whinge to her about this sort of crap!” Remus was aware that his voice was getting louder, a few third years walking past turned and looked at him, before running away giggling.
“哦，天哪，我不会向她抱怨这种垃圾！”雷木斯意识到自己的声音越来越大，几个三年级学生经过时转头看了他一眼，然后笑着跑开了。

“你太荒谬了。”天狼星双臂交叉，甩了甩头发，“她是护士，她应该让你感觉好些。如果我告诉你我疼了五年，你会怎么做？！”

“It’s not the same!”
“这不一样！”

“What are you on about??”
“你在说什么？？”

“ You’re not a fucking werew---” He stopped himself just in time. They both looked around themselves furtively, checking no one was listening in. Remus scolded himself. It had been a very long time since he’d let anyone get the better of his temper.
“你不是他妈的狼人——”他及时住了口。他们都偷偷地四下张望，检查是否有人在偷听。雷木斯责怪自己。已经很久没有让任何人激怒过他了。

Sirius leaned forward, glaring at him.
天狼星向前倾身，瞪着他。

“You don’t deserve to suffer, for fuck’s sake.” He muttered.
“你不该受这种罪，真他妈的。”他嘟囔道。

That hurt. He didn’t know why, but it struck Remus so sharply it knocked the breath out of him, and his eyes pricked. He straightened up, careful to remain expressionless this time. He jutted his chin out at Sirius, meeting his glare.
这句话伤人。他不知道为什么，但这句话狠狠地击中了雷木斯，使他喘不过气来，眼睛刺痛。他挺直身子，这次小心翼翼地保持面无表情。他抬起下巴，迎着天狼星的目光。

“I’m not talking about this any more. Come on, we’ll miss dinner.” And began to stride ahead, biting back against the stabbing in his side.
“我不再谈论这个了。走吧，我们会错过晚餐。”然后开始大步向前走，强忍着侧面的刺痛。

 

Chapter 137: Seventh Year: Remus the Martyr 

I was born with a plastic spoon in my mouth

The north side of my town faced east, and the east was facing south

And now you dare to look me in the eye

Those crocodile tears are what you cry

It's a genuine problem, you won't try

To work it out at all you just pass it by, pass it by

 

Substitute me for him

Substitute my coke for gin

Substitute you for my mum

At least I'll get my washing done.

**Wednesday 22nd February 1978**

 

The stalemate between Remus and Sirius lasted for the rest of the weekend. Sunday was the Gryffindor vs. Ravenclaw quidditch game, so they got away with not speaking much. They both sat together in the stands, cheering when it was appropriate, and booing any time the Ravenclaw’s scored.  

雷木斯和天狼星之间的僵局持续了整个周末。星期天是格兰芬多对拉文克劳的魁地奇比赛，所以他们几乎没有说话。他们都坐在看台上，在适当的时候欢呼，在拉文克劳得分时嘘声四起。

 

“Aaaand that’s another ten points to Gryffindor!” The commentator called out through the megaphone, “An overwhelming sixty points now scored by team captain James Potter, no surprises there - fans are starting to wonder what will become of the mighty lions next year when they don’t have their golden boy to depend on--oof, mind that bludger, Simms! … nicely done! Though I must say, I’d have veered left, but I suppose not everybody is chosen for their dexterity, sometimes it’s just about giving everyone a chance, regardless of ability…”  

“又是十分给格兰芬多！”解说员通过扩音器喊道，“现在队长James Potter已经得了压倒性的六十分，这不奇怪——球迷们开始想知道明年没有他们的金童依靠的强大狮子会怎样——小心那个游走球，Simms！……干得好！不过我得说，我会向左转，但我想不是每个人都因灵活而被选中，有时只是给每个人一个机会，无论能力如何……”

 

“Who let Lockhart do the commentary?” Sirius grumbled. “Stupid prat doesn’t even know anything about quidditch.”  

“谁让洛哈特来解说的？”天狼星抱怨道。“这个蠢货连魁地奇都不懂。”

 

“He told me he was lined up to play for Puddlemere,” Peter said, “And the only reason he never played for Ravenclaw was that his coach said he shouldn’t squander his gift in school games.”  

“他告诉我他被安排为Puddlemere效力，”Peter说，“他从未为拉文克劳效力的唯一原因是他的教练说他不应该在学校比赛中浪费他的天赋。”

 

“You’re so gullible, Pete,” Remus nudged him, “I know more about quidditch than that twat.”  

“你真容易上当，Pete，”雷木斯推了推他，“我比那个傻瓜懂得更多魁地奇。”

 

“Yeah, and Moony knows about as much about quidditch as you know about judging character.” Sirius added, his voice unnecessarily sharp.  

“是啊，月亮脸对魁地奇的了解就像你对判断人品的了解一样。”天狼星补充道，声音过于尖锐。

 

Remus coloured. Fine, if Sirius wanted to be passive aggressive.  

雷木斯脸色变了。好吧，如果天狼星想被动攻击的话。

 

“Well, Padfoot,” he replied, coolly, “If you want to do it so much, go and ask McGonagall. I think you’d be perfect for the job.”  

“好吧，破釜酒吧，”他冷静地回答，“如果你这么想做，那就去找McGonagall。我认为你是这个工作的最佳人选。”

 

“You-what?” Sirius gaped at him. Remus raised an eyebrow,  

“你-什么？”天狼星瞪大眼睛看着他。雷木斯扬起眉毛，

 

“Oh yeah, you’re the only person in this school who chats more shit than Lockhart does.”  

“哦，是的，你是这个学校唯一一个比洛哈特还会胡扯的人。”

 

Mary and Lily burst into giggles, covering their mouth. Sirius scowled.  

Mary和Lily笑得合不拢嘴，捂住了嘴。天狼星皱起了眉头。

 

“Up yours.” He muttered.  

“去你的。”他嘟囔道。

 

The game ended with 280 points to Gryffindor, but Sirius wasn't cheering.  

比赛以格兰芬多280分结束，但天狼星并没有欢呼。

 

Quidditch matches generally took up most of the day, from an early breakfast listening to James’s pep talks, to the inevitable after party in the common room. Sirius stayed up late, so nobody noticed that they didn’t go to bed together.  

魁地奇比赛通常占据大部分时间，从早上早饭时听James的鼓舞讲话，到公共休息室里不可避免的赛后聚会。天狼星熬夜了，所以没有人注意到他们没有一起上床睡觉。

 

By Monday, they were on slightly more civil terms - or at least, neither of them wanted any of their friends to know they’d been fighting. Remus immersed himself in his NEWT revision - if he wasn’t alone in the library, he was extending his group study sessions to run an hour longer than usual, each night. It was the week of the full moon, and he was utterly exhausted, but at least it made getting to sleep easier.  

到了星期一，他们的关系稍微缓和了一些——或者至少，他们都不希望朋友们知道他们在吵架。雷木斯沉浸在他的NEWT复习中——如果他不在图书馆一个人呆着，他就会将他的集体学习时间每晚延长一个小时。这是满月的一周，他疲惫不堪，但至少这样更容易入睡。

 

And he had to avoid Marlene too, of course. He deliberately skipped going to Madam Pomfrey’s Tuesday night healing classes, just in case the subject of werewolves reared its ugly head again. Marlene was the sort of girl who would derail an entire lesson if she thought injustice was being done somewhere.  

当然，他也不得不避开Marlene。他故意避开庞弗雷夫人周二晚上的治疗课程，以防万一狼人这个话题再次出现。Marlene是那种如果认为哪里有不公正行为就会破坏整个课程的女孩。

 

To Remus’s surprise, Gilderoy Lockhart, the smarmy Ravenclaw commentator, made a guest appearance in his Wednesday revision group. Lockhart was in the year below, and hadn’t crossed the marauder’s radar much so far. He was a bit camp and annoying, prone to laughing too loudly in the dining hall, but that was all Remus knew about him.  

令雷木斯惊讶的是，油腔滑调的拉文克劳解说员Gilderoy Lockhart出现在他周三的复习小组中。洛哈特比他们低一年级，到目前为止没有太多进入掠夺者的视线。他有点娘娘腔，令人讨厌，容易在餐厅里笑得太大声，但这就是雷木斯对他的全部了解。

 

He sidled up to Remus, his hair in ridiculous blond bouffant curls. He stank of aftershave, too.  

他凑到雷木斯身边，他的头发是滑稽的金色泡芙卷。他还散发着剃须水的臭味。

 

“Love this idea,” he gushed, “Helping other students to achieve, really great!”  

“喜欢这个主意，”他滔滔不绝地说，“帮助其他学生取得成就，真是太棒了！”

 

“Er, yeah, I s’pose.” Remus replied, shuffling his papers.  

“呃，是的，我想是的。”雷木斯回答，翻看着他的文件。

“我想帮把手，”洛哈特露齿一笑，“我自己也是个高手，你知道的。魔咒、变形术、魔药——你说得出我都会。”

 

“Um. Great. Cheers.” Remus nodded, “I said I’d go through anti-Giant legislation with the third years today, but have a chat with Chris,” He moved away, quickly, leaving Christopher to deal with it.  

“嗯。很好。谢谢。”雷木斯点点头，“我说过我要和三年级的学生一起学习反巨人立法，但和克里斯聊聊，”他迅速离开，让克里斯托弗去处理。

 

Wednesday was also the second official meeting of the prank-planning group, so Remus and Chris stayed back in the Charms room after study group. Chris had a vaguely dazed expression as they leaned against Flitwick’s desk, waiting.  

星期三也是恶作剧策划小组的第二次正式会议，所以雷木斯和克里斯在学习小组后留在魔咒教室。克里斯靠在Flitwick的桌子上，表情有些迷茫，等待着。

 

“Sorry about that,” Remus offered, lighting up a cigarette as Lockhart swanned out. “I dunno how to deal with him.”  

“抱歉，”雷

 

木斯说，点燃了一根香烟，看着洛哈特走出去。“我不知道该怎么应付他。”

 

“Oh, it’s fine, he’s in half my classes, so I’m used to it.” Chris replied, still looking a bit disturbed.  

“哦，没事，他上了一半的课，我已经习惯了。”克里斯回答，仍然有点不安。

“他想要什么？”

 

“It took a while to figure out,” Christopher frowned, “He kept telling me how good he is at everything… but I think he wanted help with Charms.”  

“花了一段时间才弄清楚，”克里斯托弗皱着眉头说，“他一直在告诉我他在所有事情上都很擅长……但我想他需要魔咒方面的帮助。”

 

Remus snorted disdainfully.  

雷木斯轻蔑地哼了一声。

 

The prank planning session was shorter than the week before - it turned out that no one had had any decent ideas yet. The fourth year Ravenclaws had uncovered some frankly terrifying curses which they were all eager to share, but Lily stepped in, reiterating the rule that nobody ought to get hurt.  

恶作剧策划会议比上周要短——事实证明没有人有任何像样的主意。四年级的拉文克劳发现了一些坦白说令人恐惧的诅咒，他们都急于分享，但莉莉介入，重申了不应该伤害任何人的规则。

 

They split up again for the journey back to their common rooms, and Remus was faced with a choice between Marlene and Yaz or Sirius and Mary. In the end, he decided it was better the devil he knew, and chose Sirius and Mary. She did most of the talking, which was a relief, and the only awkward moment came when the boys were all back in the dormitory.  

他们再次分开回到各自的休息室，雷木斯面临在Marlene和Yaz以及天狼星和Mary之间的选择。最终，他决定选择熟悉的恶魔，选择了天狼星和Mary。她做了大部分的谈话，这让人松了口气，唯一的尴尬时刻是在男孩们都回到宿舍的时候。

 

Remus went over to his own bed, pulling back the duvet.  

雷木斯走到自己的床边，拉开羽绒被。

 

“You’re sleeping there, then?” Sirius asked, out of the blue. Remus frowned, turning to look at him. He hadn’t thought it was up for debate - they were barely speaking to each other, why on earth would they sleep together? And why on earth did Sirius want to call attention to it in front of the others?!  

“你要睡在那里吗？”天狼星突然问道。雷木斯皱眉，转头看着他。他从没想过这是可以讨论的——他们几乎不说话了，为什么他们还要睡在一起？天狼星为什么要在其他人面前引起注意？！

 

“Yeah.” He nodded, turning back, “Full moon tomorrow. Thought we should all get as much sleep as possible.”  

“是的。”他点点头，转过身，“明天是满月。我想我们应该尽量多睡些。”

 

“Yeah, fair enough.” Sirius replied. Remus climbed in and drew his curtains shut, without another word.  

“是的，公平合理。”天狼星回答。雷木斯爬进去，拉上了窗帘，没有再说一句话。
