“都好吗？”詹姆斯大声地低声说。天狼星哼了一声作为回应，就这样。

**Thursday 23rd February 1978**

 

Remus was more on edge than usual on the day of the full moon. He’d slept badly anyway, thinking about the McKinnons and Sirius and wondering how he was ever going to fix any of it.  

满月那天，雷木斯比平时更加紧张。他本来就睡得不好，想着麦金农一家和天狼星，想着如何才能修复这一切。

 

At breakfast, it looked as though Marlene had had a difficult night too. Her eyes were rimmed red, and her hair was messier than usual. Yaz and Mary sat either side of her, vying to be the one who comforted her the most.  

早餐时，Marlene似乎也度过了一个艰难的夜晚。她的眼睛红肿，头发比平时更乱。Yaz和Mary坐在她的两侧，争相安慰她。

 

“I just can’t stop thinking about him,” Marlene shook her head, staring into her bowl of cornflakes. “I’ve read so many books and accounts, and they all say it hurts a lot…”  

“我就是忍不住想起他，”Marlene摇着头，盯着她的玉米片碗。“我看了很多书和记述，都说很痛……”

 

Remus stopped eating his own breakfast, and sipped his tea instead, trying to hide his distress.  

雷木斯停止吃自己的早餐，改为喝茶，试图掩饰自己的痛苦。

 

“I’ve read that too,” Sirius said, “But I’m sure that as long as Danny asks for the help he needs he’ll be fine.”  

“我也看过那些，”天狼星说，“但我相信只要Danny寻求他需要的帮助，他会没事的。”

 

Remus tried to ignore this, seething quietly under his collar.  

雷木斯试图忽视这一点，默默地在衣领下怒火中烧。

 

“Mum’s had to take him to the ministry.” Marlene continued, miserable, “They have cells there, apparently. We asked if there would be healers present, but no one can tell me anything.”  

“妈妈不得不带他去魔法部。”Marlene继续说道，痛苦不堪，“那里显然有牢房。我们问过是否会有治疗师在场，但没有人能告诉我。”

 

“I’m sure it’s the best place,” Yaz squeezed her arm, gently.  

“我相信那是最好的地方，”Yaz轻轻握住她的手臂。

 

Nobody agreed with her. Mary pursed her lips.  

没有人同意她的看法。Mary抿着嘴唇。

 

“He doesn’t deserve this!” Marlene burst into tears, “He doesn’t deserve to be locked up alone! He’s my lovely brother, not some… some animal.”  

“他不该这样！”Marlene哭了起来，“他不该被单独关起来！他是我可爱的哥哥，不是……不是某种动物。”

 

The nausea of guilt threatened to overwhelm Remus, and he left as soon as he could. The rest of the day he could barely concentrate on his lessons. Perverse as it was, ever since the marauders had become animagi, he’d sort of looked forward to full moons at Hogwarts. It had been a while since he’d dreaded one quite so much as this.  

内疚的恶心感威胁着要淹没雷木斯，他尽快离开了。接下来的整天他几乎无法集中精力上课。虽然很扭曲，但自从掠夺者们成为阿尼玛格斯以来，他有点期待在霍格沃茨的满月。已经有一段时间他没有如此害怕过一次满月了。

 

When he arrived at Madam Pomfrey’s office in the evening, he found her frowning her way through a pile of letters. He’d never seen her doing paperwork before.  

晚上当他到达庞弗雷夫人的办公室时，发现她正在皱眉翻看一堆信件。他以前从未见过她做文书工作。

 

“Oh, hello dear,” she smiled at him, tiredly, “Shall we get going?”  

“哦，你好亲爱的，”她疲倦地对他笑了笑，“我们走吧？”

 

He nodded, and waited patiently for her to put on her cloak. She saw him staring at the letters. “They’re from ex-pupils, mostly,” she explained, “Ones who were affected by the attacks. Some of them have family members facing their first full moon, and want to know if I know anything helpful.”  

他点点头，耐心地等待她穿上斗篷。她看到他盯着那些信件。“这些主要是以前的学生写的，”她解释道，“那些受到袭击影响的人。有些人的家人正面临第一次满月，想知道我是否有任何有用的信息。”

 

“Oh.”  

“哦。”

 

“I’ve been able to pass on a bit about aftercare, but you and I know how little real information there is,” she continued, as they walked out. Remus remained mute. “I’ve had poor Miss McKinnon here every day, almost. She’s a friend of yours, isn’t she?”  

“我能传递一些关于后续护理的信息，但你我都知道真正有用的信息很少，”她继续说道，两人走了出去。雷木斯保持沉默。“可怜的McKinnon小姐几乎每天都来这里。她是你的朋友，对吧？”

 

“Yes.” Remus’s voice cracked slightly. Madam Pomfrey patted his arm, softly.  

“是的。”雷木斯的声音微微裂开。庞弗雷夫人轻轻拍了拍他的手臂。

 

“It must be very hard for you, my dear.”  

“这对你来说一定很难，亲爱的。”

 

“It’s fine.”  

“没事。”

 

“You know you can always talk to me, if you need to.”  

“你知道如果需要，你随时可以找我聊聊。”

 

“Thanks.” He could hear Sirius’s voice in the back of his head, taunting him, I told you so…  

“谢谢。”他在脑海中听到了天狼星的声音，嘲讽道，我早就告诉你了……

 

But Sirius was wrong. Physical pain was the very least of Remus’s problems, and something he was willing to bear, if he had to. It reminded him what he owed.  

但天狼星错了。身体的痛苦是雷木斯最小的问题，如果必须，他愿意忍受。这提醒了他所欠的东西。

 

Despite his apprehension, the full moon was a relief. Remus didn’t even cry out from the pain of transformation, he just let it consume him. As ashamed as it made him, it was good to become something else for a few hours; to relinquish control. The wolf was still on good terms with Padfoot, at least, and they could play and run and hunt without any messy human problems getting in the way.  

尽管担忧，满月却成了一种解脱。雷木斯甚至没有因变形的痛苦而喊叫，他只是任由其吞噬他。尽管这让他感到羞愧，但变成另一个东西几个小时还是好的；放弃控制。至少狼仍然和破釜酒吧关系不错，他们可以玩耍、奔跑和狩猎，没有任何乱七八糟的人类问题阻碍。

 

But it wasn’t to last.  

但这不会持久。

**Friday 24th February 1978**

 

The routine was standard by now. Remus transformed back, the others checked he was ok, then left, Madam Pomfrey came to collect him, he spent the morning under a sleeping draught, woke up in time for lunch, then headed back to his own bed in the afternoon.  

现在这一切已经成了常规。雷木斯变回人形，其他人检查他是否没事，然后离开，庞弗雷夫人来接他，他在早上服用了一剂催眠药水，醒来时正好是午餐时间，然后下午回到自己的床上。

 

More recently, Sirius had been coming to collect him from the infirmary, if his timetable allowed for it. (And, actually, even when his timetable didn’t allow for it - Sirius took any excuse to bunk off.) Of course, given the way Remus had been acting, he didn’t expect Sirius to come that day.  

最近，天狼星如果时间允许的话，会来接他离开医务室。（实际上，即使他的时间表不允许，天狼星也会找借口逃课。）当然，鉴于雷木斯的表现，他没指望天狼星那天会来。

 

But Sirius was always full of surprises.  

但天狼星总是充满惊喜。

 

“Brought you a frog,” he said, waiting patiently as Remus finished tying his laces. He handed over a chocolate frog box, which Remus accepted. His temper had cooled quite a bit; perhaps a good long sleep had been all he needed.  

“给你带了只青蛙，”天狼星说，耐心等待雷木斯系好鞋带。他递过一盒巧克力青蛙，雷木斯接受了。他的脾气已经平静了许多；也许一个好长的睡眠就是他所需要的。

 

“Thanks.”  

“谢谢。”

 

“Can we be ok, again?” Sirius asked, sounding genuinely sorry. “Can we both just admit we said some stupid stuff, but it’s over, now?”  

“我们能重新好吗？”天狼星问，听起来真的很抱歉。“我们都承认我们说了一些愚蠢的话，但现在已经过去了，可以吗？”

 

Remus looked at him for a long time, letting him stew a little bit. Then he smiled,  

雷木斯盯着他看了很长时间，让他稍微煎熬一下。然后他笑了，

 

“Yeah, go on then.”  

“嗯，好吧。”

 

They walked back to the tower quite happily, though Remus was pushing himself a bit harder than normal, trying not to limp or show any trace of discomfort.  

他们愉快地走回塔楼，尽管雷木斯比平时更加努力地走路，试图不跛行或显示出任何不适的迹象。

 

“Is Marlene ok?” Remus asked, as they neared the common room.  

“玛琳娜还好吗？”雷木斯问，接近公共休息室时。

 

“Yeah, think so,” Sirius nodded, “She got a letter from her mum this morning, saying Danny’s ok. Cried a bit, but she’s less of a state now.”  

“嗯，我想是的，”天狼星点头，“她今天早上收到了她妈妈的信，说Danny没事。哭了一会儿，但她现在状态好多了。”

 

“Good. That’s good.”  

“很好。那就好。”

 

They pushed through the portrait hole and walked through the common room.  

他们推开画像门，走过公共休息室。

 

“I think I’ll go straight to bed for a bit,” Remus said, making for the dorm. “If that’s ok?”  

“我想我会直接去床上休息一会儿，”雷木斯说，朝宿舍走去。“这样可以吗？”

 

“Of course!” Sirius nodded, over polite, as they headed up yet another flight of stairs. Remus was seriously struggling now, but he’d be damned if he’d let Sirius see it.  

“当然可以！”天狼星点头，非常礼貌，他们又上了一层楼。雷木斯现在确实在挣扎，但他绝不会让天狼星看到。

 

“You tired?” Remus asked.  

“累了吗？”雷木斯问。

 

“Nah,” Sirius said, “Slept all morning. Peter too.”  

“不，”天狼星说，“睡了整个早上。彼得也是。”

 

“Oh good.” Remus finally reached his bed and sat down. Without even thinking, his hand went to rub his hip. He stopped as soon as he realised, but Sirius’s eyes zeroed in on it at once. He looked Remus in the eye reproachfully.  

“哦，太好了。”雷木斯终于到达自己的床边坐下。不假思索地，他的手去揉了揉他的臀部。他意识到后立即停下，但天狼星的目光立刻锁定了这个动作。他责备地看着雷木斯。

 

“Did you speak to Madam Pomfrey?”  

“你跟庞弗雷夫人谈过了吗？”

 

“We had a lovely chat, thanks.” Remus stiffened, defences back up, “About all her poor ex-students who had to transform for the first time last night. It was really cheery.”  

“我们聊得很好，谢谢。”雷木斯僵硬了起来，重新建立起防线，“聊了一些她可怜的前学生们昨晚第一次变形的事。真是太愉快了。”

 

Sirius tutted.  

天狼星发出不满的声音。

 

“But did you talk to her about your hip?!”  

“但你跟她谈过你的臀部吗？！”

 

“No.” Remus huffed, lying down.  

“没有。”雷木斯哼了一声，躺下。

 

“Remus, stop being difficult! You see her every week! Just mention to her—I mean, I’ll do it if you want me to.”  

“雷木斯，别那么难对付！你每周都会见到她的！只要提一下——我可以替你说，如果你需要的话。”

 

“Jesus Christ, not this again! Leave me alone!” Remus sat up again.  

“天哪，又来了！别打扰我！”雷木斯再次坐起来。

 

“No!” Sirius retorted, just as viciously, “I don’t understand why you won’t tell her about it. I’m sure she could help.”  

“不！”天狼星同样激烈地反击，“我不明白你为什么不告诉她。我相信她可以帮忙。”

 

“Oh my god, why can’t you just drop it? I said I don’t want to bother her with crap like this. You’re making such a big fuss over nothing!” Remus was on his feet now, the wolf inside him wanting the higher ground; asserting dominance.  

“天啊，你为什么不能放弃？我说过我不想打扰她处理这种垃圾。你对这事大惊小怪！”雷木斯现在站起来，内心的狼想要占据更高的地位；展现主导权。

 

“And you’re avoiding your problems again!” Sirius raged, “You always do this and it’s so bloody exhausting! You think you’re being so mature, do you? Keeping everything bottled up. It’s stupid! You’re just making a martyr of yourself, it’s like you want to be miserable.”  

“你又在回避问题！”天狼星愤怒地说，“你总是这样，真是让人疲惫！你认为自己很成熟吗？把一切都藏在心里。太蠢了！你只是自我牺牲，像是想要让自己痛苦。”

 

“Oh, get fucked, Black!” Remus shouted back. “Easy for you to have a go, isn’t it?! Why do we always have to talk about my shit life, hm?! Mr ‘tell me a fucking secret’?!”  

“去你妈的，黑！”雷木斯回喊道。“你说得轻松，不是吗？！为什么我们总是要谈论我的糟糕生活？嗯？！‘告诉我一个该死的秘密’先生？！”

 

Sirius blinked, shocked, and Remus was elated; he had something now. He had Sirius in his jaws, he wasn’t letting go until he tasted blood. “What about you, Sirius?! How come we never get to talk about your fucked up family, with your death eater brother and your insane cousin?! Why don’t we talk about your pain, and your scars for a little while, see how that feels.”  

天狼星愣住了，震惊不已，雷木斯感到兴奋；他现在有了把柄。他抓住了天狼星，他不会放手，直到尝到血腥。“那你呢，天狼星？！我们怎么从来不谈论你的破碎家庭，你那个食死徒的兄弟和你那疯癫的表亲？！为什么我们不谈谈你的痛苦和伤疤，看看感觉如何。”

 

“Remus, for fuck’s sake—”  

“雷木斯，去他妈的——”

 

“No, I know! Why don’t we talk about your mother ?” Remus went in for the kill, and it was more effective than even he had expected. Sirius changed completely; his expression froze, his posture tensed, as if he’d been punched in the gut.

“我知道！为什么我们不谈谈你的母亲？”雷木斯一语致命，比他预料的还要有效。天狼星完全变了；他的表情冻结，姿态紧绷，仿佛被狠狠打了一拳。

 

Remus almost wished he had punched him, because then at least Sirius could just punch him back, and they could have a fair fight, and that would be it. But that hadn’t been fair, and he couldn’t take it back.

雷木斯几乎希望他真的打了他，因为那样至少天狼星可以还手，他们可以公平地打一架，这样就解决了。但这并不公平，他也无法收回。

 

Sirius gave him a look of utter hurt and shock, before turning quickly to anger.

天狼星给了他一个充满伤痛和震惊的眼神，然后迅速转为愤怒。

 

“Go fuck yourself, Lupin.” He spat, storming out.

“去你妈的，卢平。”他狠狠地说道，怒气冲冲地离开了。

 

“Yeah, piss off, then!” Remus shouted as the door slammed.

“是啊，那就滚吧！”雷木斯在门砰地关上时大喊。

 

He was breathing hard, and his face was very hot. He wished Sirius would come back and shout at him a bit more, so he could shout back, but he settled for chain smoking and The Sex Pistols. Fuck everybody.

他喘着粗气，脸很烫。他希望天狼星能回来再对他吼几句，这样他也可以吼回去，但他选择了接连不断地抽烟和听性手枪乐队的音乐。去他妈的所有人。

 

Sirius did not return, and Remus didn’t know where the map was, so he couldn’t look for him.

天狼星没有回来，雷木斯也不知道地图在哪里，所以他找不到他。

 

Eventually, the dorm room door did open again, and Lily and James came in, very close together and whispering happily,

最终，宿舍的门再次打开，莉莉和詹姆斯走了进来，非常亲密地在一起低声说笑。

 

“Oh, hiya Moony!” James stopped as he caught sight of Remus brooding by the window. He looked a bit sheepish, “Sorry, we thought you’d be in the hospital wing, still.”

“哦，你好啊，穆尼！”詹姆斯看到窗边沉思的雷木斯时停下了脚步，看起来有点不好意思，“抱歉，我们以为你还在医院翼呢。”

 

“No. She lets me go after lunch, normally.” Remus replied, monotone. He got up, “I’ll get out of your way.”

“没有。她通常在午饭后让我走。”雷木斯用单调的语调回答。他站起来，“我会让开。”

 

“No, no, Remus, don’t!” Lily said, flustered, “We just came up here for the quiet.”

“不要，不要，雷木斯，别这样！”莉莉慌张地说，“我们只是上来找个安静的地方。”

 

“Really?” Remus raised a sarcastic eyebrow, and Lily and James blushed, looking away.

“真的？”雷木斯讽刺地扬起眉毛，莉莉和詹姆斯脸红了，转过脸去。

 

“Where’s Padfoot?” James went over to sit on his bed.

“天狼星在哪儿？”詹姆斯走过去坐在床上。

 

“Don’t know.”

“不知道。”

 

“What?”

“什么？”

 

“Don’t know. Don’t care.” Remus withdrew another cigarette from his matchbox and lit it with the end of the last one.

“不知道。不在乎。”雷木斯从火柴盒里又拿出一支烟，用上一支烟的烟头点燃。

 

“Are you… having a fight?”

“你们……吵架了吗？”

 

“Look, stay out of it, Potter.” Remus snarled.

“看，别管这事，波特。”雷木斯咆哮道。

 

James recoiled, and looked at Lily, who shrugged back at him.

詹姆斯退缩了一下，看向莉莉，莉莉对他耸了耸肩。

 

At that very moment, as if it had been summoned just to break the tension, an owl flew in the open window, surprising all three of them. It was from the Potters, and James retrieved two letters tied to its leg. He glanced down at one and held it out to Remus.

就在那一刻，仿佛为了打破紧张气氛，一只猫头鹰飞进了敞开的窗户，吓了他们三个人一跳。是从波特家来的，詹姆斯取下系在它腿上的两封信。他看了一眼其中一封，递给雷木斯。

 

“For you, Moony.”

“给你的，穆尼。”

 

Clicking his tongue irritably, Remus got up off the sill and went to snatch it from James’s outstretched hand. He opened it, skimming the brief note from Mrs Potter, who had been so kindly forwarding all of his correspondence.

雷木斯恼火地咂了咂舌，从窗台上站起来，从詹姆斯伸出的手中抢过信。他打开信，浏览了波特夫人简短的便条，夫人一直好心地转发他的所有信件。

 

He expected another postcard from Grant, but it was a neatly folded envelope. He didn’t recognise the tidy, blue ink handwriting, but it had a muggle stamp.

他本以为是格兰特的另一张明信片，但却是一个整齐折叠的信封。他不认识那工整的蓝色墨水字迹，但信上有麻瓜的邮票。

 

He looked down at the return address, written in tiny script on the back.

他低头看了看背面用小字写的回信地址。

 

If undelivered, please return to:

如果无法投递，请退回：

 

Ms Hope Jenkins, Sparrow Ward, Cardiff City Hospital, Cardiff.

霍普·詹金斯女士，斯帕罗病房，加的夫市医院，加的夫。

 

Chapter 138: Seventh Year: Hope 

They fuck you up, your mum and dad.   

    They may not mean to, but they do.   

They fill you with the faults they had

    And add some extra, just for you.

 

But they were fucked up in their turn

    By fools in old-style hats and coats,   

Who half the time were soppy-stern

    And half at one another’s throats.

 

Man hands on misery to man.

    It deepens like a coastal shelf.

Get out as early as you can,

    And don’t have any kids yourself.





Ms Hope Jenkins.

Remus choked on his fag, then dropped it, burning a hole in his trousers. Yelping with pain, he leapt up, patting wildly at the hot patch on his thigh.

雷木斯被烟呛了一下，然后把它掉在地上，烧了他裤子上的一个洞。因为疼痛而尖叫，他跳起来，疯狂地拍打着大腿上的热斑。

 

“Remus!” Lily stared at him, alarmed, “Are you ok?!”

“雷木斯！”莉莉惊恐地看着他，“你还好吗？！”

 

“Yeah, yeah…” He picked up the cigarette and tossed it out of the window. He’d scrunched up the little envelope in his other hand. He stuffed the crumpled paper into his pocket. “Just… nipping to the loo.”

“嗯，嗯……”他捡起烟，把它扔出了窗外。他用另一只手把小信封揉成一团，塞进了口袋里。“我只是……去趟厕所。”

 

He hurried into the little bathroom and slammed the door shut, trying to regulate his breathing a bit. Ok. Ok. He ought to have expected this. He was the one who’d written to her, after all.

他匆忙走进小浴室，砰地关上了门，试图调整一下呼吸。好吧。好吧。他应该预料到这一点。毕竟是他写了信给她。

 

Remus pulled the letter out of his pocket and smoothed it out. He couldn’t have opened it in front of Lily and James; it might say anything, and he was so unprepared. He bit his lip. He wanted another cigarette, badly, but he’d just chucked the last one out of the window. Typical.

雷木斯从口袋里拿出信，展开它。他不能在莉莉和詹姆斯面前打开它；它可能会说任何事，而他又没有准备好。他咬了咬嘴唇。他非常想要另一支烟，但他刚刚把最后一支扔出了窗外。真是典型。

 

He peeled open the envelope slowly, taking care not to tear it, as if that might mean something. The paper was tissue-thin, and he unfolded it gently. The handwriting was more recognisable now. He knew it from the original letter, written all those years ago, except now it was more spindly; noticeably crooked, as though the hand had been shaking.

他慢慢地撕开信封，小心翼翼地避免撕破，好像那可能意味着什么。纸很薄，他轻轻地展开它。字迹现在更容易识别了。他从多年前的原始信件中认得出来，只是现在更细长了；明显歪斜，好像手在颤抖。

 

Dear Remus,

 

I am sorry it has taken me so long to reply to you. I am afraid I have been unwell, and I have not been at home to receive post.

 

I was so happy to hear from you. I am sorry I cannot write more, my darling, but I would love to hear how you are getting on. Please write again, to the address below.

 

Love Mum.

 

亲爱的雷木斯，

 

对不起，我回复你花了这么长时间。我担心我一直不太好，没在家收信。

 

收到你的来信我很高兴。我很抱歉不能写更多，我的亲爱的，但我很想知道你过得怎么样。请再次写信到下面的地址。

 

爱你的妈妈。

 

Remus’s own hands were shaking now. ‘Love Mum.’ What the fuck did that mean?!

雷木斯自己的手也在颤抖。“爱妈妈。”这是什么意思？！

 

He felt rage creeping up on him, ready to swallow him whole. The spat with Sirius faded into insignificance; now he was truly furious. It was an anger that had lain dormant for a long time now, but it had always been there, in the core of him. An anger that had no direction, no purpose other than filling him up with red hot mania. Maybe Greyback had put it there. Maybe Hope’s abandonment had. Right now he didn’t give a shit.

他感到愤怒在他体内蔓延，准备吞噬他。与天狼星的争吵变得微不足道；现在他真正的愤怒了。这种愤怒已经沉睡了很长时间，但它一直存在于他的核心。没有方向、没有目的，只是让他充满炙热的狂躁。也许是格雷巴克把它放在了那里。也许是霍普的抛弃。现在他不在乎。

 

Unable to control himself, he kicked the bathroom door. He kicked it so hard that he splintered the wood, cracking it right through.

他无法控制自己，踢了浴室的门。他踢得很用力，木头都裂开了，整个门都破裂了。

 

“Fuck.” He muttered. “Ow.” He hoped he hadn’t broken a toe.

“该死。”他喃喃道。“疼。”他希望自己没有踢断脚趾。

 

“Oh my god, Remus?!” Lily’s voice sang out again.

“哦我的天，雷木斯？！”莉莉的声音再次传来。

 

“Sorry.” He said, almost on instinct, as he wrenched his foot free from the door. He unlocked it.

“对不起。”他几乎是本能地说道，一边从门上抽回脚来。他解锁了门。

 

James was standing right there, his eyes big and wide, Lily just behind him, as if he was shielding her from Remus.

詹姆斯正站在那里，眼睛睁得大大的，莉莉就在他身后，好像他在保护她不受雷木斯的伤害。

 

“What the bloody hell are you playing at?!” James said, his voice hard. “Look, if you’re having a tiff with Padfoot then sort it out between you, don’t start tearing our room apart!”

“你到底在搞什么鬼？！”詹姆斯声音严厉地说道。“看看，如果你和天狼星有点争执，那就自己解决，别开始搞砸我们的房间！”

 

“Sorry.” Remus said again, feeling quite small. He’d never been told off by James before; it was scarier than he’d expected.

“对不起。”雷木斯再次说道，感觉自己很渺小。他以前从未被詹姆斯训斥过；这比他预期的要吓人。

 

“Remus?” Lily pushed her boyfriend aside, impatiently, “What’s wrong?”

“雷木斯？”莉莉不耐烦地推开她的男朋友，“怎么了？”

 

He shook his head, looking down at the letter in his hands. His shoulders slumped. He was still breathing too hard to be able to speak. He handed it to her.

他摇了摇头，低头看着手中的信。肩膀垂落。他仍然喘着粗气，无法说话。他把信递给了她。

 

Lily gave him a quizzical look, but took the paper from him. As she read it, her eyes grew bigger and her mouth dropped open. James read it over her shoulder, and soon enough their expressions matched. Remus couldn’t seem to get his breathing under control; he wasn’t quite sure what was happening. His chest grew very tight, as if all the air had been sucked out of the room. He suddenly felt very hot and very dizzy, and he was seeing stars.

莉莉给了他一个疑惑的眼神，但接过了纸。当她阅读时，她的眼睛变得更大，嘴巴张开了。詹姆斯从她肩膀上读了一遍，很快他们的表情也变得一致。雷木斯似乎无法控制自己的呼吸；他不太确定发生了什么。他的胸口变得非常紧绷，仿佛房间里的空气都被抽走了。他突然感到非常热，非常眩晕，眼前出现了星星。

 

He stumbled, clutching the door frame for dear life.

他踉跄着，紧紧抓住门框，生怕掉下去。

 

“Remus?!” Lily’s voice came to him in an echo, as if he was at the bottom of a deep well. Her soft hands were on his shoulders, and she guided him down towards the floor - which was a good thing, because his legs had just decided to give up. She started rubbing his back slowly, and was speaking very calmly, “Deep breaths, Remus, do you hear me? In through your mouth, then out through your nose, ok? With me; one… two… three…”

“雷木斯？！”莉莉的声音在他耳边回响，好像他在深井底部。她柔软的手搭在他的肩膀上，她把他引导到地板上——这还不错，因为他的腿已经决定放弃了。她开始慢慢地揉他的背，声音非常平静地说：“深呼吸，雷木斯，你听到我说话了吗？通过嘴巴吸气，然后从鼻子呼气，好吗？跟我一起；一……二……三……”

 

He didn’t know what sort of magic that was, but it started to work, and after ten deep breaths he began to feel normal

 

 again. His vision clearing, he looked up. Lily was sitting beside him on the dusty bedroom floor. James was standing over them, looking worried. He had the letter.

他不知道那是什么魔法，但它开始奏效了，十次深呼吸之后，他开始感觉正常了。视线变得清晰，他抬起头。莉莉坐在他身边，坐在尘土飞扬的卧室地板上。詹姆斯站在他们身边，看起来很担心。他拿着信。

 

“Thanks,” Remus said, still short of breath, “Sorry, I dunno what happened there.”

“谢谢，”雷木斯说道，仍然气喘吁吁，“对不起，我不知道刚才发生了什么。”

 

“My sister has funny turns like that all the time, when she gets anxious,” Lily explained. “Got anything sweet? She normally has a biscuit after the worst has passed.”

“我姐姐经常会有那种奇怪的发作，当她感到焦虑的时候，”莉莉解释道。“有甜的东西吗？她通常在最糟糕的情况过去后会吃一块饼干。”

 

“Um… yeah.” Remus delved into his pocket for the chocolate frog Sirius had given him earlier. He unwrapped it and bit the head off, quickly. His mouth filled with rich sweetness, and he really did feel much better.

“嗯……有。”雷木斯从口袋里拿出之前天狼星给他的巧克力青蛙。他快速地拆开包装，咬掉了头。嘴里充满了浓郁的甜味，他确实感觉好多了。

 

He tried to get up, and James immediately offered a steady arm to help,

他试着站起来，詹姆斯立即伸出稳固的手臂来帮助，

 

“Sorry I had a go, Moony,” he said, still sounding very worried, “I was a right dick.”

“对不起我刚才说了那些，穆尼，”他说，声音仍然非常担心，“我真的很傻。”

 

“No, I shouldn’t have broken the door…” Remus replied, carefully brushing his trousers down and walking to his bed to sit.

“没事，我不该打破门……”雷木斯回答说，小心地整理裤子，走到床边坐下。

 

“Oh, that’s nothing,” Lily got up and withdrew her wand, “Reparo. See?”

“哦，那没什么，”莉莉站起来，拿出她的魔杖，“修复咒。看？”

 

“Can I have the letter back?” Remus asked, weakly.

“我可以拿回信吗？”雷木斯虚弱地问。

 

“Yeah, sorry!” James hurried to pass it back. Remus read it again. His stomach tightened, but he didn’t get dizzy again. Love Mum. “I didn’t know you’d sent her a letter.” James said. “I didn’t know you even knew where she was.”

“是的，对不起！”詹姆斯急忙把信递回来。雷木斯再次读了一遍。他的胃收紧了，但没有再感到眩晕。“爱妈妈。”詹姆斯说。“我不知道你给她写了信。我不知道你甚至知道她在哪里。”

 

“Your parents helped me.” Remus said, still re-reading. “I only told Sirius about it.”

“是你的父母帮了我。”雷木斯说，仍然在重读。“我只告诉了天狼星。”

 

“Oh, love,” Lily came to sit by him, she squeezed his hand. “Are you going to write back?”

“哦，亲爱的，”莉莉走过来坐在他身边，握住他的手。“你打算回信吗？”

 

Remus looked up, staring ahead. He made a decision.

雷木斯抬头望着前方。他做出了决定。

 

“No. I’m going to see her.”

“不。我打算去见她。”

 

“Oh!” Lily squeaked, “Yes, of course… er… I bet McGonagall would help you arrange it for the weekend, maybe--”

“哦！”莉莉尖叫道，“是的，当然……呃……我敢打赌麦格教授会帮你安排周末去见她，也许——”

 

“No.” Remus shook his head, “I’m going right now.”

“不。”雷木斯摇头，“我现在就去。”

 

“What?!” James said.

“什么？！”詹姆斯说道。

 

“I’ve waited long enough.” Remus said. “I’ve got the address. I’m going.”

“我等得够久了。”雷木斯说道。“我有地址。我现在就去。”

 

“Remus, don’t you want to just have a think--” Lily started.

“雷木斯，你不想考虑一下——”莉莉开口。

 

“No.” Remus said, pulling his hand away from her.

“不。”雷木斯说道，抽回了他的手。

 

His hand brushed against the cigarette burn in his leg. Bugger. Where was he going to get another pair? Better try a mending spell once he’d calmed down a bit. He got up and went to his trunk to find a clean pair of trousers. Couldn’t meet his mother with cigarette burns on his clothes, could he?

他的手碰到了腿上的烟烧伤。糟糕。他要去哪儿找另一条裤子？最好在冷静下来后试试修复咒语。他站起来，走到行李箱前找一条干净的裤子。不能穿着有烟烧伤的衣服去见妈妈，对吧？

 

“No thinking.” He said to Lily. “She’s in a hospital, god knows why, but I might not have long.”

“别想太多。”他说给莉莉。“她在医院里，天知道为什么，但我可能没时间了。”

 

He undressed without even thinking. Lily looked away, quickly, blushing, but he didn't care. “Prongs,” he said, “Can I have your cloak?”

他没有多想就脱了衣服。莉莉迅速转过脸去，脸红了，但他不在乎。“角鹿，”他说，“我可以借你的斗篷吗？”

 

“Of course.” James nodded, without hesitation.

“当然。”詹姆斯毫不犹豫地点了点头。

 

“Thanks. I’m going to try and apparate from Honeyduke’s, I think. Shouldn’t be gone all night, I can be back before curfew, I bet.”

 

“谢谢。我打算试着从霍尼杜克的糖果店使用消失术。我想不会整晚不在，我敢打赌我能在宵禁之前回来。”

“Good plan.” James nodded.  

“好主意。”詹姆斯点头道。

 

“How are you going to get to Honeyduke’s?!” Lily asked, looking very confused. Remus looked at James, curiously. The other boy gave a sheepish chuckle and pushed his glasses up his nose.  

“你打算怎么去霍尼杜克的糖果店？！”莉莉问，看起来非常困惑。雷木斯好奇地看着詹姆斯。另一个男孩不好意思地笑了笑，推了推眼镜。

 

“Er… there's sort of a secret passageway…”  

“呃……其实有一条秘密通道……”

 

Less than half an hour later, they had passed the hunchbacked witch statue and were about to begin the journey to Hogsmeade. They’d hurriedly dressed in muggle clothes, something Lily had suggested almost at the very last minute. James had wanted to tell Sirius and Peter, but Remus refused. Peter couldn’t apparate anyway, and Remus didn’t have room for Sirius in his head right now. Luckily, James respected this reasoning.  

不到半小时，他们穿过了驼背女巫的雕像，准备开始前往霍格斯梅德的旅程。他们匆忙换上了麻瓜衣服，这是莉莉几乎在最后一刻才建议的。詹姆斯本想告诉天狼星和彼得，但雷木斯拒绝了。彼得反正无法使用消失术，而雷木斯现在脑子里没空间容下天狼星。幸运的是，詹姆斯尊重了这个理由。

 

“How many more secrets do you lot have?!” Lily was whispering, staring about her as they progressed along the dark tunnel.  

“你们还有多少秘密？！”莉莉在黑暗的隧道中低声问道，四处张望。

 

“Does she know about the map?” Remus asked, innocently.  

“她知道那个地图吗？”雷木斯无辜地问。

 

“What map?! Potter! What map??”  

“什么地图？！波特！什么地图？？！”

 

They weren’t really fighting. It was just part of the fun, for Lily and James, all the bickering. They’d spent so many years doing it already they just didn’t know how to stop. Remus liked it. It kept his mind off everything else.  

他们并没有真正争吵。这只是莉莉和詹姆斯的乐趣之一，所有的争吵。他们已经这样做了这么多年，以至于不知道怎么停下来。雷木斯喜欢这样。它让他的注意力从其他事情上转移开。

 

Because he’d calmed down now, and the rational thoughts were starting to creep back in. Where are you going? Why would you think she wants to see you, after all these years? You’ll get caught out of bounds and expelled, and you’ll drag Lily and James down with you.  

因为他现在已经平静下来，理性的思维开始回到脑海里。你要去哪里？你怎么会认为她想见你，毕竟这些年过去了？你会被抓到禁区并被开除，还会拖累莉莉和詹姆斯。

 

And Sirius. He wanted more than anything to have Sirius nearby, if only they weren’t fighting. Perhaps he’d brought this all on himself, invoking Sirius’s mother like that. Oh god, what if Hope was like Walpurga?!  

还有天狼星。他最希望天狼星在身边，只要他们不再争吵。也许他是自作自受，挑起了天狼星的母亲。哦，天哪，要是霍普像沃尔普加一样怎么办？！

 

But he pressed on, because he’d come this far now. Soon enough they were in the cellar of Honeyduke’s and all memorising the hospital address, preparing to apparate.  

但他坚持下去，因为他已经走到了这一步。不久，他们便到了霍尼杜克糖果店的地下室，大家都记住了医院的地址，准备使用消失术。

 

That part was easy. Remus was so full of emotions and adrenaline that he barely had to turn his head and he was whooshing through space, following the current of magic towards Cardiff. Lily and James landed moments later, holding hands.  

那部分很简单。雷木斯充满了情绪和肾上腺素，他几乎没转头就飞速穿过了空间，沿着魔法的流向卡迪夫。莉莉和詹姆斯几分钟后也着陆了，手牵着手。

 

“This is Wales, then,” Lily said, looking around at the quiet city street they found themselves on. “Never been before.”  

“这是威尔士，”莉莉环顾四周说道，“我以前从未来过。”

 

“Me neither.” James and Remus replied in unison.  

“我也没来过。”詹姆斯和雷木斯异口同声地回答。

 

“Let’s look for the hospital, then,” she smiled. She dropped James’s hand and took Remus’s instead, half leading him to the end of the road.  

“那我们找找医院吧，”她笑了笑。她放开了詹姆斯的手，拉着雷木斯走到路的尽头。

 

They’d overshot by only a street or two. The main building was ornate, old and red brick, the rest of it ‘60s grey concrete. It had that cold institutional atmosphere which reminded Remus too much of St Edmund’s.  

他们只偏离了一两条街道。主楼是古雅的红砖建筑，其余的则是60年代的灰色混凝土。那种冷漠的机构气氛让雷木斯太过于想起圣埃德蒙兹。

 

“Right!” Lily said, brightly, facing a large map of the building, beneath a signpost pointing in various directions. “It was Sparrow ward, wasn’t it… so that's… over there.”  

“好！”莉莉开心地说道，面对着一块大地图，上面有各种方向的指示牌。“是斯帕罗病房，对吧……那就是……那边。”

 

She set off again, and Remus was so, so glad she was there, because everything in him was telling him to run away and never look back. Sparrow was in one of the concrete blocks. They stopped just outside.  

她再次出发，雷木斯非常感激她在身边，因为他内心的每一部分都告诉他要逃跑，永远不要回头。斯帕罗在其中一个混凝土建筑块里。他们在外面停下。

 

“Um… Lily? James?” Remus said, holding them back. “Do you mind… not coming with me? I just… I want to do it by myself. Sorry.”  

“嗯……莉莉？詹姆斯？”雷木斯说道，拉住他们。“你们介意……不要跟着我吗？我只是……我想自己来。对不起。”

 

“Of course.” Lily said, patting his shoulder. “We’ll wait right here, right James?”  

“当然。”莉莉拍了拍他的肩膀。“我们就在这里等着，好吗詹姆斯？”

 

“Ok.” James nodded, carefully, “Moony, are you sure you don’t want me to get--”  

“好的。”詹姆斯点了点头，小心地说：“穆尼，你确定不让我去找——”

 

“He won’t come.” Remus said, with absolute certainty. “You were right, we did have a fight. I was awful to him, I said some really shitty stuff. He’s angry and he's got a right to be.”  

“他不会来的。”雷木斯肯定地说道。“你说得对，我们确实吵架了。我对他很糟糕，说了一些很恶心的话。他生气是有理由的。”

 

“Yeah, but still--”  

“是的，但……”

 

“It's fine, Prongs.” Remus assured him, “I’m fine. Ok, I’m going in now.”  

“没事的，角鹿。”雷木斯安慰道，“我没事。好了，我现在要进去了。”

 

“Good luck!” Lily smiled. He nodded, grimly, and approached the revolving doors.  

“祝好运！”莉莉微笑道。他严肃地点了点头，走向旋转门。

 

Inside the hospital there were signs pointing in all sorts of directions, and three times Remus had to go back on himself because he’d taken a wrong turn, or got in the wrong lift somewhere. It was an awful place; it stank of sickness and piss and disinfectant masking blood and death. Remus’s nerve was weakening by the minute.  

医院内部有各种各样的指示牌，雷木斯三次走错了路，要么走错了电梯，要么走错了转弯。这个地方很糟糕；空气中弥漫着疾病、尿液和消毒剂掩盖着血液和死亡的气味。雷木斯的神经每分钟都在减弱。

 

Finally, he passed through a set of double doors with ‘Sparrow’ printed neatly above in blue and white. It led to a quieter corridor, with a nurses station at the end and lots of light open rooms with neat rows of people

 

 lying in beds.  

终于，他穿过了一扇印有‘斯帕罗’的双开门，走进了一个较安静的走廊，走廊尽头有一个护士站，旁边是许多明亮的开放病房，整齐地排列着躺在床上的人们。

 

Remus shuffled along to the nurses station, trying to get a look at the names of the patients listed on the wall behind.  

雷木斯慢慢走到护士站，试图看清墙上列出的病人名字。

 

“Who’re you looking for, lovie?” A plump nurse asked him with a pleasant smile.  

“你在找谁，亲爱的？”一个丰满的护士带着愉快的微笑问他。

 

“Um. Hope Jenkins…” Remus mumbled.  

“嗯。霍普·詹金斯……”雷木斯喃喃道。

“Ah! Relative, are you?”  

“啊！是亲属吗？”

“Yes. I’m her son.”  

“是的。我是她的儿子。”

“Oh, she’ll be so pleased! She talks about her kids all the time, does Hope. Just follow me, pet.”  

“哦，她会很高兴的！霍普总是谈论她的孩子们。跟我来吧，亲爱的。”

 

He didn’t have time to be stunned by this latest revelation that his mother had ‘kids’, plural. Speechless, Remus followed the nurse down the squeaky green lino corridor, onto a ward with six or eight beds in it. She led him to the far window, where light poured in. “Hope, my love, you’ve got a visitor! Your boy’s come up to see you, isn’t that nice?”  

他没有时间对这个最新的发现感到震惊，霍普竟然有“孩子们”，复数。雷木斯无言地跟着护士走过发出吱吱声的绿色塑料地板，来到一个有六或八张床的病房。她把他带到远处的窗边，光线洒进来。“霍普，我的爱，你有一个访客！你的孩子来见你了，不是很好吗？”

 

The nurse ushered him in, and he stood at the end of the bed, helplessly. The woman lying in the bed looked as though she had been dozing, though she was propped up in a half-sitting position. She was blinking now, disoriented, and frowned slightly at the nurse.  

护士把他引进房间，他站在床尾，无助地看着。躺在床上的女人看起来像是刚刚打了个盹，虽然她半坐着。她现在在眨眼，迷茫地皱着眉头看着护士。

 

“Who?” She spoke in a quiet, hoarse voice, still confused until her dark eyes landed on Remus. Her pale eyebrows shot up. “Oh.” She said.  

“谁？”她用沙哑的声音问，直到她的黑色眼睛落在雷木斯身上。她的苍白眉毛立刻抬起。“哦。”她说道。

 

“Hello.” He waved, feeling stupid.  

“你好。”他挥了挥手，感觉自己很愚蠢。

 

“I’ll give you two some privacy,” the nurse was saying now, drawing the pale hospital curtains around the bed, “Can I get anyone a cup of tea?”  

“我给你们俩留些隐私，”护士一边说着，一边拉上了床周围的淡色窗帘，“我可以给你们拿杯茶吗？”

 

“No thank you.” They both replied, still staring at each other.  

“不，谢谢。”他们俩回答道，仍然盯着彼此。

 

She was very small, and very frail. Skeletal, even; her bones and tendons showing through the skin. She looked much older than Remus had imagined; but perhaps that was just the illness. Her face was sunken, and had a morbid, skull-like quality. He remembered how lovely she’d looked in her photograph, and how pretty she might still be, if she was well.  

她非常小，且非常脆弱。甚至可以说是骨瘦如柴；她的骨头和肌腱从皮肤下显现出来。她看起来比雷木斯想象的要老得多；但也许这只是疾病的缘故。她的脸凹陷了，有一种病态的、骷髅般的特质。他记得她在照片中的模样是多么美丽，以及如果她健康的话，可能还会有多么漂亮。

 

More alert now, her watery black eyes stared up at him, with an almost greedy glint; as if she was absorbing every inch of his gangly frame. He stood still, and let her.  

现在她变得更加警觉，她那水汪汪的黑眼睛盯着他，好像她要吸收他每一寸瘦长的身体。他站着不动，让她看。

 

“Oh,” she whispered, hoarsely. Her eyes filled with tears. “Oh, you look just like him.”  

“哦，”她喃喃道，声音沙哑。她的眼睛充满了泪水。“哦，你真像他。”

 

So this was his mother. He looked down at her and felt nothing at all.  

这就是他的母亲。他低头看着她，却什么也没有感觉。

 

He cleared his throat,  

他清了清喉咙，

 

“I got your letter.” He didn’t know what else to say. He wished he hadn’t come at all.  

“我收到了你的信。”他不知道还该说些什么。他希望自己根本没来过。

 

“You didn’t have to come.” She replied, softly. “I didn’t dare ask you to. But I did want to see you. I’ve wanted to see you… for years.” She closed her eyes and the tears ran tracks down her thin face.  

“你不必来。”她轻声说道。“我不敢让你来。但我确实想见你。我想见你……已经很多年了。”她闭上了眼睛，泪水沿着她瘦削的脸颊流下。

 

He bit his tongue. All sorts of foul, nasty things boiled in his throat, wanting to be spoken. But what use was it? She was clearly dying, he could smell it on her. Angry words would make no difference. She spoke again. “You’re at Hogwarts?”  

他咬了咬嘴唇。各种恶心的、让人厌恶的东西在他喉咙里翻腾，想要说出来。但有什么用呢？她显然已经快死了，他能闻到她身上的气味。愤怒的话语毫无意义。她再次开口问道：“你在霍格沃茨吗？”

 

“Yeah,” he nodded. “Final year.”  

“是的，”他点头道。“最后一年。”

“He’d be so pleased. Lyall. Your father.”  

“他会很高兴的。莱尔。你的父亲。”

Silence again. Remus didn’t want to look at her for too long. She looked so sad, so very weak and sick. “Is there anything you want to ask me?”  

再次陷入沉默。雷木斯不想长时间看着她。她看起来如此悲伤，如此虚弱和生病。“你有什么想问我的吗？”

Remus shrugged. This was more horrible than he could have imagined. She laughed, softly,  

雷木斯耸耸肩。这比他想象的更糟糕。她轻声笑了笑，

“You won’t hurt my feelings, you know. This might be your only chance.”  

“你不会伤害我的感情的，你知道的。这可能是你唯一的机会。”

She swallowed, when he still did not speak. “All right then, I’ll just tell you. I’m sorry for what I did. I’m not proud. I loved your father more than… well, I loved him with all of my heart. He was everything to me, I wish you could have known him. When you were hurt, and he died… I just didn’t know what to do. I was so young, I was alone. I hadn’t seen my own family in years, and I didn’t even know the neighbours because Lyall said we had to keep things secret.”  

她吞了吞口水，当他仍然没有说话时。“好了，我就告诉你。我为我所做的事感到抱歉。我不骄傲。我比任何事都更爱你的父亲……我全心全意地爱他。他对我来说是一切，我希望你能认识他。当你受伤了，他去世了……我真不知道该怎么办。我还很年轻，我一个人。我已经多年没见到自己的家人了，也根本不认识邻居，因为莱尔说我们必须保密。”

 

She was Welsh, he recognised the accent now. The way she spoke his father’s name in two gentle syllables - Ly-all. He felt stupid for not realising, seeing as they were in Cardiff, but still. No one had ever told him she was Welsh. He supposed it wasn’t pertinent information to anyone but him.  

她是威尔士人，他现在识别出了口音。她用两个轻 柔的音节来念他父亲的名字——莱·尔。他觉得自己很愚蠢，因为他们在加的夫，但仍然没有意识到这一点。没有人告诉过他她是威尔士人。他想这可能对除了他以外的任何人都不重要。

“Look,” he said, “It’s fine, you don’t have to explain.”  

“看，”他说，“没关系，你不必解释。”

 

“I’ve thought about you,” she said, desperately, “Every day. My boy, my poor little boy.”  

“我一直在想你，”她绝望地说，“每天。我孩子，我可怜的小宝贝。”

 

“Don’t.” He said, feeling uncomfortable - frightened, even. “It’s ok, please don’t…”  

“不要。”他说，感到不安——甚至有些害怕。“没事的，请不要……”

 

He sat down in the stiff backed hospital chair beside her. He didn’t reach for her, or hold her hand, that felt like too much.  

他坐在她旁边那张僵硬靠背的医院椅子上。他没有伸手去碰她，也没有握她的手，这感觉太过了。

 

“I thought it was the best thing,” she wept, the tears tickling down into the pillow she lay on, “I couldn’t have looked after you, you were so strong, even when you were that small. I had to lock you up, you were so frightened and you were crying for me and I couldn’t go in…”  

“我觉得这是最好的办法，”她哭泣着，眼泪滴落在她躺着的枕头上，“我不能照顾你，你那么坚强，即使你那么小。我不得不把你锁起来，你那么害怕，你在哭着叫我，我却不能进去……”

 

He felt as if a heavy block of ice had settled in the pit of his stomach. He just wanted her to stop talking, he didn’t want to hear this,  

他感觉像是一块沉重的冰块沉在了胃底。他只想让她停止说话，他不想听这些，

 

“You did the right thing.” He said, “You did. You did everything you could, I never blamed you.”  

“你做对了。”他说，“你做对了。你做了你能做的一切，我从未责怪过你。”

 

That was true. He’d blamed his father over and over again in his head, hated him fiercely for years. But he had somehow felt more sympathy for his mother, a muggle who was left just as much at sea by Lyall’s death as he was.  

这是真的。他在脑海中一再责怪父亲，多年来对他充满了强烈的仇恨。但他对母亲的同情却更深，她是个麻瓜，像他一样对莱尔的死感到茫然。

 

“Does it still… happen?” She asked, her eyes big. They were the same greeny brown as his own. He nodded,  

“现在还会……发生吗？”她问，眼睛睁得大大的。她的眼睛和他的相似。雷木斯点了点头，

 

“It’s not as bad,” he lied, “I have help. It’s safer.”  

“没那么糟糕了，”他撒谎道，“我有帮助。更安全了。”

 

She looked relieved, which made him happy.  

她看起来松了口气，这让他感到高兴。

 

“And school? I bet you’re as clever as your dad!”  

“那学校呢？我敢打赌你和你父亲一样聪明！”

 

“I like school,” he said, “I do pretty well.” He wasn’t sure what else to say about it, “I er… I have his wand. Lyall’s.”  

“我喜欢学校，”他说，“我做得很好。”他不确定还能说些什么，“那个，我……我有他的魔杖。莱尔的。”

 

She smiled, paper white thin stretching over her hollow face, like a skull.  

她微笑了，纸一样白的笑容拉伸在她凹陷的脸上，像骷髅。

 

“And do you… have someone? In your life, looking after you?”  

“那你……有谁吗？在你的生活中，照顾你的人？”

 

“I…” He thought Lily and James, and Peter and Grant, and Madam Pomfrey, and Mary and Marlene, and even Professor McGonagall. And Sirius. “Yeah, I do. I have friends.”  

“我……”他想到莉莉和詹姆斯，还有彼得和格兰特，麦格教授，玛丽和玛琳，甚至是教授。还有天狼星。“是的，我有。我有朋友。”

 

He glanced at the record player on her bedside table, and the little pile of records on the chair. The Beatles, Cliff Richard, The Kinks. “Are these yours?” He asked, genuinely curious for the first time.  

他瞥了一眼她床头桌上的唱片机，还有椅子上的那一小堆唱片。《披头士》、《克里夫·理查德》、《金斯》。 “这些是你的吗？”他第一次真正好奇地问道。

 

“Oh yes,” she nodded, “Love a bit of a dance, I do. Lyall was the reader, but I’m happiest with a nice pop song. He used to tease me.”  

“哦，是的，”她点头道，“我喜欢跳舞。莱尔是读书的，但我最喜欢的是听流行歌曲。他常常取笑我。”

 

Her accent was lovely, a sweet, friendly up and down. He was glad she wasn’t posh; he hoped he didn’t sound too common for her.  

她的口音很可爱，甜美友善地上下起伏。他很高兴她并不高傲；他希望自己说话的方式不会显得太普通。

 

“I like music too.” He said, softly. He couldn’t bring himself to raise his voice, but she didn’t mind. “David Bowie, mostly.”  

“我也喜欢音乐。”他说，声音很柔和。他没有勇气提高声音，但她并不介意。“大卫·鲍伊，主要是。”

 

“You must take after me,” she said, sleepily, still smiling. “My bouncy little boy. I used to set you down on the rug while I did the housework, and play my records and you’d jump around on your bottom and wriggle like you were dancing. Love Me Do was playing on the radio when you took your first steps.”  

“你一定像我，”她困倦地说，仍然微笑着。“我那活泼的小宝贝。我过去做家务时会把你放在地毯上，放我的唱片，你会在地上跳来跳去，像是在跳舞。你第一次走路时收音机里放着《Love Me Do》。”

 

She’d grown tearful, saying all this, her eyes had welled up.  

她说这些话时已经泪水盈眶。

 

“I think I remember,” he said, quickly – it was a lie, but it would make her happy. He didn’t want her to be this sad, not for his sake. Without thinking, he reached out and took her hand, gently, as if she might shatter. It was a very little hand – she was a very little woman. “I love the Beatles,” he said, “Always have.”  

“我想我记得，”他说，迅速地——这是一个谎言，但这会让她开心。他不希望她因他而如此伤心。在没有思考的情况下，他伸出手，轻轻握住她的手，仿佛她会破碎。这是一只非常小的手——她是个非常小的女人。“我喜欢披头士，”他说，“一直都喜欢。”

 

She beamed. Even through the hollow cheeks and dark eyes of her illness, she had a lovely smile. Hope squeezed her son’s hand and smiled up at him, and they were comfortable like that for quite some time. Remus felt the stirring of something towards her – something warm and old and familiar.  

她露出了笑容。即使在她生病的凹陷脸颊和黑眼睛中，她也有着美丽的微笑。霍普握住儿子的手，抬头对他微笑，他们就这样舒适地待了一段时间。雷木斯感受到了一种温暖、古老而熟悉的情感在她身上涌动。

 

Eventually he offered to put some music on for her.  

最终，他提议为她放点音乐。

 

“Oh, the player’s broken.” She replied.  

“哦，播放器坏了。”她回答道。

 

“Really? Let me see…” Remus fumbled in his pocket for his wand, and gave the black wooden box a tap. He did it without letting go of her hand, and she made a small sound of delight and pride, seeing him use magic.  

“真的？让我看看……”雷木斯在口袋里摸索他的魔杖，轻轻敲了敲那个黑色木箱。他在没有放开她的手的情况下做了这个动作，她看到他施展魔法时发出了小小的愉悦和自豪的声音。

 

The record began to turn, and the sound which came out was clear and lovely. It was a Fairport Convention record; Remus had never bothered with them much before; too hippie for him. But she smiled as Sandy Denny’s larksong voice began to fill the room. So he listened.  

唱片开始转动，发出的声音清晰而美妙。这是一张Fairport Convention的唱片；雷木斯以前从未太在意这些；对他来说太嬉皮了。但她微笑着，当桑迪·丹尼的燕雀歌声开始充满房间时。他于是静静地听着。

Across the evening sky, all the birds are leaving

But how can they know it's time for them to go?

Before the winter fire, I will still be dreaming.

I have no thought of time.

For who knows where the time goes?

Who knows where the time goes?

 

They both sat listening quietly to the music, and Remus saw that he got some of his shyness from her, maybe. She never held eye contact too long, and never pushed him into talking. Remus had a sense that they could sit in contented silence like that for hours, and understand each other just as well as if they’d done nothing but talk.  

他们两个静静地坐着听音乐，雷木斯发现自己或许继承了她的一些羞怯。她从不长时间保持眼神接触，也从不逼他开口。雷木斯有种感觉，他们可以这样心满意足地静坐几个小时，彼此了解得和他们一直交谈一样好。

 

In a little while, the nurse came back. It was already after visiting hours, she said, and Matron would be on her case. Remus didn’t want to go, and Hope didn’t want him to leave.  

不久之后，护士回来了。她说已经过了探视时间，护士长会找她麻烦。雷木斯不想离开，霍普也不想让他走。

 

“Will you come back?” She pleaded, turning weepy again.  

“你会回来吗？”她恳求道，再次变得泪水盈眶。

 

“I will.” He promised. “As soon as I can, I will.”  

“我会的。”他承诺道。“只要我能，就会回来的。”

 

She pulled his hand to her lips. She was very weak, but he let her. She kissed his scarred knuckles.  

她把他的手拉到嘴唇上。她非常虚弱，但他让她这样做。她吻了他伤痕累累的指关节。

 

“I love you, my darling.”  

“我爱你，我的亲爱的。”

 

Something inside him broke when he realised he couldn’t say it back. He didn’t know how to say it and mean it.  

当他意识到自己不能回应时，内心有种东西崩溃了。他不知道怎么说出这句话并且真心实意。

 

“I’ll see you soon.” He promised again, hoping she didn’t mind too much.  

“我很快会再见到你。”他再次承诺，希望她不要太在意。

 

He left the room in a daze, and it was a miracle he managed to get out of the hospital at all. It must have taken twice as long as it took him to get in.  

他恍惚地离开了房间，能够顺利离开医院简直是一个奇迹。他离开医院的时间肯定是进来的两倍长。

 

Outside, it had grown dark. Lily was sitting on a bench, with a big black dog at her side. She stood up, the street light behind her illuminating her hair, seeming to set it alight; a halogen halo.  

外面已经变暗了。莉莉坐在长椅上，旁边有一只大黑狗。她站了起来，身后的路灯照亮了她的头发，仿佛点燃了一圈氙气灯光环。

 

“Alright, Moony?” She asked, eyes serious.  

“怎么样，月亮？”她问，眼神严肃。

He shrugged, speechless. Instantly, Lily stepped forward and wound her arms around his waist, laying her head against his chest and squeezing. He wrapped his arms around her, gratefully, and hugged her back, bowing his head to inhale the lovely apple skin smell of her. He was crying, and Sirius was right there, but he didn’t care, he just let Lily keep squeezing him, feeling as if she was holding him together. He could hear Padfoot whining and panting. Finally, he broke away, rubbing his eyes.  

他耸了耸肩，无法言语。莉莉立即向前一步，将双臂绕在他的腰间，把头靠在他的胸前，紧紧拥抱着他。他感激地环抱着她，低下头吸入她身上那迷人的苹果香味。他在哭泣，而天狼星就在旁边，但他并不在意，他只是让莉莉继续抱着他，感觉她像是在把他拼凑在一起。他能听到帕德弗特的呜咽和喘息声。最后，他抽身而退，擦了擦眼睛。

“Sorry,” he said, bashfully.  

“对不起，”他说，腼腆地。

“Don’t be stupid,” she squeezed his arm, her own sea green eyes shimmering. “Want to go home?”  

“别傻了，”她捏了捏他的手臂，自己海洋般绿色的眼睛闪闪发光。“想回家吗？”

“Actually,” Remus sniffed, “I want to get really, really pissed.”  

“其实，”雷木斯抽噎道，“我想喝得酩酊大醉。”

Padfoot barked.  

 

帕德弗特叫了起来。

The poem is 'This Is The Verse' by Philip Larkin.

The song is 'Who knows where the time goes' by Sandy Denny.

“Right. Pub, then?” Lily said, business-like once more. “I think we’d better go back to Hogsmeade, don’t you? I don’t fancy our chances apparating back to Scotland drunk…”  

“那好，去酒吧吧？”莉莉再次以商业化的口吻说道。“我想我们最好还是回霍格斯米德去吧，你不觉得？我不太敢冒险喝醉了再回苏格兰……”

“Yeah, good plan,” Remus nodded, wiping his nose on his sleeve, still sniffing. “...where’s James?”  

“嗯，好主意，”雷木斯点头道，擦了擦袖子上的鼻子，仍在抽噎。“……詹姆斯在哪儿？”

“Well we realised that it was going to look really suspicious if both the head boy and the head girl were missing,” Lily laughed. “So he went back to cover for us. He um… he sent Sirius. We both thought…”  

“嗯，我们意识到如果两个学生会主席都不在会显得很可疑，”莉莉笑道。“所以他回去掩饰了我们的缺席。他呃……他派了天狼星过来。我们都觉得……”

“It’s ok.” Remus nodded. He finally turned to address the dog, sitting patiently by. “Sirius?”  

“没事的。”雷木斯点头道。他终于转过身去面对那只耐心坐着的狗。“天狼星？”

 

He transformed back at once, and stood there looking awkward, rubbing one arm with the other.  

他立刻变回了人形，站在那里显得有些尴尬，一只手臂揉着另一只。

 

“Hello, Moony.” He said, softly.  

“你好，月亮。”他说，声音柔和。

 

“Hi.” Remus nodded back, suddenly very shy.  

“嗨。”雷木斯点了点头，突然感到非常羞涩。

 

“Oh, Remus, I forgot!” Lily broke the atmosphere. She handed him a small square cardboard box. A carton of Silk Cut. “James’s idea,” she shrugged.  

“哦，雷木斯，我忘了！”莉莉打破了沉默。她递给他一个小方形纸盒，一包丝绸切割烟。“这是詹姆斯的主意，”她耸了耸肩。

 

“Life saver, thanks!” Remus accepted them gratefully.  

“救命恩人，谢谢！”雷木斯感激地接受了。

“其实，我最好去联系一下他，”莉莉继续说道，瞥了一眼两个男孩。“天狼星，把镜子给我？我去告诉他在哪里见面。”

 

Sirius handed her the compact, and she smiled at them both, before walking a little ways away - so that she was just out of earshot.  

天狼星把镜子递给她，她对他们俩微笑了一下，然后走开了几步——让她离开了耳朵的听力范围。

 

Remus sat down on the bench, opening the box of fags with his teeth, then pulling one out. He held it up to Sirius,  

雷木斯坐在长椅上，用牙齿打开了烟盒，然后拿出一根。他把烟递给天狼星，

“给我点燃它好吗？我这么紧张，它可能会在我脸上炸开。”

 

Sirius clicked his fingers, and the cylinder lit. Remus sucked on it appreciatively. Sirius sat next to him.  

天狼星打了个响指，香烟点燃了。雷木斯欣赏地吸了一口。天狼星坐在他旁边。

 

“Moony I’m--”  

“月亮，我——”

 

“Sirius--”  

“天狼星——”

 

They both tried to speak at once, then smiled at each other timidly.  

他们都试图同时说话，然后害羞地相视而笑。

 

“Sirius.” Remus said, “I’m sorry. I was a twat.”  

“天狼星。”雷木斯说，“对不起。我真是个蠢货。”

 

“You were.” Sirius nodded, taking a cigarette of his own. “But you weren’t completely wrong.”  

“你是。”天狼星点头道，抽出了一根烟。“但你并非完全错了。”

 

“Nor were you.” Remus sighed. “I dunno what’s wrong with me.”  

“你也不是。”雷木斯叹了口气。“我不知道我怎么了。”

 

“There’s nothing wrong with you, Remus.” Sirius touched his knee, gently, looking him in the eye. He was in muggle clothes, which was a nice change, Remus thought. Black jeans and his black leather jacket. Remus smiled.  

“你没有问题，雷木斯。”天狼星轻轻地摸了摸他的膝盖，直视着他的眼睛。他穿着麻瓜衣服，雷木斯觉得这是个不错的变化。黑色牛仔裤和黑色皮夹克。雷木斯笑了。

 

“You look really good.”  

“你看起来真不错。”

 

“So what else is new.” Sirius stuck out his tongue. He turned solemn again, “I couldn’t believe it when Prongs told me about the letter. I felt like shit for shouting at you, I just wanted to make sure you were ok, then he said you’d gone...”  

“那有什么新鲜事。”天狼星吐了吐舌头。他又变得严肃了，“当詹姆斯告诉我关于那封信的事时，我简直不敢相信。我为对你大喊大叫感到很糟糕，我只是想确保你没事，然后他说你走了……”

 

“Sorry,” Remus replied. “I just had to get here straight away, I didn’t even think.”  

“对不起，”雷木斯回答道。“我只是必须立刻到这里，我甚至没来得及考虑。”

 

“I wouldn’t have, either.” Sirius admitted. “Though, actually, I dunno if I would exactly rush to my mother’s bedside.”  

“我也不会。”天狼星承认道。“不过，实际上，我不知道我是否会急着去我母亲的床前。”

 

Remus snorted, half-heartedly, and they were both quiet for a bit, thinking about their mothers.  

雷木斯半心半意地哼了一声，他们都沉默了一会儿，想着他们的母亲。

 

“What’s she like?” Sirius asked, finally.  

“她是什么样的？”天狼星终于问道。

 

Remus considered this carefully before answering. He tried to recall her voice, her eyes, the way her hand felt in his.  

雷木斯仔细考虑了一下才回答。他试图回忆她的声音，她的眼睛，她的手在他手中的感觉。

 

“She’s nice.” He said. “I think I like her.”  

“她很好。”他说。“我觉得我喜欢她。”

 

“All right, you two, ready?” Lily returned, obviously having judged them suitably made up.  

“好了，你们俩，准备好了吗？”莉莉回来了，显然她认为他们已经准备好了。

 

“Yeah,” they both replied, smiling.  

 

“嗯，”他们都回答道，微笑着。

* * *

They ended up in the Three Broomsticks, all five of them—James had brought Peter down from the castle with him. Three firewhiskies in, and Remus was feeling pleasantly warm and loose, grinning dopily as his friends made a racket for his benefit.  

他们最终来到了“三把扫帚”酒吧，五个人全到齐了——詹姆斯还带下了彼得。喝了三杯火威士忌，雷木斯感到暖洋洋的，脸上挂着傻笑，朋友们为他热闹地制造声响。

No one asked him any questions, which was perfect; they just drank, laughed, and talked like real teenagers for once.  

没人问他任何问题，这正合他的心意；他们只是喝酒、笑谈，像真正的青少年一样。

“This map is some of the best magic I’ve ever seen.” Lily marvelled, after studying it for some time. “And you only use it for pranks?!”  

“这个地图是我见过的最棒的魔法之一。”莉莉赞叹道，研究了一会儿。“你们只用它来搞恶作剧？！”

“What else would we use it for?” Sirius raised an eyebrow.  

“那还用来做什么呢？”天狼星挑了挑眉。

“You’ve even got the moving staircases!” Lily exclaimed, clearly delighted.  

“你们甚至连会移动的楼梯都有！”莉莉惊呼道，显然很高兴。

“That was one of mine.” Remus said, eagerly.  

“那是我做的。”雷木斯兴奋地说。

“It was all yours,” Sirius said, “The whole thing was your idea, Mr Moony.”  

“完全是你的主意，”天狼星说道，“整个地图都是你的创意，月亮先生。”

“Yeah, but you lot did loads of work on it…”  

“是的，但你们也做了很多工作……”

“What are you going to do with it at the end of the year?” Lily asked.  

“到年底你们打算怎么办？”莉莉问道。

The four boys looked at each other with a note of sadness. The map would no longer be useful to them if they weren't at Hogwarts. Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, and Prongs would no longer be Hogwarts’ premiere mischief makers. James shrugged,  

四个男孩互相看了一眼，带着一丝忧伤。如果他们不在霍格沃茨，地图就不再对他们有用。月亮、蠕虫、小天狼星和詹姆斯将不再是霍格沃茨的顶级恶作剧制造者。詹姆斯耸了耸肩，

“Pass it on, I s’pose? Maybe to someone in the co-operative.”  

“我想只能转交给别人了？也许交给合作社里的人。”

Remus hated that idea and finished his fourth drink.  

雷木斯讨厌这个主意，喝完了他的第四杯酒。

“Rosmerta!” Sirius called out, raising a hand, “Another round, darling?”  

“罗斯梅塔！”天狼星喊道，举起手，“再来一轮，亲爱的？”

“Right you are my love…” she called back.  

“好的，我的爱……”她回道。

“Flirt.” Remus nudged him under the table.  

“花言巧语。”雷木斯在桌子下碰了碰他。

“I’m trying to get you drunk.” Sirius replied, piously, “As requested.”  

“我在努力让你喝醉。”天狼星庄严地回答道，“正如你所要求的。”

“I’m already drunk,” Lily slurred, blinking hard. “I don’t know how I’m going to walk back to school…”  

“我已经喝醉了，”莉莉含糊地说，努力眨眼。“我不知道怎么回学校……”

“I’ll carry you.” James said, valiantly, though he was clearly starting to get a bit wobbly himself.  

“我会抱着你回去。”詹姆斯英勇地说，尽管他自己显然也开始有点晃了。

“I don’t want it to be over.” Peter said, morosely.  

“我不想结束。”彼得忧郁地说道。

“Calm down, Wormy, we’re not going back yet.” Sirius said, as Rosmerta appeared with a tray of drinks. Remus grabbed another firewhisky and knocked it back. He liked the burn; it felt like it was working.  

“别激动，蠕虫，我们还没有回去。”天狼星说道，罗斯梅塔端着酒托出现了。雷木斯拿了一杯火威士忌，喝了下去。他喜欢那种烧灼感；感觉有效果。

“I don’t mean tonight.” Peter said, clumsily slamming his chubby fist on the table, “I mean school, I mean everything.”  

“我不是说今晚。”彼得笨拙地把胖乎乎的拳头重重地拍在桌子上，“我是说学校，我是说一切。”

“School isn’t everything.” Lily patted him gently.  

“学校不是一切。”莉莉轻轻拍了拍他。

“No.” He sighed, “But it’s all going to change, isn’t it? We won’t see each other all the time, we’ll all have jobs.”  

“不。”他叹了口气，“但一切都会改变，对吧？我们不会一直见面，我们都会有工作。”

“Speak for yourself,” Sirius laughed, “Some of us are independently wealthy. Anyway, of course we’ll see each other every day, idiot, we’re all moving in together!”  

“你说说你自己，”天狼星笑道，“我们中有些人是独立富裕的。无论如何，我们当然每天都会见面，傻瓜，我们都会一起住！”

Lily and James looked at each other, suddenly sober. Sirius's eyes narrowed, “What?”  

莉莉和詹姆斯对视了一下，突然清醒了过来。天狼星的眼睛眯了起来，“怎么了？”

“Mate,” James said, awkwardly, “Er. Lily and I have been talking about… maybe getting a flat together, after the summer.”  

“伙计，”詹姆斯尴尬地说，“呃。莉莉和我谈过……也许暑假后租个公寓住。”

“Yeah,” Sirius nodded, “We’ll all move in, and--”  

“是的，”天狼星点头道，“我们都会一起住，然后——”

“Padfoot,” Remus touched his knee, “He means just the two of them.”  

“天狼星，”雷木斯摸了摸他的膝盖，“他是说只有他们两个。”

“What? Why?!”  

“什么？为什么？！”

“Let’s not talk about this now!” Lily said, hurriedly, “Nothing’s decided!”  

“我们现在别谈这个！”莉莉匆忙说，“什么都还没决定！”

But everyone could see that it was.  

但每个人都能看出来，事情已经决定了。

“What about this prank, then?” James said, still eyeing Sirius, “What are we going to do if no one comes up with anything good?”  

“那这个恶作剧呢？”詹姆斯说，仍盯着天狼星，“如果没人想出什么好的点子怎么办？”

“We will,” Remus said, “There’s time. Is it me or is the mass-levitation idea starting to sound good?”  

“我们会想出来的，”雷木斯说，“还有时间。难道只有我觉得大规模升空的点子开始听起来不错吗？”

“Oh good, you are drunk.” Sirius smirked, “How the fuck are we supposed to levitate two hundred students? And why would we?”  

“哦，好吧，你确实喝醉了。”天狼星笑道，“我们怎么可能让两百个学生悬浮起来？而且我们为什么要这么做？”

“Be funny.” Remus shrugged, then giggled. Everything seemed like it would be funny, right then.  

“会很好笑。”雷木斯耸了耸肩，然后咯咯笑了。那时一切都显得很有趣。

“There are enough of us,” James said, “If everyone concentrates, we could easily levitate them all.”  

“我们人够多，”詹姆斯说，“如果大家集中精力，我们可以很容易地把他们都升空。”

“And do what with them?! Practical jokes need a practical element!” Sirius insisted. Everyone else burst out laughing at him. He shook his head disdainfully and took a swig of his butterbeer.  

“那我们要怎么做？！恶作剧需要实际的元素！”天狼星坚持道。其他人都笑了起来。他不满地摇了摇头，喝了一口黄油啤酒。

“You’re not drinking?” Remus said, suddenly.  

“你不喝酒？”雷木斯突然问道。

“Er… no.” Sirius looked down, self-consciously. “Thought someone better stay responsible enough to get you lot back in one piece.”  

“呃……不。”天狼星低下头，自觉地说道。“觉得还是有人要负责把你们带回去

。”

“Ahhh,” Lily grinned dopily, “You do care, Black! You’re all soft and sensitive really, aren’t you?”  

“啊，”莉莉傻乎乎地笑道，“你真关心，天狼星！你实际上是个温柔敏感的人，不是吗？”

“I just don’t want anyone expelled before we can get this prank off the ground!”  

“我只是希望在我们搞恶作剧之前，没人被开除！”

“Off the ground! So you agree with the levitation idea!” James cackled.  

“搞起来！所以你同意升空的主意！”詹姆斯咯咯笑道。

“Oh for goodness’ sake…” Sirius rolled his eyes. “I’m going to the loo.” He got up and left them laughing.  

“天哪……”天狼星翻了个白眼。“我去趟洗手间。”他站起身，离开了他们的笑声。

Remus took the opportunity to pop out for a cigarette. He could have smoked in the pub and thought that Lily and James might even let him get away with it, but he wanted a minute to himself. Outside was nice and cool, the air felt clean. He lit up and started puffing away, wrapping his arms around himself against the chill. He was really drunk. He had to lean against the wall just to stay up. It was nice; he didn’t have to worry about anything if he was drunk. No one would expect him to.  

雷木斯趁机出去抽烟。他本可以在酒吧里抽烟，莉莉和詹姆斯可能甚至会让他这样做，但他想要独处一会儿。外面的空气很清新，凉爽的微风让人感到舒服。他点燃了香烟，开始抽着，双臂抱着自己以抵御寒冷。他真的喝醉了。他不得不靠在墙上才能站稳。这样很好；他不必担心任何事，因为他喝醉了。没有人会对他有任何期待。

He leaned his head back against the wall, catching sight of the pale crescent moon glowing through the scudding clouds. He thought about Livia, as he often did when he saw the moon. And Castor. He thought about their warning and how it had been so meaningless, in the end. Why was that? Remus’s whisky-addled mind hit on something—something he hadn’t thought about before. But as soon as it was there, it was gone again. He shook his head, dazedly.  

他靠在墙上，抬头看到那弯弯的月牙在云层中闪烁。他想起了莉维亚，就像他每次看到月亮时常常会想的那样。还有卡斯托。他想起了他们的警告，最终感觉如此无意义。这是为什么？雷木斯酒醉的思绪闪过一个念头——一个他之前从未想过的念头。但它刚一出现，又立刻消失了。他迷茫地摇了摇头。

“All right?” Sirius came out and joined him.  

“怎么样？”天狼星走出来，加入了他。

“Mmm.” Remus nodded, smiling widely.  

“嗯。”雷木斯点头，笑得很开怀。

“Pisshead.” Sirius smirked.  

“醉鬼。”天狼星笑道。

“Oi!” Remus shot back playfully, “I can hold my drink, ffffank you very much. Unlike some.”  

“喂！”雷木斯调皮地回击道，“我能喝酒，谢谢你。不像某些人。”

“Oh yeah?” Sirius humoured him, leaning against the wall too. He took Remus’s hand and laced their fingers together.  

“哦，是吗？”天狼星逗他，靠在墙上。他握住雷木斯的手，把他们的手指交织在一起。

“Yeah,” Remus nodded emphatically, “Remember my fifteenth? You and Pete got so wankered, you threw up in the tunnel.”  

“是的，”雷木斯郑重其事地说，“记得我十五岁那年吗？你和彼得喝得酩酊大醉，把隧道弄得一团糟。”

“Godric, how could I forget,” Sirius laughed. “Horrific.”  

“神秘神，怎么可能忘记，”天狼星笑道。“太可怕了。”

“Nahh,” Remus sighed happily, squeezing Sirius’s fingers. “It was nice. You fell asleep on my shoulder and told me I was magic.”  

“不，”雷木斯幸福地叹了口气，握紧天狼星的手指。“那时很温馨。你在我肩上睡着了，还告诉我我是魔法。”

“Did I?”  

“我说了吗？”

“You did.”  

“你说了。”

“That does sound nice. I must have been very drunk.” He laughed, “Not that I don’t think you’re magic, Moony.”  

“这听起来确实很不错。我一定是喝醉了。”他笑道，“不是我不觉得你是魔法，月亮。”

Remus’s mind had drifted, though. His cigarette had gone out, and he dropped it.  

不过雷木斯的思绪已经飘远。他的香烟熄灭了，他扔掉了它。

“Wish I could say stuff like that.”  

“真希望我能说这样的话。”

“Like what?” Sirius frowned.  

“像什么？”天狼星皱起了眉头。

“Nice stuff.”  

“那些好听的话。”

“You say lots of nice stuff, Moony.”  

“你说了很多好听的话，月亮。”

Remus shook his head, frowning. It was no good.  

雷木斯摇了摇头，皱着眉头。这样不行。

“Need another drink.”  

“需要再喝一杯。”

“Ok, come on then…”  

“好的，来吧……”

Inside, Peter was half asleep, propped up on his elbow, and Lily was sitting in James's lap. She seemed to be trying to locate his tonsils with her tongue.  

里面，彼得半睡着了，靠在手肘上，莉莉坐在詹姆斯的腿上。她似乎在用舌头寻找他的扁桃体。

“Bloody hell.” Sirius groaned, “Give it a rest, you two.”  

“该死的。”天狼星抱怨道，“你们俩休息一下吧。”

Remus sniggered, finishing the last of his whisky. That was better.  

雷木斯咯咯笑着，喝完了最后一杯威士忌。感觉好多了。

“You can talk!” Lily poked her pink tongue out at him. “Marlene told me she caught you two snogging in the corridor the other night!”  

“你也有资格说！”莉莉吐出粉红色的舌头对他说。“玛琳告诉我她看到你们俩在走廊里亲吻了！”

“So what if she did?” Sirius replied primly, “It was private enough until she showed up.”  

“那又怎样？”天狼星正经地回答道，“直到她出现之前，这都很私密。”

“Christopher was there,” Remus put in. Lily laughed and pointed at Sirius,  

“克里斯托弗也在那儿，”雷木斯插话道。莉莉笑了，指着天狼星，

“Ha! Exhibitionist!”  

“哈！爱显摆的！”

“She’s right.” Remus nodded drunkenly, “You are. Remember I caught you with Mary all the time when I was a prefect.”  

“她说得对。”雷木斯醉醺醺地点头，“你确实是。记得我当监控的时候总是抓到你和玛丽在一起。”

“Oh well, that was Mary, you know what Mary’s like…”  

“哦，那是玛丽，你知道玛丽是什么样的……”

“Remus!” Lily said, still giggling and quite pink in the face now, “You won’t believe what Mary told me about you last year!”  

“雷木斯！”莉莉说道，仍在咯咯笑，脸颊变得相当红，“你不会相信玛丽去年告诉我的事！”

“What?”  

“什么事？”

“It was before you came out, so you’d think she’d admit it was made up by now, but she told me and Marlene that you and she… you know…”  

“那是在你出柜之前，你会认为她现在会承认是编造的，但她告诉我和玛琳，她和你……你知道的……”

“Made sweet heterosexual love?” Sirius supplied, barely stifling his own laughter now.  

“做了甜蜜的异性恋爱？”天狼星补充道，几乎忍不住自己的笑声。

“Oh!” Remus said, “Yeah, that’s true, actually.”  

“哦！”雷木斯说，“是的，其实是真的。”

“What?!” Lily stared at him, her mouth open.  

“什么？！”莉莉瞪大了眼睛，嘴巴张开。

“Ages ago…”  

“很久以前……”

“Last year, actually.” Sirius corrected. “It’s fine, Lily, he only did it to make me jealous.”

“实际上是去年。”天狼星纠正道。“没关系，莉莉，他这么做只是为了让我嫉妒。”

“Arrogant prick.” Remus snorted.  

“自大混蛋。”雷木斯哼了一声。

Peter began to snore. James looked at him, then at his pocket watch,  

彼得开始打鼾。詹姆斯看了看他，然后看了看他的怀表，

“Reckon we’d better head back?”  

“我们最好还是回去吧？”

 

* * *

 

Remus insisted on finishing not only his drink, but everyone else’s before they left. He wanted to be good and drunk, so that he would fall straight to sleep, without any of the intrusive thoughts that had been plaguing him since Marlene’s return. Plus, though he wasn’t going to tell Sirius, his hip didn’t hurt as much with all that liquor in his blood.  

雷木斯坚持不仅要喝完自己的酒，还要喝完其他人的酒才离开。他想要彻底醉倒，这样他才会直接睡去，不会被自玛琳回归以来困扰他的侵扰性思绪打扰。而且，虽然他不打算告诉天狼星，他的髋部在这些酒精的影响下感觉不那么疼了。

 

James was true to his word, and gave Lily a piggyback all the way to Honeyduke’s. Remus looked at Sirius with a quirked eyebrow. The other boy laughed,  

詹姆斯言出必行，把莉莉背到霍尼杜克的糖果店。雷木斯用挑起的眉毛看着天狼星。另一个男孩笑了，

 

“I’ll levitate you, if you want, but I am not carrying you.”  

“如果你愿意，我可以让你漂浮起来，但我不打算背着你。”

 

“Who says romance is dead,” Peter yawned, rubbing his eyes and trailing along beside them.  

“谁说浪漫已经死了，”彼得打了个哈欠，揉着眼睛，跟在他们身边。

 

By the time they were descending the steps into the cellar of the sweet shop, Remus was feeling a lot less cheerful about the whole thing. Perhaps the last few whiskies had been a bad idea. His head was starting to throb painfully, and his vision was swimming. His limbs felt heavy, and as they sank into the darkness of the tunnel, he quite fancied just curling up to sleep right there.  

当他们下楼到达糖果店的地窖时，雷木斯对整个事情的感觉变得不那么愉快了。也许最后几杯威士忌是个坏主意。他的头开始剧烈地疼痛，视线模糊。他的四肢感到沉重，当他们沉入隧道的黑暗中时，他很想就在那儿蜷缩起来睡觉。

 

“No one’ll miss us,” he mumbled as Sirius gently pulled him along, “S’a weekend tomorrow.”  

“没人会想念我们的，”他喃喃道，天狼星轻轻地拖着他，“明天是周末。”

 

“I really don’t think you’ll be happy waking up here, Moony,” Sirius chided gently. “Trust me.”  

“我真的不认为你会喜欢在这里醒来，月亮，”天狼星温柔地责备道。“相信我。”

 

“I trust you.” Remus replied, his mouth thick with saliva.  

“我相信你。”雷木斯回答道，嘴里满是唾液。

 

It was all right for Peter. He’d transformed into a rat and curled up to sleep in Lily’s pocket.  

彼得倒没问题。他变成了一只老鼠，蜷缩在莉莉的口袋里睡觉。

 

“He’s so good at that,” Sirius marvelled, “I can’t transform drunk.”  

“他在这方面真厉害，”天狼星惊叹道，“我喝醉了没法变身。”

她。”

Remus didn’t think he had ever hated fire whisky more. When he woke up the next morning his throat was raw, his limbs ached and his head was throbbing. He’d take a full moon over a hangover any day. At least after a full moon everyone was sympathetic.

Christ.  

天啊。

**On the fat lady’s corridor, Remus paused.**  

在胖夫人的走廊上，雷木斯停了下来。

 

**“You lot go on, I’ll just be a minute.” He stopped outside Professor McGonagall’s office door.**  

“你们继续，我马上就回来。”他在麦格教授的办公室门外停下了。

 

**Sirius glanced back and gave him a nod of understanding, before carrying on with James and Peter, loudly arguing over the best place to plant the dungbombs.**  

天狼星回头看了他一眼，表示理解，然后继续和詹姆斯、彼得讨论在哪里放置粪便炸弹。

 

**Remus knocked on the office door, timidly.**  

雷木斯小心翼翼地敲了敲办公室的门。

 

**“Enter,” came a voice from within.**  

“进来。”里面传来声音。

 

**He pushed the door open, and poked his head around nervously before going inside.**  

他推开门，小心翼翼地探出头来，然后走了进去。

 

**“Hello, professor.” He said, approaching her desk.**  

“您好，教授。”他说道，走向她的桌子。

 

**McGonagall was marking some essays, piled up neatly in front of her, a red quill flicking smoothly across the parchment as she read. She looked up and smiled at him pleasantly,**  

麦格教授正在批改一些整齐堆放在她面前的作文，红色的羽毛笔在羊皮纸上流畅地滑动。她抬起头来，对他露出了愉快的微笑，

 

**“Lupin, lovely to see you. Please have a seat.”**  

“雷木斯，很高兴见到你

 

。请坐。”

 

**He sat carefully, strangely reminded of the very first time he’d been in her office, and how tall and frightening she had seemed. He’d really thought he would hate her, she’d seemed so much like matron. Now he was able to meet her eye, and smile back as though she were a real friend. “How can I help?” She asked, as the red quill came to rest in the inkwell beside the papers.**  

他小心翼翼地坐下，奇怪地想起了第一次进她办公室时的情景，她当时显得那么高大和可怕。他真的以为自己会讨厌她，她看起来很像保健医。现在他能直视她的眼睛，微笑着像对待真正的朋友一样。“我怎么帮忙？”她问道，同时将红色羽毛笔放在了墨水瓶旁边。

 

**“I… I wanted to ask a favour,” he said, carefully. He felt inside his pockets and pulled out the letter from his mother. He put it on the desk, and slid it across. “Over Christmas the Potters helped me track down my mum. I wrote to her, and she wrote back. She’s in a muggle hospital, in Wales. I’d like to have permission to go and see her.”**  

“我……我想请个忙，”他说，小心翼翼地将母亲的信从口袋里拿出来，放到桌上并推过去。“圣诞节期间，波特一家帮我找到了我妈妈。我给她写了信，她也回了信。她在威尔士的一家麻瓜医院。我想申请去看她的许可。”

 

**McGonagall only glanced down at the letter briefly, before looking at him again.**  

麦格教授只是简短地看了一眼信件，然后又看向他。

 

**“Of course. We can make arrangements as soon as you’d like.”**  

“当然。我们可以尽快安排。”

 

**“Really?!” He was amazed it had been that easy.**  

“真的？！”他惊讶于竟然这么简单。

 

**“Really,” she replied, “Mr Lupin, this is a school, not a prison. Students are permitted to visit family members.”**  

“真的，”她回答道，“雷木斯先生，这是一所学校，不是监狱。学生可以探望家人。”

 

**“Oh. Well, great. I thought maybe on the next Hogsmeade weekend?”**  

“哦，那太好了。我想也许在下一个霍格斯梅德的周末？”

 

**“Certainly,” she opened a notebook and jotted something down, “Come and see me on the morning of, and I’ll write your permission slip.”**  

“当然，”她打开一个笔记本，写下了一些东西，“到时早上来找我，我会写你的许可条。”

 

**“Thank you.”**  

“谢谢。”

 

**“Would you like somebody to go with you?”**  

“你需要有人陪你去吗？”

 

**“Er… no. Thanks, but no.” Now that he’d done it once, he realised that it was something he needed to do alone. He wasn’t looking forward to breaking that to Sirius, but there was no helping it.**  

“呃……不。谢谢，但不需要。”既然他已经做了一次，他意识到这是他需要独自完成的事情。他不太期待把这个消息告诉天狼星，但没办法。

 

**“I’m very pleased for you, Remus,” McGonagall said, smiling again. “You know that my door is always open, if you need somebody to talk to. Though I know you aren’t short of friends.”**  

“我为你感到非常高兴，雷木斯，”麦格教授再次笑道。“你知道，如果你需要人倾诉，我的门总是敞开的。尽管我知道你朋友不少。”

 

**“Thanks,” he looked down, bashfully.**  

“谢谢，”他害羞地低下了头。

 

**“How is your revision going, Mr Lupin?”**  

“雷木斯先生，你的复习进展如何？”

 

**“Good, thanks.” Remus nodded, glad to be onto an easier subject.**  

“很好，谢谢。”雷木斯点了点头，欣慰于能开始较简单的科目。

 

**“Better than good, from what I’ve heard,” she continued, smiling, “All of your professors have given excellent reports on your achievements. In most classes you’re performing well above your peers, and I hear you’ve not only been working hard for yourself, but to help others, too?”**  

“从我听说的情况来看，比‘好’更好，”她继续说道，笑着说，“你所有的教授都对你的成绩给予了极高的评价。在大多数课程中，你的表现远超同龄人，而且我听说你不仅为自己努力，还帮助了其他人？”

 

**“The study groups are a collaborative thing…” Remus said, awkwardly.**  

“学习小组是一个合作的事情……”雷木斯尴尬地说道。

 

**“Nevertheless,” Professor McGonagall shook her head, “I’m proud to have you in my house, Mr Lupin.”**  

“尽管如此，”麦格教授摇了摇头，“雷木斯先生，我很自豪你在我的学院。”

 

**He didn’t know what to say to that, so he just looked at his hands. “Mr Lupin,” his head of house continued, “I have a favour to ask…”**  

他不知道该怎么回答，于是只得看着自己的手。“雷木斯先生，”他的院长继续说道，“我有个忙要请你帮……”

 

**“A favour?” Remus looked up, surprised. What on earth?**  

“请个忙？”雷木斯抬头惊讶地问道。到底是什么事？

 

**“Ahem, yes…” McGonagall looked a bit sheepish, and leaned in slightly, “As I’m sure you know, the final quidditch match of the year will be taking place in April, just before exams,”**  

“咳，嗯……”麦格教授显得有些不好意思，稍微倾身说道，“我相信你知道，今年的最后一场魁地奇比赛将在四月举行，就在考试前。”

 

**“Yeah, James has the schedule posted up in our room with an enchanted countdown in seconds and everything.”**  

“是的，詹姆斯在我们房间里贴了赛程表，还有一个用魔法倒计时的。”

 

**McGonagall smiled fondly.**  

麦格教授温柔地笑了。

 

**“James has been an absolute asset to the team, he's led Gryffindor on a record winning streak during his time here. The team he has assembled is first rate, primed to win their sixth cup in as many years… which brings me to my problem.”**  

“詹姆斯对球队来说是绝对的财富，他带领格兰芬多创造了连胜的纪录。他组建的球队是一流的，准备赢得他们连续第六个杯赛……这就引出了我的问题。”

 

**“Er… you want my help with a quidditch problem?!”**  

“呃……你需要我帮忙解决一个魁地奇问题？！”

 

**“Indeed. Now, I cannot go into too much detail, but I am sorry to say that Alexander Gordon, our beater, will be returning home for the rest of the term. I shall be telling Potter on Monday, of course, a replacement must be found as soon as possible, which is why I wanted to speak with you first..”**  

“确实如此。现在，我不能详细说明，但很遗憾，我要告诉你亚历山大·戈登，我们的击球手，将会在本学期剩下的时间里回家。我会在周一告诉波特，当然，必须尽快找到替代者，这就是我首先想和你谈谈的原因……”

 

**“Professor, I’m awful at quidditch!” Remus said, breaking out in a cold sweat.**  

“教授，我对魁地奇一窍不通！”雷木斯说道，冷汗直冒。

 

**McGonagall stared at him with a frown for a moment, before breaking into a (highly out of character) chuckle. She raised her hand to her mouth, apologetically,**  

麦格教授皱着眉头盯着他看了一会儿，然后（极其不符合她性格地）笑了起来。她抱歉地将手放到嘴边，

 

**“Goodness, Lupin! I didn't mean to suggest... though I’m sure you are quite capable on a broom, it wasn’t you I had in mind.”**  

“天哪，雷木斯！我不是想暗示……虽然我相信你在扫帚上很有能力，但我并没有把你当作考虑对象。”

 

**“Oh!” Remus exhaled, his shoulders relaxing. “Oh, good. Er… then how can I help?”**  

“哦！”雷木斯舒了口气，肩膀放松了下来。“哦，那就好。呃……那我能怎么帮忙？”

 

**“Well,” McGonagall turned serious once more. “We do have rather a good beater already in Gryffindor. But as you are aware, he was struck off the team two years ago.”**  

“嗯，”麦格教授再次变得严肃。“我们格兰芬多确实有一位相当优秀的击球手。但如你所知，他在两年前被从球队中除名。”

 

**“Sirius.”**  

“天狼星。”

 

**“Now, I don't wish to condone his behaviour, nor diminish the enormity of the incident which occurred in your fifth year…”**  

“现在，我不想为他的行为开脱，也不想淡化发生在你五年级时事件的严重性……”

 

**“No…” Remus swallowed, finding his mouth quite dry. He didn’t like to think about that, not ever. Like his hip, it was a pain which sometimes surfaced, but that he had to ignore in order to keep going.**  

“不……”雷木斯吞了口唾沫，感觉口干舌燥。他不喜欢去想那些事情，绝不。他像他的髋关节一样，那是一种时不时会浮现的痛苦，但他必须忽略它才能继续前行。

 

**“And I stand by the punishment he received,” his teacher continued, “But… well he was only struck off the team, he wasn’t placed under permanent ban.”**  

“我坚持他所受到的惩罚，”他的老师继续说道，“但是……他只是被除名了，并没有被永久禁赛。”

 

**“Right,” Remus nodded, soberly. “So he can play again, if he wants to.”**  

“对，”雷木斯严肃地点了点头。“所以他可以再次参赛，如果他愿意的话。”

 

**“Remus, I’m not going to allow it unless you agree.” McGonagall said, placing a hand on the desk between them. “It was you that Sirius put in danger, and if you feel--”**  

“雷木斯，除非你同意，否则我不会允许的。”麦格教授说道，将手放在他们之间的桌子上。“是你被天狼星置于危险之中，如果你觉得——”

 

**“No.” Remus said, “I mean yes, I mean… let him back on the team.”**  

“不。”雷木斯说道，“我是说，是的，我是说……让他重新回到球队。”

 

**“Are you sure?” She peered over her spectacles at him, as if trying to read his expression.**  

“你确定吗？”她透过眼镜看着他，好像试图读懂他的表情。

 

**“Absolutely!” Remus forced a smile. “Of course. It was two years ago.”**  

“绝对确定！”雷木斯强作笑容。“当然了。那是两年前的事了。”

 

**McGonagall watched him a bit longer, then smiled back, visibly relieved. He’d done the right thing, then. The thing she’d wanted.**  

麦格教授又看了他一会儿，然后笑了起来，显然感到松了一口气。他做了正确的决定，那正是她希望的。

 

**“Thank you, Mr Lupin,” she nodded, leaning back again. “I’ll tell Potter first thing tomorrow.”**  

“谢谢你，雷木斯先生，”她点了点头，重新靠在椅背上。“我会在明天一早告诉波特的。”

 

**“Great.” Remus nodded, getting up from his seat. “Thanks, professor, see you Monday.”**  

“太好了。”雷木斯点了点头，站起身来。“谢谢教授，周一见。”

Chapter 141: Seventh Year: Star Star 

He could have told James and Sirius straight away, if he’d wanted to. Could have played the hero, enjoyed the spotlight and being the cause of their joy. But he didn’t. He told himself it was to preserve Alexander Gordon’s privacy, or to respect McGonagall’s authority. But the truth was that he just didn’t want anything to do with it at all.

他本可以立即告诉詹姆斯和天狼星，如果他愿意的话。他本可以扮演英雄，享受那种关注和带给他们的快乐。但他没有这么做。他告诉自己这样做是为了保护亚历山大·戈登的隐私，或者尊重麦格教授的权威。但事实是他根本不想参与其中。

Obviously he wanted Sirius to be happy. Obviously he didn’t want to be an obstacle to Sirius’s happiness. And obviously he wanted Gryffindor to beat Slytherin in the final match; for James to have his moment of glory. He didn’t want to see Sirius punished forever for a mistake he made at sixteen. He didn’t want betrayal to hang over them like that, or to bring it all up again. And yet, there it was.
显然，他希望天狼星快乐。显然，他不想成为天狼星快乐的障碍。显然，他希望格兰芬多在决赛中击败斯莱特林；希望詹姆斯能拥有他的荣耀时刻。他不想看到天狼星因为一个十六岁时犯的错误而被永远惩罚。他不想让背叛像这样悬在他们之间，或者再次提起一切。然而，事情就是这样。

Remus had forgiven Sirius, back in the Potters’ bathroom two years ago; had absolved a truly repentant boy with blood on his hands and sorrowful eyes. It had been before they understood each other, before so many other good memories, of good things which had changed their friendship. But Remus hadn’t forgotten how it had felt. Sirius could destroy him completely without even meaning to. If anything, Remus was even more vulnerable to that now than he had been at sixteen.
雷木斯在两年前波特家的浴室里已经原谅了天狼星；原谅了那个手上沾满血迹和眼中满是悔恨的男孩。这发生在他们彼此了解之前，在那些改变了他们友谊的美好回忆之前。但雷木斯没有忘记那种感觉。天狼星可以在毫不经意间彻底摧毁他。如果说有什么不同的话，雷木斯现在比十六岁时更容易受到这种伤害。

No, Remus told himself. There was a difference between atonement and revenge. Sirius had earned this.
不，雷木斯告诉自己。赎罪和复仇之间是有区别的。天狼星应得这一切。

On Monday morning, James received a note from McGonagall, asking to see him before quidditch practice. He hurried off without even finishing his breakfast - nothing was more important than the final match. Marlene and Yaz began speculating on what it could be, Peter and Sirius leaning across the table eagerly to join in. Remus just waited, feeling half pleased and half something else. As breakfast was finishing, James’s muffled voice began emanating from the two-way mirror Sirius’s robe pocket.
在周一早晨，詹姆斯收到了一张麦格教授的便条，请他在魁地奇训练前去见她。他急匆匆地离开了，连早餐都没吃完——没有什么比决赛更重要了。玛琳和雅兹开始猜测可能是什么事，彼得和天狼星也兴奋地倾身过来参与。雷木斯只是等待，感觉有一半是高兴，另一半则是其他的情绪。早餐快结束时，詹姆斯的声音从天狼星的袍子口袋里的双向镜子中传了出来。

“Padfoot! Padfoot! Quidditch pitch! Now!”
“天狼星！天狼星！魁地奇场地！现在！”

“What’dyou reckon he wants?” Sirius scratched his head as they got up from the table.
“你觉得他想要什么？”天狼星边挠头边起身离开餐桌。

“Oh, I think you’ll like it.” Remus replied, cryptically. “Go on, he sounds excited.”
“哦，我想你会喜欢的。”雷木斯神秘地回答道。“快去吧，他听起来很兴奋。”

“You know what it is, don’t you?” Sirius eyed him suspiciously.
“你知道是什么吗？”天狼星怀疑地看着他。

“Maybe.”
“也许吧。”

“Don’t you want me to walk you to Care of Magical Creatures?”
“你不想让我送你去魔法生物护理课吗？”

“I’ll manage. Go! Hurry!”
“我自己能搞定。快去！赶紧的！”

Remus didn’t see James and Sirius again until lunch, and both of them were grinning from ear to ear. James had the quidditch schedule out and was marking out extra practice days so that Sirius could get back up to speed.
雷木斯直到午餐时才再次看到詹姆斯和天狼星，两人都笑得合不拢嘴。詹姆斯拿出了魁地奇赛程表，标记出了额外的训练日，以便天狼星能重新找回状态。

“You were right,” Sirius beamed, practically bouncing in his seat as Remus arrived, “I did like it.”
“你说得对，”天狼星笑得满面春风，几乎在座位上跳起来，“我确实喜欢。”

Remus just smiled back. It was enough to see him happy; and if love was something you did, then Remus hoped this was enough.
雷木斯只是微笑回应。看到他快乐就足够了；如果爱是行动的话，那么雷木斯希望这已经足够了。

“What are you so happy about?” Marlene asked, sitting down opposite the boys.
“你们这么高兴是为了什么？”玛琳问道，坐到男孩们对面。

“Say hello to your new beater,” Sirius burst out.
“欢迎你们的新击球手，”天狼星兴奋地说道。

James laughed, nodding.
詹姆斯笑了，点了点头。

“Oh!” Marlene smiled brightly, “Excellent! Er… what happened to Gordon?”
“哦！”玛琳笑容灿烂，“太棒了！呃……戈登怎么了？”

“Gone home.” James replied, “Not supposed to ask.”
“回家了。”詹姆斯回答道，“不该问。”

“Ah. Well, anyway,” Marlene shook her head, “That’s fantastic, I’ve missed having you watching my back. So how come McGonagall let you? I thought you got kicked off for doing something unspeakable…?”
“哦。好吧，”玛琳摇了摇头，“那太棒了，我很想念你保护我的样子。那么麦格教授怎么会让你回去呢？我以为你是因为做了不可告人的事才被踢下去的……？”

“Oh yeah,” Mary added, stirring grated cheese into her leek and potato soup, “I remember something like that too, what did you do?”
“哦，对了，”玛丽补充道，一边搅拌着加了奶酪的韭菜土豆汤，“我也记得类似的事，你做了什么？”

Sirius visibly balked at this, his eyes widening.
天狼星显然被这个问题吓到了，眼睛瞪得大大的。

Remus frowned slightly. Was this the first time it had occurred to him? Had Remus been agonising over the implications of an event Sirius barely even remembered?! He decided to rescue him, nonetheless,
雷木斯略微皱眉。难道这是天狼星第一次意识到这个问题？雷木斯是否一直在为天狼星几乎不记得的事件的含义而苦恼？！尽管如此，他决定拯救他，

“Ha, you can’t expect Sirius to remember every stupid stunt he pulls that gets him into trouble.” He said, cheerfully.
“哈哈，你不能指望天狼星记住每一个让他惹麻烦的愚蠢恶作剧。”他愉快地说道。

The girls accepted this, and lunch continued, but Remus could feel Sirius’s eyes on him the whole time. Apparently he had caught up. Well, Remus thought, at least it only takes him a few hours now. This time last year it would have been months.
女生们接受了这个说法，午餐继续进行，但雷木斯能感觉到天狼星一直在看着他。显然他已经明白了。雷木斯想，至少现在只需要几个小时。去年这个时候可能需要几个月。

Throughout the rest of the afternoon lessons, Remus’s gut instinct was to be evasive; to make a quick get away after his final class and stay in the library as late as he could, then go straight to bed without speaking.
在下午剩下的课程中，雷木斯的直觉是要回避；在最后一节课后迅速离开，尽可能晚地呆在图书馆，然后直接上床睡觉，不说话。

But really, he tried to reason with himself, wasn’t that just another way to punish Sirius? It certainly didn’t demonstrate forgiveness. He hadn’t forgotten their recent fight, and how Sirius had called him ‘bloody exhausting’. It had actually hurt his feelings quite a lot, at the time, and he knew that this was because it was so painfully true.
但他真的试图说服自己，这不只是另一种惩罚天狼星的方式吗？这确实没有表现出宽恕。他没有忘记他们最近的争吵，以及天狼星怎么称他为“让人受够了”。那时确实很伤他的感情，他知道这正是因为这句话非常真实。

So. He’d try it Sirius’s way.
所以。他决定试试天狼星的方式。

“Fancy a walk after dinner?” He asked, casually, tapping the box of matches where he kept his cigarettes and - sometimes - something more recreational.
“晚饭后想去散步吗？”他随意地问道，拍了拍他放烟草和——有时——其他休闲物品的火柴盒。

“Yeah,” Sirius smiled, surprised, “Sounds good.”
“嗯，”天狼星惊讶地笑了，“听起来不错。”

Pudding appeared on the table in front of them. James was taking notes on the teleportation mechanism, and kept picking up plates as soon as they emptied, to see if they would refill in mid-air, or land on the table itself.
布丁出现在他们面前的桌子上。詹姆斯正在记录传送机制，并不断地拿起盘子，一旦盘子空了，就看看它们是会在空中重新装满，还是直接落在桌子上。

“Potter if you drop even one treacle tart I’ll have your guts for garters…” Lily threatened.
“波特，如果你掉了一个焦糖挞，我会把你的肠子拿来做护腿！”莉莉威胁道。

 

* * *

It was easy enough for them to get away that evening, and they wandered towards the astronomy tower, because the evenings were nice now that winter was finally on its way out, and no one would have a go at them for smoking.

那天晚上，他们很容易就溜了出去，朝着天文学塔走去，因为现在冬天终于要过去了，晚上的天气很好，也不会有人对他们抽烟指责。

They interrupted a couple of fifth years clumsily groping on the parapets, and used their seventh year privilege to send them on their way.
他们打断了几名笨拙地在护栏上摸索的五年级学生，并利用他们七年级的特权将他们赶走了。

“Honestly, when we were their age, we never…” Sirius tutted disapprovingly.
“说实话，我们那个年纪的时候，从来没有……”天狼星不满地咂嘴道。

“Sure you want to finish that?” Remus raised a wry eyebrow.
“确定你想继续说下去吗？”雷木斯挑了挑眉。

They settled down. Remus rolled up his robes to use as a cushion, and they sat with their backs to the wall, companionably rolling spliffs. “I’m really happy for you.” Remus started, after his first inhale. “About the quidditch. You deserve it.”
他们安顿下来。雷木斯把长袍卷起来当作垫子，然后他们背靠着墙，亲切地卷着大麻烟。“我真的为你感到高兴。”雷木斯在第一次吸烟后说道，“关于魁地奇的事，你值得。”

“谢谢，”天狼星点了点头，语气中带着放松。“我真的……嗯。我问了詹姆斯，他说麦格教授先问了你是否同意。”

“She did.” Remus agreed, keeping his voice steady. “Obviously I said it was fine. Obviously.”
“她确实问了。”雷木斯同意道，保持着平稳的语气。“显然我说没问题。显然。”

“I’m really grateful. You didn’t have to, I would have understood.”
“我真的很感激。你本不必这样做，我会理解的。”

“Really?” Remus looked at him, finally.
“真的？”雷木斯终于看着他。

“Of course,” Sirius said, earnestly, “I deserved to be struck off; I deserved to be expelled for what I did. Locked up in Azkaban. I got off easy, and I know it.”
“当然，”天狼星认真地说，“我应该被除名；我应该因为我做的事被开除。被关在阿兹卡班。我过得太轻松了，我知道。”

他说这些话时感觉有些头晕。这些话不多，但他知道他们都感受到这些话的重量。天狼星一直比任何人都努力理解他。

“我们不必谈论这个……”雷木斯不安地说道。他真的不想谈论这个。

“我只是想让你知道，我确实仍然感到有责任。我不怪任何人，除了我自己——连斯内普也不怪。连……连她也不怪。”

“谁？”雷木斯皱眉，不知所措。

Remus nodded. How could he ever forget? It had been one of the worst nights of his life, and he had had more than his fair share.
雷木斯点了点头。他怎么可能忘记？那是他一生中最糟糕的夜晚之一，他经历了不止一次这样的夜晚。

天狼星继续说道，低头看着自己的膝盖，缩成一团靠在石头护栏上。

He paused, apparently to take a few deep breaths, then pressed on bravely. “It was always the most important thing, when I was growing up; family. Family loyalty. “但后来真的发生了——他们以前惩罚过我那么多次，我以为我知道会发生什么。但不是那样。我从未如此……如此害怕。”他的眼睛现在闪着泪光，愤怒地直视前方，“我讨厌那种感觉，而我唯一能想到的，就是你或詹姆斯会做得更好。更勇敢，或想出办法反击。我没有反击，因为……因为他们是我的家人。”

“Sirius…” Remus tried to sound gentle, but Sirius shook his head, wiping his eyes quickly,
“天狼星……”雷木斯试图温柔地说道，但天狼星摇了摇头，迅速擦干眼泪，

“No, it’s ok, I’m not telling you so you feel sorry for me, I’m not making excuses. There’s no excuse. I’m just… I dunno, trying to explain. Anyway; that happened at Christmas, and then I was living at the Potters after that, so it was all ok, for me, wasn’t it? Like… I was safe, and I had nothing to be scared of. But I still felt like she could get me. I had these nightmares, remembering the curse. Sorry, I know it sounds stupid.”
“不，没事，我不是告诉你让你可怜我，我不是在找借口。没有借口。我只是……我不知道，试图解释一下。反正，那件事发生在圣诞节，然后我住在波特家，所以对我来说一切都还好，不是吗？就像……我安全了，不再害怕了。但我仍然觉得她会找到我。我做了这些噩梦，记得那个诅咒。对不起，我知道这听起来很傻。”

“It doesn’t sound stupid at all!”
“这一点也不傻！”

“Still. I felt like I had to do something, and maybe I didn’t always have the best ideas. You know what I was like - all over the place, acting like a twat. Me and James, we both used to egg each other on, didn’t we? And Snape was so easy to pick on, because he’s so foul and nasty already. Godric, so nasty. He tried to attack Mary, and then him and Reg tried to hurt you too, remember? And he just kept going, no matter what we did. And I just… not like Snape is like my mother or anything - I think there are at least six degrees of evil between them - but he made me feel the way she made me feel. Like I couldn’t control it.
