“但我感觉我必须做点什么，也许我的想法并不总是最好的。你知道我是什么样的——到处乱七八糟，表现得像个傻瓜。我和詹姆斯，我们以前都互相挑唆，不是吗？而斯内普非常容易被挑衅，因为他本来就很恶心。天神，他真是太恶心了。他试图攻击玛丽，然后他和雷格也试图伤害你，记得吗？他无论我们怎么做都不停。我只是……不是说斯内普和我母亲一样——我觉得他们之间至少有六度的邪恶——但他让我感到像我母亲让我感到的那样。就像我无法控制它一样。我只是想让他害怕；让他也感受到那种感觉，这样他也许就会停下来。这不是借口，我真的很抱歉，月亮。”

Remus had not let go of Sirius’s hand. Something strange was happening inside of him. Something which he had rarely felt outside of a full moon. A fierce and overwhelming desire to protect this boy sitting next to him. To make sure he was never frightened again. He pulled Sirius to him, taking his spliff and pressing their lips together.
雷木斯没有放开天狼星的手。他内心发生了一些奇怪的事。他很少在满月之外感受到这种情感。强烈而压倒性的保护欲望，想要保护这个坐在他身边的男孩。确保他再也不会感到害怕。他把天狼星拉到自己身边，拿过他的烟，吻上了他的唇。

“It's forgiven.” He said, “I mean it.”
“我原谅你了。”他说，“我是认真的。”

Sirius didn’t speak, just looked up at him, grateful and happy, and Remus thought if he could bottle that look then he’d never struggle with a patronus again. “And you can blame your mother for it if you like.” Remus said, pulling away, “She sounds like a right cunt.”
天狼星没有说话，只是感激地幸福地看着他，雷木斯想着如果他能把那种表情装在瓶子里，那他就再也不会为护神咒而挣扎了。“你可以把这个怪罪到你母亲身上，”雷木斯说道，拉开， “她听起来真是个烂货。”

Sirius snorted with laughter and buried his face in Remus’s shoulder,
天狼星哼了一声笑，把脸埋在雷木斯的肩膀上，

“You oik,” he chuckled, gleefully. “I really bloody l--”
“你这小子，”他高兴地笑道，“我真他妈喜欢——”

“Who’s up here?!” Mary came tiptoeing around the corner. “Oh.” She sighed, upon seeing them. “I was hoping you were Marlene and Yaz, been trying to catch them for ages, finally put an end to this sneaking around malarkey.”
“谁在这儿？！”玛丽踮起脚尖转过角落。“哦。”看到他们后，她叹了口气。“我还以为你们是玛琳娜和雅兹，一直在试图抓到她们，终于结束了这鬼鬼祟祟的事。”

Sirius leaned back against the wall, wiping his eyes quickly.
天狼星靠在墙上，迅速擦干眼泪。

“All right, MacDonald,” he grinned, squinting up at her.
“好吧，麦克唐纳，”他笑着说道，眯着眼睛看着她。

“Ohhh, is that what I think it is?” Mary glimpsed the spliff in Remus’s hand, “Sharesies!”
“哦，这就是我想的那样吗？”玛丽瞥见雷木斯手中的烟，“共享吧！”

Friday 10th March 1978 - Just before midnight.

“Moony! Where have you gone? They’re going to do your cake before James really gets drunk…” Sirius called up the stairs.
“月亮脸！你去哪儿了？他们要给你切蛋糕了，詹姆斯还没真正喝醉之前...”天狼星在楼下喊道。

Remus smirked to himself, tipsily. James was too far gone already, if you asked him. He’d been leaping all over the common room furniture to ‘Jean Genie’ for half an hour already.
雷木斯自嘲地笑了笑，有些醉意。如果你问他，詹姆斯早就已经喝得不省人事了。他已经在休息室的家具上跳了半个小时的《Jean Genie》。

“Yeah I’ll just be a sec!” Remus called back.
“好的，我马上来！”雷木斯回喊道。

He was looking for something to use as a vase, and finally settled on transfiguring an old Wellington boot which must have been one of Peter's from first year. “Aguamente,” he murmured, his wandwork a bit sloppy from the cider. He had thought cider would be a smarter choice than whisky, but if anything it seemed to have made him stupider than normal.
他在找可以用作花瓶的东西，最后决定把一只旧的威灵顿靴子变成花瓶，那应该是彼得一年级时的。“阿瓜门提，”他喃喃道，由于喝了苹果酒，他的魔杖施法有些不稳。他以为苹果酒比威士忌聪明，但似乎让他变得比平时更愚蠢。

He dunked the bunch of tulips into the very rubbery looking vase, and grinned to himself.
他把一束郁金香插进看起来非常橡胶质感的花瓶里，自己笑了起来。

“What are you doing up here?” Sirius came in, now. He was drunk too; he had acquired a wide brimmed mauve hat from somewhere, and was wearing it at a jaunty angle. “Flowers?” He looked confused.
“你在这儿干什么？”天狼星走了进来。他也喝醉了；不知道从哪里弄到了一顶宽边的紫色帽子，歪斜地戴在头上。“花？”他看起来很困惑。

“Er yeah. From one of the Hufflepuffs in my study group,”
“呃，是的。是我学习小组里的一个赫奇帕奇给的。”

“Who’s giving you flowers?!”
“谁给你花？！”

“Miranda O’dell. Fourth year.”
“米兰达·奥德尔。四年级。”

“But why?!”
“为什么？！”

“I asked her to,” Remus smirked, enjoying the game.
“是我让她给的，”雷木斯狡黠地笑着，享受这个游戏。

Sirius threw his hands up,
天狼星举起双手，

“Moony! I am too drunk for your puzzles!”
“月亮脸！我喝得太醉了，玩不动你的谜语！”

“They’re for Hope,” Remus poked his tongue out. “Seeing her tomorrow, remember?”
“是给霍普的，”雷木斯吐了吐舌头。“明天见她，记得吗？”

“Oh yeah!” Sirius smiled again, eyes practically violet under the shade of his ridiculously flattering purple hat. “Looking forward to it?”
“哦，对！”天狼星又笑了起来，眼睛在他那顶荒唐但极其衬他的紫色帽子的阴影下几乎显得紫色。“期待吗？”

“D’you know what, I sort of am? At least I don’t want to throw up, like last time.”
“你知道吗，我有点期待？至少不像上次那样想吐。”

“Progress!” Sirius flung his arms out. The volume of the music downstairs increased by a good few decibels, as that trilling guitar started all over again, and James’s voice could be heard booming;
“进步了！”天狼星挥舞着双臂。楼下的音乐音量增加了好几分贝，响亮的吉他声再次响起，詹姆斯的声音传来；

“A small Jean Genie snuck off to the city, strung out on lasers and slash-back blazers, ate all your razors while pulling the waiters…”
“小小的Jean Genie溜进了城市，迷失在激光和回弹夹克中，吃掉了你的剃刀，同时拉扯着侍者……”

“James really likes this song, eh?” Remus grinned, hands in his pockets, enjoying being away from it all for a little bit.
“詹姆斯真的很喜欢这首歌，是吧？”雷木斯笑了笑，双手插在口袋里，享受着片刻的宁静。

“经过多年的努力，鲍伊终于打动了他。”天狼星回道，轻轻地向雷木斯走了几步，以那种迷人的随意姿态靠在床柱上。“你喜欢你的派对吗？”他低下头问道，眼睛像女孩一样大而调情。

“Very much,” Remus bobbed his head, returning the smile.
“非常喜欢，”雷木斯点点头，回以微笑。

“Someone invited Lockhart, the prick.”
“有人邀请了洛哈特，那混蛋。”

“Oh yeah?”
“哦，真的？”

“Yeah, how come he’s like that, anyway?!”
“是的，他怎么会那样？！”

Remus just shrugged, eyes fixed on the way Sirius swung his hips unconsciously back and forth in time with the bass reverberating from the floorboards. When they left school, Remus would buy him a hundred pairs of black jeans, and that would be all he’d allow him to wear.
雷木斯只是耸了耸肩，眼睛盯着天狼星无意识地随着地板上传来的低音来回摆动的臀部。当他们离开学校时，雷木斯会给他买一百条黑色牛仔裤，那将是他唯一允许他穿的东西。

“Want your present?” Sirius asked, suddenly, catching Remus’s eye.
“想要你的礼物吗？”天狼星突然问道，抓住了雷木斯的目光。

“You already got me a present!” Remus protested. A full year's supply of chocolate frogs - though Remus was pretty sure he could polish it off by the time exams were over.
“你已经给了我一个礼物！”雷木斯抗议道。一整年的巧克力蛙供应——虽然雷木斯很确定到考试结束时他就能吃完。

“I’m allowed to get you more than one thing.” Sirius said, petulantly.
“我可以给你多于一个礼物。”天狼星任性地说。

He stood away from the bed, legs apart, and waved his hands flamboyantly through the air like a muggle magician. Then, with a dramatic bow, he swept the hat from his head in one fluid motion, delved his hand inside and withdrew a small metal thing.

他递给雷木斯，雷木斯闻到那是纯金的。那是一个长方形的盒子，比他的手掌大一点。上面有着与他的金表相同的叶藤状设计，手感很好，重量感十足。他啪地一声打开它，发现里面嵌着一排十八支整齐卷好的香烟。内盖上也有一个设计，精细地雕刻着，当它们捕捉到光线时，精美的线条闪闪发光。那是一片闪烁的夜空，一角有一轮大大的月亮，还有母贝镶嵌的天狼星座。

“Sirius.” Remus said quietly, staring at it.
“天狼星。”雷木斯轻声说道，盯着它看。

“So you can get rid of that manky old matchbox.”
“这样你就可以丢掉那个脏兮兮的旧火柴盒了。”

“Thank you… it’s beautiful.”
“谢谢…它真漂亮。”

“Oi you two, hurry up or Wormtail’s going to start on the cake!” James screamed up the stairs, ignoring Lily’s attempts to shush him.
“喂，你们两个，快点，不然虫尾巴就要开始切蛋糕了！”詹姆斯在楼梯上大叫，不理会莉莉试图让他安静的举动。

Remus and Sirius grinned at each other, and headed down, holding hands right until the bottom step.
雷木斯和天狼星相视而笑，然后牵着手下楼，一直到最后一步。

The common room was in an incredible state; barely recognisable. Multi coloured fairy lights hung from every rafter, balloons drifted up and down like weird bloated jellyfish, the suits of armour occasionally belched flame-free fireworks, and there were people on every stretch of carpet and bottles on every surface.

休息室一片混乱，几乎无法辨认。每根椽子上都挂着五颜六色的小彩灯，气球像奇怪的膨胀水母一样上下漂浮，盔甲不时喷出无火焰的烟火，地毯上到处都是人，表面上堆满了瓶子。

“Jean Genie! Lives on his back! Jean Genie! Loves chimney stacks! He’s outrageous, he screams and he bawls…”
“Jean Genie！背上住着Jean Genie！爱烟囱堆！他放肆无忌，他尖叫大喊…”

Most of the revellers were now leaping around the room with all the grace and dignity of kids on pogo sticks, led by James, Peter, Lily and Mary, who were jumping the most vigorously. James stopped when he saw Remus, and raised his arms cheering,
大多数狂欢者现在像跳跳杆上的孩子一样优雅而体面地在房间里跳来跳去，由詹姆斯、彼得、莉莉和玛丽带头，他们跳得最起劲。詹姆斯看到雷木斯时停下来，举起双臂欢呼，

“Moonyyyyy!”
“月亮脸——！”

“Cake!” Peter began to chant, “Cake, cake cake!”
“蛋糕！”彼得开始喊，“蛋糕，蛋糕蛋糕！”

Everybody joined in, and the crowd parted for Christopher and Marlene, who carried between them an enormous rectangular cake, the size of an overstuffed pillowcase. As they brought it to Remus, he saw with a flush of delight that it was decorated with chocolate buttercream icing to look like a gigantic leatherbound book.
所有人都加入了进来，人群为克里斯托弗和马琳让开，他们抬着一个巨大的长方形蛋糕，像一个装满的枕套那么大。当他们把蛋糕带到雷木斯面前时，他惊喜地看到蛋糕上装饰着巧克力奶油糖霜，看起来像一本巨大的皮革书。

“My two favourite things,” he laughed, ignoring the elbow in the ribs from Sirius.
“我最喜欢的两样东西，”他笑着说，无视天狼星的肘击。

He blew out the candles, and cut the cake, making the same wish both times. After that, James started leading everyone in a series of toasts; each more convoluted and elaborate than the last, encouraged by Sirius and Peter. That meant at least two more pints of cider, and some of Mary’s witches brew when he ran out.
他吹灭蜡烛，切了蛋糕，两次都许了同一个愿。之后，詹姆斯开始带领大家一系列的祝酒；每次都比上一次更复杂和精致，在天狼星和彼得的鼓励下。这意味着至少再喝两品脱的苹果酒，还有玛丽的女巫酿造，当他喝完时。

Remus’s last memory of his eighteenth birthday party was some lunatic deciding to put on Goats Head Soup - which had to be his least favourite Rolling Stones album, but he was pissed and he didn’t care. The jumping and flailing continued, and the room was hot and loud and sweaty, and everyone was red faced and grinning - and Remus didn’t even care when Lily and James pointed and laughed at him as the final track began to play and everyone belted out at the top of their lungs;
雷木斯对自己十八岁生日派对的最后记忆是，有个疯子决定播放《Goats Head Soup》——那一定是他最不喜欢的滚石乐队专辑，但他喝醉了，不在乎。跳跃和挥舞继续，房间里热闹、吵闹、汗流浃背，所有人都脸红且咧嘴大笑——当最后一首歌开始播放时，每个人都高声唱起，莉莉和詹姆斯指着他笑时，雷木斯甚至都不在乎

“ If I ever get back to New York, girl

Gonna make you scream all night

Yeah, a star fucker, star fucker, star fucker, star fucker, star!

Chapter 142: Seventh Year: Hospital VisitsShe loved tulips. She loved daisies. She loved forget-me-nots, and gerberas and roses and daffodils - she loved every flower he brought her. He always tried to bring something. Flowers were free, as long as he kept Madam Sprout on side, and Hope hadn’t much appetite, so chocolate was no good.

她爱郁金香。她爱雏菊。她爱勿忘我，和非洲菊、玫瑰、黄水仙——她爱他带来的每一朵花。他总是尽量带些东西。只要他和斯普劳特夫人关系好，花都是免费的，而霍普没有什么胃口，所以巧克力不好。

 

They had five more meetings over the spring of 1978, and Remus would forever mark each of them by the flowers he’d brought to her. The conversations they had too, of course - but the flowers seemed to bookend everything; colouring each session with its own personality.

在1978年春天，他们又见了五次面，而雷木斯永远会用他带给她的花来标记每次见面。当然，他们的谈话也很重要——但这些花似乎给每次会面都打上了独特的印记。

 

Tulips had presided over their second meeting. They were orange, pink and yellow, with sturdy dusky green stems and sumptuous velvet petals. A very generous flower, Remus thought.

在他们第二次见面时，郁金香占据了主角。它们是橙色、粉色和黄色的，有结实的暗绿色茎秆和丰厚的天鹅绒花瓣。雷木斯认为，这是种非常慷慨的花。

 

She was ready for him, this time; she’d had her hair washed and combed, and it gleamed sunny platinum blonde against the pink hospital blankets. She’d put a spot of makeup on, too, though Remus felt bad for noticing that, because he felt he ought not to care how she looked.

这次，她已经为他的到来做好了准备；她把头发洗净并梳理好，金色的头发在粉色的医院毯子上闪耀着阳光般的光芒。她还化了点妆，尽管雷木斯注意到这点时感到有些不安，因为他觉得自己不应该在意她的外貌。

 

“I got my sister to dig out some pictures,” Hope said eagerly, tapping a brown paper envelope on her bedside, as Remus set down the weird vase he’d drunkenly transfigured.

“我让我的妹妹找出了一些照片，”霍普急切地说，一边轻轻拍打床边的一个棕色纸袋，雷木斯则放下了他醉酒时变出的那个奇怪的花瓶。

 

“What are they pictures of?” He asked, cautiously, pulling up a seat beside her. He didn’t want to be caught unawares by anything too painful.

“这些照片是什么？”他小心翼翼地问，拉过一把椅子坐在她旁边。他不想被任何痛苦的记忆打个措手不及。

 

“Some of you, as a baby,” she smiled with shiny coral lips, “Some of me and your father.”

“有一些是你小时候的照片，”她露出闪亮的珊瑚色嘴唇微笑着说，“还有一些是我和你父亲的。”

 

“Lyall.” Remus said, quickly.

“莱尔。”雷木斯迅速地说道。

 

“Me and Lyall,” she corrected herself, out of politeness.

“我和莱尔，”她出于礼貌纠正道。

 

Hope would bend over backwards to save Remus even the smallest upset; that much was clear from the beginning. He found it unsettling; very few people had ever cared about his feelings so intensely before.

从一开始，霍普就尽量避免让雷木斯哪怕有一丁点的不开心。这点非常明显。他觉得这有些不安；很少有人曾如此关心他的感受。

 

He picked up the envelope, and held it for a moment.

他拿起信封，握了一会儿。

 

“You don’t have to look. We can do it another time.” Hope said, a tremor of fear in her voice. He didn’t want to frighten her. He wanted to tell her not to worry; that he wasn’t going to run away, or disappear forever; that he wanted to be there, and get to know her. But that was all too much, so he just opened the package and smiled,

“你不必现在看。我们可以另找时间。”霍普说，声音中带着一丝恐惧。他不想吓到她。他想告诉她不要担心；他不会逃跑，也不会永远消失；他想在这里，想了解她。但这些话太多了，所以他只是打开了包裹，微笑着说，

 

“No, I want to see.”

“不，我想看。”

 

Fortunately there weren’t very many - but he was surprised to find that more than half of the photographs were magical, and the images moved in his hands like film reels.

幸运的是，照片并不多——但他惊讶地发现，超过一半的照片是魔法照片，图像在他手中像电影胶片一样移动。

 

“I’ve had to keep them hidden,” Hope confided, “Lyall never liked the usual sort of photography; he said they were too flat.”

“我不得不把它们藏起来，”霍普吐露道，“莱尔从不喜欢普通的摄影；他说它们太平淡了。”

 

“How old is he, in this one?” Remus held up a photograph of both of his parents, standing in someone’s back garden. Lyall was wearing a muggle suit, and they were both squinting against the sunshine, but smiling. He had his arm around Hope’s waist.

“他在这张照片里多大了？”雷木斯举起一张他父母站在某个后花园的照片。莱尔穿着麻瓜西装，他们都眯着眼睛对着阳光微笑着。他的手臂搂着霍普的腰。

 

“Oh, I think we’d only met a few weeks before that was taken,” Hope said, taking it from him to look closer, “He’d have been… thirty, I think?”

“哦，我想那张照片拍摄前我们才认识几周，”霍普接过照片仔细看了看，“他那时应该……三十岁吧？”

 

Remus looked at it again. He knew he looked like Lyall, he’d been told so a few times, and to some extent he agreed. They were both gangly; tall and skinny with bad posture. But Lyall looked more at ease than Remus had ever felt in his over-long body; his movements in the photograph were confident and self-assured.

雷木斯再次看了看照片。他知道自己长得像莱尔，这点他听过几次，而且在某种程度上他也同意。他们都是瘦长的；高个子，身材瘦削，姿势不好。但莱尔看起来比雷木斯在自己过长的身体里感受到的要自在得多；他在照片中的动作自信而从容。

 

She let him take the pictures back to school, and he tentatively showed his friends. Over his seven years at Hogwarts, he had been shown a lot of family photos. Peter and James kept pictures in frames on their bedside, or else tacked up on the walls over their dressers. Lily had an album that she flipped through when she was homesick, and Mary had a shoebox full of holiday snaps, Christmases, postcards and pictures of her cousins in Jamaica. So it was a surprisingly nice experience, Remus thought, being able to share his own modest collection.

她让他把照片带回学校，他试探性地给朋友们看。在霍格沃茨的七年里，他看过很多家庭照片。彼得和詹姆斯把照片放在床头的相框里，或者钉在梳妆台上的墙上。莉莉有一本相册，想家时会翻看，玛丽有一个装满假期照片、圣诞节、明信片和牙买加表亲照片的鞋盒。所以雷木斯觉得，能够分享自己的这一小小收藏是一个出乎意料的美好体验。

 

“That’s them,” he said, shyly, as they sat around the fireplace, “They’re my parents.”

“那是他们，”他腼腆地说，他们围坐在壁炉旁，“他们是我的父母。”

 

“Remus you look just like your dad!” Lily said, meaning to be kind.

“雷木斯，你看起来和你爸爸一模一样！”莉莉善意地说道。

 

“Wow, look at your mum’s hair!” Mary grinned, “What a glamour puss!”

“哇，看看你妈妈的头发！”玛丽咧嘴笑道，“真是个魅力十足的美人！”

 

“Ahhh!” James snatched another picture, waving it at everyone, “Look at little baby Moony!”

“啊！”詹姆斯抢过另一张照片，向大家挥舞着，“看看小婴儿月亮脸！”

 

It was silly, Remus knew, but he even felt the

 

 beginnings of pride, sharing his family like that. Proof that he’d been normal, once; just like his friends. This is who I am. This is who I came from.

雷木斯知道，这有点傻，但他甚至感到一丝骄傲，能够这样分享他的家庭。证明他曾经是正常的；就像他的朋友们一样。这就是我。这就是我的来历。

 

One afternoon he even returned to the Ravenclaw corridor to see the duelling trophy with Lyall’s name on it. It was the same as ever, but no longer gave him that mysterious ache of longing as it had in second year.

一个下午，他甚至回到拉文克劳走廊去看上面刻有莱尔名字的决斗奖杯。它和以前一样，但不再像二年级时那样给他带来神秘的渴望。

 

Christopher and Marlene walked past, while he was looking at it.

克里斯托弗和玛琳走过来时，他正在看着它。

 

“Oh, ‘Lupin’!” Christopher said, surprised, peering into the case to read the trophy, “Is that your dad? Cool!”

“哦，‘卢平’！”克里斯托弗惊讶地说，仔细看了看柜子里的奖杯，“那是你爸爸吗？真酷！”

 

“Thanks,” Remus put his hands in his pockets, suddenly bashful. Marlene touched his shoulder in a friendly, comforting way. He smiled at her, gratefully. “I met my mum recently,” Remus explained to Christopher, “And it just had me thinking.”

“谢谢，”雷木斯把手插进兜里，突然变得害羞起来。玛琳友好而安慰地拍了拍他的肩膀。他感激地对她笑了笑。“我最近见了我妈妈，”雷木斯对克里斯托弗解释道，“这让我开始思考。”

 

“You met your mum? I thought your parents were dead.” Christopher scratched his head. Honestly, if it wasn’t written down in a book then he could be incredibly dense about some things.

“你见了你妈妈？我以为你父母都去世了。”克里斯托弗挠了挠头。说实话，如果不是书上写明，他在某些事情上真是太迟钝了。

 

“Just Lyall.” Remus said, calmly, nodding at the trophy.

“只有莱尔。”雷木斯平静地说，点了点奖杯。

 

“So if you mum’s ok, why did you live in a home?”

“所以如果你妈妈没事，为什么你要住在孤儿院？”

 

“Shut up, Chris.” Marlene said, tutting. She slipped her arm through Remus’s, linking them together, “Come on, love, it’s dinner soon.” She began to lead him away.

“闭嘴，克里斯。”玛琳咂嘴说。她挽起雷木斯的胳膊，把他们连在一起，“走吧，亲爱的，快到晚饭时间了。”她开始带他离开。

 

“I didn’t mean to be rude!” Christopher said, hurrying along behind them.

“我不是故意无礼的！”克里斯托弗说，匆匆跟在他们后面。

 

“It’s ok.” Remus reassured him, doing some quick thinking. “My mum’s in the hospital; she’s not been well enough to look after me.” It was only half a lie.

“没关系。”雷木斯安慰他说，快速思考了一下。“我妈妈在医院；她一直身体不好，无法照顾我。”这只是半个谎言。

* * *

 “What was he like?” Remus asked Hope, next time he saw her. A pot of geraniums, this time, bright red and gaudy, with lovely wide leaves like Chinese fans. “他是什么样的人？”雷木斯下次见到霍普时问道。这次带了一盆天竺葵，鲜红而俗丽，叶子宽大像中国扇子。

“Lyall?” She asked. “莱尔？”她问道。

He nodded, braced for impact. 他点点头，做好了心理准备。

“He was the cleverest man I ever met.” Hope said, decisively. “I never understood half the things he said, but I loved to listen - and he loved to talk.” “他是我见过的最聪明的人。”霍普果断地说。“我从来没听懂过他说的一半话，但我喜欢听——而且他喜欢说。”

“Sounds a bit… arrogant?” Remus said, uncomfortably. Hope laughed, “听起来有点……傲慢？”雷木斯不舒服地说。霍普笑了，

“Oh, he was arrogant, all right! He knew it, too. Always had to be right, had to have the last word. We fought like cat and dog over it, sometimes.” She saw Remus’s look of dismay, and hurried to clarify, “I loved him for it, though. I loved how sure he was; how reliable. He never let me down.” “哦，他的确傲慢！他也知道。总是要对，总要有最后一句话。我们有时为此吵得像猫狗一样。”她看到雷木斯的失望表情，急忙澄清道，“但我爱他这一点。我爱他的自信；爱他的可靠。他从未让我失望。”

Yes he did. Remus thought, bitterly. She was forgetful about things like that - perhaps it was her illness, or just a side effect of a shortened life. She was relentlessly optimistic, unable to find fault in the people she loved. 他确实让人失望。雷木斯苦涩地想。她对这些事情忘得一干二净——也许是她的病，或者只是短命的副作用。她总是乐观，对她爱的人找不出任何毛病。

She told him how they’d met, like it was a fairytale. 她告诉他他们是如何相遇的，就像一个童话。

“I was walking home from work one afternoon - I was an operator at the telephone exchange, back then. I took a shortcut - same one I always did, from the main bus stop in town - through a little bit of woodland. Then, from out of nowhere, this man came and attacked me - a vagrant, I thought, or an escaped prisoner. I screamed, and it was Lyall who saved me. Well, I loved him the moment he held me in his arms; he was a hero. Of course, he told me later it had only been a boggart, but it was still very brave, wasn’t it?” “有一天下午，我下班回家——那时我在电话交换台做操作员。我抄了一条近路——就是我经常走的那条，从市中心的主要公交车站穿过一小片树林。然后，突然出现了一个男人，袭击了我——我以为是个流浪汉，或者是逃犯。我尖叫起来，是莱尔救了我。当他抱着我的时候，我立刻爱上了他；他是个英雄。当然，他后来告诉我，那只是一只博格特，但那仍然很勇敢，不是吗？”

Remus nodded absently. 雷木斯心不在焉地点了点头。

“I’ve met some people who knew him,” He said, “They’ve told me he had a bad temper.” “我见过一些认识他的人，”他说，“他们告诉我他脾气不好。”

“What? No.” She frowned, “He got het up sometimes - don’t we all? But he was always kind, and always gentle with us. He hated violence.” “什么？不。”她皱起眉头，“他有时会激动——难道我们不都会吗？但他总是很善良，对我们总是很温柔。他讨厌暴力。”

“Right.” Remus nodded. He never knew what to think about Lyall. Nothing about him ever felt real, because nothing Remus ever learnt could wipe away what he’d done. “对。”雷木斯点点头。他从来不知道该怎么想莱尔。关于他的一切都不真实，因为雷木斯学到的任何东西都无法抹去他所做的事。

Conversations with Hope weren’t always difficult. Often they were very pleasant; they talked about small, inconsequential things; likes and dislikes, favourite foods, favourite films or songs. 与霍普的谈话并不总是困难的。通常它们非常愉快；他们谈论一些琐碎、不重要的事情；喜欢和不喜欢的东西，最喜欢的食物，最喜欢的电影或歌曲。

She loved The Beatles, and Fairport Convention - and most of all she liked Simon and Garfunkel. She liked sad songs. She hummed along to ‘The Only Living Boy in New York’, when it came on the record player, but ‘America’ was her favourite, because it made her cry. I’m empty and aching and I don’t know why. 她喜欢披头士，和费尔波特大会——最喜欢的是西蒙和加芬克尔。她喜欢悲伤的歌曲。当唱片机播放《纽约唯一的活着的男孩》时，她会跟着哼唱，但她最喜欢的是《美国》，因为它让她哭泣。我空虚而痛苦，不知道为什么。

Sometimes she was very unwell, and she dozed, wavering in and out of consciousness. He just sat by and read his book until it was time to go. She even asked him to read to her, once or twice, 有时她病得很重，昏昏欲睡，意识模糊。他只是坐在旁边读书，直到该走的时候。她甚至有一两次让他读给她听，

“I don’t care what it’s about, I just like your voice,” she would smile under heavy eyelids. He liked those times; he really felt like they belonged to each other, then. “我不在乎内容是什么，我只喜欢你的声音，”她在沉重的眼皮下微笑着说。他喜欢那些时刻；那时他真的觉得他们属于彼此。

“Have you asked her why, yet?” Sirius asked him one evening, when he’d returned from a day at the hospital. “你问她为什么了吗？”有一天晚上，天狼星问他，当他从医院回来时。

“Asked her why what?” Remus yawned, stretching out and placing his feet in Sirius’s lap. He thought they could get away with that - it wasn’t too intimate, and the common room was relatively quiet. “问她为什么什么？”雷木斯打了个哈欠，伸展开身体，把脚放在天狼星的腿上。他认为他们可以这样——这并不太亲密，而且休息室相对安静。

“You know. Why she never got in touch.” “你知道的。为什么她从没联系过。”

Remus frowned. He leaned his head back on the arm of the settee and stared up at the ceiling. 雷木斯皱起眉头。他把头靠在沙发扶手上，仰望天花板。

“No.” He said, “I don’t see the point asking.” “没有。”他说，“我觉得没必要问。”

“I’d want to know.” Sirius replied, fiddling with Remus’s bootlaces. “我会想知道。”天狼星回答，摆弄着雷木斯的鞋带。

“Well.” Remus replied, coldly, “That’s you.” “好吧。”雷木斯冷冷地回答，“那是你。”

“Ok,” Sirius replied, “Sorry.” “好吧，”天狼星回答，“对不起。”

Remus felt a twinge of guilt. Sirius had been extremely sensitive about bringing up Hope, letting Remus take the lead when it came to discussing it, so it wasn’t fair to snap. 雷木斯感到一阵内疚。天狼星在提到霍普时一直非常敏感，让雷木斯在讨论时主导，所以他不应该发脾气。

In truth, he was terrified. He wanted very much to know exactly what Hope had been doing with herself for thirteen years, but he knew that there was no answer that would satisfy him. The other children that had been mentioned by the nurse on his first visit were never brought up, and she didn’t wear a wedding ring. There were no other photographs around her hospital bed, and no sign that anyone else was visiting. 事实上，他很害怕。他非常想知道霍普在这十三年里到底在做什么，但他知道没有一个答案能让他满意。第一次探访时护士提到的其他孩子从未被提起，她也没戴结婚戒指。她的病床周围没有其他照片，也没有其他人探访的迹象。

And Remus was selfish. He liked having Hope all to himself; pretending there was no one else in the world. It was the only way they could communicate for now, he decided; to shut out all the noise of other people, and just be themselves together.

而且雷木斯很自私。他喜欢独自拥有霍普；假装世界上没有其他人。他决定这是他们现在唯一的交流方式；排除其他人的噪音，只是彼此在一起。

 

“That’s a big book,” she smiled, waking up halfway through another visit. Daisies, that time; big, cheerful, friendly flowers. “What’s it about?”

“这是一本大书，”她微笑着说，半途中醒来。那次是雏菊；大而愉快，友好的花朵。“这本书讲的是什么？”

 

“History revision.” He explained, closing it carefully, now she was awake. “I’ve got my final exams coming up.”

“历史复习。”他解释道，小心地合上书本，因为她已经醒了。“我有期末考试要准备。”

 

“Clever boy,” she murmured, her eyelids fluttering. “What’s your best subject?”

“聪明的孩子，”她低声说，眼皮颤动。“你最擅长的科目是什么？”

 

“Um… History, I s’pose.” He replied, “But I’m good at Charms, and I like Care of Magical Creatures a lot.”

“嗯……历史吧。”他回答，“但我在咒语学上也不错，我很喜欢魔法生物学。”

 

“Just like your dad,” she smiled, eyes closing. Her face was very pale, that day, and he didn’t try to correct her, she was obviously exhausted. “Maybe you’ll save a pretty girl from a boggart, one day.” She chuckled quietly.

“就像你爸爸一样，”她微笑着，眼睛闭上。那天她的脸色非常苍白，他没有试图纠正她，她显然很疲惫。“也许有一天你会从博格特中救出一个漂亮的女孩。”她轻声笑了。

 

“Yeah, maybe.” He replied. Then, because he felt bad about lying, “I like Transfiguration, too, but my friend Sirius is the best in the class - he can turn himself into a dog and everything.”

“是啊，也许吧。”他回答。然后，因为觉得撒谎不太好，“我也喜欢变形学，但我朋友天狼星在班上最好——他能变成一只狗，什么都会。”

 

She smiled,

她微笑着，

 

“Sirius is a nice name.”

“天狼星是个好名字。”

 

“Yeah. Sirius Black.” Remus said. He was glad her eyes were closed, it made things easier. “He’s my best friend. ...I mean, I have a lot of friends, but he’s the most… we’re probably going to live together, after school finishes.”

“是的。天狼星·布莱克。”雷木斯说。他很高兴她的眼睛闭着，这让事情变得更简单。“他是我最好的朋友……我的意思是，我有很多朋友，但他是最……我们可能会在学业结束后一起住。”

 

“That’ll be nice…” she fell asleep again. Remus fidgeted for a bit, feeling anxious, then returned to his revision. He woke her up just before he had to leave, though.

“那会很不错……”她又睡着了。雷木斯焦虑地坐了一会儿，然后回到复习中。他在不得不离开之前唤醒了她。

 

“See you next week?” She clasped his hand with surprising strength.

“下周见？”她以惊人的力量握住他的手。

 

“No, sorry,” he shook his head, “I… next Friday is a full moon, so I won’t be able to travel on Saturday.”

“不，抱歉，”他摇摇头，“我……下周五是满月，所以我星期六不能旅行。”

 

“Full moon…” she murmured, taking a few seconds to understand. When the fog cleared she had a sharp look of panic which Remus couldn’t bear,

“满月……”她低声说，花了几秒钟才理解过来。当迷雾散去，她脸上露出了一种雷木斯无法忍受的尖锐恐慌表情，

 

“Maybe I can come on Sunday, though. I’ll see.” He bent down and kissed her cheek, very lightly. She began to cry, and he had to go. He was halfway across the ward when he heard her mutter, very quietly,

“也许我可以在周日来。我要看看。”他弯下腰，轻轻吻了吻她的脸颊。她开始哭泣，他不得不离开。当他走到病房中间时，他听到她非常低声地喃喃自语，

 

“Damn you, Lyall Lupin, you bastard.”

“该死的你，莱尔·卢平，你这个混蛋。”

Notes:Song lyric taken from 'America' by Simon and Garfunkel.

Remus first discovers the duelling trophy in Chapter 35.

 

Chapter 143: Seventh Year: Breakdown 

If I seem a little jittery I can't restrain myself

I'm falling into fancy fragments

Can't contain myself

I gotta breakdown, breakdown, yeah

I gotta breakdown, breakdown, yeah

Friday 24th March 1978  
1978年3月24日，星期五
03:00 AM  
凌晨3点
Remus rolled over again. He couldn’t sleep; he was too hot with the duvet on; too cold if he pushed it off. His legs kept getting all tangled up in the bedsheets, his pillow had lumps in it, and somewhere in Gryffindor tower a tap was dripping, which was driving him insane. On top of this, he just didn’t feel tired.  
雷木斯又翻了个身。他无法入睡；盖着被子太热，推开被子又太冷。他的腿总是缠在床单里，枕头上有 lumps，格兰芬多塔楼里某处的水龙头在滴水，这让他快疯了。再加上他根本感觉不到疲倦。
He sighed heavily and rolled over again. Beside him, Sirius groaned.  
他重重地叹了口气，再次翻身。在他旁边，天狼星发出了呻吟声。
“Moony, you are my best friend, and I would probably dive in front of a curse for you, but if you wake me up one more time then I cannot be held responsible for my actions.” He said this all without opening his eyes.  
“月亮，你是我最好的朋友，我可能会为了你而冒着诅咒，但如果你再把我叫醒一次，那我就不对自己的行为负责了。”他说这话时没有睁开眼睛。
“Sorry,” Remus whispered, “I think it’s the moon, I can’t sleep.”  
“对不起，”雷木斯低声说，“我想是满月的原因，我无法入睡。”
“Mmmrgh.”  
“嗯嗯。”
“Sorry.”  
“对不起。”
He got out of bed. It was no use keeping both of them up.  
他下了床。让他们俩都无法入睡是没用的。
Outside of the bed curtains, in the early morning gloom of their bedroom, Remus stood at the window for a while. It was a clear night, and the moon was almost full. Just one slither missing; he wondered if he had ever seen a full moon with his own human eyes. Perhaps he’d been too young to remember.  
在床帘外面，在他们卧室的黎明朦胧中，雷木斯站在窗边看了一会儿。今夜月光明亮，月亮几乎是满的。只差一丝，他想知道自己是否曾经用人类的眼睛见过满月。也许那时他还太年轻，记不起了。
The forest beneath the moon was black with shadow, and it seemed unbelievable to Remus that in only a few hours he and his friends would be running through those dark mysterious trees as if it was their own personal playground. Just now, it looked terrifying; a great black pit that could swallow you whole.  
月光下的森林黑暗而阴影重重，雷木斯难以相信，只过几个小时，他和他的朋友们就会在那些黑暗神秘的树林中奔跑，就像那是他们自己的游乐场一样。现在看起来却很吓人；像一个能吞噬你的大黑洞。
Only four more moons at Hogwarts. And then what?  
霍格沃茨只剩下四个满月。然后呢？
He put that thought away for another time.  
他把这个念头搁置到另一个时间。
Remus looked at his own empty bed, unenthusiastically. The curtains hadn’t been drawn over for weeks, because he never slept there; only used it for homework. As a consequence it was covered with books, broken quills, chocolate wrappers, scrunched up balls of paper. Even if it had been tidy, the sheets looked somehow cold and uninviting in the moonlight. He’d have sighed again, but he didn’t want to make any more noise.  
雷木斯不情愿地看着自己空荡荡的床。窗帘已经好几周没拉开过，因为他从不在那儿睡觉；只是用来做作业。因此，床上满是书本、破损的羽毛笔、巧克力包装纸、揉成一团的纸球。即使它整洁些，月光下的床单看起来也冷冷的、不太诱人。他本来还想再叹一口气，但不想再发出任何声音。
There were some biscuits in the common room. A tin of garibaldi’s from Mrs Potter. If he took his book and his fags, he could have quite a pleasant few hours before he finally fell asleep or it was time for breakfast. His stomach growled, and that was the decision made. He pulled on a pair of thick socks (they were Peter’s, actually, but he never minded lending stuff like that too much), picked up his wand and his book, and crept down to the common room, careful to step over the squeaky stair as he did.  
休息室里有些饼干。是波特夫人的加里波尔迪饼干罐。如果他带上书和烟，他可以在最后入睡或吃早餐之前享受几个愉快的小时。他的胃咕咕叫，这让他做出了决定。他穿上一双厚厚的袜子（其实是彼得的，但他不介意借这些东西），拿起魔杖和书，小心地踩过吱吱作响的楼梯，悄悄下到休息室。
As Remus pushed open the door to the common room, he realised too late that he was not alone. The fireplace was roaring, and the lamps around the couches glowing warmly. A figure was curled up on the largest red velvet settee, wrapped in a thick maroon blanket, with just a long black plait poking out of the top. In the armchair, clutching a mug of warm ovaltine, staring fixedly at the fire, was Marlene. She looked up as he entered, and Remus had no choice but to smile affably and approach her.  
当雷木斯推开休息室的门时，他才意识到自己不是一个人。壁炉里火焰熊熊，沙发上的灯光温暖地闪烁。一个身影蜷缩在最大的红色天鹅绒沙发上，裹着厚厚的酒红色毛毯，只露出一条长长的黑色辫子。在扶手椅上，紧握着一杯热奥法丁，目不转睛地盯着火焰的，是玛琳。她看到他进来时抬起了头，雷木斯只能和蔼地微笑着走向她。
As he neared, he could see that her eyes were dark and heavy, her cheeks red and tearstained.  
当他走近时，他看到她的眼睛又暗又重，脸颊红润且沾满泪痕。
“Hi,” he said, low, so as not to wake Yaz.  
“嗨，”他说，声音低沉，以免吵醒雅兹。
She gave a small, faraway smile, unfurling slightly, wiping her cheeks.  
她露出一个小小的、遥远的笑容，稍微舒展开，擦拭着她的脸颊。
“Hi.”  
“嗨。”
“You ok?” He stood just close enough. He didn’t want to know the answer. He regretted everything, and wished with every fibre of his being that he was back in bed with Sirius, getting kicked in the shin every time he rolled over.  
“你还好吗？”他站得很近。他不想知道答案。他对一切感到后悔，渴望着回到床上和天狼星在一起，每次翻身都被踢到小腿。
Marlene shook her head mournfully, staring at the fire, her eyes filling up with tears. It was a familiar sight, these days, and not just Marlene. Bad news was so common. Family members in hospital, or dead, or - worse than either - missing.  
玛琳悲伤地摇摇头，盯着火焰，眼里充满了泪水。这些天来，这种情景很熟悉，不仅仅是玛琳。坏消息如此常见。家人住院，或者去世，或者——比这两者更糟——失踪了。
“I said he could get in touch through the fireplace, if he wanted to talk tonight.” She whispered, her voice hoarse as an old woman's. “Danny. It's the full moon tomorrow. Well, tonight, I suppose.” She glanced at the grandfather clock.  
“我说过，如果他今晚想谈话的话，可以通过火炉联系我。”她低声说道，声音沙哑得像个老人的。“丹尼。明天是满月。嗯，今晚吧。”她瞥了一眼祖父钟。
“Oh, is it?” Remus assumed as casual an air as possible.  
“哦，是吗？”雷木斯尽可能地装作随意。
Marlene nodded, still looking at the fire.  

玛琳点点头，仍然盯着火焰。
“It has to be tonight, you see; he’s going to
 the ministry tomorrow and they’ll lock him up in the cells there. I wanted to go home for it, but he says there’s nothing I can do.”  
“你看，今晚必须这样；他明天要去魔法部，那里的牢房会把他锁起来。我想回家去看他，但他说我无能为力。”
“I suppose there isn’t.” Remus’s stomach was clenching so hard he wanted to double over, he was so nervous and jittery already. “He’ll be ok…” he tried, hoping he sounded kind.  
“我想也是。”雷木斯的胃紧得让他想要弯腰，他已经如此紧张和神经质。“他会没事的……”他尝试着说，希望听起来温柔些。
“He’ll survive it.” She said, bitterly. “But I don’t think he’ll be ok. It takes a bit of you away, every time. I’ve seen them, at St Mungo’s. And… he told me. How it feels.”  
“他会活下来的。”她苦涩地说。“但我不认为他会好起来。每次都会带走你的一部分。我在圣芒戈见过那些人。还有……他告诉我了。那种感觉。”
“Why?!”  
“为什么？！”，
“I asked.” She shrugged. “Madam Pomfrey says I have a curious mind, that's why I’ll be a good healer. I wanted to know, so I could help. But he was so down after last month, so weak.”  
“我问过。”她耸耸肩。“波莫弗雷夫人说我有好奇心，这就是我会成为一个好治疗师的原因。我想知道，以便能帮忙。但他在上个月之后变得很沮丧，很虚弱。”
“I’m sure just being there for him helps.” Remus tried.  
“我相信只要在他身边就会有帮助。”雷木斯尝试道。
Marlene wiped her eyes again with her sleeves.  
玛琳再次用袖子擦拭眼睛。
“It just doesn’t seem like enough.” She sighed heavily, and her focus seemed to return a bit. She looked at him properly, for the first one, “Sorry love, is everything ok with you? What are you doing up?”  
“这似乎不够。”她重重地叹了口气，她的注意力似乎恢复了一些。她第一次正眼看着他，“对不起，亲爱的，你还好吗？你怎么还没睡？”
“Oh, just couldn’t sleep.” He raised his book to demonstrate.  
“哦，只是无法入睡。”他举起书来展示。
“Me neither. I knew Danny probably wouldn’t try to get through, but I couldn’t go to bed, just in case. Poor Yaz tried her best,” she gave the girl sleeping on the couch an affectionate look. “She’s too good for me by half.”  
“我也一样。我知道丹尼可能不会尝试联系，但我不能上床，以防万一。可怜的雅兹尽力了，”她给了躺在沙发上睡觉的女孩一个充满感情的看法。“她对我太好了。”
“Personally I don’t think anyone’s good enough for you.” Remus said - though it wasn’t him speaking, not really - they were Sirius’s words. He’d noticed himself sounding more and more like Sirius, and found he didn't mind it. Anyway, it made Marlene smile again.  
“我个人觉得没有人配得上你。”雷木斯说——虽然这并不是他自己在说，不完全是——这是天狼星的话。他发现自己越来越像天狼星，觉得没什么不好。无论如何，这让玛琳再次微笑。
“Lovely boy.” She said, softly. “Sit down, eh? You’re making me nervous hovering like that.”  
“可爱的孩子。”她轻声说。“坐下来，好吗？你这样在空中徘徊让我很紧张。”
He sat awkwardly on the sofa opposite Yaz. Marlene sat up, stretching, as though her back hurt. As she unfolded her legs from underneath her a quill fell onto the floor.  
他尴尬地坐在对面沙发上。玛琳坐起身来，伸展着，仿佛她的背部很疼。当她从下面伸展双腿时，一支羽毛笔掉到了地上。
“Oops,” she leaned over to pick it up, “I was going to try and write him a letter. But I don’t know what to say.” She pulled the blank parchment out from the side of the armchair cushion.  
“哎呀，”她俯身去捡起羽毛笔，“我打算试着给他写一封信。但我不知道说什么。”她从扶手椅垫子旁边拿出一张空白的羊皮纸。
Remus sat stiffly with his book on his lap.  
雷木斯僵硬地坐着，书本放在膝盖上。
“Is it really a cell they put him in? At the ministry?” He asked, unable to contain his grim curiosity. She stood up to stretch more, and nodded,  
“真的有牢房把他放在魔法部吗？”他问，无法抑制自己阴郁的好奇心。她站起来伸展，点点头，
“Yeah. Mum said. He wouldn’t tell me about it - which means it must be bad. Mum said it’s better I don’t know too much…”  
“是的。妈妈说的。他不愿告诉我——这意味着一定很糟糕。妈妈说最好不要知道太多……”
“Mmm.” Remus kept his mouth shut, not trusting himself. Marlene tilted her head sympathetically,  
“嗯。”雷木斯保持沉默，不相信自己。玛琳同情地歪了歪头，
“I’m so sorry, Remus, I didn’t even think. I feel awful whinging to you about this, given your situation.”  
“对不起，雷木斯，我没想到。我觉得向你抱怨这件事很糟糕，考虑到你的情况。”
“What?!” He stared up at her, his heart skipping a beat.  
“什么？！”他瞪大眼睛看着她，心跳漏了一拍。
“With your mum being in the hospital,” Marlene replied, yawning, setting down the quill and parchment on the coffee table between them. “No wonder you can’t sleep, either.”  
“你妈妈在医院，”玛琳回答，打了个哈欠，把羽毛笔和羊皮纸放在他们之间的咖啡桌上。“难怪你也无法入睡。”
“Oh, yeah…” He willed himself to calm down. “Yeah. It’s ok, though, I understand.”  
“哦，是的……”他强迫自己冷静下来。“是的。不过没关系，我理解。”
“Can I sit with you for a bit? You can read your book, I won’t bother you.” She asked, biting her lip. “I just don’t want to be the only one awake.”  
“我可以和你坐一会儿吗？你可以看你的书，我不会打扰你。”她咬着嘴唇问。“我只是希望我不是唯一一个醒着的人。”
“Yeah, of course.”  
“嗯，当然。”
To his surprise, she didn’t sit back down, but came over to join him on the couch. She settled in, making herself comfortable, pulling a blanket up to her chin. He pretended to do the same, opening his book and leaning casually against the arm of the chair.  
令他惊讶的是，她没有重新坐回去，而是走过来坐在沙发上。她安顿下来，让自己舒适地靠在沙发上，把毯子拉到下巴处。他假装也这样做，打开书本，随意地靠在椅子扶手上。
“Revision?” She asked, resting her cheek on his shoulder.  
“复习？”她问，脸颊靠在他的肩膀上。
“What else,” he replied. “Advanced Arithmancy.”  
“还有什么，”他回答。“高级算命术。”
“Oh Remus,” she yawned again, her voice thick, “How fascinating .” She relaxed a bit, and rested a hand on his knee. He gave it a quick squeeze for comfort.  
“哦，雷木斯，”她再次打了个哈欠，声音沉重，“多么迷人。”她稍微放松了一些，把手搭在他的膝盖上。他给了她一个简短的安慰握手。
“You know me,” he said softly, joining in her sarcasm, “I live dangerously.”  
“你知道我，”他轻声说，带着她的讽刺，“我活得很危险。”
She gave a quiet chuckle, her eyes closing. He read, and felt her heartbeat steady, her breathing even out, and in only a few minutes she was fast asleep, a dead weight curled up against him. He didn’t mind; it was quite nice.  
她轻轻地笑了笑，眼睛闭上了。他继续阅读，感受到她的心跳稳定下来，呼吸均匀，几分钟后她就快速入睡，像个死重般蜷缩在他身边。他并不介意，这其实
很舒服。
Remus stopped reading after Marlene had fallen asleep. He gently closed his book and just sat pondering for a while. He could smell the salt of her tears drying on her skin, and the anxiety in her blood. And he couldn’t get Danny out of his mind, in an imagined Ministry of Magic cell - probably underground, probably bare and dark and cold…  
玛琳入睡后，雷木斯停止了阅读。他轻轻地合上书本，静静地坐着思索了一会儿。他能闻到她眼泪在皮肤上干了的咸味和她血液中的焦虑。他无法摆脱对丹尼的想象，设想他在魔法部的牢房里——可能在地下，可能是光秃秃、黑暗而寒冷的……
The pain would be a real shock, if you’d never experienced it before, Remus thought. He could well imagine that the second full moon would feel even worse; because you’d know what was coming. No wonder Danny didn’t want to talk about it.  
雷木斯想，如果你从未经历过，这种痛苦将是一个真正的冲击。他可以很容易地想象，第二次满月的感觉会更糟；因为你会知道即将发生什么。难怪丹尼不想谈论这件事。
If what Marlene said was true, then her brother had no one else to ask about it. No one to tell him that if you tried to fight the transformation; if you tried to brace yourself against it, then it only hurt more. That murtlap essence was best for the initial cuts, but if you used muggle disinfectant too then the skin knit back together neater. Then there were the things that Remus wasn’t sure if anyone knew - about the scent of magic, or how you could draw from it. How it made you stronger, as long as you could channel it right. How being a werewolf meant lots of things, and not all of them were awful.  
如果玛琳说的是真的，那她的哥哥就没有其他人可以问了。没有人告诉他，如果你试图抵抗变形；如果你试图让自己做好准备，那么痛苦会更剧烈。那种海刺藤精华对于最初的伤口最有效，但如果你也使用麻瓜消毒剂，皮肤会更整齐地愈合。然后还有雷木斯不确定是否有人知道的事情——关于魔法的气味，或者如何从中汲取。如何让你变得更强，只要你能正确引导它。成为狼人意味着很多事情，而并非所有都是可怕的。
No closer to sleep, Remus reached for the blank bit of parchment and began to write.  
还没有更接近睡眠，雷木斯伸手拿起那张空白的羊皮纸，开始写字。

Taken leave of my senses and I'm in arrears

My legs buckle over, I'm living on my knees

I gotta breakdown, yeah

You gimme breakdown, yeah

I'm gonna breakdown, yeah, uh-huh

雷木斯没有减速，直到他们走到医务室的一半路程。

Saturday 25th March 1978

The transformation hadn’t been as bad as he’d expected - maybe because nothing can ever be that bad, when you truly expect the worst. And the night itself was wonderful; he had run and run and run, until Prongs and Wormtail were lost, miles behind them, and it was just the wolf and the dog, snapping at each other playfully, goading each other on.  
这次变身没有他预期的那么糟糕——也许是因为当你真的期待最糟糕的情况时，什么都不会那么糟糕。而夜晚本身也很美妙；他不停地奔跑，直到詹姆斯和彼得被甩在几英里之外，只剩下狼和狗在嬉戏地咬着对方，激励着对方。
In the morning, once Remus had writhed and twisted back into his human body, he felt as though his bones were made of cooked spaghetti, he was so exhausted. He stumbled back to the hospital wing with Madam Pomfrey, half asleep, and was grateful to collapse into his favourite bed by the far window and sleep the whole morning away. It was blissful, to not be worrying; not fidgeting or clenching his jaw or looking for a distraction.  
早晨，当雷木斯扭曲着回到他的人类身体时，他感觉自己的骨头就像煮熟的意大利面一样，他太累了。他半睡半醒地跟着波莫弗雷夫人回到医务室，感激地倒在靠窗的最爱床上，整整睡了一上午。不必担忧，不必坐立不安，不必咬紧牙关或寻求分散注意力的事物，真是幸福。
It was late afternoon, before Marlene finally heard about the letter.  
直到下午晚些时候，玛琳才终于得知了那封信的事。
The noise of her arguing with Madam Pomfrey woke Remus. He jolted awake, heart beating faster at the sound of raised voices. The first thing he saw was Sirius, fast asleep in the chair next to him, arms folded across his chest, head lolling, feet propped up on the edge of the hospital bedframe. There was a plate of at least twenty millionaire shortcakes on the bedside table.  
她与波莫弗雷夫人争吵的声音吵醒了雷木斯。他被惊醒了，听到提高的声音，心跳加速。他看到的第一件事是天狼星在他旁边的椅子上睡得很香，双臂交叉在胸前，头低垂，脚搭在医务床边的边框上。床头柜上摆着一盘至少二十块的百万富翁短面包。
Sirius’s eyes snapped open a few seconds after Remus, and he blinked, surprised, and frowned.  
天狼星在雷木斯几秒钟后也睁开了眼睛，惊讶地眨了眨眼，皱起了眉头。
“Is that McKinnon?!”  
“那是麦金农吗？！”
“LET ME SEE HIM POPPY!”  
“让我见见他，波莫弗雷夫人！”
“MISS MCKINNON, I ABSOLUTELY WILL NOT HAVE THIS--”  
“麦金农小姐，我绝对不允许这种事——”
“I KNOW HE’S HERE!”  
“我知道他在这里！”
“I SHALL CALL PROFESSOR MCGONAGALL!”  
“我要去叫麦格教授！”
“REMUS?! REMUS LUPIN!”  
“雷木斯？！雷木斯·卢平！”
“I’m here, Marlene,” Remus began to get out of bed, ready to face the music. If it was all over, he’d still made it seven years. He was still legally allowed to perform magic, even if he did get exposed. “It’s ok, Madam Pomfrey,” he called, as Marlene came clattering across the ward, yanking back the screen which hid him.  
“我在这儿，玛琳，”雷木斯开始下床，准备面对一切。如果一切结束了，他也已经坚持了七年。他仍然在法律上被允许施展魔法，即使他被暴露了。“没关系，波莫弗雷夫人，”他喊道，玛琳大步走过病房，拉开了遮住他的帘子。
“Is it true?!” Her hair flew about her face as she stormed in, her eyes wide and wild.  
“是真的吗？！”她闯进来时，头发飞舞，眼睛瞪得大大的，显得疯狂。
She stared at him, and Remus knew she was really seeing him, for the first time; analysing. A natural Healer, Marlene looked at the bed, and Sirius, and Remus’s scars and battered frame, and he knew she was remembering every time he had been tired, or missed a lesson, or had a new scratch. The light of truth flashed her her eyes, and she burst into tears. “You fucking bastard.”  
她盯着他，雷木斯知道她真正第一次看到他；在分析。作为一个天生的治疗师，玛琳看着床，天狼星，以及雷木斯的伤疤和疲惫的身体，他知道她在回忆他每次疲倦、错过课程或有新伤的时刻。真相的光芒闪过她的眼睛，她突然泪水涌出。“你这该死的混蛋。”

她把一张纸扔到床上。那是一封信，折叠起来，经过这么多折腾已经有点磨损。雷木斯用颤抖的手伸手去拿。玛琳站在那里，脸色冷漠，等待他读完。

他展开信纸，看着下面，尽力去读。现在他大多数时间阅读没有问题。但是他仍然非常疲倦，神经紧张，以至于突然间他感觉自己又回到了十一岁，字母似乎在变化，难以理解。

“这太危险了。”她低声说，“你本可以害死某人的。”
“No.” Sirius said, hands on his hips, “It’s all been perfectly safe, ever since first year, hasn’t it, Poppy? Remus would never hurt anyone.”  
“不。”天狼星说道，双手插在腰间，“从一年级开始就一直非常安全，不是吗，波莫弗雷夫人？雷木斯绝不会伤害任何人。”
“Remus wouldn’t.” Marlene met his eyes, “But the wolf might.”  
“雷木斯不会。”玛琳与他的目光相遇，“但狼可能会。”
“I haven’t, not ever.” Remus felt the need to confirm. “We’ve done everything possible.”  
“我没有，绝不会。”雷木斯感到需要确认，“我们已经做了一切可能的保护措施。”
“Are you registered?” She snapped.  
“你有注册吗？”她冷冷地问。
“Er… well almost everything possible.” He conceded.  
“呃……几乎所有可能的措施。”他承认道。
“And you… you just wanted to help Danny? You weren’t trying to… I don’t know, get him on side?”  
“而你……你只是想帮丹尼？你不是想……我不知道，让他站到你这边吗？”
“What side are you talking about, McKinnon?!” Sirius stepped forward, threateningly, “Moony’s on our side. He’s your friend.”  
“麦金农你说的是什么边啊？！”天狼星威胁性地迈前一步，“雷木斯在我们这边。他是你的朋友。”
“I thought he was.” Marlene replied. She wasn’t afraid of Sirius; she could best him on the quidditch pitch any day, and Madam Pomfrey was standing right there.  
“我以为他是。”玛琳回答。她不怕天狼星；她可以在魁地奇场上打败他，波莫弗雷夫人就站在那里。
“I had to keep it secret, Marlene,” Remus pleaded, the tension too unbearable, “I had to, otherwise I could never have come to Hogwarts at all. You know what it’s like when there’s something… different about you. You know what people are like.”  
“玛琳，我不得不保密，”雷木斯
恳求道，紧张到难以忍受，“我必须这样做，否则我根本无法来到霍格沃茨。你知道当你有一些……与众不同的东西时是什么感觉。你知道人们是什么样的。”
He met her eye as he said this, and saw her turn cold with fear as it dawned on her exactly what he was alluding to.  
他说这话时与她对视，看到她随着意识到他暗示的是什么而变得恐惧。
“How dare you.” She said. “How dare you.”  
“你怎么敢。”她说，“你怎么敢。”
“No, I didn’t mean--” He held his hands up, but it was too late.  
“不，我不是那个意思——”他举起手，但已经为时已晚。
“Stay away from my family!” She snapped, before turning on her heel and storming away, in much the same way as she had arrived.  
“离我的家人远点！”她厉声道，然后转身离开，就像她来时一样。
Remus exhaled. He didn’t really feel afraid, though he had no idea what Marlene planned to do next. He wondered vaguely if he could do his NEWT exams by correspondence - or if the Potters would let him stay at theirs without James or Sirius being there. But his head was too much of a muddle to make a proper plan, and he thought he’d rather just get some sleep while he could.  
雷木斯叹了口气。他并不真正感到害怕，尽管他不知道玛琳接下来打算做什么。他模糊地想知道是否可以通过通讯方式参加NEWTS考试——或者波特夫妇是否会让他在没有詹姆斯或天狼星的情况下住在他们家。但他的头脑太混乱了，无法制定一个合理的计划，他觉得不如趁机好好睡一觉。
He lay back down on the bed, Madam Pomfrey and Sirius watching him.  
他躺回床上，波莫弗雷夫人和天狼星在看着他。
“I’m ok.” He said, “Honestly. Just going to have a little rest.”  
“我没事。”他说，“真的。只是要小休一下。”
“I’m going to speak to Professor McGonagall at once.” Madam Pomfrey said, finally.  
“我马上去找麦格教授。”波莫弗雷夫人终于说道。
“I think,” Remus said, sleepily, closing his eyes, “You might be better off talking to Marlene, once she’s calmed down. She respects your opinion. Don’t get her in trouble, she hasn’t done anything wrong.”  
“我觉得，”雷木斯睡意朦胧地说，闭上眼睛，“你还是去找玛琳谈谈吧，等她冷静下来。她尊重你的意见。不要让她陷入麻烦，她没有做错任何事。”
Madam Pomfrey gave him a very soft look, then, and came over to smooth his bedsheets a bit, touching his hand gently before leaving.  
波莫弗雷夫人给了他一个非常柔和的目光，然后走过来轻轻整理了一下他的床单，在离开前轻轻触碰了他的手。
“Hasn’t done anything wrong.” Sirius muttered, scuffing his feet against the flagstone floor. “She’s being a bigoted little cow.”  
“没做错任何事。”天狼星嘟囔道，脚在石板地上摩擦。“她真是个偏执的小母牛。”
“It’s not an uncommon point of view,” Remus sighed, “I might as well get used to it some time.”  
“这并不是一个不常见的观点，”雷木斯叹了口气，“我可能还是得早点习惯。”
“I ought to go and--”  
“我应该去……”
“No.” Remus said, sharply, “Leave her alone.”  
“不。”雷木斯尖锐地说，“别打扰她。”
“But she’s going to--”  
“但她要……”
“She’s going to talk to her friends, first.” Remus said, firmly. “Lily and Mary. I’d rather she talked to them. They’re the best people in this situation.” He yawned.  
“她会先去找她的朋友们谈谈。”雷木斯坚定地说，“莉莉和玛丽。我希望她去找他们。他们在这种情况下是最合适的人。”他打了个哈欠。
“Bloody hell, Moony.” Sirius shook his head. “How can you be so calm?!”  
“天哪，雷木斯。”天狼星摇了摇头。“你怎么能这么冷静？！ ”
“I’m knackered.” Remus replied. And it was the last thing he said for hours.  
“我累坏了。”雷木斯回答道。接下来几小时内他没有再说话。

 * * *

The thing was, whichever way it went, Remus couldn’t see much of a future for himself at Hogwarts anyway. He was grateful, obviously, for everything Dumbledore, McGonagall and Madam Pomfrey had done for him. He’d loved every one of his subjects (except Potions, maybe) and above all he had a group of friends who were dearer to him than any family would ever be. But the good things would stay good, if he had to go.  
问题是，无论结果如何，雷木斯自己也看不到在霍格沃茨的未来。他显然对邓布利多、麦格教授和波莫弗雷夫人所做的一切心怀感激。他爱过每一门课程（也许除了魔药课），最重要的是，他有一群比任何家人都亲近的朋友。但即使他必须离开，那些美好的事物也会保持美好。
He might have more time to spend with Hope. More time to dedicate to winning this terrible war. Remus was no longer really learning anything at school that he hadn’t already got from books. He yearned for practical experience; he wanted to be truly tested. You didn’t need NEWTs for that, just a well stocked library and enough nerve. Remus had everything he needed now, to do the thing he had wanted to do almost all his life.  
他可能会有更多时间与霍普在一起。更多时间致力于赢得这场可怕的战争。雷木斯在学校里已经没有真正学到任何书本以外的东西。他渴望实践经验；他想要真正的考验。你不需要NEWTS，只需要一个充足的图书馆和足够的勇气。雷木斯现在拥有了一切，他可以做他几乎一生都想做的事。
If Marlene got him dismissed from school, then Remus was finally free to seek out Greyback.  
如果玛琳让他被学校开除，那么雷木斯就可以最终自由去寻找格雷伯克。
The idea had been ticking away ever since he learnt the werewolf's name. And that night he’d written to Danny, everything seemed very clear.  
这个想法自从他了解到那只狼人名字以来就一直在盘旋。那天晚上他给丹尼写了信，一切似乎变得非常清晰。
It was the thing he was born to do. Almost as if he had inherited the task from Lyall.  
这正是他生来要做的事。几乎就像是他从莱尔那里继承了这个任务。
Gawky, insignificant, second-class Remus Lupin was never going to bring down anyone so insidiously terrible and all powerful as Lord Voldemort. But the wolf in him knew he might have a chance at Fenrir Greyback. Remus knew it might kill him, but he was bloody well going to do some damage first.  
笨拙、不重要、二等公民的雷木斯·卢平永远无法击败像伏地魔那样阴险恐怖而全能的敌人。但他内心的狼知道他可能有机会对付芬里尔·格雷伯克。雷木斯知道这可能会杀了他，但他一定要先造成一些伤害。
He’d said nothing to Sirius about this. As far as they’d come together, Remus was deeply ashamed of his own desire for revenge; his inability to tame that reckless rage. Sirius looked to him for self control; for a reasonable, measured response, and Remus wasn’t about to shatter that illusion and risk ruining everything that worked about their dynamic.  
他没有对天狼星提起这事。尽管他们一起走过了很多路，雷木斯对自己复仇的欲望深感羞愧；对那种鲁莽的愤怒无法驾驭。天狼星对他寄予自控的期望；期望一个合理、冷静的回应，雷木斯不想打破这种幻想，冒险破坏他们关系中一切有效的部分。
Anyway, Remus was eighteen now, and muggle or wizard, he could make choices for himself, no matter how dangerous. And if it took upsetting Marlene to kick everything off, then at least he’d been able to help her brother in some small way. One of Matron’s fatalistic catchphrases popped into his head, then: “ no good deed goes unpunished”. Though what good deeds Matron had ever done, he didn’t know.  
无论如何，雷木斯现在已经十八岁，无论是麻瓜还是巫师，他都可以为自己做出选择，不管多么危险。如果要让玛琳不高兴才能开始一切，那么至少他能以某种小方式帮助她的兄弟。然后，院长的宿命论口号出现在他的脑海中：“善行不免受惩罚”。尽管他不知道院长曾经做过什么善事。
It was dinner time, when he woke for the second time that day. Sirius wasn’t there any more, but the marauder’s map was tucked under Remus’s pillow. He withdrew it and saw that the marauders were all in the common room, Mary and Lily close by. There was a chicken pie on a plate by his bedside, magically kept warm somehow - Remus hadn’t worked it out yet, maybe a charm on the plate?  
这是一天中他第二次醒来的晚餐时间。天狼星已经不在了，但地图被藏在雷木斯的枕头下。他拿出地图，看到悍马们都在公共休息室，玛丽和莉莉也在附近。他床边的盘子上有一块鸡肉派，不知怎么的被魔法保持温暖——雷木斯还没搞明白，可能是盘子上的某个咒语？
He decided he would eat before anything else, and did so in silence, thinking at a mile a minute, as if his brain was making up for all the time he’d wasted sleeping. He scanned the map for Marlene. She was in the girls’ dorm, with Yaz.  
他决定先吃东西，然后一言不发地吃着，思维飞快运转，就像他的脑袋在弥补所有睡觉浪费的时间一样。他扫描了地图，寻找玛琳。她在女生宿舍，和雅兹在一起。
He didn’t know if that was good or bad. No angry mobs had come by brandishing pitchforks yet, which was probably a good sign. Madam Pomfrey came over just as he was finishing his second slice of millionaire shortbread. The thick oozy caramel was very comforting.  
他不知道这是否好或坏。还没有愤怒的暴民拿着叉子来找他，这可能是个好兆头。就在他吃完第二片千层短饼时，波莫弗雷夫人过来了。厚厚的焦糖非常令人安慰。
“How are you feeling, dear?” She asked, deep frown lines in her face.  
“你感觉怎么样，亲爱的？”她问，脸上带着深深的皱纹。
“Fine!” He said, brightly. He held out the plate to her, “Want one? I’ll never eat them all.” This was a lie and they both knew it, but Madam Pomfrey was polite enough to go along with him.  
“很好！”他说，神采奕奕地。把盘子递给她，“要一块吗？我永远吃不完。”这句话是谎言，他们都知道，但波莫弗雷夫人足够礼貌，愿意顺着他。
“Well… as there’s no one else on the ward today,” she smiled, sitting in the chair beside him and accepting a sweet. She conjured up two saucers, then poured steaming hot tea from her wand, and it was all very pleasant, but Remus could feel a Big Talk coming on.  
“好吧……因为今天病房里没有其他人，”她微笑着，坐在他旁边的椅子上，接受了一块糖果。她用魔杖召唤了两个茶杯，然后倒出了冒着热气的茶，一切都很愉快，但雷木斯能感觉到一场重要的谈话即将开始。
“I’ll go, after this,” he said, “Get out of your hair.”  
“我吃完这个就走，”他说，“不会再打扰你。”
“You’re never any trouble, Remus,” she replied kindly, blowing on her tea to cool it. “Even when you were a little boy.”  
“你从来没有麻烦过，雷木斯，”她善意地回答道，吹着茶水以使其冷却。“即使你还是个小男孩的时候也是如此。”
“I was a right little git, in first year.” Remus countered. She smiled and shook her head,  
“我一年级的时候是个讨厌鬼。”雷木斯反驳道。她笑了，摇了摇头，
“Not at all. A diamond in the rough.”  
“完全不是。你是块未经雕琢的璞玉。”
“Oh.” He said, feeling himself heat up. Anyone else he’d have told to ‘shuddup’ or ‘piss off’, but he would never, ever have a rude word to say to Madam Pomfrey.  
“哦。”他说
，感觉自己脸红了。其他人他可能会告诉他们“闭嘴”或“滚开”，但他绝对不会对波莫弗雷夫人说一句粗鲁的话。
“It’s flown by, the last few years,” she sighed, “I remember that little scrap of a thing you were; all eyes and elbows. You’ve grown into a fine young man.”  
“这几年过得很快，”她叹了口气，“我记得你以前那副小模样；全是眼睛和肘子。你已经成长为一个出色的年轻人。”
He wished she’d stop, as nice as all of this was; he didn’t know what to do with it. “And you deserve every success, Remus, do you hear me?” She continued, “It’s not going to be easy for you, after school - and I know you know that.”  
他希望她停下来，尽管这一切都很美好；他不知道该如何应对。“雷木斯，你值得拥有每一份成功，你听见了吗？”她继续说道，“学校毕业后对你来说不会容易——我知道你知道这一点。”
He nodded.  
他点了点头。
“I’ll be ok.”  
“我会没事的。”
“You will.” She smiled, her eyes brightening with tears, “And if you ever need anything, you know where to reach me.”  
“你会的。”她微笑着，眼中闪烁着泪光，“如果你需要任何帮助，你知道在哪里找到我。”
“Of course.”  
“当然。”
“I knew Danny McKinnon, you know,” She said, clearing her throat, here it comes, Remus thought. But she’d cunningly overpowered him with all that nice stuff, and he just had to grit his teeth and listen now.  
“你知道，我认识丹尼·麦金农，”她说道，清了清喉咙，雷木斯想，这就来了。但她巧妙地用所有那些温暖的话打破了他的防线，他只能咬紧牙关听下去。
“Yeah?” He said, casually, taking another slice of cake.  
“是吗？”他随意地说，拿了一块蛋糕。
“Yes, when he was a student here. Had him in here a hundred times for patching up - he was Gryffindor Beater, like Marlene. He was a bit more outgoing than she is.”  
“是的，当他还是这里的学生时。我这儿接待了他一百次来修补伤口——他是格兰芬多的击球手，和玛琳一样。他比她更外向一些。”
“I dunno,” Remus returned, dryly, “She’s hardly a shrinking violet.”  
“我不知道，”雷木斯干涩地回答，“她可不是什么胆小鬼。”
Madam Pomfrey smirked, despite herself,  
波莫弗雷夫人忍不住微笑，
“No, quite. She has that McKinnon tenacity, and a keen sense of right and wrong.”  
“是的，确实如此。她有麦金农的坚韧，还有对对错的敏锐感。”
“She does.” He sighed. He’d always liked that about Marlene; her straightforwardness, “And I know what you’re going to say - that everything isn’t that simple, that there are shades of grey, and that it doesn’t matter what people think about you, it matters what you do…”  
“确实如此。”他叹了口气。他一直喜欢玛琳的这种直率，“我知道你要说什么——一切并不像表面那么简单，有灰色地带，不在乎别人对你的看法，重要的是你做了什么……”
“Well… yes.”  
“嗯……是的。”
“I know all that, and it’s fine. I knew all that when I wrote to Danny, I even know how Marlene would react. But in the end, it didn't matter. The only thing that mattered was helping him.”  
“我知道这些，也没关系。我写信给丹尼时就知道了，我甚至知道玛琳会有什么反应。但最后，这些都无所谓。唯一重要的是帮助他。”
“I’m proud of you, Remus.”  
“我为你感到骄傲，雷木斯。”
That threw him for a loop. His throat constricted, and he almost choked trying to swallow the last of his slice, the sugar turning to acid on its way down. He spluttered and coughed, reaching for the tea to wash it down. Madam Pomfrey got up, smiling. She patted him on the shoulder as he recovered.  
这让他有些惊讶。他的喉咙收缩，几乎因为吞下最后一片蛋糕而窒息，糖在下咽的过程中变成了酸。他呛到并咳嗽，伸手去拿茶水来冲淡。波莫弗雷夫人站起来，微笑着。她在他恢复时拍了拍他的肩膀。
“I’ll let you get on.”  
“我让你继续吧。”
He took a few moments to compose himself before getting up. He brushed the crumbs from the sheets and made the bed, though he knew he didn't really need to. The rest of the sweets he wrapped up into some parchment and carefully slid the package into his bag. He might need them, later.  
他花了几分钟来整理自己，然后才起身。他扫去床单上的碎屑，整理了床铺，虽然他知道自己其实不需要这样做。他把剩下的糖果包在一些羊皮纸里，小心翼翼地把包裹滑进了他的包里。他可能会在以后需要它们。
Remus was almost surprised by how calm he felt. There was a sense of closing; of coming to an inevitable end. Someone was always going to find out, he told himself. He’d have been an idiot to think they could all hide such a big thing forever. They’d done a bloody good job, but it had all been luck, and they’d taken so many risks. At least this way, it had been Remus’s choice; he’d controlled it as much as he could. This way, the marauders were safe too. No one would know what they’d all been up to every full moon.  
雷木斯几乎对自己感到平静感到惊讶。感觉到了一种结局的感觉；一种不可避免的结局。他告诉自己，总会有人发现的。他要是以为他们能永远隐藏这样一个大秘密，那才真是傻子。他们做得非常好，但全凭运气，他们冒了很多风险。至少这样一来，这个决定是雷木斯自己的选择；他尽可能地掌控了局面。这样一来，悍马们也安全了。没有人会知道他们在每个满月期间都在干什么。
He made his way slowly back to Gryffindor Tower. He was all stiff from sleeping all day, and was grateful for the opportunity to stretch his legs in privacy. Sirius hadn’t mentioned the hip problem for a while, but Remus saw him purse his lips, or frown whenever he noticed Remus limping or rubbing his side.  
他慢慢地回到了格兰芬多塔楼。他因为整天睡觉而全身僵硬，感激能有机会在隐私中伸展一下腿。天狼星已经有一段时间没有提到髋部问题了，但雷木斯注意到他每当看到雷木斯跛行或揉着侧腰时，就会抿紧嘴唇或皱眉。
“Blatherskite,” he said to the fat lady, who barely looked up from filing her fingernails to let him through.  
“胡说八道，”他说着，对着肥婆，那位几乎没有抬头看自己，只是让他进去了。
He entered the room and felt six pairs of eyes on him at once. Steeling himself and pasting on a careless smile, he approached his friends, sitting in their usual place, taking up two sofas and an armchair.  
他进入房间时，感到六双眼睛同时盯着他。鼓起勇气，挂上一个随意的笑容，他走向他的朋友们，他们坐在他们的常坐位置上，占据了两张沙发和一个扶手椅。
“Moony!” Sirius got up from where he’d been sprawling to make room, “I was just going to come up and see if you were awake.”  
“月亮！”天狼星从他伸展开的姿势中站起来，腾出位置，“我正打算上来看看你是否醒了。”
“I’m awake,” he said redundantly, taking his seat.  
“我醒了，”他说，重复了一遍，坐下了。
“Sirius told us what you did.” Peter said, as if he couldn’t contain himself. He was fiddling with a chess piece - there was a game going on, but Remus couldn’t tell who Peter was playing.  
“天狼星告诉我们你做了什么。”彼得说，似乎无法抑制自己。他在摆弄一个棋子——游戏正在进行，但雷木斯看不出彼得在和谁对弈。
“Good,” Remus nodded. “Er… anyone spoken to Marlene?”  
“很好，”雷木斯点头。“呃……
有人和玛琳谈过吗？”
“We got yelled at,” Mary sighed, indicating herself and Lily. “I think she's mostly hurt that she was the last to find out.”  
“我们被训斥了，”玛丽叹了口气，指着自己和莉莉。“我觉得她主要是因为是最后一个知道这件事而感到伤心。”
“Mm.”  
“嗯。”
“She's not said much else, though. Been locked away with Yaz.”  
“不过，她没说太多其他的话。一直锁在和雅兹在一起。”
“Right.”  
“对。”
“Listen, Moony,” James leaned over, eyes very serious, “We’ve been talking, and remember fifth year? Dumbledore stopped Snape from telling everyone. He can stop Marlene too, if it comes to that.”  
“听着，月亮，”詹姆斯俯身过来，眼神非常严肃，“我们一直在讨论，还记得第五年吗？邓布利多阻止了斯内普告诉大家。他也可以阻止玛琳，如果到了那一步的话。”
“He might.” Remus nodded, though he wasn’t so sure. He might serve Dumbledore better out of school now than he could have at sixteen. Especially considering the contacts Remus had already made. “But leave him out if it for now, ok?”  
“他可能会。”雷木斯点了点头，尽管他并不太确定。他现在可能比在十六岁时更能为邓布利多服务。尤其是考虑到雷木斯已经建立的联系。“但现在先不让他插手，好吗？”
“Why did you do it?!” Peter asked, still clutching the chess piece.  
“你为什么要这样做？！”彼得问道，仍然紧握着棋子。
“To help Danny.” Remus replied, surprised. He looked at all of them, “He was alone, no one was helping him, Marlene told me that herself.”  
“为了帮助丹尼。”雷木斯回答，感到惊讶。他看着他们所有人，“他一个人，没人帮他，玛琳亲口告诉我的。”
“But Remus…” Lily said, “You knew how she would feel about it. You knew she wouldn’t understand.”  
“但雷木斯……”莉莉说，“你知道她会对这件事有怎样的感受。你知道她不会理解。”
“I knew that. But it was for Danny.” Remus repeated, firmly.  
“我知道那点。但这是为了丹尼。”雷木斯坚定地重复道。
They all promised to give it time, and see what Marlene decided to do next. Lily and Mary vowed that they would do everything they could, that night in their dorm, they would explain, try to convince her. Remus thanked them, because he knew how much they cared about him.  
他们都承诺给玛琳一些时间，看看她接下来决定做什么。莉莉和玛丽发誓他们会尽全力，那晚在宿舍里，他们会解释，尽力说服她。雷木斯感谢他们，因为他知道他们有多么关心他。
They had a quiet evening. Remus played chess with Peter and lost, then Sirius took over and they tied. James and Lily quizzed each other on potion ingredients and Mary half heartedly worked on job applications.  
他们度过了一个安静的晚上。雷木斯和彼得下棋输了，然后天狼星接管了，他们打成了平局。詹姆斯和莉莉互相提问关于魔药的成分，玛丽半心半意地处理工作申请。
“Half boring muggle secretarial stuff to please mum and half boring ministry of magic stuff to please McGonagall,” She sighed.  
“有一半无聊的麻瓜秘书工作是为了让妈妈高兴，另一半无聊的魔法部工作是为了让麦格教授高兴，”她叹了口气。
Eventually they went to bed, one by one, and though Remus had barely been awake for three hours that day, he climbed the stairs yawning. Sirius had been very patient. He hadn’t said so much as a word yet, and Remus knew how difficult that must be for him. So when they were finally in bed, and as alone as they could ever be at Hogwarts, he lay quietly on his back and stared up at the velvet hangings, and let Sirius speak.  
最后，他们一个一个上了床。尽管雷木斯那天几乎只醒了三个小时，但他还是打着哈欠爬上了楼梯。天狼星一直非常耐心。他还没有说过一句话，雷木斯知道这对他来说一定很困难。因此，当他们终于躺在床上，尽可能地独处时，他静静地躺在背上，仰望着天鹅绒帷幔，让天狼星说话。
“I won’t let her do this.” Sirius whispered into his ear, reaching for his hand, “I’ll talk to her, Mary and Lily’ll talk to her, and we’ll make her understand. McGonagall and Madam Pomfrey - they’ll want to help you, she'll listen to them if she won’t listen to her friends. Or Dumbledore. James could kick her off the team - anything. We won’t lose you, Moony, you’ve worked too hard, you’re not getting kicked out just for trying to be nice to that ungrateful, stuck up, intolerant…”  
“我不会让她这样做。”天狼星低声对他说，伸手握住他的手，“我会和她谈谈，玛丽和莉莉也会和她谈谈，我们会让她明白的。麦格教授和波莫弗雷夫人——他们会想要帮助你，如果她不听她的朋友，那她会听他们的。或者邓布利多。詹姆斯可以把她踢出球队——任何事情。我们不会失去你，月亮，你付出了太多努力，你不会因为试图对那个不知恩怜、傲慢、无法容忍的……人好而被踢出去的……”
“It's going to be ok, Padfoot.” Remus said.  
“会没事的，垫脚石。”雷木斯说道。
“Exactly!” Sirius nodded, his hair rustling against the pillow, “Exactly, because we’re going to stop her.”  
“没错！”天狼星点头，他的头发在枕头上沙沙作响，“没错，因为我们会阻止她。”
“No, I mean - it doesn’t matter what happens; it's going to be ok. If I leave in three months or I have to go tomorrow, everything will still be ok.”  
“不，我是说——无论发生什么；都会没事的。如果我三个月后离开，或者明天必须离开，一切仍然会没事。”
“But your NEWTs!”  
“但你的巫师等级考试！”
“Well I was looking forward to completely destroying you in History and Charms…”  
“嗯，我本来期待在历史和咒语上彻底击败你的……”
“And Arithmancy, I’ve been copying off you all year.”  
“还有算命学，我整年都在抄你的东西。”
“And Arithmancy.” Remus laughed. “But… well the NEWTs don’t mean much. I still won’t be able to enter any of the ministry training programmes without registering as a werewolf - and I’m not going to do that, not ever. I dunno if I even really want to do that sort of job. What I want is to start changing things. That's why I wrote to Danny in the first place.”  
“还有算命学。”雷木斯笑了。“不过……嗯，巫师等级考试没什么意义。我仍然无法进入任何魔法部培训项目而不注册为狼人——而且我绝不会这么做。我不确定我是否真的想做那种工作。我想做的是开始改变现状。这就是我最初写信给丹尼的原因。”
“...you mean you want to get kicked out?!”  
“……你是说你想被开除？！”
“I don’t think it will come to that. I don’t think Marlene would, even if she’s angry. But she might ask me to leave, and if it's what she wants, then I will.”  
“我不认为会变成这样。我不认为玛琳会这么做，即使她生气。但她可能会让我离开，如果这是她想要的，那我会离开。”
“And join the war.” Sirius finished. His voice sounded strange. Not bad, but Remus knew he understood.  
“然后参战。”天狼星补充道。他的声音听起来很奇怪。不是坏的，但雷木斯知道他理解了。
“Yes, I suppose you could put it that way.” Remus nodded.  
“是的，我想你可以这么说。”雷木斯点了点头。
“I’ll come with you, then. I don’t need NEWTs either, I’m a Black.”  
“那我会和你一起去。我也不需要巫师等级考试，我是布莱克家族的人。”
“I wouldn't ask you to do that.”  
“我不会要求你这么做。”
“I know. But I will. We’ll go together.”  
“我知道。但我会的。我们会一起去
的。”
“I suppose we will.”  
“我想我们会的。”
They lay together in silence. The air was heavy with the understanding that the next few months might bring dramatic changes, and neither of them were quite ready for that. But, together, they could face it all.  
他们静静地躺在一起。空气中弥漫着对接下来几个月可能带来剧变的理解，他们都还没有完全准备好。但在一起，他们可以面对一切。

 

Notes:Song at the beginning is Germ Free Adolescents by X-ray Spex

 

Chapter 145: Seventh Year: What We Lack 

 

They were wonderful promises, but it wasn’t to be. Remus would not have the chance to make a mysterious and dignified early exit from Hogwarts, and Sirius would not get the opportunity to prove he would follow his Moony anywhere.

这些承诺都很美好，但注定不会实现。雷木斯没有机会神秘而庄重地提前离开霍格沃茨，天狼星也没有机会证明他会跟随他的月亮到任何地方。

 

 

Later - after the war was over and everything else was over too - Remus would wonder whether things might have gone differently if he and Sirius had left school then. Perhaps they could have kept each other closer, or by removing themselves they could have kept other people safer.

后来——战争结束，一切都结束了——雷木斯会想，如果他和天狼星那时就离开学校，事情是否会有所不同。也许他们可以让彼此更加亲近，或者通过离开，他们可以让其他人更加安全。

 

 

Anyway. It didn’t happen, and it did no good to dwell on.

反正。这件事没有发生，沉溺于此也没有好处。

 

 

For years and years afterwards, once the agony of all those funerals and obituaries and memorials and speeches had faded, Remus would be left with memories of his last months at Hogwarts, when they had been stupid and naive and indescribably happy without even knowing it.

在随后的多年里，一旦那些葬礼、讣告、纪念活动和演讲的痛苦消退，雷木斯将只剩下对霍格沃茨最后几个月的回忆，那时他们无知、天真、幸福得无法形容，甚至不知道。

 

Wednesday 29th March 1978

The weekend passed quietly; there was homework to complete and quidditch to train for and an enormously complicated prank to plan, and Marlene did not make a move in any direction.
周末平静地度过了；有作业要完成，还有魁地奇训练和一个极其复杂的恶作剧要计划，玛琳没有在任何方向上有所行动。

Sirius and James reported that she attended quidditch practice, and played as well as she ever had, but hadn't spoken to them. Mary said she was still upset, but that she hadn’t made her mind up whether or not to tell.
天狼星和詹姆斯报告说她参加了魁地奇训练，表现得和以前一样好，但没有跟他们说话。玛丽说她仍然很不高兴，但她还没决定是否要说出来。

They were well into the next week by the time Marlene finally decided to approach Remus again. She caught him alone - which was rare, these days.
等到玛琳最终决定再次接触雷木斯时，他们已经进入了下一周。她抓住了他独自一人——这在这些日子里很少见。

He was tidying up the Charms classroom following a revision session, just before the Wednesday ‘inter-house-prank-planning-co-operative’ meeting. Usually Chris helped, but he was down with a head cold, and had taken the afternoon off. Remus had half wanted to call off the group altogether. It all seemed so futile; learning and learning and learning - for what? To pass an exam, get a good mark, and then? If Greyback didn’t kill him before he was twenty then he would still be unemployable. But everyone seemed to like the study groups, and he hated letting them down.
他在一次复习课后整理咒语教室，正好在星期三的“跨学院恶作剧计划合作”会议之前。通常是克里斯帮忙，但他感冒了，下午请了假。雷木斯一度想完全取消小组活动。一切似乎如此徒劳；学习、学习、再学习——为了什么？为了通过考试，获得好成绩，然后呢？如果格雷伯克在他二十岁之前没有杀了他，他仍然会找不到工作。但每个人似乎都喜欢这些学习小组，他讨厌让他们失望。

She entered the room smelling of herbs from the greenhouse - rosemary and sage and rich earthy soil. He turned, and unconsciously backed himself against a wall.
她走进房间，身上带着温室里草药的气味——迷迭香、鼠尾草和丰富的泥土气息。他转过身来，不自觉地靠在了墙上。

“Hello.” He said.
“你好。”他说道。

She stood still for a while, staring at him in total silence, before replying.
她站了一会儿，一言不发地盯着他，才回答道。

“Hello. I’m furious with you.”
“你好。我对你很生气。”

“I know.” He nodded, trying to be understanding, “I think that’s fair enough. Are… um. Are you ready to talk about it?”
“我知道。”他点了点头，尽量表现得理解，“我觉得这很公平。你……嗯。你准备好谈谈了吗？”

“No.” She shot, folding her arms. She glared at him, and he averted his eyes, like a supplicant begging forgiveness. He heard her fidget a bit, and sigh impatiently. “But Danny says I have to.”
“不。”她冷冷地说，抱着胳膊。她瞪着他，他像一个乞求原谅的祈求者一样移开了视线。他听到她有些焦躁不安，叹了口气。“但丹尼说我必须这样做。”

Remus consciously avoided smiling, but couldn’t ignore the flood of relief he felt at those words. He looked up again, carefully.
雷木斯刻意避免微笑，但无法忽视听到这些话后感到的释然。他再次小心翼翼地抬起头。

“You’ve spoken to him properly, then?”
“那你跟他好好谈过了吗？”

“Yes. He said he tried the murtlap essence combined with muggle TCP, and he’s healing faster. And you were right about taking a sleeping draught.”
“是的。他说他尝试了将鼠尾草精华与麻瓜TCP结合使用，他的伤愈合得更快了。你说得对，服用安眠药。”

“It’s the best thing, I’ve found. For healing.” Remus replied, warily, averting his eyes again. She made him feel so ashamed of himself.
“我发现这是最好的治疗方法。”雷木斯小心翼翼地回答，再次移开视线。她让他感到很羞愧。

“Everyone knew except me.” Marlene said. She was leaning against the opposite wall now; the whole room between them, the jumble of chairs and desks. “Even Mary.”
“除了我，大家都知道。”玛琳说道。她现在靠在对面的墙上；他们之间隔着整个房间，满是杂乱的椅子和桌子。“连玛丽都知道。”

“She worked it out, I didn’t tell her.”
“她猜到了，我没有告诉她。”

“I always thought you were weird because you were queer.”
“我一直认为你很奇怪，因为你是个怪人。”

He frowned a bit. Was he weird? He didn’t say anything, he couldn’t think of anything that would make it better.
他微微皱了皱眉。他很奇怪吗？他什么也没说，也想不出有什么能让事情变得更好的话。

“You really hurt my feelings, Remus.” Marlene continued, “You lied to me for years. I thought we were friends, I shared things with you I haven’t told anyone else.”
“你真的伤害了我的感情，雷木斯。”玛琳继续说道，“你对我撒谎了好几年。我以为我们是朋友，我和你分享了我没告诉其他任何人的事情。”

“We are friends!” Remus protested, “I’m your friend, anyway.”
“我们是朋友！”雷木斯抗议道，“我至少是你的朋友。”

He sighed heavily. Would it always be like this, when people found out? “Look, I couldn’t tell you; there were too many people involved… Madam Pomfrey, and even Dumbledore. I had to keep it quiet for their sakes, too. And… you’ve made it quite clear, in the past, how you feel about people like me.”
他重重地叹了口气。人们知道真相时总是这样吗？“听着，我不能告诉你；涉及的人太多了……波莫弗雷夫人，甚至还有邓布利多。我也不得不为了他们的利益保密。而且……你过去已经很明确地表达过你对像我这样的人是什么感觉。”

“You should have told me.”
“你应该告诉我。”

“What would you have done?” Remus was getting annoyed now. “Complained? Told everyone? Got me expelled?”
“那你会怎么做？”雷木斯现在有些恼火。“抱怨？告诉大家？让我被开除？”

“I might not have.” She bit her lip and looked away. The less certain she was, the more angry Remus grew.
“我可能不会。”她咬了咬嘴唇，移开了视线。她越是不确定，雷木斯就越是生气。

“Well I didn’t much fancy taking the risk!” He said, “I haven’t got a family, or a real home to go to, in case you’d forgotten. I haven’t got anything going for me outside of this school, so forgive me for doing everything I could to stay.”
“我可不想冒这个险！”他说道，“我没有家人，也没有真正的家可去，万一你忘了的话。我在这所学校之外一无所有，所以请原谅我尽一切可能留在这里。”

“I understand that,” She looked up, quickly, reaching her hands out, “--and I’d never want to cause you any trouble, but Remus, can’t you see how dangerous--”
“我理解这一点，”她迅速抬头，伸出手，“——而且我绝不想给你带来麻烦，但雷木斯，你难道看不出这有多危险——”

“I was eleven! I was only a kid, and this old man shows up and tells me I’m going to magic school - what would you have done?!”
“我才十一岁！我只是个孩子，这个老人出现告诉我我将上魔法学校——你会怎么做？！”

“Don’t shout at me!” She frowned, shrinking a bit. “I didn’t come to shout.”
“不要对我大喊！”她皱了皱眉，缩了缩身子。“我不是来吼的。”

“Sorry.” He muttered. “I didn’t get my chance the other day.”
“对不起。”他喃喃道。“前几天我没有机会。”

“I’m sorry about that.”
“对不起。”

“Good.”
“好。”

They were quiet after that, both looking at the ground, both fidgeting with their hands. Remus could hear Marlene’s heart thudding in a steady, anxious rhythm.
之后他们都很安静，两人都低着头，手指不停地动来动去。雷木斯能听到玛琳心跳的稳重而焦虑的节奏。

“Look.” He said, keeping his voice low and steady, unclenching his fists. “If you want me to leave Hogwarts, then I will. As long as you promise not to get anyone else in trouble, I’m not going to put up a fight.”
“听着。”他说，保持声音低沉而稳定，放松了拳头。“如果你想让我离开霍格沃茨，我就会离开。只要你保证不把其他人也牵扯进去，我不会做任何反抗。”

“But your NEWTs…”
“但你的普通巫师资格考试……”

“They won’t matter if you’re going to tell everyone how dangerous I am.”
“如果你打算告诉大家我有多危险，那它们就无所谓了。”

“You sound like Danny.”
“你听起来像丹尼。”

Quiet again. Remus shook his head, tired and exasperated. He tried a different tack.
再次安静下来。雷木斯摇了摇头，感到疲惫和恼火。他换了种方式。

“How is he, now? The letter said he wanted to meet me?”
“他现在怎么样了？信上说他想见我？”

“He's ok.” She nodded, her eyes a bit bright. “I think it cheered him up, knowing that someone else was going through the same thing.”
“他没事。”她点点头，眼中有些光亮。“我觉得知道还有其他人经历相同的事情让他心情好多了。”

“Yeah,” Remus nodded, “It's something I would have liked. James and Sirius and Pete… they’ve always made sure I never felt alone. So I know how much of a difference it makes.”
“是的，”雷木斯点头道，“这是我也希望的。詹姆斯、天狼星和皮特……他们总是确保我不会感到孤独。所以我知道这有多大的不同。”

Marlene nodded and wiped her eyes.
玛琳点了点头，擦了擦眼睛。

“I’m angry.” She said, tiredly. “But I don’t know if I’m angry with you. You just… it was such a shock, and I’m not sure how many more shocks I can take, these days.”
“我很生气。”她疲惫地说，“但我不知道我是否对你生气。你只是……这真是个震惊，我不确定这些天我还能接受多少这样的震惊。”

He laughed, and didn’t really know why.
他笑了笑，实际上并不知道为什么。

She smiled, weakly. “I’m not going to say anything. I don’t want you to go anywhere. Danny says… he says we need to focus on our similarities, not our differences. Now more than ever. Lily and Mary said the same. I know they’re right, it’s just harder than I expected.”
她虚弱地笑了笑。“我不会说什么的。我不希望你离开。丹尼说……他说我们需要关注我们的相似之处，而不是我们的差异。现在比以往任何时候都更重要。莉莉和玛丽也这么说。我知道她们是对的，只是比我预期的要困难。”

“I can’t have you hating me.” He said, warily.
“我不能让你恨我。”他说，小心翼翼地。

“I don’t hate you.”
“我不恨你。”

“Hating what I am is the same thing.”
“恨我是什么样的人和恨我一样。”

“I’m trying, Remus.” She blinked away tears. “I swear, I’ll try.”
“我在努力，雷木斯。”她抹去了眼泪。“我发誓，我会尽力而为。”

“Thank you.” He nodded.
“谢谢。”他点了点头。

For a split second he was disappointed; he’d been so ready for a change. Knowing he’d have to wait a bit longer stung for a moment, but dissipated quickly, like a door closing. That was that. He would finish school and beat everyone in History - Arithmancy too, probably - and watch the final quidditch game, and get too drunk celebrating with his friends. Greyback would wait.
在那一瞬间，他感到失望；他已经迫不及待地想要改变。知道还要再等一会儿有些刺痛，但很快消散，就像一扇门关上了。就是这样。他将完成学业，击败所有人在历史学上的成绩——可能还有算命术——观看最后的魁地奇比赛，和朋友们庆祝时喝得醉醺醺的。格雷伯克会等的。

“Can I help you with this?” Marlene gestured at the messy classroom. “Potter and Black and their gang of miscreants will be here in a minute to plan their raid on Slytherin…”
“我可以帮你处理这个吗？”玛琳指着那个乱七八糟的教室。“波特和布莱克和他们那帮调皮捣蛋的家伙会很快来这里计划袭击斯莱特林……”

“Yeah, ok,” Remus nodded, and they both began moving the desks. The confrontation seemed to be over, and for now they were both satisfied. He was glad; it had been awful not having Marlene as a friend.
“好，没问题。”雷木斯点了点头，他们开始搬动桌子。争论似乎结束了，现在他们都感到满意。他很高兴；没有玛琳作为朋友是件可怕的事。

Remus and Chris usually used magic to move the classroom furniture back, but Marlene had never been good at locomotion spells, so she just started lifting and pushing things. Remus didn’t want to show off now that they were back on tentative talking terms, so he did his best to match her.
雷木斯和克里斯通常用魔法来搬回教室的家具，但玛琳从未擅长移动咒语，所以她只是开始搬抬东西。现在他们又恢复了试探性的对话，雷木斯不想炫耀，所以尽力配合她。

“I’m going to talk to Mary.” Marlene said, suddenly, lifting a chair and pushing it under a desk. “Yaz wants me to. I told Danny already.”
“我要去找玛丽谈谈。”玛琳突然说道，抬起一把椅子，把它推到一张桌子下。“雅兹让我去。我已经告诉丹尼了。”

“That's good.” Remus smiled, encouragingly. “I’m sure Mary will be fine. She’s the least judgmental person I know.”
“那很好。”雷木斯微笑着鼓励道。“我相信玛丽会没事的。她是我认识的最不具评判性的人。”

“Yeah you’re probably right.” Marlene watched him, thoughtfully as he moved the final table back into place. “Remus?”
“是的，你可能是对的。”玛琳注视着他，思索着他把最后一张桌子摆回原位。“雷木斯？”

“Hm?”
“嗯？”

“Is your limp because of the transformations?”
“你的跛行是因为变形吗？”

“Am I limping?” Remus stood a bit straighter, self conscious.
“我在跛行吗？”雷木斯站得稍微笔直了一些，感到有些自觉。

“Sometimes more than others,” she replied, matter of factly. “I always thought… with your upbringing. Someone did it to you.”
“有时候比其他时候更明显，”她直截了当地回答。“我总是认为……以你的成长背景。有人对你做过这种事。”

 

He shook his head.
他摇了摇头。

“When I was thirteen or so, I think something clicked back into place a bit wonky.” He shrugged. “Gets a bit stiff now and then. I hardly think about it now.”
“当我十三岁左右的时候，我觉得有些东西好像回到了一个不太正常的状态。”他耸了耸肩。“现在有时候会有点僵硬。我现在几乎不怎么考虑它了。”

“Mmm.” She replied, looking thoughtful.
“嗯。”她回答道，显得很深思。

“-- How many times ?!”
“——多少次 ?！”

The door flew open and Lily entered, looking furious, James trailing behind her, Peter and Sirius close behind, both smirking. “We said no pranks until the end of term! We’re supposed to be keeping a low profile, you’re Head Boy !”
门猛地打开，莉莉怒气冲冲地进来了，詹姆斯跟在她身后，皮特和天狼星紧随其后，两人都带着讽刺的笑容。“我们说过考试结束前不要恶作剧！我们应该保持低调，你可是级长！”

“C’mon, Evans,” James said, hands out, “That was nothing, barely even a prank, it was… er…” he cast a pleading glance at Sirius,
“拜托，埃文斯，”詹姆斯说，双手摊开，“这没什么，几乎不算恶作剧，那个……呃……”他向天狼星投去求助的目光，

“High spirits!” Sirius supplied.
“高涨的精神！”天狼星补充道。

“High spirits!” James nodded, grinning.
“高涨的精神！”詹姆斯点了点头，咧嘴笑了。

“All of the bathroom mirrors suddenly reflecting back troll faces is high spirits?!” Lily rounded on them both.
“所有浴室的镜子突然映出巨怪的脸就是高涨的精神？！”莉莉转向他们俩。

It was no good, all three boys collapsed into peals of laughter.
没用，三个男孩都笑得前仰后合。

Remus sniggered too; he’d done half the research for that one. The week before he’d spent hours searching through books of troll dynasty histories for portraits to get all the features right. He hoped he’d get a chance to catch some of the reactions before Flitwick managed to break the glamour spell they’d used.
雷木斯也咯咯笑了；他为这次恶作剧做了半数的研究。前一周，他花了好几个小时在研究巨怪王朝历史的书籍中查找肖像，以确保所有特征都准确。他希望能在弗利维克破除他们使用的魅惑咒语之前，抓住一些反应的机会。

“You nutters.” Marlene smiled shyly.
“你们这些疯子。”玛琳害羞地笑了。

“Marlene!” Lily gasped.
“玛琳！”莉莉惊呼道。

They all turned to look at her, and then to Remus, agape. He made a point of smiling back at them all, relaxing his shoulders and clapping his hands together.
他们都转过头来看着她，然后又看向雷木斯，目瞪口呆。他特意对他们所有人微笑，放松了肩膀，拍了拍手。

“Come on then! This co-operative isn’t going to run itself…”
“那走吧！这个合作项目不会自己运作的……”

Sirius still had some opinions about Marlene, of course. Remus refused to hear them. He wanted the matter closed, he wanted to move on. And he wanted to meet Danny, as soon as he possibly could. For the first time, for better or for worse, Remus felt he had an ally out there. Someone who was like him, on their side. He wrote another letter, then scrapped it and tried again. Then again, and again. There was so much to say Remus wasn’t sure where to start.
天狼星当然对玛琳还有一些意见。雷木斯拒绝听取。他想要把这个问题解决，他想要继续前进。他还想尽快见到丹尼。第一次，无论好坏，雷木斯感到他在外面有一个盟友。一个像他一样、站在他们这一边的人。他写了另一封信，然后又废弃了，再次尝试。一次又一次。雷木斯有太多话要说，不知道从何说起。

“What do you want to talk to him for, though?” Sirius yawned one night in bed, as Remus gave up on another attempt to properly introduce himself. “You know more about being a werewolf than he does, it's not as if he’ll have any special insight.”
“不过你想跟他谈什么？”天狼星在床上打了个哈欠，一边雷木斯放弃了另一种正确介绍自己的尝试。“你对成为狼人了解的比他多，他不会有特别的见解。”

“It's not really about that.” Remus yawned back, putting out his wand light and lying down. He rubbed the knuckles and fingers on his right hand. Some days he felt as if he never put his quill down; he was always writing, if not feverishly revising his notes for NEWTs, then making complex calculations in aid of the big prank, or writing to Grant or Ferox or Danny.
“这不是主要问题。”雷木斯也打了个哈欠，熄灭了魔杖光芒，躺下了。他揉了揉右手的指关节和手指。有时他感觉自己好像从未放下过笔；要么在为普通巫师资格考试疯狂地复习笔记，要么进行复杂的计算以帮助大型恶作剧，或者写信给格兰特、费罗克斯或丹尼。

“Wait until school’s finished, then.” Sirius advised. “Safer for both of you.”
“等到学校结束再说吧。”天狼星建议道。“对你们俩都更安全。”

“There are three moons between now and then.” Remus replied, trying to get comfortable. The sheets always ended up wrinkled in Sirius’s bed, he had no idea how the other boy managed it.
“从现在到那时之间有三个月亮。”雷木斯回答道，试图让自己舒适一点。床单总是会在天狼星的床上皱成一团，他不知道另一个男孩是怎么做到的。

“I know that,” Sirius replied, indignantly. “But there’s not much you can do, is there?”
“我知道，”天狼星愤愤不平地回答，“但你也没什么能做的，不是吗？”

“S’pose not.”
“也许是吧。”

“And you don’t owe him anything.”
“而且你也不欠他什么。”

“No.” Remus chose his words carefully. “But I owe it to myself to do the right thing, don’t I?”
“没有。”雷木斯小心地选择了词语。“但我欠我自己做正确的事，不是吗？”

“Is that what got into your head?” Sirius was frowning, Remus could tell.
“这就是你脑子里想的？”天狼星皱着眉，雷木斯能看出来。

A flutter in his belly told him they were heading for a fight, and he could avert it right now by just changing the subject.
腹中的躁动告诉他他们正朝着争吵的方向发展，他可以通过改变话题来立即避免。

“What do you mean, ‘what got into my head’?!” Remus snapped.
“你说‘是什么让我的脑袋里出现这些想法’是什么意思？！”雷木斯厉声说道。

“When you wrote to Danny in the first place. You’ve got to admit it was a bit reckless.”
“当你第一次写信给丹尼的时候。你得承认这有点鲁莽。”

“Excuse me?!”

“Well for someone who’s spent seven years trying to keep every aspect of himself completely private, it was a bit bonkers to just go and send a letter to a stranger--”

“--my friend’s brother-- ”
“——我朋友的兄弟——”

“--spilling your guts about everything-- ”
“——倾诉你所有的事——”

“Not everything!”
“不是所有事！”

“--but if it was all in the service of doing the right thing, then I suppose that’s fine .”
“——但如果这一切都是为了做正确的事，那我想这也没问题。”

“Look, if you’re pissed off with me then just say so, this sarcastic crap doesn’t suit you, Black.” Remus rolled over onto his side.
“听着，如果你对我生气就直接说，这种讽刺的态度不适合你，布莱克。”雷木斯翻身侧躺。

“I’m not pissed off.” Sirius said.
“我没生气。”天狼星说。

“Good.”
“很好。”

Remus knew that wasn’t the end of it. He waited, practically champing at the bit.
雷木斯知道这还不是结束。他等着，几乎是急不可耐。

“...I’ve just been thinking, that’s all.” Sirius said, finally. Remus smirked to himself, before rolling back over, frowning,
“……我只是一直在想这些。”天狼星终于说道。雷木斯对自己露出了得意的笑容，然后翻了个身，皱着眉头，

“What?”
“什么事？”

“It’s like you wanted to leave, or something.”
“好像你想离开，或者说些什么。”

“Obviously I wanted to leave,” Remus hissed, going in, “I told you. It’s pointless, me doing NEWTs, pissing about with silly exams and clubs and pranks, when things are happening out there, right now . I had a chance to help, and I took it. So what if I didn’t care about the consequences?! Calling me reckless?! I thought you’d understand! What happened to wanting to get back at your family? What happened to wanting to put a stop to it?”
“显然我想离开，”雷木斯咬牙切齿地说，“我告诉过你了。做普通巫师资格考试、浪费时间在愚蠢的考试、社团和恶作剧上是毫无意义的，外面正在发生事情。我有机会去帮助，我就去做了。我不在乎后果又怎么样？！叫我鲁莽？！我以为你会理解的！你想报复你的家人呢？你想终结这一切呢？”

“I do want to…” Sirius said, sounding smaller.
“我确实想……”天狼星的声音变得有些小。

“Well you’re not acting like it. You seem more fussed about that stupid quidditch match than the war. Maybe they’re the same thing to you.”
“那么你并没有表现出这样。你似乎比战争更关心那个愚蠢的魁地奇比赛。也许对你来说它们是一样的。”

“Merlin!’ Sirius replied, weakly, “You don’t stop until you’ve tasted blood, do you?”
“梅林！”天狼星无力地回答道，“你不尝到血的味道是不会停下来的，对吧？”

“Must be the wolf in me.” Remus said, shortly.
“这可能是我内心的狼。”雷木斯简短地说。

He rolled over again and shut his eyes.
他再次翻身，闭上了眼睛。
