Chapter 146: Seventh Year: Superego 

Oh mine eyes have seen the glory of the theories of Freud,

He has taught me all the evils that my ego must avoid.

Repression of the impulses results in paranoid

As the id goes marching on.

 

Saturday 1st April 1978

“Wotcher!”  

“你好！”

“Hello.”  
“你好。”
“Gawd, cheer up a bit, sunshine! After I went to all that effort to book a bloody audience wiv’ ya!”  
“天哪，开朗点儿，阳光！我可是花了不少劲儿才预约了这次该死的会面！”
“Sorry! I’m really, really happy to hear from you.”  
“对不起！我真的非常非常高兴听到你的声音。”
“Christ, you get posher by the day.”  
“天哪，你变得越来越讲究了。”
Remus laughed, despite himself. The sound echoed back through the receiver, and made him think about Grant’s voice travelling all the way through the telephone wire, from the very bottom of England, up through to him in the Scottish Highlands. Muggles were pretty magic too, really.  
雷木斯忍不住笑了。声音通过听筒回响，让他想到格兰特的声音通过电话线从英格兰的最底端传到苏格兰高地的他这里。麻瓜其实也很神奇。
“How are you?” He asked, “Still enjoying the seaside?”  
“你怎么样？”他问道，“还在享受海边的生活吗？”
“Winter was fucking dire.” Grant replied, settling into the conversation. Remus could hear the cigarette between his teeth, the grind-click of a zippo lighter. He longed to see the other boy, to see his face and watch his expressions. “Rain. Freezing cold wind - it comes in off the sea, rattles the windows worse than at St Eddy’s. Mind you, the students made up for it.”  
“冬天糟透了。”格兰特回答道，进入谈话状态。雷木斯能听到他牙齿间的香烟声，以及打火机的咔嗒声。他渴望见到另一个男孩，看看他的脸和表情。“下雨。冷得刺骨的风——从海里吹来，吓得窗户比在圣艾迪的还要响。不过，学生们弥补了这些。”
“Students?”  
“学生们？”
“At the Art College, and Brighton Poly. You get loads of our sort, at art schools. I was seeing an engineer, a poet and a painter.”  
“在艺术学院和布赖顿理工学院。你会在艺术学校遇到很多我们这种人。我见过一个工程师、一个诗人和一个画家。”
“Is that three separate people, or one very clever person?” Remus asked, wryly.  
“那是三个人，还是一个非常聪明的人？”雷木斯挖苦道。
“Cheeky beggar. Wouldn’t you like to know.” Grant snickered. “What about you, anyway? How’s lover boy?”  
“无礼的家伙。你想知道吗？”格兰特轻笑道。“那你呢？‘情人’怎么样？”
Remus snorted derisively.  
雷木斯冷笑了一下。
“Fine.”  
“还好。”
“Fine?”  
“还好？”
“Fine.”  
“还好。”
Grant exhaled loudly.  
格兰特长叹了一声。
“Lord, not another fight, is it? Tell you what, sweetheart, you want to get on top of these moods of yours.”  
“天哪，又不是吵架吧？告诉你，亲爱的，你得控制好这些情绪。”
“What moods?!” Remus frowned. Grant laughed,  
“什么情绪？！”雷木斯皱了皱眉。格兰特笑了，
“You’re the moodiest bloke I know, worse than a girl on the blob when something’s pissed you off. And you ‘aven’t half got a mouth on ya. I’ve ‘ad broken ribs hurt less than some things you’ve said.”  
“你是我认识的情绪最不稳定的人，比起那些生气时像女孩儿一样的情绪波动更严重。而且你的嘴也没轻没重。我受过的肋骨骨折比你说过的一些话还要少受伤。”
“You never said…”  
“你从没说过……”
“No, well, I let you get away with it because it's easier than picking a fight. ‘sides, it’s not your fault. I'm the same, in’t I? We all are, institutionalised kids.”  
“没有，我让你过得去，因为这比起吵架更简单。而且，这不是你的错。我也一样，不是吗？我们都是被制度化的孩子。”
“Institutionalised?!”
It was an enormous word coming from Grant, but it felt rude to say so. God, Remus thought to himself, when did I become such a snob?  
“制度化？！”这是格兰特说出来的一个大词，但觉得这样说有点不礼貌。天哪，雷木斯在心里想，我什么时候变得这么势利了？
“Yep, ‘pparently that’s what we are. The poet told me - ‘e was doing a course in psychology. Said I’m afraid to stay with one person too long ‘cos I was abandoned too much when I was small. Dumped him after that, obviously.”  
“没错，显然这就是我们。那位诗人告诉我——他在修心理学课程。他说我害怕和一个人待得太久，因为我小时候被抛弃过多。之后我当然就甩了他。”
“I’ve been with Sirius for ages.” Remus replied, defensively. “It’s only ever been him.”  
“我和天狼星在一起很久了。”雷木斯 defensively地回答道。“只有他一个人。”
“Got the same problem, though.” Grant mused, as though they were just passing the time of day, “When was the last time you let anyone be nice to you without saying something 'orrible back?”  
“不过问题一样。”格兰特若有所思地说，好像只是闲聊一样，“你上次让别人对你好而不反击是什么时候？”
Remus pressed his lips together.  
雷木斯抿紧了嘴唇。
“I don’t do that.” He said, though he already knew Grant was right. Bastard.  
“我不会那样做。”他说道，虽然他已经知道格兰特说得对。混蛋。
“If you say so.” Grant returned, casually. “How’s everything else, anyway?”  
“如果你这么说。”格兰特随意地回答。“那其他方面怎么样？”
“I met my mother.”  
“我见到了我母亲。”
“Crikey.”  
“天哪。”
“Yeah. She’s ok.”  
“是的。她还好。”
“That what’s got you all moody?”  
“这就是让你情绪低落的原因？”
“No. Maybe.”  
“不是。也许吧。”
“Wouldn’t blame you if it was. I lose it for weeks after I see mine. Loves telling me how much she hates me.” He always sounded as if he was smiling, even as he said this. It made it more unpleasant somehow.  
“如果是这样我也不会怪你。我见到我妈后会失控好几个星期。她喜欢告诉我她有多么讨厌我。”他说这话时总是带着笑意，这让人听着更不舒服。
“Well. Mine didn’t say that.” Remus said. “Actually, she said she loves me.”  
“嗯。我母亲没有那样说。”雷木斯说。“实际上，她说她爱我。”
“That’s nice, then.”  
“那就好。”
“Yeah.”  
“是的。”
“You don’t have to say it back, y’know. She dumped you, the callous cow, she’s got no right to expect it.”  
“你不需要回应的。她甩了你，这个冷酷的母亲，她没有权利期待你的回应。”
Remus reeled back a little at that, shocked.  
雷木斯对此感到震惊，稍微退后了一步。
“She had her reasons. Anyway, it’s not like I don’t feel anything for her. It’s just hard to say. S’pose your psychologist friend would think that’s down to me being ‘institutionalised’.”  
“她有她的理由。反正，我并不是对她没有感情。只是很难说出来。可能你那心理学家朋友会认为这是因为我‘被制度化’了。”
“S’pose so.”  
“可能是吧。”
“But you never had a problem. With, er… affection.”  
“但你从来没有问题。关于，呃……感情。”
Grant laughed again, a joyful cackle.  
格兰特再次笑了，发出了愉快的笑声。
“If you don’t reckon shagging every lad who looks at me sideways is a problem.”  
“如果你不认为和每个看着我斜眼的家伙上床是个问题的话。”
“I just meant you’re more open …”  
“我只是觉得你更开放……”
Remus couldn’t go on, Grant’s laughter was drowning everything out.  
雷木斯无法继续说下去，格兰特的笑声淹没了一切。
“Sorry!” He wheezed, “Gawd, I forgot how funny you were.”  
“对不起！”他喘着气说，“天哪，我忘了
你有多搞笑。”
“I thought I was moody.”  
“我还以为我很情绪化。”
“You’re a complicated man, Remus bloody Lupin. S’why I love you.”  
“你是个复杂的男人，雷木斯·该死的·卢平。这就是我爱你的原因。”
Remus groaned. Grant laughed again. “Don’t worry, not in a queer way.”  
雷木斯呻吟了一声。格兰特再次笑了。“别担心，不是那种奇怪的方式。”
That made Remus laugh, and for a good few minutes after that laughter was all that passed between them, through miles and miles of telephone wire.  

这让雷木斯笑了，而在接下来的几分钟里，笑声成为了他们之间唯一的交流，穿越了数英里长的电话线。
* * *

 

 

Remus walked back to Hogsmeade with a lighter step than he’d had an hour before. Just talking to someone outside of Hogwarts, someone outside of the war, was a wonderful relief.
雷木斯比一个小时前走回霍格斯米德的步伐轻快了许多。仅仅和一个霍格沃茨以外的人交谈，和一个战斗之外的人交流，真是一种极大的解脱。

(“I wish there was a phone at school I could use,” he’d said, apologetically, “I’d call you all the time.”
（“我希望学校里有一部电话可以用，”他带着歉意说道，“我会一直给你打电话。”）

“When we’re eccentric millionaires,” Grant mused, “We can pay someone to carry a phone around for us, everywhere we go. The engineer said they’ll be able to do that, maybe by the eighties.”
“当我们成为古怪的百万富翁时，”格兰特沉思道，“我们可以雇人随身携带电话，无论我们走到哪里。工程师说，也许在八十年代他们就能做到这一点。”

“I don’t see how that would work,” Remus frowned, “Where would you plug it in?”
“我不明白这怎么能行，”雷木斯皱眉道，“那要在哪里插上呢？”

“You’re the one at the posh school, you tell me.”)
“你在那所讲究的学校里，你告诉我吧。”）

He’d promised to meet the others in The Three Broomsticks after the phone call, which had taken weeks to plan. Sirius hadn’t said anything when Remus headed towards the phone box outside of town - maybe a few weeks ago he’d have offered to walk with him, but they still weren't being nice to each other. They weren’t being nasty, but they weren’t happy. It was tiring, but giving ground seemed like even harder work.
他在电话之后承诺去“三把扫帚”与其他人见面，这次电话的安排花了好几个星期。雷木斯前往镇外的电话亭时，天狼星没有说什么——也许几周前他会提出陪他一起走，但他们现在还是彼此不太友好。他们没有恶意，但也不快乐。这让人疲惫，而让步似乎更困难。

Remus took a moment for himself before entering the pub. He smoked, leaning against the wall under the signpost. It was a bright spring day, and the first weekend he’d had in ages which wasn’t organised within an inch of its life. He watched the busy high street, happy students walking this way and that with their friends, shopping bags bulging and faces beaming. How different was he, from them? Was he any less?
雷木斯在进入酒吧之前给自己留了一会儿时间。他抽烟，靠在路标下的墙上。那是一个明亮的春天日子，也是他很久以来第一个没有被安排得过于紧凑的周末。他看着繁忙的主要街道，快乐的学生们与朋友们走来走去，购物袋鼓鼓的，脸上满是笑容。他与他们有多么不同？他是不是更差呢？

Not to his friends, he thought, confidently. Not to Sirius.
他自信地想着，对他的朋友们来说不是这样。对天狼星也不是。

Suddenly, he caught a familiar scent on the wind, and he searched the crowd quickly to find Chris, hurrying past.
突然，他在风中闻到了熟悉的气味，他迅速在人群中寻找克里斯，发现他正匆匆路过。

“Oi! Oi, Christopher!” Remus called to him.
“喂！喂，克里斯托弗！”雷木斯呼喊道。

The mousy boy stopped, saw who was shouting, then came over - a bit reluctantly.
那个像小老鼠一样的男孩停下了，看到是谁在喊，然后过来——有些勉强。

“Hello, Remus,” he nodded, looking agitated. He didn’t have his usual bag of books, and his clothes were smarter than usual. He smelled slightly different too - a new soap, or… it couldn’t be cologne?!
“你好，雷木斯，”他点点头，看起来很不安。他没有带着平常的书包，衣服也比平时更讲究。他闻起来也有点不同——是新的香皂，还是……不可能是香水吧？！

“Hiya, not seen you in ages,” Remus smiled down at him.
“嗨，好久没见了，”雷木斯对他笑道。

“Yeah, been so busy… then I had that cold, remember?” Christopher didn’t quite meet his eyes. He was blushing; but Christopher was always blushing, so Remus didn’t put much stock in it.
“是的，最近忙得不可开交……然后我得了感冒，你还记得吗？”克里斯托弗没有直视他的眼睛。他脸红了；但克里斯托弗总是脸红的，所以雷木斯没太在意。

“Oh yeah, feeling better?”
“哦，是的，感觉好些了吗？”

“Yes, thanks.
“是的，谢谢。

“Come in, the others are all inside…”
“进来吧，其他人都在里面……”

“Oh… no, sorry, Remus, um. I’m meeting someone…”
“哦……不，抱歉，雷木斯，嗯。我正在和人见面……”

“Oh!” Remus looked him up and down again. Well now it made a bit more sense. “Who?”
“哦！”雷木斯再次打量了他一眼。现在这有点说得通了。“谁？”

“Erm. Not anyone you know… sorry, but… do you mind? I’m going to be late.”
“嗯。不认识的人……抱歉，不过……你介意吗？我会迟到的。”

“‘Course! Sorry…” Remus said, a little bit annoyed. Christopher had never brushed him off like that before. He watched him hurry off down the street and turn a corner.
“当然！对不起……”雷木斯有些恼火地说道。克里斯托弗以前从未这样冷落过他。他看着他匆忙走下街道并转过一个拐角。

Fine.
很好。

Remus stubbed out his cigarette in the pot of red geraniums on the doorstep of the pub, then pushed the door open and entered. James, Lily, Mary, Peter, Marlene and Yaz were sitting in a booth in the far corner, the table laden with empty glasses.
雷木斯在酒吧门口的红色天竺葵盆栽里熄灭了香烟，然后推开门走了进去。詹姆斯、莉莉、玛丽、彼得、玛琳和亚兹坐在远处角落的一个包厢里，桌上满是空酒杯。

He smiled walking over to them, ducking his head under the low black ceiling beams and raising a hand in greeting.
他对他们微笑着走过去，低头避过低矮的黑色天花板横梁，并举手致意。

“Moony!” James grinned, waving back. Peter and Mary moved along on the plush green velvet seat to make room for him.
“月亮！”詹姆斯笑着，挥手回应。彼得和玛丽在柔软的绿色天鹅绒座位上挪了挪，为他腾出地方。

“How was your phone call?” Lily asked, brightly.
“电话打得怎么样？”莉莉明亮地问道。

“Good, thanks.” Remus nodded. “What have you lot been up to?”
“很好，谢谢。”雷木斯点点头。“你们都在忙些什么？”

“Planning the end of year party.” Mary smiled eagerly.
“在计划年终派对。”玛丽兴奋地笑道。

“My folks said they’ll host.” James said. “We’ll invite the whole year. Most of them, anyway…”
“我父母说他们会主办。”詹姆斯说道。“我们会邀请整个年级。大多数人，反正……”

“Sounds great.” Remus grinned back.
“听起来不错。”雷木斯笑着回应。

Things had been awkward between all of them, because it was painfully obvious that he and Sirius were fighting. Lily tried to be practical and act as if she was above it all, but James was perpetually caught between them, and never knew where to look.
他们之间的关系一直很尴尬，因为很明显他和天狼星在争吵。莉莉试图表现得实际一些，好像她超越了一切，但詹姆斯却永远在他们之间徘徊，不知道该看哪里。

“Right, come and get them…!” Sirius suddenly appeared over James’s shoulder from the bar, a tray of pints in his arms. He looked up and saw Remus, and the smile died on his lips.
“好了，过来拿酒……”天狼星突然从酒吧的吧台上出现在詹姆斯的肩膀上，手里端着一盘啤酒。他抬起头看到雷木斯，笑容在他嘴唇上消失了。

Everyone looked away, embarrassed, and Remus felt something harden in his chest. A stream of scathing one-liners flashed up in his mind; spiteful, sharp things. It took an enormous effort to push them down. He didn’t want it to be easier to be cruel than kind. He refused to be that kind of person. St Edmund’s couldn't be all he ever was.
大家都转过头，尴尬地避开了目光，雷木斯感觉到胸口有些东西变得坚硬。他脑海中闪过一连串尖刻的讽刺话语；恶意而尖锐的东西。压制这些情绪需要付出巨大的努力。他不希望对别人冷酷比善良更容易。他拒绝成为那种人。圣爱德蒙德学院不能是他全部的存在。

“Hiya,” he smiled, lowering his head so that his hair fell into his eyes and he had to push the curls back. He was such a mess, he ought to get it cut.
“嗨，”他微笑着说，低下头让头发垂入眼中，并不得不把卷发推回去。他现在一团糟，应该去剪个发。

“Hi.” Sirius set the tray down with a clank. “I’ll go back and get you--”
“你好。”天狼星把托盘放下，发出一声响。“我去拿给你……”

“Remus can have mine,” Mary said, getting out of the booth, “Samuel from my Charms group has been throwing me looks all afternoon… have my seat, Black.” She nudged him into the seat, and Sirius gingerly took his place beside Remus.
“雷木斯可以坐我的位置，”玛丽说着，起身离开包厢，“我的咒语课上的萨缪尔整下午都在盯着我看……黑，你坐我的座位吧。”她把他推到座位上，天狼星小心翼翼地坐在雷木斯旁边。

“See you later!” Mary trilled, sashaying across the pub floor to a group of Ravenclaw boys.
“稍后见！”玛丽高兴地说着，摇曳着走向一群拉文克劳的男孩。

Marlene grinned and shook her head at Yaz, who laughed and squeezed her hand on top of the table. Remus’s heart skipped and he glanced around furtively.
玛琳对亚兹露出笑容，摇了摇头，亚兹笑着把手握在桌子上。雷木斯的心跳漏了一拍，他偷偷环顾四周。

No one else was looking - their little booth was in an awkward corner of the room, away from the windows and poorly lit by gaslights. No doubt the privacy was why they’d chosen it, Remus saw now that all of his friends were rosy cheeked and glassy eyed from beer. Lily was practically sitting in James’s lap, and his right hand had vanished up the back of her jumper.
没有其他人在看——他们的小包厢在房间的一个尴尬角落，远离窗户，灯光微弱。毫无疑问，隐私是他们选择这个位置的原因，雷木斯现在看到他所有的朋友脸上都带着酒红色的酒意和闪烁的眼神。莉莉几乎坐在詹姆斯的腿上，他的右手消失在她的毛衣后面。

“How was the call?” Sirius asked, neutrally, looking down at his beer.
“电话打得怎么样？”天狼星冷淡地问，低头看着他的啤酒。

“Good.” Remus replied quietly, “He sounded really well. Happy.”
“很好。”雷木斯低声回答，“他听起来很健康。很开心。”

“That's nice.”
“那很好。”

Remus took a deep swig of beer for courage. Peter was talking quidditch with Marlene and Yaz, James and Lily only had eyes for each other. He turned to Sirius, twisting sideways in the seat,
雷木斯大口喝了酒以鼓起勇气。彼得在和玛琳及亚兹谈起魁地奇，詹姆斯和莉莉只顾对视。他转向天狼星，侧身坐在座位上，

“I’m such a prick.” He said.
“我真是个混蛋。”他说。

“Yep.” Sirius drank too, still not really looking at Remus, though the corner of his lips turned up as he tilted his head back.
“是的。”天狼星也喝了酒，仍然没有真正看雷木斯，尽管他向后仰头时嘴角微微上扬。

The flash of white skin on his neck as he swallowed caught Remus’s attention. He budged up on the seat, closer to Sirius.
他吞咽时脖子上白皙的皮肤引起了雷木斯的注意。他在座位上挪近了些，靠近天狼星。

“I’m sorry.” He whispered, so that only Sirius could hear him.
“对不起。”他低声说，只有天狼星能听到。

“I can’t talk to you about anything sometimes without you biting my head off.” Sirius grumbled. “You get into these moods and I can’t reach you.”
“有时候我跟你谈什么事都不行，你总是会发火。”天狼星抱怨道。“你会进入这种情绪，我就无法触及到你。”

“I know…” Remus said, trying not to get too sidetracked by the way Sirius’s adam’s apple bobbed, or the way his pulse fluttered in that hollow above his collar bone, or his lovely slender wrists, and how he’d love to hold them fast and…
“我知道……”雷木斯说，试图不被天狼星的喉结上下跳动，或者他颈部上方凹陷处的脉搏跳动，或者他那纤细的手腕所分散注意力，他多么想紧紧握住这些……

Remus looked around once more, just in case, before leaning in even closer, pushing Sirius’s hair back with his fingers and kissing that beautiful neck, flicking his tongue up, just behind his earlobe. He heard Sirius’s sharp intake of breath, and the blood rushing so fast in his veins it sounded like fizzing, and Remus’s own temperature began to rise.
雷木斯再次环顾四周，以防万一，然后更靠近一点，轻轻推开天狼星的头发，用手指轻吻那美丽的脖子，舌头轻舔耳垂后面。他听到天狼星的急促吸气声，血液在他血管中急速流动，听起来像是气泡声，雷木斯的体温也开始上升。

“I’m really sorry,” he said again, “It’s my fault, and I’ll do better.”
“我真的很抱歉，”他说道，“这是我的错，我会做得更好。”

“Better?” Sirius muttered, his head bowed so that his hair fell over his face.
“更好？”天狼星低声道，头低下，头发垂到脸上。

“Better. I’m sorry. I lose my temper when people tell me what to do, but I’m going to try.”
“更好。我很抱歉。我会对人发脾气当别人告诉我该怎么做，但我会尝试。”

Sirius’s head inclined towards him, and Remus pulled away so that they could look each other in the eye. He wasn’t angry, or guarded anymore, which was a relief.
天狼星的头向他倾斜，雷木斯退开，让他们可以对视。他不再生气或防备，这让他松了口气。

“S’pose it’s not really my job to tell you what to do in the first place…” Sirius said, giving way so easily. He couldn’t hold grudges, except maybe for his family. He was too good, inside and out. Remus felt another pang of guilt at that, and it fortified his resolve. He would do everything to change; to deserve Sirius’s blind loyalty.
“我想这本来就不是我的工作去告诉你该怎么做……”天狼星说，轻易地让步。他无法心怀怨恨，除了对他的家人。他内外都太好了。雷木斯对此感到更深的内疚，这增强了他的决心。他会尽一切努力改变自己，去配得上天狼星的盲目忠诚。

“No, but I don’t have to be such a dick about it,” Remus countered, moving back a bit more and reaching for his drink. “I’ll make it up to you, I promise.”
“不是，但我不必这样做个混蛋，”雷木斯反驳道，稍微退后一点，伸手去拿饮料。“我会弥补的，我保证。”

“Oh yeah?” Sirius cocked an eyebrow. All things forgiven, his mind had clearly returned to its usual preoccupation.
“哦，是吗？”天狼星挑了挑眉毛。所有问题都得到原谅，他的心思显然回到了他习惯的专注上。

“Later.” Remus returned, imperiously, giving him a light slap on the thigh.
“之后。”雷木斯傲慢地回应，轻拍他的腿部。

“So what did Grant say?” Sirius settled back comfortably into the corner of the booth. The uncomfortable part over, his posture relaxed, he rested a boot against the nearest free stool, leaning forward on his knee.
“那么，格兰特说了什么？”天狼星舒适地靠在包厢的角落里。尴尬的部分结束后，他的姿势放松了，把一只靴子靠在最近的空凳上，身体前倾靠在膝盖上。

“Oh, we just caught up,” Remus said, swilling his beer lightly, “He’s still working in Brighton, has his own flat; wants to get a car for weekends.”
“哦，我们只是聊了聊，”雷木斯说，轻轻摇晃他的啤酒，“他还在布赖顿工作，有自己的公寓；想要买辆车来周末用。”

“We could go there, after school’s finished.” Sirius suggested, “If you wanted? If there’s time for a holiday.”
“我们可以去那里，学校结束后。”天狼星建议，“如果你愿意的话？如果有假期时间的话。”

“Maybe,” Remus nodded, drinking again. None of them knew what would happen when school ended; not really. Even James and Lily were hazy on the details.
“也许吧，”雷木斯点了点头，再次喝酒。没人知道学校结束后会发生什么；实际上没有。即使是詹姆斯和莉莉对细节也模糊不清。

“--so I told him I’d hex his bollocks off if he asked me one more time.” Yaz was just saying, Marlene giggling and hiding her face in her hands,
“——所以我告诉他如果他再问我一次，我会用咒语弄断他的命根子。”亚兹正说着，玛琳笑着掩饰自己的脸，

“You’re awful!”
“你真是太可怕了！”

“Well he needs to learn his lesson!”
“那他需要好好学一课！”

“Who?” James and Sirius both asked, neither one of them wanting to be left out of any gossip.
“谁？”詹姆斯和天狼星同时问，两人都不愿意错过任何八卦。

“Ugh, Lockhart,” Yaz tossed her head haughtily, her ponytail swinging.
“唔，洛克哈特，”亚兹傲慢地扔了扔头发，她的马尾摆动着。

“Is he bothering you lot again?” James frowned, “I told him to stay away from my team! I’ll tell Flitwick--”
“他又来烦你们了吗？”詹姆斯皱眉道，“我告诉过他离我的队伍远点！我会告诉弗利特维克——”

“Don’t worry, he got the message this time,” Marlene laughed, “Yaz is convincing.”
“别担心，这次他明白了，”玛琳笑道，“亚兹说得很有说服力。”

“What does he want?” Sirius asked.
“他想要什么？”天狼星问。

“He just keeps sniffing around, trying to find out what we’re up to.” James sighed, shaking his head, “Reckons he’s being left out. He’s like a more hygiene conscious version of Snape in fifth year.”
“他只是不断地打探，试图弄清楚我们在干什么。”詹姆斯叹了口气，摇了摇头，“他觉得自己被排除在外。他就像是比斯内普第五年更注重卫生的版本。”

Lily elbowed him in the ribs, which only made James laugh.
莉莉用肘子戳了戳他，这只让詹姆斯笑了起来。

“Left out of what?” Remus frowned, “He doesn’t even play, and he’s a Ravenclaw - they lost the last game.”
“被排除在什么之外？”雷木斯皱眉道，“他甚至不参加比赛，而且他还是拉文克劳——他们输掉了上一场比赛。”

“Moony!” Sirius exclaimed, “Did you just demonstrate quidditch knowledge?!”
“穆尼！”天狼星惊呼，“你刚刚展示了对魁地奇的了解？！”

Everybody laughed at him, and Remus mock-sulked, drinking more beer.
大家都笑了，雷木斯装作生气的样子，喝了更多的啤酒。

“Hard to avoid it in our bloody dorm.” He retorted.
“在我们该死的宿舍里很难避免。”他反驳道。

“Anyway, it’s not the quidditch team he’s interested in.” James shook his head, grinning, “It’s the other thing.” He said this very ominously, eyebrows knit together and casting suspicious looks around the pub. Ah, Remus thought; the prank.
“反正，他对的不是魁地奇队感兴趣。”詹姆斯摇了摇头，笑着说，“是另一个东西。”他说得非常神秘，眉头紧皱，怀疑地环顾着酒吧。啊，雷木斯想；恶作剧。

“He hasn’t asked me,” Remus said, with a shrug.
“他没问过我，”雷木斯耸耸肩说。

“That’s because you’ve got everyone fooled,” Marlene replied. “The whole school somehow thinks you’re the mild one out of this lot.”
“那是因为你把所有人都骗了，”玛琳回答道。“整个学校不知怎么的认为你是这群人中最温和的一个。”

Remus smiled at her very sweetly.
雷木斯对她甜甜地笑了笑。

“Are you suggesting I’m not?” He raised an eyebrow, grinning at her.
“你是在暗示我不是吗？”他扬起一只眉毛，冲她笑道。

Beside him, Sirius made a small strained noise in the back of his throat. His pulse still hadn’t quite settled down yet.
在他旁边，天狼星喉咙里发出了一声轻微的紧张声音。他的脉搏仍未完全平静下来。

“Right,” Lily stood up, draining her drink and wiping her lips on the back of her sleeve, “We’ve got two hours before I’ve got to start herding the prefects back, and I need to go to Scrivenshaft's before it closes. Potter?”
“好了，”莉莉站起来，喝光了饮料，用袖子擦了擦嘴，“我们还有两个小时才要开始把学生会的成员带回去，我得在斯克里文斯哈夫特关门前去一趟。波特？”

“Yep, coming,” James necked the dregs of his own pint.
“好的，马上来，”詹姆斯喝下了自己杯中的残酒。

“We both need broom polish, if you want to come, Pete?” Marlene said, kindly. Wormtail had been left out of a lot, lately; even Dorcas was ignoring him.
“我们俩都需要扫帚抛光剂，如果你想来的话，皮特？”玛琳善意地说。最近，虫尾蛇被冷落了很多；连多卡斯都在忽视他。

“Great!” He stood up eagerly, following James out of the booth.
“太好了！”他兴奋地站起来，跟着詹姆斯离开包厢。

“Black?” Marlene looked at Sirius. “Didn’t you want new gloves?”
“黑？”玛琳看着天狼星。“你不是想要新的手套吗？”

“I’ll order them from Quidditch Monthly.” He replied, barely looking up at her.
“我会从《魁地奇月刊》上订购。”他回答道，几乎没抬头看她。

“Suit yourself,” she shrugged. There was a bit of commotion as they all got their things together and settled the bill, but finally Remus and Sirius were left alone. Remus turned to him slowly, trying to look innocent.
“随你便，”她耸耸肩。大家在整理东西和结账时有些喧闹，但最终雷木斯和天狼星被留在了那里。雷木斯慢慢转向他，试图表现得无辜。

“What do you fancy doing, then? Walk? Honeyduke’s?”
“那你想做什么呢？散步？霍尼杜克糖果店？”

“When the dorm room is guaranteed to be empty for at least two hours?!” Sirius licked his lips.
“当宿舍房间确保至少空置两个小时的时候？！”天狼星舔了舔嘴唇。

“More like an hour and a half, by the time we get up there…”
“差不多一个半小时，到我们上去的时候……”

“Better get a move on then.”
“那最好快点行动。”

“Oi,” Remus smirked, standing up, hands in his pockets. “I thought I told you I don’t like being told what to do.”
“喂，”雷木斯带着得意的笑容站起身来，双手插在口袋里。“我不是告诉过你我不喜欢被人指示吗？”

They walked out of the pub single file, and Remus held the door open. As Sirius edged past him, shuffling sideways, he leaned forward subtly and whispered,
他们单行走出酒吧，雷木斯撑着门。天狼星挤过他，侧身走开时，他轻轻前倾，低声说道，

“You’ll just have to tell me what to do, then.”
“那你就得告诉我该做什么了。”

Remus grinned.
雷木斯咧嘴一笑。

Notes:Song at the beginning is 'Psychotherapy' by Melanie.

Weird British words dictionary:
Brighton Poly - Brighton Polytechnic (Now the University of Brighton). Polys were higher education centres which focused on the sciences, engineering and other vocational subjects. They couldn't offer degrees, and were seen as 'second-rate' universities. The majority of Polytechnics became Universities under the Further and Higher Education Act 1992.

'Girl on the blob' - 'blob' is UK slang for a period/menstruation.

Brighton Poly - 布莱顿理工学院（现在的布莱顿大学）。理工学院（Polys）是专注于科学、工程及其他职业课程的高等教育机构。它们不能授予学位，被视为“二流”大学。大多数理工学院在1992年的《进一步和高等教育法案》中变成了大学。

'Girl on the blob' - “blob”是英国俚语，指月经/生理期。

“Remus… Remus. Fuck’s sake, wake up…”

He didn’t turn the light on in the bathroom, in an attempt to stay semi-asleep, but it was no good. By the time he’d got up, crossed the room, peed and washed his hands, Remus was fully awake. And his jaw hurt, so Sirius must have been right about the grinding. It was for the same reason Peter had been up and down all night, and probably the same reason Sirius couldn’t sleep. NEWTs started next week.
他没有打开浴室的灯，试图保持半睡眠状态，但没有用。等他起床，穿过房间，尿尿，洗手的时候，雷木斯已经完全醒了。而且他的下巴很痛，天狼星一定说得对，磨牙了。这也是彼得整夜上上下下的原因，也可能是天狼星无法入睡的原因。NEWTS 下周开始。

“Sorry, sorry!” Peter said, hopping from foot to foot as he fumbled with the switches on the wall, “I didn’t mean to get that one…”

“闭嘴，混蛋，”彼得回答道，听起来又困又烦恼，“我觉得自己喜欢和你们俩共享一个房间吗？！”

“我和Moony怎么样？！”天狼星猛地坐起身来。

天狼星抿了抿嘴唇，立刻安静下来，眼睛盯着雷木斯。

“乖孩子，”雷木斯露出了得意的笑容。他揉了揉自己的后脑勺，看了一眼彼得床头柜上的时钟。三点半。他说：“我要下楼了，我现在没法再睡觉了。”他说道，“你可以安静一会儿。”
They’d been sharing Remus’s bed for the past few nights now, and though it was large, it wasn’t really meant for two fully grown boys. Unfortunately they no longer had a choice, since Sirius’s own bed had disappeared earlier that week. They’d been practicing for the prank, and hit a bit of a snag with the main incantation. Sirius remained cheerfully optimistic that it would show up again eventually, but Remus was less sure.
他们已经在过去的几晚里共用雷木斯的床，虽然床很大，但其实并不适合两个完全长大的男孩。不幸的是，他们现在没有选择，因为天狼星自己的床在那周早些时候消失了。他们一直在为恶作剧练习，遇到了主咒语的小麻烦。天狼星依然乐观地认为它最终会出现，但雷木斯却不太确定。
He went quietly down the stairs, book under his arm.
他安静地下楼，胳膊下夹着一本书。
Remus loved the common room when it was empty; it was filled with some of his very happiest memories of Hogwarts.
雷木斯喜欢空荡荡的公共休息室；这里充满了他在霍格沃茨最幸福的回忆。
He went over and opened the big bay window. He was always too warm, and forever getting yelled at for opening windows to let cold air in - but no one was around to complain. Remus inhaled the scent of the forest, and the castle; the night sky and the snow from the mountains; the velvety smooth water of the lake and every blade of grass on the quidditch pitch. Hogwarts. Remus shook his head, realising how silly and sentimental he was being. He left the windows wide and turned back into the room, settling down on the big velvet couch and opening his book. 雷木斯摇了摇头，意识到自己有多么傻乎乎和多愁善感。他把窗户留开，转回房间，坐到大天鹅绒沙发上，打开了书。他挥了挥魔杖对着悬挂在火上的水壶，它开始加热。他在茶水煮好的时候翻阅自己的书，试图找到位置。

他毕业后要从哪里获取书籍呢？加入一个麻瓜图书馆很容易——但巫师们也有图书馆吗？这是另一个问题要问天狼星——或者也许是克里斯，等雷木斯下一次见到他的时候。自从他们在霍格斯密德碰面后，克里斯托弗变得非常难以捉摸。

“我知道。”天狼星温柔地吻了他一次，再次把他抱在怀里，紧紧地回抱着他。“我也是。”

“Stoic and modest, my dream man.” Mary sighed. “冷静又谦虚，我的梦中情人。”玛丽叹了口气。

“Yasmin.” Mary finished for her, a bit cattily. She let Marlene out from under her arm. “Off you, pop, then.” “Yasmin。”玛丽有些尖刻地替她完成了句子。她让玛琳从她的怀抱中出来。“走吧，去吧。”
“Moody cow,” Marlene poked her tongue out, “You know I love you forever.” “情绪化的家伙，”玛琳吐了吐舌头，“你知道我永远爱你。”

Oh fuck. Oh buggering hell. How on earth had this happened?! How had he let it get this far?! Remus’s mouth was dry, his palms damp, and the less said about his insides the better. He wished he had Sirius nearby, or even James, to help him calm down. But no one could help him now. He was on his own.  
哦，操。哦，真是糟糕透顶。这到底是怎么发生的？！他怎么让事情发展到这一步？！雷木斯的嘴巴干燥，手掌湿润，更别提他的内心了。他希望身边有天狼星，甚至詹姆斯，来帮助他冷静下来。但现在没有人能帮他。他只能靠自己。
McGonagall turned to him,  
麦格转向他，  
“Ready, Mr Lupin?”  
“准备好了吗，Lupin先生？”
He swallowed, hard, and nodded. Time to bite the bullet.  
他艰难地咽了口唾沫，点了点头。是时候咬紧牙关了。
Fuck’s sake. This was all Christopher’s fault.  
真是的。这都是Christopher的错。

The whole mess had started four days earlier. The marauders were in the library studying for their very last exam; Arithmancy. Well, Peter didn’t take Arithmancy, but he was there anyway; ostensibly for moral support, but mostly to provide sustenance. He’d been a godsend to Remus in particular, making hourly trips down to the kitchens and back with cauldron cakes, pasties, bacon butties and jam tarts.  
一切的麻烦开始于四天前。四人组正在图书馆为他们的最后一场考试——算命术——做准备。嗯，彼得没有修算命术，但他还是在那里；名义上是为了提供精神支持，但主要是提供食物。他对雷木斯尤其是救星，往返厨房，带来了锅炉蛋糕、饼点、培根三明治和果酱挞。

“现在十一点半了，”天狼星打了个哈欠，“来吧，我觉得我今晚的大脑再也无法吸收更多知识了。”

彼得期待地看着雷木斯，显然无聊至极。雷木斯对他们所有人皱了皱眉。

子里也几乎算不上工人阶级——

“我不这样认为……”雷木斯皱了皱眉。他伸出手，轻轻地摸了摸克里斯托弗的手臂，缓慢地说道，“克里斯托弗？你在干什么？快熄灯了，你在巡逻吗？”  
“Patrol?” Christopher stared at him blankly, before blinking, then nodding again, grinning, “Yes! Yes, that must be it!”  
“巡逻？”克里斯托弗茫然地盯着他，然后眨了眨眼，再次点头，笑着说，“是的！是的，这一定是了！”
“He’s confounded.” James said. “Christopher? Has anyone cast a spell on you tonight? Or near you, and it backfired?”  
“他被迷惑了。”詹姆斯说。“克里斯托弗？今晚有人对你施了魔法吗？或者在你附近，魔法反弹了吗？”  
“Maybe he did it to himself,” Wormtail suggested. “I did that once, remember?”  
“也许他自己弄的，”蛭尾建议道。“我曾经也这样过，记得吗？”  
“No, Chris wouldn’t try to confound someone.” Remus shook his head. “Chris, who was the last person you saw?”  
“不，克里斯不会试图迷惑别人。”雷木斯摇了摇头。“克里斯，最后一个你看到的人是谁？”  
“Hm? Oh er… was it… you?”  
“嗯？哦，呃……是……你吗？”  
“No,” Remus put his hands on Christopher's shoulders, meeting his eyes and trying to hold his attention, “No, not me. Concentrate. Before I got here, what were you doing?”  
“不是，”雷木斯把手放在克里斯托弗的肩膀上，与他的眼睛对视，试图引起他的注意，“不是我。集中精神。在我到这里之前，你在做什么？”
“Was I patrolling?”  
“我在巡逻吗？”
“No, I mean… oh, come on, let’s go back to the tower, eh?” Remus kept his hand on Christopher's shoulder and began gently but firmly steering him up the corridor, throwing anxious looks at the others.  
“不，我是说……哦，算了，我们回到塔楼吧，嗯？”雷木斯保持着手在克里斯托弗的肩膀上，开始温柔而坚定地引导他走过走廊，一边焦急地看着其他人。  
“Should we tell someone?” Sirius asked James, “Or… I dunno, take him to Madam Pomfrey?”  
“我们应该告诉谁吗？”天狼星问詹姆斯，“或者……我不知道，带他去找Pomfrey夫人？”  
“I’m not ill!” Christopher piped up, chirpily.  
“我没生病！”克里斯托弗高声说道，显得很开心。
James ran his hands through his hair, shrugging.  
詹姆斯揉了揉头发，耸了耸肩。  
“I dunno. We’ll ask Lily, she’ll know what to do.”  
“我不知道。我们去问莉莉，她会知道该怎么做的。”
Lily did not know what to do. She stood with a hand on her hip and a skeptical look on her face, and asked him a few questions, but was as stumped as the rest of them. He sat before her, quite happily, in an armchair, smiling back up at her. He didn’t seem to mind the interrogation, and while he couldn’t give them any real information, he answered everything with cheerful, blank politeness. Giving up, Lily clicked her tongue.  
莉莉不知道该怎么办。她一手叉腰，脸上带着怀疑的表情，问了他几个问题，但和其他人一样困惑。他坐在她面前，十分开心，微笑着看向她。他似乎不介意被审问，虽然不能给他们提供任何有用的信息，但他用愉快、呆板的礼貌回答了所有问题。莉莉无奈地咂了咂嘴。
“I mean, he looks ok… and he doesn’t seem upset… Christopher? Did you get into a fight with someone? An argument?”  
“我的意思是，他看起来还好……而且他似乎也不沮丧……克里斯托弗？你和某人打架了？争吵了吗？”  
“I don’t think so.” Christopher said, thoughtfully, his voice thick and dreamy. He yawned. “I think I’ll go to bed, if that’s alright with you lot.”  
“我不这么认为。”克里斯托弗思索地说，声音浓重而梦幻。他打了个哈欠。“如果你们没意见的话，我想去睡觉了。”
Remus, James and Lily all looked at each other helplessly. Then Lily turned to James,  
雷木斯、詹姆斯和莉莉无奈地互相看了看。然后莉莉转向詹姆斯，  
“Take him up, will you? Just make sure he doesn’t get lost on the way.”  
“把他送上去，好吗？只要确保他在路上不会迷路。”
James nodded, happy to be able to take action, and slapped Christopher on the back,  
詹姆斯点了点头，乐意采取行动，拍了拍克里斯托弗的背，  
“C’mon then, mate, let’s get you to your dorm…”  
“来吧，伙计，我们带你回宿舍……”
Lily, Remus, Sirius and Peter watched them vanish up the staircase.  
莉莉、雷木斯、天狼星和彼得看着他们消失在楼梯上。
“Weird.” Lily said. “And no one else was around?”  
“真奇怪。”莉莉说。“没有其他人吗？”
“Not that I saw,” Remus said. “But god knows how long he was standing there.”  
“我没看到，”雷木斯说。“但天知道他在那里站了多久。”
“Well, he was on the rota for patrol this evening,” she said, pulling out her little leather-bound organiser to check. “I always tell the prefects to go round in pairs, though, so he shouldn’t have been alone. He’s usually so reliable. I’ll talk to him in the morning, maybe he’ll be a bit sharper then.”  
“嗯，他今晚在巡逻名单上，”她说，拿出她的小皮革记事本查看。“不过我总是告诉值日生要成对行动，所以他不应该是一个人。他通常很可靠。我会在早上跟他谈谈，也许他那时候会清醒一些。”
“Doesn’t look like he came to any harm,” Peter said, offhandedly, flicking through an old copy of Quidditch Weekly, “Maybe he was drunk, or stoned or whatever, and he’s just trying to cover his tracks.”  
“看起来他没有受伤，”彼得随口说，一边翻看一本旧版的《魁地奇周刊》，“也许他喝醉了，或者嗨了什么的，他只是试图掩盖他的踪
迹。”
Remus disagreed - it was too wildly out of character. But then, he hadn’t seen much of Chris, lately, they’d both been so busy. He remembered bumping into the younger boy in Hogsmeade a while ago - he’d been acting strangely then, too, but Remus had just assumed he was meeting someone and didn’t want Remus to know who. And if anyone respected other people's privacy, it was Remus.  
雷木斯不同意——这太不符合克里斯托弗的性格了。但最近他没怎么见过克里斯托弗，他们俩都很忙。他记得不久前在霍格斯梅德碰到过这个年轻男孩——那时他也表现得很奇怪，但雷木斯只是以为他在见某人，不想让雷木斯知道是谁。若有谁尊重他人隐私，那就是雷木斯了。
James returned, saying Chris had seemed fine once he was in his bedroom, and they didn’t talk about it much for the rest of the evening. Just one of those things. In a school full of adolescents learning to use magic, it wasn’t entirely out of the ordinary for accidents to happen.  
詹姆斯回来了，说克里斯托弗在他的卧室里看起来很好，接着他们在晚上的时候没再多谈这件事。只是这种事情。在一个充满青少年学习魔法的学校里，发生意外并不完全不寻常。
Talk soon turned to the upcoming Gryffindor vs. Slytherin quidditch match; the final match of the year, and the final game of James and Sirius’s school careers. Remus zoned out a bit, letting his three friends work themselves up about it. Secretly he couldn’t wait for it to be done with - as much as it made them all happy, and as much as he wanted Gryffindor to win, it wasn’t half boring to listen to all the time. He picked up his Arithmancy book and returned to his revision, settling into the comfiest armchair.  
谈话很快转向即将到来的格兰芬多对斯莱特林的魁地奇比赛；今年的最后一场比赛，也是詹姆斯和天狼星学校生涯的最后一场比赛。雷木斯有些走神，让他的三个朋友对此激动不已。实际上，他迫不及待地想结束这件事——尽管这让他们都很高兴，尽管他想让格兰芬多赢，但一直听着这些也实在无聊。他拿起他的算命书，继续复习，坐进了最舒适的扶手椅里。
“Moony, c’mon, bedtime.” Sirius woke him, half an hour later. Damn.  
“月亮狗，快起来，该睡觉了。”半小时后，天狼星叫醒了他。该死。
Remus blinked, blearily, looking down at his textbook. He’d barely got past the first paragraph before falling asleep, his quill still poised between his fingers.  
雷木斯迷迷糊糊地眨了眨眼，看着他的教科书。他才刚刚读完第一段就睡着了，羽毛笔还在他的手指间悬着。  
“Bollocks.” He muttered, closing the book and stretching.  
“狗屎。”他嘟囔道，合上书本，伸了个懒腰。
Sirius chuckled,  
天狼星笑了起来，  
“Told you that was enough for one day.”  
“告诉过你今天够了。”
Remus just yawned at him, getting up. The common room had cleared out almost completely, now, except for James and Lily, who were ‘saying goodnight’ on the couch. That usually took a while, so the other three marauders left them to it, climbing the stairs to bed.  
雷木斯只是对他打了个哈欠，起身。公共休息室几乎完全清空了，现在只剩下詹姆斯和莉莉在沙发上“说晚安”。这通常需要一些时间，所以其他三个同学就让他们自己待着，爬上楼去睡觉了。
* * *  
The next morning, Remus was awoken by Sirius - or rather, the absence of Sirius. He was just crawling out of bed, and trying to be sneaky about it.  
* * *
第二天早晨，雷木斯被天狼星——或者说，是天狼星的缺席吵醒了。他正爬出床，试图偷偷摸摸地做这件事。  
“Mmm, stay…” Remus reached for him sleepily, trying to pull him back. His hands ran over the skin of Sirius’s upper arms. Sirius had fantastic skin, it was so smooth, and unblemished everywhere except for the backs of his legs. He kept talking about wanting tattoos, a thought which horrified Remus.  
“嗯，留在这里……”雷木斯昏昏欲睡地伸手去抓他，试图把他拉回来。他的手在天狼星的上臂皮肤上滑过。天狼星的皮肤非常棒，光滑无瑕，除了腿背部外的地方。他一直谈论想要纹身，这个想法让雷木斯感到恐惧。  
“Sorry, Moony,” Sirius grinned, gently untangling himself, “Big game in two days, got to practice.”  
“对不起，月亮狗，”天狼星笑着，轻轻解开自己，“两天后有场重要比赛，得练习。”
“What time is it?”  
“现在几点了？”
“Just gone five.”  
“刚过五点。”
“Ugh.” Remus flopped back down on the bed, throwing the blankets over his head, “You’re all mental.”  
“呃。”雷木斯往床上倒回去，把被子扔在头上，“你们都疯了。”
“Yup.” Sirius laughed, “Go back to sleep, I’ll see you later.”  
“是的。”天狼星笑着，“继续睡吧，我待会儿见。”
He left carefully, closing the curtains behind him. Remus rolled into the warm hollow Sirius’s body had left behind, inhaled the scent on his pillow, and drifted back to sleep.  
他小心翼翼地离开，关上了帘子。雷木斯滚进了天狼星留下的温暖凹陷处，吸入枕头上的气息，重新进入梦乡。  
He woke up just in time to catch the last of breakfast, and then returned to the library where he met Lily for more Arithmancy study.  
他刚好醒来赶上了早餐的最后部分，然后回到图书馆，和莉莉一起进行更多的算命学习。  
“I’m so tired of numbers!” Lily groaned rubbing her eyes. They were a few hours in and it would be lunch soon.  
“我对数字厌倦了！”莉莉抱怨道，揉着她的眼睛。他们已经学习了几个小时了，很快就要到午餐时间了。
“I’m going to miss it,” Remus replied, “I like the charts, they’re relaxing.”  
“我会想念它的，”雷木斯回答道，“我喜欢那些图表，它们让人放松。”
“Well I’m just glad there’s nothing like this in potions.”  
“嗯，我很高兴在药剂学中没有这样的东西。”
“James said you were looking into a job in an apothecary?”  
“詹姆斯说你在考虑药剂师的工作吗？”
“Maybe,” Lily shrugged. “I’d like to do something like that. Maybe research for St Mungo’s. Slughorn offered to write recommendations for me. But things will be complicated for a while I think. James is optimistic, but…”  
“也许吧，”莉莉耸了耸肩。“我想做一些这样的事情。也许是为圣芒戈医院做研究。斯拉赫霍恩说愿意为我写推荐信。但是我觉得事情会有点复杂。詹姆斯很乐观，但……”
“Yeah.” Remus nodded. “We’ll just have to see.”  
“是的。”雷木斯点了点头。“我们只能看看。”
“Shall we go down for lunch?” She closed her book, brushing her hair over one shoulder, “The boys’ll be finished soon, we can meet them.”  
“我们去吃午餐吧？”她合上书本，把头发挽到一边，“他们很快就会结束，我们可以去找他们。”
Remus’s stomach growled, and he gave in.  
雷木斯的肚子咕咕叫了起来，他就此妥协了。
“Go on then.”  
“那我们走吧。”
Just as they were getting up to go, the library doors swung open, and Madam Pince screeched, “No running!”  
就在他们准备离开时，图书馆的门猛地打开，品斯夫人尖叫道，“不许跑！”
“Lily! Remus! I need your help!” Christopher came charging up to them so fast his legs hit their desk, banging all the books forward.  
“莉
莉！雷木斯！我需要你们的帮助！”克里斯托弗飞快地跑到他们面前，腿撞到了桌子，把所有书都碰到了前面。  
“What’s wrong?!” Lily asked, her emerald eyes wide.  
“怎么了？！”莉莉问，眼睛睁得大大的。
“I can’t explain, you just need to see…”  
“我没法解释，你们只需要看看……”
“See what?” Remus asked, re-ordering his book pile.  
“看什么？”雷木斯问，一边重新整理书堆。  
“I’ve… I’ve done something stupid. Please just come now?” Chris pleaded. His face was red and shiny from running, and while he was definitely looking more alert than he had the evening before, he was clearly genuinely upset by something. So they went.  
“我……我做了件愚蠢的事。请你们现在过来好吗？”克里斯托弗恳求道。他的脸因跑步而红扑扑的，尽管他现在比昨天晚上看起来清醒多了，但显然还是对某件事感到非常沮丧。于是他们就去了。  
He led them to the Charms corridor, and the whole way there kept babbling about how it had been an accident, and how he hadn’t meant it to happen. Lily kept trying to get some sense out of him, but he wouldn’t give them so much as a hint.  
他把他们带到咒语走廊，一路上不停地喋喋不休地说这是一场意外，他并不想让事情发生。莉莉不断尝试从他口中得到一些线索，但他什么都不肯透露。  
Finally, he stood before the closed Charms classroom door. Professor Flitwick really ought to start locking it, Remus thought to himself, as Christopher faced them, pale and trembling. He fidgeted with the sleeves of his robes, looking down,  
最后，他站在了关闭的咒语教室门前。弗利维教授真的应该开始锁门了，雷木斯心想，克里斯托弗面向他们，脸色苍白，身体发抖。他不停摆弄着袍子的袖口，低着头，
“Ok… please don’t panic… it was an accident…”  
“好吧……请不要慌张……这是一次意外……”
“Christopher, just show us, will you?!” Snapped Lily, tapping her foot on the flagstone floor.  
“克里斯托弗，快给我们看看，好吗？！”莉莉厉声说道，脚在石板地上跺了跺。
Christopher jumped at her authoritative tone, usually reserved for students who were misbehaving, but he took a deep breath and pushed the door open, ushering them in and slamming it shut behind them.  
克里斯托弗被她权威的语气吓了一跳，这通常是用来训斥不守规矩的学生的，但他深呼吸了一下，推开了门，迎他们进去，然后把门猛地关上。
“What on earth…” Lily breathed, when they saw it.  
“这到底是什么……”莉莉惊呼道，当他们看到那一幕时。
What stood before them was an enormous, quivering, glistening blue jelly. It was easily the size of Flitwick’s desk, and just stood there in the middle of the classroom, translucent and wobbling. Remus stifled a laugh. In seven years at Hogwarts this was definitely one of the most ridiculous things he’s ever seen.  
眼前是一团巨大的、颤抖的、闪闪发光的蓝色果冻。它的大小足以与弗利维教授的桌子相匹敌，就那样在教室的中央静静地立着，透明而摇晃。雷木斯忍住了笑。在霍格沃茨的七年里，这绝对是他见过的最荒谬的事情之一。  
Christopher hung his head,  
克里斯托弗垂下了头，
“He attacked me, it was self defence!”  
“他攻击了我，这是自卫！”
Remus stopped laughing and looked again,  
雷木斯停止了笑声，再次看向那团果冻，  
“That’s a person ?! Chris! What the fuck?!”  
“那是一个人？克里斯托弗！这是什么鬼？！”
“Remus, language,” Lily elbowed him. “Christopher, who is that?”  
“雷木斯，注意你的语言，”莉莉肘击了他一下。“克里斯托弗，那是谁？”
“It’s Roy. Guilderoy.”  
“是罗伊·吉尔德罗伊。”
“Lockhart??”  
“洛克哈特？！”
“Am I going to get in trouble?” Chris blinked at them both, his brown eyes huge and frightened.  
“我会惹上麻烦吗？”克里斯托弗眨着眼睛，看着他们，眼中充满了惊恐。
“What did you… how did you?!” Lily gaped.  
“你……你怎么做的？！”莉莉惊愕地问道。
“It was a jelly legs jinx. I just expanded on it a bit - Remus taught me!”  
“这是个果冻腿的咒语。我只是稍微扩展了一下——雷木斯教我的！”
Lily glared at Remus, who held his hands up,  
莉莉瞪了雷木斯一眼，雷木斯举起了双手，  
“James taught me ! And it never had that result.”  
“是詹姆斯教我的！结果从未如此。”
“But why did you do it, Chris?” Lily asked, still staring.  
“那你为什么要这样做，克里斯托弗？”莉莉问道，依旧盯着他。
“He was going to confound me again!”  
“他打算再次迷惑我！”
“Wait, what? It was Lockhart?”  
“等等，什么？是洛克哈特？”
Christopher nodded, shrinking from Lily’s temper. He was embarrassed, Remus could tell. He looked at his feet.  
克里斯托弗点了点头，畏缩着接受莉莉的怒火。他显得很尴尬，雷木斯能看出来。他看着自己的脚。
“He did it the other day, but it backfired, I think I tried to dodge it. Maybe he's done it before, I dunno.”  
“他前几天对我施过这个咒语，但失败了。我想我试图躲开了。也许他以前也这样做过，我不清楚。”
“But why?”
“He was… he was worried I was going to tell…”
“Tell what?!”
“He was… we… he…”
“Christopher, for goodness sake!” Lily folded her arms angrily. Remus felt a stab of sympathy as Chris’s cheeks turned a deeper shade of red. “克里斯托弗，天哪！”莉莉生气地抱住双臂。雷穆斯看到克里斯的脸颊变得更加红润，心中感到一丝同情。
“Look, Lily, it doesn’t matter now, does It?” He said, turning to her to try and shift focus away from Christopher. “We ought to get Lockhart looked at, first…” “看，莉莉，现在这没什么关系，对吧？”他转向她，试图将注意力从克里斯身上移开。“我们应该先让洛克哈特看病……”
He wasn’t sure how he managed it, but in the end he convinced Lily to go and get Madam Pomfrey, while he and Christopher waited with the jellified Lockhart. 他不确定自己是怎么做到的，但最终他说服了莉莉去找庞弗雷夫人，而他和克里斯则和被果冻化的洛克哈特等在一起。
Once she’d gone, Christopher seemed to become even more anxious, “我会被开除的！”
“No, you’re not,” Remus leaned against the wall casually, pulling out his cigarette case. He offered one to Chris, who shook his head, fidgeting and worrying the cuffs of his sleeves. “James and Sirius have done worse than this.” “不，你不会的，”雷穆斯随意地靠在墙上，拿出香烟盒。他递给克里斯一支，克里斯摇了摇头，坐立不安地担心着袖口。“詹姆斯和天狼星做过比这更糟糕的事。”
“I’ve never even had a detention before!” “我以前从未被罚过！”
“Seriously?!” Remus raised his eyebrows as he lit his fag, “Well it's not that bad. You’ll survive. So… do you want to tell me what's been going on?” “真的？！”雷穆斯扬起眉毛点燃香烟，“嗯，这没那么糟糕。你会熬过去的。那么……你想告诉我发生了什么事吗？”
Christopher looked at him, his cheeks darkening again. 克里斯看着他，脸颊再次变暗。
“It was just… we just…” “只是……我们只是……”
“I’m guessing this is who you were meeting in Hogsmeade that time?” Remus prompted, trying to make it easier. “我猜这是你那次在霍格斯梅德见的人？”雷穆斯引导道，试图让事情变得简单些。
Chris looked at his feet again and nodded. 克里斯再次看向自己的脚，点了点头。

“We got lucky with the weather,” Remus commented, gazing up at the clear blue sky. “Would have been a nightmare getting them all outside if it was raining.” 雷穆斯评论道，仰望着晴朗的蓝天，“如果下雨的话，把他们都弄到外面将会是一场噩梦。”
He was not going to miss Scottish ‘summers’. 他一点也不怀念苏格兰的“夏天”。
He and Christopher were alone in the owlery, waiting. It would begin any moment. 他和克里斯托弗独自待在猫头鹰棚里，等待着。一切即将开始。
“Don’t make fun of me, ok?” Christopher whispered, looking down at the grounds from the high open windows, “But this is the most exciting thing I’ve ever done.” 克里斯托弗低声说道，望着高高的敞开窗户外的地面，“但是这是我做过的最激动人心的事情。”

Remus had never seen anything so magnificent; every single owl in Hogwarts spread its wings and soared out of the window, each one snatching a blank addressed letter as it passed. It must have taken two full minutes for them all to manage it, and when it was over, Remus and Christopher jumped at the window to watch them disappear down towards the courtyard, through the arches and on to their destination. 雷穆斯从未见过如此壮观的景象；霍格沃茨的每只猫头鹰都展开翅膀，从窗户飞出，每只都抓住一封空白的地址信。大约花了整整两分钟才完成，当一切结束后，雷穆斯和克里斯托弗跳到窗边，观看它们消失在庭院中，通过拱门，前往目的地。

“You’ve taught so many people things they never would have learnt,” Christopher marvelled as they walked. The big clock outside the Great Hall was whirling madly, hands spinning - so was every other clock, if the sixth years’ spell had worked correctly. 克里斯托弗边走边惊叹道，“你教了这么多人他们从未学过的东西。”大厅外的大钟疯狂地旋转，指针在转——如果六年级的咒语起作用的话，其他所有钟表也是如此。
“Oh yeah,” Remus snorted, “Blowing up toilets and levitating desks. Very useful.” “哦，是的，”雷穆斯哼了一声，“炸厕所和漂浮课桌。非常有用。”
“Don’t forget all the defensive stuff,” Christopher frowned, “I’d have been confounded again if not for you.” “别忘了所有的防御技巧，”克里斯托弗皱眉道，“
要不是你，我早就被困惑咒困住了。”
They followed the steady stream of students exiting the building. Remus just hoped they’d caused enough mayhem in enough areas of the castle to get everyone outside onto the lawn. It wouldn’t be any fun if half the school missed the main event. 他们跟着不断离开建筑物的学生流。雷穆斯只希望他们在城堡的足够多地方制造了足够的混乱，把所有人都弄到草坪上。如果一半的学校错过了主要活动，那就没意思了。
“How is Lockhart?” He asked, casually. “洛哈特怎么样？”他随意地问道。
“Fine, I think. Leaving me alone, anyway.” “很好，我想。无论如何，他不再打扰我了。”
“Good. S’pose you can handle him if he doesn’t.” “好吧。假设如果他不这样做，你能应付他。”
“Yeah.” They’d reached the courtyard now, and were within sight of the grounds. Christopher squinted in the bright summer sunshine and looked up at Remus, stopping a moment. “I’ll really miss you, though.” “是的。”他们现在已经到了庭院，可以看到操场。克里斯托弗在明亮的夏日阳光下眯起眼睛，抬头看着雷穆斯，停了一会儿。“不过，我真的会想念你。”
“You’re only here one more year,” Remus replied, “You’ll be too busy with NEWTs to think about anything else; trust me.” “你只剩下一年了，”雷穆斯回答，“你会忙着考NEWTs，没时间想其他的；相信我。”
“No, I’m still going to miss you.” Chris said, firmly. “I’ll keep the study group going - but it won’t be the same. Everyone likes you so much, you’re patient with them.” “不，我还是会想念你。”克里斯坚定地说。“我会继续维持学习小组——但这不会一样。大家都很喜欢你，你对他们很有耐心。”
Remus didn’t know how to respond to that, so he didn’t. There was a funny lump in his throat, all the same. 雷穆斯不知道该如何回应，所以他没有回应。尽管如此，他喉咙里有一种奇怪的哽咽感。
“C’mon,” he pulled Christopher’s arm, moving towards the grounds. “Don’t want to miss it!” “来吧，”他拉着克里斯托弗的胳膊，朝操场走去。“不要错过！”
More than half the school had gathered on Hogwarts’ expansive lawn, all chattering a mile a minute about the various interruptions and intrusions to their mornings. 超过一半的学校聚集在霍格沃茨宽阔的草坪上，大家都在喋喋不休地讨论早上的各种干扰和入侵。
“Did you see all those owls?” “你看到那些猫头鹰了吗？”
“The Great Hall is flooded! Flooded !” “礼堂被淹了！淹了！”
“The Ravenclaw door-knocker is speaking gobbledygook, apparently, won’t let anyone in.” “拉文克劳的门环在胡言乱语，显然不让任何人进去。”
“The statue of the knight on the fifth floor threw water balloons at me!” “五楼的骑士雕像向我扔了水球！”
“Marauders, do you reckon?” “你觉得是掠夺者干的吗？”
“Definitely.” “绝对是。”
“No! I saw Emmeline Vance casting a spell on the portraits - and a group of sixth years planting dung bombs. It can’t be the marauders.” “不！我看到埃米琳·范斯对画像施咒——还有一群六年级的学生在放粪弹。这不可能是掠夺者干的。”
“Well it can’t be everyone-- ” “那不可能是所有人——”
The conjecture was interrupted as the last of the Slytherins - Regulus, Barty Crouch, Mulciber and Snape, much to Remus’s satisfaction - emerged from the castle. They were all plastered in green slime. Lily’s surprise bogey-bombs had worked a treat. Remus made a mental note to congratulate her later. She’d be a marauder, yet. 这种猜测被最后一批斯莱特林学生——雷古勒斯、巴蒂·克劳奇、穆尔西伯和斯内普——从城堡里出来时打断了，这让雷穆斯非常满意。他们身上都沾满了绿色的粘液。莉莉的惊喜鼻涕炸弹效果极佳。雷穆斯记下了以后要祝贺她的事。她迟早会成为掠夺者。

“Whatever’s the matter, Snivellus?” Remus asked, coolly, holding his ground, “You don’t look any different to me.” “怎么了，鼻涕虫？”雷穆斯冷静地问，站稳脚跟，“在我看来你没什么不同。”

“Hey Prongs, look, they got Snivellus!” Sirius appeared through the crowd, grinning, followed by James, and Peter, “Excellent!” “嘿，叉子，看，他们抓到了鼻涕虫！”天狼星穿过人群出现，咧嘴笑着，后面跟着詹姆斯和彼得，“太好了！”
“It’s a good look, if you want my opinion,” James smirked, patting Remus on the shoulder by way of greeting. “如果你问我，这个样子不错，”詹姆斯得意地笑了笑，拍了拍雷穆斯的肩膀打招呼。
At the sight of Sirius, Regulus rolled his eyes and walked away, joining a group of Slytherins near the edge of the lake, huddled together muttering between themselves like a murder of crows. 看到天狼星，雷古勒斯翻了个白眼，走开了，加入了一群在湖边聚集的斯莱特林学生，像一群乌鸦一样低声咕哝着。
“When Dumbledore finds out you’re all behind this, he’ll--” Snape raged. “当邓布利多发现你们都是幕后黑手时，他会——”斯内普怒气冲冲地说。
“What?” Sirius cocked an eyebrow, leaning on James’s shoulder casually, as though they were just chatting, “Expel us? On the last day of school?!” “什么？”天狼星挑起眉毛，随意地靠在詹姆斯的肩膀上，好像他们只是在聊天，“开除我们？在学期的最后一天？！"
“You’ll pay!” Snape snarled. He turned and began to stalk back to the school, his robes still dripping. “你们会付出代价的！”斯内普咆哮着。他转身开始往学校走，他的长袍还在滴水。
“Slow down, Snivelly!” Peter called out, hardly able to contain his excitement, “You don’t want to miss the grand finale!” “慢点，鼻涕虫！”彼得喊道，几乎抑制不住自己的兴奋，“你不想错过大结局吧！”
“Wormtail!” Sirius hissed, kicking his shin. “Shh!” “虫尾巴！”天狼星嘶嘶地说，踢了他的小腿。“嘘！”
“Come on, it’s nearly time,” Remus said, trying to draw them all away from Snape. He was obviously about to lose it, and Remus didn’t trust the others not to push him over the edge. “快点，快到了，”雷穆斯说，试图把他们都从斯内普身边拉开。他显然快要失控了，而雷穆斯不相信其他人不会把他逼到崩溃。
Worryingly, they ended up quite close to Regulus and his clique, by the lake - but it was getting crowded and there weren’t many places to stand. Remus had never been one for public displays of affection, but he really wished he could hold Sirius’s hand right then, if only to stop him doing anything stupid. 令人担忧的是，他们最终靠近了雷古勒斯和他的小圈子，在湖边——但人越来越多，几乎没有地方站了。雷穆斯从来不喜欢在公众场合展示感情，但他真的希望现在能握住天狼星的手，哪怕只是为了阻止他做傻事。
No such luck. 没有这种运气。
“Reggie-boy,” Sirius nodded at his brother pleasantly, eyes glittering with mischief. “雷吉男孩，”天狼星愉快地向他的弟弟点头，眼睛里闪烁着顽皮的光芒。
“Sirius.” Regulus replied, facing forward, head held high. He was like an alabaster statue; a cold marble version of his hot-blooded sibling. “I had hoped you’d learnt to put these childish games behind you.” Regulus drawled, sounding bored as ever. “Silly pranks and schemes won’t be any use to you once the war is won. The Dark Lord demands order.” “天狼星。”雷古勒斯回答，面对前方，头抬得高高的。他像一尊雪花石膏雕像；是他热血兄弟的冷血版。“我本希望你已经学会把这些幼稚的游戏抛在脑后。”雷古勒斯拖长声音说道，听起来一如既往地无聊。“一旦战争胜利，这些愚蠢的恶作剧和阴谋对你没有任何用处。黑魔王需要秩序。”
“Sod your stupid old dark lord,” Sirius tutted, folding his arms. Remus realised the two brothers were mirroring each other’s body language. “去你的愚蠢老黑魔王，”天狼星咂舌，双臂交叉。雷穆斯意识到这对兄弟的肢体语言相互映衬。
All around the lake, students were gathering; they were seconds away. Remus took the opportunity to glance about at the most familiar faces - there was Christopher, talking animatedly to a few of his sixth year friends, no double re-telling what he had done in the owlery. Marlene, Mary and Yaz were giggling between themselves, and a bit further along was Emmeline Vance, still a perfect ice maiden, flirting with poor old Roman Rotherhide. A gaggle of younger students from the study group were practicing the incantation they were about to perform, and beside Remus, Lily and James were holding hands, wands at the ready. 湖边周围，学生们正在聚集；他们距离爆发只有几秒钟的时间。雷穆斯趁机扫视了一下最熟悉的面孔——克里斯托弗正生动地和几个六年级的朋友说话，肯定在重述他在猫头鹰塔里做的事情。玛琳、玛丽和亚兹在自己之间咯咯笑着，稍远一点是埃米琳·范斯，仍然是一位完美的冰姑娘，和可怜的罗曼·罗瑟希德调情。一群学习小组的年轻学生正在练习他们即将施展的咒语，而在雷穆斯旁边，莉莉和詹姆斯手拉着手，魔杖准备就绪。
 With a great clang, the Hogwarts clock tower struck midday, and James gave off a loud whistle, commanding everyone’s attention. It was now! 随着一声巨响，霍格沃茨的钟楼敲响了正午的钟声，James发出了一声响亮的口哨，吸引了所有人的注意力。就是现在！

 

It seemed to Remus that they were all holding their breath for a few beats, and he gripped his own wand tighter, throwing a quick grin at Sirius, before turning his attention back to the lake - and what lay beneath. Remus觉得他们都屏住了呼吸几拍，他更紧地握住了自己的魔杖，快速地对Sirius笑了一下，然后将注意力转回到湖上——以及湖下的东西。

 

All working as one, the members of The Marauders’ Inter-House Pranking Collective raised their wands and gathered their strength, shouting; “Attollo Magna!” 作为一个整体，The Marauders’ Inter-House Pranking Collective的成员们举起魔杖，聚集他们的力量，大喊：“Attollo Magna！”

 

Remus’s knees weakened. They’d tested the spell a few times, just the four of them in their bedroom (hence Sirius’s vanishing bed), but never with so many others - never so much magic at once. He felt as though he’d stuck his wand arm into a beehive; the magic began to thrum and vibrate through him, filling his mouth and nostrils like battery acid and pooling deep inside. Power. He was giddy with it; practically drunk. He shook his head doggishly, trying to maintain his focus and hold on - he had no idea what would happen if he let go. Remus的膝盖变得无力。他们测试过几次这个咒语，只是他们四个人在卧室里（这就是Sirius的床消失的原因），但从来没有和这么多人一起测试——从来没有这么多魔法一次出现。他感觉就像把魔杖手臂插进了蜂巢；魔法开始在他体内嗡嗡作响，填满了他的口腔和鼻孔，像电池酸一样积聚在深处。力量。他为此感到头晕目眩；几乎醉了。他狗狗地摇了摇头，试图保持专注并坚持下去——他不知道如果放手会发生什么。

 

Meanwhile, something was happening on the lake. The surface began to ripple and shimmer; an odd groaning creaking sound came from a mile below, and then… then… *POP*. With almost comical immediacy, the spell had worked. Remus felt a great twist inside himself - which was not unpleasant, but not ignorable either, causing him to gasp. 与此同时，湖面上发生了一些事情。湖面开始波动和闪烁；从一英里以下传来一种奇怪的呻吟声，然后……然后……*POP*。几乎滑稽地立即，咒语起作用了。Remus感觉到自己内部有一个巨大的扭曲——这并不令人不愉快，但也无法忽视，让他喘不过气来。

 

They’d done it. Students began to laugh and point, the Slytherins were crying out, one by one, stupid with shock. Even Regulus’s mouth had dropped open. 他们做到了。学生们开始笑着指指点点，Slytherins一个接一个地尖叫，震惊得愚蠢。甚至Regulus的嘴巴也张开了。

 

There, hovering just meters above the still waters, directly over the dungeons, hovered every bed and trunk from the Slytherin dormitories. It was beautiful. Absolutely perfect in every way. The layout of each dorm had been preserved; all they’d had to do was transport everything a mile or so upwards. The barrier charm (soft-hearted Lily’s idea) was working well too - meaning that no one's possessions were really in any danger of getting wet. They’d just have to work out the counter-spell, and everything would return to normal - provided all of the Slytherins worked together, of course. 就在那里，悬浮在静止的水面上方几米处，正对着地牢，悬浮着Slytherin宿舍的每一张床和每一个箱子。它很美。每一个方面都绝对完美。每个宿舍的布局都被保留了；他们只需要把所有东西往上一英里左右。屏障咒语（心软的Lily的主意）也运作得很好——这意味着没有人的财物真的有被弄湿的危险。他们只需要研究出解除咒语的方法，一切就会恢复正常——当然，前提是所有Slytherins一起合作。

 

That had been a Hufflepuff idea. 这是一个Hufflepuff的主意。

 

Remus’s muscles were still twitching from channelling all that magic. He was a live wire; static buzzed at his fingertips. Luckily, very few people noticed; they were too busy cheering or screaming with dismay at the sight before them. Fireworks were flying over the tops of the beds now, spelling out; Remus的肌肉仍然在因引导所有这些魔法而抽搐。他就像一条带电的电线；静电在他的指尖嗡嗡作响。幸运的是，很少有人注意到；他们都忙着为眼前的景象欢呼或惊叫。烟火现在飞过床顶，拼写出：

 

Have a Great Summer, Slytherin! From; Gryffindor, Ravenclaw and Hufflepuff! 祝你们有一个美好的暑假，Slytherin！来自；Gryffindor，Ravenclaw和Hufflepuff！

 

“Are you ok, Moony?” Sirius looked at him, reaching an arm out. “你还好吗，Moony？”Sirius看着他，伸出一只手臂。

 

“Don’t touch me!” Remus snapped, stepping back and shrugging Sirius off, hurriedly. He didn’t know what would happen; but he didn’t feel at all safe to be around. “别碰我！”Remus厉声道，急忙后退，甩开Sirius。他不知道会发生什么；但他觉得周围一点都不安全。

 

Sirius rubbed his own arm, looking hurt. Sirius揉了揉自己的手臂，看起来很受伤。

 

“Sorry,” Remus breathed, shaking his head again, “Just give me a minute--” “对不起，”Remus喘息着，摇了摇头，“给我一分钟——”

 

“YOU!” Oh no. Severus had re-appeared, and was charging towards the marauders, wand raised, red faced. It looked like he’d got off most of the slime. “你们！”哦不。Severus又出现了，正向恶作剧者们冲来，举起魔杖，脸色通红。看起来他已经去掉了大部分的黏液。

 

“Thieves!” He hissed, glaring at James and Sirius, “Give me my things back! Get them down at ONCE!” “小偷！”他嘶嘶地说，瞪着James和Sirius，“把我的东西还给我！立刻把它们放下来！”

 

Sirius and James were beside themselves with laughter, which didn’t help matters, but Snape really had brought this on himself. No one else was ranting and raving like a lunatic. Sirius和James笑得前仰后合，这并没有帮助，Snape真的自找的。没有其他人像疯子一样咆哮和狂怒。

 

Lily tried to intervene, breaking away from James. Lily试图干预，脱离了James。

 

“Severus, it’s not what you think, it’s easy enough to--” “Severus，这不是你想的那样，很容易——”

 

But it was too late. Snape had already turned to the lake and aimed his wand at whichever bed was his. He was trying a basic levitation spell; but it wasn’t going to work - the marauders had designed the spell specifically to ward against that kind of measure. 但已经太迟了。Snape已经转向湖面，把魔杖对准了他的任何一张床。他正在尝试一个基本的悬浮咒语；但它不会起作用——恶作剧者们设计的这个咒语就是为了防止这种措施。

 

“No, don’t!” Lily yelled, covering her eyes. “不，不要！”Lily喊道，捂住了眼睛。

 

But of course Snape never listened; not when he felt he’d been wronged. It seemed to work for a moment; one of the beds jerked a bit, and wobbled. But only for a microsecond. The next thing anyone knew, it had come loose, plummeting into the sparkling waters below with a loud splash. 但Snape当然不会听；尤其是当他觉得自己被冤枉的时候。它似乎起作用了一会儿；其中一张床猛地抖了一下，摇晃了一下。但只是瞬间。接下来任何人都知道的事，它已经松开了，随着一声巨

 

大的溅水声，跌入了下面闪闪发光的水中。

 

Severus stared; his mean mouth a hard straight line, dark greasy hair falling into his eyes. Severus盯着；他那张刻薄的嘴巴是一条硬直的线，黑色油腻的头发垂到眼前。

 

He turned, wand raised, and Remus caught a scent - a scent he had only recognised twice before; like charred flesh. Dark magic. A curse. Another twist in his gut, this time far less pleasant, and Remus felt a change inside him. 他转过身，举起魔杖，Remus闻到了一股气味——他之前只认出过两次的气味；像烧焦的肉。黑魔法。一个诅咒。腹部又一次扭动，这次远没有那么愉快，Remus感到自己内部发生了变化。

 

“Sectumsempra!” Snape cried. “Sectumsempra！”Snape喊道。

 

Remus didn’t even need his wand; he had more than enough power, and without thinking, stepped in front of James, raising his hand as Severus flung the curse. Remus甚至不需要他的魔杖；他有足够的力量，毫不犹豫地走到James前面，举起手，当Severus施展诅咒时。

 

The world seemed to take on a strange red hue, and wind roared in Remus’s ears, so that he only very faintly heard Lily’s scream, and James and Sirius shout, “Moony!” 世界似乎变成了一种奇怪的红色，风在Remus的耳边咆哮，使他只能隐约听到Lily的尖叫，James和Sirius喊道，“Moony！”

 

The curse hit Remus - but he felt nothing. It seemed to simply dissipate as soon as it touched his skin, leaving him with nothing worse than a feeling of mild sunburn. Still; he was weaker now than he had been two minutes ago. As if the force of the barrier he’d created had sapped him of all of his other magic. 诅咒击中了Remus——但他没有感觉到任何东西。它似乎一触碰到他的皮肤就消散了，除了轻微的晒伤感之外没有留下任何更糟的感觉。不过；他现在比两分钟前更虚弱了。就像他创造的屏障的力量耗尽了他的所有其他魔法。

 

He blinked, and everything came back to normal. Snape was still standing in front of him, looking terrified and furious in equal measure. Sirius’s hand was on Remus’s arm, and James was now charging towards Snape. 他眨了眨眼，一切恢复正常。Snape仍然站在他面前，既恐惧又愤怒。Sirius的手在Remus的手臂上，而James现在正向Snape冲去。

 

Remus sank slowly to the grass below, exhausted. He sat cross-legged on the ground, dazed, Sirius crouched beside him, Remus慢慢地坐到下面的草地上，筋疲力尽。他盘腿坐在地上，茫然不知所措，Sirius蹲在他旁边，

 

“Moony?!” “Moony?!”

 

“I’m ok.” “我没事。”

 

“What the fuck was that?!” Sirius whispered, urgently. He sounded scared. “那到底是什么鬼？！”Sirius紧张地低声说。他听起来很害怕。

 

“I… I don’t know.” Remus whispered back, bowing his head. “我……我不知道。”Remus低声回答，低下头。

 

“It was just a counter-jinx!” Lily suddenly shouted, and Remus realised she was addressing the students that had gathered around, curious. Always quick on her feet, that girl, “Snape tried to curse Potter, you all saw it! Lupin just caught it in time.” “这只是一个反咒！”Lily突然喊道，Remus意识到她是在对周围好奇的学生们说话。这个女孩总是行动迅速，“Snape试图诅咒Potter，你们都看到了！Lupin及时抓住了它。”

 

“Can you get up?” Sirius was asking, tugging at his elbow. “We’ll go to Madam Pomfrey--” “你能站起来吗？”Sirius问道，拉着他的肘部。“我们去找Pomfrey夫人——”

 

“No,” Remus shook his head, fiercely, getting up, “I’m ok. Honestly. Just surprised myself. Wordless magic or something, I haven’t got the hang of it yet.” “不，”Remus猛烈地摇了摇头，站起来，“我没事。真的。只是吓到了自己。无声魔法之类的，我还没掌握它。”

 

“Ok…” Sirius was looking at him warily. Lily was on crowd control, and James seemed to have chased Snape away - or else he’d gone to Slughorn to formally complain about the prank. “好吧……”Sirius警惕地看着他。Lily在控制人群，James似乎已经把Snape赶走了——否则他已经去找Slughorn正式投诉这个恶作剧了。

 

Equilibrium restored itself. Remus gave Sirius his best smile, and gave his arm a gentle squeeze to show that it was all ok now. Sirius relaxed a bit, nodding. 平衡恢复了。Remus给了Sirius他最好的微笑，轻轻握了握他的手臂，表明现在一切都好了。Sirius放松了一些，点了点头。

 

The older Slytherins a bit further along the lake edge were now conferring amongst themselves. It seemed that Snape’s misfortune had benefited his house-mates. At least now they knew what wouldn’t work. 湖边稍远处的年长Slytherins现在正在互相商量。看起来Snape的不幸对他的舍友们有好处。至少现在他们知道什么是行不通的。

 

“Sort of nice, isn’t it?” Mary sauntered over, smiling broadly and completely oblivious to what had just happened. “See them all employing a bit of teamwork. We might have house unity yet!” “有点不错，不是吗？”Mary漫步过来，咧嘴笑着，完全不知道刚刚发生了什么。“看到他们都在使用一点团队合作。我们可能会有舍内团结！”

 

“Don’t count on it,” Marlene smirked, just behind her. “别指望了，”Marlene在她后面讥笑道。

 

The Slytherins had begun to argue loudly. Slytherins已经开始大声争吵。

 

They all stayed to watch the drama unfold a while longer. One particularly hilarious attempt to restore order resulted in every second bed lifting a few feet higher. Another spell caused them all to face west, for no discernable reason. After an hour had past, a group of Ravenclaws took an interest and began workshopping more ideas with the desperate Slytherins. 他们都留在原地观看这场戏剧的展开。一次特别搞笑的尝试恢复秩序导致每隔一张床升高几英尺。另一个咒语使它们都朝西，没有明显的原因。一个小时过去了，一群Ravenclaws开始感兴趣，并与绝望的Slytherins一起探讨更多的想法。

 

At that point, Remus was feeling normal again, which meant only one thing. 那时，Remus又感觉正常了，这意味着只有一件事。

 

“I’m hungry.” He announced. “我饿了。”他宣布。

 

“Feast’ll be in half an hour,” Lily said, distracted by the squid, who was playing with one of the Slytherin's bedside tables, trying to bat it with its longest tentacle. “盛宴将在半小时后举行，”Lily说，被那个鱿鱼分散了注意力，它正在玩弄Slytherin的一张床头柜，试图用它最长的触手打它。

 

“I might go up and get changed then.” Mary said. “那我可能会上去换衣服。”Mary说。

 

Everyone agreed. Leave the Slytherins to it. 每个人都同意。让Slytherins自己处理吧。

 

As they walked back up to the castle, grinning and laughing together, Remus was aware of Sirius’s eyes still on him, but still couldn’t offer any explanation. Whatever had happened had only ever occurred once before - that afternoon in the forest with Castor and Livia. And that was hardly a pleasant memory for either him or Sirius. 当他们一起微笑着、笑着走回城堡时，Remus注意到Sirius的目光仍然在他身上，但仍然无法给出任何解释。无论发生了什么，这只发生过一次——在那天午后与Castor和Livia在森林里。而且这对他或Sirius来说都不是一个愉快的记忆。

 

“Oi, Black,” Marlene said, appearing beside them, “Ever get your bed back?” “嘿，Black，”Marlene说，出现在他们身边，“你拿回你的床了吗？”

 

“Hm?” Sirius frowned, “Oh, no, I never did

 

. Long gone now, I s’pose, seeking its fortune on the open road. Godspeed, old bed.” He sighed, wistfully. “嗯？”Sirius皱眉，“哦，不，我从来没有。现在早就不见了，我想，它在开放的道路上寻找自己的命运。一路顺风，老床。”他叹了口气，满怀遗憾。

 

Remus sniggered. Remus窃笑了一下。

 

“Aren’t you worried the school’ll charge you for it?” Marlene said. “你不担心学校会向你收费吗？”Marlene说。

 

He shrugged. Marlene tutted, 他耸了耸肩。Marlene咂了咂嘴，

 

“Spoilt brat.” “被宠坏的孩子。”

 

“Did you even try to get it back?” Lily asked. “你有没有尝试过把它找回来？”Lily问。

 

“Well, we don’t know where it went.” James replied, chuckling at the memory. “嗯，我们不知道它去了哪里。”James回答，回忆起这段记忆时笑了。

 

“Not even a basic summoning charm?” “连基本的召唤咒语都没试过？”

 

“No, we never--” “不，我们从来没有——”

 

“Accio bed!” Sirius yelled at the top of his lungs, waving his wand. “Accio床！”Sirius用尽全力喊道，挥动他的魔杖。

 

A faint and distant rumble. 一阵微弱而遥远的隆隆声。

 

“Oh shit…” Sirius murmured. “哦，糟了……”Sirius喃喃道。

 

The lake behind them began to bubble, and they all turned in time to see Sirius’s four poster bed rising from the water like a great mahogany submarine. Draped in seaweed and heavy waterlogged velvet hangings, it rose into the air and flew towards them so that they had to scatter and dive to the ground, covering the heads. It crashed on the spot Sirius had summoned it to with a heavy, squelchy THUD, and promptly splintered into several pieces. 他们身后的湖开始冒泡，他们及时转身看到Sirius的四柱床从水中升起，像一艘巨大的红木潜水艇。它披着海藻和沉重的湿透的天鹅绒挂毯，升到空中，向他们飞来，他们不得不散开并跳到地上，遮住头。它在Sirius召唤它的地方重重地摔下，发出沉重的“扑通”声，迅速碎成几块。

 

Silence for a few seconds, as Lily, Marlene, Mary, Yaz, James, Peter, Remus and Sirius raised their heads once more, climbing to their feet in amazement. Then laughter from every quarter - especially the Slytherins still gathered by the lake’s edge. 几秒钟的沉默，Lily、Marlene、Mary、Yaz、James、Peter、Remus和Sirius再次抬起头，惊讶地站起来。然后是四处的笑声——尤其是仍然聚集在湖边的Slytherins。

 

Sirius just stood there, scratching his head. Sirius只是站在那里，挠着头。

 

“Hm.” He said. “Bottom of the lake all along, eh?” “嗯。”他说。“一直在湖底，对吧？”

 

It was still dripping. The sheets were green with algae and sand and grit piled up on the mattress. 它还在滴水。床单上长满了海藻，床垫上堆积着沙子和砂砾。

 

“Oi, you wanker!” James said, approaching the rescued bed and snatching up a rectangular pile of greyish mulch, “Is this my quidditch magazine?!” “嘿，你这个混蛋！”James说，走近被救起的床，抓起一堆灰色的堆肥，“这是我的魁地奇杂志吗？！”

 

“Er… maybe…” Sirius grinned - then, catching the murderous glint in James’s eye, began to run at full pelt back to the castle, James chasing after him. “呃……可能吧……”Sirius咧嘴笑了——然后，看到James眼中的杀意，开始全速跑回城堡，James在后面追赶。

 

“I suppose now’s as good a time as any,” Peter whispered to Remus, “But, er… Filch caught me with the map earlier. He confiscated it.” “我想现在是个好时机，”Peter低声对Remus说，“但是，呃……Filch之前抓到了我和地图。他没收了它。”

 

“What?!” Remus rounded on him, angry. That map was his! His idea, his magic! “什么？！”Remus转向他，愤怒地说。那张地图是他的！他的主意，他的魔法！

 

“Don’t be angry with me, Moony!” Peter cringed, “It was locked and everything, I promise! No one can get into it unless they’re up to no good -- and they’d have to break into Filch’s office!” “不要对我生气，Moony！”Peter畏缩道，“它是锁着的，一切都是，我保证！没有人能进去，除非他们别有用心——而且他们必须闯进Filch的办公室！”

 

Remus stopped at these words. He was right about that. After all; anyone who could achieve both those feats would certainly be worthy of the map. And he had wanted to leave something behind; a true legacy. This way, perhaps Messrs Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot & Prongs might be remembered, one day. Remus停在这些话前。他对此是对的。毕竟；任何能完成这两个壮举的人肯定值得拥有这张地图。而且他一直想留下点什么；一个真正的遗产。这样，也许Messrs Moony、Wormtail、Padfoot和Prongs有一天会被记住。

 

He squinted ahead at the two dark haired boys chasing each other and whooping with laughter. He looked at the four girls, who’d all linked arms and were walking cheerfully back to the castle, voices light and carefree. 他眯眼看着前方两个黑发男孩互相追逐，欢笑着。他看了看那四个女孩，她们都挽着胳膊，愉快地走回城堡，声音轻松无忧。

 

What did Remus Lupin have to be angry about? What had he to worry about? His heart swelled, and he was reminded of something Sirius had told him a few months ago. Love was something you did, not something you said; and every one of these people had proved that to him. Remus Lupin有什么可生气的？他有什么可担心的？他的心膨胀了起来，他想起了几个月前Sirius告诉他的一句话。爱是你做的事情，而不是你说的事情；这些人每一个都向他证明了这一点。

 

“Alright, Wormy,” Remus flung his arm around Peter’s shoulders, grinning, “You’re forgiven. C’mon, let’s catch up.” “好了，Wormy，”Remus把胳膊甩到Peter的肩膀上，笑着说，“你被原谅了。来吧，我们赶上去。”

Chapter 151: The War: July 1978All our times have come

Here but now they're gone

Seasons don't fear the reaper

Nor do the wind, the sun or the rain,

(We can be like they are)

 

Come on baby, (don't fear the reaper)

Baby take my hand, (don't fear the reaper)

We'll be able to fly, (don't fear the reaper)

Baby I'm your man.


Sunday 2nd July 1978
“Hurry up, Potter!” Remus hammered on the glass in the door of the phone box. “Other people need to make phonecalls y’know!” 1978年7月2日星期日
“快点, Potter!” Remus在电话亭门的玻璃上敲击着。“还有其他人需要打电话呢！”
James rather rudely turned his back, hunching his shoulders and speaking furtively into the receiver. James很不礼貌地转过身，缩起肩膀，偷偷地对着听筒说话。
“Leave him be, Moony,” Sirius murmured, leaning heavily on the fence. He was wearing very dark sunglasses and looked paler than normal. “And stop all the banging, will you?!” “别管他，Moony，”Sirius嘟囔着，沉重地靠在围栏上。他戴着很深的太阳镜，看起来比平时更苍白。“别再敲了，好吗?!”
“Take another painkilling draught,” Remus tutted, “You’re just hungover, it’s your own fault for getting so smashed.” “再喝点止痛药剂，”Remus咂嘴道，“你只是宿醉了，这是你自己喝得太醉的错。”
“I was the life and soul, I’ll have you know.” Sirius retorted, folding his arms as Remus came to sit beside him. “我可是聚会的灵魂人物，你要知道。”Sirius反驳道，双臂交叉，Remus坐在他旁边。
The Potters had hosted the end of school party the night before, for all Hogwarts leavers and their friends. Yaz and Chris had come, even though they both had another year to go. A few members of the Order of the Phoenix were there too - no Dumbledore, but Ferox and Moody and Frank Longbottom and his pretty blonde girlfriend (now fiance, apparently). Moody had called Remus over to them a few times, only to be intercepted by Mrs Potter. Potters昨晚主办了毕业派对，邀请了所有霍格沃茨的毕业生和他们的朋友。Yaz和Chris也来了，尽管他们还要再读一年。凤凰社的一些成员也在场——没有Dumbledore，但有Ferox、Moody和Frank Longbottom及其漂亮的金发女友（现在是未婚妻，显然）。Moody几次叫Remus过去，但都被Potter夫人拦住了。
“It's his school leavers party, Alastor!” She hissed, after the fourth time. “Let him enjoy himself for five minutes before forming a flipping war council!” “这是他的毕业派对，Alastor！”她在第四次之后嘶嘶地说。“让他享受五分钟的时间，然后再形成该死的战争委员会！”
She said this so sharply that they desisted - Remus was a bit shocked too. That was the closest he’d ever heard Mrs Potter come to swearing. 她说得如此尖锐，以至于他们停止了——Remus也有点震惊。这是他听到Potter夫人最接近骂人的一次。
The rest of the party had felt just like the Gryffindor common room - while at the same time feeling nothing like the Gryffindor common room. Remus tried not to be so sad. He tried to imagine that one day he would find somewhere else that felt as much like home as Hogwarts had. 派对的其余部分感觉就像格兰芬多的公共休息室——但同时又完全不像格兰芬多的公共休息室。Remus试图不那么难过。他试图想象有一天他会找到一个像霍格沃茨一样感觉像家的地方。
Lily, Mary and Marlene all had to leave at midnight - they’d promised their parents they’d spend the night at Lily’s. Apparently their families felt that after seven years of boarding school, enough was enough. Lily、Mary和Marlene都在午夜离开了——她们答应了父母要在Lily家过夜。显然，他们的家人觉得在寄宿学校七年后，已经足够了。
Which brought Remus back to the present, watching James through the phone box door, talking to his girlfriend. Who he had literally said goodbye to eight hours earlier. 这让Remus回到了现在，通过电话亭的门看着James和他的女朋友通话。八小时前他刚和她告别。
“So unfair, him making us race down here - as if I could ever beat James ‘hangover free since ‘73’ Potter.” Remus grumbled. “And it was unsportsmanlike. He knows I have a handicap.” “太不公平了，他让我们赶紧下来——好像我能打败自‘73年以来从未宿醉的James Potter似的。”Remus抱怨道。“而且这不公平。他知道我有个障碍。”
“I thought your hip was better since you got that stuff off Marls?” Sirius frowned, making his sunglasses slip down his nose. “我以为自从你从Marls那儿拿到东西后，你的臀部好多了？”Sirius皱眉，使他的太阳镜滑落到鼻子上。
“It is.” Remus replied. “I meant my smoking.” “是的。”Remus回答。“我是说我的抽烟。”
There was a low rumble somewhere in the distance. Sirius sat up, suddenly, ripping off his glasses. 远处传来低沉的隆隆声。Sirius突然坐起身来，摘下他的眼镜。
“Is that?!” “那是?!”
Remus sighed. Remus叹了口气。
“Sounds like it, yeah…” “听起来像，是的…”
In a few moments, the neighbour’s motorbike came streaking through the village, growling all the way. Sirius gazed after it, starstruck. Once it was nothing but a shiny chrome dot in the distance, he leaned back, smiling to himself. 过了一会儿，邻居的摩托车咆哮着穿过村庄。Sirius看着它，惊叹不已。当它只剩下远处一个闪亮的铬点时，他靠回去，自己笑了笑。
“Ah, I’ve missed her.” “啊，我想她了。”
“It would be a ‘she’.” Remus muttered, folding his arms. “那肯定是个‘她’。”Remus嘟囔着，交叉双臂。
“Potter!” Sirius now got up to thump on the phone box door, “Get out here right now!” He turned to Remus, “Will you cheer the fuck up after you’ve had your phonecall?!” “Potter!” Sirius现在站起来敲打电话亭的门，“现在就出来！”他转向Remus，“打完电话你能高兴点吗？！”
“Yes.” Remus said, petulantly, looking at his feet. “是的。”Remus任性地说，看着他的脚。
It was another five minutes of ‘goodbyes’ and ‘speak soons’ before Remus got his chance. He dialed the number eagerly, and coiled the plastic cord around his fingers as he listened to it ring. 又过了五分钟的‘再见’和‘回头见’后，Remus才有机会。他急切地拨了号码，用手指卷着塑料线听着铃声。
“Yeah?” “喂？”
“Is that how you answer the phone?!” “你就这么接电话的吗？！”
“Remus?” “Remus？”
“Hiya!” “嗨！”
“Crikey! Wasn’t expecting you, did we set something up?” “天啊！没想到是你，我们有约定吗？”
“Nope,” Remus shook his head, grinning madly, “I finished school - I can call whenever I like now!” “没有，”Remus疯狂地摇头笑道，“我毕业了——现在我可以随时打电话！”
“Brilliant!” “太棒了！”
He heard some rustling on the other end of the phone and assumed Grant was making himself comfortable. Good. Sirius and James could wait a good long time. “So when you coming down to see me, eh?” Grant was asking now. 他听到电话那头有些沙沙声，猜想Grant在让自己舒服。很好。Sirius和James可以等很久。“那你什么时候下来见我？”Grant现在在问。
“Soon!” Remus said, automatically. He could apparate to Brighton in a matter of seconds, now the thought struck him. But that would be a tough one to explain. “Next week?” “很快！”Remus自动地说。他可以在几秒钟内幻影移形到布莱顿，现在这个想法让他震惊。但这很难解释。“下周？”
That would hit the sweet spot between full moons, at least. 至少，这样可以避开满月期。


“Working Saturday,” Grant replied. “On lates at the pub. Saving up for a holiday… er… August?” “星期六上班，”Grant回答。“在酒吧上晚班。为度假攒钱……呃……八月？”
“Oh. Um. Well, ok,” Remus said, a bit disheartened. “哦。嗯。好吧，”Remus有点沮丧地说。
“Sorry, just I’ve been waiting for a proper summer holiday ages, and I’m getting on a plane and everything…” “对不起，我只是等待了很久的一个正经暑假，我要坐飞机什么的……”
“No, no, August is fine!” “不，不，八月很好！”
“Good, I’ll remember to get some milk in. So where you living now?” “好，我会记得买些牛奶。那么你现在住哪儿？”
“At my friend James’s. His parents are really nice.” “在我朋友James家。他的父母很好。”
“Not moved in with lover boy, then?” “那你没和情人一起住？”
“He’s here too.” Remus explained, knowing it sounded a bit weird. “We’re going to start looking for somewhere to live soon, though. London, hopefully.” “他也在这里。”Remus解释道，知道这听起来有点奇怪。“不过我们很快就会开始找地方住。希望是伦敦。”
“He rich, then?” Grant snorted, “Shoulda’ guessed that. Looks well-heeled, don’t he?” “他很有钱，对吧？”Grant嗤笑道，“应该猜到的。他看起来很有钱，不是吗？”
“I s’pose.” “我想是吧。”
“He does. Got that good posture. Oi, let me tell you about this bloke I had round the other night…” Grant said, and began a very long and almost unbelievable story about an encounter he’d had with a fisherman (“a genuine, honest to jesus fisherman, for fuck’s sake.”) who’d done something very odd in Grant’s bathtub before making a hasty exit in the early hours of the morning. By the end of it, Remus was hunched over in the phone box, wheezing with laughter, tears streaming down his cheeks. “他确实有。姿势很好。喂，让我告诉你我前几晚遇到的一个家伙……”Grant说，然后开始讲述一个非常长且几乎不可思议的故事，关于他遇到的一位渔夫（“一个真正的、诚实的、上帝保佑的渔夫，真是的。”）在Grant的浴缸里做了些非常奇怪的事，然后在清晨匆忙离开。到最后，Remus在电话亭里弯腰笑得喘不过气来，眼泪流淌。
“What’s so funny?!” James and Sirius were keen to know, when he finally emerged. “有什么好笑的？！”James和Sirius急切地想知道，当他终于出来时。
“Couldn’t possibly tell you,” Remus replied, hiccupping, “Muggle humour.” “我实在无法告诉你，”Remus回答，打了个嗝，“麻瓜幽默。”
“Reckon we ought to see how Pete’s doing?” James asked as they walked back to the house. “我们应该去看看Pete怎么样？”James在他们走回房子时问。
“Nah, you know how he is with hangovers,” Sirius replied, dark shades still firmly in place. “不，你知道他宿醉的样子，”Sirius回答，深色太阳镜依然戴着。
“All right, but we need to make sure not to leave him out,” James said, opening the garden gate, “I think he’s worried about it…” “好吧，但我们需要确保不要把他落下，”James说，打开了花园门，“我觉得他很担心这件事……”
“Yeah, yeah.” Sirius yawned. “Oi, quidditch?” “是的，是的。”Sirius打了个哈欠。“喂，魁地奇？”
“Yes!” James grinned, “Just let me change…” “是的！”James笑道，“让我换件衣服……”

Whatever makes you happy, dears.” She patted Remus gently on the shoulder, and kissed Sirius’s cheek as she passed him on her way downstairs. “嗯，如果你们喜欢的话，”她慢慢地点头道。“我想床够大，两个也可以。只要你们开心就好，亲爱的。”她轻轻拍了拍Remus的肩膀，然后在下楼时亲吻了Sirius的脸颊。
And that was pretty much that. 就这样了。
Wednesday 5th July 1978
They were permitted a longer holiday than expected - two days longer, in fact. The invitations came late Tuesday night; a note each from Dumbledore, requesting their presence at a secret location known only to James’s father, reachable only by portkey. The notes vanished as soon as they’d been read, simply dissolved away in their hands. 1978年7月5日星期三
他们被允许比预期的假期多待两天。邀请函是在周二晚上很晚才来的；每人一张来自Dumbledore的便条，请求他们到一个只有James的父亲知道的秘密地点，只能通过传送门到达。便条一读完就消失了，在他们手中简单地溶解了。
They’d all been expecting something like it, but Remus was surprised how nervous he suddenly grew. He was not the only one. “Tell me something.” He mumbled, thickly, “Anything.” “告诉我点什么。”他含糊地喃喃道，“什么都行。”
“I’m really scared about tomorrow.” Remus whispered. “It feels so real now. But I think it’s normal to be scared. I think anyone would be.” “我真的很害怕明天。”Remus低声说。“现在感觉真的很真实。但我觉得害怕是正常的。我觉得任何人都会的。”

“I’m really scared about tomorrow.” Remus whispered. “It feels so real now. But I think it’s normal to be scared. I think anyone would be.”

Sirius just made a discontented sort of grunt. Remus squeezed him and tried a different tack. “But d’you know what scares me more?”

“Hm?”

“The fact that we’re planning to move in together and neither of us can cook.”

Sirius began to laugh, and eventually they must have both fallen asleep properly. When they woke up they were still wound around each other, sweat had gathered where their bare skin pressed together, and Remus had big wide red patches all over until he’d showered.

It was a bit of a walk to the portkey, which turned out to be a bright yellow rubber duck, left in some long grass at the end of one of the fields surrounding the village. Remus didn’t mind, he liked stretching his legs now it didn’t hurt so much. 他们走了好一段路才到港口钥匙，结果是一只亮黄色的橡皮鸭，放在村庄周围田野尽头的长草里。Remus不介意，他喜欢现在不再那么疼的伸展双腿。
“Can’t believe we’re only a few miles from London,” he marvelled, looking up at the cloudless summer sky, the rolling green hillsides. “真不敢相信我们离伦敦只有几英里，”他惊叹道，抬头看着无云的夏日天空，连绵起伏的绿色山丘。
“Garden of England,” James grinned. “英格兰花园，”James笑了。
Fleamont solemnly held out the duck for them all to put their hands on. Fleamont郑重地举起那只鸭子，让他们都把手放上去。
“All got your wands?” He asked, sharply, and they each nodded, swallowing hard. Peter was sweating and looked faintly ill - Remus hoped he wouldn’t throw up until they’d arrived wherever they were going. “都拿到魔杖了吗？”他尖锐地问道，他们每个人都点了点头，艰难地吞咽着。Peter在冒汗，看起来有点病恹恹的——Remus希望他在到达目的地之前不要吐出来。
They all touched the duck, and suddenly found themselves whirling through space and time at an incredible rate. It was worse than apparating, but better than floo powder, Remus decided. 他们都触碰了那只鸭子，突然发现自己以惊人的速度在时空中旋转。Remus觉得这比幻影移形更糟糕，但比飞路粉要好。
Moments later, all five men landed in a very small, chintzy living room. The carpet was thick, soft pink, the sofas an ugly yellowish cream fake leather, and the wallpaper a hideous floral design with metallic streaks that caught the light. 片刻之后，五个人都落在了一个非常小的、俗气的客厅里。地毯是厚厚的软粉色，沙发是丑陋的黄色奶油色人造皮革，墙纸是一种可怕的花卉设计，有金属条纹在光线下闪烁。

Remus smiled, politely, privately thinking that Molly must be right. Remus礼貌地笑了笑，心里暗想Molly一定是对的。

Frank and Alice were in the kitchen, lining up a queue of mugs on the counter. 他说话时，他带他们走出了过于女性化的客厅，穿过狭窄的走廊，进入一个小厨房，厨房后面有个温室。Frank和Alice在厨房里，把杯子排成一排。

After the shadowy gloom of the narrow 1930s kitchen, the conservatory was blindingly bright and extremely warm. It had a clean terracotta tile floor, covered over with a homespun rag rug. The surrounding windows were glass and displayed an immaculately kept garden which had a double swing set and a slide; the roof was clear perspex and smattered with old dead leaves leftover from winter. There was a strong smell of fertiliser and geranium, potted plants were dotted about the place on shelves and end tables. 穿过阴暗狭窄的1930年代厨房后，温室显得异常明亮和温暖。地板是干净的赤陶瓷砖，上面铺着自制的布毯。周围的窗户是玻璃的，展示着一个保存完好的花园，里面有一套双人秋千和一个滑梯；屋顶是透明的有机玻璃，点缀着冬天留下的旧枯叶。有一种浓烈的肥料和天竺葵的气味，盆栽植物散布在架子和边桌上。

 

After the shadowy gloom of the narrow 1930s kitchen, the conservatory was blindingly bright and extremely warm. It had a clean terracotta tile floor, covered over with a homespun rag rug. The surrounding windows were glass and displayed an immaculately kept garden which had a double swing set and a slide; the roof was clear perspex and smattered with old dead leaves leftover from winter. There was a strong smell of fertiliser and geranium, potted plants were dotted about the place on shelves and end tables.
在狭窄的1930年代厨房的阴暗昏暗之后，温室明亮得刺眼且极其温暖。地板是干净的红土砖，覆盖着自制的旧地毯。周围的窗户是玻璃的，展示了一片精心维护的花园，里面有一套双人秋千和一个滑梯；屋顶是透明的有机玻璃，撒满了冬天遗留下来的旧枯叶。空气中有强烈的肥料和天竺葵的气味，花盆植物点缀在架子和边桌上。

Remus didn’t notice any of these things at first, because the room was packed full of people. There must have been twenty or thirty witches and wizards, gathered solemnly around a large wooden table, or else standing, or crammed into the wicker garden furniture in the corner. Hagrid loomed largest - Remus had never seen Hagrid anywhere but Hogwarts, which was so big that it sort of compensated for the gamekeeper’s gargantuan proportions. In this hot little sun room he barely seemed real.
一开始，Remus没有注意到这些东西，因为房间里挤满了人。那里一定有二三十个巫师，严肃地围坐在一张大木桌周围，或者站着，或者挤在角落里的藤制花园家具中。Hagrid最显眼——Remus从未在霍格沃茨以外的地方见过Hagrid，霍格沃茨很大，某种程度上弥补了这位猎场看守的巨型体型。在这个小小的阳光房里，他几乎不显得真实。

There were other recognisable faces; the Prewett twins, Mad-eye Moody, Professor Ferox, Ted Tonks, Emmeline Vance and Dorcas Meadowes - no Dumbledore, but to Remus’s delight, Lily, Mary and Marlene were huddled in one corner, looking awfully young and shy in such a crowd. They greeted the boys with an eager kind of relief. Mary clung to Remus’s neck very tightly.
还有其他熟悉的面孔；Prewett双胞胎，Mad-eye Moody，Ferox教授，Ted Tonks，Emmeline Vance和Dorcas Meadowes——没有Dumbledore，但让Remus欣喜的是，Lily，Mary和Marlene挤在一个角落，看起来在这样的群体中非常年轻和害羞。她们热情地迎接男孩们，显得松了一口气。Mary紧紧抱住Remus的脖子。

“你们来了！”他惊讶地说。

“I never was that bright,” she smiled ruefully.
“我从来不那么聪明，”她苦笑着说。

“Remus!” Marlene reached for him, “This is Danny!”
“Remus！”Marlene伸手招呼他，“这是Danny！”

A tall man stood just behind her. He had Marlene’s smile; her ruddy cheeks and straw coloured hair.
一个高个子男子站在她身后。他有着Marlene的微笑；她红润的脸颊和稻草色的头发。

“Danny McKinnon！”James突然喊道。终于向Lily打了足够的招呼，他才刚刚注意到这次尴尬的见面。他大步上前，“我能不能说你绝对是火箭队有史以来最棒的击球手？！”

Danny友好地笑了，

That shut everyone up, and they gathered around the table looking very serious. They began with a few introductions, though one way or another most people knew each other. When Sirius’s name was spoken there was a bit of hushed murmuring, but he just stared defiantly back at them all. 这让大家都安静了，他们围绕着桌子，神情严肃。虽然大家或多或少都认识，但他们还是开始了几次介绍。当提到Sirius的名字时，有些低声的议论，但他只是 defiantly地盯着大家。Remus为他感到自豪——让他们看看，你永远无法以貌取人，或以名字来判断一个人。

After that, someone read minutes from the last meeting - Remus didn’t understand any of it. 之后，有人读了上次会议的记录——Remus一点也听不懂。他们似乎都在用一种奇怪的成人代码说话，没有人像在学校时那样停下来解释。提到了许多名字；全国各地的支持他们的人——或者已经转向对方的人。各种政策正在推动通过Wizengamot，影响投票的方式；如何说服人们接受订单的思维方式。

Remus dared glance over at Sirius, James and Peter, and was relieved to see that they were just as puzzled as he was. Then the list of missing was read, and everyone followed that all right. Alice proposed a minute’s silence, which they all observed.
Remus敢于瞥了一眼Sirius、James和Peter，感到欣慰的是他们和他一样困惑。然后念出了失踪人员的名单，大家都听得很清楚。Alice提议默哀一分钟，他们都遵守了。
