“妈妈，拜托……”雷穆斯转过头，震惊于自己感到的痛苦。“我还没准备好……现在还不行，好吗？”

 

Her face softened. She sighed,  

她的脸柔和下来。她叹了口气，

 

“All right, my darling. I’m sorry.”  

“好吧，亲爱的。对不起。”

 

Who the fuck is Gethin?! He wanted to shout. How many surprises are waiting for me, after you’re gone? He’d known this was coming, but it was still the worst news of his life. He couldn’t shake the sense of betrayal. They’d only just found each other.  

格辛到底是谁？！他想大喊。你走了之后，还有多少惊喜等着我？他早就知道会有这一天，但这仍然是他一生中最糟糕的消息。他无法摆脱被背叛的感觉。他们才刚刚找到彼此。

 

Sirius grew uncomfortable in the silence that followed. He didn’t understand Hope and Remus’s shared inability to say the important things; Sirius could never see why everyone didn’t just say what they felt as soon as they felt it. But he respected their privacy, and got up,  

在随后的沉默中，天狼星变得不安。他不理解霍普和雷穆斯之间无法说出重要事情的习惯；天狼星从来不明白为什么大家不能在感觉到的时候马上说出自己的感受。但他尊重他们的隐私，站了起来，

 

“I’m going to get a cup of tea, Remus,” he said, gently, “Would you like one?”  

“雷穆斯，我去喝杯茶，”他说，温柔地，“你要一杯吗？”

 

Remus nodded,  

雷穆斯点点头，

 

“Canteen’s down the hall,” he said, staring at the floor, still holding Hope’s hand. “I’ll meet you there, in a minute.”  

“餐厅在走廊尽头，”他说，盯着地板，仍然握着霍普的手。“我一会儿去找你。”

 

“Can I get you anything, Ms. Lupin?”  

“卢平女士，你需要什么吗？”

 

She shook her head,  

她摇摇头，

 

“No thank you, dear. It was lovely to meet you.”  

“不用了，亲爱的。很高兴见到你。”

 

He inclined his head, gallantly, smiling politely - god, he could be charming in even the most desperate situations - then quickly left.  

他优雅地点点头，礼貌地微笑——天啊，即使在最绝望的情况下他也能如此迷人——然后迅速离开。

 

Remus let go of Hope’s hand, and buried his face in his palms. Fuck . Couldn’t he just enjoy something for five minutes without a tragedy?  

雷穆斯松开霍普的手，把脸埋进手掌中。该死。他就不能享受五分钟没有悲剧的时光吗？

 

“He’s a very nice young man.” Hope said, brightly.  

“他是个很好的年轻人。”霍普愉快地说。

 

“Yeah,” Remus replied, huffing a joyless laugh, rubbing the back of his head, nervously.  

“是啊，”雷穆斯回应道，苦笑了一声，紧张地揉了揉后脑勺。

 

“I can see why you like him.” She prompted.  

“我明白你为什么喜欢他。”她提示道。

 

She wanted the unpleasantness over, clearly. Perhaps she wanted to go back to talking about Lyall. Well, he wasn’t going to let her. She wasn’t the only one who could drop bombshells.  

显然，她想结束不

 

愉快的对话。也许她想回到谈论莱尔的话题。好吧，他不会让她得逞。她不是唯一一个能投下震撼弹的人。

 

He looked at her, trying to meet her eye.  

他看着她，试图与她对视。

 

“Look, there’s something I really feel like I ought to explain, er. About Sirius. About Sirius and me.”  

“听着，我真的觉得有件事我应该解释一下，呃。关于天狼星。关于我和天狼星。”

 

Hope closed her eyes with a soft smile and gently shook her head,  

霍普闭上眼睛，微笑着，轻轻摇了摇头，

 

“It’s all right, cariad ,” she took his hand and patted it, “I knew the moment I saw the two of you.”  

“没关系，亲爱的，”她握住他的手，拍了拍，“我看到你们俩的那一刻就知道了。”

 

“You… really?” Remus stared at her. He’d never talked about this with anyone older than himself before.  

“你……真的？”雷穆斯盯着她。他以前从未和比自己年长的人谈过这件事。

 

“I’ve had a feeling for a while. I won’t pretend it makes no difference at all,” she replied, choosing her words carefully, “But it doesn’t change who you are, my darling boy.”  

“我有一阵子感觉到了。我不会假装这完全没有影响，”她回答，慎重选择着措辞，“但这不会改变你的本质，我亲爱的孩子。”

 

She reached for his hand again and he held it. She stroked his knuckles softly with her thumb.  

她再次伸手，他握住了她的手。她用拇指轻柔地抚摸他的指关节。

 

“You love him, don’t you?”  

“你爱他，是吗？”

 

“I…” Remus felt the familiar panic rising at the sound of that word, but as it was just the two of them, and he felt he owed it to her to be honest, he nodded. “Yes.”  

“我……”雷穆斯听到那个词感到熟悉的恐慌，但因为只有他们两个人，他觉得自己应该对她诚实，于是点了点头。“是的。”

 

“And he loves you.”  

“而且他爱你。”

 

“I think so. Yes, he does.”  

“我想是的。他确实爱我。”

 

“That’s all I need to know, then.” She smiled again. She let out a great sigh, “Love. It’s the only thing you get to take with you, you know.”  

 

“那就够了。”她再次微笑，长叹了一口气，“爱。那是你唯一能带走的东西，你知道吗。”

 

Chapter 154: The War: Autumn 1978 

Stop your messing around (ah-ah-ah)

Better think of your future (ah-ah-ah)

Time you straighten right out (ah-ah-ah)

Creating problems in town (ah-ah-ah)

 

Remus peered over the top of his book through the cafe window to see if there had been any change in the street ahead of him. He looked at the clock on the greasy wall beside him. Five minutes to go, if Pete wasn’t running late.  
Remus透过咖啡馆的窗户从书的顶部望去，看前面的街道是否有任何变化。他看了看旁边油腻的墙上的钟。还有五分钟，如果Pete不迟到的话。
Remus looked at his book again. He hadn’t really been reading it, he was too distracted. He found himself rarely in the mood for studying, these days, between Order meetings, strange and half-explained assignments, visiting Hope in the hospice - which he tried to do every other day, now.  
Remus再次看了看他的书。他其实并没有真正读进去，他太分心了。这些天来，他发现自己很少有心情学习，在Order会议、奇怪且未完全解释的任务、以及去临终关怀医院探望Hope之间——他现在尽量每隔一天去一次。
On top of this, Remus and Sirius were learning to look after themselves for the first time. After a week of takeaways, Remus admitted defeat and asked to borrow a recipe book from Mrs Potter. Results had been mixed, so far. Sirius, meanwhile, seemed to have reached crisis point at the state of the bathroom, and dedicated several evenings to finally learning some cleaning spells.  
除此之外，Remus和Sirius正在第一次学着照顾自己。在吃了一周的外卖后，Remus承认失败并向Potter夫人借了一本食谱。目前结果参差不齐。与此同时，Sirius似乎已经无法忍受浴室的状态，花了几个晚上终于学会了一些清洁咒语。
They’d had a fight over whether or not to get a television (Sirius was bizarrely suspicious of this muggle technology; he couldn’t see the point), and then another one over the motorbike (Remus hated everything about it, but most of all the highly dangerous flying charms Sirius was attempting).  
他们曾为是否买电视争吵过（Sirius对这种麻瓜技术有着奇怪的怀疑；他看不出有什么意义），然后又为摩托车争吵过（Remus讨厌一切与之相关的东西，但最讨厌的是Sirius试图施展的那些极其危险的飞行咒语）。
Other than that, things were going pretty well. Well. As well as anyone could expect.  
除此之外，一切都进行得相当顺利。嗯。尽可能地顺利。
The clock kept ticking. Remus lifted the chipped mug of tea to his lips, drank, then grimaced. Stone cold. He’d been there an hour at least, but it wasn’t as if he had anywhere else to be.  
时钟继续滴答作响。Remus把缺口的茶杯举到嘴边，喝了一口，然后皱起眉头。冰凉。他至少在这里待了一个小时，但也不是没有其他地方可去。
Since the botched mission to Knockturn Alley back in July, Remus had noticed a clear shift in the nature of his missions. He was often paired with Peter, and generally only sent on ‘soft’ assignments - passing on messages, collecting dead portkeys - once or twice he’d been stuck making sandwiches for visitors to the Potters.  
自从七月份失败的Knockturn Alley任务以来，Remus注意到他的任务性质发生了明显变化。他经常与Peter搭档，通常只被派去执行一些“轻松”的任务——传递信息、收集失效的portkey——有一两次他被困在为Potter家的访客做三明治。
Meanwhile, Sirius and James’s fortunes had taken them in a completely different direction. They both spent much of their time with Frank and Alice, or the Prewett twins, up to all sorts of interesting things like advanced defense, guard duties, and even one or two midnight raids.  
与此同时，Sirius和James的运气把他们带向了完全不同的方向。他们大部分时间都和Frank和Alice，或者Prewett双胞胎在一起，从事各种有趣的事情，如高级防御、守卫任务，甚至有一两次午夜突袭。
Sirius was having the time of his life. Remus was miserable, but not saying so. In other words, business as usual.  
Sirius过得非常开心。Remus很痛苦，但没有说出口。换句话说，一切如常。
Finally, Remus looked up and saw movement. It was the end of the working day, and men in smart suits and hats began to fill the pavements. If you looked very closely, you could see that some of these men and women were dressed a bit less conservatively than the others. It was the end of the day at the Ministry of Magic, too.  
最后，Remus抬头看到了一些动静。工作日结束了，穿着讲究西装和帽子的男人们开始挤满人行道。如果你仔细看，你会发现这些男人和女人中的一些人穿得比其他人稍微不那么保守。魔法部的一天也结束了。
Remus got up, quickly, banging his shins on the orange plastic chair beside him. Hissing through his teeth, he limped slightly on his way out. Outside it was muggy - not sunny, but hot and sticky; headache weather. Thick, queasy storm clouds hung above the grey buildings, and a powerful reek rose up from the cafe bins, old food putrefying in the unseasonable September heat.  
Remus快速站起来，撞到了旁边橙色塑料椅子的小腿。他咬紧牙关，微微一瘸一拐地走出去。外面闷热——没有阳光，但又热又黏；让人头痛的天气。厚重的、令人不安的暴风云悬挂在灰色建筑物上方，咖啡馆垃圾桶里散发出一股强烈的臭味，旧食物在异常炎热的九月中腐烂。
Remus hung back a moment, waiting and watching, not wanting to be seen. A tall, handsome young man strode past, wearing black robes and a bottle green waistcoat. He had sharp cheekbones and platinum hair, though he was very young - Remus recognised him at once as Lucius Malfoy, the man Narcissa had risked her life to marry. Remus watched him stalk up the street, fleetingly commending Sirius’s cousin on her excellent taste.  
Remus停了一会儿，等待并观察，不想被人看到。一个高大英俊的年轻人走过，穿着黑色长袍和瓶绿色背心。他有着锐利的颧骨和铂金色的头发，虽然他还很年轻——Remus一眼就认出他是Lucius Malfoy，Narcissa冒着生命危险嫁给的男人。Remus看着他沿街走去，短暂地称赞Sirius的表妹有很好的品味。
“Oh, hello Moony,”  
“哦，你好，Moony。”
Remus jumped. Peter somehow still had the ability to take him by surprise - you almost never saw him coming.  
Remus吓了一跳。Peter不知怎么总能让他吃惊——你几乎从未见过他来。
“Christ, Pete, you scared me.”  
“天啊，Pete，你吓到我了。”
“Well if you hadn’t been perving on Malfoy’s arse--”  
“要不是你一直盯着Malfoy的屁股看——”
“Shut up.” Remus was already in a bad mood, and much too sensitive to be teased by Peter Pettigrew, of all people.  
“闭嘴。”Remus已经心情不好了，而且太敏感了，不能被Peter Pettigrew这样的人取笑。
“Didn’t expect to see you,” Peter was saying, glancing at his pocket watch and tucking it back into his trouser pocket.  
“没想到会看到你，”Peter说着，瞥了一眼他的怀表，然后把它塞回裤子口袋。
He was wearing a tweed jacket and a stupid little bowler hat, mustard coloured. He looked like an off-brand leprechaun.  
他穿着一件花呢夹克和一顶愚蠢的小圆礼帽，芥末色的。他看起来像一个山寨版的精灵。
Remus scolded himself internally, ashamed of himself for being jealous of his friend - who despite only having scooped up a handful of NEWTs had managed to walk into an entry level position in the ministry, no bother.  
Remus在心里责备自己，为嫉妒朋友而感到羞愧——尽管他只考了几个NEWTs，但却顺利地进入了魔法部的初级职位，毫不费力。
“What do you mean?” Remus frowned, “I’m on time, aren’t I?”  
“你什么意思？”Remus皱眉，“我没迟到，对吧？”
“Didn’t you get Arthur’s message?” Peter looked up at him, innocently, “Got cancelled. They sent Caradoc
.”  
“你没收到Arthur的信息吗？”Peter天真地抬头看着他，“取消了。他们派了Caradoc。”
“Oh.” Remus pursed his lips.  
“哦。”Remus抿了抿嘴。
“So we can go home!” Peter said cheerily, “Thank Godric too, I’m exhausted. Work was mayhem today, I’m rushed off my feet.”  
“所以我们可以回家了！”Peter愉快地说，“谢谢Godric，我累坏了。今天工作一团糟，我忙得不可开交。”
“Right, of course.” Remus nodded, his shoulders slumping.  
“对，当然。”Remus点了点头，肩膀垂了下来。
He hadn’t got out of bed until midday. Then all he’d done was read the papers and smoke and eat half a loaf of bread - which Sirius had bought only the morning before. This had been his longest conversation with another human being all day.  
他直到中午才起床。然后他所做的一切就是看报纸、抽烟和吃了半条面包——那是Sirius前一天早上才买的。这是他一整天与另一个人类进行的最长对话。
“Are you sure they don’t need us?” He said, hopefully, “Maybe if we went along anyway--"  
“你确定他们不需要我们吗？”他充满希望地说，“也许我们还是去一趟——”
“Best not,” Peter shook his head, “You know what Moody’s like about protocol. Anyway, I’m starving, I barely had time for lunch.”  
“最好不要，”Peter摇了摇头，“你知道Moody对规程的态度。无论如何，我快饿死了，我几乎没有时间吃午饭。”
“Really? Want to go and get something at the Leaky Cauldron?”  
“真的？想去Leaky Cauldron吃点东西吗？”
“Sorry, promised mum I’d be home. She worries, you know.”  
“抱歉，答应了妈妈要回家。她会担心的，你知道。”
“Oh. Of course.”  
“哦。当然。”
“Padfoot is at your flat, isn’t he?”  
“Padfoot在你家吧？”
“Yeah, he should be back by now.”  
“是的，他现在应该已经回来了。”
“See you at the next meeting, Moony!”  
“下次会议见，Moony！”
“Yeah, see you.”  
“嗯，回头见。”
They walked off in opposite directions, Peter heading for the nearest floo grate (he still hadn’t learnt to apparate), Remus for the nearest quiet alley he could slink into and vanish in peace.  
他们朝相反的方向走去，Peter前往最近的Floo炉格（他还没有学会幻影移形），Remus则前往最近的安静小巷，以便可以安静地消失。
He tried to cheer up a bit as he stood outside the door to his flat. He shook himself, attempted to clear his mind, forced a smile. He opened the door.  
他站在公寓门外时试图振作起来。他抖了抖自己，试图清空脑袋，强迫自己微笑。他打开了门。
“You’re back early!” Sirius’s voice trilled from the kitchen, and that was enough to throw Remus back onto his dark mood. It felt like an accusation.  
“你回来得早啊！”Sirius的声音从厨房传来，这足以让Remus重新陷入阴郁的情绪中。这感觉像是在指责他。
“Mm.” He grunted, shutting the door and pulling off his cardigan, the hairs on his arms itching and prickling in the heat. It made his scars raised too, like barbed wire.  
“嗯。”他哼了一声，关上门，脱下羊毛衫，手臂上的汗毛在热气中发痒刺痛。这也使他的疤痕凸起，就像铁丝网一样。
“What's up?” Sirius appeared. He’d showered recently, his hair still gleamed. “Something happen?”  
“怎么了？”Sirius出现了。他最近刚洗过澡，头发还在闪闪发光。“发生了什么事吗？”
Remus snorted, kicking his shoes off and flinging them under the coffee table.  
Remus哼了一声，踢掉鞋子，把它们扔到咖啡桌下。
“Nothing happened. It got cancelled. Or someone else did it. Doesn't matter anyway, it was just busy-work.”  
“什么也没发生。任务取消了。或者是别人做了。反正没关系，只是些杂事。”
“No it wasn’t.” Sirius tutted. “Why would Dumbledore give you busy-work?”  
“不是这样的。”Sirius咂了咂舌。“Dumbledore为什么会给你安排杂事？”
“Because I can’t be trusted to do anything else but they still want to keep me on side so I don’t suddenly go evil.”  
“因为他们不能信任我做其他事情，但仍然想让我站在他们这边，所以我不会突然变坏。”
“Moony…” Sirius had his hands on his hips, now.  
“Moony……”Sirius现在双手叉腰。
Remus sighed and waved a hand.  
Remus叹了口气，挥了挥手。
“Forget about it. How was your day?”  
“算了吧。你今天怎么样？”
“It was… busy. Long.” Sirius said, carefully, obviously not wanting to provoke Remus any further. “The usual stuff, you know.”  
“嗯……忙。很长。”Sirius小心翼翼地说，显然不想再激怒Remus。“老样子，你知道的。”
“I don’t know.” Remus muttered. “You get to hang around with Aurors all day. The best I get is Wormtail.”  
“我不知道。”Remus嘟囔道。“你整天和傲罗混在一起。我最好的伙伴就是Wormtail。”
“Don’t be like that.” Sirius sat beside Remus on the couch, “You’re doing plenty of useful stuff, still. And they sent you on that mission at the beginning of the summer, that was huge!”  
“别这样。”Sirius坐在Remus旁边的沙发上，“你仍然在做很多有用的事情。他们在夏初派你去执行的那个任务，那可是个大事！”
Remus didn’t say anything. He hadn’t told Sirius what had happened, how he’d lost control yet again, and how Moody clearly didn’t trust him anymore, and Danny probably hated him.  
Remus什么也没说。他还没有告诉Sirius发生了什么，他又一次失控了，Moody显然不再信任他了，而Danny可能讨厌他。
In the pause that followed, Sirius tutted.  
在接下来的沉默中，Sirius咂了咂舌。
“Look, if you’re in a mood, I’d rather just get out of your way. I haven’t had a brilliant day either.”  
“听着，如果你心情不好，我宁愿让开。我今天也过得不太好。”
“Fine.” Remus said, sharply.  
“好吧。”Remus尖锐地说。
It wasn’t fine. Part of him wanted to grab Sirius for a kiss, pull him into the bedroom, and apologise for being a dick. The other part wanted a full blown fight, with lots of shouting and swearing. Either way, he didn’t want Sirius going anywhere.  
其实一点也不好。他的一部分想抓住Sirius亲吻，把他拉进卧室，为自己的混蛋行为道歉。另一部分想要大吵一架，充满喊叫和咒骂。不管怎样，他都不想让Sirius离开。
Sirius sighed and got up.  
Sirius叹了口气，站了起来。
“Fine then.” He grabbed his keys on the way out. “Going to work on the bike,” he said. “I’ll get bread on the way back, seeing as we’ve run out again.”  
“那好吧。”他在出去的路上抓起钥匙。“去修摩托车，”他说。“我回来时会买面包，因为我们又吃完了。”
Remus grunted in response, staring at a hole in his sock, rather than meet Sirius’s eye. They’d make it all up later, they always did.  
Remus哼了一声作为回应，盯着袜子上的一个洞，而不是看Sirius的眼睛。他们稍后会和好的，他们总是这样。

* * *
The problem with not being at Hogwarts was that Remus never had any idea where anyone was. He missed the Marauder’s Map sorely and felt anxious when he pictured Sirius, James, and Peter out in the world, facing who knew what.  
不在霍格沃茨的最大问题是Remus从不知道其他人在哪里。他非常想念淘气地图，当他想到Sirius、James和Peter在外面的世界里面对未知的危险时，他感到焦虑。
It typified the way he felt about almost everything now that school was over. At Hogwarts, he had been in control; he’d had a place, a certain status. In the real world, he was nothing and nobody; back to the bottom of the deck.  
这几乎是他对现在一切事物的感觉。在霍格沃茨时，他曾经掌控一切；他有一个位置，有一定的地位。在现实世界中，他一无所有，无名无分；回到了最底层。
As a mature and educated young man, he knew that he ought to face these new challenges with fortitude; set out to prove his worth, like James and Sirius—and even Pete. But Remus didn’t. He sulked.  
作为一个成熟且受过教育的年轻人，他知道自己应该勇敢面对这些新的挑战；像James和Sirius一样证明自己的价值——甚至像Pete那样。但Remus没有。他闷闷不乐。
After the cancelled mission with Peter, there had been another long and confusing meeting with the Order, and barely anyone had glanced in Remus’s direction. Moody hadn’t been there, nor Ferox, so Remus couldn’t even go and ask them whether there had been any developments on the Greyback front.  
在与Peter的任务取消后，Order又进行了一次漫长而混乱的会议，几乎没有人看Remus一眼。Moody和Ferox都不在，所以Remus甚至无法去问他们关于Greyback方面的进展。
It was nice to see the girls—Lily was apprenticing in the potions research department at St Mungo’s, and she and Marlene had made a whole gang of new friends at the hospital. Mary was at muggle secretarial college, and—like Remus—had been unimpressed with her assignments from the Order so far.  
见到女孩们倒是很高兴——Lily在圣芒戈的魔药研究部门当学徒，她和Marlene在医院结识了一大群新朋友。Mary在麻瓜秘书学院上学，而且——和Remus一样——对Order目前给她的任务不太满意。
“S’pose they don’t want my mucky blood blowing anyone’s cover,” she rolled her eyes. He snickered. Good old Mary.  
“我想他们不希望我的脏血暴露任何人的身份，”她翻了个白眼。他偷笑。老好的Mary。
Since that meeting, Remus had spent much of his time alone. He slept in, listened to the radio, went downstairs to the corner shop to buy fags, and pretended to read. He told Sirius he was researching defensive magic, but he couldn’t see the point in studying for no reason.  
自那次会议以来，Remus大部分时间都是独处的。他睡懒觉，听收音机，下楼去街角小店买烟，假装看书。他告诉Sirius他在研究防御魔法，但他看不出无缘无故学习的意义。
Remus was sprawled on the couch one day doing the crossword in a free paper he’d picked up somewhere. Well. He wasn’t so much ‘doing the crossword’ as trying to write the most imaginative swear words he could think of into the boxes. He was stuck on twelve down, ‘_ _ _ E _ _ _ _ F’, when the phone rang.  
一天，Remus摊在沙发上做他在某处捡到的免费报纸上的填字游戏。实际上，他不是在做填字游戏，而是尽可能在格子里写出他能想到的最具想象力的脏话。他在“十二格向下，‘_ _ _ E _ _ _ _ F’”处卡住了，这时电话响了。
It made him jump; the phone never rang.  
电话铃声让他吓了一跳；电话从未响过。
“H-hello?” he said, croakily, realising it was after one o’clock in the afternoon and the first time he’d spoken.  
“喂-喂？”他沙哑地说，意识到现在已经是下午一点多，这是他今天第一次说话。
“Wotcher sweetheart.”  
“你好，亲爱的。”
“Grant?”  
“Grant？”
“Someone else calling you sweetheart? You slag.”  
“还有别人叫你亲爱的吗？你这个荡妇。”
Remus laughed, grinning ear to ear.  
Remus笑了起来，笑得合不拢嘴。
“Sarky tosser. Where have you been?”  
“讽刺的混蛋。你去哪了？”
“Here and there. Sorry, I’ve had a bit of a busy summer… er… you’re at home, then?”  
“这里那里都有。抱歉，我夏天有点忙……呃……你在家，对吧？”
“Yeah.”  
“是的。”
“Brilliant, I’m five minutes away.”  
“太好了，我五分钟后到。”
“What?!”  
“什么？！”
“See you soon!” The line went dead.  
“很快见！”电话挂断了。
Not knowing what else to do, and mildly stunned, Remus went to the bathroom quickly to check himself in the mirror. He was wearing a creased t-shirt and threw on a jumper lying on the floor to cover up his scarred forearms. His hair never seemed to change, no matter what he did, so he ran his fingers through the curls and watched them spring back into place. He wished he’d showered when he woke up that morning, but it was too late now.  
不知道该做什么，有些惊愕的Remus赶紧去浴室照镜子。他穿着一件皱巴巴的T恤，捡起地板上的一件毛衣套上，以掩盖他布满伤疤的前臂。他的头发似乎从来没有变化，无论他做什么，于是他用手指梳理卷发，看着它们弹回原位。他希望早上醒来时洗了个澡，但现在已经太迟了。
There was a knock at the door and Remus hurried to answer it, pointing his wand at the kettle as he passed the kitchen door to flick it on. His pulse quickened, and he realised how excited he was to see someone not involved in the war.  
有人敲门，Remus赶紧去开门，经过厨房门口时用魔杖指着水壶打开了开关。他的脉搏加快了，他意识到自己有多么兴奋能见到一个与战争无关的人。
He wrenched the door open harder than he needed to, so that it nearly slammed into the wall.  
他用力打开门，比需要的力度还要大，以至于门几乎撞到墙上。
“Hiya,” Grant stood in the doorway, wide-eyed but grinning, his face round and sunny as it had been at fifteen, chipped tooth and bright clothes and everything else that was right in the world.  
“嗨，”Grant站在门口，瞪大眼睛但满面笑容，他的脸像十五岁时一样圆润而阳光，缺了一颗牙，穿着鲜亮的衣服，一切都很美好。
“Hi!” Remus breathed, standing back to allow Grant entry, “I’m so happy to see you!”  
“嗨！”Remus深吸一口气，退后让Grant进来，“见到你真高兴！”
“Blimey,” Grant nudged him with his trainer as he came inside, “If I’d known I’d get this sort of welcome I’d ‘ave shown up weeks ago.”  
“哎呀，”Grant进来时用运动鞋顶了顶他，“如果我早知道会有这样的欢迎，我几周前就来了。”
He stood in the middle of the living room, hands on his hips, staring around it in awe. He let out a low whistle, “Done alright for yourself ‘ere, eh? Very nice.”  
他站在客厅中央，双手叉腰，惊讶地四处张望。他低声吹了个口哨，“你这里过得不错啊？真不错。”
“Yeah, I s’pose,” Remus rubbed the back of his head. It was a bit messy, old newspapers and half-empty mugs of tea all over the place, not to mention the overflowing ashtrays. Suddenly he was very embarrassed.  
“是的，我想是的，”Remus挠了挠后脑勺。这里有点乱，到处都是旧报纸和半空的茶杯，更不用说满溢的烟灰缸了。突然，他感到非常尴尬。
“What you got a fireplace for?” Grant chuckled, “Thought these modern flats all had central heating?”  
“你要壁炉干嘛？”Grant笑道，“我以为这些现代公寓都有中央供暖？”
“Mm.” Remus mumbled, “Cup of tea?”
  
“嗯。”Remus咕哝道，“要杯茶吗？”
“Champion.”  
“当然。”
Remus went into the kitchen and used a bit of wordless magic to hurry it all along, before bringing the mugs through to the living room, where Grant stood inspecting the bookcase. He looked so well. His clothes were clean and smart—he was even wearing a dress shirt, which had a wide floral collar and cuffs.  
Remus进了厨房，用无声魔法加快了进度，然后端着茶杯回到客厅，Grant正站在那里检查书架。他看起来很好。他的衣服干净而得体——他甚至穿着一件衬衫，带有宽大的花领和袖口。
Remus gave him his tea and did a bit of quick tidying before sitting down.  
Remus把茶递给他，稍微整理了一下，然后坐下。
“I can’t believe you’re here.” He said. Grant laughed,
“Me neither, to be honest. Been a long time, eh?”
“How was your holiday?”
“Oh, er…” Grant appeared to be blushing. His ears turned cherry red. “That was a bit of a fib… I just didn’t want to jinx anything.”
“Jinx what? What have you been doing?”
“I um. Look, don’t laugh at me, all right? I’ve been doing evening classes. You know, get my O-Levels.” He looked down.
“That’s brilliant!” Remus said. Grant looked up at him cautiously, as if waiting for the punchline.
“Better late than never, I s’pose. I had my CSE Maths exam today, over in Russell Square. Bloody difficult, but I reckon I did enough to pass. Fucking Pythagoras was a right tosser, eh?”  
「迟到总比不到好。我今天在拉塞尔广场考了CSE数学考试。真他妈难，但我觉得我应该能及格。该死的毕达哥拉斯真是个混蛋，对吧？」
Remus laughed.  
雷穆斯笑了。
“Well done, though! What brought that on?”  
“做得好！是什么促使你这样做的？”
“Want to work somewhere other than a pub, one day.” Grant shrugged, “Shagging all them students opened my eyes a bit. Don’t want to be a thicko all my life.”  
“想要有一天能在酒吧之外的地方工作。”格兰特耸耸肩，“跟那些学生上床让我开了眼。我不想一辈子当个傻子。”
“You are not thick.” Remus said, firmly, giving him a stern look.  
“你不是傻子。”雷穆斯坚定地说，给了他一个严厉的眼神。
“Well, we’ll see,” Grant waved a hand, shy again. “If I get my Maths and my English sorted - and I reckon I did ok on English too - you ought to see my spelling, it’s miles better - then I’m ‘oping I can start A-Levels in January. I wanna do psychology, I think.”  
“嗯，我们拭目以待，”格兰特挥了挥手，再次显得害羞。“如果我把数学和英语搞定了——我觉得我英语也做得不错——你得看看我的拼写，进步大了——那么我希望能在一月开始A-Level课程。我想学心理学，我觉得。”
“Psychology.” Remus said, in awe.  
“心理学。”雷穆斯惊叹道。
“Yeah,” Grant chuckled, “Ricky - that’s one of the students I was seeing - ‘e reckoned I better do Politics, but to be honest I’ve had it up to ‘ere with Trotsky. ‘E was a communist.”  
“是啊，”格兰特笑道，“里基——那是我见的一个学生——他说我最好学政治，但说实话，我对托洛茨基已经受够了。他是个共产主义者。”
“Trotsky?”  
“托洛茨基？”
“Ricky.”  
“里基。”
“Right.” Remus sipped his tea, thoughtfully. Everyone was doing things. Everyone had a direction. And here he was, just sitting by and watching, as per usual. Self-hatred rose inside him.  
“对。”雷穆斯若有所思地啜饮着茶。每个人都在做事情。每个人都有方向。而他，只是在一旁坐着观看，一如既往。自我厌恶在他心中涌起。
“So… how’s Sirius?” Grant asked, politely.  
“那么……天狼星怎么样？”格兰特礼貌地问。
“Yeah, good. He’s out just now. Um... Uni lecture.”  
“嗯，还不错。他现在出去了。嗯……上大学讲座。”
“Nice. And… your mum? How’s she?”  
“很好。那……你妈妈呢？她怎么样了？”
“Dying.” Remus grunted.  
“快死了。”雷穆斯哼了一声。
“Bummer.”  
“真是糟糕。”
Remus practically spat his tea out, laughing. Grant grinned.  
雷穆斯差点把茶喷出来了，笑了起来。格兰特咧嘴笑了。
“Oi, did ya hear about St Eddy’s?”  
“喂，你听说过圣埃迪学校吗？”
“What about it?” Remus frowned.  
“怎么了？”雷穆斯皱了皱眉。
“Shut down. Last Approved School in Britain, apparently - they’re all ‘Community Homes’ now.”  
“关停了。显然是英国最后一所经批准的学校——现在它们都变成‘社区之家’了。”
“What happened to all the boys?”  
“那些男孩都去哪了？”
“Some of them sent to Borstal. The rest got re-housed. They’re knocking it down, putting up flats instead.”  
“有些被送去了Borstal（青少年拘留所）。剩下的被重新安置了。他们正在拆除那栋楼，改建成公寓。”
“Good riddance.” Remus said, darkly.  
“再见也好。”雷穆斯阴沉地说。
“I’ll drink to that,” Grant snorted, raising his mug of tea. They chatted for a bit longer, reminiscing. Grant wasn’t seeing anyone serious, and didn’t know how much longer he’d be in Brighton. He missed London, but he knew he needed to save up more money if he wanted to move back and make a proper go of it. He was so different from the last time Remus had seen him.  
“为此干杯，”格兰特哼了一声，举起他的茶杯。他们聊了一会儿，回忆往事。格兰特没有稳定的恋人，也不知道自己在布莱顿会待多久。他想念伦敦，但知道自己需要存更多的钱才行，如果想要搬回去好好过日子。他和雷穆斯上次见面时大相径庭。
“‘Nuff about me, what about you? You at uni too?”  
“说够了我，那你呢？你也在上大学吗？”
“I’m not really doing anything.” Remus sighed. “It’s hard to get a job right now. I’ve mostly just been here.”  
“我其实没做什么。”雷穆斯叹了口气。“现在很难找工作。我主要就待在这里。”
“Lucky you’ve got this set up, eh?” Grant gestured around, picking up the cigarette box on the coffee table and shaking it. Remus nodded, and took one himself too.  
“你有这样的安排真好，”格兰特指了指四周，拿起咖啡桌上的香烟盒摇了摇。雷穆斯点了点头，也拿了一支。
“Yeah, lucky.” He said, glumly, as he lit it.  
“是啊，运气好。”他点燃香烟时说道，神情黯淡。
“You need to get out more, sweetheart.” Grant said, sounding serious.  
“你需要多出去走走，亲爱的。”格兰特认真地说。
“What?”  
“什么？”
Grant tutted, blowing smoke and looking Remus up and down.  
格兰特咂了咂嘴，吹着烟，打量着雷穆斯。
“Look at you, you miserable git. I’m not blind, y’know. Cooped up in here feeling sorry for yourself, is it?”  
“看看你，真是个痛苦的家伙。我又不是瞎子。就是窝在这里自怨自艾吗？”
“No, I--”  
“不，我——”
“Remus,” Grant sighed, shaking his head, “I’m not being ‘orrible, I’m just saying. Remember when I left St Edmund’s, and I lived in that squat?”  
“雷穆斯，”格兰特叹了口气，摇摇头，“我不是在刻薄，只是说说罢了。记得我离开圣埃德蒙学校时，住在那间废弃的房子里吗？”
“Yeah…?” Remus wished he could forget that, but it was burned in his memory. The dirty mattresses, the bare floorboards, the damp.  
“是啊……”雷穆斯希望自己能忘记，但那一幕深深地刻在了记忆里。脏兮兮的床垫，裸露的地板，还有潮湿。
“I thought it was great at first - no more school, no more matron telling me what to do, just me looking out for myself.” He shook his head, pursing his lips, “I liked running away. I done it all the time, when I was a kid. Run away from me mum, from me grandad - the prick - from anywhere people tried to keep me in. And the thing is, they always let me. Matron never called the police, mum never tried to find me. Actually, you were the only person who ever tried to track me down.”  
“最开始我觉得那很好——没有学校了，没有保姆告诉我该做什么，只有我自己照顾自己。”他摇了摇头，抿了抿嘴，“我喜欢逃跑。我从小就一直这样做。逃离我妈，逃离我那个混蛋爷爷——逃离任何想要把我困住的地方。最奇怪的是，他们总是放我走。保姆从没报警，我妈也从没试图找我。其实，你是唯一一个试图追踪我的人。”
“I…” Remus hadn’t known that.  
“我……”雷穆斯对此并不知情。
“I dunno how you did it,” Grant chuckled, scratching his chin, “Maybe you’ve got a magic wand or summink. But you found me. Twice. Thought about that a lot, over the past
 year.”  
“我不知道你是怎么做到的，”格兰特笑道，摸了摸下巴，“也许你有魔法棒什么的。但你找到了我。两次。过去一年里，我想了很多这事。”
“I just wanted to make sure you were ok.”  
“我只是想确保你没事。”
“I know ya did,” Grant smiled, softly, “That’s what amazed me. Here’s this lad - this clever, funny, posho lad - who gives a shit about me, when no one else ever did. Made me feel like someone worthwhile. So I thought I’d better do something worthwhile.”  
“我知道你这么做了，”格兰特柔和地笑道，“这就是让我惊讶的地方。这个小子——聪明、有趣、又高贵的小子——关心我，而其他人从未在意过。这让我觉得自己有价值。所以我觉得我最好也做点有价值的事。”
Remus didn’t know what to say. He put his tea down.  
雷穆斯不知道该说什么。他放下了茶杯。
“That’s why I wanted to wait ‘til my exams were all done before I saw ya,” Grant continued, “Even if I fail the lot, I wanted to tell you I’d done it, I’m trying to be better.”  
“这就是为什么我想等到考试都结束后再来看你，”格兰特继续说道，“即使我全都考砸了，我也想告诉你我已经做到了，我在努力变得更好。”
“You never needed to prove anything to me,” Remus said, earnestly.  
“你从来不需要向我证明什么，”雷穆斯认真地说。
“I know,” Grant nodded, “I did it for me, really. I did it because running away and avoiding all the stuff that made me feel like shit was pointless in the end. If you want people to think you’re worth it, you’ve got to start acting like you want it.”  
“我知道，”格兰特点了点头，“其实我做这些是为了我自己。我这么做是因为逃避和避免那些让我觉得自己很糟糕的东西最终是没用的。如果你想让人们觉得你值得，就得开始表现出你想要它的样子。”
Remus laughed humourlessly,  
雷穆斯无奈地笑了，
“Sounds like you’re already taking psychology.”  
“听起来你已经在学心理学了。”
“Been reading lots,” Grant winked, “You get what I’m telling you, then?”  
“读了很多书，”格兰特眨了眨眼，“你明白我在告诉你什么了吗？”
“Yes.” Remus sighed. Do something worthwhile. Stop moping.  
“明白了。”雷穆斯叹了口气。做些有价值的事。别再抱怨了。
“Good.” Grant said, brightly, “Cos if you’re not happy here, I’ll switch wiv ya. Nice flat, lots of books, gorgeous boyfriend…”  
“很好。”格兰特明亮地说，“因为如果你不开心，我可以和你交换。漂亮的公寓，大量的书籍，还有迷人的男朋友……”
Remus laughed again, and kicked Grant’s shin playfully,  
雷穆斯再次笑了，调皮地踢了踢格兰特的小腿，
“Shut up.”  
“闭嘴。”
“Never. Anyway, best be off, I’ve got a train to catch - I’ll be popping back in a month or so, though, s’long as I get the results I need.”  
“绝不。好了，我该走了，我还有火车要赶——不过我会在一个月左右再回来，只要我能拿到我需要的成绩。”
“You will.” Remus said confidently, “I know you will.”  
“你会的。”雷穆斯自信地说，“我知道你会的。”
“Cheers. Give me a ring soon, eh?”  
“谢谢。尽快打个电话给我，好吗？”
They hugged at the door, and Remus watched him go, hopping down the steps two at a time, whistling a pop tune.  
他们在门口拥抱，雷穆斯看着他走下台阶，一次跳下两个台阶，吹着流行歌曲的口哨。
Remus felt lighter; his cheeks ached from smiling. He closed the door and looked at the messy room. He felt like doing the washing up. Then he might nip to the shops and get something in for dinner. Sirius had been out all day; he’d like coming home to a proper meal.  
雷穆斯感到心情轻松了许多；他的脸颊因笑而酸痛。他关上门，看着那间凌乱的房间。他想洗碗。然后他可能会去商店买点东西做晚餐。天狼星整天都在外面；他会喜欢回家时能吃到一顿正经的饭。
Tomorrow, Remus could make a proper start on everything else. There was so much to do.  
明天，雷穆斯可以正式开始做其他所有事情。还有很多事要做。

 

 

 

 

Notes:Song is 'A message to you Rudy' by The Specials

So much Brit-speak in this - not to mention 1970s specific stuff:

- Trainers - sneakers/tennis shoes
- Cornershop - a convenience store, usually on the corner of a block.
- GCE O-Levels - The standard school qualification in Britain before 1988. Taken at age 16, you needed this qualification to move onto further education. Grant left school at fifteen and never sat his exams.
- A-Level - 'Advanced level' educational certificate, typically taken between the age of 16 - 18, before university.
- Approved School - basically what St. Edmund's was. A residential institution to which young people could be sent by a court, usually for committing offences but sometimes because they were deemed to be beyond parental control.
- Borstal - Youth prison. (They're now called 'young offenders' institutions'.)

 

Chapter 155: The War: Winter 1978-1979Rows and flows of angel hair

And ice cream castles in the air

And feather canyons everywhere

I've looked at clouds that way

 

But now they only block the sun

They rain and snow on everyone

So many things I would have done

But clouds got in my way

 

Saturday 23rd December 1978

He fumbled on the bedside for his glass of water, and found it empty. “Aguamenti,” he rasped, his wand hand shaking.  

他在床头摸索他的水杯，却发现杯子是空的。“水源，显现！”他喃喃地说，手中的魔杖抖动着。

 

The glass filled with water, and he gulped it down greedily. He rolled onto his back, pressing the heels of his hands into his eyes, hoping to mitigate the headache threatening to start gnawing on his brain. He turned his head slightly and addressed the lump under the duvet,  

杯子里充满了水，他贪婪地喝了下去。他翻身仰卧，手掌的跟部压在眼睛上，希望缓解即将侵蚀他大脑的头痛。他稍微转动头，问道被子下的那团人影，“你醒了吗？”

 

There was a sort of a shudder and a grunt. Remus tutted. It was too hot in the bedroom, even for December. He got up and went to the window to crack it open. He pressed his forehead against the cold glass and let the cold air wash over his hot skin.  

有一种颤抖和呻吟声。雷穆斯咂了咂嘴。即使是在十二月，卧室里也太热了。他起身走到窗边，打开了窗户。他把额头贴在冰冷的玻璃上，让寒冷的空气拂过炙热的皮肤。

 

They’d been out at the Leaky Cauldron the night before - pre-Christmas drinks. The marauders and Lily would be spending Christmas itself at the Potters, but everyone who was working had finished for the year, and Mary had suggested blowing off some steam away from the older members of the Order of the Phoenix, for once.  

他们前一晚在破釜酒吧呆过——圣诞前的饮酒聚会。麻瓜们和莉莉会在圣诞节当天去波特家，但所有工作的人都已经完成了年度工作，玛丽提议这次远离凤凰社的老成员们，好好放松一下。

 

As with most of Mary’s ideas, it was brilliant fun. Marlene came, and brought Yaz, who was visiting the McKinnons because her family didn’t do Christmas anyway. Frank and Alice popped by to say hello, and Sirius and James insisted on getting in every other round.  

像玛丽的大多数主意一样，这次聚会非常有趣。玛琳来了，还带了雅兹，雅兹正在拜访麦金农家，因为她的家人不庆祝圣诞节。弗兰克和爱丽丝来打了个招呼，天狼星和詹姆斯坚持轮流买酒。

 

After last orders, those still standing had piled into a taxi back to Remus and Sirius’s flat, where they may not have had any milk or bread in, but the bar was always fully stocked.  

最后点单后，那些还站着的人挤进了出租车，回到了雷穆斯和天狼星的公寓。虽然他们可能没有牛奶或面包，但酒吧总是备货充足。

 

Everything had been a bit of a blur, after that. Remus had a horrible feeling that he and Lily had started singing muggle Christmas Carols at some point.  

之后的一切都有些模糊。雷穆斯有一种可怕的感觉，他和莉莉在某个时刻开始唱起了麻瓜圣诞颂歌。

 

He groaned loudly, “Why did you let me drink so much?!”  

他大声抱怨道：“你们为什么让我喝这么多？！”

 

“Oi, don’t blame me!” Lily suddenly appeared, her fluffy red hair sticking up like a dandelion as she emerged from under the duvet.  

“喂，别怪我！”莉莉突然出现了，她那蓬松的红发像蒲公英一样竖起，从被子下露出来。

 

Remus jumped, whirling around. He wrapped his arms protectively around himself,  

雷穆斯吓了一跳，猛地转过身来。他保护性地把手臂环绕在自己身上，

 

“Fucking hell, Evans, what are you doing here?!”  

“天呐，埃文斯，你在这里干什么？！”

 

“Couldn’t get James to leave,” she yawned, “And I wasn’t going to sleep on the couch, they started building a fort.”  

“让詹姆斯离开不了，”她打了个哈欠，“我可不想睡在沙发上，他们开始建堡垒了。”

 

“This is the second time you’ve shown up in my bedroom unannounced, Evans, people will talk.” Remus searched for a t-shirt.  

“这是你第二次未经允许出现在我的卧室里了，埃文斯，人们会说闲话的。”雷穆斯找着一件T恤。

“I do,” she looked at him, puzzled, blinking through tears, “You and Siân.”
“我有，”她看着他，困惑地眨着泪眼，“你和西安。”

“Oh.” He felt dreadful. All this time he’d thought he was one of Hope’s terrible secrets.
“哦。”他感到非常糟糕。一直以来，他以为自己是霍普的可怕秘密之一。

“I’ve never been ashamed.” She said, a note of defiance entering her voice. “Not of my lovely boy. Never.”
“我从未感到羞愧。”她说，声音里带着一丝反抗。“不对我的可爱儿子。绝不。”

“Mum…” he felt as though he’d been punched in the gut. He was crying too, all of a sudden, and he squeezed her hand desperately.
“妈妈……”他感觉自己像是被打了一拳。他突然也开始哭泣，绝望地握住她的手。

“Come here,” she reached out for him, and he got up to sit carefully on the edge of the bed, leaning over so that she could wrap her arms around him. He rested his head on her shoulder, trying not to put too much weight on her frail body, but she was stronger than he gave her credit for, and held him tightly.
“过来，”她伸手向他，他小心翼翼地坐在床边，俯身让她能拥抱他。他将头靠在她的肩膀上，尽量不把太多重量压在她脆弱的身体上，但她比他想象的要坚强，紧紧抱着他。

“I’m sorry, mum,” he said, his words muffled by her soft nightgown. She smelled of talcum powder and lavender, and family. She stroked his hair,
“对不起，妈妈，”他说，声音被她柔软的睡衣所遮挡。她身上散发着爽身粉和薰衣草的味道，还有家的气息。她抚摸着他的头发，

 “You’ve nothing to be sorry for, sweetheart. I love you.”

“I love you too,” he wept.

 

I've looked at clouds from both sides now

From up and down, and still somehow

It's cloud illusions I recall

I really don't know clouds at all

 

* * *

 

Moons and Junes and Ferris wheels

The dizzy dancing way you feel

As every fairy tale comes real

I've looked at love that way

 

But now it's just another show

You leave 'em laughing when you go

And if you care, don't let them know

Don't give yourself away

 

He stayed at the Hospice for longer than usual, and by the time he had apparated to the Potter’s front gate, he was exhausted. He felt like laundry that had been wrung out and splayed on a clothesline, weak and bare and empty.  

他在临终关怀中心待得比平时久，直到他瞬移到波特家的前门时，已经疲惫不堪。他感觉自己就像是被拧干、挂在晾衣绳上的衣物，虚弱、裸露、空荡荡的。

 

James had to question him at the door - it was second nature now.  

詹姆斯在门口问了他几个问题——这现在已经成为第二天性。

 

“Which film did we see in the summer of 1974?”  

“我们在1974年夏天看了哪部电影？”

 

“The Great Gatsby.” He replied, grimly.  

“《了不起的盖茨比》。”他阴沉地回答。

 

James saw the look on his face and stepped aside at once.  

詹姆斯看到他脸上的神情，立刻让开了。

 

“All right, Moony?” he asked, putting a hand on Remus’s shoulder.  

“怎么了，月亮？”他问，拍了拍雷穆斯的肩膀。

 

“Yeah,” Remus nodded, hoping he just looked tired, “I don’t want to be rude, but would it be all right if I just went to bed? Um. Tell your parents I’m really sorry, I’m just…”  

“嗯，”雷穆斯点了点头，希望自己看起来只是累了，“我不想不礼貌，但我能直接去睡觉吗？嗯，告诉你父母我真的很抱歉，我只是……”

 

“Yeah, of course, mate!” James said eagerly, “You go up, I’ll tell ‘em you’re knackered.”  

“当然，伙计！”詹姆斯热切地说，“你上去吧，我会告诉他们你累坏了。”

 

“Thank you.” Remus smiled. He climbed the familiar stairs to bed. He really hoped Mrs Potter wouldn’t mind - he’d be fine in the morning, but just now he wasn’t sure if his nerves could handle seeing her. She always hugged him, too, and being hugged by one mother today was about as much as he could take.  

“谢谢。”雷穆斯笑了。他爬上了熟悉的楼梯去上床。他真的希望波特夫人不会介意——他明天会没事的，但现在他不确定自己的神经能否承受见到她。她总是拥抱他，今天被一个母亲拥抱已经是他能接受的极限了。

 

Of course, it wasn’t long before Sirius poked his head around the bedroom door.  

当然，不久之后，西里斯就把头探进了卧室门口。

 

“I’ll leave you be, if you want,” he said, carrying in a tray loaded with cheese, pickle, ham, crackers and of course Mrs Potter’s famous mince pies. “I just thought you might be peckish?”  

“如果你想的话，我可以离开，”他说，端着一个装满奶酪、腌菜、火腿、饼干，当然还有波特夫人著名的肉馅饼的托盘。“我只是觉得你可能会有点饿？”

 

“I’m starving,” Remus grinned at him, “Thank you.”  

“我饿得要死了，”雷穆斯对他笑了笑，“谢谢。”

 

Looking very pleased with himself, Sirius crossed the room more confidently, and set the tray down on the bed between them. They sat quietly for a while, cross-legged on the duvet cover, Remus eating, Sirius pretending not to watch him. When he was finished, Sirius took the tray away, and Remus lay down, stretching out his aching limbs.  

西里斯看起来很自得，他更自信地穿过房间，把托盘放在他们之间的床上。他们静静地坐了一会儿，盘腿坐在被子上，雷穆斯在吃东西，西里斯假装不看他。雷穆斯吃完后，西里斯拿走了托盘，雷穆斯躺下，伸展着酸痛的四肢。

 

“Shall I go?” Sirius asked.  

“我走吗？”西里斯问。

 

“No.” Remus said. “Just… don’t expect too much, ok?”  

“不要。”雷穆斯说。“只是……不要期待太多，好吗？”

 

“Ok.” He lay down next to Remus, on his back.  

“好的。”他躺在雷穆斯旁边，仰面朝上。

 

“How’s the hangover?” Remus asked, remembering the state they’d all been in that morning.  

“宿醉怎么样？”雷穆斯问，记起他们那天早晨的状态。

 

“Fine,” Sirius snorted, “Evans and her potions.”  

“还好，”西里斯哼了一声，“埃文斯和她的药水。”

 

“Great.”  

“太好了。”

 

Remus closed his eyes, letting the events of the day settle in his mind. It was good to have Sirius there, he decided. Being alone might be really awful. If only there was a way to express that without having it come out wrong.  

雷穆斯闭上了眼睛，让一天的事情在脑海中沉淀。他决定有西里斯在身边是好的。独处可能真的很糟糕。如果有办法表达这种感觉而不会弄巧成拙就好了。

 

“I’ve got a sister.” He said, finally. “She’s eight.”  

“我有一个妹妹。”他说，终于说道。“她八岁。”

 

“Wow.”  

“哇。”

 

“Mm.” He reached for Sirius’s hand and held it. “It took her months to tell me. God knows what else I don’t know. I wish we had more time together.”  

“嗯。”他伸手握住西里斯的手。“她花了几个月才告诉我。天知道我还不知道什么。我希望我们能有更多的时间在一起。”

 

Sirius squeezed his hand sympathetically. Remus licked his lips, steeling himself for the next bit. “I wish we had more time, but I also… I also wish she would be more open. It really hurts, knowing that there are parts of her she keeps private.”  

西里斯同情地握紧了他的手。雷穆斯舔了舔嘴唇，鼓起勇气说出接下来的话。“我希望我们能有更多的时间，但我也……我也希望她能更开放。知道她有些部分对我保密真的很痛苦。”

 

“Oh?” Sirius was doing an excellent job of keeping his cool. If Remus hadn’t been so sad it would be comical.  

“哦？”西里斯做得很好，保持了冷静。如果雷穆斯没有那么伤心，这会很滑稽。

 

“Yeah.” He said. He turned to look at Sirius. Sirius turned to look back at him. “So I’m sorry,” Remus said, nervously, “If I ever make you feel that way.”  

“是的。”他说。他转过身看向西里斯。西里斯转过身来回看着他。“所以我很抱歉，”雷穆斯紧张地说，“如果我让你有那种感觉。”

 

“Moony--”  

“月亮——”

 

“--It’s just that I get worried,” Remus said quickly, “That you won’t… if you knew some things…”  

“——只是我有点担心，”雷穆斯迅速说，“如果你知道一些事情，你会……”

 

“There’s nothing you could tell me that would change how I feel.” Sirius said.  

“没有什么你能告诉我的，会改变我的感受。”西里斯说。

 

Remus was speechless at that. But it was a good feeling. A happy feeling, even considering the circumstances. He couldn’t look at Sirius any more so he rolled onto his side. Luckily, Sirius seemed to understand and followed suit, draping an arm across Remus’s body. Remus breathed in slowly.  

雷穆斯听到这话无言以对。但这是一种好的感觉。即使考虑到情况，这也是一种快乐的感觉。他不能再看西里斯了，于是他侧身躺下。幸运的是，西里斯似乎理解了，也跟着躺下，把手臂搭在雷穆斯的身体上。雷穆斯缓缓呼吸。

 

“That mission I did, back in the summer? It went really badly.” He said, feeling the weight already lifting.  

“我在夏天做的那个任务？情况很糟糕。”他说，感觉负担已经减轻。

 

“I thought something had happened.” Sirius said. “Go on.”  

“我以为发生了什么事。”西里斯说。“继续说。”

 

“I… do you remember how I got, the last time there were werewolves nearby? Like… really pushy and sort of not thinking? That happened again. No one got hurt, but I’m pretty sure Danny thinks I’m dangerously mad now.”  

“我……你还记得上次有狼人出现时我是什么状态吗？就像……非常急躁、缺乏思考？这次又发生了。没有人受伤，但

 

我很确定丹尼现在认为我非常疯狂。”

 

“It didn’t happen to him?”  

“没有发生在他身上吗？”

 

“I think he must have felt it. But we reacted differently. I sort of - took charge. Not on purpose, it just felt natural at the time.”  

“我想他一定感受到了。但我们反应不同。我有点——掌控了局面。不是故意的，只是当时感觉很自然。”

 

“That makes sense,” Sirius said, “That's what you do on full moons, we have to let you be the leader.”  

“这很有道理，”西里斯说，“那是你在满月时的做法，我们得让你做领导者。”

 

“Yeah, I hadn’t thought of it like that.”  

“是的，我没这么想过。”

 

“So… if no one got hurt, what happened?”  

“所以……如果没有人受伤，那发生了什么？”

 

“One of the werewolves tried to attack me, but I overpowered him.” Remus said, “I was supposed to get information, but all I did was rile them up.”  

“一个狼人试图攻击我，但我制服了他。”雷穆斯说，“我本应该获得信息，但我做的只是激怒他们。”

 

“What did Moody say about it?”  

“穆迪对此说了什么？”

 

“He was… cryptic. I don’t think he was angry. He asked me if I minded going alone next time - without Danny. But he hasn’t sent me on any other missions, not proper ones, and it’s been months…”  

“他……含糊其辞。我觉得他没有生气。他问我下次是否介意单独去——没有丹尼。但他没有派我去做其他任务，没有正式的任务，已经好几个月了……”

 

“They have to be saving you for something.” Sirius said, “I know they have to be - James keeps telling Frank and Alice how good you are at defensive magic, and they just say they can’t do anything without an order from someone above them.”  

“他们一定是在为某个任务留着你。”西里斯说，“我知道他们一定是这样——詹姆斯一直告诉弗兰克和爱丽丝你在防御魔法方面很出色，他们只是说没有上级的命令他们什么也做不了。”

 

“Maybe.” Remus sighed.  

“也许吧。”雷穆斯叹了口气。

 

“Did he really say you had to go alone next time?”  

“他真的说下次你必须一个人去吗？”

 

“He didn’t say I had to… just asked if I minded. And I don’t think there’s any other way - Danny won’t work with me again, he was too scared. So I suppose… yeah, it’ll be just me next time.”  

“他没有说我必须……只是问我是否介意。而且我觉得没有其他办法——丹尼不会再和我合作了，他太害怕了。所以我想……是的，下次就只有我一个人了。”

 

Sirius’s arms tightened around Remus.  

西里斯的手臂紧紧地环绕着雷穆斯。

 

“I hate that.”  

“我讨厌这样。”

 

Remus didn’t have a response, and Sirius didn’t seem to be looking for one, so they just lay like that quietly for a while, until Remus fell asleep.  

 

雷穆斯没有回应，西里斯也似乎没有期待回应，所以他们就这样安静地躺了一会儿，直到雷穆斯入睡。

* * *

Boxing Day 1978

 

As Lily had predicted, Christmas Day 1978 was a welcome break from everyone’s troubles. In fact - perhaps because it had been a particularly difficult year - Remus always remembered that Christmas as one of the most pleasant and happy they had together.  

正如莉莉所预测的那样，1978年的圣诞节成为了大家烦恼中的一片清新。事实上——也许是因为这一年特别艰难——雷穆斯总是记得那个圣诞节是他们一起度过的最愉快和幸福的时光之一。

 

Mr and Mrs Potter were slowing down a bit - Euphemia said she wasn’t up to hosting a big party as she usually did, and anyway, the Ministry had warned against large social gatherings. Mr Potter had to be locked out of his study - James and Sirius stole the key - but he saw the funny side, and joined in with the festivities whole-heartedly.  

波特先生和波特夫妇有些放慢了脚步——尤菲米亚说她没法像往常一样举办大派对了，而且，魔法部也警告说要避免大型社交聚会。波特先生不得不被锁在书房外——詹姆斯和西里斯偷走了钥匙——但他看到了幽默的一面， wholehearted地参与了庆祝活动。

 

Remus noticed that this year it was really James and Lily who were the hosts. She co-ordinated most of the cooking, the decorating, the card writing; while he made sure that everyone always had a drink, that all of the usual Christmas games were played, and that the house was full of joy at all times.  

雷穆斯注意到，今年真正的东道主是詹姆斯和莉莉。她协调了大部分的烹饪、装饰和贺卡书写，而他则确保每个人都有饮料，所有惯常的圣诞游戏都进行，房子里始终充满欢乐。

 

As for presents, it was all of the usual fare - sweets and nuts and candied fruit, new socks and underwear, a pair of pyjamas from Lily as a joke (“so I stop catching you in your knickers!”), and a shiny new pair of doc martens from Sirius.  

至于礼物，都是一些常见的东西——糖果、坚果、蜜饯、新袜子和内裤，一套莉莉开的玩笑的睡衣（“这样我就不会再抓到你穿着内裤了！”），以及一双西里斯送的闪亮的新军靴。

 

Surprisingly, Remus also received a gift from Grant that year, and felt guilty for not getting him one in return. He laughed when he opened it - a filofax organiser. Grant had written his own address and phone number in the first page, and in the back where the notes had written the heading: “New Year's Resolutions: 1. Stop and smell the roses.”  

出乎意料的是，雷穆斯那年也收到了格兰特的礼物，并为没有回赠礼物而感到内疚。他在打开礼物时笑了——一个文件夹组织器。格兰特在第一页上写了自己的地址和电话号码，在背面写着标题：“新年决心：1. 停下来闻闻玫瑰花。”

 

Christmas Day over and done with, James and Lily were heading to the Evans’s for Boxing Day (James was absolutely dreading it, having met Lily’s sister twice already, and failed to impress her either time.) So Sirius and Remus went back to their own home to settle in and get ready for the New Year. Sirius rather liked the idea of hosting his own party, and Remus was prepared to give in, as long as they only invited people they knew.  

圣诞节结束后，詹姆斯和莉莉正前往埃文斯家过节（詹姆斯非常害怕，已经见过莉莉的姐姐两次，但每次都没能给她留下好印象）。所以西里斯和雷穆斯回到自己的家，准备安顿下来，迎接新年。西里斯非常喜欢举办自己的派对的主意，而雷穆斯准备妥协，只要他们邀请的都是他们认识的人。

 

“How many do you reckon we can fit in this flat anyway?” Remus asked as they opened the door. “It’s not like we’ve got a ballroom, there’s only one sofa!”  

“你觉得我们这公寓能容纳多少人？”雷穆斯一边开门一边问。“不像我们有舞厅，只有一个沙发！”

 

“We ought to knock through the kitchen, have it all open plan,” Sirius replied, as they walked in. The phone was ringing, and he went to answer it. “Hello?” He frowned, then held out the phone to Remus, “For you, I think?”  

“我们应该打通厨房，把它改成开放式的，”西里斯回答道。他们走进来时，电话响了，他去接听。“你好？”他皱起了眉头，然后把电话递给雷穆斯，“我想是给你的。”

 

Remus took the receiver from him. Of course it was for him - Sirius didn’t know anyone who could use a telephone.  

雷穆斯接过电话。的确是给他的——西里斯不认识任何会用电话的人。

 

“Hello?”  

“你好？”

 

“Hullo? Is that Remus Lupin?” It was a man with a deep voice and a broad Welsh accent. Remus’s insides went cold, and he sat down on the arm of the couch, steadying himself.  

“你好？是雷穆斯·卢平吗？”是一个声音深沉、带有浓厚威尔士口音的男人。雷穆斯的内心突然冰冷，他坐在沙发扶手上，稳住自己。

 

“Yes, that’s right…”  

“是的，没错……”

 

“Ah, good. Ah. My name’s Gethin Rees.”  

“啊，好。啊，我叫盖思温·里斯。”

 

Remus swallowed, and found his throat dry.  

雷穆斯吞了吞口水，发现喉咙干涩。

 

“Is she... She’s gone, isn’t she?”  

“她……她走了吗？”

 

There was a long quiet on the other end of the phone, and Remus began to cry. Finally, Gethin spoke, his own voice sounding very rough.  

电话那头沉默了很久，雷穆斯开始哭泣。终于，盖思温开口了，他的声音听起来非常粗糙。

 

“I’m sorry, lad. Funeral’s next Wednesday.”  

 

“对不起，小伙子。葬礼在下周三。”

 

I've looked at love from both sides now

From give and take, and still somehow

It's love's illusions I recall

I really don't know love at all

* * *

Tears and fears and feeling proud

To say "I love you" right out loud

Dreams and schemes and circus crowds

I've looked at life that way

 

But now old friends are acting strange

They shake their heads, they say I've changed

Well something's lost, but something's gained

In living every day.

 

Wednesday 3rd January 1979

Remus sighed, staring out of their bedroom window watching the raindrops sliding down the glass. When he was a little boy and it rained, he would sit on the biggest windowsill he could find at St Edmunds and pick two droplets, then pretend they were racing to the bottom of the pane. An idea he’d got from a poem; maybe one Hope had read him, which he’d forgotten now.  

雷穆斯叹了口气，凝视着卧室窗户上滑下的雨滴。当他还是个小男孩时，每当下雨，他会坐在圣埃德蒙兹找到的最大的窗台上，挑选两滴雨水，然后假装它们在窗格底部比赛。这是他从一首诗中得到的主意；也许是希望读给他听的，但现在他已经忘记了。

 

It always rained at funerals in films. That was called ‘pathetic fallacy’, Remus had read about it in an old A-level English textbook. Of course, if you had a funeral in Wales in January, the chances of rain were extremely high, too. It was a strange thing to be glad about, but it seemed proper. A sunny day would have been intolerable.  

电影中的葬礼总是下雨。这被称为“悲惨谬误”，雷穆斯在一本旧的A-level英语教科书中读到过。当然，如果你在一月的威尔士举办葬礼，降雨的可能性也非常高。这是一个奇怪的让人感到高兴的事，但似乎很合适。阳光明媚的日子会令人无法忍受。

 

“Ready?” Sirius asked, very gently, entering the room.  

“准备好了吗？”西里斯非常温柔地问道，走进房间。

 

Remus looked up at him, feeling numb, and nodded. Sirius looked gorgeous in a black suit, his hair tied back. Remus felt scruffy, though they were dressed identically, Sirius just wore clothes better. Remus had wanted to cut his hair short, to make it look tidier, but he’d been convinced not to, in the end. Still, the urge to do something drastic was there.  

雷穆斯抬头看着他，感觉麻木，点了点头。西里斯穿着黑色西装，头发束在后面，看起来很迷人。虽然他们穿得一模一样，但雷穆斯感觉自己很邋遢，西里斯只是穿衣服更好看。雷穆斯曾想剪短头发，让它看起来更整洁，但最后还是被说服了。尽管如此，他仍然有一种做点激烈的事的冲动。

 

“Take your time,” Sirius said, “We’ve got an hour or so.”  

“慢慢来，”西里斯说，“我们还有一个小时左右。”

 

Remus nodded again. The service was supposed to start at eleven, but Gethin had said that if he wanted to come earlier and greet the mourners, then he was welcome to. Remus still wasn’t sure.  

雷穆斯再次点头。仪式本该在十一点开始，但盖思温说，如果他想早点来迎接悼念者，他是受欢迎的。雷穆斯仍然不确定。

 

Sirius closed the bedroom door, and came to sit next to him. He held his hand, and stared out of the window too.  

西里斯关上卧室的门，坐到他旁边。他握住雷穆斯的手，也看向窗外。

 

“Have you ever been to a funeral before?” Remus asked, finally.  

“你以前参加过葬礼吗？”雷穆斯终于问道。

 

“Uncle Alphard’s,” Sirius replied, “I was only little, though. Nine or ten. Don’t remember it. I’ve never… lost anyone close.”  

“阿尔法德叔叔的，”西里斯回答，“不过那时我还很小，大约九岁或十岁。我记不太清楚。我从未……失去过亲近的人。”

 

“Mm.” Remus inclined his head, still watching the raindrops against the grey sky, “I don’t know if I knew Hope all that well. I didn’t even know her for a whole year.”  

“嗯。”雷穆斯低下头，仍然看着灰色天空中的雨滴，“我不知道我是否真的了解希望。我甚至没有认识她整整一年。”

 

“I don’t think that matters.”  

“我觉得那不重要。”

 

“Nor do I.” Remus bowed his head.  

“我也这样认为。”雷穆斯低下头。

 

He wasn’t going to cry again, he didn’t think he could. It had felt good at first, a big rush of emotion. But since then, nothing. Just a blankness, and empty feeling he hadn’t had before.  

他不打算再哭了，他觉得自己可能做不到。一开始哭泣的感觉很好，一股情感的冲动。但从那以后，什么都没有。只是空白和他之前没有过的空虚感。

 

Sirius gripped his hand again.  

西里斯再次握住他的手。

 

“I’ll be with you the whole time.”  

“我会一直陪着你。”

 

Remus looked at him and smiled weakly.  

雷穆斯看着他，勉强笑了笑。

 

“Thank you. Ok, I think I’m ready.” He stood up, finally whirring into action. “Oh shit!” He said, slapping his forehead, “The flowers! Padfoot, I forgot to pick up the bloody flowers!”  

“谢谢你。好，我想我准备好了。”他终于站了起来，开始行动。“哦，糟糕！”他说，一边拍打额头，“花！帕德弗， 我忘了去取该死的花了！”

 

Sirius put a hand on his shoulder,  

西里斯把手放在他的肩膀上，

 

“I got Wormtail to do it, he’s got them. And Lily’s got the address for the church, so we don’t get lost - Prongs has the food for the wake, his mum sent along some pork pies and sausage rolls, and I’ve got the umbrellas sorted. All you need to do is apparate, everything else is taken care of, all right?”  

“我让沃姆塔尔去拿了，他已经拿到了。而且莉莉有教堂的地址，所以我们不会迷路——詹姆斯负责带酒葬的食物，他的妈妈送了一些猪肉派和香肠卷，我也准备好了伞。你只需要瞬移，其他的一切都安排好了，好吗？”

 

Overwhelmed, Remus grabbed him and hugged him tightly.  

感到不知所措，雷穆斯抓住他，紧紧地抱住他。

 

“Thank you,” he said.  

“谢谢你，”他说。

 

Sirius hugged him back,  

西里斯也拥抱了他，

 

“Anything for our Moony, eh?”  

“为我们的月亮做任何事，嗯？”

 

Remus smiled, breathing in Sirius’s hair, his scent, letting it anchor him. The words popped into his head almost out of nowhere, and finally, finally, it was easy to say.  

雷穆斯微笑着，深吸西里斯的发香，任凭它让自己安定下来。这些话几乎是突然出现在他脑海中的，终于，终于，轻松地说出来了。

 

“Sirius?” He whispered, still holding on.  

“西里斯？”他低声说道，仍然抱着。

 

“Yeah?”  

“嗯？”

 

“Love you.”  

“爱你。”

 

Sirius kissed his cheek, huffing a soft laugh, which sounded like relief.  

西里斯亲吻了他的脸颊，轻轻笑了一声，听起来像是松了口气。

 

“Love you too.”  

“我也爱你。”

 

They walked into the living room hand in hand. James and Peter were also in suits, and Lily in a simple black dress, her usually vibrant hair neatly tied back in a bun. She was carrying an enormous bouquet of flowers. They all gave Remus cautious, sympathetic smiles, which he was getting used to now. He nodded back at them all, gratefully.  

他们手牵手走进了客厅。詹姆斯和彼得也穿着西装，莉莉则穿着一件简单的黑色连衣裙，她那通常充满活力的头发整齐地扎成了发髻。她还提着一大束花。他们都给了雷穆斯小心翼翼、充满同情的微笑，雷穆斯现在已经习惯了这种笑容。他感激地向他们点了点头。

 

“Right.” Sirius said, taking charge, “Let’s do this.”  

“好了。”西里斯说道，开始掌控局面，“我们开始吧。”

 

It was a small village church, just outside of Hope’s hometown - it was where she had been christened, and if she had married a muggle, it was where the wedding would have been. Remus knew from their brief conversations that Hope had not been particularly religious, but that her family belonged to the Church in Wales, so she went along for tradition’s sake.  

这是一个小村庄的教堂，就在希望的家乡外

 

面——这是她受洗的地方，如果她嫁给了一个麻瓜，那么婚礼也会在这里举行。雷穆斯从他们的简短对话中知道，希望并不是特别虔诚，但她的家庭属于威尔士教会，所以她还是遵循传统去的。

 

It was a very pretty building - or at least it would have been, if it wasn’t raining so hard. Soft grey granite, with a bell tower and a pointed steeple, simple but pretty stained glass windows. Like a church in a picture book. The graveyard was full of ancient tombstones and stone crosses, but Hope would be cremated, as per her wishes.  

这是一个非常漂亮的建筑——或者至少如果不下这么大的雨的话，它会更漂亮。柔和的灰色花岗岩，配有钟楼和尖顶，简单却美丽的彩色玻璃窗。就像一本图画书中的教堂。墓地里满是古老的墓碑和石十字架，但希望将按她的愿望火化。

 

The marauders and Lily approached slowly, walking up the sodden pathway to join the cluster of mourners gathered in the doorway. Remus spotted Gethin straight away, standing just inside the porch, shaking hands with each attendee as they entered. He was a tall man, like Lyall, but not as spindly. He had dark hair, thick black eyebrows and rather a weak chin. He looked completely broken, and Remus was instantly less nervous about meeting him.  

魔法四人组和莉莉缓缓走近，沿着湿透的小路走向门口聚集的悼念者群体。雷穆斯立刻看到了盖思温，站在门廊里，与每位进门的悼念者握手。他是一个高大的男人，像莱尔一样，但没有那么瘦。他有黑色的头发，浓密的黑眉毛和一个相当削弱的下巴。他看起来完全崩溃了，雷穆斯立刻对见到他感到不那么紧张了。

 

Lily, James and Peter hung back, looking for somewhere to put all the food they’d brought for the wake, which was supposed to be in the church hall around the back. Remus and Sirius silently waited their turn to go in.  

莉莉、詹姆斯和彼得退在后面，寻找一个地方放置他们带来的所有酒葬食物，这些食物本应该放在教堂后面的大厅里。雷穆斯和西里斯默默地等待着他们的入场机会。

 

“Hullo,” Gethin said, barely looking up as Remus approached, “Thank you for coming…”  

“你好，”盖思温说，几乎没有抬头看雷穆斯走近，“谢谢你们来……”

 

“I’m Remus.” Remus said, shaking the proffered hand. Gethin looked up at once, blinking. They were about eye-level.  

“我是雷穆斯。”雷穆斯说道，握住伸出的手。盖思温立刻抬头，眨了眨眼。他们差不多在同一高度。

 

“Remus.” Gethin shook his hand weakly, his dark eyes raking Remus over. “Hope talked about you all the time. It’s a shame we’re meeting like this.”  

“雷穆斯。”盖思温虚弱地握了握他的手，他那深色的眼睛扫过雷穆斯。“希望总是提到你。我们以这样的方式见面真是太遗憾了。”

 

“Yes.” Remus nodded.  

“是的。”雷穆斯点头。

 

They stood awkwardly for a while, just looking at each other, before Gethin came to his senses, “Go in,” he said, gesturing, “Your mum was keen on you sitting in the front row, but it’s up to you…”  

他们尴尬地站了会儿，只是互相看着，之后盖思温才回过神来，“进去吧，”他说，做了个手势，“你妈妈希望你坐在前排，但这由你决定……”

 

“Thanks,” Remus nodded again.  

“谢谢，”雷穆斯再次点头。

 

“See you after, eh?” Gethin patted his shoulder.  

“之后见吧？”盖思温拍了拍他的肩膀。

 

“Yeah. Good,” Remus said, aware that he was speaking in single-syllables.  

“嗯。好，”雷穆斯说道，意识到自己在用单音节的词说话。

 

In the end, Sirius had to nudge him into the church, as he seemed to have forgotten how to move. They made their way slowly to the front, and sat down. Remus could hear people whispering about him; a few of them knew who he was, and the reaction was mixed. He ignored it. He was there for Hope, and no one else.  

最后，西里斯不得不推他进入教堂，因为他似乎忘记了如何移动。他们慢慢走到前面，坐了下来。雷穆斯能听到有人在窃窃私语；他们中的一些人知道他是谁，反应也不一。他无视这一切。他是来为希望而来的，其他人无关紧要。

 

The service itself was a blur, and he barely listened. He just stared at the eagle shaped lectern and tried to conjure up a decent memory of his mother.  

仪式本身是模糊的，他几乎没有听进去。他只是盯着鹰形讲台，试图回忆起他母亲的美好记忆。

 

They didn’t sing a hymn, they played a Joni Mitchell song instead. Hope had never mentioned Joni Mitchell to Remus, but he supposed it must have meant something to her. That was a painful thought. They’d had so little time. It wasn’t fair.  

他们没有唱圣歌，而是播放了一首琼妮·米歇尔的歌。希望从未向雷穆斯提到过琼妮·米歇尔，但他认为这一定对她有特别的意义。这是一个令人痛苦的想法。他们的时间如此短暂。这不公平。

 

Siân was there, of course. Remus recognised her at once - she was the only child present. She was dressed in a cream coloured frock with a black satin sash, and kept her head buried in the lap of an old woman Remus didn’t know - he assumed that was Gethin’s mother, Siân’s grandmother. She cried all the way through, and for some reason that was comforting to Remus. Hope must have been a wonderful mother.  

当然，西安也在那里。雷穆斯立刻认出了她——她是唯一一个在场的孩子。她穿着一件奶油色的连衣裙，系着黑色缎带，把头埋在雷穆斯不认识的一个老妇人的膝盖上——他猜那是盖思温的母亲，西安的祖母。她一直哭泣，这让雷穆斯感到某种安慰。希望一定是一位了不起的母亲。

 

Afterwards, Remus’s legs felt like lead; he was rooted to the spot. He didn’t get up with the rest of the family to walk out (there was no coffin to follow - her body was already at the crematorium, apparently), but waited behind for the church to clear. Sirius waited with him.  

之后，雷穆斯的腿感觉像铅一样沉重，他站在原地动不了。他没有像其他家人那样起身离开（没有棺材跟随——她的遗体显然已经在火葬场了），而是留在后面等教堂清理完毕。西里斯陪着他。

 

When the church was all but empty, Sirius whispered,  

当教堂几乎空了时，西里斯低声说，

 

“You ok?”  

“你还好吗？”

 

Remus nodded.  

雷穆斯点了点头。

 

Sirius touched his knee lightly, but no more than that. “That was really sad. It’s ok if you’re tired and want to go home?”  

西里斯轻轻地碰了碰他的膝盖，但仅此而已。“那真的很伤感。如果你累了想回家也没关系。”

 

“No, it’s fine.” Remus shook his head, “I ought to go. I told Gethin I would. Just. Five more minutes?”  

“不，没事。”雷穆斯摇摇头，“我应该去的。我告诉过盖思温我会来的。只是……再等五分钟？”

 

They had to leave eventually, the caretaker wanted to tidy up.  

他们最终不得不离开，照料员想要打扫卫生。

 

The church hall was very small, and crammed full of people and people’s emotions. Some of them were laughing, reminiscing. Others were still red-nosed and sombre. It was a drab little room, which needed refurbishing; the wooden floorboards were splintering in places, there were notice boards dedicated to drawings by the children who attended sunday school there, and another one for the local scout troup.  

教堂大厅非常小，挤满了人和他们的情感。有些人在笑着，回忆往事。其他人则仍然红着鼻子，神情

 

凝重。那是一个沉闷的小房间，需要翻修；木地板在某些地方已经开裂，墙上贴着孩子们在主日学上绘制的画，还有一个是本地童子军的公告板。

 

Three trestle tables were groaning under the weight of the food people had brought - piles of sandwiches, meat pies, crisps, cheese and pineapple skewers, fruit cake, leftover turkey curry, slices of ham and other cold cuts. It was a dry funeral, and an old lady in the corner was serving weak cups of milky tea. For once in his life, Remus was not hungry.  

三张折叠桌在食物的重量下发出吱吱声——一堆堆的三明治、肉饼、薯片、奶酪和菠萝串、水果蛋糕、剩余的火鸡咖喱、火腿片和其他冷切肉。那是一个干酒葬，角落里的一个老太太在端着稀薄的奶茶。雷穆斯人生中第一次没有感到饥饿。

 

Worst of all, there was a table covered in framed photographs and albums. Most of them were of Hope, and apart from one or two snaps of her as a little girl, not one of them had been taken before 1965. Remus looked at them all, tried to fix the imagine in his mind - a happy, healthy woman who had always tried to do what was best, even when other people let her down.  

最糟糕的是，有一张桌子上摆满了裱框的照片和相册。大多数照片都是希望的，除了几张她小时候的照片外，没有一张是在1965年之前拍的。雷穆斯看着它们，试图在脑海中固定住那个形象——一个幸福、健康的女人，她总是尽力做好事，即使其他人让她失望。

 

“She’d be so glad you came.” Gethin appeared beside him. He reached out and stroked the glass on one of the photo frames. Hope’s black and white face beamed out at him, static and lifeless.  

“她会很高兴你来。”盖思温出现在他身边。他伸手抚摸着一个相框上的玻璃。希望的黑白面孔向他微笑，静止而无生命。

 

“I had to.” Remus said, quietly. Sirius stood at his other shoulder, ready for anything. Remus looked at Gethin, “I wish I had been there. For… well, to say goodbye.”  

“我必须来。”雷穆斯轻声说道。西里斯站在他的另一边，准备好应对任何情况。雷穆斯看着盖思温，“我希望我能在那里。为了……好吧，告别。”

 

“It was very quiet, like she was.” The older man said. “She was awake on Christmas morning, and went to sleep after lunch. There was no pain.”  

“那是非常安静的，就像她一样。”老人说。“她在圣诞节早晨醒着，午饭后就去睡了。没有疼痛。”

 

Remus hadn’t thought about her being in pain. He wished Gethin hadn’t put that in his head.  

雷穆斯没有考虑到她会有疼痛。他希望盖思温没有把这个念头放在他的脑海里。

 

“I know what you’re thinking,” Gethin said, nodding at the photo display, “No pictures of you. It wasn’t deliberate - she put them all in a box for me to send to you, only I’ve lost track of your address…”  

“我知道你在想什么，”盖思温说，指着照片展示，“没有你的照片。这不是故意的——她把所有照片都放在一个盒子里让我寄给你，只是我已经找不到你的地址了……”

 

“I don’t want them.” Remus shook his head.  

“我不想要它们。”雷穆斯摇摇头。

 

“Remus,” Sirius said, softly, “Don’t make any decisions yet.”  

“雷穆斯，”西里斯轻声说道，“不要急于做决定。”

 

Remus just shrugged.  

雷穆斯只是耸耸肩。

 

“There are a few other bits,” Gethin said, eyeing Sirius with some confusion, then looking at Remus again, “I’ll hang onto them as long as you like.”  

“还有一些其他的东西，”盖思温说，看向西里斯有些困惑，然后再次看向雷穆斯，“我会保留它们，只要你愿意。”

 

“Bits?” Remus looked at him blankly.  

“什么东西？”雷穆斯茫然地看着他。

 

“Things she wanted you to have,” Gethin said. “Not money, or anything--”  

“她希望你得到的东西，”盖思温说。“不是钱，或其他东西——”

 

“I’m not interested in money!” Remus said, sharply.  

“我对钱不感兴趣！”雷穆斯严厉地说。

 

Gethin frowned, he looked hurt. His eyes were rimmed red, with dark rings under them, like smudges of coal dust. Remus pursed his lips, and took a step back, shaking his head.  

盖思温皱起了眉头，他看起来很受伤。他的眼睛周围泛红，下方有黑圈，就像煤灰的痕迹。雷穆斯抿了抿嘴，退后一步，摇摇头。

 

“I’m sorry. I can’t be here. I’m sorry.” And with that, turned and walked straight out of the hall.  

“对不起。我不能待在这里。对不起。”说完，他转身径直走出了大厅。

 

It had stopped raining by now, but the grass was still wet and the scent of delicious earth rising all around. There was a group of old men sitting on some benches outside. They’d loosened their ties and sat slouched, smoking and passing around an illicit flask of something very strong smelling. Remus tutted, disgusted, and kept walking, wanting to get away from everything.  

现在雨停了，但草地仍然湿漉漉的，四周弥漫着美味泥土的气息。外面有一群老人坐在长椅上。他们松开了领带，倚坐着，抽烟并传递着一瓶味道很强的非法饮品。雷穆斯嗤之以鼻，感到厌恶，继续走着，想要远离一切。

 

“Remus!” Sirius came jogging up the path to catch him, Lily, James and Peter not far behind.  

“雷穆斯！”西里斯跑步上前追上他，莉莉、詹姆斯和彼得紧随其后。

 

“I want to go.” Remus said.  

“我想离开。”雷穆斯说。

 

“You can come back to mum and dad’s if you want?” James suggested, “Mum said she’ll do us all dinner.”  

“你可以回妈妈和爸爸那儿，如果你愿意的话？”詹姆斯建议道，“妈妈说她会为我们做晚饭。”

 

“No,” Remus shook his head, he grabbed Sirius arm, and looked at him, imploring, “Please, can we just go back to the flat? Just you and me?”  

“不，”雷穆斯摇摇头，他抓住西里斯的手臂，恳求道，“请，我们能不能回公寓？就你和我？”

 

“Of course we can,” Sirius put his own calm hand over Remus’s desperate one, and Remus felt his heart begin to steady.  

“当然可以，”西里斯把他平静的手放在雷穆斯急切的手上，雷穆斯感到自己的心开始平静下来。

 

So that was what they did, Remus promising himself that he would apologise to the Potters and his friends another time.  

于是他们就这样做了，雷穆斯向自己承诺，他会在其他时间向波特一家和朋友们道歉。

 

But if he’d been hoping for a respite from the rest of the world, to lock himself away with Sirius and pretend that just for a moment, nothing else mattered, then he was in for a disappointment.  

但如果他希望从这个世界中得到短暂的喘息，与西里斯一起锁住自己，假装这一刻其他一切都不重要，那他将会感到失望。

 

There was an owl sitting on top of the mantelpiece when they got in, with a note tied to its scaly leg.  

他们进门时，发现一只猫头鹰坐在壁炉架上，腿上绑着一张纸条。

Remus.

My condolences(哀悼).

Please meet me at the Auror’s Office at 9am on Monday.

A. Moody.

From win and lose and still somehow

It's life's illusions I recall

I really don't know life at all

Chapter 156: The War: Auror Headquarters 

Monday 8th January 1979

“Please let me come with you?” Was the last thing Sirius said as Remus left the flat early Monday morning.

“I’ll be fine.” Remus shook his head, trying to give Sirius a reassuring smile. He didn’t say what he was thinking, which was ‘how would that look?!’. It was bad enough he’d been summoned to Moody’s actual office at the ministry; what would he think if Remus brought his boyfriend along for moral support?

Still, Remus had to admit that he had a difficult time leaving their cosy little home that morning. He’d barely left the bedroom since they’d returned from the funeral, let alone got dressed or left the flat. To go to the ministry he had to wear full robes for the first time since school, which helped a little bit - at least he’d be able to blend in.

The visitors entrance for the Ministry of Magic was about twenty minutes’ walk from Soho, and Remus found the early morning stroll more pleasant than he’d expected. It was a crisp, cold January day, and his breath turned white in the winter air. Peter was there to meet him,

“Hiya Moony,” Wormtail smiled up at him, giving him an awkward pat on the arm, “How’re you holding up?”

“Oh, you know.” Remus shrugged. Grief was a funny thing. He never knew if he was doing it right.

“Looking forward to saturday!”

“Yeah, me too.”

The full moon was due on the thirteenth. So far since Hogwarts the marauders had got away with apparating (Peter side-alonged) to the most remote places possible and transforming there. So far they’d been to the Brecon Beacons, the Outer Hebrides, Dartmoor and the Forest of Dean. No one in the Order had brought it up yet, though Remus supposed they all assumed he was registered.  

十三号是满月。从霍格沃茨毕业以来，掠夺者们已经多次使用幻影移形（Peter 带着他们）到最偏远的地方并在那里变形。到目前为止，他们已经去过布雷肯比肯、外赫布里底群岛、达特穆尔和迪恩森林。虽然没人提起过，但Remus认为大家都认为他已经登记了。

 

Peter and Remus entered the ministry via a telephone box. Peter needed to be there, because after Remus had stated his business, a small silver visitors badge dropped out of the telephone’s change slot. Wormtail picked it up quickly, and muttered the incantation to turn it to tin, before giving it to Remus.  

Peter 和 Remus 通过电话亭进入魔法部。Peter 必须在场，因为Remus陈述完他的来意后，一个小银色的访客徽章从电话的零钱槽中掉了出来。Wormtail 快速捡起来，念了咒语将其变成锡，然后递给了 Remus。

 

They descended into the ministry atrium, which was heaving with activity. It was an enormous hall, bigger than Gringotts, with rows of fireplaces lining the walls. Green lights flashed intermittently from each hearth as wizards and witches arrived for work.  

他们走进魔法部大厅，那里人声鼎沸。那是一个巨大的大厅，比古灵阁还大，墙壁上排列着一排排壁炉。绿色的光芒从每个壁炉中间歇性闪烁着，巫师们陆续到达工作。

 

Peter led Remus through the security stand, where his wand was weighed by a mean-spirited wizard with a long beard. Remus was incredibly grateful to have a friend with him, and secretly quite glad it was quiet, genial Peter, rather than Sirius who had a tendency to get a bit overprotective of Remus when it came to the wizarding community.  

Peter 带着 Remus 通过安全站，那里有一个长胡子的刻薄巫师称量了他的魔杖。Remus 非常感激有朋友陪在身边，内心也很高兴是安静、和善的 Peter，而不是天狼星，他对巫师界的事总是有点过度保护 Remus。

 

Next they moved through to another hall with a set of lifts, and entered the nearest one.  

接着他们走到另一个有一排电梯的大厅，并进入最近的一部。

 

“You’re on level two,” Peter explained chirpily, “I’m with the Floo Network Authority on four. Do you need me to show you where the Auror’s office is?”  

“你在二楼，”Peter 轻快地解释道，“我在四楼的飞路网络管理局。需要我带你去傲罗办公室吗？”

 

Remus thought he would quite like Peter’s help, if only Peter wasn’t so clearly enjoying having the upper hand.  

Remus 想他确实需要 Peter 的帮助，只是 Peter 显然很享受自己占上风的感觉。

 

“No,” he smiled, “I’ll manage. Cheers mate.”  

“不用了，”他笑了笑，“我能应付的。谢谢，兄弟。”

 

Peter gave him a kind smile as he left the lift. Remus nodded back, and the door slid closed.  

Peter 离开电梯时对他友好地笑了笑。Remus 点了点头，门滑动关上了。

 

Soon enough the tannoy announced; “Level two, Department of Magical Law Enforcement; including the Improper Use of Magic Office, Auror Headquarters, and Wizengamot Administration Services.”  

很快广播宣布：“二楼，魔法法律执行部；包括不正当使用魔法办公室、傲罗总部和威森加摩行政服务。”

 

Remus shuffled his way out of the lift and onto the corridor. The lift doors closed behind him with a ‘ping’ and Remus stood there for a few moments, blindsided. It was a very busy hallway, wizards and witches striding up and down, some deep in conversation, others hastily scribbling down notes on scraps of parchment - and some of them muttering to themselves. Over his head, purple paper aeroplanes zoomed back and forth, fluttering into the office doors which lined the corridor.  

Remus 慢吞吞地走出电梯，进入走廊。电梯门在他身后“叮”地一声关上了，Remus 站在那里愣了几秒钟。走廊非常繁忙，巫师们来回穿梭，有些在深谈，有些匆忙地在羊皮纸片上写笔记——还有一些人在自言自语。在他头顶上，紫色的纸飞机来回飞舞，扑向排在走廊上的办公室门。

 

He wished he hadn’t been so proud now, and asked Pete to walk him to the right office. There had to be a sign somewhere…  

他现在真希望自己没有那么骄傲，应该让 Peter 带他去正确的办公室。一定有指示牌在某处……

 

“Lupin!” A loud and familiar voice boomed. Remus turned around with some relief and smiled, seeing Ferox barrelling towards him, hand raised in salutation.  

“Lupin！”一个响亮而熟悉的声音响起。Remus 松了一口气，转身微笑，看到 Ferox 向他跑来，手举起来打招呼。

 

“Hi,” he said.  

“嗨，”他说道。

 

“Lost? Come with me!”  

“迷路了？跟我来！”

 

Remus followed Ferox along the hallway, past office after office until they reached an elaborate door with a carved wood frame. Auror Headquarters.  

Remus 跟着 Ferox 沿着走廊走过一个个办公室，直到他们来到一个有雕刻木框的精致门前。傲罗总部。

 

“Nervous?” Ferox glanced at him sideways. Remus looked back,  

“紧张吗？”Ferox 斜眼看了他一眼。Remus 回看过去，

 

“Is it that obvious?”  

“那么明显吗？”

 

Ferox laughed and clapped him on the shoulder,  

Ferox 笑着拍了拍他的肩膀，

 

“I’d be concerned if you weren’t. C’mon now, it’s only Moody.” And he pushed the door open with one big hand, the other still on Remus’s shoulder, as if to stop him from running away.  

“如果你不紧张，我才会担心。来吧，现在只是穆迪。”他说着用一只大手推开了门，另一只手仍放在 Remus 的肩膀上，仿佛在防止他逃跑。

 

As a child, Remus had had some experience with muggle law enforcement. Only ever for silly things like running away from the Home, or being caught ‘causing a disturbance’ - which usually meant he was just somewhere public and other people would prefer him not to be. The police were extra rough with you, once they clocked you were a St Edmund’s boy, they’d call you things and shove you in their car, or else give off thinly veiled threats of physical violence if you didn’t do as you were told. As a result, Remus had never felt that comfortable around authority figures, even if he was a poshboy nowadays.  

小时候，Remus 曾与麻瓜执法部门打过交道。仅仅是因为一些愚蠢的事情，比如从家里逃跑，或被抓到“制造骚乱”——通常意味着他只是在某个公共场所，而其他人不希望他在那里。一旦警察发现你是圣埃德蒙的孩子，他们会对你格外粗暴，他们会叫你一些难听的话，把你推上车，或者在你不按他们说的做时发出隐约的暴力威胁。因此，即使他现在是个上流社会的孩子，Remus 也从未对权威人物感到过舒服。

 

He wasn’t sure exactly how similar the Aurors were to muggle police. He’d only met Moody, Frank and Alice so far. Moody was completely terrifying, but Remus had known him long enough now that he was used to him. Alice and Frank were very nice, very earnest people - but then, they didn’t know what he really was.  

他不确定傲罗与麻瓜警察有多相似。他到目前为止只见过穆迪、Frank 和 Alice。穆迪是完全令人恐惧的，但 Remus 认识他时间足够长，已经习惯了他。Alice 和 Frank 是非常好、非常认真的人——不过，他们并不知道他真正是什么。

 

The inside of the office was very busy, with rows of desks divided up into cubicles. There were posters of criminals, magically enchanted maps and printed lists on notice boards

 

 all around the walls, and memos whizzing back and forth. But the most striking thing about it for Remus was the incredibly concentrated scent of strong magic - and dark magic too.  

办公室内部非常繁忙，一排排桌子分隔成隔间。墙上到处都是罪犯的海报、魔法地图和公告栏上的打印清单，还有来回飞舞的备忘录。但对 Remus 来说，最显眼的还是那浓烈的强大魔法气味——还有黑魔法的气息。

 

Ferox, hand still on Remus’s shoulder, steered him towards a desk near the back corner, which had the best vantage point over the rest of the chaotic office.  

Ferox 仍然把手放在 Remus 的肩膀上，把他引导到靠后角的一个桌子，那是俯瞰整个混乱办公室的最佳视角。

 

Moody’s desk and the shelves around it were cluttered with weird and wonderful magical devices; whirring telescopes, glowing crystals, strange humming orbs. Moody himself was bent over a map. Forgetting his nerves, Remus peered over his shoulder to look - he’d never got over his interest in cartography - and Moody barked,  

穆迪的桌子和周围的架子上堆满了奇怪而奇妙的魔法装置；嗡嗡作响的望远镜、发光的水晶、奇怪的嗡嗡球。穆迪本人则弯腰看着一张地图。忘记了紧张的 Remus 趴在他肩膀上看——他对制图的兴趣从未减退过——穆迪吼道，

 

“Never sneak up on an Auror, Lupin.”  

“永远不要偷偷接近一个傲罗，Lupin。”

Remus jumped back, alarmed, and Moody turned to face him, grinning. His mad eye swivelled sickly in its socket.  

Remus 吓了一跳，退后一步，穆迪转身面对他，咧嘴笑了笑。他那只疯眼在眼窝里病态地转动着。

 

“Leo,” Moody reached out and shook hands with Ferox, then with Remus. “Glad to see you’re nice and punctual. Have a seat.”  

“Leo，”穆迪伸出手与 Ferox 握手，然后与 Remus 握手。“很高兴看到你准时到达。坐下吧。”

 

He gestured at a long velvet-covered seat against the wall of his cubicle which hadn’t been there a moment ago. Remus and Ferox sat down as Moody cast a spell which muted the noise around them, creating a bubble of peace around his desk that was not dissimilar to James and Sirius’s silencing charms.  

他指了指靠在他隔间墙上的一张长长的天鹅绒椅子，那椅子刚刚还不存在。Remus 和 Ferox 坐下，穆迪施了一个静音咒，使他们周围形成了一个宁静的泡泡，这与 James 和天狼星的静音咒非常相似。

 

Remus was relieved by the quiet, but Moody’s spell had done nothing to mitigate the overwhelming scent of power which filled his nostrils, swam down his throat and filled up his chest with glorious rich syrupy magic. He tried to relax, to let it find its place in him rather than fighting it, but he felt ever so slightly drunk with it all the same.  

Remus 对这片宁静感到宽慰，但穆迪的咒语并没有减轻那充斥他鼻腔、顺着喉咙游走，充满他胸腔的那股浓烈的力量气息。这种辉煌而浓稠的魔法让他感觉稍微有点醉。他试着放松，让这种力量在他体内找到自己的位置，而不是抗拒它，但他仍然感觉有点微醺。

 

“Once again, Lupin,” Moody said gruffly, sitting down in his office chair which looked like a plush green leather armchair, but swivelled on one stem. “I was sorry to hear about your loss. I didn’t know Hope myself, but--”  

“再一次，Lupin，”穆迪粗声说道，坐在他的办公椅上，那椅子看起来像一张豪华的绿色皮革扶手椅，但能在一个轴上旋转。“听说你失去了亲人，我很遗憾。我自己不认识 Hope，但——”

 

“That’s ok.” Remus said quickly, “I barely knew her either.”  

“没关系。”Remus 迅速说道，“我也几乎不认识她。”

 

He was keen to keep his mother out of any conversation he had today. He hadn’t the strength for two things at once, and if Moody had a mission for him, then that had to be his main concern.  

他不想在今天的谈话中提及他的母亲。他没有精力同时处理两件事，如果穆迪有任务要交给他，那必须是他主要的关注点。

 

Moody - who was either an excellent legilimens or simply extremely astute and empathetic, nodded manfully and continued.  

穆迪——不论他是一个出色的摄神取念师还是只是非常机敏和有同理心——男人般地点了点头，继续说道。

 

“Straight to business, then.” He said, “Good chap.” He swivelled slightly in his chair to pick up the map he’d been looking at, and handed it to Remus.  

“那么直接谈正事吧。”他说，“好小伙。”他稍微转动椅子，拿起他一直在看的地图，递给 Remus。

 

Remus took it eagerly, and looked. It was a map of Britain and Ireland, but not like ones he had seen before - there were no roads marked, no towns or cities, only the woodland areas, rendered in mossy green splodges of ink. Some of these splodges seemed to shimmer and twinkle, as if there were stars hiding beneath the tree branches.  

Remus 迫不及待地接过地图，仔细看着。这是一张英国和爱尔兰的地图，但与他以前见过的不同——上面没有标注道路，没有城镇或城市，只有以苔绿色墨迹描绘的森林区域。这些斑点有些似乎在闪烁，好像树枝下藏着星星。

 

“Got that from the Control of Magical Creatures office,” Moody explained, “Thanks to Ferox here. Know what it is, lad?”  

“从魔法生物管理办公室得到的，”穆迪解释道，“多亏了 Ferox 在这里。知道这是什么吗，小子？”

 

“It’s…” Remus poured over it, “It’s all of the forests with magic in it? Or magical creatures?”  

“这是……”Remus 仔细研究道，“所有有魔法的森林？还是有魔法生物的森林？”

 

“Exactly.” Moody nodded, looking very pleased with him, “We’ve noticed that most of the werewolf sightings over the past few years have been in enchanted woodland, forests with a denser population of magical creatures. Now, that could just mean they’re keeping their ears to the ground for you-know-who, or that there are other creatures working with them…”  

“正是如此。”穆迪点点头，看起来对他很满意，“我们注意到，过去几年大多数狼人目击事件都发生在被施了魔法的森林里，那些魔法生物密集的森林。现在，这可能意味着他们在为你知道的那个人打探消息，或者有其他生物在与他们合作……”

 

Or because the scent of all that natural magic is just too good to resist, Remus thought, his own blood fizzing like champagne just from the twenty or so powerful wizards nearby. He didn’t say this, of course, for his own sake.  

或者是因为所有那些自然魔法的气息太难以抗拒，Remus 想着，仅仅是附近二十多个强大巫师的存在，就让他的血液像香槟一样起泡。当然，他不会为了自己的安全说出来。

 

“...and for the last couple of full moons there’s been a lot of activity here,” Moody pointed a stubby, scarred finger at a point on the map, somewhere in the midlands.  

“……而在过去几个月圆之夜，这里有很多活动，”穆迪用他粗短的、有疤痕的手指指着地图上的一个点，那是英格兰中部的某个地方。

 

“Why are you telling me now?” Remus asked, “If you’ve been following them for months?”  

“你们跟踪了他们几个月，为什么现在才告诉我？”Remus 问道。

 

“It’s time.” Moody said, fixing him with a hard stare, one blue eye, one brown. “Greyback’s in the country for the first time since the sixties; it’s been confirmed.”  

“是时候了。”穆迪说道，用一种坚硬的目光看着他，一只蓝眼睛，一只棕眼睛。“自六十年代以来，Greyback 第一次进入这个国家；已经确认了。”

 

“Oh.” Remus pursed his lips to quell the rage inside him, rearing up like a cobra, showing its teeth. Where is he?! Take me to him right now! “Right.”  

“哦。”Remus 抿着嘴唇压抑着内心的愤怒，这种愤怒像眼镜蛇一样抬起头，露出牙齿。他在哪里？！现在就带我去找他！“好的。”

 

“Last time you made contact you came back with some good information,” Moody continued, “Those who want to join Greyback need to transform with the pack three times, that right?”  

“上次你接触到的信息很好，”穆迪继续说道，“那些想加入 Greyback 的人需要和狼群一起变形三次，对吗？”

 

“Mm.” Remus nodded. He wanted to stand up and pace, or do something physical, but he couldn’t afford for either Ferox or Moody to know that there was anything wrong.  

“嗯。”Remus 点点头。他想站起来走动，或者做一些体力活动，但他不能让 Ferox 或穆迪知道有什么不对劲。

 

“And the next full moon is on Saturday?”  

“下次满月是在星期六？”

 

Remus nodded. He looked at Ferox, then Moody again,  

Remus 点点头。他看了看 Ferox，然后又看向穆迪，

 

“You want me to go already? To start… to…”  

“你想让我现在就去？开始……？”

 

“Just for the moons,” Ferox said, his voice calming, “Just until they trust you.”  

“只是为了满月，”Ferox 说道，他的声音很平静，“直到他们信任你为止。”

 

“But once they trust me,” Remus said, looking at his hands, “Then… I need to meet him, right?”  

“但一旦他们信任我，”Remus 低头看着自己的手说道，“那么……我需要见他，对吗？”

 

“Let’s see

 

 how things go.” Moody said, choosing his words carefully. “We’ve three months to plan for that.”  

“让我们看看事情的发展。”穆迪谨慎地选择着词语说道。“我们还有三个月的时间来计划。”

 

“Ok.”  

“好的。”

 

Remus didn’t know what else to say. His head was full and his nerves were raw and he felt almost ready to explode, but for some weird reason he just sat there like a polite schoolboy, listening to Moody lay out the plan.  

Remus 不知道还能说什么。他的脑子很满，神经很紧张，感觉自己快要爆炸了，但不知为何，他就像一个礼貌的学生一样坐在那里，听穆迪讲述计划。

 

He was given a lot of rules. He would have to go alone. He could take his wand, but nothing else. He could tell nobody, not even the other members of the order, not even his best friends. Ferox began suggesting things Remus could say or do to get the pack to trust him, but Remus ignored him. He knew what to do.  

他被给了很多规定。他必须独自前往。他可以带上他的魔杖，但不能带其他东西。他不能告诉任何人，甚至是其他成员，甚至是他最好的朋友。Ferox 开始建议 Remus 可以说或做些什么来让狼群信任他，但 Remus 没有理会。他知道该怎么做。

 

“I’ll walk you out, shall I, Lupin?” Ferox said finally, with a note of paternal kindness.  

“我送你出去，好吗，Lupin？”Ferox 最后说道，带着一点父亲般的善意。

 

“Thank you,” Remus said, standing up quickly.  

“谢谢，”Remus 迅速站起来说道。

 

“You’re a man of few words, Lupin,” Moody said, standing up too, holding out his hand once more for Remus to shake, “But I’ve every faith in you. I’ll send the coordinates before Saturday. Make sure you’re at home to receive them.”  

“你是个沉默寡言的人，Lupin，”穆迪也站起来，伸出手再次与 Remus 握手，“但我对你充满信心。我会在星期六前把坐标发送给你。确保你在家接收。”

 

Remus nodded blankly, shaking the proffered hand. Just as he had guided him in, Ferox led Remus back out of the Auror Headquarters.  

Remus 茫然地点点头，握住了递过来的手。就像他带他进来一样，Ferox 领着 Remus 离开了傲罗总部。

 

“Alright there, fella?” Ferox asked, once they were clear of the doors. The corridor was a bit quieter than it had been at nine o’clock.  

“还好吗，伙计？”一离开门口，Ferox 问道。走廊比九点时安静了不少。

 

“Yes. Fine.”  

“是的，没事。”

 

“If there’s anything you think you need, if you want me to ask Moody for something that will help, you can just--”  

“如果你觉得需要什么，如果你想让我问穆迪要一些有帮助的东西，你可以——”

 

“How will it help?” Remus asked, suddenly, stopping in the middle of the hallway. He twitched his thumb and cast muffliato, without any effort at all. Ferox blinked, surprised,  

“这有什么用？”Remus 突然问道，停在走廊中间。他微微动了动拇指，毫不费力地施了一个消音咒。Ferox 眨了眨眼，惊讶地问，

 

“How will what help?”  

“什么有用？”

 

“Me, meeting Greyback? I’ve met three members of his pack now, and it’s only made things worse each time.”  

“我，见 Greyback？我现在已经见过他手下的三名成员，每次都只会让事情变得更糟。”

 

“That’s not true. You’ve given us some extremely valuable information.”  

“那不是真的。你给了我们一些非常有价值的信息。”

 

“If I have,” Remus said, “Then I want to know what you’re using it for.”  

“如果我有，”Remus 说道，“那么我想知道你们是用它来做什么的。”

 

“To win the war, Remus.” Ferox shook his head.  

“为了赢得战争，Remus。”Ferox 摇了摇头。

 

“When I met Castor last year,” Remus said, his voice very low, but more out of anger than a desire to be discreet, “He told me in no uncertain terms that they were planning an attack.
