“Because I never felt like that before - they were my family, and we were all the same, we were all at home there, and it was… it felt like the only place in the world I was meant to be! All that, it was all that except…” and now tears were coming, scalding hot, “Except he was there, that fucking… that monster. He was so evil, so… and I was scared, and I wanted to come home, to you, I did, but I couldn’t just leave them with a man like that. And they could… they could do things I didn’t know I could do, they taught me… And I just didn’t know who I was anymore.”

He wiped his face, the tears dripping off his chin. He looked Sirius in the eye. “I don’t know who I am.”

They stared each other out, as the echoes subsided. Remus was breathing heavily, his cheeks hot, but he felt good. Relieved.

Finally, Sirius spoke. He put his hands in his pockets and squinted around, off into the distance. He smiled,

“因为我从来没有过这样的感觉——他们是我的家人，我们都是一样的，我们都在那儿感到归属，就好像那是我唯一该待的地方！所有那些，都是这样的，只是……”眼泪现在也涌了出来，烫得让人心疼，“只是他在那儿，那该死的……那个怪物。他是如此邪恶，如此……我很害怕，我想回家，回到你身边，我确实想，但我不能就这样离开他们，面对那样的人。而且他们可以……他们可以做我不知道我能做的事，他们教我……我只是再也不知道自己是谁了。”

“Why is it always this beach eh?”

“What?” Remus blinked, caught off guard. Sirius looked at him, eyes twinkling.

“Why is this the beach where we have all the big revelations?”

“Maybe we’re just dramatic.”

“How very dare you!” Sirius was smirking, and Remus laughed, despite himself. “Well?” Sirius said, “Feel better?”

“Yeah. Oi, wait a minute, did you just deliberately try to piss me off??”

“No…” Sirius looked away again, piously, “Not at first…”

“Dickhead.”

“It worked.”

Remus didn’t respond, because he really did feel better, and he didn’t want to fight again. They kept walking, and eventually reached roughly the spot where they had all camped out two years ago. The wind was kicking up, sweeping across the grassy sand dunes, and the campsite was empty. It didn’t look like the same place.

Remus没有回答，因为他确实感觉好多了，也不想再争吵了。他们继续走，最终到达了大约两年前他们露营的地方。风在吹拂，扫过草地上的沙丘，营地已经空了。看起来不像是原来的地方了。

“Think we’ll ever come back here?” Remus asked, hands deep in his pockets to stop his coat flapping in the breeze.“你觉得我们会再回来这里吗？”Remus问，双手深深地插在口袋里，以防外套在风中飞扬。

“I hope so.” Sirius replied. “It’s my patronus thought, this place.”

“我希望会。”Sirius回答，“这是我护符的思绪，这个地方。”

“Is it?” Remus looked at him, surprised.

“Haven’t had any better summers yet.”

“Fair point.”

“Oi, look!” Sirius wandered off towards a group of rocks, bent and picked up a big long stick. He waggled it at Remus, grinning, “Want to play fetch?”

Remus laughed,

“Go on then.”

Sirius glanced around covertly to confirm they were alone, then transformed into Padfoot. Remus was grateful—he’d done enough talking now, and it was a relief to just play with canine-Sirius for a few hours. The big black dog raced up and down the beach, chased waves, played fetch, and generally had an excellent time, and on the bus back to the pub both of them fell asleep.Sirius偷偷环顾四周，确认他们是独自一人，然后变成了Padfoot。Remus很感激——他已经说够多了，现在能和犬形Sirius玩几个小时是一种解脱。那只大黑狗在海滩上奔跑，追逐海浪，玩接球游戏，总之玩得很开心。在回旅馆的公共汽车上，他们俩都睡着了。

It wasn’t until much later that night, after dinner (oh, how Remus had missed real food! Mashed potato! Sausages! Gravy!), when they were getting ready for bed, that Sirius brought it up again.直到那晚晚些时候，晚餐后（哦，Remus多么想念真正的食物！土豆泥！香肠！肉汁！），他们准备上床时，Sirius才再次提起这件事。

Remus was yawning as he crawled under the covers, and Sirius got in beside him quietly, turning off the bedside lamp. The bed was so narrow that Remus had to lie with his back to the wall, an arm around Sirius’s waist, and a face full of silky black hair, which he didn’t really mind.Remus在爬进被窝时打着哈欠，Sirius静静地在他身边躺下，关掉了床头灯。床很窄，Remus不得不背靠墙，手臂环绕着Sirius的腰，脸上贴满了柔软的黑发，这让他并不介意。

“I know who you are.” Sirius whispered into the empty quiet of the dark bedroom.

“Hm?” Remus asked, sleepy and confused. Sirius pulled Remus’s hand to his mouth and kissed his fingers.

“You said you don’t know who you are any more. But I do. You’re my Moony. Always will be. Ok?”

“Ok, Padfoot.”

For now it was enough.

* * *

Moody got word to them that they could return to their flat, provided that Remus kept a low profile for a while - he didn’t specify for how long. This meant no Order meetings and no missions - he wasn’t even allowed to visit the Potters’ house. For all intents and purposes, Remus Lupin had vanished off the face of the earth a month ago and never returned.  

穆迪通知他们可以回到他们的公寓，只要Remus保持低调——他没有具体说明多长时间。这意味着不能参加凤凰社的会议，也不能执行任务——他甚至不被允许去波特家的住所。从各方面来看，Remus Lupin已经从地球上消失了一个月，未曾返回。

 

“I bet he just wants to wait for the next full moon to get the all clear.” Sirius suggested. “Anyway, you deserve a break.”  

“我敢打赌他只是想等到下一个满月再确认你没问题。”Sirius建议道。“无论如何，你也该休息一下了。”

 

Remus just shrugged.  

Remus只是耸了耸肩。

 

“Served my purpose now, I s’pose. They don’t know what to do with me.”  

“现在我大概已经完成了我的目的。他们不知道该怎么处理我。”

 

“Don’t talk about yourself like that.” Sirius snapped irritably. They’d been stuck in the same tiny room for too long.  

“别这么说自己。”Sirius不耐烦地说道。他们已经在同一个狭小的房间里待了太久。

 

They apparated back, and Remus began to feel a bit more himself once he was really home. The flat was immaculately tidy - apparently Sirius had a lot of nervous energy while Remus was away - but otherwise everything was as it should be.  

他们使用闪现术回到了公寓，Remus一回到真正的家里，感觉自己稍微恢复了一些。公寓里一尘不染——显然Sirius在Remus离开期间有很多紧张的精力——但其他方面一切都很正常。

 

No one was supposed to know that Remus was back, but of course James had told Lily and Peter, and Marlene had told Mary, so the first evening they were home everyone came over at once. Luckily Lily had the presence of mind to bring food, because Sirius had nothing at all in the house.  

没有人应该知道Remus回来了，但当然James已经告诉了Lily和Peter，Marlene也告诉了Mary，所以他们回家的第一晚，大家都一下子来了。幸运的是，Lily有足够的头脑带来了食物，因为Sirius家里什么都没有。

 

“Been eating at the Potters’.” He mumbled, bashfully.  

“在波特家吃饭。”他羞怯地嘟囔道。

“对不起！”她抽泣着说，声音在他最好的毛衣上变得沉重而模糊，“我只是……我没想到我会再见到你！”

“天哪，你比Padfoot还要大惊小怪。”

“所以你有事要告诉我？”

Marlene和Peter很快就从工作中赶到。Peter甚至有了一个公文包，上面有他的名字首字母。显然他在魔法部做得不错，Remus尽量不对此感到太过心怀不满。

Marlene坚持在卧室里再给Remus检查一次，检查他的脚踝，现在恢复得像新的一样，还有他的胸部，情况好多了。

“说真的，我不能相信你还在抽烟。”她不满地说，当他点燃烟时，扣上他的衬衫。“你知道这会杀死麻瓜。”

Mary一到就泪如雨下，扑到Remus的怀里。

“你这个绝对的混蛋！”她在他脖子里低声说，“我真想杀了你！”

“我也很想你。”Remus说，紧紧拥抱着她。

“What’s your news?”

“大家，”James清了清
喉咙，“呃。Lily和我有些事要——”

“Mary！”Lily的脸色更红了，“不是那个！”

“我们要结婚了！”Lily急忙喊道，在Mary能再说什么之前。
You could have heard a quill drop.  
你能听到笔掉落的声音。

“你求婚了？”Marlene戳了戳Lily，“真是个了不起的女权英雄，Evans。”

“这有点更为相互，”Lily笑道，“我们只是聊天，然后——”

“但我们才刚刚离开学校。”Sirius说，声音有些沉闷。

“一年前，”Peter提醒他，整理着他绿色格子西装的翻领。

“你们真的考虑过这个问题吗？！”

“我相信他们考虑过了，Black，冷静点。”Mary说，试图缓解气氛。她站起来，“我去外面看看能不能弄到便宜的气泡酒？这值得庆祝！”

“好！”Marlene也站起来了。她拥抱了Lily，然后亲吻了James的脸颊，“祝贺你们两个！”

“祝贺你们！”Peter醉醺醺地举起了他的啤酒罐。

“你们都疯了吗？！”Sirius几乎喊道。Remus看到Lily脸上的失望表情，决定够了。他站了起来。

“Padfoot。”他坚定地说，使用了那种语气，“不。”

Sirius现在瞪着他。他的嘴巴突然闭合，像个情绪化的少女一样甩了甩头，然后推开他们，走出了房间。卧室的门猛地关上了。

他没有敲门，直接走了进去。毕竟，这也是他的公寓。Sirius已经做好了准备，Remus关上门后，他立即开始了。

“实际上，我认为这些都是举行婚礼的足够理由。”Remus叹了口气，坐在床上。

“They’re in love.” Remus tried reasoning. Sirius laughed - a mean, cruel laugh -  
“他们相爱。”Remus试图讲理。Sirius笑了——是一种刻薄、残酷的笑声——
“Oh, and you’re going to start waxing lyrical about love, are you Moony?!”  
“哦，你要开始说教关于爱情的事了，Moony？！”
“Watch it.” Remus stood up, sharply, using his height to tower over Sirius. “I don’t know why you’re being such a tosser to James and Lily, but I’m not going to sit here and have you fling bitchy little comments at me.”  
“注意点。”Remus直起身来，用他的身高俯视Sirius。“我不知道你为什么对James和Lily那么不耐烦，但我不打算坐在这里让你对我抛出刻薄的评论。”
Sirius was about to retort, when the door swung open again, and this time James barrelled in, angrier than Remus had ever seen him.  
Sirius正要反驳时，门再次猛地打开，这一次James闯了进来，比Remus见过的任何时候都要愤怒。
“You dick!”
 He yelled, “What the fuck are you playing at?! Moony, don’t defend him!”  
“你个混蛋！”他吼道，“你到底在搞什么？！Moony，不要替他辩护！”
“I’m not!” Remus said, stepping away and crossing his arms, “I was saying the same!”  
“我不是！”Remus说，退后一步，交叉着双臂，“我也是这么说的！”
“Well?!” James rounded on Sirius again, “Want to explain yourself?!”  
“那呢？！”James再次转向Sirius，“想解释一下吗？！”
“No, I want you to explain yourself!” Sirius snapped, “What the fuck?! You’re getting married, just like that? I know you’ve had this mad thing for Evans since you were twelve, but bloody hell! What’s the rush?!”  
“不，我要你解释！”Sirius咆哮道，“什么鬼？！你们就这样结婚了？我知道你从十二岁开始就对Evans有这种疯狂的感觉，但该死的，急什么？！”
“It’s not a ‘mad thing’!” James shouted, “I love her! I’ve been in love with her forever, as you well know!”  
“这不是‘疯狂的感觉’！”James喊道，“我爱她！我一直爱她，正如你所知道的！”
“So you have to get married all of a sudden?!”  
“所以你们突然要结婚吗？！”
“I want to get married, and it’s not sudden! We’ve been talking about it for ages.”  
“我想结婚，这不是突然的！我们谈论了很久。”
“First I’ve heard of it!”  
“这是我第一次听说！”
“Yeah, well, I don’t have to tell you everything! I didn’t want to say anything until Moony was back.”  
“是的，我不必把所有事情都告诉你！我不想在Moony回来之前说任何事。”
“What about your parents?! What do they think??” Sirius was losing steam, but obviously not willing to stop being angry yet.  
“你的父母呢？！他们怎么看？？”Sirius的愤怒逐渐减退，但显然还不愿意停止愤怒。
“They’re thrilled, actually! They love Lily! And I thought you did too! You’re my best friend, I thought you’d be supportive!”  
“他们实际上很高兴！他们喜欢Lily！我还以为你也喜欢！你是我最好的朋友，我以为你会支持！”
“Oh!” Sirius’s eyes gleamed, “Because you’ve always been so supportive of my relationships!”  
“哦！”Sirius的眼睛闪闪发光，“因为你总是如此支持我的感情生活！”
James’s eyes flickered towards Remus, then back again - it was only a split second, but Remus definitely felt it. What the hell was that about?  
James的眼睛闪向Remus，然后又回到Sirius身上——这只是一个瞬间，但Remus明显感觉到了。这到底是怎么回事？
“You know that’s not...” James said, fiercely, jaw clenched.  
“你知道这不是……”James激烈地说，咬紧了牙关。
Remus took that as his cue to leave. Whatever was going on between the two of them, he didn’t want any part in it. He went straight to the kitchen and looked under the sink. There was a bottle of firewhisky he’d put there after the last party for safekeeping. He uncorked it and took a long swig.  
Remus把这当作离开的信号。不管他们之间发生了什么，他都不想参与其中。他直接去了厨房，查看水槽下的地方。那里有一瓶他在上次聚会后为了保存安全放在那里了的firewhisky。他拔开瓶塞，喝了一大口。
“Remus?”  
“Remus？”
He almost choked as Lily entered the kitchen. She laughed and reached out a hand,  
当Lily走进厨房时，他几乎呛住了。她笑了，伸出手来，
“Give us some, then? Mum always said never to drink alone.”  
“那给我一点吧？妈妈总是说不要一个人喝酒。”
He laughed, wiping his mouth with the back of his sleeve and handing her the bottle. She drank deeply, and didn’t wince - Remus watched her with awe and thought that if you had to marry a girl, then she’d better be exactly like Lily Evans.  
他笑了，用袖子擦了擦嘴，把瓶子递给她。她痛痛快快地喝了一大口，丝毫没有皱眉——Remus惊叹地看着她，心想如果必须娶一个女孩，那她最好就像Lily Evans一样。
“Sorry I ruined your homecoming party.” She said, forlorn.  
“对不起我毁了你的归来派对。”她伤感地说。
“You didn’t,” Remus shook his head, “Sorry about Sirius.”  
“你没有，”Remus摇了摇头，“对不起Sirius。”
“Oh, don’t be silly - you’re not his keeper.”  
“哦，别傻了——你不是他的保姆。”
“He’s being a prat.”  
“他在发疯。”
“He’s just jealous, I knew he would be.” She laughed, catching Remus’s look, “Not like that , Moony, it’s obvious he’s madly in love with you, I mean he’s worried he’s going to lose his best friend.”  
“他只是嫉妒，我知道他会这样。”她笑着，看到Remus的表情，“不是那样的，Moony，很明显他疯狂地爱着你，我的意思是他担心会失去他的最好的朋友。”
“You’re probably right.”  
“你说的可能对。”
“I’m usually right.” She raised an eyebrow at him, and he laughed again.  
“我通常是对的。”她挑了挑眉，他再次笑了。
“Congratulations,” he said, sincerely, this time. “I think it’s brilliant.”  
“恭喜你，”他说，真诚地这次。“我觉得这很棒。”
“Thanks, love,” she smiled softly. “It is a bit rushed, I know - my parents went spare; Pet was only married last year, and she’s three years older than me. But… you know Euphemia and Monty aren’t well?”  
“谢谢，亲爱的，”她柔和地笑道。“我知道有点急——我的父母很生气；Pet去年才结婚，她比我大三岁。但……你知道Euphemia和Monty身体不好吗？”
“Yeah, I wish I could go and see them, but… Moody’s orders, y’know.”  
“是的，我希望我能去看看他们，但……Moody的命令，你知道的。”
“They understand.” She touched his arm gently, “Anyway, they’re really… I mean, they’re not suffering or anything, but they’re very old. I knew how much it meant to James - having them see him with me. They want to know he’ll be ok when they’re gone.”  
“他们理解的。”她轻轻地触碰他的手臂，“反正，他们真的……我是说，他们并没有痛苦，但他们年纪很大。我知道对James来说这意味着多少——让他们看到他和我在一起。他们想知道他在他们离开后会好好的。”
Maybe he’d had too much to drink, but tears pricked in Remus’s eyes unexpectedly. He covered his face and groaned,  
也许他喝多了，但Remus的眼睛突然湿润了。他捂住脸，呻吟道，
“Jesus Christ, Evans, can I have five minutes without an emotional breakdown?!”  
“天哪，Evans，我能有五分钟时间没有情感崩溃吗？！”
She laughed and hugged him again,  
她笑了，再次拥抱了他，
“Lovely boy.”  
“好孩子。”
“We’ve baa-ack!” Mary and Marlene sang as they stumbled into the flat once more, giggling merrily.  
“我们回来了！”Mary和Marlene唱道，再次跌跌撞撞地进入公寓，开心地笑着。
“Hide that, quick!” Lily gave Remus his bottle back, and he stowed it back under the sink behind a box of laundry powder.  
“快把它藏起来！”Lily把瓶子还给了Remus，他把瓶子放回水槽下的洗衣粉盒后面。
By the time Mary had poured everyone a glass (or a mug) of babycham (“the closest thing to champagne you can get in Soho after midnight”), James and Sirius had re-emerged from the bedroom, both still red faced, but apparently on better terms. Sirius joined in the toast, at least, and even gave Lily a polite kiss on the cheek.  
当Mary给每个人倒上一杯（或一个杯子）babycham（“午夜后在Soho能买到的最接近香槟的酒”）时，James和Sirius已经从卧室重新出现了，脸色仍然红润，但显然关系有所改善。Sirius至少参加了祝酒，甚至给了Lily一个礼貌的吻在脸颊上。


 

Still, the atmosphere had changed, and everyone left within the next hour or so - Marlene was staying over at Mary’s in Croydon, Peter went back with James and Lily. When the door closed for the last time at one in the morning, Remus felt like curling up on the couch, covering his head and staying there for a week.
不过，气氛已经改变了，每个人在接下来的一个小时左右离开了——Marlene去Mary在Croydon的家过夜，Peter和James、Lily一起回去了。当早上一点钟最后一次关门时，Remus感觉像是蜷缩在沙发上，盖住头，待上一个星期。

Sirius didn’t say much, just did a bit of perfunctory tidying up, then went to the bathroom. Remus heard the lock click shut and took the opportunity for one last glass of whisky and a cigarette before bed. He felt grimy; his teeth were furry, his throat scorched and his eyes itching, but it suited his mood.
Sirius没说多少，只是做了一些敷衍的收拾，然后去了浴室。Remus听到锁的咔嚓声，抓住机会再喝一杯威士忌，抽一支烟再上床。他感觉很脏；牙齿发黏，喉咙灼热，眼睛发痒，但这正适合他的心情。

He didn’t feel like talking anymore; especially if it led to another fight. He even considered just falling asleep on the couch. But then - that might just mean a fight in the morning, and he already knew he was going to be hungover then. Only one thing for it.
他不想再说话了；尤其是如果这会引发另一场争吵。他甚至考虑直接在沙发上睡觉。但那样的话——早上可能就会吵架，而他已经知道那时自己会宿醉。只有一种解决办法。

Sirius unclicked the door and Remus heard him padding through to the bedroom. Maybe if Remus took his time brushing his teeth Sirius would doze off before he got there - they’d both had a lot to drink. He hoisted himself off the couch and headed for the bathroom.
Sirius解开了门锁，Remus听到他轻步走向卧室。也许如果Remus慢慢刷牙，Sirius会在他到达之前打盹——他们俩都喝了很多酒。他从沙发上站起来，朝浴室走去。

Remus washed his face and the back of his neck in cold water, and stared at himself in the medicine cabinet mirror above the sink. He’d been avoiding his reflection since he got back. He looked like shit; still too hollow in the cheeks, eyes darker and wider somehow. He was pale from too much drink and his scars stood out like silver wires under his skin.
Remus用冷水洗了洗脸和脖子，盯着水槽上方药柜镜子里的自己。从回来以来，他一直避免看自己的倒影。他看起来很糟糕；脸颊仍然太凹陷，眼睛不知为何更暗更大。他因为喝酒过多而脸色苍白，伤疤在皮肤下像银色的线一样突出。

Did he have that same haunted look that they had; the pack? Had he caught that feral glint, that rangy wolfish smirk? Or was he just seeing the angry, frightened care home kid that has always been there?
他有着和他们一样的那种被困扰的表情吗；那个狼群？他捕捉到了那种野性光芒，那种瘦削的狼样笑容吗？还是他只是看到了那个一直存在的愤怒、害怕的养老院孩子？

He sighed, defeated, and flicked off the light, going to bed at last.
他叹了口气，感到沮丧，关掉了灯，终于上了床。

The lights were still on, and Sirius was under the covers, only his silky black hair visible, draped over the pillow. He always slept like that; hidden. With a flash of clarity Remus was reminded of the child Sirius had once been; alone in a big house full of family who couldn’t understand him, the weight of expectation pressing in on all sides.
灯还亮着，Sirius在被子下，只有他丝滑的黑发显露出来，垂在枕头上。他总是这样睡；隐藏起来。Remus突然清晰地想起了曾经的Sirius；在一个充满不了解他的家人的大房子里孤独，期待的重压四面八方地逼近他。

Remus turned his loneliness inwards; always had. But Sirius - he pushed his loneliness out, and let other people take it from him. So he got a bit possessive sometimes, a bit panicky - so what? Nobody was perfect. Softening, Remus got in beside him and very gently stroked Sirius’s hair.
Remus把孤独向内转；一直都是这样。但Sirius——他把孤独推向外界，让其他人从他身上拿走。所以他有时候会变得有点占有欲，有点惊慌——那又怎样？没有人是完美的。Remus的心情软化了，他躺在Sirius身边，非常温柔地抚摸着Sirius的头发。

“All right?” He whispered.
“还好吗？”他低声问道。

Sirius’s head bobbed in a sort of nod under the duvet, and he reached out to wind his arms around Remus’s waist. Remus sighed, relieved. It felt so good to be back in his own bed. They could always just not fight, he thought to himself. “Love you,” he murmured, kissing the top of Sirius’s head.
Sirius的头在被子下点了点，伸手把胳膊绕在Remus的腰上。Remus叹了口气，感到松了口气。回到自己的床上感觉真好。他想，至少可以不再争吵。“爱你，”他低声说道，吻了吻Sirius的头顶。

Sirius’s arms grew tighter around him, and soon enough they both fell asleep.
Sirius的胳膊紧紧环绕着他，不久之后他们俩都睡着了。

Chapter 164: The War: Summer 1979Notes:BEFORE YOU BEGIN: The lyrics used in this chapter are from a song called 'Rex's Blues', which was written/performed in 1977 by Townes Van Zandt. So it counts as an era appropriate song for this fic - BUT, the version which I first heard, and which I had in mind when writing this chapter is by Jolie Holland.

Chapter TextRide the blue wind, high and free

She'll lead you down through misery

Leave you low, come time to go

Alone and low, as low can be.

 

 

Lily and James’s wedding was set for late September. It was going to be a relatively small affair - order members and school friends, mostly - and it would be held at the Potters’ estate. They were hoping the weather would be nice enough to have it in the gardens, but even if it rained there was plenty of room indoors.
莉莉和詹姆斯的婚礼定在了九月底。这将是一个相对小型的聚会——主要是成员和学校朋友——将在波特家族的庄园举行。他们希望天气好到可以在花园里举行，但即使下雨，室内也有足够的空间。

After making such a fuss on the night of Remus’s homecoming, Sirius was clearly very embarrassed by how he’d acted, and made up for it by doing pretty much anything James and Lily asked of him. He ordered dress robes for the boys in Madam Malkin’s, went to pick up the rings from the jeweller, and offered his entire record collection up for use at the reception.
在Remus回家的那晚大闹了一番之后，Sirius显然对自己的行为感到非常尴尬，他通过几乎满足詹姆斯和莉莉的所有要求来弥补。他为男孩们在Madam Malkin’s定制了礼服，去珠宝店取了戒指，并把自己的整个唱片收藏提供给婚礼接待使用。

Remus, who had never been to a wedding, tried to stay well back. As far as he knew, his duty as groomsman was to show up, keep Sirius’s head from exploding, and make sure none of Lily’s muggle family saw anything too scarring.
从未参加过婚礼的Remus尽量保持距离。就他所知，作为伴郎的职责就是出现，确保Sirius不会爆炸，确保莉莉的麻瓜家人不会看到任何过于刺激的东西。

Sirius’s most bonkers act of contrition was to hand-write all of the invitations. His talent for calligraphy was still one of Sirius’s darkest secrets, (and Remus’s favourite thing to tease him about) but he was determined to be the perfect Best Man, so he sat hunched over the dining table one afternoon and worked at it for a solid four hours.
Sirius最疯狂的悔过行为是亲手书写所有的邀请函。他的书法才华仍然是Sirius最黑暗的秘密之一（也是Remus最喜欢拿来调侃他的事），但他决心成为完美的最佳男伴，所以他在一个下午蜷缩在餐桌旁，认真地写了整整四个小时。

“Fifty-eight!” Sirius said, triumphantly, finishing the last invitation with a flourish of his quill.
“五十八张！”Sirius得意地说，完成了最后一张邀请函，挥了挥他的羽毛笔。

“Well done,” Remus said, glancing over the top of his newspaper, “Ahh, look at your pretty handwriting! So dainty!”
“做得好，”Remus说，瞥了一眼报纸上方，“啊，看看你的漂亮字迹！真精致！”

“Better than your chicken-scratch!” Sirius poked his tongue out.
“比你的乱七八糟好！”Sirius吐了吐舌头。

“Just don’t tell anyone you did them,” Remus advised, “Or you’ll start getting requests.”
“只要别告诉别人是你做的，”Remus建议道，“否则你会开始收到请求。”

“Do you really think they’re that good?” Sirius asked, holding one up to the light to inspect the delicate whorls of black ink.
“你真的觉得它们那么好吗？”Sirius问道，把一张邀请函举到光线下，检查那精致的黑色墨迹。

“They’re gorgeous. Really.” Remus said, fondly.
“真的很漂亮。”Remus温柔地说。

“Well, this is the only time I’m doing it,” Sirius sniffed, tidying up the pile, “This is the one and only wedding I will ever support.”
“好吧，这是我唯一一次这样做，”Sirius嗤嗤地说道，整理堆积的邀请函，“这是我唯一支持的婚礼。”

“What if Mary got married? Or Pete?”
“那如果Mary结婚了呢？或者Pete呢？”

“I’d show up and get drunk, but secretly I would hate every minute.”
“我会出现然后喝醉，但心里会恨每一分钟。”

“Very reasonable,” Remus nodded.
“很合理，”Remus点了点头。

“Another thing you can blame the noble and most ancient house of cack for.” Sirius said, “Do you know how many engagement dinners and weddings I’ve been to? Ugh.” He shuddered visibly. “So I’m sorry, Moony, but you’ll never make an honest man of me.”
“这是你可以怪罪于那个高贵且古老的家族的另一件事。”Sirius说道，“你知道我参加过多少次订婚晚宴和婚礼吗？呃。”他明显地颤抖了一下。“所以抱歉，Moony，但你永远无法让我成为一个诚实的男人。”

“Oh, and I was just about to propose,” Remus said dryly, getting up, “Tea?”
“哦，我正打算求婚呢，”Remus干巴巴地说道，站起身，“要喝茶吗？”

“Please.” Sirius nodded, rubbing his sore knuckles.
“请。”Sirius点了点头，揉着酸痛的指关节。

Remus entered the kitchen, tapping the kettle with his wand - they’d gone to get it the same day as the dress robes. It had reminded Remus a bit of going to get his school shoes as a boy; Ollivander measured him and then hummed and ahhed and muttered to himself under his breath. He’d rummaged about in the stock room and bought out box after box of wands for Remus to try. Eventually they’d settled on a flexible cypress number, with a unicorn hair core.
Remus走进厨房，用魔杖敲了敲水壶——他们是在同一天去取的，礼服也是那天买的。这让Remus想起了小时候去买校鞋的情景；Ollivander量了他的尺寸，然后哼哼唧唧地自言自语。他在仓库里翻找，拿出一盒又一盒的魔杖让Remus试。最终他们决定了一个灵活的柏木魔杖，里面有独角兽的毛发。

He’d been trying to get used to it. It wasn’t the same as Lyall’s wand (which he’d found out had been blackthorn, with a kelpie hair core) - it seemed less rigid, more inclined to do what Remus told it. Which meant that Remus had to remember not to put too much force behind his magic, as he’d grown used to doing.
他一直在尝试适应它。它和Lyall的魔杖不一样（他发现Lyall的魔杖是黑刺树的，里面有海妖的毛发）——它似乎不那么僵硬，更容易按照Remus的指示行事。这意味着Remus必须记住不要对魔法施加过多的力量，因为他已经习惯了这样做。

He watched the steam rising from the kettle spout thoughtfully.
他若有所思地看着水壶嘴冒出的蒸汽。

“It would really piss them off, though,” Remus called through the thin wall.
“不过，这真的会让他们恼火，”Remus透过薄墙说道。

“What? Who?”
“什么？谁？”

“Your family.” Remus said, plonking two tea bags into two mugs, “If you married a bloke. A half-blood, werewolf, bloke.”
“你的家人。”Remus说道，把两个茶包放进两个杯子里，“如果你嫁给一个家伙。一个混血，狼人，家伙。”

“Don’t forget poor!” Sirius laughed. “Merlin, just imagine sending my mother an invitation to that!”
“别忘了还很穷！”Sirius笑道。“梅林，想象一下给我母亲寄那样的邀请函！”

“Imagine sending anyone an invitation to that,” Remus snorted, “Christ, I can already hear James making horrible puns about the honey moon.” He carried the mugs of tea back through to the living room, setting them down on the coffee table.
“想象一下给任何人寄那样的邀请函，”Remus哼了一声，“天哪，我已经能听到James在对蜜月做恶劣的双关了。”他把茶杯端回到客厅，放在咖啡桌上。

“I’ve already been engaged once, I really don’t fancy doing it again.” Sirius said, with an air of finality.
“我已经订过一次婚了，真的不想再这样做一次。”Sirius带着一种最终的语气说道。

“Oh yeah, you’re welcome for that.” Remus winked.
“哦，是的，别客气。”Remus眨了眨眼。

Well, if I had a nickel, I'd find a game

If I won a dollar, I'd make it rain

If it rained an ocean, I'd drink it dry

And lay me down dissatisfied.

 

It's legs to walk and thoughts to fly

Eyes to laugh and lips to cry

A restless tongue to classify

All born to grow and grown to die

 

The wedding planning was actually a very welcome distraction, as the summer opened up before them. Sirius, James, Peter and Lily were often called out urgently for order missions, and the list of missing read out at the beginning of every meeting was growing longer.
婚礼计划实际上是一个非常受欢迎的分心，因为夏天在他们面前展开。Sirius、James、Peter和Lily经常被紧急召唤去执行任务，每次会议开始时读出的失踪人员名单越来越长。

Benjy Fenwick, who had been working with Moody for years was horribly murdered - they couldn’t even have a casket at his funeral; there wasn’t enough of him left. Darius Barebones - who Remus had never liked, but who was nonetheless a dedicated agent - was found flayed alive in his own office at the ministry. They were miserable times.
Benjy Fenwick，一个与Moody合作多年的老手，被残忍杀害——他们甚至无法为他的葬礼准备棺材；他剩下的东西不够多。Darius Barebones——Remus曾经不喜欢，但他仍然是一个尽职尽责的特工——被发现活活剥皮在他自己的办公室里。这是令人痛苦的时光。

Remus was finally allowed to return to the Order officially after two full moons had passed without incident. Ferox believed that the split Castor had instigated meant that Greyback’s pack was too weak to be much use to Voldemort - and somehow everyone had got the idea that Remus was responsible for this.
在经过两个完整的满月没有发生意外后，Remus终于被正式允许回到密谋者组织中。Ferox相信，Castor制造的分裂意味着Greyback的狼群已经太弱，无法对伏地魔有多大帮助——而且不知怎么的，每个人都觉得Remus对此负有责任。

Dumbledore actually shook his hand, saying, “You’ve done us all so proud, Mr Lupin.”
邓布利多实际上握了握他的手，说：“你让我们所有人都感到骄傲，Lupin先生。”

Danny McKinnon had even apologised to him - Remus thought that was probably Marlene’s doing.
Danny McKinnon甚至向他道了歉——Remus认为那可能是Marlene的安排。

By July, the Order’s numbers had dwindled so much that even Remus was getting sent out - and he was often paired with Mary, which made things bearable. Their general orders were to backup Aurors by standing guard, or managing surveillance on some of the better known death eaters. Remus and Mary spent a lot of time sitting in cafes together, or hiding behind bushes.
到了七月，密谋者组织的成员数量减少得如此严重，连Remus也被派出去执行任务——而且他经常和Mary搭档，这让事情变得可以忍受。他们的主要任务是通过站岗来支持Aurors，或者对一些较为知名的食死徒进行监视。Remus和Mary花了很多时间一起坐在咖啡馆里，或者藏在灌木丛后面。

One such mission involved following a death eater called Travers, who was known to drink at a wizard’s pub near Stoke Mandeville. They were just supposed to see where he went; how he spent an average day. Caradoc Dearborn, a hero of the Order of the Phoenix, had last been seen entering the pub, but no one had heard from him since.
其中一个任务涉及跟踪一个叫Travers的食死徒，他以在斯托克曼德维尔附近的一家巫师酒吧喝酒而闻名。他们的任务只是看他去了哪里；他怎么度过一个普通的一天。Caradoc Dearborn，凤凰社的英雄，最后一次被看到进入酒吧，但之后没有人再听到他的消息。

“You came back,” Mary whispered, as they waited in the backseat of an ancient Ford Cortina, parked across the road. “So maybe Caradoc will too.”
“你回来了，”Mary低声说道，他们在一辆古老的Ford Cortina的后座上等待，车子停在对面。“所以也许Caradoc也会回来。”

“I hope so.” Remus replied.
“我希望如此。”Remus回答道。

“I just can’t bear not knowing.” Mary’s leg was shaking nervously, “I keep imagining… and what they did to the Prewetts!”
“我实在无法忍受不知道。”Mary的腿紧张地颤抖着，“我一直在想象……他们对Prewetts做了什么！”

“Don’t think about it.” He put a hand on her knee to keep her still, and searched for a distraction, “Hey, did Lily decide on flowers in the end?”
“别想这些。”他把手放在她的膝盖上以保持她的稳定，寻找转移注意力的方法，“嘿，莉莉最后决定花卉了吗？”

“Anything except lillies or petunias,” Mary said, with a grateful smile, “Me and Marls are wearing lavender, so whatever goes with that.”
“除了百合或矮牵牛花之外的任何花，”Mary带着感激的微笑说道，“我和Marls穿的是熏衣草色的，所以随便什么搭配。”

“Sounds nice.” Remus nodded, though he couldn’t for the life of him picture the colour lavender - was it purple? Or blue?
“听起来不错。”Remus点了点头，虽然他实在想象不出熏衣草的颜色——是紫色吗？还是蓝色？

“I’m so glad you’re here with me, Remus,” Mary said, “I could only ever get my defensive spells right in your study groups.”
“我很高兴你和我在一起，Remus，”Mary说道，“我只在你的学习小组里才能把防御咒语做对。”

“We’re just here to watch. Everything will be alright.”
“我们只是来观察的。一切都会好的。”

They waited for hours, and when Travers finally came out, staggering and reeking of spirits, he was not alone. Remus had to nudge Mary, who’d nodded off, lolling against his shoulder.
他们等了几个小时，当Travers终于出来时，他踉跄着，满身是酒气，他并不孤单。Remus不得不轻轻碰了碰Mary，她已经打瞌睡，靠在他的肩膀上。

“Oh shit!” She whispered, her voice hoarse with terror, “Six of them, Remus!”
“哦，糟了！”她低声说道，声音因恐惧而沙哑，“六个人，Remus！”

Remus held a finger to his lips, signalling her to be quiet. He watched the death eaters spill out of the pub onto the quiet country road. He recognised a few of them from pictures Moody had shown the order - Karkaroff, Dolohov, and Alecto Carrow. Two of them he recognised by scent.
Remus伸出手指示意她保持安静。他看着食死徒们从酒吧溢出到宁静的乡村道路上。他认出了几个人，是Moody在组织中展示过的照片中的人——Karkaroff、Dolohov和Alecto Carrow。他通过气味也认出了其中的两个人。

“Fuck.” He said under his breath, “It’s Mulciber and Snape.”
“该死。”他低声说道，“是Mulciber和Snape。”

“No!” Mary grabbed his arm, peering to look, “Oh my god! We’ve got to get out of here!”
“不！”Mary抓住他的胳膊，探头去看，“天啊！我们得离开这里！”

The problem was, the car was just for show, and anyway neither of them could drive.
问题是，这辆车只是摆设，而且他们两个都不会开车。

“Stay calm,” Remus said, “We’ll just wait for them to go - I bet they’re going to app--”
“保持冷静，”Remus说道，“我们只要等他们走——我敢打赌他们会使用——”

“Oooh, muggles!” Alecto Carrow, a stocky, horsey faced young woman pointed gleefully at the Cortina, “Let’s play!”
“哦，麻瓜！”Alecto Carrow，一个魁梧的、长着马脸的年轻女人兴奋地指着Cortina车，“让我们玩吧！”

“Fuck.” Remus said again. The six dark robed wizards glided towards them, drawing their wands. Remus pulled his out too, Mary following suit. “Quick,” he said, “Let’s get out, maybe we can--”
“该死。”Remus再次说道。六个穿着黑袍的巫师滑向他们，抽出魔杖。Remus也抽出了魔杖，Mary跟着他的动作。“快，”他说，“我们离开，或许我们可以——”

“APERIO!” Travers whipped his wand at the car, and the doors ripped away, wrenched from their hinges with a horrible, crunching metal sound.
“开门！”Travers用魔杖对准车子，车门被撕开，随着可怕的金属咯吱声从铰链上扯下。

Mary screamed, but she kept her wand up. Remus pushed her backwards, shielding her with his body and hoping they could get out the other side. He’d feel much better with a car between them and the six dangerous killers.
Mary尖叫了一声，但她保持着魔杖。Remus把她推向后面，用身体挡住她，希望他们能从另一边逃出去。他希望有辆车在他们和这六个危险的杀手之间，这样他会感觉好一些。

“They’re not muggles!” One of the death eaters said, gleefully - was it Mulciber? “They’re mudbloods!”
“他们不是麻瓜！”一个食死徒兴奋地说道——是Mulciber吗？“他们是泥巴种！”

“Ahh even better!” Alecto cackled.
“啊，那更好！”Alecto咯咯笑道。

“Impedimenta!” Remus yelled, as he and Mary got free of the car.
“减速咒！”Remus大喊，随着他和Mary从车子里出来。

“Loony Lupin, is that you?!” Snape now, “What luck! Sectumsc --”
“疯疯癫癫的Lupin，是你吗？！”现在是Snape，“真幸运！撕裂咒——”

“LANGLOCK!” Mary cried, with so much emotion that Remus heard the click as Snape’s teeth snapped shut, and he clutched his jaw with both hands, unable to speak.
“封嘴咒！”Mary大喊，情绪激动到Remus听到Snape的牙齿咬合的声音，他双手捂住下巴，无法说话。

“Crucio!” Mulciber shouted, aiming at Mary, but Remus jumped in quickly with a shield charm.
“酷刑咒！”Mulciber大喊，瞄准Mary，但Remus迅速用盾牌咒防护住了她。

“Stupefy!” Mary got Mulciber, but the others were still advancing, even Snape, though he was still disabled.
“麻痹咒！”Mary击中了Mulciber，但其他人仍在逼近，甚至Snape，虽然他还被封嘴咒困住。

“Quick, Mary!” Remus grabbed her hand, and they disapparated, landing just about on their feet in the middle of Cardiff town centre. Luckily it was so late there were no muggles about - except for a very drunk looking tramp, who rubbed his eyes at the sight of them.
“快点，Mary！”Remus抓住她的手，他们消失了，最终在卡迪夫市中心落地。幸运的是，现在很晚了，没有麻瓜在附近——只有一个看起来非常醉醺醺的流浪汉，他揉了揉眼睛看见了他们。

“Where are we?” Mary asked, shakily, her eyes huge.
“我们在哪里？”Mary颤抖着问，眼睛睁得很大。

“Doesn’t matter,” Remus panted, “We need to do it again - six times to be safe, remember?”
“没关系，”Remus喘息着，“我们需要再做一次——安全起见，六次，记得吗？”

“Right, yes, ok,” she nodded, clearly in shock. Remus realised he’d have to do it again. He squeezed her hand once more, and they were in Essex, only a mile or so from St Edmund’s. The landing was even harder this time, and Remus had to bend forward to stop his head spinning.
“对，是的，好的，”她点了点头，明显处于震惊之中。Remus意识到他还得再做一次。他再次握紧她的手，他们出现在埃塞克斯，只离St Edmund’s大约一英里。这次落地更加困难，Remus不得不弯下腰来阻止头晕。

“Again.” He grunted.
“再来一次。”他咕哝道。

“I’ll do it.” Mary took his hand, and dragged him whirling through space once more. Next they had arrived in an industrial estate somewhere, trucks and lorries parked outside big warehouses, glowing under faint yellow street lamps. “Ugh,” Mary pressed a hand to her forehead, wincing, “Ok, again.”
“我来做。”Mary握住他的手，再次将他拖过空间。接着他们来到了一个工业区，卡车和货车停在大仓库外面，黄昏的街灯下微弱发光。“呃，”Mary把手按在额头上，皱起了眉头，“好，再来一次。”

The fourth time, they had to cling to each other to stop from falling over. The fifth time, they landed on their backs - thankfully in a soft grassy field somewhere in the Lake District. Remus hauled himself up, his legs practically jelly, his head spinning. He pulled Mary up too, and she stumbled against him, woozy.
第四次，他们不得不互相抓住才能防止摔倒。第五次，他们仰面落地——幸好是在湖区的一个柔软的草地上。Remus艰难地站起来，腿几乎变成了果冻，头晕目眩。他也拉起Mary，她踉跄着靠在他身上，迷糊不清。

“I’m going to be sick.” She said, then promptly turned around and threw up. Remus rubbed her back gently, blinking sweat out of his eyes,
“我要呕吐了。”她说，然后立刻转过身去呕吐。Remus轻轻拍了拍她的背，眨了眨眼中的汗水，

“You’re doing so well,” he choked, “Just once more…”
“你做得很好，”他哽咽道，“再一次……”

It was almost dawn when they got back to London, exhausted and queasy, heads throbbing. Mary stayed at their flat, saying she couldn’t go to her mum’s looking so rough. Sirius summoned Moody through the fireplace, and he arrived immediately, interrogating Remus and Mary who sat shaking on the couch, wrapped in blankets and sipping weak tea.
当他们回到伦敦时，天快要亮了，疲惫不堪，恶心，头痛。Mary留在他们的公寓里，说她不能以这么糟糕的状态去她妈妈那里。Sirius通过壁炉召唤了Moody，他立刻到达，对坐在沙发上、裹着毯子、喝着淡茶的Remus和Mary进行了审问。

“Excellent work, you two,” He nodded to them before leaving, “Keep it up, and you’ll both make it through.”
“干得好，你们两个，”他在离开之前对他们点了点头，“继续保持，你们俩都会活下来的。”

Mary burst into tears.
Mary突然哭了起来。

-------

 

It was bad all round. Remus and Mary’s narrow escape that night was not their last, nor were they the only ones to find themselves in a tight spot. Remus frequently had to leave the room while James and Sirius recounted their own misadventures, and Peter had developed a bit of a stammer whenever anyone mentioned death eaters.
情况很糟糕。Remus和Mary那晚的勉强逃脱并不是他们最后一次遇险，他们也不是唯一陷入困境的人。Remus经常不得不离开房间，当James和Sirius讲述他们自己的冒险经历时，Peter也因为每次提到食死徒而有些结巴。

All told, the wedding felt like the only bright spot in their rapidly shortening futures. They’d certainly had their fill of funerals.
总的来说，婚礼感觉是他们逐渐缩短的未来中唯一的亮点。他们确实已经受够了葬礼。

So, in late August when Remus and Sirius had an unexpected visit from Lily, who was in a state of panic, they immediately assumed the worst.
所以，在八月底，当Remus和Sirius突然接到处于恐慌状态的Lily的拜访时，他们立刻以为出了大事。

“Oh, thank god you’re here!” She said, bursting into their living room. Her hair was up in a messy ponytail, and she looked over tired and overworked.
“哦，谢天谢地你们在这里！”她说，冲进他们的客厅。她的头发扎成了一个乱糟糟的马尾辫，看起来非常疲惫和过度工作。

“What’s the matter?!” Remus stood up, quickly.
“怎么了？！”Remus立刻站起来。

“Not you,” she brushed him aside dismissively, then turned to Sirius, “I need you!”
“不是你，”她不屑一顾地推开他，然后转向Sirius，“我需要你！”

“What’s up?” Sirius looked just as puzzled as Remus. Lily never needed his help. “Is it Prongs?”
“怎么了？”Sirius看起来和Remus一样困惑。Lily从不需要他的帮助。“是Prongs吗？”

“Yes, the bastard.”
“是的，那混蛋。”

The worry left Sirius’s face and he smirked.
Sirius脸上的担忧消失了，他露出了笑容。

“Look, if this is about the stag do…”
“听着，如果这是关于单身派对的事……”

“Oh, I don’t care what you lot get up to,” she tutted impatiently, “This is much, much more important.”
“哦，我不在乎你们搞什么，”她不耐烦地嘟囔道，“这件事更重要得多。”

“I’ll put the kettle on, then…” Remus said, disappearing into the kitchen. He could still hear them through the wall.
“那我去烧水……”Remus说着，消失在厨房里。他还能透过墙壁听到他们的声音。

“So, what is it then?” Sirius was asking.
“那到底是什么？”Sirius问道。

“I can’t dance.”
“我不会跳舞。”

“What?!” He scoffed, “I’ve seen you dance.”
“什么？！”他嗤笑道，“我见过你跳舞。”

“Yeah, I can shake my hips to pop music, but I’m talking about proper dancing. With steps, and James leading, and counting ‘one two three’, the whole shebang!”
“是的，我能随着流行音乐扭动腰部，但我说的是正规的舞蹈。包括步伐，还有James带领着，数着‘一二三’，整个大场面！”

Sirius was laughing, now.
Sirius现在在笑。

“It’s going to be that sort of wedding? Prongs practically promised me there would be modern music!”
“这会是那种婚礼？Prongs几乎向我保证会有现代音乐！”

“There will be!” Lily returned, defensively, “But… well it’s traditional to have a first dance, and I think his mum would like to see it. I agreed to do it ages ago; I thought ‘fine, we’ll just stick on something soppy and just sort of cling on to each other for a few minutes’, but that wanker just casually mentioned the fact that he’s been ballroom dancing since he could walk!”
“会有的！”Lily辩解道，“但是……首先跳舞是传统，我觉得他的妈妈想看看。我早就同意做这个；我想‘好吧，我们就随便放首柔情的歌曲，互相依偎几分钟’，但那个混蛋却随意提到他从会走路时就开始学芭蕾舞！”

Sirius snorted,
Sirius哼了一声，

“Yep, sounds about right. Look, Evans, you’re the one bonkers enough to marry a pureblood, you’ve made your bed now.”
“是的，听起来很对。听着，Evans，你是唯一一个疯狂到要嫁给纯血巫师的人，你现在只能自食其果。”

“But you have to help me!”
“但你得帮我！”

“Ohhhh no…”
“哦，不……”

Remus re-entered the room with a tray balancing three mugs of tea.
Remus带着托盘进了房间，托盘上放着三杯茶。

“Go on,” he said, slyly, “I’d love to see this.”
“继续，”他说，狡黠地，“我很想看看这个。”

“Absolutely not.” Sirius folded his arms decisively. “Get Pete to do it! He’s a pureblood too!”
“绝对不行。”Sirius果断地抱着胳膊说。“让Pete来做吧！他也是纯血巫师！”

“He’s too short,” Lily shook her head, “And… well I don’t want to be mean, but he’s very clumsy, and I don’t want him stepping on my feet while I’m breaking in my wedding shoes. They’re white satin. Please, Sirius? I’m a fast learner, I swear, you just need to get me through one dance.”
“他太矮了，”Lily摇摇头，“而且……我不想说得太过分，但他非常笨拙，我不想他在我磨合婚鞋时踩到我的脚。它们是白色缎子做的。请，Sirius？我学习很快，我发誓，你只需要让我完成一次舞蹈。”

“Moony!” Sirius pleaded, as Remus sat beside him, “Save me!”
“Moony！”Sirius恳求道，当Remus坐在他旁边时，“救救我！”

“I think you should do it,” Remus replied, sipping his tea, “For James.”
“我觉得你应该做这个，”Remus一边喝茶一边回答，“为了James。”

“Yes!” Lily nodded enthusiastically, “For James!”
“是的！”Lily热情地点头，“为了James！”

“He doesn’t deserve me.” Sirius grumbled. “Fine. One lesson. A waltz is easy enough. Moony, go away.”
“他不配我。”Sirius抱怨道。“好吧。一次课。华尔兹很简单。Moony，走开。”

“Absolutely not.” Remus sat down on the couch, settling in for the show, “I’ve never seen you waltz before, and I’m not going to miss it.”
“绝对不行。”Remus坐在沙发上，准备看戏，“我从没见过你跳华尔兹，我不想错过。”

Sirius held up his middle finger, then tossed his head and turned to Lily.
Sirius竖起中指，然后甩了甩头，转向Lily。

“Right,” he said, haughtily, “Give me your hands…”
“好，”他说，傲慢地，“把你的手给我……”

As amusing as it first seemed, fifteen minutes into the lesson Remus was completely entranced.
最初看起来很有趣，但十五分钟的课程后，Remus完全被吸引住了。

Sirius worked hard to hide his pure-bloodedness most of the time. Ever since they were kids, Remus had been aware of Sirius mimicking his accent, and sometimes even his mannerisms in an effort to seem less privileged. He slouched, he swore, he wore ripped jeans and leather jackets. But here was proof that Sirius Orion Black, heir to the most prestigious and ruthless magical house in Britain, had not completely forgotten his roots.
Sirius大多数时间都努力隐藏自己的纯血身份。从他们还是孩子时起，Remus就知道Sirius模仿他的口音，有时甚至模仿他的举止，以显得不那么优越。他耷拉着肩膀，咒骂，穿着破旧的牛仔裤和皮夹克。但现在这证明了Sirius Orion Black，英国最著名和最残酷的魔法家族的继承人，并没有完全忘记自己的根源。

At the time, Remus found it charming - as he found almost everything about Sirius charming. He held his head high, showing off his long white neck and regal jawline. He took Lily in his arms like a real gentleman - like a courtly prince. When he moved, he glided; not a step out of place. He was the picture of incorruptible nobility. It drove Remus mad.
当时，Remus觉得这很迷人——就像他觉得几乎所有关于Sirius的事物都很迷人一样。他昂首挺胸，展示着自己修长的白色脖颈和高贵的下巴线。他像真正的绅士——像一位宫廷王子一样拥抱Lily。当他移动时，他优雅地滑动；步伐完美无缺。他是不可腐蚀的贵族的典范。这让Remus发疯。

“Thank you so much!” Lily gushed, rather pink cheeked after two hours of dancing, “I have to get back, or he’ll wonder where I am, but I seriously owe you one, Black.”
“非常感谢！”Lily在两小时的舞蹈后，脸颊微红地说，“我得回去了，不然他会想我去哪了，但我真的欠你一个人情，Black。”

“Oh, just your first born will do.” Sirius waved a hand gallantly, grinning. He looked like he’d enjoyed himself too.
“哦，随便你第一个孩子吧。”Sirius风度翩翩地挥挥手，笑着。他看起来也玩得很开心。

Sirius snorted, “You’ll have to come to the garage, then.” Sirius哼了一声，“那你得来车库。”

Remus had only ever been to their shared garage once. There were a few things stored there - mainly Sirius’s quidditch kit and various childhood things which wouldn’t fit in the flat. And the bike, of course. It was a Triumph Bonneville T120, the same as the one Sirius had first fallen in love with years ago at the Potters’. He’d painted a lion on the tank, and done some kind of enlarging spell on the body. Remus只去过他们共用的车库一次。那里存放着一些东西——主要是Sirius的魁地奇装备和各种不适合放在公寓里的童年物品。当然还有摩托车。那是一辆Triumph Bonneville T120，就像Sirius多年前在Potters家第一次爱上的那辆一样。他在油箱上画了一个狮子，并对车身做了一种放大咒语。

Sirius pulled out a rag and polished it, though it was already glistening. Remus stood quietly by, watching. Sirius prodded it with his wand in a few places, oiled it in others. Sirius拿出一块抹布擦拭摩托车，尽管它已经闪闪发光。Remus静静地站在一旁观看。Sirius在几个地方用魔杖戳了戳，又在其他地方加了油。

“When do you think it’ll be finished?” Remus asked, finally. “Ready to ride?” “你觉得什么时候会完成？”Remus终于问道。“准备好骑了吗？”

“Last week,” Sirius replied, not looking up. “上周，”Sirius回答，没抬头。

“You what?” “你说什么？”

“It’s done. Engine runs, flying function works. I’m finished. I think so, anyway, haven’t taken it out yet.” “已经完成了。引擎运行，飞行功能正常。我已经完成了。我想是这样，反正还没出去试过。”

“Why not?” “为什么不？”

Sirius just shrugged, and resumed his polishing. Remus watched him a bit longer. Obviously Sirius didn’t feel like talking, and that was fair enough - Remus understood that better than most people. But he also understood the need to do something when you couldn’t express yourself properly. Sirius只是耸了耸肩，然后继续擦拭摩托车。Remus多看了他一会儿。显然Sirius不想说话，这也没什么不对——Remus比大多数人都更理解这一点。但他也理解当你无法正确表达自己时，做一些事情的必要性。

“Let’s go, then.” He said. Sirius, crouching in front of the bike rocked back on his heels and looked at Remus. “那我们走吧。”他说。Sirius蹲在摩托车前，脚跟向后靠，抬头看着Remus。

“Go? Go where?” “去哪？去哪里？”

“Anywhere you like,” Remus shrugged, “Let’s take it for a spin.” “哪里都行，”Remus耸耸肩，“我们去兜风吧。”

Sirius blinked, “Really? You’ll come with me?” Sirius眨了眨眼，“真的？你会陪我吗？”

“Well I’m hardly going to let you fly off on that deathtrap alone, am I?” Remus laughed, “What sort of boyfriend would I be if I didn’t follow you into the jaws of certain doom?” “我可不会让你一个人骑着那个危险的东西飞走，对吧？”Remus笑道，“如果我不跟着你去面临某种危险，那我算什么样的男朋友？”

The ghost of a smile flickered on Sirius’s face, and he stood up. Sirius脸上闪过一丝微笑，他站了起来。

“Ok, then,” he nodded, “Let’s do it.” “好的，”他点点头，“那我们就去吧。”

Remus had never liked flying. He was competent on a broom these days, but it would never be his chosen form of transportation. He just didn’t like heights very much. Remus从来不喜欢飞行。他现在能熟练使用扫帚，但这永远不会是他选择的交通工具。他只是很不喜欢高处。

Still, he would do almost anything for Sirius, so he clambered onto the back seat and wrapped his arms around Sirius’s waist and took lots of very deep breaths. Sirius actually laughed at him, which was progress, 尽管如此，他愿意为Sirius做几乎任何事情，于是他爬上了后座，环抱着Sirius的腰，深深地吸了几口气。Sirius实际上笑了他，这算是一种进步，

“Moony, are you sure you want to do this? I can feel your heart pounding!” “Moony，你确定你想这样做吗？我能感觉到你的心脏在跳动！”

“Absolutely.” Remus nodded, squeezing his eyes shut as Sirius gripped the handlebars, “I’m sure I’ve faced worse than your driving.” “绝对确定。”Remus点头道，当Sirius握住车把时他紧闭着眼睛，“我确信我曾面对过比你的驾驶更糟糕的情况。”

“Well, if you’re sure…” Sirius revved the engine and Remus clung on even tighter as the seat began to rumble. “好吧，如果你确定……”Sirius轰鸣着发动机，当座椅开始震动时，Remus抓得更紧了。

They went slowly at first, Sirius navigated carefully out of the garage, pointing his wand at the door so that it closed and locked behind them, then trundled slowly along the quiet back street. Then he flicked a switch, and pressed down his foot, and they sped away, Remus still trying not to look, his stomach doing backflips. 一开始他们很慢，Sirius小心翼翼地驶出车库，指着门用魔杖使它关上并锁好，然后沿着安静的后街慢慢前行。然后他按下了一个开关，踩下了脚，他们迅速离开，Remus依然尽量不去看，他的胃翻腾着。

“Here we go!” Sirius called out, and Remus buried his head in Sirius’s shoulder as they lifted off the ground, engine roaring as they gained height. Remus felt himself sliding backwards and yelped as his tailbone hit the metal back of his seat. “来了！”Sirius叫道，当他们离开地面时，Remus把头埋在Sirius的肩膀上，发动机咆哮着随着高度的增加。Remus感觉自己在滑向后面，尖叫着因为尾骨撞到座椅的金属部分。

“Christ…” he whimpered. He really was going to die. Sirius laughed again, “We did it, Moony!” He cried, “Open your eyes you big wuss!” “天啊……”他呜咽道。他真的要死了。Sirius再次笑了，“我们成功了，Moony！”他喊道，“睁开你的眼睛，你这个大胆子！”

Remus did, and instantly regretted it. They were a few hundred feet above the London skyline already; he could see the broad concrete rooftops and beige streets below. The people looked like tadpoles and the cars like beetles and it was such a long way down. Remus睁开了眼睛，立刻后悔了。他们已经在伦敦天际线几百英尺的高度；他可以看到下面广阔的混凝土屋顶和米色的街道。人们看起来像蝌蚪，汽车像甲虫，距离下方的距离实在太远了。

“Oh my god…” he moaned. “哦我的天……”

Sirius cheered happily, “Isn’t it amazing!?” - he was facing forward, eyes on the horizon. It was blue skies as far as the eye could see. The wind rushed past their ears, cold and fresh, and Remus had to squint against the sun. Sirius高兴地欢呼道，“这不是很棒吗！？”——他面朝前方，眼睛盯着地平线。眼睛能看到的都是蓝天。风从他们耳边吹过，寒冷而清新，Remus不得不眯着眼睛迎着阳光。

“‘mazing,” he shouted back, feeling quite sick, but pleased that Sirius was happy. “太棒了，”他回应道，感觉很晕，但看到Sirius很开心也很满足。

They zoomed all over London for the better part of an hour - going as low as Sirius dared along the winding Thames, taking sharp corners around skyscrapers and almost crashing right into the dome of St Paul’s. Finally, the engine began to slow, and Remus noticed they were losing height. He looked down, bravely and squinted at the unfamiliar streets below, 他们在伦敦飞行了将近一个小时——沿着弯曲的泰晤士河尽可能低飞，绕过摩天大楼急转弯，差点撞上圣保罗大教堂的圆顶。最后，发动机开始减速，Remus注意到他们正在下降。他勇敢地往下看，眯着眼睛看着下面陌生的街道，

“Where are we?” “我们在哪里？”

“Islington.” “Islington。”

“What?! Sirius!” “什么？！Sirius！”

Shit! He was supposed to be keeping him away from the Blacks, and now they were heading right for them! 糟糕！他本该将Sirius远离Black家族，现在他们却正朝着他们的方向前进！

“Calm down,” Sirius replied, as they sank even further. They appeared to be aiming for a huge stretch of green space - a public park with trees and a lake and neat gravel paths around brightly coloured flower beds. “冷静下来，”Sirius回答道，当他们进一步下降时。他们似乎正瞄准一片巨大的绿地——一个有树木、湖泊和整洁的砾石小径环绕着鲜艳的花坛的公共公园。

The landing was less than perfect. They hit the grass so hard they drove great muddy tracks in it, and Remus was finally thrown from the saddle altogether (though he was so relieved to be back on solid ground he could have kissed the grass). 着陆并不完美。他们重重地撞在草地上，留下了大大的泥迹，Remus最终完全被从座位上抛下（尽管他非常高兴能回到坚实的地面上，甚至想吻一吻草地）。

“Bugger,” Sirius said, cutting the engine and leaping off gracefully, “I’ll get better at that bit - you ok?” He held out a hand to help Remus up. “该死，”Sirius说，切断了发动机，优雅地跃下车，“我会在这方面做得更好——你没事吧？”他伸出手来帮Remus站起来。

“Fine, I think,” Remus brushed his trousers and arms. “Where are we?” “没事，我想，”Remus拍了拍裤子和手臂。“我们在哪里？”

“Highbury Fields.” Sirius cast obfuscate on the bike and then did his best to mend the ruined lawn. “I used to come here a lot before I left home.” “Highbury Fields。”Sirius对摩托车施了隐形咒，然后尽力修复被毁坏的草坪。“我以前离家之前经常来这里。”

“Oh, right,” Remus said, softly, “With Reg?” “哦，是吗，”Remus柔声说，“和Reg一起？”

“Sometimes,” Sirius sniffed, “Our governess brought us.” “有时候，”Sirius抽泣道，“我们的家庭教师带我们来的。”

Remus decided to store away this new revelation that Sirius had had a governess for another time. Remus决定将Sirius有家庭教师这个新的发现留待以后再谈。

“It’s nice,” he said, looking around at the lush green parkland, “Pretty. Want to show me around?” “这里不错，”他说，环顾四周的郁郁葱葱的公园，“很漂亮。想给我展示一下吗？”

Sirius smiled at him gratefully, and they went for a quiet Sunday afternoon walk. Here and there Sirius would stop and point something out - a tree he had climbed once, or a bridge he’d hidden under. Remus enjoyed listening. He had rarely heard any happy childhood memories from Sirius, and for a little while he even forgot why they were there. Sirius感激地对他笑了，他们进行了一次安静的周日下午散步。在这里，Sirius会停下来指着某些地方——他曾爬过的一棵树，或者他曾藏身的桥梁。Remus喜欢听这些。他很少听到Sirius的快乐童年记忆，暂时甚至忘记了他们为什么在这里。

They stopped by the war memorial. It was particularly fancy - Remus supposed because there was a fair bit of money in Islington. Atop the white plinth stood the green-hued statue of a young woman in ancient robes, holding aloft a laurel crown. An allegory for victory. 他们停在战争纪念碑旁边。这座纪念碑特别华丽——Remus猜测这是因为Islington有不少钱。白色基座上站着一尊绿色调的古代长袍年轻女性的雕像，举着桂冠。这是胜利的象征。

“I did my first magic here.” Sirius said with a grin, “When I was four.” “我第一次施魔法就在这里。”Sirius带着笑容说，“当我四岁的时候。”

“Really? What did you do?” “真的？你做了什么？”

“Set fire to her head,” he nodded at the statue. “Always been a rebel.” “点燃了她的头，”他指着雕像说道。“一直是个叛逆者。”

“Amazing,” Remus laughed. “太棒了，”Remus笑道。

“Yeah, Douceline - our governess - went mad trying to put it out. But we kept laughing, me and Reggie, and every time she extinguished it I just did it again, because it made him so happy.” “是的，Douceline——我们的家庭教师——试图扑灭火焰时疯了。但我和Reggie却一直在笑，每次她熄灭了火焰，我就再点燃一次，因为这让他很开心。”

Sirius looked down. He was quiet for a while, and Remus just put a hand on his shoulder, to show that he didn’t have to speak, if he didn’t want to. Sirius低下了头。他沉默了一会儿，Remus只是把手放在他的肩膀上，以示他可以选择不说话，如果他不愿意的话。

They looked at the plaque on the memorial. How sleep the brave who sink to rest, By all their country’s wishes bless’d. Remus couldn’t help but wonder about the names of the men listed below. How old had they been? Robert Fenn, Peter Cross, Arthur Hill… Had they all thought they were doing the right thing? Had they all been brave in their last moments? Had they thought of their family, their brothers? 他们看着纪念碑上的铭文。如何在所有国家的祝福中沉睡的勇士。Remus忍不住想那些下面列出的名字。这些人曾经多大年纪？Robert Fenn, Peter Cross, Arthur Hill……他们是否都认为自己在做正确的事？他们是否在最后的时刻表现出勇敢？他们是否想过他们的家人，他们的兄弟？

And when this war was over, would there be a plaque just like this in Diagon Alley? Whose names would it bear? Not Regulus’s. 当这场战争结束时，Diagon Alley会有一块这样的铭牌吗？上面会刻上谁的名字？不会是Regulus的名字。

“Come on.” Sirius said, finally. “I’m ready to go home, now.” “走吧。”Sirius终于说。“我现在准备回家了。”

Notes:The chapter title is from the Wilfred Owen poem of the same name, which itself is taken from Horace.

Friday 7th September 1979

 “Uuurrgh, bugger!” Remus groaned, cradling his shoulder and biting his lip. “唔呃，该死！”Remus呻吟道，捧着肩膀咬着嘴唇。

 

Padfoot came bounding over, yapped, then transformed back into Sirius, “帕德弗特”跳跃过来，吠了一声，然后变回了Sirius，“怎么了？”

“What’s up?” “怎么了？”

“Dislocated.” Remus grimaced, still clutching his arm. “Have you got my wand?” “脱臼了。”Remus面露痛苦之色，仍旧抓着自己的手臂。“你拿到我的魔杖了吗？”

“Yeah, hang on...” “是的，稍等一下……”

“All right, Moony?” James and Peter came sauntering out of the thicket. “That was great!” “没事吧，Moony？”James和Peter从灌木丛中悠闲地走出来。“真棒！”

“Yeah, great…” Remus accepted his wand from Sirius and pointed it at his sore arm. He thought about Livia and Castor, as he did every full moon since meeting the pack. He hoped they were both safe, and he sort of wished he had them nearby, just for the healing benefits. “是的，很棒……”Remus接过Sirius递来的魔杖，指向他疼痛的手臂。他想到了Livia和Castor，就像他在每个月圆之夜见到狼群时那样。他希望他们都平安，也有点希望他们能在身边，以便疗愈。

Arm fixed - or as close as he could get it, he struggled to his feet and pulled on his clothes, stashed under a nearby bush. “手臂修好了——或者说尽可能地修好了，他挣扎着站起来，穿上了藏在附近灌木丛下的衣服。

“Ok?” Sirius asked, watching him warily, “You look a bit shaky.” “好了吗？”Sirius小心翼翼地看着他，“你看起来有点不稳。”

“Just hurts a bit,” Remus said, having to stop himself from shrugging, “Can I side-along with you to get back?” “只是有点疼，”Remus说，努力阻止自己耸肩，“我能跟你一起回去吗？”

“Of course. Oi, Prongs,” Sirius nudged James with his elbow, grinning, “Bloody good stag do, eh? Eh?? Stag do?!” “当然可以。喂，Prongs，”Sirius用肘子碰了碰James，笑着说，“真是棒极了的单身派对，对吧？对吧？？单身派对？！”

“Yes, Padfoot, very funny,” James snorted, “Just as funny as the last hundred times.” “是的，Padfoot，非常搞笑，”James嗤笑道，“就像过去一百次一样搞笑。”

“I’m wasted on you lot,” Sirius sighed. “我对你们这些人真是白费力气，”Sirius叹了口气。

“Less than twenty-four hours to go!” Peter said, “How are you feeling?” “不到二十四小时了！”Peter说，“你感觉怎么样？”

“Tired.” James said, with a yawn. “Shall we?” “累。”James说道，打了个哈欠。“我们走吧？”

They apparated back to the Potters’, which was already a hive of activity. They’d hired four extra house elves in preparation for the wedding the next day, and the tiny little creatures darted back and forth across the kitchen whipping up a feast. 他们瞬间移动回了Potter家，那里已经是一个忙碌的蜂巢。他们雇佣了四个额外的家养小精灵来为第二天的婚礼做准备，那些小小的生物在厨房里来回飞奔，准备丰盛的宴席。

Lily and Mrs Potter were sitting at the kitchen table - Mrs Potter in her dressing gown and slippers, which she was never out of these days. Lily jumped up to kiss James, “Morning darling - I just stayed long enough to see you, but I’ll be off now. How are you, Remus?” Lily和Mrs Potter坐在厨房的桌子旁——Mrs Potter穿着她的睡袍和拖鞋，这些天她几乎没离开过这些衣服。Lily跳起来亲吻James，“早安，亲爱的——我只是呆了足够长的时间看你，但我现在要走了。你怎么样，Remus？”

Remus nodded, blank and exhausted. “Remus点头，神情呆滞且疲惫。”

Lily cocked her head and tutted, “Go to bed, the lot of you, you all need your beauty sleep. James, I’ve left you a list of things you need to get sorted this afternoon - give me a ring when it’s all finished or I’ll never sleep. Sirius, did he give you the rings? Oh no, silly me, I’ve got them, here you go… Remus, will you make sure he doesn't lose them? Pete, your mum popped round and I said you’d gone out with the lads and were sleeping off a hangover, so better if you don’t go home. I’m sending Mary over this evening with the buttonholes for you all, and the ties if Madam Malkin hurries up and gets them finished… oooh, do you all have shoes?!” “Lily歪了歪头，啧了一声，“都去睡觉吧，你们都需要美容觉。James，我给你留了一份下午需要整理的事项清单——全部完成后给我打电话，否则我无法入睡。Sirius，他给你戒指了吗？哦不，傻我，我有它们，这里给你……Remus，你能确保他不会丢失吗？Pete，你的妈妈来了，我说你和小伙子们出去解酒了，所以最好不要回家。我今晚会送Mary过来，给你们所有人带上胸花，还有领带，如果Madam Malkin赶紧做完……哦，你们都穿鞋了吗？！”

“Merlin, Evans,” Sirius yawned, “Anyone would think you’re getting married tomorrow.” “天啊，Evans，”Sirius打了个哈欠，“谁都以为你明天要结婚呢。”

She stuck her tongue out at him, kissed James, hugged Remus and hurried out the door. “她对他吐了吐舌头，亲吻了James，拥抱了Remus，然后匆忙离开了。”

“Go to bed, boys!” She shouted, as she left. “See you at the top of the aisle, Potter!” “去睡觉，孩子们！”她离开时喊道。“在过道顶端见，Potter！”

Remus looked down at the list Lily had left James - it was at least fifteen inches of parchment, and Lily had small handwriting. James ignored it, “Remus低头看了看Lily留给James的清单——那是一张至少十五英寸的羊皮纸，Lily的字迹很小。James没有理会它，

“Alright, mum?” He said, going over to Mrs Potter. She had two dark smudges under her eyes, and her hair was pale and stringy. Remus was finding it hard to meet her eye, these days - she reminded him so much of his last visit with Hope. ““好的，妈妈？”他说，走向Mrs Potter。她眼下有两个黑色的污迹，头发苍白而稀疏。Remus发现自己很难与她对视，这些天她让他想起了上次见Hope时的情景。

“Fine, fine,” She beamed up at him, “There’s so much to do!” ““没事，没事，”她对他笑道，“有很多事情要做！”

“Leave it for now,” he said, an arm around her, “Let’s all go to bed…” “先放下吧，”他说，搂着她，“我们都去睡觉吧……”

“That Lily,” Mrs Potter said as they all made slow progress up the stairs, “She’s a force to be reckoned with.” “那Lily，”Mrs Potter一边慢慢地走上楼梯一边说道，“她真是个不可忽视的力量。”

“Too right.” The boys all agreed. “完全正确。”男孩们都同意道。

Remus collapsed into bed without even taking his clothes off, and could have fallen asleep right there. “Remus没有脱下衣服就倒在床上，简直可以马上入睡。”

“Moony,” Sirius yawned again, pulling his boots off, “Don’t conk out until you’ve had your potion, McKinnon’s orders.” “Moony，”Sirius再次打了个哈欠，脱下靴子，“在喝完药水之前不要睡着，McKinnon的命令。”

“Mmmph.” Remus groaned, rolling over and reaching for the bottle on the bedside table. Sirius clambered in beside him as he finished it. “嗯哼。”Remus呻吟着，翻身去拿床头柜上的药瓶。Sirius爬到他身边，他喝完药水。

“Whose idea was it to have a wedding right after a full moon?!” He complained, another yawn encroaching. “谁的主意是在满月之后办婚礼？！”他抱怨道，又一个哈欠涌上。

“I told you all to just leave me to it,” Remus replied, closing his eyes and flinging an arm over his face. “我告诉你们都放手不管，”Remus回答道，闭上眼睛，将手臂搭在脸上。

“And miss the chance to make ‘stag do’ puns for the rest of the week? No chance.” “错过了在接下来的一周内做‘单身派对’双关语的机会？没门。”

Remus chuckled and quickly fell asleep. “Remus笑了笑，很快就入睡了。”

* * *

 

Having never attended a wedding in his life, Remus was very grateful to Lily for having left a list. It meant he always knew what to do. However, he quickly learnt that very little about weddings made any sense at all. For example, once they’d all woken up around midday, their first task was to decorate the quidditch hoops in the back garden. 从未参加过婚礼的Remus非常感激Lily留下的清单。这意味着他总是知道该做什么。然而，他很快发现婚礼的很多事情根本没有任何意义。例如，他们中午醒来后的第一个任务是装饰后花园里的魁地奇球门。

“Why are we doing this?” Remus asked, frowning up at the goals, as Peter arrived levitating a crate of white flowers. “为什么我们要做这个？”Remus皱着眉头看着球门，Peter漂浮着一箱白花走过来时问道。

“So they look nice,” James replied, broom in hand. “It’s the only way Lily would get married under them.” “为了让它们看起来好看，”James手拿扫帚回答。“这是Lily唯一会在它们下面结婚的方式。”

Remus stared at him, “You’re getting married under your old quidditch hoops?!” Remus盯着他，“你要在你旧的魁地奇球门下结婚？！”

“I know!” He grinned, “Brilliant, isn’t?!” “我知道！”他咧嘴笑道，“很棒，不是吗？！”

“Err…” “呃……”

“Moony,” Sirius said quickly, “You and Pete work on the growing charm down here, Prongs and I will fly up and do the hoops.” “Moony，”Sirius快速说道，“你和Pete在下面施生长咒，Prongs和我会飞上去装饰球门。”

Once they were finished, the three goal posts looked like a bizarre spindly rose bush had tried to take over. Next they had to decorate the nearby trees with the same flowers, and summon all of the chairs from the Potters’ extensive attic, then get them to line up neatly in rows of eight. After that, Mrs Potter asked Peter and Sirius to help her with all of the crockery for the reception, and gave James and Sirius instructions to ‘sort out the ballroom’. 完成后，这三个球门看起来像是奇怪的细长玫瑰灌木想要占据它们。接下来，他们必须用同样的花装饰附近的树木，并从Potter家宽敞的阁楼里召唤所有的椅子，然后让它们整齐地排成八排。之后，Mrs Potter让Peter和Sirius帮她整理招待会用的所有餐具，并让James和Sirius“整理舞厅”。

“Ballroom?!” Remus looked at James, confused. He’d been visiting the Potters’ for years now, and felt he knew the house pretty well - but he’d never seen a ballroom. “舞厅？！”Remus困惑地看着James。他已经来Potter家多年了，觉得自己很了解这栋房子——但他从未见过舞厅。

“Yeah, we don’t use it much,” James replied casually, “Keep it in storage.” “是的，我们不常用它，”James随意回答，“把它存放起来。”

“In… storage?” How on earth you ‘stored’ an entire room, Remus did not know. “存放起来？”Remus不知道你如何“存放”一整个房间。

“Yup, I just need to remember where the instructions are…” “是的，我只需要记得说明书在哪里……”

They went into James’s dad’s study, and James located a map inside one of the desk drawers. Remus got quite interested then - he would always be very fond of maps. This one was a blueprint for the Potters’ mansion, which made it extra fascinating. There were all kinds of special little spells and enchantments labelled on it, but they had work to do, so he couldn’t get a good look. 他们进入James父亲的书房，James在其中一个抽屉里找到了地图。Remus立刻感兴趣了——他一直很喜欢地图。这是一张Potter庄园的蓝图，格外引人入胜。上面标注了各种特殊的小咒语和魔法，但他们还有工作要做，所以他不能仔细看。

The ballroom was hidden behind the living room couch. James and Remus both had to concentrate very hard and murmur some ancient incantations to get the doors to appear. Then, of course, the couch had to be moved and the door unlocked, which was annoyingly fiddly. 舞厅藏在客厅沙发后面。James和Remus都得非常专注地默念一些古老的咒语才能让门出现。然后，当然，必须移动沙发并解锁门，这非常烦人。

When James finally pushed the oak panelled double-doors open, Remus’s jaw dropped. It was one of the most beautiful rooms he had ever seen; art deco marble pillars as far as the eye could see, and a glorious stained glass ceiling which cast jewel coloured patches of sunlight onto the dark hardwood floor. 当James终于推开镶有橡木面板的双扇门时，Remus的下巴掉了下来。这是他见过的最美丽的房间之一；极尽奢华的装饰艺术大理石柱子延展到视线尽头，辉煌的彩绘玻璃天花板将宝石色的阳光斑点洒在黑暗的硬木地板上。

“Bloody hell.” He swallowed, feeling very small. He remembered watching Sirius and Lily rehearsing dance steps in their tiny living room, and for the first time in a long time Remus felt very poor and grubby next to his wealthy pureblood friends. “该死。”他咽了咽口水，感觉自己很渺小。他记得看着Sirius和Lily在他们小小的客厅里排练舞步，这是很久以来第一次，Remus在他富有的纯血朋友旁边感到自己非常贫穷和肮脏。

“I know,” James laughed, “Stupid, isn’t it? But y’know, at least we’ll fit everyone in. I think we’ve got thirty-three Weasleys coming already.” “我知道，”James笑了，“很傻，不是吗？但你知道，至少我们能容纳所有人。我想我们已经有三十三个Weasley要来了。”

Feeling a bit better, Remus set about helping James check the room, and then they conjured some mops to begin cleaning the floor. James closed the doors while they did this, so that they would not be disturbed, “好了一点后，Remus开始帮James检查房间，然后他们召唤了一些拖把开始清理地板。James在他们这样做时关上了门，以免被打扰，

“I know we’re not really doing anything,” he said guiltily, leaning against a marble column, “But I just want five minutes without someone giving me an order. I wouldn’t mind, but Moody’s only giving us two days off for the wedding - we’re expected to report for duty on Sunday.” “我知道我们实际上没在做什么，”他内疚地说，靠在大理石柱子上，“但我只想有五分钟不被人指使。我倒不介意，但Moody只给我们两天的婚假——我们预期周日要报到。”

“Christ,” Remus shook his head, tutting. They stood quietly for a bit, watching the mops glide back and forth like funny skinny ballroom dancers. Remus was grateful for a breather, too. The weekend had begun with a full moon, and was only going to get more hectic as it went on. “天啊，”Remus摇了摇头，啧啧地说。他们安静地站了一会儿，看着拖把来回滑动，像有趣的瘦长舞厅舞者。Remus也很感激这次喘息的机会。这个周末从满月开始，随着时间的推移只会变得更加忙碌。

“How’s Sirius?” James asked, out of the blue. “Sirius怎么样？”James突然问道。

“Eh? Fine. Why?” Remus frowned. “嗯？很好。为什么？”Remus皱眉。

“Just checking.” “只是确认一下。”

“You see him almost as much as I do.” Remus teased him. It was true - James was much keener on the flying motorbike than Remus was, and they went for rides together almost every evening. “你见他的次数几乎和我一样多。”Remus取笑他。这是真的——James对飞行摩托车的热情比Remus高多了，他们几乎每天晚上都一起去骑行。

“I know,” James nodded, “But he hasn’t said anything about Regulus since… well, since he died.” “我知道，”James点头，“但自从……好吧，自从他去世后，他就没有说过关于Regulus的任何事。”

“No.” Remus sighed, “No, he hasn’t.” “没有。”Remus叹气，“没有，他没有。”

It wasn’t as if Remus had been pushing Sirius to talk about it, either - but he didn’t think James would understand their policy of never discussing family stuff. 也不是说Remus一直在催Sirius谈论这件事——但他不认为James会理解他们从不讨论家庭事务的政策。

“I don’t like him bottling it up,” James said, “I know he had a complicated relationship with Reg, but it can’t be normal to just pretend like he never existed.” “我不喜欢他把事情憋在心里，”James说，“我知道他和Regulus的关系很复杂，但假装他从未存在过肯定不正常。”

“Who’s to say what’s normal?” Remus countered, “Everyone grieves differently.” “谁能说什么是正常的？”Remus反驳道，“每个人哀悼的方式都不同。”

“So he is grieving?” James was giving Remus a very intense look, and it made him uncomfortable. He didn’t like other people asking him about Sirius’s personal stuff - that was between them. “所以他在哀悼？”James用一种非常强烈的目光看着Remus，这让他感到不舒服。他不喜欢别人问他关于Sirius的私人事情——那是他们之间的事。

“Yeah, of course.” He lied. That seemed to work. “是的，当然。”他撒了谎。这似乎奏效了。

“Good. I’ve been worried about him, it’s been a shit year all round, eh?” “好。我一直担心他，这一年真是糟透了，不是吗？”

“Could say that,” Remus snorted. “It’s about to get a lot better though. Any pre-game nerves?” “可以这么说，”Remus哼了一声。“不过情况即将好转。有赛前紧张吗？”

“Nah,” James grinned, the worry leaving his face, “Feel like I’ve already won the cup.” “没有，”James咧嘴笑了，脸上的担忧消失了，“感觉我已经赢得了杯赛。”

“Oh my god Prongs, you soppy git. That’s what you get for going out with girls.” “天哪Prongs，你这个多愁善感的家伙。这就是你和女生约会的结果。”

James roared with laughter, and by the time he had regained his composure the mops had finished their task, and the floor was gleaming as if brand new. James大笑起来，当他恢复镇定时，拖把已经完成了任务，地板闪闪发光，仿佛是全新的。

* * *

Saturday 8th September 1979

 

 

The first wedding Remus ever attended was the most beautiful and the happiest - and there was no way you could convince him otherwise. Everything went off without a hitch (well, he did have to talk an overexcited Sirius out of transforming into Padfoot to deliver the rings, but luckily it was only a fleeting mania), and it was smiles all around. Remus参加的第一个婚礼是最美丽、最幸福的——不管怎么说，你都不能说服他认为其他的更好。一切都很顺利（嗯，他确实要劝说过度兴奋的Sirius不要变成Padfoot来递戒指，但幸运的是，这只是短暂的疯狂），每个人都在微笑。

James’s parents looked as though they would burst with pride, both appearing healthier than Remus had seen them in ages, decked out in red and gold dress robes - Gryffindor colours. Marlene and Mary made beautiful bridesmaids in simple pale mauve dresses with circlets of gypsophila in their hair, and of course Lily herself was a vision in white lace. James的父母看起来似乎要因自豪而爆炸，他们看起来比Remus见过的健康多了，穿着红色和金色的礼袍——格兰芬多的颜色。Marlene和Mary穿着简单的淡紫色礼服，头上戴着满天星花环，成为美丽的伴娘，当然Lily本人则穿着白色蕾丝礼服，宛如仙境中的美景。

It seemed to Remus that the day flew by in a pastel-hued blur. He was always supposed to be somewhere, or doing something; there was barely a moment to relax and take stock. He was very glad that he’d never be getting married because just being a groomsman was exhausting enough. 对Remus来说，这一天似乎在柔和的色彩模糊中飞逝。他总是应该在某个地方，或做某件事；几乎没有时间放松和反思。他很高兴自己永远不会结婚，因为仅仅是做个伴郎就已经够累了。

Once the ceremony was over and they had to start mingling, Remus found himself feeling very shy. He hadn’t been around so many wizards and witches since Hogwarts - the magic in the air was palpable; muggy. It bothered him less now. His time with Greyback’s pack had taught him to cope with it, and as long as he didn’t need to do magic, he was fine. 仪式结束后，他们不得不开始与人交往，Remus发现自己感到非常害羞。自霍格沃茨以来，他从未在这么多巫师和女巫中间过——空气中的魔法是显而易见的；湿热的。现在他不再那么烦恼了。他与Greyback的狼群一起度过的时间教会了他如何应对，只要他不需要施魔法，他就没问题。

There were plenty of people he knew, of course. He spotted the Weasleys without too much bother; Arthur and Molly were running around all over the place after their five rambunctious redheaded sons; the eldest two had decided they wanted to play quidditch with the decorated hoops now that the boring bit of the day was over. 当然，有很多他认识的人。他很快就找到了Weasleys；Arthur和Molly在他们五个活泼的红发儿子后面跑来跑去；最大的两个决定现在无聊的部分已经结束，他们想用装饰好的球门打魁地奇。

Then, of course, there were Moody and Hagrid and Dumbledore, and lots of other people from the Order. It was nice to see them all at a happy event for once; it made everyone look younger. Frank and Alice were just back from their honeymoon - which Alice confided to Remus had actually involved quite a lot of work; they’d gone to Slovenia on a knowledge transfer mission with the local Aurors. 然后，当然，还有Moody、Hagrid和Dumbledore，以及很多来自凤凰社的其他人。很高兴能看到他们都在一次愉快的活动中；这让每个人看起来都更年轻。Frank和Alice刚刚从蜜月回来——Alice向Remus透露，他们实际上做了很多工作；他们去了斯洛文尼亚，与当地的傲罗进行知识转移任务。

And of course Ferox was there. He came over to shake Remus’s hand manfully, “Looking very smart, Lupin,” he nodded, and Remus felt himself blush head to toe - though he knew Sirius looked a million times better in exactly the same robes. “And Ms. McDonald,” Ferox kissed her hand, which made her blush too, “Very beautiful indeed. Will it be wedding bells for you two, next?” 当然，Ferox也在那儿。他过来硬朗地握了Remus的手，“看起来很帅气，Lupin，”他点点头，Remus感觉自己从头到脚都在脸红——虽然他知道Sirius穿着同样的礼服看起来好一百万倍。“还有McDonald小姐，”Ferox吻了她的手，这也让她脸红，“你们两个会是下一个结婚的人吗？”

Remus blinked - he hadn’t come out to very many people, fair enough, but he sort of thought most people had cottoned on by now. Mary laughed, “As if Remus would marry me! I’d drive him up the wall!” Remus眨了眨眼——他没有向很多人出柜，公平地说，但他觉得大多数人现在应该都明白了。Mary笑了，“Remus怎么会娶我！我会把他逼疯的！”

“Ah well,” Ferox clapped him on the shoulder, “You’re still young. Lots of wild oats to sow.” “啊，好吧，”Ferox拍了拍他的肩膀，“你还年轻。有很多野心要播种。”

“I live with Sirius,” Remus said, raising his eyebrows a little bit to see if his old teacher took the hint. But apparently not. Why were grownups always so dense? “我和Sirius住在一起，”Remus说，稍微扬起眉毛，看他以前的老师是否明白。但显然没有。为什么大人总是这么迟钝？

“Free-wheeling bachelors, eh?” Ferox laughed gruffly. Mary looked as though she was about to say something, but Remus caught her eye and gave the tiniest shake of his head. Not worth it. “自由自在的单身汉，是吧？”Ferox粗声笑道。Mary看起来似乎要说些什么，但Remus看了她一眼，微微摇了摇头。不值得。

“That’s right,” he nodded enthusiastically at Ferox. “没错，”他热情地对Ferox点点头。

After dinner (the best part of the day, in Remus’s opinion) Lily and James cut the cake - a huge towering affair with thirteen tiers covered in buttercream icing and pink piped roses - and then the dancing began. 晚餐后（在Remus看来是一天中最好的部分）Lily和James切蛋糕——一个巨大的高耸蛋糕，有十三层，上面覆盖着奶油糖霜和粉色管状玫瑰——然后开始跳舞。

Lily did Sirius proud - Remus could hear him counting under his breath as he watched them; “One two three, one two three… straighten that back, Evans! Good girl…” Lily让Sirius感到骄傲——Remus可以听到他在看着他们时小声数数；“一二三，一二三……挺直背，Evans！好女孩……”

The waltz over and done with, someone cast an amplifying charm on the Potters’ old turntable, and a Bad Company song began playing, which got all of the young people up and dancing - including Sirius, who Remus was grateful to hand over to Andromeda. Remus Lupin did not dance. 华尔兹结束后，有人对Potter家的旧唱机施了一个放大咒，然后开始播放一首Bad Company的歌，这让所有的年轻人都站起来跳舞——包括Sirius，Remus很高兴将他交给Andromeda。Remus Lupin不跳舞。

He was happy enough to sit by with a glass of champagne just watching, as usual. He looked for Peter, who liked to dance but often lost steam after a few songs, but couldn’t see him anywhere. He’d probably found some friends from work and gone to chat with them. Yaz and Marlene were on the dancefloor - they were both pretty dreadful, Marene wasn’t used to heels - but it was very sweet all the same. Yaz had cut her hair since leaving Hogwarts in June, and the cropped pixie look really suited her. 他很高兴能像往常一样坐在一旁，手拿一杯香槟观看。他找Peter，他喜欢跳舞，但几首歌后经常失去劲头，但哪里都找不到他。他可能找了一些工作上的朋友去聊天了。Yaz和Marlene在舞池里——他们两个都很糟糕，Marlene不习惯高跟鞋——但这很甜蜜。自从六月离开霍格沃茨后，Yaz剪了头发，精灵般的短发非常适合她。

Mary came to Remus’s rescue, in the end, as always. She hobbled over with a pained expression on her face and plonked down beside him. 最后，Mary像往常一样来救Remus。她带着痛苦的表情一瘸一拐地走过来，坐在他旁边。

“Blimey, these French knickers she’s got us in go right up your bum.” “天哪，她给我们穿的这些法国内裤直接插进了屁股。”

“Charming as ever, MacDonald,” Remus smirked. “一如既往地迷人，MacDonald，”Remus笑道。

James and Lily whirled past them, smiling at each other like maniacs. James和Lily旋转着从他们身边经过，像疯子一样互相微笑。

“Look at them,” Mary sighed. “Why can’t I find a bloke who loves me that much, eh? Not like I haven’t been looking.” “看看他们，”Mary叹了口气。“为什么我找不到一个如此爱我的男人，嗯？不是说我没在找。”

“You’ll find him,” Remus replied, just as happy. “你会找到他的，”Remus同样开心地回答。

“I’ll know it when I see it, that's what my mum says.” “见到的时候我就会知道，这是我妈妈说的。”

“If you’re lucky,” Remus snorted. He was a bit drunker than he’d initially thought, and his tongue was loose. But it was only Mary. “They say ‘love is blind’ for a reason.” “如果你幸运的话，”Remus哼了一声。他比最初想象的要醉一些，舌头也松了。但这只是Mary。“他们说‘爱情是盲目的’是有原因的。”

“I never had trouble recognising it, to be honest.” Mary confided. “It’s letting it in, that's the hard part.” “说实话，我从来没有认不出来。”Mary坦言。“让它进来，才是最难的部分。”

Remus nodded in agreement, though he wasn’t sure he followed. She continued, sipping her champagne. “Like you did, with Sirius.” Remus点头表示同意，尽管他不确定是否明白。她继续喝着香槟。“就像你和Sirius一样。”

“Oh yeah, my freewheeling bachelor friend.” Remus poked his tongue out, making Mary crease up, giggling. Remus grinned, happy to make her happy. He squeezed her knee, “You’re going to fall in love one day, how could you not? Anyone would be lucky to have you.” “哦，是的，我自由自在的单身朋友。”Remus伸出舌头，逗得Mary笑弯了腰。Remus咧嘴一笑，乐于让她开心。他捏了捏她的膝盖，“你总有一天会坠入爱河，怎么可能不呢？任何人拥有你都会很幸运。”

“Maybe once the war is over.” She said, lowering her voice, still watching the dancing. “I’m not sure I could survive falling in love right now, not with everything else on top.” “也许战争结束后。”她低声说，仍然看着舞蹈。“现在，我不确定我能在这所有的事情之上幸存下来。”

“Mm.” Remus looked away. “嗯。”Remus看向别处。

“Hiya,” Marlene appeared, drink in hand, “Remus, your boyfriend stole my partner.” She nodded across the dancefloor at Sirius and Yaz, who were swinging each other around wildly, apparently unable to decide who should lead. “嗨，”Marlene出现了，手里拿着饮料，“Remus，你的男朋友抢走了我的舞伴。”她点头示意舞池对面的Sirius和Yaz，他们疯狂地互相旋转，显然无法决定谁应该领舞。

Remus laughed, and Mary frowned, shifting uncomfortably in her seat. Marlene gave her a sympathetic look, “French knickers?” Mary nodded, wearily. Marlene leaned in and whispered, “I took mine off in the loos after the ceremony.” Remus笑了，Mary皱着眉，不舒服地在座位上移动。Marlene给了她一个同情的眼神，“法国内裤？”Mary疲倦地点点头。Marlene靠近低声说，“仪式后我在厕所里脱了。”

“Oh my god McKinnon, you genius.” Mary sat up abruptly and strode across the room towards the doors. Marlene laughed, taking her seat. “哦我的天哪McKinnon，你真是个天才。”Mary突然坐起来，跨步走向房门。Marlene笑了，坐下了。

One of the Weasley kids came skidding past, sliding on his knees across the highly polished ballroom floor. Molly came chasing after him, panting, “WILLIAM ARTHUR WEASLEY YOU WILL RUIN THOSE TROUSERS!” 一个Weasley的孩子滑了过去，跪着滑过高抛光的舞厅地板。Molly气喘吁吁地追赶着，“WILLIAM ARTHUR WEASLEY，你会毁了那条裤子！”

Marlene giggled, covering her mouth with her hand politely. She leaned in and whispered to Remus, “I heard her tell Hattie Bones that she’s pregnant again - and she only just had twins last year!” Marlene咯咯笑着，用手礼貌地捂住嘴。她靠近Remus低声说，“我听她告诉Hattie Bones她又怀孕了——而她去年刚生了一对双胞胎！”

“Crikey.” Remus said, developing a whole new respect for quiet and reserved Arthur Weasley. “天啊。”Remus说，对安静而拘谨的Arthur Weasley产生了全新的敬意。

“I reckon those two are having kids as soon as possible.” Marlene nodded at James and Lily, “Be very surprised if we don’t get an announcement before Christmas.” “我想那两个人会尽快生孩子。”Marlene点头示意James和Lily，“如果圣诞节前没有宣布，我会很惊讶。”

“Oh…” Remus sighed. “Ok, but only because they haven’t served the cake yet.” “哦……”Remus叹了口气。“好吧，但只是因为他们还没上蛋糕。”

 

Chapter 167: The War: Winter 1979Summary:Finishing off 1979 with a few wintry evenings. This chapter (and likely the new few chapters) is really more a series of episodes to give a shape of Remus's life from 1979 onwards.

 

I wanna be straight! I wanna be straight!

Friday 23rd November 1979

 After all of the excitement of autumn, the beginning of winter felt remarkably unremarkable. Remus tried to be grateful for it; for once in his life, things were quiet. He didn’t get kidnapped by werewolves; there were no parents’ funerals or brothers dying. 经过秋天的所有兴奋，冬天的开始显得异常平淡。Remus尽量对此心存感激；他的生活中难得有安静的时候。他没有被狼人绑架；没有父母的葬礼或兄弟的死亡。

He tried to make himself useful to the Order. Sometimes they wanted things researched—help identifying curses that the Death Eaters were using, or coming up with new spells that could be used against them. He occasionally worked with Alice on this, and got to know her fairly well. She was incredibly intelligent, one of the most skilled duelists Remus had ever met. He got very good at defensive charms and spent a lot of time visiting various safehouses, setting up barriers and early warning systems. 他努力让自己对凤凰社有用。有时他们需要研究一些东西——帮助识别食死徒使用的诅咒，或者想出可以用来对抗他们的新咒语。他偶尔和Alice一起工作，并且相当了解她。她非常聪明，是Remus见过的最熟练的决斗者之一。他在防御咒语方面变得非常出色，并花了很多时间访问各个安全屋，设置屏障和预警系统。

Remus worked hard. He threw himself into it. He had a very strong desire to be involved, to strive for something good. Maybe he was growing up. Maybe he was just sick of having no control over his own life. Remus工作很努力。他全身心投入其中。他非常渴望参与，努力追求一些好的东西。也许他在成长。也许他只是厌倦了对自己的生活毫无控制。

Marlene came over a few evenings a week after work. She and Remus would sit up at the kitchen table, and he would tell her as much as he could about being a werewolf—his sense of smell, his increased metabolism, and how he cared for himself during and after a full moon. He tried to be as honest as he could without getting anyone else in trouble, and she diligently took notes, asked questions, and suggested improvements. Marlene每周有几个晚上下班后会过来。她和Remus会坐在厨房的桌子旁，Remus尽可能地告诉她关于狼人的一切——他的嗅觉、他的新陈代谢增加以及他在满月期间和之后如何照顾自己。他尽量诚实，不让别人陷入麻烦，她认真地做笔记，提出问题，并提出改进建议。

It was difficult for Remus, but also necessary. Marlene’s earnest nature and fierce determination to improve living standards for werewolves made him feel a bit better—like he might be doing some good after all. 对Remus来说，这很困难，但也是必要的。Marlene的诚挚性格和改善狼人生活水平的坚定决心让他感觉好多了——就像他毕竟在做一些好事。

“We need to get the Ministry away from this idea that cells and bars are the only remedy,” she would say, “From what you’ve told me, woodland is far better for the health of the subject—and we’re hardly short of woodland, are we? A few protective barrier spells would do it… all we need is some creative thinking, some compassion…” “我们需要让魔法部摆脱认为牢房和铁栏杆是唯一解决办法的想法，”她会说，“根据你告诉我的，森林对受试者的健康要好得多——而我们并不缺少森林，不是吗？几个保护屏障咒语就可以了……我们需要的是一些创造性的思维，一些同情心……”

Remus smiled at her. Marlene made him feel like there really would be change one day. And it was nice to spend time with a friend—Sirius was so often out in the evenings on missions or at meetings. Remus对她笑了。Marlene让他觉得有一天真的会有改变。而且和朋友一起度过时间也很好——天狼星经常在晚上执行任务或开会。

“How are you finding it, living with Sirius?” Marlene asked one evening as she was packing up. She looked around at the dark empty flat, “Quieter than my house.” “和天狼星一起住得怎么样？”Marlene有一天晚上收拾东西时问道。她环顾四周这间黑暗空荡的公寓，“比我家安静多了。”

Marlene was still living with her mother and step-dad, and Danny ever since he’d been bitten. More recently, Yaz had moved in too. Remus didn't know all the details, but it sounded as though Yaz’s parents hadn’t been thrilled when they found out about Marlene. Marlene仍然和她的母亲和继父一起住，还有自从被咬伤后的Danny。最近，Yaz也搬了进来。Remus不知道所有的细节，但听起来Yaz的父母在得知Marlene的事情后并不高兴。

“It's fine,” Remus nodded, helping her collect together her notes. “Different from school, obviously.” “很好，”Remus点点头，帮她收集笔记。“显然和学校不同。”

“Oh,” Marlene sighed, lowering her eyes. “Maybe it's just us then. Maybe because my family's around all the time.” “哦，”Marlene叹了口气，低下眼睛。“也许只是我们这样。也许因为我的家人一直在身边。”

And while it felt cathartic to admit that they were both struggling, there was nothing that could be done to improve things. People were still dying, the death eaters were still gaining power, Sirius and James were still super heroes. 这算不上是突破——他们仍然没有比真正需要的更多谈论战争——但那时感觉还不错。尽管承认他们都在挣扎感觉有些宣泄，但没有什么可以改善的。人们仍在死亡，食死徒仍在壮大，天狼星和James仍然是超级英雄。
