The men sniggered meanly, still advancing. One spoke to another, as if Grant and Remus were deaf—or just not worth addressing at all. 那些人恶意地窃笑着，仍在向前走。一个对另一个说话，仿佛Grant和Remus听不见——或者根本不值得理会。

“Looks like a couple’a nancy boys to me, couple’a dirty queers out looking for trouble.” “在我看来像是一对娘娘腔的家伙，一对肮脏的同性恋在寻衅滋事。”

“If they’re looking for trouble,” another said, “I know where they can get it.” He slammed his fist into his open hand, as if to demonstrate. “如果他们在找麻烦，”另一个人说，“我知道他们可以在哪里找到。”他将拳头重重地打在另一只手上，仿佛在演示。

“Remus…” Grant hissed, tugging on his coat, “Come on!” “Remus……”Grant低声说，拉扯着他的外套，“快走！”

Remus ignored him. He faced the three men, and raised his chin. Using his very politest private-school voice, he said, Remus无视了他。他面对着三个人，抬起下巴。用他非常礼貌的私立学校口吻说，

“Move along, gentlemen, before I do something you’ll regret.” “各位先生，离开吧，否则我会做一些你们会后悔的事情。”

The men crowed with laughter, and did not move alone. Remus was glad. His lips curled, he shifted position, legs apart, and stared them down. With a slight turn of his wrist, they froze to the spot. It took them a second to realise what had happened, their gormless faces now visible in the red light of a neon ‘SEXXX’ sign flashing in the shop window next to them. 那些人哈哈大笑，却没有离开。Remus很高兴。他的嘴角上翘，换了个姿势，双腿分开，目光直视着他们。他轻轻转动了一下手腕，他们立刻僵住了。他们花了一秒钟才意识到发生了什么，他们呆滞的脸庞在旁边商店闪烁的霓虹“SEXXX”标志的红光中变得清晰可见。

They stared at each other, tried to move their legs, but were fixed in place, as if they’d stepped into quick-setting concrete. 他们互相瞪着，试图移动双腿，但却像是踩进了快速凝固的混凝土中一样，无法动弹。

“What the fuck?!” One of them grunted angrily. “什么鬼？！”一个愤怒地咕哝道。

“Don’t be scared, boys,” Remus grinned, rather enjoying himself, “I don’t bite. Often.” “别怕，伙计们，”Remus带着笑容说，显然很享受这个过程，“我不会咬人。经常。”

“I’m gonna fucking batter ya, yer poof!” One of the men yelled, “I’m gonna beat the piss out of ya!” “我要他妈的揍扁你，你这娘们！”一个人吼道，“我要把你打得屁都没得拉！”

That gave Remus an excellent idea. He snapped his fingers quickly, and watched the men’s faces. One by one, a look of horror crossed each of them, and Remus caught the scent moments before their jeans began to visibly darken. 这给了Remus一个绝妙的主意。他迅速打了个响指，看着这些人的脸色。一个接一个，恐惧的表情出现在他们脸上，Remus在他们的牛仔裤开始明显变暗之前闻到了气味。

“Poor loves,” Remus chuckled. Even Grant stopped tugging his sleeve, then, and stared in disbelief. “可怜的小家伙们，”Remus笑着说。即使Grant也停止了拉扯他的袖子，目瞪口呆地看着。

“Have you pissed yourselves?!”

The three humiliated men started shouting insults then - each one worse than the last, but it didn’t matter. Remus and Grant were both practically hysterical.

“Come on,” Remus said, slinging an arm around Grant’s shoulder, “Let’s go.”

He did not release them until they were two streets away, locked inside the flat.

It was hugely risky, doing magic on a busy street in central London in front of muggles. But Remus couldn’t work himself up to feel guilty about it; he was jubilant. 在繁忙的伦敦市中心街道上对麻瓜施展魔法非常冒险。但Remus没法对这件事感到内疚；他感到非常高兴。

It didn’t seem like Grant understood what had happened—he was pretty drunk, and mostly just relieved to be safe, so Remus thought he’d got away with it. Back in the flat he cracked out the whisky to toast his own success—this was met with roaring approval from Grant. Grant似乎没明白发生了什么——他很醉，主要是对安全感到宽慰，所以Remus觉得他没事了。回到公寓后，他拿出威士忌来庆祝自己的成功——Grant对此大加赞赏。

Sirius wasn’t back yet, and Remus decided not to care about that, either. Most likely he’d decided to stay at the Potters’ for the night. Remus dug out some blankets and pillows to make up a bed on the couch for Grant, and then they settled in for another few hours of drinking and smoking and laughing. Sirius还没回来，Remus决定不去在意这个。很可能他决定在Potters家过夜。Remus找出了一些毯子和枕头，在沙发上铺成床，然后他们又喝酒、抽烟、笑了几个小时。时间开始扭曲；随着Remus的醉意加深，时间变得越来越伸缩不定。

It must have been almost two in the morning when they hit the bottom of the bottle. Remus ran his finger around the bottom of his glass tumbler, then sucked it. 当他们喝光了酒瓶底部时，可能已经快到凌晨两点了。Remus用手指沿着玻璃杯的底部转动，然后舔了舔。

“Ungh.” Grant whined from the sofa, “Gotta give up the booze. New year’s resolution.” “呃。”Grant从沙发上抱怨道，“得戒酒了。新年决心。”

“Ha.” Remus barked, slouching down in his armchair, rolling a cigarette. “哈。”Remus大笑着，靠在扶手椅上，卷着烟。

 

“Remusss?” Grant asked, dopily, his head lolling over the arm of the couch, blonde curls tumbling back from his upside-down face. “Remusss？”Grant傻乎乎地问，他的头垂在沙发的扶手上，金色的卷发从他倒立的脸上垂下。

“Yeah?” Remus slurred in response.

“Can I ask you summink?”

“Yeah.”

“‘ave you got a plan?”

“A plan?” Remus frowned, confused and bleary.

“For what you’re gonna do wiv your life, y’know.”

“Oh.” Remus scratched his head, arms slow and heavy. “I dunno. You?”

“Dunno.” Grant sighed. “Been thinking. Maybe I wanna just find a girl or summink. Get married.”

“Get married ?!” Remus choked. “Christ, you’re pissed.”

“It might not be awful!” Grant defended himself, “Don’t mind spending time wiv girls. They can be fun.”

“Yeah, but… y’know, if you got married you’d be expected to...” Remus gestured delicately. Grant snorted.萊姆斯小心翼翼地做了個手勢。格蘭特哼了一聲。

“She might not wanna do it much. Anyway, might not hate it. Never given it a try, ‘ave I?”

Remus put his fag between his teeth, thoughtfully. “I did, once.”

“Oh yeah?” Grant sat up interested, “And?”

 

“It was ok.” He shrugged, lighting up. “Not much to say about it really. Mostly just embarrassing. But we’re still friends and stuff.”

 

 

“Can’t be that bad then.” Grant sighed, leaning back once more. He looked sad, and Remus wished he knew how to cheer him up. Grant reached his hand out towards Remus, who sighed and handed him the newly lit cigarette. He began to roll another. “那就没那么糟糕了。”Grant叹了口气，再次靠回去。他看起来很伤心，Remus希望自己知道怎么让他开心起来。Grant伸出手向Remus要烟，Remus叹了口气，把刚点燃的香烟递给他，然后开始卷另一支。

Grant sighed, rolling his head back and blowing plumes of smoke up at the ceiling. “They just always let me down, that’s all. Men.” Grant叹了口气，把头仰回去，把烟雾吹向天花板。“他们总是让我失望，仅此而已。男人。”

“Not always,” Remus said, not liking the melancholy turn things were taking. “不总是这样，”Remus说，不喜欢事情变得如此忧郁的样子。

“No,” Grant replied wistfully, glancing up, meeting Remus’s eye, “No, I s’pose you never did.” “不，”Grant若有所思地回答，抬眼看向Remus，“不，我想你从未让我失望。”

Remus felt a flutter of warm pleasure at that—though maybe it was because he was just so drunk. Grant was still staring at him intensely, and smiling a bit now. Something passed between them. A very small thing; but something. Remus感到一阵温暖的愉悦——虽然也许是因为他喝得太醉了。Grant依然紧盯着他，现在微微地笑了笑。两人之间有了某种默契。很小的一点，但确实存在。

The door opened and Sirius entered, bringing the winter chill in with him. He stopped in his tracks when he saw Grant, who scrambled to sit up right. 门打开了，Sirius走了进来，把冬天的寒冷带了进来。当他看到Grant时，停下了脚步，Grant急忙坐直了身子。

“...hello.” Sirius said, eyes darting back and forth cautiously. Remus never had guests over—let alone muggles. “...你好。”Sirius说，眼睛小心翼翼地来回瞟动。Remus从未招待过客人——更不用说麻瓜了。

“Hiya mate!” Grant stood up quickly, extending a hand across the coffee table, the empty whisky bottle on top. Sirius shook it, politely. “嗨，朋友！”Grant迅速站起身，把手伸过咖啡桌，上面摆着空的威士忌瓶。Sirius礼貌地握了握手。

“Grant’s celebrating the end of his exams,” Remus explained, feeling guilty but not sure why. “Grant在庆祝期末考试结束，”Remus解释道，感到内疚但不确定原因。

“Oh, congratulations,” Sirius nodded, his expression guarded. “哦，恭喜，”Sirius点了点头，表情警惕。

“Cheers!” Grant grinned, “‘ave a drink? Oh bugger, we’ve ‘ad it all...” “干杯！”Grant笑道，“要不要喝一杯？哦，该死，我们已经喝光了...”

“It’s fine.” Sirius folded his arms across his chest and raised an eyebrow, putting on his bored aristocrat routine. “I’m going to bed.” “没关系。”Sirius把胳膊抱在胸前，抬起一只眉毛，摆出一副无聊贵族的样子。“我要去睡觉了。”

He didn’t give Remus so much as a second glance, just walked through the living room, down the hall to the bedroom. 他没再看Remus一眼，直接走过客厅，沿着走廊去卧室。

“‘Ave I got you in trouble?” Grant whispered. Remus shook his head,

“He’s just tired. I’d better…”

“Oh yeah, ‘course. I’m knackered, anyway - thanks again for letting me stay.”

“Any time.” Remus smiled, meaning it, “Thanks for inviting me out. I really needed it.” He patted Grant’s shoulder as he left.

Sirius was undressing. He ignored Remus, who closed the door quietly behind himself and sat on the end of the bed.

“How did the mission go?” He asked, gently, “Is James--”

“A muggle in the flat, Remus?!” Sirius snapped, “Did you even think about the danger?!”

“What danger?” Remus frowned, confused.

“There’s a war on! This place is supposed to be a safe house, it’s supposed to be locked down tighter than Gringotts!”

“Funny.” Remus said, flatly, “I thought it was supposed to be our home.”

Sirius didn’t respond, just glowered, tying the string on his pyjama bottoms. Remus rubbed the back of his neck, sighing, “Look, he lives in Brighton; I couldn’t have just abandoned him at a train station, he was plastered.” Remus tried to explain.

“So the solution was to get even more plastered?” Sirius shot back.“所以解決辦法就是塗更多的膏藥？”天狼星反擊。

“ Sonoro Quiescis .” Remus said, casting a silencing charm on the bedroom - the first time they’d needed it since Hogwarts. “If you want a fight,” he said, stretching his arms out invitingly, “Let’s go, I’m more than happy to oblige.” “如果你想打架，”他說道，並邀請地伸出雙臂，“我們走吧，我非常樂意效勞。”

“I don’t want to fight, I want to sleep.” Sirius said.

 

“Ok, fine.” Remus shrugged. He pulled off his jumper, t-shirt coming with it, and began changing for bed too. Sirius got in under the duvet and watched him, still scowling. He definitely did want a fight.天狼星鑽進羽絨被下面看著他，仍然皺著眉頭。他確實想打架。

“It’s Christmas.” Remus muttered, “Sorry if I wanted to squeeze a tiny bit of joy out of the season.”

“You couldn’t wait, could you? The second I left the house you had to--”

“You’re always leaving! Am I supposed to sit around worrying myself sick all night?! I still exist when you’re not here, you know, I still need to talk to people sometimes.”

“Ha!” Sirius scoffed, “You want someone to pour your heart out to, all of a sudden? That’s rich.” “哈！”Sirius冷笑道，“突然想找人倾诉？真是够讽刺的。”

“Go fuck yourself!” Remus yelled at the top of his voice. “去你妈的！”Remus用尽全力大喊。

“Go and fuck your muggle! That’s obviously what he’s here for!” Sirius shot back. Remus reeled as if he’d been struck. He stared at Sirius, and saw the hurt in his eyes. Was this all just boring old run-of-the-mill jealousy? “去操你的麻瓜吧！显然他就是为了这个来的！”Sirius反击道。Remus如同被击中般摇晃了一下。他盯着Sirius，看到他眼中的伤痛。这难道只是普通的嫉妒吗？

Remus forced himself to relax, to lower his shoulders and unclench his jaw. He closed his eyes, breathing in. Remus强迫自己放松，放下肩膀，放松下颚。他闭上眼睛，深吸了一口气。

“Grant’s on the couch because he’s my friend and I didn’t want any harm to come to him.” He said, very steadily. “And I’m in here with you, because there’s nobody else I’d rather be in a room with. Even when you’re being a massive tosser.” “Grant在沙发上因为他是我的朋友，我不想让他受到任何伤害。”他很平稳地说。“而我在这里陪着你，因为没有人比你更值得我待在一个房间里。即使你有时像个大混蛋。”

Sirius’s lips pursed, then relaxed. He looked very much like he wanted to keep arguing, but had nothing left to say. In the end he just slumped back in the bed, arms folded, and said to the ceiling, “You’re a massive tosser.” Sirius的嘴唇紧抿，然后放松。他看起来很想继续争论，但无话可说。最后他只是靠在床上，双臂交叉，望着天花板，说道，“你是个大混蛋。”

Remus laughed, finished changing, and climbed onto the bed, crawling towards Sirius. “我就是你的大混蛋。”他笑了，换好衣服，爬上床，向Sirius爬去。

“I’m your massive tosser.” He reached up for the edge of the duvet and pulled it down, peeling it back from Sirius’s body. Sirius allowed it, watching Remus, who started to untangle the knot of string on Sirius’s pyjama bottoms. He pulled those down next, and licked his lips. “Let me make it up to you?” “我是你的大混蛋。”他伸手拉开被子的一边，把它从Sirius的身体上拉下来。Sirius允许了，看着Remus开始解开Sirius睡裤上的绳结。他接着拉下睡裤，舔了舔嘴唇。“让我弥补一下好吗？”

Sirius bit his lip, nodded, then arched his back, and they didn’t speak again for hours. Sirius咬了咬嘴唇，点了点头，然后拱起背部，他们接下来的几个小时里再没说话。

In the morning, Grant had gone. 早晨时，Grant已经离开了。

British-isms

- Everything Grant says - I kind of write his speech phonetically, and he has a strong London accent (mostly dropping h's/turning 'th' sounds into 'v' sounds), so let me know if it's just impossible to understand and I'll soften it.

 

Chapter 168: The War: Spring & Summer 1980 

You know I'm born to lose,

and gambling's for fools.

But that's the way I like it baby

I don't wanna live forever

 

That January, just over a year after his mother’s funeral, Remus attended another memorial service - this time for Fleamont and Euphemia Potter.

 They passed away within hours of each other in the final bleak days of December. Their loss was felt immensely, and not only by the members of the Order. The Potter mansion was full for weeks with visitors, mourners and old friends, and every one of them had a story of some kindness James’s parents had performed.

 

“Euphemia always said I could ask her anything when I saw her at St Mungo’s.” Marlene sobbed, “She was such a brilliant healer, I wish I’d known her longer.” “Euphemia总是说，只要我在圣芒戈遇到她，就可以问她任何问题。”Marlene抽泣道，“她是如此出色的治疗师，我希望我能认识她更久一点。”

“They were so kind to us after we eloped,” Andromeda said, holding Ted’s hand and bouncing her daughter on her hip, “Checked in on us all the time, made sure we never struggled for anything… I just can’t believe they’re gone…” “我们私奔后，他们对我们非常好。”Andromeda说道，握着Ted的手，一边抱着女儿，“他们总是时刻关心我们，确保我们没有困难……我真的不敢相信他们已经离开了……”

“If our home is even half as welcoming as theirs, I’ll be proud.” Arthur Weasley added, cleaning his glasses, which had grown misty. “如果我们的家能有他们家的一半温馨，那我会感到自豪。”Arthur Weasley补充道，擦拭着已经起雾的眼镜。

“The very best of wizard kind,” Dumbledore intoned in the speech he gave at the service. “A beacon of understanding, tolerance, good humour and community - all those values we hold most dear.” “巫师界的最佳代表，”邓布利多在葬礼上说道。“理解、宽容、幽默和社区的灯塔——所有我们最珍视的价值观。”

“Sort of fitting to have them go at Christmas,” one wizened old crone said at the wake, “Always loved coming to the Potters’ boxing day party.” “他们在圣诞节离世似乎有些合适，”一个年迈的老太太在守夜时说，“总是喜欢去波特家的节礼日派对。”

“I’ll miss Effie’s mince pies!” An old man added. “我会怀念Effie的肉馅饼！”一个老人补充道。

“I’ll miss Monty’s home brew!” Another cackled. A smatter of fond laughter, followed by tender silence as everyone recalled the Potters’ limitless hospitality. “我会怀念Monty的自制啤酒！”另一个人笑道。大家回忆起波特家的无尽好客，笑声中夹杂着温柔的沉默。

Remus kept his own memories of the Potters to himself, because he felt he had the least claim on them. Still, he would never forget that it was they who had taken him in when he’d found himself homeless at seventeen, and they who had helped him locate his mother. Remus将自己对波特家的回忆藏在心中，因为他觉得自己最没有资格拥有这些回忆。尽管如此，他永远不会忘记是他们在他十七岁时无家可归时收留了他，也是在他们帮助他找到母亲。

In a way it was different from the earlier deaths in the Order, because the Potters had died at an advanced age, and they hadn’t been murdered - so there was more room for happy memories. 在某种程度上，这与之前在凤凰社中的死亡不同，因为波特夫妇是年长时去世的，并且他们并没有被谋杀——因此有更多的空间来怀念快乐的回忆。

It still didn’t feel very fair. Time is meaningless, when it comes to the people you love, Remus reflected. Eleven months had not been enough time with Hope - and twenty years had probably not been enough for James. 这仍然觉得不太公平。时间对你爱的人来说是毫无意义的，Remus反思道。与Hope度过的十一个月不够——而二十年可能对James来说也不够。

Sirius, Peter and Remus silently made the decision to pull together for James. He had been the source of the marauders’ strength ever since they were children; had selflessly defended or supported each of them at one time or another, and there was no question that they return the favour now, in his darkest hour. Sirius、Peter和Remus默默地决定团结起来支持James。他一直是捣蛋鬼们的力量源泉，从他们小时候开始；曾无私地保护或支持他们中的每一个人，如今在他最黑暗的时刻，他们理所当然地要回报这一份恩情。

They took up the task of greeting as many of the droppers-by as possible, and keeping them away from James, who had quite enough to deal with. For a solid two weeks, the three of them spent their days accepting bunches of flowers and pots of home cooking (which was useful, because Gully the house elf had been inconsolable, and spent his time curled up under the aga sobbing and drinking butterbeer). Lily handled everything financial or legal - Remus couldn’t help but admire how quickly she took to wizard property law - while Alice and Molly helped her manage the house and pack up the things which needed to be packed up. 他们承担了迎接尽可能多的来访者的任务，确保他们远离James，因为他已经有足够的事情要处理。整整两个星期，三人每天接受花束和家常菜（这很有用，因为Gully那个房子精灵一直无法自拔，时间都花在了在aga炉子下蜷缩着哭泣和喝黄油啤酒上）。Lily处理所有的财务和法律事务——Remus不禁钦佩她对巫师财产法的掌握速度——而Alice和Molly则帮助她管理房子和整理需要打包的东西。

It was grimly fitting that 1980 began with death. Years later, it would mark a turning point in the war for Remus; as if losing the Potters had shaken the very foundations of reality. After their funeral less and less things began to make sense. Things he had once felt sure of became uncertain, and the - already small - circle of people he trusted and loved began to shrink further. 1980年以死亡开端，令人感到凄凉。多年后，这将标志着战争中的一个转折点，对Remus来说；仿佛失去波特夫妇动摇了现实的根基。在他们的葬礼之后，越来越多的事情开始变得不再清晰。他曾经感到确信的事情变得不确定，曾经很小的他信任和爱的圈子变得更加缩小了。

For the rest of January, Sirius and Remus passed each other like ships in the night - one would be up late, the other awake with the dawn for some mission or other. They were both determined to make up the slack for James, and it kept them busier than ever. One or both of them might sleep at the Potters one night, or else stay with someone else in the order, for safety's sake. 在一月余下的时间里，Sirius和Remus像夜晚的船只一样错过——一个熬夜，另一个天明时分醒来执行任务。他们都决心弥补James的空缺，这使他们比以往任何时候都忙碌。他们中的一个或两个可能会在波特家过夜，或者为了安全起见与凤凰社中的其他人待在一起。

Mourning Fleamont and Euphemia on top of all that meant that the short hours they did spend together were filled with silence. 悼念Fleamont和Euphemia使得他们在一起的短暂时光充满了沉默。

Sirius had cried, the day they found out. They both had, but the pain was more raw for Sirius, “It’s not fair! It’s not fair!” He repeated over and over, eyes wild and desperate. Sirius在他们得知消息的那天哭了。他们都哭了，但对Sirius来说，痛苦更为尖锐，“这不公平！这不公平！”他一次次重复，眼神狂乱而绝望。

It was very hard work, and for a while it seemed there would be nothing at all to feel happy about again. Their only piece of good news came completely out of the blue (as good news generally does) one Sunday in early February. 这非常辛苦，一段时间似乎没有什么能让人再感到快乐。唯一的好消息完全是出乎意料的（就像好消息通常一样），发生在二月初的一个星期天。

I’ll cook dinner. ’ And of course he got ready to leave at once. “Too bloody right, Moony.”

And so, as per usual, it was James and Lily who managed to bring everyone out of that gloomy winter slog, just in time for spring. The marauders and their friends faced the rest of their year with fresh eyes and renewed purpose. In June, after the full moon, Remus was invited for another meeting with Moody and Ferox. A year older and wiser, he requested not to meet them at the Auror’s office this time. They agreed - they didn’t have much choice. Remus had grown very flippant about his role as unofficial werewolf liaison officer, and it probably showed. They met in a small working man’s pub just outside of Derby. Remus arrived first and got himself a pint, then sat down with a newspaper he’d picked up at the train station. They had all received instructions to start using fake names when out on Order business, in case anyone listened in. Moody - ‘Mr. Thompson’ - arrived a few moments later. He was looking more haggard than ever. The war seemed to affect him physically - he had accumulated more scars than anyone Remus knew (except himself, maybe). Moody——“Thompson先生”——几分钟后到达。他看起来比以往更加憔悴。战争似乎对他产生了身体上的影响——他比Remus认识的任何人都积累了更多的伤疤（也许除了他自己）。相应地，他失去了更多的身体部位——如果Moody不再小心，Remus想，他会像老教授Kettleburn一样。

That meant Greyback. Remus swallowed, nodding, 这意味着Greyback。Remus吞咽了一下，点头，

Remus没有回应。他怎么能告诉这两个比他年长、经验丰富、智慧更多、可能更强大的人，他们在做傻事？即使在Lyall Lupin死后十五年，部里仍然低估Greyback。这完全荒谬。他们拒绝从错误中吸取任何教训。

Remus pursed his lips. Danny McKinnon! Greyback must be laughing at them; they just had no idea. Remus紧抿嘴唇。Danny McKinnon！Greyback肯定在嘲笑他们；他们根本不知道。

“Well, we know he’s on the move. He left Dublin after the last full moon, without a trace. Him and a young female.” “嗯，我们知道他在移动。上次满月后他离开了都柏林，没有留下任何痕迹。他和一个年轻的女性。”

“You know who she is?” “你知道她是谁吗？”

Remus nodded. Remus点头。

“Ok. But you need to tell me, next time--” “好。但是你们下次需要告诉我——”

Remus told them as much as he knew. He felt he was re-treading old territory, but no one ever listened to him anyway. He explained what Livia looked like - that was easy enough, she was hardly an ordinary-looking witch. Remus告诉他们他所知道的一切。他觉得自己又在重复旧话题，但反正没人听他解释。他描述了Livia的外貌——这很容易，她根本不是一个普通的女巫。

“We’ll get them lad, don’t you worry,” Ferox said as he shook Remus’s hand before leaving. He had completely missed the point. “我们会抓住他们的，孩子，别担心，”Ferox在离开前握着Remus的手说。他完全没有抓住重点。

They hadn’t tracked down Castor’s pack - if they were still a pack. Moody thought they’d left the country, and Remus hoped so. He hoped no one ever found them again. By the time they were all ready to go, Remus needed a shot, never mind another pint - his back was twinging with every step, threatening a full-on spasm. And he was in a seriously bad mood. 他们没有追踪到Castor的狼群——如果他们还是一个狼群的话。Moody认为他们已经离开了这个国家，而Remus希望如此。他希望再也没有人找到他们。当他们都准备好离开时，Remus需要打一针，不再想着再喝一品脱——他的每一步都在抽痛，威胁着全身痉挛。而且他的心情非常不好。

He apparated back to London and pushed his front door open so hard the knob banged against the plasterboard. 他幻影移形回到伦敦，把前门推得砰地一声撞上了石膏板。

Remus did, and closed his eyes, sighing gratefully as Sirius began to rub his shoulders firmly, wringing the pain out with his clever fingers. Remus照做了，闭上眼睛，感激地叹了口气，Sirius开始用灵巧的手指坚定地揉捏他的肩膀，缓解疼痛。

“What happened?” He asked, “They’re not… you don’t have to go again, do you?” “发生了什么？”他问，“他们没有……你不必再去了，对吧？”

“No,” Remus said, “No, just… I dunno, do you ever feel like everyone thinks you’re just some idiotic kid who doesn’t know anything?” “没有，”Remus说，“不，只是……我不知道，你有没有觉得大家都认为你只是个什么都不懂的傻孩子？”

“I know you lot don’t, but… ugh. They just don’t listen to me. I know more about the werewolves than anyone in the Order. I’m Greyback’s prodigal son, for god’s sake!” “我知道你们不会，但……唉。他们就是不听我的。我比Order里任何人都了解狼人。天哪，我是Greyback的浪子！”

“Don’t say that.” Sirius suddenly wrapped his arms around Remus’s waist, pulling him close and tight, as if he was about to bolt. “If Moody and Ferox keep you away from that monster then good.” “别这么说。”Sirius突然把胳膊绕到Remus的腰上，把他紧紧地拉近，好像他随时会逃跑。“如果Moody和Ferox能让你远离那个怪物，那就好。”

Remus leaned into Sirius and didn’t say any more. Remus靠在Sirius身上，再也没有说话。

Wednesday 3rd September 1980

Whooosh - splash.

Remus landed on his feet - just about - right in a muddy puddle in the middle of the high street. Remus勉强站稳脚跟，正好落在大街中央的一个泥坑里。

“Bugger.” He muttered, yanking his cloak up out of the way - his boots were beyond saving, socks already soaked through. He hadn’t realised the holes were that bad, it was definitely time for a new pair, he’d need to check his savings. “该死。”他低声咒骂着，把斗篷提起来——他的靴子已经无药可救了，袜子也全湿透了。他没意识到这些洞这么糟糕，看来确实是时候换一双新的了，他得检查一下自己的存款。

It looked like it might rain later, too. Bloody perfect. 看起来后来还可能下雨。真是糟透了。

Remus was in a very bad mood, and wet feet were the least of it. Still, he was in Hogsmeade for a reason, and he knew he just had to pull his (metaphorical) socks up and get on with it. 他心情很糟，湿脚只是其中最小的问题。不过，他来霍格莫德是有原因的，他知道他必须振作起来继续前进。

He wished he wasn’t alone, but even if someone had been available to come with him (James had the baby, Lily and Sirius were in Broadstairs on reconnaissance, Marlene, Peter and Mary were all working), he’d been told to come alone. As usual. 他希望自己不是一个人，但即使有人可以陪他来（James在照顾孩子，Lily和Sirius在布罗德斯泰尔斯进行侦察，Marlene、Peter和Mary都在工作），他还是被告知要独自前来。像往常一样。

He trudged towards the Three Broomsticks, thinking at least there would be a nice warm fire and maybe a nip of whisky waiting for him. He’d need it. Whenever he was summoned to meet someone alone, it was usually werewolf business, and that always required a stiff drink. 他跋涉向三把扫帚酒吧走去，想着至少那里会有温暖的火炉，也许还有一点威士忌等着他。他需要它。每当他被召见独自会见某人时，通常是狼人的事，总是需要一杯烈酒。

He hoped it was news of Greyback rather than Castor. 他希望是Greyback的消息，而不是Castor的。

It began to spit rain as he came within sight of the pub, and he jogged a bit to save the rest of his clothes from damp. 当他看到酒吧时，天开始下小雨了，他小跑了一会儿，以免衣服湿透。

It was a quiet afternoon in the little Scottish village - the students of Hogwarts would be in their lessons, the wizards who lived in town would be at their occupations. And very few people left the house these days, if they didn’t have to. 这是苏格兰小村庄一个安静的下午——霍格沃茨的学生们应该在上课，镇上居住的巫师们在工作。如果不是必须的话，最近很少有人会离开家。

The pub was nice and empty. Remus felt a stab of nostalgia as he entered, remembering how only two short years ago he and his friends had all sat in one of the booths, bright-eyed and naive, looking forward to their futures. Who could have known that saving the world would be such a grey, monotonous slog?

酒吧很好而且空蕩蕩的。當萊姆斯走進去時，他感到一股懷舊之情，想起就在兩年前，他和他的朋友們還坐在其中一個攤位上，眼睛明亮而天真，期待著他們的未來。誰能想到拯救世界會是一場如此灰色、單調的艱苦跋涉？

“Remus Lupin, as I live and breathe!” Rosmerta chirped from the bar, one hand on her round hip, bosom overflowing as usual. She glanced hopefully over his shoulder, “Black not joining you?” “Remus Lupin，真的是你！”Rosmerta从吧台后面欢快地说，一只手放在她圆润的臀部上，胸部一如既往地丰满。她满怀希望地瞥了一眼他的肩膀，“Black没和你一起来吗？”

Remus shook his head, and went to take a seat near the hearth, so he could at least try to dry out his shoes. Remus摇了摇头，走到炉边找了个座位，这样至少可以试着把鞋子烤干。

“Not today, Rosmerta,” he said, trying to affect good cheer, “Could I get a glass of--” “今天没有，Rosmerta，”他努力表现出愉快的心情说道，“我可以来一杯--”

“Two glasses -- of butterbeer, please,” a familiar voice intoned. Remus whipped around, finding himself face to face with Dumbledore. “两杯——黄油啤酒，谢谢，”一个熟悉的声音响起。Remus猛地转身，发现自己正面对着Dumbledore。

“Oh, h-hello, professor.” Remus said, embarrassed. “哦，你好，教授。”Remus尴尬地说。

“Remus,” Dumbledore nodded politely. He never called him ‘Mr Lupin’, not since Remus had asked him not to, years ago. “Please, be seated,” he gestured grandly, like a vicar about to give a sermon. “Remus，”Dumbledore礼貌地点点头。自从多年前Remus请求他不要这样叫他后，他就再也没叫过他‘Lupin先生’。“请坐，”他大方地示意，就像即将布道的牧师一样。

Remus sat. Dumbledore always made him feel eleven years old. Remus坐下。Dumbledore总是让他感觉自己像十一岁的小孩。

“How have you been?” His old headmaster asked, kindly, gracefully taking the armchair opposite. He set down a heavy-looking leather briefcase on the rug between them. Remus eyed it warily, but answered, “你最近怎么样？”他以前的校长亲切地问道，优雅地坐在对面的扶手椅上。他把一个看起来很重的皮质公文包放在他们之间的地毯上。Remus警惕地盯着它，但还是回答道，

“Well, thanks. You know.” “还好，谢谢。你知道的。”

“These are difficult times.” Dumbledore said, and Remus didn’t respond to that, because he wasn’t sure he was supposed to. “这些是艰难的时刻。”Dumbledore说，Remus没有回应，因为他不确定自己该怎么说。

Rosmerta bustled over with the butterbeers, setting them down on the little round side table. When she’d left, Remus lifted his tankard and drank, just for a distraction. He could pretend it was alcohol, maybe that would help steady him. He desperately wanted a cigarette, but for some reason that felt wrong in front of Dumbledore. So he just sipped the butterbeer, feeling the cloying syrupy mixture rest on his tongue, slide down his throat. Rosmerta忙碌地把黄油啤酒端过来，放在小圆边桌上。她离开后，Remus举起酒杯喝了一口，只是为了分散注意力。他可以假装那是酒，也许那样会让他平静一些。他非常想抽支烟，但出于某种原因，在Dumbledore面前这样做感觉不对。所以他只是啜饮着黄油啤酒，感觉那粘稠的糖浆混合物在舌头上停留，滑下喉咙。

“You must be wondering why I asked you here,” Dumbledore said, watching him. “你一定在想为什么我叫你来这里，”Dumbledore看着他说。

“Is it… is it… Greyback?” Remus whispered. Dumbledore smiled, “是...是...Greyback吗？”Remus低声问道。Dumbledore笑了，

“You needn’t worry about eavesdroppers, Remus, we are quite safe to speak freely here. No, alas, there have been no further reports of Greyback or the young lady he is travelling with.” “你不必担心窃听者，Remus，我们在这里可以自由交谈。不，唉，没有关于Greyback或他同行的那位年轻女士的进一步报告。”

“Oh.” Remus blinked. Well then what? “哦。”Remus眨了眨眼。那么是什么呢？

“This is rather a more pressing matter - or at least, it will be, if I am correct.” “这件事更为紧迫——至少，如果我没错的话，将会是这样。”

“Right…” Remus shifted uncomfortably. He was not usually the go-to agent when it came to ‘pressing matters’. Dumbledore seemed to read his mind. “对...”Remus不舒服地动了动。涉及‘紧迫事项’时，他通常不是首选的代理人。Dumbledore似乎看穿了他的心思。

“I am in need of someone with a keen eye for detail, and a good deal of patience.” He leaned forward and opened the briefcase a crack. Remus peered inside. “我需要一个眼光敏锐，耐心十足的人。”他向前倾身，打开公文包的缝隙。Remus往里面窥视。

“Books!” He said, surprised. There must be a hundred of them inside - some sort of extension charm perhaps. “书！”他惊讶地说。里面一定有一百本书——也许是某种扩展咒语。

“Indeed,” Dumbledore smiled, closing the briefcase again. “确实如此，”Dumbledore笑着说，再次合上公文包。

“So… you need some research done?” “所以...你需要一些研究吗？”

“I do indeed. Tell me, Remus, how much do you know about prophecy?” “确实如此。告诉我，Remus，你对预言了解多少？”

“Er… well I never took Divination,” he scratched his head. He was intrigued now, “But obviously it comes up a bit in Runes… I’ve read a bit.” “呃...我从没学过占卜，”他挠了挠头。现在他很感兴趣，“但显然在符文学中有提到一些...我读过一点。”

“You will need to read a lot more,” Dumbledore said, gravely, “And I must impress upon you both the importance of this task, and the sensitivity. Anything you learn must be kept entirely confidential, do you understand?” “你需要阅读更多，”Dumbledore严肃地说，“我必须强调这项任务的重要性和敏感性。你所学到的任何信息都必须完全保密，你明白吗？”

“I… of course,” Remus nodded, slightly alarmed. “But what do you want me to look for?” “我...当然，”Remus点点头，有些惊慌。“但你要我找什么？”

“For now, we are simply seeking a fuller understanding of the nature of prophecy. Many of these books contain secret transcripts - some of which may need translating - of known prophetic and oracular statements. I should like to know if there are any which appear to relate to Voldemort, or to this particular moment in history.” “目前，我们只是寻求对预言本质的更全面理解。这些书中有许多包含已知的预言和神谕陈述的秘密记录——其中一些可能需要翻译。我想知道是否有任何与Voldemort或这个历史时刻有关的内容。”

“So… you think someone might have already made a prophecy? About how the war ends?” “所以...你认为有人可能已经做出了预言？关于战争的结局？”

“They may have.” The professor replied, shortly. “But we cannot afford to make any rash decisions. While there is still time, I would like to know as much as we can.” “可能有。”教授简短地回答。“但我们不能做出任何轻率的决定。在还有时间的时候，我想知道尽可能多的信息。”

Dumbledore switched between ‘I’ and ‘we’ regularly, when he spoke about the war, Remus noticed. Still, he thought he pretty much understood, Dumbledore在谈论战争时，经常在‘我’和‘我们’之间切换，Remus注意到了。不过，他觉得自己基本上明白了，

“Ok.” He said, “How shall I let you know, if I find anything?” “好。”他说，“如果我发现什么，怎么告诉你？”

“I shall come to you.” Dumbledore replied, cryptically. “Once again, Remus, I cannot overstate the importance of this task. You must tell nobody, understood?” “我会来找你。”Dumbledore神秘地回答。“再说一次，Remus，这项任务的重要性无法夸大。你不能告诉任何人，明白了吗？”

“Understood.” “明白。”

That meant not telling Sirius, or James, or any one of his friends. Sometimes Remus wondered if secrets were simply his lot in life. He thought for a moment, “Professor?” 这意味着不能告诉Sirius，James，或他的任何一个朋友。有时Remus会想，秘密是否就是他的人生宿命。他想了一会儿，“教授？”

“Yes?” “是的？”

“Should I keep an eye out for prophecies that have been prevented - or--” he re-phrased, because he knew that was impossible, “Circumvented? I mean, I don’t know loads about it, but there are always loopholes, aren’t there?” “我是否应该留意那些被阻止的预言——或者——”他重新措辞，因为他知道这是不可能的，“被规避的预言？我的意思是，我对它了解不多，但总会有漏洞，不是吗？”

Dumbledore’s eyes glittered, and a small smile played on his lips. Dumbledore的眼睛闪闪发光，嘴角露出一丝微笑。

“Very good, Remus.” “很好，Remus。”

* * *

 

Friday 24th October 1980

And that was how Remus spent much of his autumn. He studied well into October. It wasn’t bad at all - actually, he enjoyed it. He’d always liked research, and though he missed the peaceful airy chambers of Hogwarts’ library, he was pretty content squirrelled away in the little London flat, with endless pots of tea and a quietly smoking ashtray on hand.

 于是，Remus度过了大部分的秋天。他一直研究到十月。其实，这并不糟糕——实际上，他很享受。他一直喜欢研究，尽管他怀念霍格沃茨图书馆那宁静而开阔的房间，但他对蜷缩在伦敦的小公寓里，手边有无尽的茶壶和一个悄悄冒烟的烟灰缸感到相当满意。

If Sirius came in, he would cast obfuscate over his books and notes, and Sirius seemed happy with this arrangement. He understood what needed to be done in the service of the war. 如果Sirius进来了，他会在书本和笔记上施加模糊咒，而Sirius似乎对此安排感到满意。他明白为了战争需要做些什么。

Anyway, they were barely at the flat - Remus only used it to work in. They spent much more of their time at the Potters’ mansion, where James’s old bedroom had been turned into a nursery, but Sirius’s old bedroom was the same as ever, only with half of Remus’s things in it too. Together, the marauders and Lily had grown into a funny little family, with baby Harry at the centre. 无论如何，他们几乎不在公寓里——Remus只在那里工作。他们大部分时间都待在Potters的庄园里，James的旧卧室已经变成了婴儿室，而Sirius的旧卧室依然如故，只是里面多了一半Remus的东西。大家一起，Marauders和Lily变成了一个有趣的小家庭，Harry是中心。

It took Remus a month or so to really get over his fear of infants - and it still made him a bit anxious to actually hold Harry - but Sirius had been a huge help. Remus花了大约一个月的时间才真正克服对婴儿的恐惧——实际上抱着Harry仍然让他有点紧张——但Sirius帮了大忙。

Sirius was utterly besotted with his godson. The child was barely ever out of his arms when they were visiting (a relief for Lily and James, who were only just bearing up under the pressure of parenthood combined with their duties for the Order). Sirius对他的教子完全迷恋。在他们探访时，孩子几乎从未离开他的怀抱（这对Lily和James来说是种解脱，他们在承受父母责任和为凤凰社服务的压力下勉强撑着）。

“Say Padfoot, Harry, go on! Pah-d-foo-t…” Sirius cooed one evening, as he bounced the tiny little green-eyed creature on his lap. “说Padfoot，Harry，快说！Pah-d-foo-t…”一天晚上，Sirius低声哄着，把这个绿眼睛的小家伙抱在膝上轻轻晃动。

“They don’t talk until they’re at least one,” Remus smirked, sitting gingerly on the arm of the couch, “I looked it up.” “他们至少一岁才会说话，”Remus笑着说，小心翼翼地坐在沙发扶手上，“我查过了。”

“Normal kids don’t,” Sirius tossed his hair back, gently holding Harry’s chubby little wrists, “But Harry Potter is no ordinary baby, he’s clearly very advanced for his age. Come on, Harry, say Pad-foot …”” “普通孩子不会，”Sirius甩了甩头发，轻轻握住Harry胖乎乎的小手腕，“但Harry Potter不是普通的婴儿，他显然比同龄的孩子要聪明。来吧，Harry，说Pad-foot…”

“Don’t get your hopes up,” Lily laughed, “James’s mum told me he didn’t speak until eighteen months.” “别抱太大希望，”Lily笑着说，“James的妈妈告诉我，他十八个月才开始说话。”

“Oi,” James yelled from his father’s study, “I was an extremely thoughtful child, that’s all.” “喂，”James从他父亲的书房里喊道，“我只是个非常深思熟虑的孩子，仅此而已。”

“Oh yeah, what changed?” Sirius yelled back, grinning. “哦，是吗，后来怎么变了？”Sirius大声回道，咧嘴笑着。

“You’re hogging him, Padfoot!” Peter whined, reaching his arms out, “Come on, I haven’t had a cuddle yet,” “你霸着他不放，Padfoot！”Peter抱怨道，伸出双臂，“来吧，我还没抱过呢。”

“Not my fault he likes me best,” Sirius replied, poking his tongue out at Peter, and then at Harry, puffing out his cheeks and bulging his eyes so that the baby giggled and burbled contentedly. “他最喜欢我不是我的错，”Sirius回道，向Peter吐了吐舌头，然后对着Harry鼓起脸颊，睁大眼睛，逗得小宝宝咯咯笑起来，咕哝着。

“I’ll give you a cuddle, Pete,” Remus teased. “我来抱抱你，Pete，”Remus戏谑道。

“Lily, tell him!” Peter tutted, folding his arms crossly. “Lily，告诉他！”Peter咂嘴说道，愤怒地抱着双臂。

“Honestly! I’ve got one son and that’s plenty,” Lily laughed, getting up, “No fighting while mummy and daddy are out, ok boys?” She gave them all a very stern look. “说真的！我有一个儿子已经够了，”Lily笑着站起来，“爸妈不在的时候不要打架，好吗，孩子们？”她严厉地看了他们一眼。

“You’ve been spending too much time with Molly.” Sirius said. “你花了太多时间和Molly在一起。”Sirius说。

“Right, I’m ready,” James came back through to the living room in his travelling cloak. Lily already had hers on. She gave him a stoic smile, “好了，我准备好了，”James穿着旅行斗篷回到客厅。Lily已经穿上了她的斗篷。她对他露出一个坚忍的微笑，

“Let’s go then.” “那我们走吧。”

A cold silence entered the room, and Remus looked at the floor, because he couldn’t bring himself to look at any of his friends, and especially not the baby. 一阵冷寂笼罩了房间，Remus看着地板，因为他无法直视任何一个朋友，尤其是那个宝宝。

Lily broke it, “Oh, stop being so melodramatic, you lot. It’s a standard mission, we’ve done a hundred of these.” She went over to Sirius and bent to kiss Harry’s head - already sprouting a thatch of fine black hair. “拜托，别这么夸张，你们这些人。这是个普通任务，我们做了上百次了。”她走向Sirius，弯下腰亲了亲Harry的头——那上面已经长出了一丛细细的黑发。“Bye bye Harry, mummy and daddy love you so much. We’ll see you soon.” “再见Harry，妈妈和爸爸非常爱你。我们很快会见面的。”

James didn’t say goodbye - he had a wooden, muted expression that Remus had been seeing more and more of since his parents’ funeral. James没有说再见——他的表情木然、沉默，这是自从他父母的葬礼以来，Remus越来越常见到的。

“Are you sure you can’t tell us where--” Pete started. “你确定不能告诉我们你们要去哪里——”Pete开口道。

“Sorry Wormy,” James held his hands up, “Moody’s orders. You know how it is.” “对不起，Wormy，”James举起双手，“Moody的命令。你知道怎么回事。”

Peter nodded, shoulders slumping. Remus knew how he felt - it was difficult enough knowing that your friends were walking into danger. It was even harder not knowing exactly what they would be facing - as though they were disappearing out of reach. Peter点点头，肩膀垂下。Remus知道他的感受——知道朋友们正走向危险已经很难了。更难的是不知道他们将面对的具体情况——就像他们在消失得无影无踪。

“Come on,” Lily hurried her husband, pulling him from the room, “Back before morning, we hope!” She called from the hallway. And then the door slammed, and Harry burst into tears. “走吧，”Lily催促她的丈夫，把他拉出房间，“我们希望天亮前回来！”她从走廊里喊道。然后门砰地一声关上了，Harry放声大哭。

“Oh bugger,” Sirius said, over the screams, “Er… have him now if you like, Pete?” “哦，糟了，”Sirius在哭声中说道，“呃…你现在要抱他吗，Pete？”

It took hours to finally calm Harry down. He bawled as if his heart was broken, and wouldn’t settle until it was nearly midnight. 他们花了几个小时才终于安抚好Harry。他哭得像心碎了一样，直到将近午夜才安静下来。

“Definitely couldn’t do this full time,” Sirius said, head in his hands as he slumped on the floor of the nursery. “绝对不能全职做这个，”Sirius说，双手抱头，瘫坐在婴儿房的地板上。

“Jesus, I swear the kid’s possessed.” Remus whispered, rubbing his temples. He had a splitting headache. “天啊，我发誓这孩子被附身了。”Remus低声说，揉着太阳穴。他头痛欲裂。

“Shit, you should go to bed,” Sirius said, looking up at him. His usually immaculate silky black hair was in knots, and there was definitely still some milky baby sick stuck in there. Without a trace of irony, he frowned at Remus, “You must be exhausted,” “该死，你应该去睡觉了，”Sirius抬头看着他说。他那通常无瑕的丝滑黑发打结了，里面还沾着一些奶味的婴儿呕吐物。毫无讽刺之意地，他皱着眉对Remus说，“你一定很累。”

“Oh, I’m fine,” Remus shrugged - he tried not to wince as he felt every tendon in his back tug. Yesterday had been a full moon. “Actually I wasn’t going to stay… you know, I’ve got that work to do.” “哦，我没事，”Remus耸了耸肩——他尽量不露出痛苦的表情，因为他感觉到背部的每根肌腱都在拉扯。昨天是满月。“其实我本来不打算留下的…你知道，我有工作要做。”

“Oh, that.” Sirius nodded. His mouth was a straight line. He climbed to his feet, glancing at the red and gold cot one last time. Harry was sleeping, thank god. They both padded quietly out of the room, leaving it open just a crack. “哦，那个。”Sirius点点头。他的嘴唇紧闭成一条线。他站起来，最后看了一眼红金色的婴儿床。谢天谢地，Harry睡着了。他们俩静静地走出房间，只留下一个小缝隙。

On the landing, where the lights were still on, Sirius looked even worse - he had rings under his eyes, which were bloodshot. Remus touched his arm gently, “You ought to go to bed.” 在楼梯平台上，灯还亮着，Sirius看起来更糟糕了——他的眼睛下方有黑眼圈，眼睛布满血丝。Remus轻轻碰了碰他的手臂，“你应该去睡觉了。”

Sirius grabbed his arm, suddenly, eyes widening, “Moony, don’t go.” Sirius突然抓住他的手臂，眼睛睁大，“Moony，别走。”

“Eh? I’m only going to the flat…” “嗯？我只是要去公寓…”

“Please?” Sirius clutched at him, half mad with tiredness, “Just take the night off, just stay here with me?” “拜托？”Sirius抓住他，半疯地疲惫不堪，“就休息一晚，留下来陪我好吗？”

“Pete’s here…” Remus turned his head slightly. He could hear Peter snoring on the couch downstairs. Not much comfort, he supposed, “Peter在这里...”Remus微微转头。他能听到楼下沙发上Peter的鼾声。他想，这并不能带来多大安慰，

“But I want you,” Sirius said, desperately. “但我想要你，”Sirius绝望地说。

That struck Remus in an unusual way. To anyone else, it might have sounded whinging; childish. After all, Sirius was a grown man, and Remus had important work to do. But somehow it dislodged a feeling Remus hadn’t had for Sirius in a long time - a desire to protect him. To hold him close and tell him everything was going to be ok, and to be strong and reliable for the man he loved. 这让Remus有种不同寻常的感觉。对其他人来说，这可能听起来像是在抱怨；幼稚。毕竟，Sirius是个成年人，而Remus有重要的工作要做。但不知为何，这激发了Remus很久没有对Sirius产生的感觉——一种想要保护他的愿望。想要紧紧抱住他，告诉他一切都会好的，并且要为他所爱的男人坚强可靠。

Amazed by this revelation, Remus did exactly that, hugging Sirius tightly and kissing his filthy hair, “Ok then,” he whispered, “I’ll stay.” 被这个启示惊讶到的Remus正是这么做的，紧紧抱住Sirius，亲吻他肮脏的头发，“好吧，”他低声说，“我会留下。”

 

After all, he thought, as Sirius trailed off to have a shower, relief evident in his posture; wouldn’t Sirius do the same for him? 毕竟，他想，当Sirius拖着疲惫的身体去洗澡时，显而易见地松了一口气；Sirius难道不会为他做同样的事吗？

* * *

Friday 21st November 1980

That time, Lily and James came back, as always; tired, a little harder, a little less bright, but otherwise perfectly ok. Remus always felt enormous relief when any of his friends returned safely, and each time swore to himself he would not take it for granted. But what does that mean, when you are young? 那次，Lily和James像往常一样回来了；疲惫，稍微更坚强一点，少了些光彩，但其他方面一切正常。每当他的朋友们安全归来时，Remus总是感到巨大的宽慰，并且每次都发誓自己不会认为这是理所当然的。但当你年轻时，这是什么意思呢？

There had been deaths - deaths in the Order, deaths of people he knew - but no one really close. No one he truly loved. The Prewetts he had been fond of. Benjy Fenwick he had chatted to once or twice. But they weren’t close, and their losses didn’t affect him severely. Compared to others, Remus had been extremely lucky. 有过死亡——在凤凰社里死去的人，他认识的人——但没有人真正与他亲近。没有他真正爱的人。Prewetts是他喜欢的。Benjy Fenwick他聊过一两次。但他们并不亲近，他们的离去对他没有太大的影响。相比之下，Remus非常幸运。

Of course, you never feel lucky, at the time. Good fortune is too often something that can only be recognised with hindsight. 当然，你在当时从来不会觉得幸运。好运常常是只有在事后才能意识到的。

Sirius turned twenty one in November. They didn’t have a party, but Hagrid baked a rather wonky - though very large and very delicious - cake, which they all ate at the Order safe house after the regular meeting. Someone took a few photos, but Remus forgot to try and track them down. Sirius在十一月满二十一岁。他们没有举行派对，但Hagrid烤了一个相当歪斜——但非常大也非常美味——的蛋糕，他们在凤凰社的安全屋例会后一起吃了。有人拍了几张照片，但Remus忘了去找。

“It’s a big deal for muggles, twenty-one.” He commented as they climbed into bed that evening. “That’s when they come of age.” “对麻瓜来说，二十一岁很重要。”那天晚上上床时他评论道。“那是他们成年的时候。”

“Why? Muggles can’t do magic.” Sirius frowned, yawning. “为什么？麻瓜不能做魔法。”Sirius皱眉打哈欠。

“No, I know, it’s just an old fashioned thing,” Remus tried to explain. “You get the key to your front door or something like that.” “不，我知道，这只是个老派的事情，”Remus试图解释。“你会得到你前门的钥匙之类的东西。”

“Daft muggles.” Sirius grumbled, his eyes already closing. “I feel old.” “蠢麻瓜。”Sirius嘟囔着，眼睛已经快闭上了。“我感觉老了。”

“Well, you’re not,” Remus settled down beside him, “I’m the one going grey. Twenty-one is young. Really really young.” “嗯，你还不老，”Remus在他身边安顿下来，“是我在变白。二十一岁还年轻。真的很年轻。”

Sirius sighed wearily. “Doesn’t feel it.” Sirius疲惫地叹了口气。“感觉不像。”

Remus knew exactly what he meant, but he didn’t like it. They were all of them caught in a confusing place between adolescence and adulthood - baby Harry had only exacerbated that. There was a sense of time running out; of needing to accomplish as much as possible as fast as possible. Peter’s crawling at his ministry job, always angling for a better position; James and Lily playing house and soldiers at the same time - Remus and his stupid drinking. Remus完全明白他的意思，但他不喜欢这种感觉。他们都处在青春期和成年期之间的一个混乱地带——小宝宝Harry只是加剧了这一点。有一种时间正在流逝的感觉；需要尽快完成尽可能多的事情。Peter在他的魔法部工作中艰难前行，总是在争取更好的职位；James和Lily同时扮演家庭和士兵角色——Remus和他愚蠢的酗酒。

At least he had the research to do. That seemed to be going well - every now and then Dumbledore dropped by to see how he was getting on. And Remus would offload as much information as he could - with detail, because he knew Dumbledore liked detail. The old man would nod sagely, stroke his beard and sit quietly, ruminating. If he came to any conclusions, he didn’t tell Remus. 至少他还有研究要做。这似乎进展顺利——Dumbledore时不时会过来看他进行得如何。Remus会尽可能详细地提供信息——因为他知道Dumbledore喜欢细节。老人会聪明地点点头，抚摸胡须，静静地坐着，沉思。如果他得出任何结论，他不会告诉Remus。

It felt good, though. Remus even felt himself warming to Dumbledore for the first time. He liked being useful. And then, just before the November full moon, Remus got his chance to be really useful. 但这感觉很好。Remus甚至第一次感到自己开始喜欢Dumbledore了。他喜欢有用的感觉。然后，就在十一月满月之前，Remus有了一个真正有用的机会。

As usual, there was a message from Moody. He was to apparate to some very specific coordinates on Friday 21st November, and meet Ferox there. 一如既往，Moody发来信息。他将在十一月二十一日星期五幻影移形到一些非常具体的坐标，并在那里与Ferox会合。

“Tell him no,” Sirius said, annoyed, “Bloody Moody, he knows that’s the night before the full moon! You shouldn’t be out running his errands when you’re not well.” “告诉他不行，”Sirius恼怒地说，“该死的Moody，他知道那是满月前的夜晚！你在身体不好的时候不应该出去跑腿。”

“Jesus, you make me sound like an invalid,” Remus rolled his eyes. “I’m sure there’s a good reason for it. I’ll be fine, don’t worry.” “天啊，你让我听起来像个病人，”Remus翻了个白眼。“我确信有充分的理由。我会没事的，别担心。”

“Send a patronus, if anything happens?” Sirius asked, solemnly. “I don’t care about protocol, just say you’ll let me know?” “如果有什么事情发生，发一个守护神好吗？”Sirius严肃地问。“我不在乎规矩，只要你告诉我？”

“It will be fine.” Remus repeated. “会没事的。”Remus重复道。

He really did feel fine about it all. When the moon was waxing he often felt stronger than usual, and usually didn’t get bouts of nausea until a few hours before sunset. 他真的觉得一切都很好。当月亮在增盈时，他常常感觉比平时更强壮，通常在日落前几个小时才会感到恶心。

It was good to get out of London; away from traffic and noise and crowds. It was good to get away from the Potters’ - from nappies and baby talk and crying and creamed spinach. At the agreed time, Remus apparated following the instructions he’d been given, and found himself on a windy clifftop, somewhere very cold and bleak. 离开伦敦是件好事；远离交通、噪音和人群。离开Potters家也是件好事——远离尿布、婴儿话、哭泣和奶油菠菜。在约定的时间，Remus按照指示幻影移形，发现自己在一个寒冷荒凉的风吹悬崖上。

The sea crashed and raged miles below, and the long grass whipped around his ankles. Remus breathed in, deeply, inhaling the salt, the soil, the sharp cold scent of the clouds. The wolf inside licked its lips, ears pricking to attention. Yes. Greyback had been here. 海浪在几英里下方咆哮，长草在他的脚踝周围抽打。Remus深深吸了一口气，吸入盐味、土味和云朵的冷峻气息。内心的狼舔了舔嘴唇，竖起了耳朵。没错。Greyback曾在这里。

“Hello!” Ferox was a way off in the distance, a stick figure man waving at him. Remus raised a palm in greeting, bent forward into the wind and trudged to meet him. “你好！”Ferox在远处，一个像火柴人的人向他挥手。Remus举起手打招呼，迎着风弯下腰，步履艰难地走向他。

“Hi,” he said, breathless as he approached, cold hands deep in his pockets, nose frozen. “Where are we?” “嗨，”他接近时气喘吁吁，冷得手插在口袋里，鼻子冻僵了。“我们在哪？”

“Galloway,” Ferox said, cheerfully. He had a thick leather cloak on, with a hood, but his face was still ruddy from the harsh weather, and white fog blew from his lips as he spoke. “Pretty, eh?” “加洛韦，”Ferox高兴地说。他穿着厚厚的皮斗篷，带着兜帽，但他的脸仍因恶劣天气而红润，说话时白雾从嘴唇间喷出。“漂亮吧？”

Remus wasn’t sure if he was being sarcastic or not, so he just gave a neutral smile. Privately he thought that yes, the landscape was beautiful, if forbidding. Remus不确定他是不是在讽刺，所以只是给了一个中性的微笑。私下里他认为是的，景色很美，如果不那么令人望而生畏的话。

“Greyback’s been here.” He said, wanting to get down to it. “Greyback曾在这里。”他说，想直奔主题。

“You know for sure?” “你确定吗？”

“One hundred percent.” Remus nodded. Ferox nodded too, “百分之百。”Remus点头。Ferox也点头，

“Excellent, we were right, then. There was a report to the muggle police about a couple of tramps, man and a woman, looking shifty. Reckon they’ve been here, then?” “太好了，我们是对的。麻瓜警察有报告说有一对流浪汉，男的和女的，看起来鬼鬼祟祟。你觉得他们来过这里吗？”

Remus considered, breathing in again, “Yeah, but the scent’s old… maybe a day or so.” Remus考虑了一下，再次吸气，“是的，但气味很旧了…也许有一天左右。”

“Right. Shall we take a walk, then? See if it gets a bit stronger?” “好的。那么我们走走看看？看看气味会不会更强？”

“Ok…” Remus wasn’t sure how he felt, being the Order’s bloodhound. But he wanted to find Greyback as much as anyone, so he did as he was told. “好吧…”Remus不确定自己感觉如何，成为了凤凰社的猎犬。但他像任何人一样想找到Greyback，所以他照做了。

They strolled up and down the clifftop for a while, until Remus could be sure which way the trail led. As they headed downhill, away from the sea and down towards a small country road, he grew confident that Livia and Greyback had been there very recently, and began to walk faster. Ferox had no trouble keeping up, of course; he was as fit and healthy as he’d ever been. 他们在悬崖顶上来回走了一会儿，直到Remus能确定踪迹的方向。当他们下坡，远离大海，向一条小乡村道路走去时，他越来越确信Livia和Greyback最近来过这里，并开始加快步伐。当然，Ferox跟上没有任何问题；他一如既往地健康。

“What will we do, if we find him?” Remus asked as they walked. He was careful not to bring Livia into it, because - ok, while she was definitely a killer, he couldn’t help feeling a bit more sympathetic towards her. After all, she was his sister, in a warped kind of way. “如果我们找到他怎么办？”Remus边走边问。他小心不提Livia，因为——好吧，尽管她肯定是个杀手，他还是忍不住对她有些同情。毕竟，她是他的妹妹，以一种扭曲的方式。

“Moody reckons they’re hunkered down somewhere for the full moon,” Ferox replied, “Based on my research, werewolves are weakest right after the moon, so we’ll wait until then.” “Moody认为他们在某个地方躲起来等待满月，”Ferox回答道，“根据我的研究，狼人在满月之后最虚弱，所以我们会等到那时。”

“Your research?” Remus gave him a funny look. “你的研究？”Remus给了他一个奇怪的表情。

“Few books I’ve picked up - there’s not a lot to go on, beyond the NEWT level stuff.” “我挑了几本书——除了NEWT级别的东西之外，没有太多可以参考的。”

“Have you spoken to Madam Pomfrey? She looked after me for seven years, she knows loads,” Remus said, trying not to sound too impatient. “Or Marlene McKinnon? She’s been constructing her own case studies, to see if any advances can be made in lycanthropy treatment. Or, y’know. You could ask me. I might know a bit.” “你和Pomfrey夫人谈过吗？她照顾了我七年，她知道很多，”Remus说，尽量不显得太不耐烦。“或者Marlene McKinnon？她一直在做自己的病例研究，看看能否在狼疮治疗方面取得进展。或者，你知道，你可以问我。我可能知道一些。”

Ferox laughed good naturedly, “All right lad, all right, I see what you’re saying. It’s just that there isn’t always time to follow umpteen leads on a prick like Greyback. Got to move fast.” Ferox好脾气地笑了笑，“好吧，小伙子，好吧，我明白你的意思。只是没有总是有时间跟随像Greyback这样的人渣的无数线索。得快速行动。”

Remus said nothing, because it would only have come out wrong. He really hated criticising Ferox, it felt so awkward and embarrassing. He’d looked up to him as an ideal vision of manhood, once, and he didn’t like tampering with that illusion too much. But honestly. The way he talked, you’d think Greyback was just some petty criminal, not a murderous creature and charismatic cult leader. Remus什么也没说，因为说出来只会弄错。他真的讨厌批评Ferox，感觉太尴尬和难堪了。他曾经把他视为男子气概的理想形象，不喜欢过多地破坏这个幻象。但说实话。他说话的方式，让人觉得Greyback只是个小罪犯，不是一个杀人犯和有魅力的邪教领袖。

The scent had grown very strong, now, and as they crested the next hill, Remus could make out a large grey-black structure in the distance. The ruins of an old castle - Scotland was littered with them of course. This one was a tower house, and looked like a big square prison squatting ominously over the remains of a boggy moat. 现在气味变得非常强烈，当他们登上下一个山顶时，Remus可以看到远处有一个大灰黑色的建筑物。一座古老城堡的废墟——当然，苏格兰到处都是这样的废墟。这是一座塔楼，看起来像一座大方形监狱，阴森地蹲在泥泞护城河的遗迹上。

“There.” Remus said, stopping short. “That’s where he’ll be.” “那里。”Remus说，猛然停下。“他会在那里。”

 

Ferox clapped him on the shoulder. “Good work, lad.” Ferox拍了拍他的肩膀。“干得好，小伙子。”

* * *

Saturday 22nd November

 

 

Ferox didn’t want Remus present for the confrontation with Greyback. Remus did not give a toss. He knew where to go, and when, and nothing would change his mind. Ferox不想让Remus出现在与Greyback的对峙中。Remus根本不在乎。他知道去哪儿，什么时候去，什么都不会改变他的主意。

“I’m coming too, then.” Sirius said, firmly, after he’d wheedled enough information out of Remus. “那我也去。”Sirius坚定地说，在他从Remus那里挖掘到足够的信息之后。

“No you’re bloody not.” Remus said. “你去不了。”Remus说。

“Am too. Sorry Moony, but there is absolutely no way I’m losing you to that monster a second time.” “我去。对不起，Moony，但绝对不可能让我第二次把你交给那个怪物。”

“You didn’t lose me last time, you big drama queen, it was a mission,” Remus countered, “Anyway, I can’t put you in that sort of danger.” “上次你没丢掉我，你这大戏精，那是一场任务，”Remus反驳道，“反正，我不能让你陷入那种危险。”

“I’m in danger every day,” Sirius shrugged, “If it’s right after the full moon, you’ll need my help apparating.” “我每天都在危险中，”Sirius耸耸肩说，“如果是在满月之后，你会需要我的帮助来瞬移。”

“I’ve done that before,” Remus dismissed, “It’s hard, but I’ll manage. Anyway, this isn’t a normal mission, you wouldn’t just be backup, you’d be leverage against me. He knows who you are. He knows what you mean to me.” “我以前做过，”Remus不以为然地说，“这很难，但我会处理的。反正，这不是一个普通的任务，你不仅仅是后备，你还会成为对付我的筹码。他知道你是谁。他知道你对我意味着什么。”

“He made you tell him?!”

“Sort of. I told you they can read minds.” “他让你告诉他？！”

“有点。我告诉过你，他们能读心。”

“That bastard. I’m definitely coming with you.” “那个混蛋。我肯定会跟你一起去。”

Remus had forgotten how strongly Sirius felt about legilimency. Walpurga had used it as a punishment, and he would forever associate mindreading with black magic. Remus hadn’t raised the fact that this appeared to be a werewolf trait, and that, when pushed, he could do it too. Probably not a good idea to mention that just yet, he decided. Remus已经忘记了Sirius对Legilimency的强烈感情。Walpurga用它作为惩罚，他将永远把读心术与黑魔法联系在一起。Remus没有提到这似乎是狼人特质，且在被逼迫时，他也能做到。决定暂时不提这件事可能更好。

So Sirius got his way, of course, and Remus just hoped he would be able to protect him. 所以Sirius当然得到了他的方式，Remus只是希望他能保护好自己。

They went to the Lake District for the full moon; a place the marauders had enjoyed themselves before, a place with happy memories. James and Peter didn’t go. James hadn’t joined them for a full moon since Harry was born, and Remus understood that he didn’t want to be away from his family too often. Peter said something vague about working late, and honestly Remus was too busy worrying about the upcoming battle with Greyback to question it. 他们去了湖区度过满月；这是流氓们曾经喜欢的地方，充满了快乐的回忆。James和Peter没有去。自从Harry出生以来，James就没有再参加满月的活动，Remus理解他不想经常离开家人。Peter说了些关于加班的模糊话，坦白说，Remus太忙于担心即将与Greyback的战斗，没去质疑这个。

The wolf probably had a good time that night, but Remus didn’t remember much about it. It all got lost in the blood red haze of transformation, the choking and clawing and groaning as he twisted back into his human form. 狼人在那晚可能玩得很开心，但Remus记不太清楚了。所有的一切都在变身的血红色迷雾中消失，窒息、抓挠和呻吟，他在扭曲回到人形时。

“Urrrgh!” “呜呜呜！”

“I’ve got you, Moony,” Sirius had him by the shoulders, pulling a cloak across his body. Remus forced his eyes open, knowing how little time there was. “我抓住你了，Moony，”Sirius握住他的肩膀，把斗篷拉到他身上。Remus强迫自己睁开眼睛，知道时间所剩无几。

“Wand,” he croaked, getting up. Sirius handed it to him. “We’ve got to go, now,” Remus said, leaning on Sirius for support while he pulled his clothes on, hands shaking and fumbling with the buttons on his shirt and trousers. “魔杖，”他嘶哑地说，站起来。Sirius把魔杖递给他。“我们现在得走，”Remus说，靠在Sirius身上换衣服，手颤抖着在衬衫和裤子的扣子上摸索。

“We’re going, just take a breath,” Sirius said, his voice calm and firm. “Hold on to me, I’ll apparate us…” “我们要走了，深呼吸一下，”Sirius说，他的声音平静而坚定。“抓紧我，我会瞬移我们…”

Sirius was as good as his word; he didn’t try to dissuade Remus from going, or try to tell him what to do. He simply got them where they needed to be. Sirius说到做到；他没有试图劝阻Remus，或是告诉他该做什么。他只是把他们带到了需要去的地方。

Ferox was there already. Ferox已经在那里了。

“All right, lads,” he nodded, keeping his voice low. It was still quite dark under the grey Galloway sky, and the grasslands were cloaked in swaths of gauzy mist, the castle ruin rising from it black and foreboding. It was quiet, no birdsong, no noise at all. Like a place out of time. “好了，伙计们，”他点了点头，声音低沉。在灰暗的加洛韦天空下仍然很黑暗，草地被一层薄纱般的雾气笼罩，城堡废墟从中升起，黑暗而不祥。四周寂静无声，没有鸟鸣，什么声音都没有。就像一个与时间脱节的地方。

“Have you seen anything?” Remus asked, desperately. He could smell them, the scent was very strong. “你看到什么了吗？”Remus绝望地问。他能闻到他们的气味，味道非常浓烈。

“Heard a bit of noise; must have been them turning back.” Ferox said. He gave Remus a look, “You ok, our kid? Looking a bit green about the gills.” “听到了一点噪音；一定是他们转身回去了。”Ferox说。他看了看Remus，“你还好吗，小子？看起来有点面黄肌瘦。”

“Fine,” Remus swallowed, “Fine. We should go in now.” “没事，”Remus咽了口唾沫，“没事。我们现在该进去了。”

“Right you are. Wands out.” Ferox straightened up and started forward, “Pity we couldn’t get ‘em when they were wolves, eh?” He said, with a smirk, “Those pelts fetch a few bob on the black market.” “对的，魔杖拿出来。”Ferox站直了身体，向前走，“真可惜我们没能在他们是狼的时候抓住他们，嗯？”他带着冷笑说，“那些皮毛在黑市上能卖几个钱。”

Remus felt sick, the sweat on his back turned cold. Sirius reached for his hand in the dark and gave it a squeeze, then tossed his head and said sharply, “Don’t say shit like that, it’s disgusting.” Remus感到恶心，背上的汗水变得冰冷。Sirius在黑暗中伸手握住他的手，然后甩了甩头，尖锐地说：“别说那种话，恶心。”

Ferox glanced back at him, shocked, then at Remus. He frowned, “Sorry lad, didn’t mean anything by it.” Ferox惊讶地回头看了看他，然后看向Remus。他皱起了眉头，“对不起，小子，我不是那个意思。”

They didn’t say another word as they approached the castle. Sirius and Ferox were trying to be quiet, but Remus knew they may as well have been a herd of elephants sneaking up on Livia and Greyback, whose senses were as sharp as his, even after the full moon. Still, they might be slower; weaker. 他们在接近城堡时没有再说话。Sirius和Ferox尽量保持安静，但Remus知道，他们可能和一群大象悄悄靠近Livia和Greyback一样，尽管他们的感官在满月后也像他的那样敏锐。尽管如此，他们可能会比较慢；比较弱。

When they were up against the castle wall, Remus felt it. Greyback was waiting. The scent changed, and his head was filled with that dreadful growling voice, “Hello, cub… brought me breakfast, have you?” 当他们靠在城堡墙上时，Remus感到了。Greyback在等待。气味发生了变化，他的脑海里充满了那令人恐惧的低吼声，“你好，小崽子…带了早餐来了吗？”

“He knows we’re here.” Remus whispered, frantically, “Be careful!” “他知道我们在这里。”Remus急切地低声说，“小心点！”

Ferox touched his brow in a sort of salute, to show he understood. Then he rounded the corner and entered, Remus hurrying behind, and Sirius too. Ferox had his wand raised, and as he stepped under the broken archway it the shadows of the ruin, he opened his mouth - he had planned to use the silver chain spell, to bind the werewolves and contain them long enough for the Auror’s to take over - but it was too late. Ferox用一种致敬的方式碰了碰额头，表示他明白了。然后他绕过角落进入，Remus急忙跟在后面，还有Sirius。Ferox举起魔杖，正当他走到破损的拱门下，在废墟的阴影中时，他张开了嘴——他计划使用银链咒语，来束缚狼人并将他们困住足够长的时间，以便Aurors接管——但为时已晚。

Remus was only a split second behind Ferox, and saw the rock come down. He stiffened, then crumpled to the ground, blood oozing from the a cut at the crown of his head. Remus仅比Ferox慢了一秒钟，看到岩石落下。他僵硬了一下，然后摔倒在地，血液从头顶的伤口中渗出。

“No!” Remus cried, over Greyback’s laughter as the beast of a man stepped into the early morning light, his face full of glee. Livia sprung out next, and lunged at Sirius, grabbing his wand and knocking him to the ground. “不！”Remus在Greyback的笑声中哭喊，那个野兽般的人走进了清晨的光线中，他的脸上充满了喜悦。Livia接着跳出来，扑向Sirius，抓住他的魔杖，把他打倒在地。

“Oooooh, who’s this then, brother? Pretty, pretty boy…” she crowed, sitting astride him, holding both of Sirius’s wrists over his head as he struggled. She looked thinner, but was obviously as strong as ever. “哦哦哦，这是谁，哥哥？漂亮的漂亮的小伙子…”她得意地叫道，骑在他身上，双手抓住Sirius的手腕，把他压在头顶，她看起来瘦了，但显然还是那么强壮。

“Let him go!” Remus snarled, raising his wand, furious. Then he screamed in agony. Greyback grabbed his wand arm and twisted it so hard he felt the bone snap. “放开他！”Remus咆哮着，举起魔杖，愤怒不已。然后他痛苦地尖叫。Greyback抓住他的魔杖手臂，狠狠地扭曲，使他感到骨头断裂的声音。

“Remus!” Sirius called out. “Remus！”Sirius呼喊道。

Remus was almost blind with pain, and Greyback laughed again, letting him go. Remus几乎因痛苦而失明，Greyback再次笑了起来，放开了他。

“Welcome back, cub,” he purred. “How I’ve missed you…” “欢迎回来，小崽子，”他低声说，“我有多么想念你…”

“Fuck you.” Remus groaned, staring about for his wand, which he’d dropped somewhere. “去你妈的。”Remus呻吟着，四处寻找他丢失的魔杖。

“Now now,” Greyback chuckled, as Remus straightened up to face him, clutching his broken arm to his chest. “You should be on your hands and knees after what you did to me.” “现在现在，”Greyback笑了笑，当Remus站直身子面对他时，紧紧抱住自己断裂的手臂。“你应该跪地求饶，因为你对我做了什么。”

“Kill him, father!” Livia cackled, “Kill the traitor Remus Lupin, just as he killed my brother Gaius! Then I can have the pretty one!” “杀了他，父亲！”Livia咯咯笑道，“杀死叛徒Remus Lupin，就像他杀了我的哥哥Gaius一样！然后我可以得到这个漂亮的家伙！”

Greyback grinned at her, fondly, “She’s full of bright ideas, my beautiful girl.” Greyback对她露出一个温柔的笑容，“她满脑子都是好主意，我美丽的女孩。”

Remus took the opportunity to look over Greyback’s shoulder - Ferox was moving. Very slowly; he was obviously hurt, but Remus saw his fist tighten around his wand. Remus抓住机会看了一眼Greyback的肩膀——Ferox在移动。非常慢；他明显受了伤，但Remus看到他紧握着魔杖的拳头。

“Go on then!” Remus said to Greyback, gritting his teeth through the pain, “Kill me. Then what?” “那你继续吧！”Remus对Greyback说，咬紧牙关忍受痛苦，“杀了我。然后呢？”

“Then what?!” Greyback sneered, “Then I rip apart your little human pet, that’s what. Then I tear him limb from fucking limb - but not before I’ve had my fun with him…” “然后呢？！”Greyback冷笑道，“然后我撕碎你的小人类宠物，这就是答案。然后我把他撕成四分五裂——但在此之前，我得先和他玩一玩…”

“You’re disgusting!” Remus shot back, stalling for time as Ferox’s eyes opened. May as well tell Greyback what he thought of him, while he had the chance, “You’re filth! You’re nothing! You talk about freedom, but you don’t have the first clue what it is! You’re nothing but a bully! Voldemort’s lapdog!” “你真恶心！”Remus反击道，争取时间让Ferox的眼睛睁开。趁机告诉Greyback他对他的看法，“你是污秽！你什么都不是！你谈论自由，却对自由一无所知！你不过是个恶霸！伏地魔的走狗！”

“Kill him!” Livia shrieked. “杀了他！”Livia尖叫道。

Greyback’s face had turned demonic with rage, yellow eyes glowing, and Remus really thought that would be the end. He scrunched his eyes shut and braced himself. Greyback的脸因愤怒而变得妖异，黄色的眼睛发光，Remus真的以为这将是结局。他紧闭眼睛，做好了准备。

“What?! Argh!” Livia cried out again, and Remus heard a dog bark. “什么？！啊！”Livia再次喊叫，Remus听到一声狗吠。

He opened his eyes to see Livia knocked backwards by Padfoot, who was growling - Remus had never seen him growl before - teeth bared, frothing at the mouth. 他睁开眼睛看到Livia被Padfoot撞倒，Padfoot在咆哮——Remus以前从未见过他咆哮——露出牙齿，口吐白沫。

“Father!” Livia yelped, “Help m---” “父亲！”Livia尖叫道，“救我——”

And with a flash of purple light, Livia was silent. Her eyes went wide, a great black slash had cut her throat. She clutched at her neck to stem the gushing blood, but it was no good, it was too late. 随着一闪而过的紫色光芒，Livia变得沉默。她的眼睛瞪大，一道巨大的黑色伤口切开了她的喉咙。她抓住脖子试图止住喷涌的血液，但已经来不及了。

Greyback gave a great roar of anguish, but Ferox was already on his feet, wand up, ready to cast the same curse again. Greyback was cornered. Greyback发出了一声巨大的痛苦咆哮，但Ferox已经站起来，魔杖在手，准备再次施放同样的咒语。Greyback被逼到了绝境。

“You’re a dead man.” He hissed at Ferox, and then, with one final snarl, he disapparated.你已經是個死人了。”他對費洛克斯發出嘶嘶聲，然後，隨著最後一聲咆哮，他消失了。 

“Bugger!” Ferox grunted, stumbling forward, still poised to curse. “混蛋！”費洛克斯咕噥著，跌跌撞撞地向前走去，仍然準備著咒罵。 

Sirius was Sirius again, and stood beside Livia, staring down at her. Remus went over too, feeling an uncomfortable mix of relief and genuine sorrow. Her grey fur cloak was matted with blood, which looked deep purple in the dim light. It was dreadful, but his first concern was for Sirius, 

天狼星又是天狼星了，他站在莉薇亞身邊，低頭看著她。萊姆斯也走了過去，心裡既感到寬慰，又感到真正的悲傷，感到一種不舒服的感覺。她的灰色毛皮斗篷上沾滿了血跡，在昏暗的燈光下顯得深紫色。這很可怕，但他首先關心的是天狼星，

 “Ok?” He asked, quietly. Sirius nodded, still looking down. “You?” 

 “Think so.” 

His arm was throbbing, sending shooting pains up into his shoulder; but he knew that could be fixed. Livia could not. Ferox joined them, a hand pressed to his head where the rock had struck him.

“也這樣覺得。”他的手臂一陣陣抽痛，肩膀上傳來陣陣刺痛。但他知道這是可以解決的。莉維亞不能。費洛克斯加入了他們，一隻手按在他被岩石擊中的頭部。

 “Merlin, what a mess.” He muttered. “At least we got the bitch.”

 “Her name’s Livia.” Remus said, angrily. 

He suddenly saw the scene as a passerby might. Three men standing over her tiny body.他突然像路人一樣看到了這一幕。三個男人站在她小小的身體旁。

 She could have ripped each of their throats out the night before without stopping for breath. She was a force of nature; queen of the night; she was one of the strongest people he had ever met. She was one of the only people in the world who truly understood what it meant to be a wolf.

 Her eyes were still open, staring blindly at the broad grey sky. Remus knelt beside her, and gently closed them.

她本可以在前一天晚上不停歇地把他們的喉嚨撕下來。她是一種自然的力量；夜女王；她是他見過的最堅強的人之一。她是世界上唯一真正理解狼意味著什麼的人之一。

 

她的眼睛仍然睜著，茫然地望著廣闊的灰色天空。萊姆斯跪在她身邊，輕輕合上它們。
