Soon found out I was losin' my mind

It seemed like the real thing but I was so blind,

Much of mistrust, love's gone behind.

 

James recovered - slowly. He was moved back to the Potter house the next day (waking up groggy, unable to say very much, quickly falling back to sleep), but Dumbledore declared this a temporary solution. He told Lily to prepare to leave at a moment’s notice. James逐渐恢复了。第二天，他被送回了波特家（醒来时有些迷糊，说不了多少话，很快又睡着了），但邓布利多宣布这只是暂时的解决方案。他告诉Lily随时准备离开。

After months of being regarded as junior members of the Order, the marauders and their friends suddenly had all eyes on them. 经过几个月被视为组织的初级成员，夺命狼人和他们的朋友们突然引起了所有人的关注。

At the next Order meeting, which James insisted on attending despite his weakened state, there were definitely whispers. 在下一次组织会议上，尽管James身体虚弱坚持参加，肯定有窃窃私语。

Seven kids - three of them wealthy heirs to pureblood houses, two muggle born, a werewolf, a novice Healer - what made them so special? Could they be trusted? They had survived the war so far, against all the odds. Were they just lucky, or was there something more to it? Who were these kids, who had escaped six death eaters and somehow reversed an almost incomprehensible curse? 七个孩子——其中三个是纯血家庭的富有继承人，两位麻瓜出生，一个狼人，一名新手治疗师——他们有什么特别之处？他们值得信任吗？他们在各种逆境中幸存下来，至今幸免于难。他们只是运气好，还是有什么更多的原因？这些孩子是谁，竟能从六个食死徒手中逃脱，并且以某种方式逆转了几乎难以理解的诅咒？

They had gathered in a small cottage, somewhere in the Peak District. It was a small living room, but the Order was small by then. 他们聚集在一个位于峰区的小别墅里。那是一个小客厅，但到那时组织已经很小了。

At the end of the regular meeting - which had really become more of a remembrance service for people they’d lost since the last time they’d met - Dumbledore asked Lily and James to stay behind while everyone else headed home. In turn, James asked Remus, Sirius and Peter to stay. 在例行会议结束时——实际上已经更像是一个悼念仪式，缅怀自上次见面以来失去的人——邓布利多要求Lily和James留下来，而其他人则回家了。接着，James请求Remus、Sirius和Peter留下。

“Are you sure?” Sirius whispered, urgently, “After everything that’s happened…?” “你确定吗？”Sirius急切地低声问，“在发生了一切之后……”

“--After everything that’s happened I want my best friends nearby.” James replied. Remus felt a swell of pride at that - to James, good sportsmanship extended to every element of his life. To mistrust the people he loved would be highly dishonourable. “——在发生了一切之后，我希望我的最好的朋友就在身边。”James回答。Remus对此感到一阵自豪——对James来说，良好的运动精神延伸到他生活中的每一个方面。不信任他爱的人是极其不光彩的。

Sirius folded his arms, but didn’t argue. Sirius交叉着双臂，但没有争论。

James sat in a chintz armchair, his back straight, his face set. He looked perfectly healthy, unless you really knew him. His cheeks were more hollow, his skin paler, and - though everyone was pretending they hadn’t noticed - his jet black hair now had a few threads of grey. Lily had brought a blanket to lay over his lap, but he kept pushing it off, irritably. James坐在一把花呢扶手椅上，背部挺直，脸色凝重。他看起来完全健康，除非你真的了解他。他的脸颊更加凹陷，皮肤苍白——尽管每个人都装作没注意到——他的黑发中现在有了几缕灰色。Lily带来了一条毯子放在他的腿上，但他不断地不耐烦地推开它。

“I’m fine,” he muttered under his breath. “Leave me be!” “我没事，”他低声嘟囔，“别打扰我！”

“There’s no need to be like that!” Lily hissed back. She was looking a lot paler, too, her tired face lined with worry. Remus had never seen Lily and James snap at each other before. It felt horrible. “没有必要这样！”Lily咬牙切齿地回答。她看起来也苍白许多，疲惫的脸上布满了担忧。Remus从未见过Lily和James如此争吵，感觉很糟糕。

Harry was fussing, flailing his arms and making a face. Lily was taking no chances now - they went everywhere as a family, or nowhere at all. Harry在烦躁，挥舞着手臂，做出各种表情。Lily现在不敢冒险——他们要么全家一起去哪里，要么干脆不去。

“Shh,” she jiggled him on her hip, “Quiet now, Mummy and Daddy are busy...” “嘘，”她在臀部晃动他，“安静点，妈妈和爸爸在忙……”

“Give him here,” Sirius held out his arms, “We’ll have a little play, won’t we Harry?” He lifted the little boy up, and Harry squirmed and giggled delightedly. “把他给我，”Sirius伸出双臂，“我们来玩一会儿，好吗，Harry？”他抱起小男孩，Harry愉快地扭动着身子，咯咯笑个不停。

He wasn’t saying many words yet - ‘Da-da’, ‘Ma-ma’, ‘No!’ and, for some reason, ‘bike!’ were about the extent of it. But he knew his godfather. Remus wondered if it was the smell of old leather. His own experiences with Harry were hit and miss. They got on ok until the kid started crying - and Remus was no good at pretend play, like Sirius was. 他还不会说太多话——‘Da-da’，‘Ma-ma’，‘No!’以及奇怪的‘bike!’大概就是他能说的范围。但他认识他的教父。Remus想知道这是否是旧皮革的味道。他自己与Harry的经历有时好有时坏。他们相处得还不错，直到小孩开始哭泣——而Remus不像Sirius那样擅长假装游戏。

The pair settled down on the living room floor, Sirius with his legs splayed out, Harry between them. Sirius pulled a little toy train out of one of his jacket pockets, and Harry began pushing it across the bumpy rug, burbling happily to himself. Sirius beamed at him. He was so good with children. Remus felt a weird sense of dissonance - did Sirius want kids of his own, one day? They’d never discussed it, and Remus had never had the slightest interest. He didn’t feel qualified to be a parent, and he wasn’t sure he ever would. 他们俩在客厅地板上坐下，Sirius双腿张开，Harry在他们之间。Sirius从他的夹克口袋里拿出一个小火车，Harry开始在凹凸不平的地毯上推着火车，开心地咕哝着。Sirius对他笑容满面。他对孩子们非常好。Remus感到一种奇怪的失调感——Sirius将来是否想要自己的孩子？他们从未讨论过这个问题，Remus也从未对此有过丝毫兴趣。他觉得自己不适合做父母，而且不确定自己是否会适合。

Maybe it was that, then. Maybe that was why Sirius was acting so strangely? 也许就是这样。也许这就是Sirius表现得如此奇怪的原因？

Remus’s private worries were interrupted then, by Dumbledore, who cleared his throat, commanding everyone’s attention. Remus的私人担忧被打断了，邓布利多清了清喉咙，引起了大家的注意。

“We have reason to believe,” he said, quite calmly, “That Voldemort’s focus has changed.” “我们有理由相信，”他说，声音非常平静，“伏地魔的注意力发生了变化。”

Everyone looked up, even Sirius. 大家都抬起头来，甚至Sirius也如此。

“We’ve received some information that the Dark Lord has become aware of a prophecy that was made early last year, which seemed to refer directly to him.” “我们收到了一些信息，黑魔王已经知道了去年年初做出的一个预言，这个预言似乎直接提到了他。”

“A prophecy?” Peter leaned forward, “What prophecy? What did it say?” “一个预言？”Peter前倾着身子，“什么预言？说了什么？”

“It is better that we share only the most pertinent details,” Dumbledore said sharply, “Particularly in mixed company.” “最好只分享最相关的细节，”邓布利多尖锐地说，“尤其是在混合人员中。”

Everyone looked around the room. Remus felt a bit queasy - he did not consider the people congregated to be ‘mixed company’. They were his friends; his comrades, and the people he trusted with his life. He tried to catch Sirius’s eye, hoping for some reassurance, but Sirius quickly looked away. 大家在房间里环顾四周。Remus感到有些恶心——他不认为聚集在一起的人是“混合人员”。他们是他的朋友；他的战友，是他把性命托付给的那些人。他试图与Sirius对视，希望得到一些安慰，但Sirius迅速转过了脸。

“So he’s changed his focus,” James said, breaking the discomforting quiet, “What does he want now?” “所以他的注意力发生了变化，”James打破了令人不安的沉默，“他现在想要什么？”

“In short, Mr Potter,” Dumbledore said, directly, “He wants you. Or rather, your son.” “简而言之，Potter先生，”邓布利多直接说，“他想要你。或者说，你的儿子。”

Lily let out a horrible gasp, her hand flying to her mouth. James gripped the arms of his chair. Peter had an odd sort of nervous spasm. Sirius gathered Harry up and stood at once, “ What?! ” Lily发出一声可怕的喘息声，手飞快地捂住了嘴巴。James紧握着椅子的扶手。Peter出现了一种奇怪的神经性抽搐。Sirius立刻抱起Harry站了起来，“什么？！”

“I am sorry,” Dumbledore said, steadily, “But I have it on very good authority--” “对不起，”邓布利多稳重地说，“但我有非常可靠的消息——”

“ Who’s authority?” Lily asked, sounding strangled. “谁的权威？”Lily问，声音听起来很窒息。

“That I cannot say. I will not place anyone else in danger.” “这个我不能说。我不想让其他人处于危险之中。”

“There’s a spy, then,” Peter said, wringing his hands anxiously, “On their side, I mean?” “那就是说，组织里有间谍，”Peter焦急地搓着手，“在他们那边，我是说？”

“I cannot say.” Dumbledore repeated. “我不能说。”邓布利多重复道。

“Well you’d better say something useful!” James returned, almost shouting, “What do you mean my son?! How can Voldemort even know about Harry?!” “那你最好说点有用的！”James几乎在喊，“你说我的儿子是什么意思？！伏地魔怎么可能知道Harry？”

“We can’t trust anybody.” Sirius said, quietly. “我们不能相信任何人。”Sirius安静地说。

James turned to look at him, a look of pure disbelief. Inwardly Remus was relieved. James trusted his friends - of course he did. Sirius was being paranoid. James转向看着他，脸上写满了纯粹的不相信。内心深处，Remus感到松了一口气。James信任他的朋友——当然，他信任他们。Sirius正变得多疑。

“But why Harry?!” Lily asked, shrilly. “但为什么是Harry？！”Lily尖声问道。

“Voldemort believes that Harry will one day grow up to defeat him.” “伏地魔相信Harry有一天会长大并打败他。”

“Is that what the prophecy said?” “这就是预言所说的？”

Dumbledore inclined his head slightly, as if considering this. “这是伏地魔的信念。”他说，最后说道：“而这就等于预言的内容。”

“You’ll have to hide,” Sirius said, talking directly to James now,“All three of you. There have to be more charms - stronger magic we haven’t tried yet - we’ll send you to bloody Timbuktu if we have to!” “你们必须藏起来，”Sirius直接对James说道，“你们三个。必须有更多的保护咒语——更强的魔法我们还没试过——如果需要的话，我们会把你们送到他妈的Tim-buktu！”

“Padfoot,” James said, raising a hand, “Calm down.” “Padfoot，”James举起手，“冷静点。”

“I will not!” Sirius shouted, red in the face. For a weird split-second, Remus didn’t recognise him at all. “我不会冷静！”Sirius大声喊道，脸色通红。在那一瞬间，Remus甚至完全不认识他。

Harry started crying, reaching for his mother. Lily took him and cuddled him close, kissing his fine black hair and whispering soothing nonsense. Harry开始哭泣，伸手向母亲。Lily接过他，紧紧抱着他，亲吻他那柔软的黑发，低声安抚着他。

“Sirius is right,” Dumbledore said, still infuriatingly calm, “You will have to hide. Plans are already in motion.” “Sirius说得对，”邓布利多仍然愤人不已地冷静地说，“你们必须藏起来。计划已经在进行中了。”

“How soon can we go?” James asked. “Today?”

“Soon.” Dumbledore said. “I will come for you.”

“Ok.” James nodded. “Ok. Right. Good.”

“You will all remain vigilant, I trust,” Dumbledore continued, beginning his closing address. He looked at each of them, as if to impress the gravity of the situation. When he met Remus’s eyes, Remus made sure to stare back, and tried to transmit an aura of reliability and strength. Dumbledore gave the briefest of nods, before moving on to Peter. “你们都会保持警惕，我相信，”邓布利多继续说道，开始了他的结束讲话。他看着每一个人，仿佛要强调这个情况的严重性。当他与Remus对视时，Remus确保回以凝视，尽力传达一种可靠和坚强的气息。邓布利多稍微点了点头，然后转向Peter。

“And none of you will share this information with anyone outside of this room.” “你们任何人都不会将这个信息告诉房间外的人。”

They all nodded. Remus’s head was spinning - if Lily and James went into hiding, what did that mean? Would they be stuck in Moody’s cellar, like he’d been? He dearly hoped not, he wouldn’t wish that on anybody, least of all his best friends and their baby. 他们都点了点头。Remus的头脑感到眩晕——如果Lily和James躲藏起来，那意味着什么？他们会像他一样被困在Moody的地下室里吗？他非常希望不会，他不愿将这样的命运强加于任何人，更不愿对他的最好的朋友和他们的孩子。

Once Dumbledore had left, they walked out of the cottage, into the thick amber evening sunlight, and looked at each other again. Harry had fallen asleep by now, nestled in Lily’s robes, one chubby hand fisting her long red plait. 当邓布利多离开后，他们走出了小屋，走进了浓厚的琥珀色晚阳下，再次互相看了一眼。Harry现在已经睡着了，蜷缩在Lily的袍子里，一只胖乎乎的手抓着她长长的红色辫子。

“You’d better all come over for dinner,” James said, with a strained smile. “Just in case we don’t get another chance.” “你们最好都来吃晚餐，”James带着勉强的微笑说道，“以防我们没有另一个机会。”

A lump developed in Remus’s throat, and lodged there for the rest of the night. Remus的喉咙里起了个疙瘩，并且在整个夜晚都卡在那里。

Still, they had a nice time. Gully the house elf prepared a full Sunday roast at short notice - glorious roast beef, golden roast potatoes and fluffy yorkshire pudding, two kinds of stuffing, mouth-watering rich dark gravy, carrots, parsnips, peas, broccoli… Remus hadn’t eaten on that scale since Hogwarts. 尽管如此，他们还是度过了一个愉快的时光。Gully，那个家养小精灵，临时准备了一顿丰盛的星期天晚餐——美味的烤牛肉、金黄的烤土豆和蓬松的约克郡布丁，两种馅料，令人垂涎的浓厚深色肉汁、胡萝卜、欧防风、豌豆、花椰菜……Remus自霍格沃茨以来没吃过这么丰盛的饭菜。

Before they began, James raised his glass to toast, “To our friends,” he said, shooting a slightly pointed glance at Sirius, “Who’ve always been there for us, through thick and thin - Lily, Harry and I love you all so much.” 在他们开始之前，James举起酒杯祝酒，“为了我们的朋友们，”他说，瞄了一眼Sirius，“他们一直在我们身边，无论顺境逆境——Lily、Harry和我都非常爱你们。”

Remus had to excuse himself after draining his glass. He spent a few minutes composing himself in the downstairs loo. When he came out, and returned to the table, Sirius was watching him again, his eyes narrow, his mouth an inscrutable straight line. Remus喝光酒杯后不得不离开。他在楼下的厕所里花了几分钟平静下来。当他出来，回到桌前时，Sirius再次注视着他，眼神狡黠，嘴巴紧抿成一条直线。

* * *

Wednesday 10th June 1981

 

Two days later, Sirius disappeared in the night. He must have crept away deliberately, because Remus didn’t even realise until he woke up the next morning, and rolled into the cold empty pillow. He sat up, confused. 两天后，Sirius在夜里消失了。他一定是故意溜走的，因为Remus直到第二天早上醒来时才意识到，转身发现冷冷的空枕头。他坐起来，感到困惑。

“Sirius?” He called to the rest of the flat. It was empty. “Sirius？”他喊着整个公寓。里面空无一人。

He got up and went to the living room, and checked the kitchen - sometimes they left each other notes. There was nothing. But Sirius’s shoes were gone, and the keys to the bike, so he must have left of his own free will, at least. 他起身走到客厅，检查了厨房——有时候他们会留给对方纸条。什么也没有。但Sirius的鞋子不见了，还有摩托车的钥匙，所以他一定是自愿离开的，至少。

Remus sat at the kitchen table and waited, chain smoking. He wanted to contact someone, but there wasn’t anyone who he was sure he could trust - Sirius’s conspiracy theorising was starting to get to him. Remus坐在厨房的桌子旁等着，接连抽烟。他想联系某人，但没有他确定可以信任的对象——Sirius的阴谋论开始让他感到困扰。

Finally, the front door clicked open, and Sirius’s familiar footfall could be heard entering the flat. Remus almost got up and ran to meet him - but he had been treating Sirius with kid gloves ever since James’s attack. 最后，前门咔哒一声打开，Sirius熟悉的脚步声传来。Remus差点儿站起来跑去迎接他——但自从James被袭击后，他一直对Sirius十分小心。

“Moony?” “Moony？”

“In here.” “在这里。”

“Oh, hello,” Sirius stood in the kitchen doorway. He looked flushed - he must have been on the bike. “All right?” “哦，你好，”Sirius站在厨房门口。他看起来有些脸红——他一定是骑了摩托车。“一切还好吗？”

“Where have you been? I was worried!” “你去哪里了？我很担心！”

“Sorry.” He pulled a face and came to sit down at the table too. Remus watched him. He seemed happy. His hair smelled of the countryside, and he was sweating a bit through his black t-shirt - it was gearing up to be a very warm summer. He picked up the cigarette packet, took one out with his teeth and snapped his fingers to light it. “对不起。”他做了个鬼脸，坐到桌旁。Remus看着他。他似乎很开心。他的头发有乡村的气息，他的黑色T恤上有些汗水——夏天正变得非常炎热。他拿起香烟包，用牙齿抽出一支，弹了弹手指点燃。

Remus waited patiently. Remus耐心地等着。

“It happened,” Sirius said, finally, his face shining strangely, pearlescent in the weak light of morning. “They’re hidden.” “事情发生了，”Sirius终于说道，他的脸在清晨微弱的光线中闪耀着奇怪的光泽，“他们已经藏起来了。”

“Lily and James?” Remus squinted, scratching his head, “How?” “Lily和James？”Remus眯着眼睛，挠了挠头，“怎么回事？”

“Dumbledore sorted it all.” “邓布利多安排好了。”

Why didn’t you take me with you? Remus wanted to ask, before scolding himself for having such a selfish thought. That wasn't the important bit. “Is it safe? I gave James a whole scroll of security charms to use, did he--” 为什么你不带我一起去？Remus想问，却在心里责备自己有这么自私的想法。那不是重点。“安全么？我给了James一整卷安全咒语，他用了吗？”

“They won’t need any of that,” Sirius waved a hand. He seemed weirdly triumphant, as if he had just bested Remus at a game of chess. “Dumbledore came up with something better.” “他们不需要那些，”Sirius挥了挥手。他显得异常得意，仿佛刚刚在一场棋局中战胜了Remus。“邓布利多想出了更好的办法。”

“What?” “什么？”

“The fidelius charm.” “Fidelius咒语。”

“The…” Remus frowned. He vaguely remembered having read about that… something to do with implanting a secret into another person. It was powerful stuff, he knew that much. No one would be able to break it, except the secret keeper themselves. “Well, that’ll do it, I suppose.” He said. “But wouldn’t they need someone to put the secret in ?… is it Dumbledore?” “那……”Remus皱起了眉头。他模糊地记得读过有关这个咒语的东西……与将秘密植入另一个人有关。他知道这是一种强大的魔法。除了秘密保管者自己，没有人能破解它。“嗯，我想这会有效。”他说。“但他们需要一个人来植入秘密吗？……是邓布利多吗？”

“He volunteered,” Sirius said. “But in the end, we thought it was better if it was one of us.” “他自愿的，”Sirius说道。“但最后，我们认为由我们中的一个人来做会更好。”

“One of us..?” It dawned on Remus all of a sudden, as if Sirius had dumped a bucket of ice over his head. “No.” Remus said, shaking his head. “我们中的一个人？”突然间，Remus明白了，就像Sirius往他头上倒了一桶冰水。“不。”Remus说，摇摇头。

Sirius was staring at him intensely, his eyes dark blue and more serious than they had ever been. Remus wanted to hit him. Shake him. Wring his neck. Anything to get some sense in his stupid thick skull. “No.” He said again. “It’s too dangerous!” Sirius紧紧地盯着他，眼神深蓝，比以往任何时候都要严肃。Remus想打他。摇他。掐他的脖子。做任何事情来让他那愚蠢的脑袋里有些明白。“不。”他再次说道。“这太危险了！”

“Moony…” Sirius started, “Moony……”Sirius开始说道，

“Don’t you ‘Moony’ me!” Remus said sharply, standing up. He had to pace; had to move, just to keep up with his thoughts. “It’s stupid! It’s the stupidest idea you’ve ever had!” “别叫我‘Moony’！”Remus严厉地说道，站起来。他必须走来走去；必须移动，只为跟上他的思绪。“这太愚蠢了！这是你曾经最愚蠢的主意！”

“It’s not my idea--” “这不是我的主意——”

“Don’t tell me you didn’t volunteer!” Remus rounded on him, furious, “Don’t tell me you didn’t jump at the chance!” “别告诉我你没有自愿！”Remus愤怒地对着他，“别告诉我你没有抓住这个机会！”

“To help my best friends?! To help Harry?! Of course I did!” Sirius was shouting too, and it was awful. “为了帮助我最好的朋友们？！为了帮助Harry？！当然我会！”Sirius也在大喊，这真是糟糕。

“Find someone else!” Remus begged, “Anyone! I’ll do it!” “找其他人！”Remus恳求道，“谁都行！我来做！”

“You can’t.” Sirius shook his head, “It has to be me, you know it does.” “你不行。”Sirius摇了摇头，“必须是我，你知道的。”

“No!” “不！”

“You can’t just keep saying ‘no’. It’s done. It’s dealt with.” “你不能只是一直说‘不’。已经决定了。这件事已经解决了。”

Remus really thought he was going to hit Sirius for a moment. Hit him, or burst into tears like a child. He did neither. He sat down, hard, and covered his face with his hands. Remus真的以为自己会打Sirius一顿。打他，或者像孩子一样哭出来。他都没有。他用力坐下，双手掩面。

“You bastard.” He muttered. “你这个混蛋。”他嘟囔道。

“It’s going to be ok. I’ve made sure.” Sirius said, reaching out to him. Remus batted his hand away. “一切都会好的。我已经确保了。”Sirius说道，伸手去摸他。Remus打掉了他的手。

“You just did it?! Without even telling me?” “你就这么做了？！甚至没告诉我？”

“I’m telling you now!” “我现在告诉你！”

Remus glared at him. He was going to say something he regretted, in a minute. If he didn’t leave, he was going to say something he could never take back. He swallowed his rage, stood up, and walked out of the flat. Remus怒视着他。他很快就会说出让他后悔的话。如果他不离开，他会说出一些永远无法挽回的话。他咽下愤怒，站起来，走出了公寓。

* * *

Friday 24th July 1981

So it was done. After that argument, everything happened very quickly. There were no goodbyes, Lily, James and Harry simply vanished without a trace. Remus knew better than to ask where they were - he wanted them to be safe, after all. And he wanted Sirius to be safe.

The Order was told that the Potters had gone into hiding; that Voldemort was after them because of Lily’s blood status, and her marriage to James.

“It’s awful, not trusting anyone, isn’t it?” Peter said as they left that meeting.

“Yeah.” Remus agreed glumly.

“It’s necessary.” Sirius said. “And if I knew who the spy was, I’d kill them myself. I wouldn’t even need magic.”

Peter and Remus stared at him, shocked.

“Sirius,” Remus said, putting a hand on is shoulder, “We can’t start acting like death eaters - James wouldn’t want--”

“James doesn’t want his child to be murdered by a lunatic on a power trip!” Sirius ranted, jerking away from Remus’s touch, “You’ve gone soft, Moony.” “James不想让他的孩子被一个发疯的权力狂谋杀！”Sirius愤怒地叫道，甩开了Remus的触碰，“你变软了，Moony。”

If I have, Remus though to himself, it’s because of you . No one fell in love with a hard heart; he’d learnt that lesson more than once.

Still, as dreadfully as Sirius was acting, Remus was inclined to make some allowances. It was a very difficult time - the darkest point in the war - and everyone was handling the pressure differently. Peter and Marlene threw themselves into work - they were rarely seen not rushing to one place or another. Mary seemed to withdraw into the muggle world more - she was always around when you needed her, but her mind often seemed to be in two places. Remus had his drinking and his self-pity. So if Sirius wanted to be the angry one for a bit, fine.

But it was still a war - war does not make allowances, or give anyone time to catch their breath. It is relentless and unforgiving, and unimaginably cruel.

It was only a week or so before Harry’s first birthday. Sirius had just got in from Diagon Alley - he’d gone in search of something appropriate for a one year old, and instead returned with an actual broomstick.

“Sirius!”

“Oh come on, Moony, it’s only little!”

“He’s a baby!”

“Got to train him young if he’s ever going to play for England!”

Remus laughed indulgently and sipped his tea while he watched Sirius wrap the toy. He hadn’t seen him so happy in a while, and it was so nice. Then it happened.

Remus耐心地笑了笑，喝了一口茶，看着Sirius包好玩具。他已经很久没见过Sirius如此开心了，感觉真好。然后，事情发生了。

There was a strange scent first, which only Remus picked up. Familiar and friendly, magical. Then, in a flash of bright light, an enormous silver Patronus burst through the wall. It was a lioness, and it prowled the room, snarling.

首先传来了一种奇怪的气味，只有Remus感知到了。熟悉而友好，充满魔力。然后，在一阵明亮的闪光中，一只巨大的银色守护神冲破了墙壁。它是一只母狮，徘徊在房间里，发出咆哮声。

“Fucking hell!” Sirius leapt up, backing away.

“该死！”Sirius跳了起来，向后退去。

The huge cat looked at them both with plaintive eyes and opened its mouth. The scream that emanated from it was bone-chilling and all too familiar. It was Mary.

那只巨大的猫用悲伤的眼神看着他们，张开了嘴。它发出的尖叫声令人毛骨悚然，非常熟悉。那是Mary的声音。

“Help!” It wailed, “Hollyhock House!”

“救命！”它哀嚎道，“Hollyhock House！”

And then it vanished.

然后它消失了。

“That’s the McKinnon’s address.” Remus said, getting up to put his shoes on.

“那是McKinnon的地址。”Remus说道，起身穿上鞋子。

“Where are you going?” Sirius asked.

“你要去哪里？”Sirius问道。

“To help Mary!” Remus said, impatiently, fumbling with his laces, “Come on!”

“去救Mary！”Remus不耐烦地说道，一边笨拙地绑鞋带，“快来！”

“Moony, no,” Sirius said, “We can’t, we have to follow protocol, contact Moody, or Arthur, or Frank, or--”

“Moony，不行，”Sirius说道，“我们不能，我们必须遵循程序，联系Moody，Arthur，或者Frank，或者——”

“Fuck protocol!” Remus shouted, “It’s Mary! She asked for help and I’m going. Stay here if you want.”

“去他妈的程序！”Remus大喊道，“这是Mary！她求救了，我要去。你想留在这里就留吧。”

Of course Sirius didn’t stay.

当然，Sirius没有留下来。

They arrived outside Hollyhock House maybe ten minutes after getting Mary’s Patronus. Neither of them had ever been to Marlene’s home before, though she’d described it a few times. It was a lovely old Tudor style cottage, located a few miles outside of a village in Sussex. There was a long garden path, with a border of bright pansies and geraniums—red, purple, yellow, pink. The front door was painted a soft dusky green, and if you craned your neck you could just make out the tops of three Quidditch hoops in the back garden.

他们在收到Mary的守护神后的十分钟左右到达了Hollyhock House。他们之前从未去过Marlene的家，尽管她曾几次描述过。那是一座漂亮的老式都铎风格的小屋，位于Sussex的一个村庄外几英里处。那里有一条长长的花园小径，边界上种着明亮的紫罗兰和天竺葵——红色、紫色、黄色、粉色。前门涂成柔和的灰绿色，如果你伸长脖子，你可以隐约看到后花园里三根魁地奇球门的顶部。

It might have been pretty, anyway. But not today.

本来可能很漂亮。但今天却不是这样。

Mary was standing at the top of the path by the roadside, frozen, staring blankly up at the blue sky. The Dark Mark hung over the yellow thatched roof; an enormous black cloud, the unmistakable shapes of skull and snake.

Mary站在小径的顶端靠近路边，僵硬地站着，呆呆地望着蓝天。黑魔标记悬在黄色茅草屋顶上方；一团巨大的黑云，显然是骷髅和蛇的形状。

“No!” Remus gasped. Mary turned to him with tears in her eyes,

“不要！”Remus倒抽一口冷气。Mary转向他，眼中含泪，

“They’re all dead.” She said.

“他们都死了。”她说。

“Are you sure?” Sirius said, taking a few steps up the path, wand raised.

“你确定吗？”Sirius问道，走上小径几步，举起了魔杖。

“Yes.” She said, “Yes, they’re all lined up very neatly.”

“是的。”她说，“是的，他们都整齐地排成一排。”

“What?” He looked back at her, frowning.

“什么？”他回头看着她，皱起眉头。

“Lined up… in a row…” she repeated. She swayed for a moment, and Remus put his arms around her, in case she was going to faint. She leaned into him, weeping silently.

“排成一排……排成一行……”她重复道。她摇晃了一下，Remus抱住了她，以防她晕倒。她依偎在他身边，默默地哭泣。

“Stay with her.” Sirius said, continuing up the path. Remus began to tremble. It was like a nightmare; like a horror film. He watched Sirius approach the door, push it open, call inside.

“照顾她。”Sirius说道，继续上小径。Remus开始颤抖。这就像是一场噩梦；像是一部恐怖片。他看着Sirius走向门口，推开门，呼喊里面。

“We were supposed to meet for lunch today, but she never came,” Mary whispered against Remus’s shoulder, still clinging to him, “I thought she was just busy at the hospital… I tried to find her after work, but they said she’d never gone in… so I came here and I…”

“我们今天应该约好一起吃午饭，但她从未出现，”Mary在Remus的肩膀上低声说道，仍紧紧抱着他，“我以为她只是忙于医院……我下班后去找她，但他们说她从未去过……所以我来了这里，我……”

“It’s ok,” Remus said, because what else do you say?

“没事的，”Remus说道，因为还有什么话可以说呢？

“The mark was there, and the door was open, and… oh god, Remus! All of them! Her mum, and her stepdad, and Yaz, and Danny… just lying there! Oh my god, their eyes!” She began to sob in earnest, and Remus held her tighter, feeling his insides turn to water.

“黑魔标记在那里，门是开着的，哦天哪，Remus！他们都死了！她的妈妈，她的继父，Yaz，还有Danny……就这样躺在那里！哦我的天，他们的眼睛！”她开始真正地哭泣，Remus紧紧抱住她，感觉内心如水般流淌。

Sirius came out of the house. Even at a distance, Remus could see the look of horror on his face. He made his way quickly towards them.

Sirius走出了房子。即使从远处，Remus也能看到他脸上的恐怖表情。他迅速走向他们。

“I’m going to get Moody,” he said. “I’ll be back as soon as possible, ok? ...don’t go in there.”

“我要去找Moody，”他说道。“我会尽快回来，好的？……不要进去那里。”

And with that, he disappeared with a loud CRACK.

说完，他发出一声巨响，消失了。

“That’s it.” Mary cried, hysterical, “It’s over, I can’t do this anymore!”

“就这样。”Mary哭喊道，情绪失控，“结束了，我再也无法承受了！”

 

Chapter 173: The War: Autumn 1981 

I loved the words you wrote to me

But that was bloody yesterday.

I can't survive on what you send

Every time you need a friend.

 

I saw two shooting stars last night

I wished on them - but they were only satellites

Is it wrong to wish on space hardware?

I wish, I wish, I wish you'd care.

 

I don't want to change the world

I'm not looking for a new England

I'm just looking for another girl.

 

 Nobody knew who had killed the McKinnons, and nobody knew why. There were theories, of course; the most logical being that with Danny and Marlene in the Order, they were simply an obvious target. Some people wondered if it was because of Marlene’s connection to James and Lily - because she’d healed James. Others thought she’d made too much fuss about werewolf rights at work.

In the end, none of it mattered, not to Remus. Why try to make sense out of something so senseless?

Due to Danny’s previous celebrity status, the murders were front page news. There was a huge picture of him in the Daily Prophet, from his Cannons days - broad, sunny face, robes billowing. No scars. A smaller picture of Marlene which must have been taken for work, because she was in her uniform. Promising young Healer, Mylene McKinnon according to the misspelt caption.

Yasmin was not mentioned at all, though Sirius told Remus they were found lying beside each other, and their fingers were still touching.

“Remember in third year,” Sirius said, in the days that followed, “We all thought you two fancied each other.”

“Yeah.” Remus replied, monotone.

“She was a better beater than me. Wish I’d told her.”

“She knew.” Remus said, with a sad smirk.

Mary was not heard from for a long while. Marlene’s death hit her harder than anyone— they had been practically inseparable since they were eleven. Remus remembered how annoying he used to find them, before he figured out that girls were just people too.

Mary长时间没有被听到消息。Marlene的死对她的打击比任何人都要大——自十一岁起，她们几乎形影不离。Remus记得在他意识到女孩也是普通人之前，曾觉得她们非常烦人。

He remembered her quiet patience, her bouts of fiery passion. The petition to remove the Whomping Willow when she was just thirteen, because someone had been hurt, and Marlene could never stand to see anyone hurt, not if there was something she could do about it. If any one of them had it in them to change the world, it had been her. But no more.

他记得她那安静的耐心和时而迸发的激情。她在十三岁时提出移除Whomping Willow的请愿书，因为有人受了伤，Marlene从来无法忍受看到任何人受伤，尤其是她能做些什么的时候。如果他们之中有谁能够改变世界，那就是她。但现在已经没有了。

Another September rolled around, and as always, Remus was reminded of his childhood and Hogwarts. The scent of parchment, new ink, leather book bags, and sealing wax. A sense of fresh beginnings; of change. How can it have been a full decade since he first arrived at King’s Cross, scrawny and angry and neglected?

又一个九月来临，Remus像往常一样被勾起了对童年和霍格沃茨的回忆。羊皮纸的气味、新墨水、皮革书包和封蜡。新开始的感觉；变化的感觉。怎么会已经过去整整十年，自从他第一次到达King’s Cross，瘦弱、愤怒、被忽视？

So much had changed since then. He had become a man. He had learnt more than he ever thought possible, achieved things he had never dreamed of—his horizons had been expanded again and again, by education, and magic, and friendship, and love. He wasn’t completely different, of course. Remus didn’t kid himself; his temper hadn’t really gone anywhere, nor had his proclivity to repress bad feelings, only to lash out when things got too much.

自那时起，许多事情发生了变化。他已经成为了一个男人。他学到了比他想象中更多的东西，实现了他从未梦想过的成就——他的视野一次又一次地被教育、魔法、友谊和爱扩展。当然，他并没有完全改变。Remus并没有自欺欺人；他的脾气并没有真的改变，他压抑坏情绪的倾向依然存在，只是当事情变得过于沉重时才会爆发。

But he thought he’d been doing better, at least with the people he loved. At least with Sirius. He had opened up and revealed more of himself to Sirius than to anyone else. He had shared feelings which every instinct told him to keep hidden. It hadn’t always been easy—they had fought, they had shouted, they had cried. But it had been worth it.

但他觉得自己做得更好了，至少对待他所爱的人。至少是对Sirius。他向Sirius敞开了心扉，展示了更多的自己。分享了那些每一个本能都告诉他要隐藏的感情。这并不总是容易——他们曾争吵、呐喊、哭泣。但这都是值得的。

At least, Remus thought it had.

至少，Remus觉得是这样。

He wasn’t so sure about Sirius. Maybe it was the toll of the war—too many deaths, too many near misses. Maybe it was the separation from James. Maybe Remus had just tested his patience one too many times. He couldn’t put his finger on it. All Remus knew was that something was very, very wrong.

他对Sirius不那么确定了。也许是战争的代价——太多的死亡，太多的险些发生的事。也许是与James的分离。也许是Remus已经一次又一次地试探了他的耐心。他无法确定是什么问题。Remus只知道，有些事情非常非常不对劲。

It was mid-September by the time he really realised it had happened. Sirius had slipped away from him. They were often apart - Remus had come to see this as a fact of life; their skills were so different, they had different jobs to do. It was nothing, in service of the war. They were glad to do it, and proud to do it.

But after some weeks, Remus came to see that this distance was something else, more than just the usual stress. Sirius had pulled back.

“Miss you.” Remus said, one night. It had taken all day to raise the courage for those two stupid words.

“I’m right here.” Sirius smiled tiredly, sitting across the table, picking at dinner with his fork.

Then, after a while, he spoke again; “It’ll all be over soon. We have to trust Dumbledore, that's all.”

Remus could have wept.

“But you’re the only one I trust.”

Sirius just looked at him, sadly. Remus couldn’t bear that look, it made him feel stupid for being in love. Stupid for caring about anything other than winning the war.

Finally Sirius got up. He picked up his plate and dumped the contents in the bin.

“Got to go.” He said. “Moody wants me to check in. Be back late, don’t stay up waiting.”

He didn’t kiss him goodbye.

Remus was at a loss. Once again, he found himself with a problem that was almost unspeakable. He couldn’t ask James or Lily—even if he knew how to reach them, they had plenty to worry about on their own. Peter had never been very keen to hear about anything to do with Remus and Sirius’s relationship, and though he was a good mate—one of Remus’s best mates—they didn’t really confide in each other like that. Marlene might have helped, but Remus didn’t want to think about it. And of course, Mary’s grief didn’t leave much room for romantic advice.

Remus陷入了困境。再次，他面临着一个几乎无法言说的问题。他不能去问James或Lily——即使他知道如何联系他们，他们自己也有很多担忧。Peter对Remus和Sirius的关系从未很感兴趣，尽管他是个好朋友——Remus最好的朋友之一——但他们并不真正像那样互相倾诉。Marlene可能会帮忙，但Remus不想去想她。而且，Mary的悲痛没有留下多少提供浪漫建议的空间。

Deep down, Remus knew that he ought to ask Sirius outright. Except.

Except he was terrified of the answer. He was terrified that it wasn’t about the war, or James or growing up. He was terrified that the problem was him. What if Sirius had just fallen out of love?

在内心深处，Remus知道他应该直接问Sirius。但。

但他害怕答案。他害怕这不是关于战争、James或成长的问题。他害怕问题是他自己。如果Sirius只是失去了爱？

This anxiety worried away at Remus as the nights drew in and the days turned colder. It all seemed to make a horrible kind of sense; the distance, the unwillingness to talk, the lack of affection, their non-existent sex life. And that look. The look Sirius kept leveling at him—as if Remus was a stranger.

随着夜晚的降临和日子的变冷，这种焦虑困扰着Remus。一切似乎都变得令人恐怖地合理；距离、不愿交谈、缺乏感情、几乎不存在的性生活。还有那种目光。Sirius对他的目光——仿佛Remus是个陌生人。

It was intolerable. Remus didn’t know if he could cope with another loss.

这是无法忍受的。Remus不知道自己是否能承受另一个失落。

So, in early October, when Moody had an assignment for him, Remus was hopeful. Mad-eye took him aside at the end of an Order meeting,

于是，在十月初，当Moody有一个任务交给他时，Remus感到了一丝希望。Mad-eye在一场Order会议结束时把他拉到一边，

“We’ve had eyes on the pack.” he grunted.

“我们已经盯上了那群人。”他咕哝道。

“Greyback?”

“Don’t think so. The insurgents, we reckon. They’re hiding out in a forest in Germany.”

“Oh,” Remus said, surprised. Was it Castor? “Have they attacked someone?”

“No, been keeping their heads down, by the looks of things.”

“That’s good, isn’t it?” Remus said, “We ought to just leave them alone.”

“Trust me, lad, I’d prefer to,” Moody replied, with a wry smile, “But desperate times call for desperate measures. We’re sending you out.”

“To do what? They left Greyback - they left Voldemort. Wasn’t that the plan?”

“It was. Two years ago. We’ve lost a lot of good people since then. Notice how cosy these meetings are getting?”

It was true. The first Order meeting Remus had attended had been overwhelming - the room was packed with witches and wizards ready to fight; to take on the death eaters. Now there were too many missing faces - the McKinnons and the Potters, the Prewetts, old Darius Barebones, Dorcas, Caradoc Dearborn, Benjy Fenwick, Ferox…

“So…” Remus thought hard, “Now you want to recruit the werewolves?”

“Bingo.”

“After years of legislating against them? After forcing them out of jobs? Out of their homes ?!” Remus knew he was being rude - no one spoke to Alastor Moody like that - but he was too tired, too battle-weary to care.

Moody didn’t seem fazed. Remus supposed he got a lot worse abuse from much scarier wizards.

“We know it’s a bit of a big ask. But as I said, desperate times.”

“And is there anything I can offer them in return for, y’know, their lives?!”

“Voldemort’s worse.” Moody returned, “Whatever their lives are now, Voldemort will only make them worse.”

Remus sighed heavily. “Fine.”

He was ready to go, anyway. He was ready for a change; ready to get out of London, out of his miserable life and back to being useful. He even entertained the idea that a long absence might help the Sirius situation. Didn’t absence make the heart grow fonder?

It might be a relief; some breathing space, some time to think. He tested this theory, in his last conversation with Sirius.

“You’ll be glad to have a few weeks off, eh?” He smiled - which took every bit of his strength.

“Hm?” Sirius frowned, looking up from some blueprints he’d been scanning. He looked annoyed at the interruption, and Remus felt a horrible tearing inside his chest. “What did you say?”

“I said you’ll be glad to be rid of me, for a bit.” Remus continued, bravely. “Have me out of the way.”

“Why would you say it like that?” Sirius stared at him, blankly.

“Like what? I just meant… you know, you can have some time to think.”

“There’s no time to think, not until the war’s over.” Sirius snapped, returning to his blueprints, “It’ll be the same whether you’re here or not.”

“没有时间去考虑，战争结束之前都是这样。”Sirius厉声说道，重新回到他的蓝图上，“无论你在不在这里都是一样的。”

That was all Remus could take. He picked up his wand and a packet of cigarettes and left for Germany with only the briefest of goodbyes—as if he was only popping to the shops. He fumed, as he walked to the portkey location. That prick! Give him two weeks on his own, then he’d see; then he’d realise what a dickhead he was being.

这已经是Remus能忍受的极限。他拿起他的魔杖和一包香烟，仅仅留下了简短的告别——仿佛他只是去商店一样，便离开了前往德国。他愤怒地走向传送门的位置。那个混蛋！让他自己待两周，然后他就会明白；然后他就会意识到自己有多么的愚蠢。

Remus would come back, fresh and wild from the forests, and Sirius would be so sorry, so affectionate, and there would be time to talk and mend, and fall in love again.

Remus会回来，带着森林中的新鲜和野性，而Sirius会感到非常抱歉，非常亲热，然后就会有时间去谈谈和修复，再次相爱。

That was all they needed; a bit more time.

* * *

Tuesday, 13 October 1981

Remus was right, too. At least for himself, he did feel much better once he’d left the country. It was so much easier not to think about Sirius - or anything at all in the wizarding world - while he was hidden away in the velvety depths of the Black Forest.

He chose to arrive the afternoon before the full moon - best to approach the pack as a wolf.

The transformation was quick—the woods around him were teaming with life and ancient magic, amplifying the razor sharp power of the full moon. The night itself was as familiar and terrifying as his wolf pelt. The pack found him, close to dawn. They welcomed him home with glee and gathered around, throwing back their necks to howl gorgeously up at the night sky, until the stars rang with their singing.

变身迅速——四周的森林充满了生机和古老的魔法，放大了满月锋利的力量。夜晚既熟悉又可怕，就像他的狼皮一样。黎明将至，狼群找到了他。他们欢欣鼓舞地欢迎他回家，围绕着他，仰起脖子，优美地在夜空中嚎叫，直到星星都在他们的歌声中震颤。

As they all returned to human form, Remus writhed back into life amongst a scrum of other bodies, and Castor’s hands on him, already healing his wounds.

当他们都变回人形时，Remus在其他身体的混乱中挣扎着回到现实，Castor的手已经在他身上，开始疗愈他的伤口。

“It is good to see you, Remus Lupin.”

“见到你很高兴，Remus Lupin。”

They all walked slowly through the trees as the butter yellow October light filtered down onto the leaf litter.

他们缓慢地穿过树林，黄油般的十月阳光透过树叶洒在地上的落叶上。

In the time the pack had been living there, they had constructed a small village of wattle huts to live in. They all curled up to sleep on soft dry moss with birdsong trilling overhead.

在狼群居住的时间里，他们建造了一个小村庄，由柳条编成的小屋组成。他们蜷缩在柔软干燥的苔藓上睡觉，头顶传来鸟儿的鸣唱。

Remus woke up without knots in his shoulders, and without his jaw clenched. He was relaxed for the first time in months. Castor lay beside him, so warm, and so peaceful, his soft brown skin pressing against Remus’s in places. Remembering his humanity, Remus pulled away slightly. Castor’s eyes opened and peered into his.

Remus醒来时肩膀没有紧绷，咬紧的下巴也放松了。他第一次在几个月里感到放松。Castor躺在他旁边，温暖而宁静，他柔软的棕色皮肤在某些地方贴在Remus身上。意识到自己的身份，Remus稍微退后了一些。Castor的眼睛睁开了，凝视着他。

“Are you well, Remus Lupin?”

“Yes, fine thanks.” He rubbed his eyes. Castor kept watching him.

“You are suffering.” He said. A statement, not a question.

“I’ve lost some people.” Remus said, “We’re losing the war.”

“Yes,” Castor agreed. “And you have come to ask for our help, is that not so, Remus Lupin?”

“I know it's not a small thing…”

“We will stay here. This is our home.”

“You understand I wouldn’t ask unless the situation was desperate. You understand… Voldemort won’t spare werewolves, either?”

“We do.” Castor said, simply. “And we are agreed. We will stay here. We will hide - we are good at it.”

“I found you.”

“Yes, Remus Lupin. You will always be welcome.”

Remus sat up, and reached for the wolfskin cloak at his feet, covering himself with it.

“Well that's that, then.” He said. “I’d better get back.”

Castor reached up and placed a hand on his arm.

“Stay a while, Remus Lupin. We have so much to show you. Perhaps then you will see.”

So Remus stayed. He thought that if he spent a bit of time with them, as before, he might be able to talk to them, change somebody’s mind. Most of them had wizarding family back in the UK; he had to be able to appeal to them, surely.

所以Remus留下来了。他认为，如果他花点时间和他们在一起，就像以前一样，也许他可以说服他们，改变某些人的想法。他们中的大多数人在英国有巫师家庭；他一定能打动他们的。

He couldn’t go back to the Order without trying—everyone else was giving their whole selves to the fight, and this was, after all, his purpose. If he couldn’t be a decent emissary to the werewolves, then what good was he at all?

他不能在没有尝试的情况下回到凤凰社——其他人都全身心投入战斗，而这毕竟是他的使命。如果他不能成为一个体面的狼人使者，那他还有什么用呢？

Still, it wasn’t a difficult decision to make. It was no great sacrifice. He had nothing to go back to except a very difficult conversation with Sirius.

不过，这并不是一个难以做出的决定。这也不是巨大的牺牲。他没有什么好回去的，除了和Sirius进行一场非常困难的对话。

And he did talk to them. Over the three weeks Remus spent with the werewolves in October 1981, he spoke to each and every one of them. He reasoned, he sermonised, he ranted. But it was no use at all; they were all happy. Not in a mad, deluded ‘everything is perfect’ way, as some of the Greyback followers had been. But in a practical, empowered way—they saw a future for themselves, they saw a way to live a life free from cruelty or intervention. It wasn’t for everyone—it definitely wasn’t for Remus—but he couldn’t deny they were making it work.

他确实和他们交谈了。在1981年10月的三周里，Remus与每一个狼人交谈了。他进行劝说、布道、发泄。但完全没有用；他们都很幸福。不是那种疯狂的、被幻想所困扰的“万事皆美好”，就像一些Greyback的追随者一样。而是一种实际的、充满力量的方式——他们看到了自己的未来，看到了一种摆脱残酷或干预的生活方式。这种生活方式并不适合所有人——对Remus来说绝对不适合——但他不能否认他们在成功地实现这一点。

In fact, as time went on, Remus lost track of who was doing the persuading. Everyone was so keen to take him hunting, to show him how to weave wood, or cast protective spells which made them almost invisible to humans. He was never hungry, or cold, or in fear for his life.

事实上，随着时间的推移，Remus已经失去了谁在说服谁的感觉。每个人都很热衷于带他去打猎，展示如何编织木材，或施放使他们几乎对人类不可见的保护咒语。他从未感到饥饿、寒冷，或对生命的恐惧。

“Do you see now?” Castor asked one evening, as Halloween approached.

“Yes, I see.” Remus replied, staring up at the thatched ceiling. “You’d all rather hide, like cowards.”

“You do not believe that, Remus Lupin.” Castor smirked, settling down to sleep. He occasionally demonstrated actual emotion, now that he and Remus were so close.

Remus had elected to keep sharing a hut with him. He didn’t like sleeping alone, and it wasn’t as if anything was going on; it just made sense. He had to stay close to the leader; it was what anyone would do. And yes, it was an intense relationship, but that simply didn’t mean it was anything to do with sex. That was simply how things were with the werewolves—everything was motivated by scent and instinct and the phases of the moon.

Remus选择继续和他共用一个小屋。他不喜欢一个人睡觉，况且也没有什么事情发生；这只是很自然的事。他必须保持和领袖的接近，这也是任何人都会做的事。是的，这是一种强烈的关系，但这并不意味着这与性有关。这只是狼人世界的常态——一切都由气味、直觉和月亮的阶段决定。

Still, Remus knew how it would look. He didn’t kid himself that Sirius was going to suddenly have a change of heart and come racing desperately to Germany to find him, but Remus knew that it was pretty wrong, even without a chance of getting caught. It was pathetic, too. He scolded himself about it through the long dark nights; you’re a ridiculous excuse for a man. A few weeks feeling ignored and you’re cosying up to the next good looking bloke who shows you any interest. And you haven’t even got the balls to do anything about it.

尽管如此，Remus知道这会给人一种怎样的印象。他不指望Sirius会突然心软，急忙赶到德国来找他，但Remus知道，即使没有被抓住的机会，这也相当不对。这也很可悲。他在漫长的黑夜里自责；你真是个可笑的男人。几周的被忽视，你就对下一个对你表示兴趣的帅哥温情脉脉。你甚至没有勇气去做点什么。

In the end, it was his desire for Castor that told him he needed to leave. And his love for Sirius. Remus had done some very drastic and very stupid things in his life, but he was not going to run away to live in a forest just to escape talking to the love of his life. He would go home, and he would force himself to confront it. He would do everything he could to keep Sirius, because deep down, he knew that it was the only thing that really mattered.

最终，正是对Castor的渴望告诉他他需要离开。还有对Sirius的爱。Remus在一生中做过一些非常激烈和愚蠢的事情，但他不会为了逃避与他生命中的挚爱对话而跑到森林里生活。他会回家，并强迫自己面对它。他会竭尽全力留住Sirius，因为他深知那是唯一真正重要的事。

* * *

 

2nd November 1981

The portkey had closed, and Remus couldn’t get in touch with anyone. He had to get himself back to Britain alone, apparating part of the way, hitching lifts the rest.

传送门已经关闭，Remus无法联系任何人。他不得不独自回到英国，一部分路程靠瞬间移动，剩下的部分则靠搭便车。

By the time Remus had staggered his way into London, he hadn’t even the energy to apparate. He got a bus instead, and fell asleep halfway to Leicester Square. He got off and stopped at his usual corner shop for a pouch of tobacco. He bought two Mars bars as well - if Sirius was in, he could have one. If not then tough luck, Remus would scoff them both.

当Remus摇摇晃晃地走进伦敦时，他甚至没有力气瞬间移动。他改乘了公交车，并在到Leicester Square的半路上睡着了。他下车后停在了他常去的便利店，买了一包烟。他还买了两根Mars巧克力棒——如果Sirius在家，他可以吃一根。如果不在，那就没办法了，Remus就自己把两根都吃了。

As he unlocked his front door, he could hear the phone ringing. It took him a few moments to get in - the wooden frame had swollen with all the rainfall, and the door got gummed up sometimes - but when he got in, it was still ringing. Must be urgent, he thought, absent-mindedly.

当他打开前门时，他能听到电话在响。他花了几分钟才进门——木框因降雨而膨胀，门有时会被粘住——但当他进门时，电话还在响。一定是紧急的，Remus心不在焉地想。

He shouted, “Padfoot? You in?” as he crossed the the room, then lifted the receiver, “Hello?”

“Hello? Hello, Remus, is that you?”

“Mary? Hi! I just got back - where the hell is everybody?!”

There was a strange silence on the end of the phone, and a horrible static prickle ran down his spine. “Mary?!”

“You haven’t heard…”

“Jesus Christ, Mary, what?!”

“Remus… something awful has happened.”

She started explaining, and Remus fell to his knees as the whole world began to fall apart.

 

Chapter 174: Armistice 

He who endured my hardships with me

He now has gone to the fate that awaits mankind

Day and night, I have wept for him

I would not give him over for burial

For what if he had risen at my cries?

Six days and seven nights I waited

Until a worm crawled out of his nose

Since he has gone

There is no life left for me.

* * *

James died first. Remus ought to have expected that. He would have been waiting right at the front door; it would never even cross his mind to hide, or run.

Then Lily, standing in front of her son. Remus pictured her defiant face, her hands gripping the sides of the cot, her green eyes blazing. She would have met death with her eyes wide open, that was certain.

接着是Lily，站在她儿子的面前。Remus想象着她坚定的面容，她的手紧紧抓着婴儿床的边缘，她那绿色的眼睛闪烁着火焰。她一定是睁着眼睛面对死亡的，这一点毫无疑问。

And then Peter, next. Oh Peter, the idiot - the brave, ridiculous idiot. He must have heard about James and Lily, he must have known at once who was to blame. After all those years in James and Sirius’s shadow, Peter’s first instinct had been to face Black himself.

然后是Peter，哦，Peter，那傻瓜——勇敢而又荒谬的傻瓜。他一定听说了James和Lily的事，他一定立刻知道了谁应该为此负责。在那些年里，Peter一直生活在James和Sirius的阴影下，但他的第一反应却是直接面对Black。

He’d inadvertently led Aurors right to Sirius, so his brutal death hadn’t been completely in vain.

他无意中把Aurors引到了Sirius那里，所以他的残忍死亡并非完全没有意义。

Right to Sirius.

正好是Sirius。

And there was the block. Like a curtain falling across the scene, Remus’s mind wouldn’t touch Sirius. He couldn’t get there; couldn’t picture any of it. He supposed that was his brain’s way of protecting him. It hurt enough just knowing the bare facts.

但到此为止。仿佛一块帷幕遮住了画面，Remus的思维无法触及Sirius。他无法到达那里；无法想象其中的任何一幕。他想这可能是他大脑保护他的方式。仅仅知道这些基本事实就已经很痛苦了。

Mary came over as soon as she’d hung up the phone. She was the only person he could have tolerated, anyway, and god; she was so strong. He lay his head in her lap, and she stroked his hair like a mother.

Mary在挂断电话后立刻过来了。她是唯一一个他可以忍受的人，天啊，她是如此坚强。他把头靠在她的膝盖上，她像母亲一样抚摸他的头发。

“Sirius,” he wept, over and over, clinging to her skirt, “Sirius!”

“Sirius，”他一遍遍地哭泣，紧紧抓住她的裙子，“Sirius！”

“I know,” she whispered back, tears streaming down her cheeks, dripping into his hair. “I know, I know...”

“我知道，”她低声回答，泪水流淌下来，滴进他的头发里。“我知道，我知道……”

She’d brought a sleeping draught with her, and Remus drank it all down greedily, eager for escape. While he slept, Mary packed up all of Sirius’s things. All of his clothes, his records, his books. When Remus got up, the flat seemed almost empty.

她带来了安眠药，Remus贪婪地喝光了，渴望逃离。在他睡觉的时候，Mary打包了Sirius的所有东西。他的衣物、唱片、书籍。当Remus醒来时，公寓几乎显得空空如也。

“I had Darren move them down to the garage,” she explained. “You don’t need to touch any of it until you’re ready. The bike’s gone, I don’t know where.”

“我让Darren把它们搬到车库去了，”她解释说。“你不需要碰任何东西，直到你准备好。摩托车不见了，我不知道去了哪里。”

“He must have taken it.” Remus said, feeling numb. He was already wondering how much alcohol he had in the flat, and whether or not he ought to wait for Mary to leave before he started working his way through it.

“他一定是拿走了。”Remus说，感到麻木。他已经在想公寓里还有多少酒，是否应该等Mary离开后再开始喝酒。

“Remus… I have to go, now.” She said, gently, standing up, hugging herself. She looked small. Mary had always been a larger than life sort of girl, but Remus realised that she could barely be 5’5.

“Remus……我现在得走了。”她温柔地说，站起来，抱着自己。她看起来很渺小。Mary一直是那种气质超凡的女孩，但Remus意识到她可能连5尺5寸都不到。

“Yes, of course.” He murmured. There was definitely some gin under the sink in the kitchen.

“是的，当然。”他低声说道。厨房水槽下肯定有些杜松子酒。

“I’ll be gone for a while,” she said. “I’m going… Darren’s taking me to Jamaica, to stay with family. I need some time away, I don’t know when I’ll be back.”

“我会离开一段时间，”她说。“我要去……Darren会带我去牙买加，和家人待在一起。我需要一些时间离开，我不知道什么时候回来。”

“Oh.” He looked her in the eye, properly. She wasn’t wearing any makeup - he hadn’t seen Mary without eyeliner and lipstick since she was twelve.

“哦。”他认真地看着她。她没有化妆——自从她十二岁以来，Remus就没有见过不化妆的Mary。

“Is there… can someone stop by, to see you? I don’t mind making a phone call for you?”

“有……有人可以过来看你吗？我不介意为你打个电话。”

“It’s fine.” He said, “Don’t worry about me.”

“没关系。”他说，“别担心我。”

“But I will.” She said, smiling half-heartedly. “Are you sure I can’t contact anyone?”

“但我会担心。”她半心不在焉地笑了笑。“你确定我不能联系任何人吗？”

“There’s no one.” He said. I’ve got no one.

“没有人。”他说。我没有人。

“Perhaps speak to Moody? Or Arthur?”

“也许找Moody？或者Arthur？”

“Yeah, good idea.” Remus nodded. He didn’t want to talk to anyone, but he didn’t want her to worry. “Do you know… What are we supposed to do, now?”

“嗯，好主意。”Remus点了点头。他不想和任何人谈话，但他不想让她担心。“你知道……我们现在该怎么办？”

“I don’t know.”

“我不知道。”

“Have you spoken to Dumbledore?”

“你和Dumbledore说过话吗？”

“Ha.” Mary snorted, “Good luck getting hold of him. Too busy being congratulated by the ministry. He’ll probably be at the… the memorial service.”

“哈哈。”Mary嗤之以鼻，“祝好运找到他。他太忙于接受魔法部的祝贺了。他可能会去……纪念服务。”

Remus felt as if an ice cold blade was twisting in his gut. This couldn’t be real.

Remus感到像是冰冷的刀刃在他的胃部扭动。这不可能是真的。

“Why us.” He said, looking up at her, desperate for answers, “Out of everyone. Why is it you and me left, and not Lily and James? Who decided that?! It’s bollocks!”

“为什么是我们。”他抬起头看着她，迫切地寻找答案，“为什么是你和我留下，而不是Lily和James？是谁决定的？！这真是扯淡！”

“I know, sweetheart.” She said, softly. “I know.”

“我知道，亲爱的。”她柔声说。“我知道。”

He couldn’t wait any longer, he went to the kitchen and grabbed the nearest open bottle from the cupboard. Gin, leftover from some party or other. He didn’t pour a glass, just drank.

他再也等不下去了，他走进厨房，拿起橱柜里最近的一瓶开过的酒。杜松子酒，是某个聚会剩下的。他没有倒酒，只是直接喝。

“Remus,” Mary said, chewing her lip, watching him from the living room, “I really do have to go… do you promise you’ll get in touch with Arthur?”

“Remus，”Mary说，咬着嘴唇，从客厅看着他，“我真的得走了……你答应我会联系Arthur吗？”

“Yeah.” He nodded. He just wanted her to leave, now. “See ya.”

“嗯。”他点了点头。他现在只想让她离开。“再见。”

“Goodbye, love. I’ll be back, I promise.”

“再见，亲爱的。我会回来的，我保证。”

And she left. And Remus was alone.

 

然后她离开了。Remus只剩下了一个人。

New Years Day 1982

THUD-THUD-THUD-THUD-THUD-THUD

Someone was banging on the door.

They’d been doing it for a while now, and showed no sign of stopping. If anything, it was getting worse.

 

 

Remus opened his eyes. His throat was dry and his head hurt. Actually, everything hurt; he’d been sleeping on the couch for weeks. Or months? Who cared. It was uncomfortable, but he couldn’t bring himself to enter the bedroom. Most nights he was too drunk to move anyway. Most days he was too drunk. He didn’t have hangovers anymore, just breaks between bottles. The kid next door didn’t mind running down to the off-licence every other day for him; he was probably making a killing in spare change.

Remus睁开眼睛。喉咙干涩，头痛得厉害。实际上，整个身体都很痛；他已经在沙发上睡了好几周，甚至几个月？谁在乎。这很不舒服，但他无法让自己走进卧室。大多数夜晚他都醉得动不了。大多数白天他也醉。已经没有宿醉了，只是瓶子之间的间隙。隔壁的孩子不介意隔几天就跑到酒类商店去买酒给他，他可能靠这些零碎的钱赚了不少。

The banging continued.

“Remus?!” The muffled sound came through the door, and whoever was on the other side kept hammering away.

敲击声继续传来。

“Remus？！”门外传来了含糊的声音，那边的人还在不停地敲打着门。

“Fuck off,” he shouted, his throat raw as sandpaper.

“滚开，”他喊道，喉咙干裂得像砂纸一样。

He reached for the nearest bottle on the floor beneath him and swigged from it. He nearly choked on the burning whisky but managed to get most of it down, thank god. He couldn’t afford to waste one drop of oblivion.

他伸手去拿地板上最近的瓶子，痛痛快快地喝了一口。差点被那烧灼的威士忌呛到，但勉强把大部分喝下去了，谢天谢地。他不能浪费一滴麻木的药水。

“Remus? Let me in!”

It was Grant. He recognised the voice now—maybe the scent too, but his senses had been a mess, ever since… no, no no no….

“Remus？让我进来！”

是Grant。他现在认出了声音——也许是气味，但自从……不，不不不……

He curled up, burying his head in the sofa cushions. He couldn’t talk to anyone. He couldn’t see anyone. He just needed to be left, to drink and to forget. Please.

他蜷缩起来，把头埋进沙发垫里。他无法和任何人谈话。他无法见任何人。他只需要被放置一旁，喝酒，忘记。求你了。

“Fuck off!” He sobbed, yelling at the door, “Leave me alone!”

“滚开！”他哭泣着喊道，“离我远点！”

“No!” Grant shouted back, and the banging got louder still, a relentless, resounding thud-thud-thud. He was actually trying to break the door down, the stupid prat.

“不！”Grant回喊道，敲击声变得更大了，持续不断的“砰砰砰”声。他居然真的试图把门打破，这个愚蠢的傻瓜。

Remus half considered just casting a silencing spell. But he wasn’t sure where his wand was. He rolled over again and got up.

Remus半考虑施个静音咒。但他不确定他的魔杖在哪里。他再次翻身起床。

There were bottles and cans all over the floor, and they clinked and rustled as he waded through. His arms and legs felt like lead. What day was it? It was cold. He rubbed his arms as he approached the door, shuddering against the chill. He’d left a window open somewhere in the flat and forgotten to shut it. Oh well.

地板上满是瓶子和罐子，他踩过去时发出叮当声和沙沙声。他的手臂和腿感觉像铅一样沉重。今天是几号？天气很冷。他走向门口时搓着手臂，感到一阵寒冷。他在公寓里某处留了个窗户没关。算了。

The door was still being thumped as he reached it; the wood would splinter if he wasn’t careful.

他到达门口时，门还在被猛烈敲击，如果不小心的话，木门可能会裂开。

“What?!” He yanked the door open.

“什么？！”他猛地拉开了门。

Grant stared at him, fist still raised, wide-eyed. His cheeks were pink from shouting, and he was breathing heavily. He looked Remus up and down.

Grant盯着他看，拳头还在半空中，瞪大了眼睛。他的脸颊因为喊叫而变得通红，呼吸急促。他上下打量着Remus。

“Jesus christ.” He said, rudely pushing his way in. “What happened? I’ve been trying to ring ya for days, what’s wrong with the phone?”

“天哪。”他说，粗鲁地推开了他。“发生了什么事？我已经试了好几天打电话，电话怎么了？”

“Off the hook.” Remus said, slowly returning to his nest on the couch, where at least it was warm. He curled his cold feet under himself and picked up the bottle again.

“没挂好。”Remus说，缓缓回到沙发上的窝里，至少那里比较温暖。他把冰冷的脚缩到自己身下，又拿起瓶子。

“The fuck’s been going on here?” Grant looked around at the mess. He looked at Remus again, “...gawd, ‘e ain’t left you, has ‘e?”

“这里到底发生了什么？”Grant看着周围的混乱，又看了看Remus，“……天哪，他没离开你吧？”

Remus stared up at him, and he couldn’t help it. He began to cry. He leaned forward on his knees, dropping his head into his hands, and he bawled like a child.

Remus抬头看着他，忍不住哭了。他趴在膝盖上，把头埋在双手里，像个孩子一样痛哭。

“Shit,” Grant hurried over to sit next to him, not minding the empty cans, the smelly cushions, and blankets. “Me and my big mouth! I’m sorry! I didn’t mean…” He pulled Remus to him without a thought, and it must have been awful, because Remus knew he hadn't washed in ages, all he’d done was drink and cry for days and days and days, but Grant held him fast.

“该死，”Grant急忙坐到他身边，不在意地上的空罐子、难闻的垫子和毯子，“我这张嘴真是不该！对不起！我不是那个意思……”他毫不犹豫地把Remus抱到自己怀里，可能是很糟糕，因为Remus知道自己已经很久没洗澡了，这几天只是喝酒和哭泣，但Grant紧紧地抱着他。

“They’re all gone.” Remus said, when he could speak. “I’m alone.”

“他们全都走了。”Remus说，当他能说话时，“我一个人。”

“Bollocks.” Said Grant. “You’re not alone.”

“胡扯。”Grant说，“你并不孤单。”

Remus cried even harder.

Remus哭得更厉害了。

* * *

Not a single day went by – and not one day would ever go by, for many years – that he did not think of Sirius and suffer. It was an abstract and cruel torture, and Remus resigned himself to a life of utter misery.

每天都没有一天过去——多年来没有一天会过去——他不去思考Sirius而受苦。这是一种抽象而残酷的折磨，Remus对彻底的痛苦生活心甘情愿。

Everywhere he looked he was haunted by thoughts and memories of his friends, of the things they could never do, and the things he had not done in time. He attended the funeral—a joint one for Lily and James, followed by a memorial for Peter. Remus sat at the back and left before the wake, in case anyone tried to speak to him.

他四处张望，思绪和记忆都被朋友们的影像所困扰，那些他们无法完成的事情，以及他没有及时做的事。他参加了葬礼——这是Lily和James的合葬仪式，随后是Peter的纪念仪式。Remus坐在最后一排，在守灵之前离开了，以防有人试图和他说话。

He was terrified that someone might ask him about Sirius—might ask him what he knew. Or tell him something he didn’t want to know. So Remus did not stay to reminisce or ‘celebrate’ his friends’ lives (honestly, what a despicable idea). He went home alone and got drunk. He got drunk every day for weeks.

他害怕有人会问他关于Sirius的事——可能会问他知道什么。或者告诉他他不想知道的事。所以Remus没有留下来回忆或者“庆祝”朋友们的生命（老实说，这真是个可憎的主意）。他一个人回家，喝酒。他连续几个星期每天都喝醉。

He stayed at the flat in Soho—he had no choice in the matter; no money, no family. No friends.

他待在Soho的公寓里——他没有选择；没有钱，没有家庭。没有朋友。

The Order disbanded and those who still had lives worth living didn’t want to know him. He couldn’t find any work in the wizarding world and—never having felt at home in it anyway—chose to withdraw.

凤凰社解散了，那些还有值得活下去的生活的人不愿意和他接触。他在魔法世界中找不到任何工作——反正他从未在其中感到归属——于是选择了退出。

After learning about the fate of the Longbottoms in the Daily Prophet, he stopped reading the papers. He did not re-connect to the floo network, he did not use magic at all unless he really had to. He never went to Diagon Alley, and for all intents and purposes lived as a Muggle.

在《预言家日报》中得知Longbottom夫妇的命运后，他停止了阅读报纸。他没有重新连接到火焰网络，除非真的不得不，他不使用魔法。他从未去过对角巷，就实际而言，过着麻瓜的生活。

Mary sent postcards from Jamaica, from Trinidad, from Saint Lucia—she seemed to have family all over the Caribbean. She kept saying sorry. Remus didn’t know what for; they’d both lost the same things. At least she cared enough to get in touch.

Mary从牙买加、特立尼达、圣卢西亚寄来了明信片——她似乎在加勒比地区有家人。她不断道歉。Remus不知道她在为什么道歉；他们都失去了相同的东西。至少她还关心到与他联系。

Dumbledore actually did try to contact him a couple of times, but Remus deliberately made himself difficult to reach. He was furious at the old man, who as far as Remus was concerned had never lifted a finger to help. Who had thrust them all into the war, young as they were, and stupid as they were, and who watched them die one by one without so much as blinking. Even the baby, Harry, was quickly tidied away into some anonymous corner of Surrey. The Marauders might never have existed at all. Better that they hadn’t.

Dumbledore确实尝试过几次联系他，但Remus故意让自己难以接触。他对这个老人非常愤怒，在Remus看来，Dumbledore从未伸出一根手指来帮助他们。这个人将他们所有人拖入了战争，无论他们多么年轻，或多么愚蠢，却眼睁睁地看着他们一个个死去，连眼睛都没眨一下。连那个婴儿Harry也被迅速送到了萨里郡的某个匿名角落。麻瓜骑士们也许从未存在过。最好他们从未存在。

For a while, Remus wondered when it would end.

有一段时间，Remus想知道这何时会结束。

After long enough, he realized it never would, and so just tried to dull the pain. It might have been selfish, but what else was left but to be selfish? He had sacrificed plenty.

过了足够长的时间，他意识到这永远不会结束，于是他试图麻木痛苦。这可能是自私的，但除了自私之外，还剩下什么？他已经牺牲了很多。

When the first full moon came, the November after that grisly Halloween, Remus was forced to leave the flat. He apparated back to the forest he’d stayed in with Greyback’s pack back in ‘79. It was better than a cell. He wouldn’t be locked up, he wouldn’t allow it. So he left, he transformed, and he wandered the woods alone, howling and hunting and snarling. The first time was a relief, but the wolf was lonely. The second time, he went to the Black Forest.

当第一个满月来临时，那是在那个可怕的万圣节后的11月，Remus被迫离开了公寓。他瞬移回到了1979年和Greyback的狼群呆过的森林。比起牢房，这要好得多。他不愿被锁起来，他不会允许。所以他离开了，变身成狼，独自在森林中游荡，嚎叫、狩猎、咆哮。第一次是种解脱，但狼感到孤独。第二次，他去了黑森林。

He didn’t intend to live amongst the werewolves, he just used them as an escape route.

他并不打算在狼人中生活，他只是把他们当作一种逃避的途径。

They knew little of the war, except that it was over. The first time, Castor sensed Remus’s pain at once. They didn’t speak of it—because there was no need. They simply transformed and dealt with it as wolves. Remus decided that whatever happened when they were not human didn’t count, as long as they didn’t hurt anyone. It was freeing, and the only relief Remus knew in those darkest months after his loss.

他们对战争知之甚少，只知道战争已经结束。第一次，Castor立刻感知到了Remus的痛苦。他们没有谈论这些——因为没有必要。他们只是变成狼，以狼的方式处理这些问题。Remus决定，无论发生什么，只要他们不伤害任何人，那些人狼之间的事都不算数。这种解脱感是Remus在失落的最黑暗时刻中唯一的安慰。

In the mornings after the moon, Remus would stay a little longer each time, just to be near them. With nothing left to lose, he gave up any pretence of superiority when it came to the pack, and in time, Castor finally got what he wanted.

月圆之后的早晨，Remus每次都会多待一会儿，只是为了靠近他们。没有什么可失去的，他放弃了对狼群的任何优越感，最终，Castor终于得到了他想要的。

Remus couldn’t deny his attraction to Castor much longer, and after all; who did he need to be loyal to? Was he supposed to live celibate for the rest of his life simply because his first love had broken his heart? And there was no love between him and Castor. Only animal need; bestial rutting. It was good, but it was only another way to forget. And Remus always returned to London, sore and still unsatisfied.

Remus再也无法否认自己对Castor的吸引，毕竟；他还需要忠诚于谁？难道他要因为第一次爱情让他心碎而终身保持禁欲吗？而他和Castor之间并没有爱情。只有动物的需求；野兽的交配。这种方式虽然好，但只是另一种忘却的方式。Remus总是回到伦敦，身体疲惫，依然无法满足。

In the human world, Grant still came back for regular visits, after that first time. He took the spare key and popped in to check on Remus between his lectures and pub shifts. He was both a help and a hindrance, bringing bottles of Muggle spirits and other substances—whatever Remus asked for.

在现实世界中，Grant在第一次之后还定期回来探望。他拿着备用钥匙，在讲座和酒吧工作之间回来看Remus。他既是帮助者，又是障碍者，带来了麻瓜的烈酒和其他物品——无论Remus要什么，他都会带来。

He’d been kicked out of his bedsit for soliciting (not true, he insisted—the landlady just had it in for him) and now Grant bounced between boyfriends’ beds and friends’ couches. Sometimes he even stayed with Remus for a night or two, and that was okay, Remus didn’t mind. He didn’t care about very much, as long as he had plenty to drink. He needed to be drunk. Before the war ended, it had just been a way to take the edge off; to change his mood. Now it was his mood; the only one he could bear.

他因卖淫被房东赶出了出租屋（他说这不是真的——房东只是对他有意见），现在Grant在男朋友的床和朋友的沙发之间辗转。有时他甚至会和Remus一起待一两晚，这也没问题，Remus不在意。他对很多事情都不在乎，只要有足够的酒。他需要喝醉。在战争结束之前，这只是减轻压力的方式；改变心情。现在这就是他的心情；唯一他能忍受的心情。

It was Grant who talked at him, nagged him, dragged him out of bed and pushed him into the shower when he needed to. He even did the laundry and bought groceries with Remus’s remaining dwindling funds.

是Grant对他说话，唠叨他，把他从床上拖出来，推他去洗澡。他甚至洗衣服，用Remus剩余不多的资金买杂货。

Remus, for his part, behaved abysmally. He made spiteful comments, hurled insults. But Grant paid it no mind and kept returning all the same.

Remus表现得非常糟糕。他发表恶意评论，发出侮辱。但Grant却毫不在意，仍然一如既往地回到Remus身边。

“You only come back because you’re basically homeless.” Remus spat one evening, from the couch, as Grant collected the rubbish littered around him. Remus couldn’t bear the clinking sound empty bottles made.“你回來只是因為你基本上無家可歸。”一天晚上，當格蘭特收集散落在他周圍的垃圾時，萊姆斯在沙發上吐了口水。萊姆斯無法忍受空瓶發出的丁當聲。

“Yep,” Grant replied, blithely, carrying on about his business, “That’s exactly right, Remus me old pal. Nuffink to do with the fact that I love your dozy arse.”

“没错，”Grant轻松地回答，继续做他的事，“没错，Remus老朋友。完全不是因为我爱你那懒洋洋的屁股。”

Remus snorted disdainfully. Grant didn’t know what he was talking about. Love! Remus knew the truth now. He knew that love was just something people said to make you weak—to keep you pliant. Never again. Never never never.

Remus不屑地嗤笑。Grant根本不知道他在说什么。爱情！Remus现在知道真相了。他知道爱情不过是人们用来让你变弱——让你屈从的东西。绝不再有。绝对绝对绝对不再有。

Miraculously, Grant never once asked what had happened. Even when Remus began to show signs of improvement, started getting himself up and dressed without hours of nudging, even when he started leaving the house. Grant never asked why.

奇迹般地，Grant从未询问过发生了什么事。即使Remus开始显示出改善的迹象，开始在没有多小时催促的情况下起床穿衣，甚至开始离开家。Grant也从未问过原因。

Remus knew he had ranted, in his drunken stupors, pouring out misery and rage about Sirius and James and Lily and poor, poor Peter, and Sirius and Sirius and Sirius...

Remus知道他在醉酒中发泄过，对Sirius、James、Lily以及可怜的Peter以及Sirius的一片片痛苦和愤怒……

Whether Grant understood half of it, or whether Remus said too much, he never knew. But Grant kept coming back, anyway.

Grant是否理解了其中的一半，或者Remus是否说了太多，他从未知道。但Grant还是不断地回来。

“I’ll keep coming, long as you need me.” He’d say, cheerfully as he flitted about. “Us care home yobs gotta stick together, innit.”

“只要你需要我，我就会一直回来。”他会一边忙碌一边高兴地说，“我们这些养老院的家伙得互相扶持。”

Remus didn’t believe him. Grant was being nice, but that could only last so long. Nobody stayed around forever.

Remus不相信他。Grant表现得很好，但这种好意只能持续一段时间。没有人会永远待在身边。

Chapter 176: 1983These people 'round here

Wear beat down eyes sunk in smoke dried faces

They're resigned to what their fate is.

But not us, (no never) no not us (no never)

We are far too young and clever.

 

6th June 1983

“Sometimes I wonder if you’re using me.” Grant said, one afternoon in the summer of 1983.

“We all use each other.” Remus replied, dryly, “And that’s what we think love is.”

“Christ. Can’t talk to you when you’re like this.” Grant sighed heavily, reaching for a packet of cigarettes on the bedside table.

“Like what?”

“A gloomy git.”“一个阴郁的家伙。”

Grant pulled a long white cylinder from the box with his teeth, and Remus lit it with his wand point. Grant sucked on it appreciatively, settling back against Remus’s body, in the crook of his arm. Remus lazily stroked Grant’s collar bone until it was his turn to smoke. They’d almost given up; sharing a quick post-sex fag was their treat.

 

Grant用牙齿从盒子里抽出一根长白色香烟，Remus用魔杖点燃了它。Grant欣赏地吸了一口，靠在Remus的身体上，躺在他的手臂弯里。Remus懒洋洋地抚摸着Grant的锁骨，直到轮到他自己抽烟。他们几乎放弃了；共享一根快速的性爱后的烟是他们的小奖赏。

“Sorry.” Remus said, “I don’t mean to be gloomy.”

“Pfft.” Grant replied, cheerfully, “Be gloomy if you want, I’m only teasin' ya. ”

Grant made everything so easy. Remus could barely remember when their relationship had grown into what it was now.

...

It had started with the regular visits, after that first intervention. They’d grown more frequent, and eventually Grant was just there all the time - first he slept on the couch, and then he didn’t anymore, and it was never discussed again.

By midsummer 1982, he’d moved all of his belongings in - such that they were.

“I travel light,” he winked, shaking out a rucksack that contained a few clean pairs of underwear and some t-shirts. One sock. For god’s sake.“我旅行轻便，”他眨眼说道，摇了摇一个背包，里面只有几条干净的内裤和几件T恤。还有一只袜子。天哪。

“I’ll give you some money.” Remus said, monotonously. “You can go shopping.” He still had a few hundred pounds Sirius had converted to muggle money in case of emergencies. Remus didn’t feel guilty about spending it; it was just sitting there.“我会给你一些钱。”Remus单调地说，“你可以去购物。”他还有几百英镑是Sirius兑换的麻瓜货币，以备紧急情况。Remus对花这些钱不感到内疚；反正就那么放着。

“I’m not here to scrounge off you.” Grant insisted.

“我不是来向你乞讨的。”Grant坚持道。

“I know. But you need clothes.”

“Yes mum. I’ll borrow some of yours for a bit, ‘til I get myself sorted.”

“Fine.”

 

 

So Remus went to Debenhams by himself one afternoon and bought as much as he could in Grant’s size. Jeans and t-shirts and underwear and socks and jumpers, pyjamas and even a cheap pair of trainers that were on offer. Bright colours, because Grant was a bright person, and Remus had seen enough black to last a lifetime. He folded it all away in the chest of drawers. It felt good to fill them; they’d been standing half-empty for over a year.
于是，Remus在一个下午独自去了Debenhams，尽可能多地购买了适合Grant的衣物。包括牛仔裤、T恤、内裤、袜子、毛衣、睡衣，甚至还买了一双打折的便宜运动鞋。鲜艳的颜色，因为Grant是一个阳光的人，而Remus已经看够了黑色。他把所有东西都折好放进抽屉里。填满这些抽屉感觉很好；它们已经空了超过一年。

Grant wore the clothes, but they never discussed it.
Grant穿上了这些衣服，但他们从未讨论过这件事。

There were some things they could not avoid talking about, though.
不过，有些话题是他们无法避免讨论的。

Remus hadn’t been doing magic at all for the first few months—actually, he found that he couldn’t, a lot of the time; even when he tried. Perhaps the grief. All those funerals. It may have had more to do with his drinking, though he couldn’t be sure. There was a block there; like a wall had gone up. He could apparate for full moons, but that was the extent of it. Then one day, it just came back, as if it had never left him.
在最初的几个月里，Remus完全没有做魔法——实际上，他发现他很多时候都做不了魔法，即使他尝试过。也许是因为悲伤，所有那些葬礼。虽然他不确定，但这可能与他的饮酒有关。魔法似乎被封锁了；仿佛墙已经竖起来了。他能在满月时使用瞬移，但这就是极限了。然后有一天，它突然回来了，仿佛从未离开过他。

They’d forgotten to pay the electric, and the lights went dead. Without thinking, Remus lit his wand,
他们忘记付电费，灯光熄灭了。Remus毫不犹豫地点亮了他的魔杖，

“ Lumos .”

“What the bloody fuck is that?!” Grant leapt away as if Remus had set himself on fire.

“Er…” Remus swallowed, then resigned himself to it. “It’s a magic wand.”

“Are you high?”

Remus laughed, a gruff, alien sound.

“I think I’d better explain some stuff to you. The school I went to was a bit… different…”

He began to explain. He knew how weird it must all sound, and he had to leave quite a lot of stuff out. Almost twenty minutes later, Grant sat staring at him, face pale in the weakening wandlight.

“You’re having me on.” He laughed, nervously, “What are you playing at, making up a load of tosh like that?!”

“Grant… look...” Remus made sparks with his wand. He levitated the coffee table, and then - showing off, because it had been so long - transformed his mug into a frog.

“All right!” Grant recoiled, as the frog hopped onto the carpet, “Ok, I believe you! Jesus Christ!”

“Oh, just ‘Remus Lupin’ will do.” Remus stuck his tongue out.

Then he stopped, realised what he was doing.

He’d stopped hurting for a moment, and chastised himself viciously for it. Your friends are dead, and you’re doing magic tricks for some muggle? Pathetic.

He went to look in the cupboards for a drink.

“Oh no, don’t…” Grant said, sounding disappointed.

Remus returned to the couch with a bottle of vodka and two tumblers. He liked vodka the most, it went down easy.

“I don’t want any.” Grant said, ignoring the second glass. “I’m going to stop getting it for you.”

Remus shrugged and knocked back his first measure.

Grant sighed. “So you’re a wizard, eh? Does that mean… Sirius was a wizard, too?”

Remus nearly choked on his second shot, but got it down. His eyes watered and he nodded.

 

“Yeah. We all are. Were.”

And he drank more, and told Grant about the war. He left out some of the more painful details, but Grant was astute, and guessed the rest.

于是他喝得更多，把战争的事告诉了Grant。他省略了一些更痛苦的细节，但Grant很聪明，猜出了其余的部分。

“Is that where you vanish off to, every month?” Grant asked, “Some magic thing?”

“Oh… no. There’s something else.”

“Bloody hell, Remus, do I know anything about you?!”

“Sorry.” Remus said. “Honestly, I’m really not worth the effort… once you know everything, you’ll understand.”

“Try me.” Grant said.

So then they had the werewolf conversation. Remus explained what happened to him on full moons, and how dangerous he was, and where he went.

“Since you were five?!” Grant said, aghast.

“Yeah.” Remus nodded, nervously.

“You poor thing,” Grant shook his head, and stroked his hand. “You’ve had a rough go of it, ‘aven’t ya?”

Remus accepted the sympathy, and didn’t say too much about Castor, because he was ashamed of himself.

Not that Grant would have been jealous. Not like Sirius, not like… oh, oh no, no no no...

...

British dictionary:
- Debenhams - National chain of department stores. Every mum's favourite.
- Trainers - Sneakers/tennis shoes/runners/kicks
- 'Penny for 'em?' - Penny for your thoughts (i.e. 'tell me what you're thinking').
- Boys' Remand Centre - Criminal detention centre for boys under 17.
- Poll Tax - Brought in by Margaret Thatcher and the Conservative government in the '80s, this tax paid for Local Government (now called 'Council Tax'). Before 1979, this was paid by each household based on the market rental value of the property. The Poll Tax was a flat rate per person - meaning that the burden of payment shifted from wealthy home owners to poor renters. It was massively unfair and resulted in nationwide protests and rioting.

由于格兰特对工作的投入，以及雷穆斯自己相对低影响的就业，雷穆斯发现自己处于一个前所未有的境地——既有空闲时间又有一点可支配收入。

他不需要太多——公寓已经付清，他们的家具还算可用，他们一般能负担得起电费和热水费。他偶尔买些衣服，但几乎不在哈罗德购物。至于喝酒，他认为既然他不再抽烟了，可以把烟草钱用来买酒。

雷穆斯喜欢做的是散步。不是乡村漫步——满月时他已经够多了——而是独自漫步在伦敦，享受街道和人群。他参观了伦敦的每一个免费博物馆——国家美术馆，肖像馆，V&A博物馆，大英博物馆。事实上，他变得相当有文化。如果他的臀部疼痛（现在进入二十多岁后经常如此），他可以轻松地上公交车。

He could just picture Arthur’s face as he watched the perpetual motion machine, and Remus smiled to himself, quite out of the blue. How was Arthur? 于是，有一个夏天的日子，他完成了所有的批改，电视上也没什么好看的节目，格兰特还要几个小时才能回家，所以他在科学博物馆闲逛了一个小时左右。有趣的是，这使他想起了亚瑟·韦斯莱，这是多年来第一次。那个傻老家伙会喜欢所有的机器，活塞，灯泡。他可以想象亚瑟看着永动机时的表情，雷穆斯不由自主地笑了。亚瑟怎么样了？他的妻子，普雷威特家的姐姐，还有他们红发的一群孩子？雷穆斯知道，已经太久没有联系了，即使联系上了，他也不知道该说什么。

“好吧……”克里斯托弗小心翼翼地抬头看着他。

“你住在附近吗？”克里斯托弗终于问道，依然没有完全与他眼神接触。

“Yeah,” Remus nodded, “Not far. You?”

“Oh, no. Out in Hampshire. I just come into the city for work, and… well.”

“Where do you work now?” Remus asked, desperate to spare him any further embarrassment.

“Gringotts.” Chris said, glancing up at the waitress as their coffees arrived. He put three sugars in his, and as much milk as he could - Remus realised he hadn’t even asked if Chris liked coffee.

“Very swish,” Remus smiled, “Always knew you’d do well.”

“I suppose.”

“Still read lots?”

“When there’s time… work keeps me busy. And other responsibilities, you know how it is. I thought we were overworked during NEWTs, but Hogwarts was a holiday compared to real life.”

Remus chewed the inside of his cheek, because that was very true, and he didn’t want to get upset about it.

“How about you?” Christopher asked, clearly trying not to grimace as he sipped his coffee. “What do you do, now?”

“This and that,” Remus shrugged. “Haven’t exactly got a career.”

“Oh, what a shame.”

 

Remus shrugged, “It’s fine, I manage.”

There was an awkward silence. Remus wanted to ask about the sauna, but he knew better. Grant would probably ask, but then Grant had a way of putting people at ease which Remus didn’t. He just drank his coffee quietly, and wished he’d suggested a pub, instead.

一陣尷尬的沉默。萊姆斯想詢問桑拿的事，但他更清楚。格蘭特可能會問，但格蘭特有辦法讓人們放鬆，而萊姆斯卻沒有。他只是安靜地喝著咖啡，希望他能推薦一家酒吧。

Yes , Remus wanted to say, yes, I bloody remember. Sometimes I wake up and it’s like it’s still happening.

“Like I said,” Christopher said, “I barely go there, really. Just stupid curiosity.”

Remus felt a twinge of guilt, for making Christopher feel bad. If Grant had taught him anything, it was that you should never add to anyone’s personal shame. It was a wasted emotion anyway, no need to make it worse.

“There’s nothing wrong with being curious,” Remus said, gently, “Lots of people go to those places.”

“Do you?” Christopher looked up at him.

“No.” Remus said, a bit too quickly. “Er… I mean, you know I was never very sociable.”

“Oh, of course. I can imagine, after everything that happened…”

Remus didn’t want to get onto that, so he changed the subject, “Seeing anyone?” he asked, “Got a boyfriend?”

Christopher shook his head. “No. It’s difficult, you know. The job I have, my family. Things have been… well, there’s been a fair bit of trial and error, in that respect.”

Remus wanted to squeeze his hand over the table, but it wasn’t really the place. He tilted his head, sympathetically,

“It will get better, Chris.”

Christopher looked at him with a resigned smile. “Mm, yes, I remember you saying something like that before, at school. Someone for everyone.”

 

“Well, there is.” Remus nodded, encouragingly. “More than one person, even.”

“I don’t know.” Chris sighed, “I don’t know if it’s healthy to think like that. There are so many factors to consider, and I don’t… I don’t think it works like in books. I don’t think everyone has that experience.”

That was a difficult thing to hear. Remus didn’t know what to say, really, and felt weirdly self-conscious and naive. Certainly, Remus did not glamourise romance any more - if he ever had at all. Love had beaten the shit out of him on more than one occasion. But it had also been the only thing worth living for. It had lifted him, protected him, and kept him human. He had a sudden longing to see Grant, and wondered if he’d be home yet.
那是一件很难听的话。雷穆斯真的不知道该说什么，感觉莫名地自觉和天真。当然，雷穆斯不再美化爱情——如果他曾经有的话。爱情不止一次把他打得体无完肤。但它也是唯一值得活下去的东西。它抬起了他，保护了他，让他保持人性。他突然很想见到Grant，不知道他是否已经回家。

I like my work, I make plenty of money, and when I get a free evening I still… you know, I’m able to enjoy myself once in a while. I just see it as a treat, rather than a lifestyle. Actually,” he leaned in a little, “I have a flat in Kensington - for when I work late, and don’t want to apparate all the way home. It’s nice there, if you’d like to see it.” He raised an eyebrow suggestively.
“别为我感到难过，”克里斯托弗干脆地说，查看他的怀表，“我过得还不错。我喜欢我的工作，挣了不少钱，有空的时候我还能……你知道，偶尔享受一下。我只是把这看作一种享受，而不是一种生活方式。实际上，”他微微靠近，“我在肯辛顿有一套公寓——为了工作到很晚，不想幻影移形回家的时候。那里很不错，如果你想去看看。”他挑了挑眉，暗示性地说。

“Well. Good for you, then. Look, I’d better go, Remus, it was very nice to see you again.” Christopher stood up, and extended a formal hand for Remus to shake. “We ought to have a proper catch up, one of these days, let me know if you’re ever in Diagon Alley, perhaps, I’ll arrange lunch.”

“Ok,” Remus nodded, shaking his hand.

He knew he would never be in Diagon Alley, and as Christopher didn’t give him any contact details Remus assumed that the invitation was merely politeness. He did not miss pureblood hypocrisy.他知道自己永遠不會去對角巷，而且由於克里斯托弗沒有給他任何聯繫方式，萊姆斯認為邀請只是出於禮貌。他並不懷念純血統的虛偽。

“Wotcher, boffin,” he grinned, “How was the museum?”

“Good, thanks. Interesting.”

“No, I just… just missed you, that’s all.”

“I’ve only been at work.”

“I know…”

“Daft sod.” Grant shook his head, still smiling, turning his back to open the cutlery drawer and find the tin opener.“愚蠢的草皮。”格蘭特搖搖頭，仍然微笑著，轉身打開餐具抽屜，找到開罐器。
