“Mmmhm.” Remus said, into his neck. “Just glad you’re here.”

 

“嗯嗯。”萊姆斯對著他的脖子說。 “很高興你在這裡。”

British-isms:
- UCL - University College London
- National insurance card - Has your national insurance number on it. In the UK you need this to get a job, as it ensures you are making the right tax contributions on your salary. National insurance payments, made over your working life, mean you are entitled to various benefits (Job seekers allowance, maternity allowance etc.) and your state pension. I'm guessing wizards don't have them lol.
- The Observer - National broadsheet newspaper.
- Kick-about - impromptu/casual game of football. I'm guessing it's the equivalent to when Americans 'toss a ball around' or 'play catch'.
- Harrods - (not sure this actually needs explaining) high-end London department store, only used by tourists and the mega-rich.
- Boffin - a clever person (nerd, geek etc.)
- Worcestershire - Worcestershire sauce - the best possible condiment for beans/hoops on toast. Pronounced 'wooster', like the place.)

 

 

Chapter 180: 1989Got on a lucky one

Came in eighteen to one

I've got a feeling

This year's for me and you

So happy Christmas

I love you baby!

I can see a better time

When all our dreams come true.


In 1989, Remus actually went to Oxford Street to do his Christmas shopping, on Grant’s insistence.

“You’ve never been?!” He had gasped, eyes wide, “You haven’t seen the lights?!”

“I didn’t think proper Londoners got involved in all that nonsense.” Remus replied, defensively.

“ Proper Londoners leave the house.” Grant said. “And buy presents for their friends.”

“I don’t have any friends.” Remus said - then felt awful. Because of course, he had Grant.

“What about that Mary bird? Sends you letters all the time.”

“Oh yeah. I could get her something, maybe.”

“That’s the spirit, Ebenezer.”
“这就对了，埃比尼泽。”

Remus shrugged off the teasing, because he knew Grant loved Christmas - or any opportunity to celebrate, really - and Grant had had a very difficult year.
雷穆斯无视了这个玩笑，因为他知道Grant喜欢圣诞节——或任何庆祝的机会——而Grant这一年过得非常艰难。

Having worked so hard to gain his school leaving certificate, pushing every step of the way to get A-Levels and various other qualifications, all so that he could have his dream job, which was helping other people, Grant had finally come up against an insurmountable opponent. The government - more specifically, The Local Government Act.
Grant辛苦地拿到了毕业证书，每一步都在努力获得A-Level和其他各种资格证书，只为了能拥有他梦想的工作，即帮助他人。但最终，Grant遇到了一个无法逾越的对手。政府——更具体地说，是《地方政府法》。

In 1988, Section 28 passed, and Grant was no longer secure in his position at work. Remus hadn’t really understood it at first, or at least, couldn’t see why Grant should have to worry.
1988年，《第28条》通过，Grant的工作不再有保障。雷穆斯一开始并没有真正理解，或者至少，不明白Grant为什么要担心。

“You don’t work for the council, though,” he frowned, flicking through the leaflets Grant and his friends had been printing for awareness-raising.
“但你不是为议会工作啊，”他皱着眉头，翻阅着Grant和他的朋友们为了提高意识而打印的小册子。

“Yes I do,” Grant replied, “Local authority includes schools and Borstals - and that's what it’s really about. They don’t want us perverting kids.”
“是的，我是，”Grant回答，“地方当局包括学校和少年犯管教所——这就是问题的实质。他们不希望我们‘诱导’孩子。”

“That’s ridiculous.” Remus said.
“这太荒谬了。”雷穆斯说道。

“I know.”
“我知道。”

Remus re-read the text.
雷穆斯重新读了一遍文本。

A local authority shall not intentionally promote homosexuality or publish material with the intention of promoting homosexuality, or promote the teaching in any maintained school of the acceptability of homosexuality as a pretended family relationship.
地方当局不得故意宣扬同性恋或出版旨在宣扬同性恋的材料，或在任何公立学校教授同性恋作为一种假装的家庭关系的可接受性。

“假装的？！”雷穆斯摇了摇头。

“I don’t know, love. I’m already trying to keep my head down over the AIDs thing.”
“我不知道，亲爱的。我已经在尽量低调处理艾滋病的事情了。”

Remus felt even worse about that. The staff at the centre Grant worked at had all been hauled into a meeting one day, and told in no uncertain terms that if any one of them contracted HIV, then they would be dismissed without notice - and the police would be notified. That was terrifying enough.
雷穆斯对此感到更加难过。Grant工作的中心的所有员工有一天都被召集到一个会议上，被明确告知如果他们中的任何一人感染了HIV，他们将被无通知解雇——并通知警方。这已经够吓人的了。

For the past eighteen months, Grant had been working tirelessly with his friends and various groups to appeal Section 28, and it wasn’t going well at all. He’d almost been arrested at one protest, and caught a black eye off an anti-protester at another.
在过去的十八个月里，Grant一直和他的朋友们以及各种团体不懈地努力，呼吁废除第28条，但进展非常不顺利。他几乎在一次抗议活动中被逮捕，在另一次抗议中被反抗议者打了黑眼圈。

“It’s war.” he said fiercely, when he returned, and Remus made him sit still so he could heal it, “It’s us and them, that’s how they want it, and that’s what they’ll get.”
“这是战争。”他凶狠地说，当他回来时，雷穆斯让他坐着不动，好让他能治愈，“这是我们和他们，他们就是这么想的，他们会得到他们想要的。”

Remus did not know what to say. He didn’t want a war, he just wanted to be left alone. He never said that, though, because deep down, he was very proud of Grant’s barefaced refusal to give up or give even an inch. He had always admired bravery most of all.
雷穆斯不知道该说什么。他不想要战争，他只想被单独留下。不过，他从来没有说过，因为在心底，他非常为Grant的毫不退让感到骄傲。他一直最钦佩勇气。

So, in late December, Remus and Grant bundled themselves up in woolly hats, gloves and scarves, and walked through the wintry grey city to Oxford Circus. Grant was right - the prat - the lights were great. Strung across the wide street like jungle vines, great gleaming golden bulbs illuminated the cheerful red double deckers, the shiny black cabs, the glorious silver and green window displays.
因此，在十二月底，雷穆斯和Grant裹上毛线帽、手套和围巾，穿过寒冷灰暗的城市走到牛津街口。Grant说得对——那个蠢人——灯光很棒。像丛林藤蔓一样跨过宽阔的街道，巨大的金色灯泡照亮了欢快的红色双层巴士，闪亮的黑色出租车，光辉的银色和绿色橱窗展示。

It was true, Remus had been avoiding Christmas and all its trappings, just like he avoided his birthdays. He was worried they’d send him hurtling backwards - to Hogwarts, to the Potters mansion, to all of his most bittersweet memories. It was very hard to be without his friends at that time of year.
确实，雷穆斯一直在避开圣诞节及其所有装饰品，就像他避开自己的生日一样。他担心这些会让他猛然回到过去——回到霍格沃茨，回到Potters的豪宅，回到他所有最苦乐参半的记忆中。在那段时间里，没有朋友在身边是非常难熬的。

But there was something very cleansing about the chaos of shopping on Oxford Street. The noise and the bustle and the smells ensured that he couldn’t sulk for very long, and Grant’s enthusiasm for the season did the rest.
但是在牛津街购物的混乱中，有一种非常净化的感觉。喧嚣和熙熙攘攘的气味确保了他不能长时间地闷闷不乐，而Grant对这个季节的热情则完成了剩下的部分。

“Whichever is trendier, I s’pose,” Remus said. “What did you have in mind?”
“哪个更时尚，我猜，”雷穆斯说。“你有什么想法？”

“天哪，我不知道。浴室用品？”

“Yeah,” Remus nodded, “Bath shit. Or perfume?”
“对，”雷穆斯点点头，“浴室用品。或者香水？”

“Ooh, perfume, eh?” Grant nudged him with his elbow, “That’s intimate. Should I be worried?”
“哦，香水，嗯？”Grant用胳膊肘轻推他，“那很亲密。我该担心吗？”

“关于Mary？”雷穆斯哼了一声，“你太晚了。”

他们在三四家大百货公司的香水部门闲逛。雷穆斯有些后悔他的选择——他过于敏感的嗅觉意味着他在第一站后就已经头疼了。

“那是我总是给你的……”

“那是我现在唯一想要的，因为我不抽烟了。”

Grant shook his head, tutting at Remus’s temperance.
Grant摇了摇头，对雷穆斯的节制咂舌。

Suddenly, Remus caught a whiff of magic. For a moment he wondered if his senses were just wrecked by all the perfume, but no, it was very clear. He looked up and down the street, curiously. Then he saw him, standing outside the Marks & Spencer’s window display.
突然，雷穆斯闻到了一丝魔法的气息。他一度怀疑是否是他的感官被所有的香水搞坏了，但不是，气息很清晰。他好奇地上下打量街道。然后他看到了他，站在马莎百货的橱窗展示外。

“Christopher？是你吗？”雷穆斯慢慢走近。

“Remus!” Christopher turned, surprised.
“雷穆斯！”Christopher转过身来，惊讶地说。

“We have to stop meeting like this,” Remus laughed. He was in a good mood, and at least he hadn’t caught Chris in a compromising situation this time.
“我们得停止这样见面了，”雷穆斯笑了。他心情很好，至少这次他没有抓到Chris在一个尴尬的境地。

“Yes, quite right,” Christopher laughed too, a little nervously, clearing his throat at the end. He was carrying several bulging shopping bags, in both hands. “How are you? Sorry I haven’t been in touch, it’s been ever so busy at work.”
“是的，非常正确，”Christopher也笑了，有点紧张，最后清了清喉咙。他双手提着几个鼓鼓的购物袋。“你好吗？抱歉我一直没有联系，工作太忙了。”

“That’s ok. I’m well,” Remus nodded. Christopher’s eyes flicked towards Grant. Remus remembered his manners, “Sorry, er, this is Grant, my…”
“没关系。我很好，”雷穆斯点点头。Christopher的目光转向Grant。雷穆斯记起了礼貌，“抱歉，呃，这是Grant，我的……”

“Better half.” Grant finished with a cheeky grin, holding out a gloved hand. Christopher looked as though he didn’t know whether to laugh along too, but he shifted his shopping bags to shake Grant’s hand.
“另一半。”Grant调皮地笑着说，伸出戴着手套的手。Christopher看起来不确定是否也要笑，但他换了购物袋来握Grant的手。

“Christopher Barley,” he said.
“Christopher Barley，”他说。

“Chris and I were at school together,” Remus explained.
“Chris和我一起上学的，”雷穆斯解释道。

“Oh, I see,” Grant nodded, eagerly, his eyes bulging. He never said anything about it, but Remus knew Grant was secretly dying to meet another wizard, just to compare. “Live in London, do ya?”
“哦，我明白了，”Grant急切地点头，眼睛瞪得大大的。他从来没有说过什么，但雷穆斯知道Grant暗地里很想见到另一个巫师，只是为了比较一下。“住在伦敦吗？”

“Er, no. Just in for shopping, you know. Christmas.”
“呃，不。只是来购物，你知道的。圣诞节。”

“Us too,” Remus said.
“我们也是，”雷穆斯说。

“How nice.” Chris said very formally. It was starting to get a bit weird - Remus felt like they were at a middle class cocktail party or something, exchanging pleasantries.
“真好。”Chris非常正式地说。事情开始变得有点奇怪了——雷穆斯觉得他们像是在中产阶级的鸡尾酒会上之类的地方，交换客套话。

“Chris dear? There you are!” A short blonde woman came trotting up the street in neat black high heels and a gorgeous ermine coat. She was tugging a little boy along by the hand - he looked about five years old, and he had Christopher’s eyes. “Can we go quite soon? There are too many muggles about, it’s suffocating.”
“亲爱的Chris？你在这里！”一个矮个子金发女人穿着整洁的黑色高跟鞋和华丽的白鼬大衣跑上街来。她牵着一个小男孩——他看起来大约五岁，有着Christopher的眼睛。“我们能快点走吗？这里有太多麻瓜了，令人窒息。”

Christopher avoided Remus’s gaze, and greeted the woman.
Christopher避开雷穆斯的目光，迎接了那个女人。

“Sorry, dear, I was just… I bumped into an old Hogwarts friend.” He gestured vaguely.
“抱歉，亲爱的，我只是……碰到了一位老霍格沃茨的朋友。”他模糊地示意。

“How lovely!” She turned her red-lipped smile on Remus. She held out a tiny hand, and he shook it awkwardly, not sure if he was supposed to kiss it.
“真可爱！”她转向雷穆斯，露出红唇微笑。她伸出一只小手，雷穆斯尴尬地握了握，不确定是否应该吻它。

“Darling, this is Remus, and his friend Grant. Remus… this is Åsa,” Christopher mumbled, “My wife. And Henrik, my son.”
“亲爱的，这是雷穆斯，他的朋友Grant。雷穆斯……这是Åsa，”Christopher含糊地说，“我的妻子。这是Henrik，我的儿子。”

“Pleased to meet you,” Remus nodded. Grant nodded too, but Remus could tell he was uncomfortable.
“很高兴见到你，”雷穆斯点头。Grant也点头，但雷穆斯能看出他不舒服。

“It is a pleasure!” Åsa gushed, “I have to say, I don’t meet so many of Christopher’s school mates. You must come for dinner one evening, and tell me all about his mischiefs!”
“很高兴见到你！”Åsa兴奋地说，“我得说，我不常见到Christopher的校友。你一定要某天晚上来吃晚饭，告诉我他所有的恶作剧！”

“Ha, yeah, definitely,” Remus laughed self-consciously, rubbing the back of his neck. He didn't even know what he was saying. Christopher was married?! He had a kid?!
“哈，是啊，当然，”雷穆斯自觉地笑着，揉了揉脖子后面。他甚至不知道自己在说什么。Christopher结婚了？！他有孩子了？！

“好了，我们该走了。”Christopher说，脸上表情奇怪地空白。“圣诞快乐，雷穆斯。”

“圣诞快乐……”雷穆斯尴尬地挥了挥手，看着那家人转身离开，朝对角巷走去。

“是我吗，”Grant说，当他们离开时，“还是那很奇怪？”

“Very.” Remus said. “He must have met her in Sweden… He said his family sent him there…”
“非常。”雷穆斯说。“他一定是在瑞典认识她的……他说他的家人把他送到那里……”

“不是她奇怪。”Grant说。

“Oh!” Grant said. “Right, I get it. Poor bloke.”
“哦！”Grant说。“对，我明白了。可怜的家伙。”

“超过十八个月。”Grant耸耸肩。

当他和Grant从雨中回来时，他们已经冻僵了，浑身湿透。他们洗了个热水澡来暖和一下，然后雷穆斯在旧的飞路连接处点燃了火，为Grant加热公寓。

“Magic.” Remus yawned, as Grant settled down beside him.

“I’m like that bloke in Bewitched married to the sexy blonde.”

“I don’t wiggle my nose though.”

“Aww, now I’ll never leave you alone until you do,” Grant grinned.

Remus gave him a haughty look, and pointed his wand at the radio. They were so cosy, it felt wrong to switch the telly on.

萊姆斯傲慢地看了他一眼，用魔杖指著收音機。他們是如此的舒適，打開電視感覺很不對勁。

"I thought you were against the commercialisation of Christmas." Remus commented, wryly. Grant elbowed him,

“Nah, it’s something beginning with a C,” Grant replied, sipping his tea.

“Siren? Isn’t that like a mermaid?”

“Sort of. They lure men in with their singing.”

“Are they real?” Grant asked. He always wanted to know.

“Yes, mermaids are. I don’t know if Calypso was.”

“Odysseus’s story is called The Odyssey. It’s all about his journey home from the Trojan War.” Remus furrowed his brow, trying to remember. It was Homer - he'd read that in his second year, either before or after The Epic of Gilgamesh, he couldn't remember. He hadn't really liked The Odyssey - he'd preferred The Illiad, because that had all the good war stuff in it. Maybe he'd feel different now, as an adult.

“特洛伊人……他们是用木马的那群人吗？”Grant问，仍在努力跟上话题。

“Yeah, that’s right. Odysseus gets into all sorts of trouble as he tries to get home to his wife, Penelope. But the sea god gets angry with him about something - can't remember what, but he destroys Odysseus’s ship, and he washes up on this island, where Calypso lives. She falls in love with him and holds him hostage for seven years.”

“对，就是他们。奥德修斯在试图回家见妻子佩内洛普的途中遇到了各种麻烦。但海神因为某些事情生气了——我不记得是什么了，但他摧毁了奥德修斯的船，奥德修斯被冲上了卡吕普索居住的岛上。她爱上了他，并把他囚禁了七年。”

“What does she do to him?”

“Oh, I dunno. Feeds him, heals his wounds and stuff. I think she dances a lot.”

“She doesn’t sound too bad. She sounds kind.”

“Maybe. But she wants to make him immortal, and Odysseus wants to get back to Penelope. Calypso isn’t his true love.”

“Sort of sad.” Grant huffed, sounding put out.

“It’s just a story.” Remus shrugged.

Chapter 176: 1983These people 'round here

Wear beat down eyes sunk in smoke dried faces

They're resigned to what their fate is.

But not us, (no never) no not us (no never)

We are far too young and clever.

 

6th June 1983

“Sometimes I wonder if you’re using me.” Grant said, one afternoon in the summer of 1983.

“We all use each other.” Remus replied, dryly, “And that’s what we think love is.”

“Christ. Can’t talk to you when you’re like this.” Grant sighed heavily, reaching for a packet of cigarettes on the bedside table.

“Like what?”

“A gloomy git.”“一个阴郁的家伙。”

Grant pulled a long white cylinder from the box with his teeth, and Remus lit it with his wand point. Grant sucked on it appreciatively, settling back against Remus’s body, in the crook of his arm. Remus lazily stroked Grant’s collar bone until it was his turn to smoke. They’d almost given up; sharing a quick post-sex fag was their treat.

 

Grant用牙齿从盒子里抽出一根长白色香烟，Remus用魔杖点燃了它。Grant欣赏地吸了一口，靠在Remus的身体上，躺在他的手臂弯里。Remus懒洋洋地抚摸着Grant的锁骨，直到轮到他自己抽烟。他们几乎放弃了；共享一根快速的性爱后的烟是他们的小奖赏。

“Sorry.” Remus said, “I don’t mean to be gloomy.”

“Pfft.” Grant replied, cheerfully, “Be gloomy if you want, I’m only teasin' ya. ”

Grant made everything so easy. Remus could barely remember when their relationship had grown into what it was now.

...

It had started with the regular visits, after that first intervention. They’d grown more frequent, and eventually Grant was just there all the time - first he slept on the couch, and then he didn’t anymore, and it was never discussed again.

By midsummer 1982, he’d moved all of his belongings in - such that they were.

“I travel light,” he winked, shaking out a rucksack that contained a few clean pairs of underwear and some t-shirts. One sock. For god’s sake.“我旅行轻便，”他眨眼说道，摇了摇一个背包，里面只有几条干净的内裤和几件T恤。还有一只袜子。天哪。

“I’ll give you some money.” Remus said, monotonously. “You can go shopping.” He still had a few hundred pounds Sirius had converted to muggle money in case of emergencies. Remus didn’t feel guilty about spending it; it was just sitting there.“我会给你一些钱。”Remus单调地说，“你可以去购物。”他还有几百英镑是Sirius兑换的麻瓜货币，以备紧急情况。Remus对花这些钱不感到内疚；反正就那么放着。

“I’m not here to scrounge off you.” Grant insisted.

“我不是来向你乞讨的。”Grant坚持道。

“I know. But you need clothes.”

“Yes mum. I’ll borrow some of yours for a bit, ‘til I get myself sorted.”

“Fine.”

 

 

So Remus went to Debenhams by himself one afternoon and bought as much as he could in Grant’s size. Jeans and t-shirts and underwear and socks and jumpers, pyjamas and even a cheap pair of trainers that were on offer. British dictionary:
- Debenhams - National chain of department stores. Every mum's favourite.
- Trainers - Sneakers/tennis shoes/runners/kicks
- 'Penny for 'em?' - Penny for your thoughts (i.e. 'tell me what you're thinking').
- Boys' Remand Centre - Criminal detention centre for boys under 17.
- Poll Tax - Brought in by Margaret Thatcher and the Conservative government in the '80s, this tax paid for Local Government (now called 'Council Tax'). Before 1979, this was paid by each household based on the market rental value of the property. The Poll Tax was a flat rate per person - meaning that the burden of payment shifted from wealthy home owners to poor renters. It was massively unfair and resulted in nationwide protests and rioting.

This was a revelation; he could do the bulk of it at home, and then just take it up to Holborn once it was done. He did need to get a national insurance card, and a muggle bank account, but that was easy enough with a few tactical glamour spells at the bank.

1987年春天，雷穆斯走了点运气。格兰特的一位老同学现在在UCL的法律系工作，设法为雷穆斯找到了一份自由编辑的工作。这对雷穆斯来说是个启示；他可以在家完成大部分工作，然后一旦完成，就带到霍尔本。他确实需要一张国民保险卡和一个麻瓜银行账户，但在银行用几个战术幻术就轻松搞定了。

Remus only cheated a little bit, using magic to help him read and correct spelling, but he found the work surprisingly enjoyable, and even started a little business marking exam papers for some of the local muggle schools.
雷穆斯只稍微作弊了一点，用魔法帮助他阅读和纠正拼写，但他发现这份工作出乎意料的有趣，甚至还开始了一些为当地麻瓜学校批改试卷的小生意。

“Dunno how you can concentrate so long.” Grant shook his head at the pile of papers Remus had amassed one evening. “I’d go out of my mind.”
“真不知道你怎么能集中这么久。”有一天晚上，格兰特对雷穆斯堆积的一堆试卷摇了摇头。“我会疯掉的。”

“It’s interesting,” Remus shrugged, “I never got the chance to learn any of this stuff. Have you heard of quadratic equations?”
“很有趣，”雷穆斯耸了耸肩，“我从来没有机会学这些东西。你听说过二次方程吗？”

Grant laughed at him fondly and ruffled his hair, “You boffin.”
格兰特宠溺地笑着揉了揉他的头发，“你这个书呆子。”

Grant himself had been going from strength to strength at work. He loved his job, and put in extra time on the weekends and evenings whenever he could. The boys Grant worked with were every bit as much trouble as the St Edmund’s boys, but that only seemed to spur Grant on. He was always telling Remus about one kid or another who’d had a little victory - a passing mark at school, a week without a fight, time off their sentence. Somehow Grant knew everything about everyone; his memory limitless, his capacity for pride and encouragement unbelievable.
格兰特自己在工作上也越来越顺利。他热爱自己的工作，尽可能在周末和晚上加班。格兰特工作的那些男孩和圣埃德蒙的男孩一样麻烦，但这似乎只会激励格兰特。他总是告诉雷穆斯某个孩子取得的小胜利——在学校及格了，一周没有打架，减刑时间。格兰特似乎对每个人的情况了如指掌；他的记忆力无限，他的自豪感和鼓励能力令人难以置信。

“Got to cut out that article in the Observer,” he might say one evening, “Sounds right up Alfie’s street.” Or, “Staying late tomorrow, with any luck - promised the older lads we’d have a kick-about if none of them get written up.”
“得把观察家报上的那篇文章剪下来，”某个晚上他说，“这听起来正合阿尔菲的口味。”或者，“明天要晚点回家，希望一切顺利——答应了那些大孩子，如果他们没人被记过，我们就踢一场球。”

When he was feeling insecure sometimes Remus would wonder if Grant was only with him because he too was a troubled boy. That Grant was just trying to save him; like he tried to save everybody. He lived for a good cause.
有时当雷穆斯感到不安时，他会想，格兰特是不是和他在一起只是因为他也是个有问题的男孩。格兰特只是想救他；就像他试图救每个人一样。他为了一个好的事业而活。

“Shut up,” Grant would grin at him, if he raised these concerns. “I’ve wanted to get in your pants since we were teenagers, it’s got nothing to do with your tortured past.”
“闭嘴，”如果雷穆斯提出这些担忧，格兰特会咧嘴笑着对他说。“我从我们还是青少年时就想上你的床，这和你的痛苦过去无关。”

And then Remus would remember that after all, Grant was a care home kid himself. Something which was easy to forget, because unlike Remus, he bore it lightly, with a casual shrug of acceptance. Poverty, lack of education, mistreatment - none of this weighed Grant down in the same way. At least not on the surface. But Remus had been wrong about people before.
然后雷穆斯会记起，毕竟，格兰特自己也是个寄养院的孩子。这点很容易忘记，因为与雷穆斯不同，他轻松地接受了这一切，随意地耸了耸肩。贫穷，缺乏教育，虐待——这些都没有以同样的方式压垮格兰特。至少表面上没有。但雷穆斯以前对人有过误判。

As a result of Grant’s dedication to his work, and Remus’s own relatively low impact employment, Remus found himself in a position he had never been in before - having both free time and a bit of disposable income.
由于格兰特对工作的投入，以及雷穆斯自己相对低影响的就业，雷穆斯发现自己处于一个前所未有的境地——既有空闲时间又有一点可支配收入。

He didn’t need much - the flat was paid for, their furniture was serviceable, and they could generally afford to keep the electric and hot water on. He bought clothes every once in a while, but he hardly shopped at Harrods. There was the drink, but he reasoned that as he didn’t smoke any more, he could put his tobacco money towards booze.
他不需要太多——公寓已经付清，他们的家具还算可用，他们一般能负担得起电费和热水费。他偶尔买些衣服，但几乎不在哈罗德购物。至于喝酒，他认为既然他不再抽烟了，可以把烟草钱用来买酒。

What Remus did enjoy doing was going for walks. Not countryside rambles - he got enough of that on full moons - but wandering through London by himself, enjoying the streets, the people. He visited every free museum in London - the National Gallery, the Portrait Gallery, the V&A, the British Museum. He became quite cultured, in fact. And if his hip hurt (which it often did, now, as he entered his late twenties), he could easily hop on a bus.
雷穆斯喜欢做的是散步。不是乡村漫步——满月时他已经够多了——而是独自漫步在伦敦，享受街道和人群。他参观了伦敦的每一个免费博物馆——国家美术馆，肖像馆，V&A博物馆，大英博物馆。事实上，他变得相当有文化。如果他的臀部疼痛（现在进入二十多岁后经常如此），他可以轻松地上公交车。

So, one summer's day, he had completed all of his marking, and there was nothing on TV, Grant would not be home for hours, so he mooched around the Science Museum for an hour or so. Funnily enough, it put him in mind of Arthur Weasley, for the first time in years. The daft old bugger would love all of the machines, the pistons, the lightbulbs. He could just picture Arthur’s face as he watched the perpetual motion machine, and Remus smiled to himself, quite out of the blue. How was Arthur? And his wife, the Prewetts’ sister, and their redhaired brood? It had been too long now to get in touch, Remus knew, and he wouldn’t know what to say, even if he did.
于是，有一个夏天的日子，他完成了所有的批改，电视上也没什么好看的节目，格兰特还要几个小时才能回家，所以他在科学博物馆闲逛了一个小时左右。有趣的是，这使他想起了亚瑟·韦斯莱，这是多年来第一次。那个傻老家伙会喜欢所有的机器，活塞，灯泡。他可以想象亚瑟看着永动机时的表情，雷穆斯不由自主地笑了。亚瑟怎么样了？他的妻子，普雷威特家的姐姐，还有他们红发的一群孩子？雷穆斯知道，已经太久没有联系了，即使联系上了，他也不知道该说什么。

Still, thinking about the Weasleys hadn’t hurt, which was the main thing. And perhaps thinking about them put him in a different mindframe for the afternoon - more alert, maybe, or nostalgic. It couldn’t be a coincidence that he bumped into an old friend only two hours later.
不过，想到韦斯莱一家并没有让他感到痛苦，这才是最重要的。也许，想到他们让他下午的心情有些不同——也许更警觉，或更怀旧。两个小时后遇到一个老朋友，这不可能是巧合。

He was nearly home, only a street or so away, shuffling anonymously through the bustling Chinatown alleyways. In fact, he was just about to pass the place they’d got their tv - the sauna off Old Compton Street. Remus always blushed a bit, walking past it, and then chastised himself for being such a prude. He ducked his head slightly, as he approached, and - horror of horrors - just as he was level with the door somebody stepped out of it.
他快到家了，只剩一条街的距离，匿名地穿过熙熙攘攘的唐人街小巷。事实上，他正要经过他们买电视的地方——旧康普顿街旁的桑拿房。雷穆斯每次走过都会脸红，然后责备自己太保守。他微微低下头，靠近时——恐怖中的恐怖——正好有人从门里走出来。

Remus had to stop short, so as not to bump into them. They turned and stared up at him, nervously.
雷穆斯不得不停下脚步，以免撞到他们。他们转过身，紧张地抬头看着他。

Remus gasped. “Christopher!”
雷穆斯倒吸一口气。“克里斯托弗！”

The man blinked, horrified. He was red faced with dark brown eyes that were rather small and watery. He was a bit chubbier than he had been at school, and his hairline was receding slightly at the temples. But it was definitely him.
那个男人眨了眨眼，惊恐万分。他脸色通红，深棕色的眼睛相当小且水汪汪的。他比在学校时胖了一点，发际线在两鬓稍稍后移。但这确实是他。

“Remus?”

“Hi! It's been…”

“Not since…”

“Yeah. How are you?” Remus winced even as he asked the question. Christopher was so clearly uncomfortable - and why shouldn’t he be? He hadn’t seen Remus in almost ten years, and now here he was, looming over him outside a gay sauna.
“嗯，你好吗？”雷穆斯一边问问题一边皱着眉头。克里斯托弗显然很不舒服——他不应该不舒服吗？他几乎有十年没见过雷穆斯了，而现在，雷穆斯就在一个同性恋桑拿房外俯视着他。

“Oh… you know.” Christopher looked at his feet.
“哦……你知道的。”克里斯托弗看着自己的脚。

He was wearing muggle clothes - a stonewashed denim shirt with the buttons done up unevenly, dress trousers and a burnt orange waistcoat with green embroidery. In short, he looked as dreadful as every pureblood wizard who tried to pass as a muggle. As always, Christopher’s general air of hopelessness endeared Remus to him.
他穿着麻瓜衣服——一件石洗牛仔衬衫，纽扣扣得不均匀，西裤和一件带绿色刺绣的烧橙色马甲。总之，他看起来和每个试图冒充麻瓜的纯血巫师一样糟糕。像往常一样，克里斯托弗那种无助的气质让雷穆斯对他充满了好感。

“Er…” Remus rubbed the back of his head. “Do you want to… um. Got time for a coffee? Or a drink? Catch up a bit?”
“呃……”雷穆斯揉了揉后脑勺。“你想……嗯。有时间喝杯咖啡吗？或者喝一杯？聊聊近况？”

“Ok then…” Christopher looked up at him, cautiously.
“好吧……”克里斯托弗小心翼翼地抬头看着他。

Remus took charge from that point, because it was clear there was no other way. He led Christopher further up the street, back towards Tottenham Court Road. There was a cafe on Denmark Street that was cheap and anonymous, and for some reason Remus wanted to get further away from home.
从那一刻起，雷穆斯接管了，因为显然没有其他办法。他带着克里斯托弗沿街走回托特纳姆法院路。丹麦街上有一家廉价而不起眼的咖啡馆，不知为何，雷穆斯想离家更远一些。

“Here we are,” he smiled kindly, holding the door open and pointing out an available table. Christopher said nothing, and sat down, fidgeting a bit. Remus wondered if this was all a terrible idea - maybe Chris didn’t want to speak to him. But he went along with it, and offered to pay when Remus went to order their coffees.
“到了，”他友善地笑着，打开门并指向一张空桌子。克里斯托弗一言不发，坐下后有些不安地扭动。雷穆斯想知道这是不是个糟糕的主意——也许克里斯不想和他说话。但他还是配合了，并在雷穆斯去点咖啡时提出付款。

 

“Do you live nearby?” Christopher asked, finally, still not fully making eye contact.
“你住在附近吗？”克里斯托弗终于问道，依然没有完全与他眼神接触。

“Yeah,” Remus nodded, “Not far. You?”

“Oh, no. Out in Hampshire. I just come into the city for work, and… well.”

“Where do you work now?” Remus asked, desperate to spare him any further embarrassment.

“Gringotts.” Chris said, glancing up at the waitress as their coffees arrived. He put three sugars in his, and as much milk as he could - Remus realised he hadn’t even asked if Chris liked coffee.

“Very swish,” Remus smiled, “Always knew you’d do well.”

“I suppose.”

“Still read lots?”

“When there’s time… work keeps me busy. And other responsibilities, you know how it is. I thought we were overworked during NEWTs, but Hogwarts was a holiday compared to real life.”

Remus chewed the inside of his cheek, because that was very true, and he didn’t want to get upset about it.

“How about you?” Christopher asked, clearly trying not to grimace as he sipped his coffee. “What do you do, now?”

“This and that,” Remus shrugged. “Haven’t exactly got a career.”

“Oh, what a shame.”

 

Remus shrugged, “It’s fine, I manage.”

There was an awkward silence. Remus wanted to ask about the sauna, but he knew better. Grant would probably ask, but then Grant had a way of putting people at ease which Remus didn’t. He just drank his coffee quietly, and wished he’d suggested a pub, instead.

一陣尷尬的沉默。萊姆斯想詢問桑拿的事，但他更清楚。格蘭特可能會問，但格蘭特有辦法讓人們放鬆，而萊姆斯卻沒有。他只是安靜地喝著咖啡，希望他能推薦一家酒吧。

“I thought you’d died.” Christopher said, suddenly. Remus nearly choked. He set down his coffee.

“You…”

“There were so many rumours, back then - you remember what it was like. And there were all these names, and when I saw what had happened to Lily, and your friend James, I just thought… especially after it came out that Sirius Black was the one who did it, I just assumed...”

Remus breathed in, sharply, and waited for the pain to retreat. When it did, he exhaled slowly, and said, very evenly,

“No. I wasn’t there, that night. I had no idea what Black was up to. No one did.”

“He was always up to something,” Christopher said, darkly. “And with his family… I suppose it didn’t come as much of a surprise, really.”

“No.” Remus said, not really knowing what he was saying anymore, just trying to ignore the roaring in his head, “I suppose not.”

“I was so upset about Lily, though. She was kind. Do you know where Harry is, now? The boy who lived?”

Remus just shook his head. He drank more coffee - probably not a brilliant idea to add caffeine to his already speeding heart rate, but he was trying to be as normal as possible.

“If you weren’t dead,” Christopher continued, “I thought you might just not want to talk to me.”

 

“Why?”

“I know you and your friends were all involved in the war - helping Dumbledore and everything. I didn’t… my parents sent me to Sweden, after I finished my NEWTs. They were worried about me, they wanted me out of the way. You remember what things were like.”

Yes , Remus wanted to say, yes, I bloody remember. Sometimes I wake up and it’s like it’s still happening.

“And with us being purebloods… I think they were worried I’d have to pick a side. So they sent me away - we have family in Gothenburg, and I got my qualification in Magical Finance.”

“Right.” Remus nodded. He really needed to talk about something else. “Good for you, Chris. So, um… are you in Soho often?”

 

Christopher turned crimson again, and looked down at his mug of coffee. “Only… only sometimes. Honestly, I just heard about that place and thought I’d take a look, I didn’t… I don’t want you to think…”

“You know you ought to be careful,” Remus said, lowering his voice in case any of the cafe patrons were listening in, “There’s this illness the muggles are getting - I’m not sure how much your lot know about it, but it’s really serious.”

“Like I said,” Christopher said, “I barely go there, really. Just stupid curiosity.”

Remus felt a twinge of guilt, for making Christopher feel bad. If Grant had taught him anything, it was that you should never add to anyone’s personal shame. It was a wasted emotion anyway, no need to make it worse.

“There’s nothing wrong with being curious,” Remus said, gently, “Lots of people go to those places.”

“Do you?” Christopher looked up at him.

“No.” Remus said, a bit too quickly. “Er… I mean, you know I was never very sociable.”

“Oh, of course. I can imagine, after everything that happened…”

Remus didn’t want to get onto that, so he changed the subject, “Seeing anyone?” he asked, “Got a boyfriend?”

Christopher shook his head. “No. It’s difficult, you know. The job I have, my family. Things have been… well, there’s been a fair bit of trial and error, in that respect.”

Remus wanted to squeeze his hand over the table, but it wasn’t really the place. He tilted his head, sympathetically,

“It will get better, Chris.”

Christopher looked at him with a resigned smile. “Mm, yes, I remember you saying something like that before, at school. Someone for everyone.”

 

“Well, there is.” Remus nodded, encouragingly. “More than one person, even.”

“I don’t know.” Chris sighed, “I don’t know if it’s healthy to think like that. There are so many factors to consider, and I don’t… I don’t think it works like in books. I don’t think everyone has that experience.”

That was a difficult thing to hear. Remus didn’t know what to say, really, and felt weirdly self-conscious and naive. Certainly, Remus did not glamourise romance any more - if he ever had at all. Love had beaten the shit out of him on more than one occasion. But it had also been the only thing worth living for. It had lifted him, protected him, and kept him human. He had a sudden longing to see Grant, and wondered if he’d be home yet.
那是一件很难听的话。雷穆斯真的不知道该说什么，感觉莫名地自觉和天真。当然，雷穆斯不再美化爱情——如果他曾经有的话。爱情不止一次把他打得体无完肤。但它也是唯一值得活下去的东西。它抬起了他，保护了他，让他保持人性。他突然很想见到Grant，不知道他是否已经回家。

 

“Don’t feel sorry for me,” Christopher said, briskly, checking his pocket watch, “I have a nice enough time. I like my work, I make plenty of money, and when I get a free evening I still… you know, I’m able to enjoy myself once in a while. I just see it as a treat, rather than a lifestyle. Actually,” he leaned in a little, “I have a flat in Kensington - for when I work late, and don’t want to apparate all the way home. It’s nice there, if you’d like to see it.” He raised an eyebrow suggestively.
“别为我感到难过，”克里斯托弗干脆地说，查看他的怀表，“我过得还不错。我喜欢我的工作，挣了不少钱，有空的时候我还能……你知道，偶尔享受一下。我只是把这看作一种享受，而不是一种生活方式。实际上，”他微微靠近，“我在肯辛顿有一套公寓——为了工作到很晚，不想幻影移形回家的时候。那里很不错，如果你想去看看。”他挑了挑眉，暗示性地说。

Remus’s mouth went dry, and he swallowed, flustered,

“Um. Nice of you to offer, really, but. I’d better be getting home. I’ve got someone waiting.”

“Oh.” Christopher sat up straighter, withdrawing. His face seemed to close up. “You’ve got someone.”

“Yes, for a few years, now.” Almost six, he realised. Longer than he’d had Sirius - if he’d ever really had Sirius.

“Well. Good for you, then. Look, I’d better go, Remus, it was very nice to see you again.” Christopher stood up, and extended a formal hand for Remus to shake. “We ought to have a proper catch up, one of these days, let me know if you’re ever in Diagon Alley, perhaps, I’ll arrange lunch.”

“Ok,” Remus nodded, shaking his hand.

He knew he would never be in Diagon Alley, and as Christopher didn’t give him any contact details Remus assumed that the invitation was merely politeness. He did not miss pureblood hypocrisy.他知道自己永遠不會去對角巷，而且由於克里斯托弗沒有給他任何聯繫方式，萊姆斯認為邀請只是出於禮貌。他並不懷念純血統的虛偽。

Remus walked home quickly, ignoring the ache in his hip, and was relieved beyond belief to find Grant already there, in the kitchen.

 

萊姆斯快步走回家，忽略了臀部的疼痛，難以置信地發現格蘭特已經在廚房裡了，他鬆了一口氣。

“Wotcher, boffin,” he grinned, “How was the museum?”

“Good, thanks. Interesting.”

“Reckon I should take some of the lads there on a trip, if I can get it past the governor.” He held up two tins, “Beans on toast, or spaghetti hoops on toast?”“我想如果我能通過州長的話，我應該帶一些小伙子去那裡旅行。”他舉起兩個罐頭，“吐司上放豆子，還是吐司上放意大利麵圈？”

“Whichever you prefer,” Remus said, watching him. Grant looked at them both cheerfully,

“Hoops then. With lots of Worcestershire, eh?”那就籃球吧。伍斯特郡有很多地方，是嗎？

“Sounds perfect.” Remus breathed.

“ Perfect ,” Grant chuckled, “You must be hungry.”

“No, I just… just missed you, that’s all.”

“I’ve only been at work.”

“I know…”

“Daft sod.” Grant shook his head, still smiling, turning his back to open the cutlery drawer and find the tin opener.“愚蠢的草皮。”格蘭特搖搖頭，仍然微笑著，轉身打開餐具抽屜，找到開罐器。

Remus crossed the room quickly, and hugged him, wrapping his arms around Grant’s waist, pulling him in and inhaling the scent of him. Grant set down the tin opener carefully, and hugged Remus back, rubbing his arms. “You alright, sweetheart?”萊姆斯快步穿過房間，擁抱了他，用雙臂環抱格蘭特的腰，把他拉進懷裡，吸入他身上的氣味。格蘭特小心翼翼地放下開罐器，回抱萊姆斯，揉搓他的手臂。 “你還好嗎，親愛的？”

 

“Mmmhm.” Remus said, into his neck. “Just glad you’re here.”

 

“嗯嗯。”萊姆斯對著他的脖子說。 “很高興你在這裡。”

British-isms:
- UCL - University College London
- National insurance card - Has your national insurance number on it. In the UK you need this to get a job, as it ensures you are making the right tax contributions on your salary. National insurance payments, made over your working life, mean you are entitled to various benefits (Job seekers allowance, maternity allowance etc.) and your state pension. I'm guessing wizards don't have them lol.
- The Observer - National broadsheet newspaper.
- Kick-about - impromptu/casual game of football. I'm guessing it's the equivalent to when Americans 'toss a ball around' or 'play catch'.
- Harrods - (not sure this actually needs explaining) high-end London department store, only used by tourists and the mega-rich.
- Boffin - a clever person (nerd, geek etc.)
- Worcestershire - Worcestershire sauce - the best possible condiment for beans/hoops on toast. Pronounced 'wooster', like the place.)

 

 

Chapter 180: 1989Got on a lucky one

Came in eighteen to one

I've got a feeling

This year's for me and you

So happy Christmas

I love you baby!

I can see a better time

When all our dreams come true.


In 1989, Remus actually went to Oxford Street to do his Christmas shopping, on Grant’s insistence.

“You’ve never been?!” He had gasped, eyes wide, “You haven’t seen the lights?!”

“I didn’t think proper Londoners got involved in all that nonsense.” Remus replied, defensively.

“ Proper Londoners leave the house.” Grant said. “And buy presents for their friends.”

“I don’t have any friends.” Remus said - then felt awful. Because of course, he had Grant.

“What about that Mary bird? Sends you letters all the time.”

“Oh yeah. I could get her something, maybe.”

“That’s the spirit, Ebenezer.”
“这就对了，埃比尼泽。”

Remus shrugged off the teasing, because he knew Grant loved Christmas - or any opportunity to celebrate, really - and Grant had had a very difficult year.
雷穆斯无视了这个玩笑，因为他知道Grant喜欢圣诞节——或任何庆祝的机会——而Grant这一年过得非常艰难。

Having worked so hard to gain his school leaving certificate, pushing every step of the way to get A-Levels and various other qualifications, all so that he could have his dream job, which was helping other people, Grant had finally come up against an insurmountable opponent. The government - more specifically, The Local Government Act.
Grant辛苦地拿到了毕业证书，每一步都在努力获得A-Level和其他各种资格证书，只为了能拥有他梦想的工作，即帮助他人。但最终，Grant遇到了一个无法逾越的对手。政府——更具体地说，是《地方政府法》。

In 1988, Section 28 passed, and Grant was no longer secure in his position at work. Remus hadn’t really understood it at first, or at least, couldn’t see why Grant should have to worry.
1988年，《第28条》通过，Grant的工作不再有保障。雷穆斯一开始并没有真正理解，或者至少，不明白Grant为什么要担心。

“You don’t work for the council, though,” he frowned, flicking through the leaflets Grant and his friends had been printing for awareness-raising.
“但你不是为议会工作啊，”他皱着眉头，翻阅着Grant和他的朋友们为了提高意识而打印的小册子。

“Yes I do,” Grant replied, “Local authority includes schools and Borstals - and that's what it’s really about. They don’t want us perverting kids.”
“是的，我是，”Grant回答，“地方当局包括学校和少年犯管教所——这就是问题的实质。他们不希望我们‘诱导’孩子。”

“That’s ridiculous.” Remus said.
“这太荒谬了。”雷穆斯说道。

“I know.”
“我知道。”

Remus re-read the text.
雷穆斯重新读了一遍文本。

A local authority shall not intentionally promote homosexuality or publish material with the intention of promoting homosexuality, or promote the teaching in any maintained school of the acceptability of homosexuality as a pretended family relationship.
地方当局不得故意宣扬同性恋或出版旨在宣扬同性恋的材料，或在任何公立学校教授同性恋作为一种假装的家庭关系的可接受性。

“Pretended?!” Remus shook his head.
“假装的？！”雷穆斯摇了摇头。

“I know.” Grant sighed.
“我知道。”Grant叹了口气。

“What does this mean, though? ‘Promote’ homosexuality? How do you promote it?”
“这是什么意思？‘宣扬’同性恋？你怎么宣扬它？”

“Well that’s where the cunts have been clever, innit.” Grant huffed, “It don’t mean anything, not really. Just means if anyone wants to argue against it the fucking Tories can accuse them of wanting to ‘promote’ queerness or some bollocks.”
“这就是那些混蛋聪明的地方。”Grant气喘吁吁地说，“它其实什么都不意味着。只是意味着如果有人想反对它，该死的保守党可以指责他们想要‘宣扬’同性恋或其他废话。”

“But that’s…”
“但这……”

“Completely mental? Evil? Immoral. Yeah. My mate Gay Bob, he’s already had to shut down the Gay Youths Support group, only started that last year. And my place ain’t exempt, the governor's already asking for a list of books we carry, check none of them are too queer.”
“完全疯了？邪恶？不道德。对。我朋友Gay Bob已经不得不关闭同性恋青年支持小组，只是去年才成立的。而且我的地方也不例外，州长已经在要求我们提供所带书籍的清单，确保其中没有太‘同性恋’的书。”

“But they can’t… they wouldn’t sack you?”
“但他们不能……他们不会解雇你吧？”

“I don’t know, love. I’m already trying to keep my head down over the AIDs thing.”
“我不知道，亲爱的。我已经在尽量低调处理艾滋病的事情了。”

Remus felt even worse about that. The staff at the centre Grant worked at had all been hauled into a meeting one day, and told in no uncertain terms that if any one of them contracted HIV, then they would be dismissed without notice - and the police would be notified. That was terrifying enough.
雷穆斯对此感到更加难过。Grant工作的中心的所有员工有一天都被召集到一个会议上，被明确告知如果他们中的任何一人感染了HIV，他们将被无通知解雇——并通知警方。这已经够吓人的了。

For the past eighteen months, Grant had been working tirelessly with his friends and various groups to appeal Section 28, and it wasn’t going well at all. He’d almost been arrested at one protest, and caught a black eye off an anti-protester at another.
在过去的十八个月里，Grant一直和他的朋友们以及各种团体不懈地努力，呼吁废除第28条，但进展非常不顺利。他几乎在一次抗议活动中被逮捕，在另一次抗议中被反抗议者打了黑眼圈。

“It’s war.” he said fiercely, when he returned, and Remus made him sit still so he could heal it, “It’s us and them, that’s how they want it, and that’s what they’ll get.”
“这是战争。”他凶狠地说，当他回来时，雷穆斯让他坐着不动，好让他能治愈，“这是我们和他们，他们就是这么想的，他们会得到他们想要的。”

Remus did not know what to say. He didn’t want a war, he just wanted to be left alone. He never said that, though, because deep down, he was very proud of Grant’s barefaced refusal to give up or give even an inch. He had always admired bravery most of all.
雷穆斯不知道该说什么。他不想要战争，他只想被单独留下。不过，他从来没有说过，因为在心底，他非常为Grant的毫不退让感到骄傲。他一直最钦佩勇气。

So, in late December, Remus and Grant bundled themselves up in woolly hats, gloves and scarves, and walked through the wintry grey city to Oxford Circus. Grant was right - the prat - the lights were great. Strung across the wide street like jungle vines, great gleaming golden bulbs illuminated the cheerful red double deckers, the shiny black cabs, the glorious silver and green window displays.
因此，在十二月底，雷穆斯和Grant裹上毛线帽、手套和围巾，穿过寒冷灰暗的城市走到牛津街口。Grant说得对——那个蠢人——灯光很棒。像丛林藤蔓一样跨过宽阔的街道，巨大的金色灯泡照亮了欢快的红色双层巴士，闪亮的黑色出租车，光辉的银色和绿色橱窗展示。

It was true, Remus had been avoiding Christmas and all its trappings, just like he avoided his birthdays. He was worried they’d send him hurtling backwards - to Hogwarts, to the Potters mansion, to all of his most bittersweet memories. It was very hard to be without his friends at that time of year.
确实，雷穆斯一直在避开圣诞节及其所有装饰品，就像他避开自己的生日一样。他担心这些会让他猛然回到过去——回到霍格沃茨，回到Potters的豪宅，回到他所有最苦乐参半的记忆中。在那段时间里，没有朋友在身边是非常难熬的。

But there was something very cleansing about the chaos of shopping on Oxford Street. The noise and the bustle and the smells ensured that he couldn’t sulk for very long, and Grant’s enthusiasm for the season did the rest.
但是在牛津街购物的混乱中，有一种非常净化的感觉。喧嚣和熙熙攘攘的气味确保了他不能长时间地闷闷不乐，而Grant对这个季节的热情则完成了剩下的部分。

“Right, let’s have a look for Mary’s pressie first, shall we?” He grinned up at Remus, bouncing on the balls of his feet. “House of Fraser? Or is she a Selfridges girl?”
“好吧，我们先看看给Mary的礼物，好吗？”他对雷穆斯咧嘴一笑，脚尖跳动着。“House of Fraser？还是她是Selfridges的女孩？”

“Whichever is trendier, I s’pose,” Remus said. “What did you have in mind?”
“哪个更时尚，我猜，”雷穆斯说。“你有什么想法？”

“Gawd, I’ve no idea. Bath shit?”
“天哪，我不知道。浴室用品？”

“Yeah,” Remus nodded, “Bath shit. Or perfume?”
“对，”雷穆斯点点头，“浴室用品。或者香水？”

“Ooh, perfume, eh?” Grant nudged him with his elbow, “That’s intimate. Should I be worried?”
“哦，香水，嗯？”Grant用胳膊肘轻推他，“那很亲密。我该担心吗？”

“About Mary?” Remus snorted, “You’d be too late.”
“关于Mary？”雷穆斯哼了一声，“你太晚了。”

They wandered through the perfume departments of three or four big department stores. Remus somewhat regretted his choice, then - his hypersensitive sense of smell meant that he was already nursing a headache after the first stop.
他们在三四家大百货公司的香水部门闲逛。雷穆斯有些后悔他的选择——他过于敏感的嗅觉意味着他在第一站后就已经头疼了。

He eventually settled on something floral, in a pink and gold bottle, because it was pretty, and stylish, and Mary was pretty and stylish. He even had it gift wrapped, in gold paper with a red satin bow. Gryffindor colours, he smiled to himself.
他最终选了一款花香型的香水，装在一个粉色和金色的瓶子里，因为它漂亮又时尚，而Mary也漂亮又时尚。他甚至把它用金色纸包好，系上红色缎带。格兰芬多的颜色，他自言自语地笑了。

“Right, you can buy my present next,” Grant grinned, tugging his sleeve, “I want new socks, mine have all got holes.”
“好吧，接下来你可以给我买礼物了，”Grant笑着说，拉着他的袖子，“我想要新的袜子，我的袜子都破洞了。”

Remus took a big gulp of cold fresh air as they came outside, relieved. “I’ve got to get you something better than socks,” he said.
雷穆斯大口呼吸着新鲜的冷空气，当他们走到外面时，他松了一口气。“我得给你买点比袜子更好的东西，”他说。

“Could do with some new Y-fronts too.” Grant winked, and Remus blushed, looking down. He’d get something really nice, later on, when Grant wasn’t looking. He wasn’t sure what, yet, and he didn’t have a lot - but maybe a new coat might not stretch things too far? Grant was in dire need of one, his second-hand duffle barely kept the chill off.
“也需要一些新的Y型前开裤。”Grant眨了眨眼，雷穆斯脸红了，低下头。他会在Grant不注意的时候买一些真的很好的东西。他还不确定是什么，而且他也没有很多钱——但也许一件新外套不会太过分？Grant急需一件，他的二手粗呢大衣几乎不能御寒。

“What do you want?” Grant asked, looking at a window display designed to look like the north pole, with big white pillows stacked up to look like igloos and gigantic stuffed toy penguins.
“你想要什么？”Grant问，看着一个设计成北极模样的橱窗展示，堆满了像冰屋一样的大白色枕头和巨大的填充玩具企鹅。

“Chocolate.” Remus shrugged.
“巧克力。”雷穆斯耸耸肩。

“That’s what I always get you…”
“那是我总是给你的……”

“That’s all I want, now I don’t smoke.”
“那是我现在唯一想要的，因为我不抽烟了。”

Grant shook his head, tutting at Remus’s temperance.
Grant摇了摇头，对雷穆斯的节制咂舌。

Suddenly, Remus caught a whiff of magic. For a moment he wondered if his senses were just wrecked by all the perfume, but no, it was very clear. He looked up and down the street, curiously. Then he saw him, standing outside the Marks & Spencer’s window display.
突然，雷穆斯闻到了一丝魔法的气息。他一度怀疑是否是他的感官被所有的香水搞坏了，但不是，气息很清晰。他好奇地上下打量街道。然后他看到了他，站在马莎百货的橱窗展示外。

“Christopher? Is that you?” Remus approached slowly.
“Christopher？是你吗？”雷穆斯慢慢走近。

“Remus!” Christopher turned, surprised.
“雷穆斯！”Christopher转过身来，惊讶地说。

“We have to stop meeting like this,” Remus laughed. He was in a good mood, and at least he hadn’t caught Chris in a compromising situation this time.
“我们得停止这样见面了，”雷穆斯笑了。他心情很好，至少这次他没有抓到Chris在一个尴尬的境地。

“Yes, quite right,” Christopher laughed too, a little nervously, clearing his throat at the end. He was carrying several bulging shopping bags, in both hands. “How are you? Sorry I haven’t been in touch, it’s been ever so busy at work.”
“是的，非常正确，”Christopher也笑了，有点紧张，最后清了清喉咙。他双手提着几个鼓鼓的购物袋。“你好吗？抱歉我一直没有联系，工作太忙了。”

“That’s ok. I’m well,” Remus nodded. Christopher’s eyes flicked towards Grant. Remus remembered his manners, “Sorry, er, this is Grant, my…”
“没关系。我很好，”雷穆斯点点头。Christopher的目光转向Grant。雷穆斯记起了礼貌，“抱歉，呃，这是Grant，我的……”

“Better half.” Grant finished with a cheeky grin, holding out a gloved hand. Christopher looked as though he didn’t know whether to laugh along too, but he shifted his shopping bags to shake Grant’s hand.
“另一半。”Grant调皮地笑着说，伸出戴着手套的手。Christopher看起来不确定是否也要笑，但他换了购物袋来握Grant的手。

“Christopher Barley,” he said.
“Christopher Barley，”他说。

“Chris and I were at school together,” Remus explained.
“Chris和我一起上学的，”雷穆斯解释道。

“Oh, I see,” Grant nodded, eagerly, his eyes bulging. He never said anything about it, but Remus knew Grant was secretly dying to meet another wizard, just to compare. “Live in London, do ya?”
“哦，我明白了，”Grant急切地点头，眼睛瞪得大大的。他从来没有说过什么，但雷穆斯知道Grant暗地里很想见到另一个巫师，只是为了比较一下。“住在伦敦吗？”

“Er, no. Just in for shopping, you know. Christmas.”
“呃，不。只是来购物，你知道的。圣诞节。”

“Us too,” Remus said.
“我们也是，”雷穆斯说。

“How nice.” Chris said very formally. It was starting to get a bit weird - Remus felt like they were at a middle class cocktail party or something, exchanging pleasantries.
“真好。”Chris非常正式地说。事情开始变得有点奇怪了——雷穆斯觉得他们像是在中产阶级的鸡尾酒会上之类的地方，交换客套话。

“Chris dear? There you are!” A short blonde woman came trotting up the street in neat black high heels and a gorgeous ermine coat. She was tugging a little boy along by the hand - he looked about five years old, and he had Christopher’s eyes. “Can we go quite soon? There are too many muggles about, it’s suffocating.”
“亲爱的Chris？你在这里！”一个矮个子金发女人穿着整洁的黑色高跟鞋和华丽的白鼬大衣跑上街来。她牵着一个小男孩——他看起来大约五岁，有着Christopher的眼睛。“我们能快点走吗？这里有太多麻瓜了，令人窒息。”

Christopher avoided Remus’s gaze, and greeted the woman.
Christopher避开雷穆斯的目光，迎接了那个女人。

“Sorry, dear, I was just… I bumped into an old Hogwarts friend.” He gestured vaguely.
“抱歉，亲爱的，我只是……碰到了一位老霍格沃茨的朋友。”他模糊地示意。

“How lovely!” She turned her red-lipped smile on Remus. She held out a tiny hand, and he shook it awkwardly, not sure if he was supposed to kiss it.
“真可爱！”她转向雷穆斯，露出红唇微笑。她伸出一只小手，雷穆斯尴尬地握了握，不确定是否应该吻它。

“Darling, this is Remus, and his friend Grant. Remus… this is Åsa,” Christopher mumbled, “My wife. And Henrik, my son.”
“亲爱的，这是雷穆斯，他的朋友Grant。雷穆斯……这是Åsa，”Christopher含糊地说，“我的妻子。这是Henrik，我的儿子。”

“Pleased to meet you,” Remus nodded. Grant nodded too, but Remus could tell he was uncomfortable.
“很高兴见到你，”雷穆斯点头。Grant也点头，但雷穆斯能看出他不舒服。

“It is a pleasure!” Åsa gushed, “I have to say, I don’t meet so many of Christopher’s school mates. You must come for dinner one evening, and tell me all about his mischiefs!”
“很高兴见到你！”Åsa兴奋地说，“我得说，我不常见到Christopher的校友。你一定要某天晚上来吃晚饭，告诉我他所有的恶作剧！”

“Ha, yeah, definitely,” Remus laughed self-consciously, rubbing the back of his neck. He didn't even know what he was saying. Christopher was married?! He had a kid?!
“哈，是啊，当然，”雷穆斯自觉地笑着，揉了揉脖子后面。他甚至不知道自己在说什么。Christopher结婚了？！他有孩子了？！

“Well, we’d better be going.” Christopher said, his face weirdly blank. “Merry Christmas, Remus.”
“好了，我们该走了。”Christopher说，脸上表情奇怪地空白。“圣诞快乐，雷穆斯。”

“Merry Christmas…” Remus gave an awkward wave, as the family turned to walk away, towards Diagon Alley.
“圣诞快乐……”雷穆斯尴尬地挥了挥手，看着那家人转身离开，朝对角巷走去。

“Is it just me,” Grant said, as they left, “Or was that strange?”
“是我吗，”Grant说，当他们离开时，“还是那很奇怪？”

“Very.” Remus said. “He must have met her in Sweden… He said his family sent him there…”
“非常。”雷穆斯说。“他一定是在瑞典认识她的……他说他的家人把他送到那里……”

“It wasn’t her that was strange.” Grant said.
“不是她奇怪。”Grant说。

“No, I mean…” Remus bit his lip, “Er… so I know Chris from school, but I’ve seen him since. About eighteen months ago, coming out of that sauna in Soho.”
“不，我的意思是……”雷穆斯咬了咬嘴唇，“呃……我从学校认识Chris，但我之后见过他。大约十八个月前，他从Soho的那个桑拿浴室出来。”

“Oh!” Grant said. “Right, I get it. Poor bloke.”
“哦！”Grant说。“对，我明白了。可怜的家伙。”

“He never said anything then… he… how old did the kid look, to you?”
“那时他什么也没说……他……你觉得那个孩子看起来多大？”

“Older than eighteen months.” Grant shrugged.
“超过十八个月。”Grant耸耸肩。

“Yeah…”
“是啊……”

It soon began to rain; icy cold December rain, so they ran for the next bus and went home. Remus often thought about Christopher, after that, and it troubled him. There was nothing much he thought he could do about it, and really it was none of his business - but he didn’t understand at all. Had Christopher been convinced, or coerced? Did he love her, was he happy?
很快开始下雨了；冰冷的十二月雨，他们赶上下一班公交车回家。雷穆斯经常想到Christopher，之后，这让他很困扰。他认为自己没什么能做的，而且真的也不关他的事——但他完全不理解。Christopher是被说服了，还是被胁迫了？他爱她吗，他幸福吗？

By the time he and Grant got in from the rain they were freezing and soaked through. They took a hot shower to warm up, then Remus lit a fire in the old floo connection to heat up the flat for Grant.
当他和Grant从雨中回来时，他们已经冻僵了，浑身湿透。他们洗了个热水澡来暖和一下，然后雷穆斯在旧的飞路连接处点燃了火，为Grant加热公寓。

“How does that work when we ain’t got a chimney?” Grant asked, bringing in the tea.

“Magic.” Remus yawned, as Grant settled down beside him.

“I’m like that bloke in Bewitched married to the sexy blonde.”

“I don’t wiggle my nose though.”

“Aww, now I’ll never leave you alone until you do,” Grant grinned.

Remus gave him a haughty look, and pointed his wand at the radio. They were so cosy, it felt wrong to switch the telly on.

萊姆斯傲慢地看了他一眼，用魔杖指著收音機。他們是如此的舒適，打開電視感覺很不對勁。

"Thanks for coming with me, today." Grant said, wrapping his hands around his mug of tea to warm them, "I know you hate crowds."

"I don't mind, really. Thanks for getting me out of the house. And showing me the lights."

"Any time," Grant snorted. "Always cheers me up, Christmas shopping. Y'know, no one's thinking about themselves - just making other people happy - it's nice."

"I thought you were against the commercialisation of Christmas." Remus commented, wryly. Grant elbowed him,

"I am, but some of it's still nice. Anyway, thought you'd like a break from politics this weekend."

Remus didn't respond, just kissed Grant's cheek, and settled in to listen to the radio. The tail end of a Suzanne Vega song was playing. “Love this tune,” Grant murmured, leaning against his shoulder, “Love her voice, all clear and weird, you know what I mean?”

“It’s a greek myth,” Remus replied, drowsily, “Odysseus.”

“Nah, it’s something beginning with a C,” Grant replied, sipping his tea.

“Yes, Calypso - she’s the siren, but Odysseus is the main character.”

“Siren? Isn’t that like a mermaid?”

“Sort of. They lure men in with their singing.”

“Are they real?” Grant asked. He always wanted to know.

“Yes, mermaids are. I don’t know if Calypso was.”

“So what did she do? They fell in love, or what?”

“Odysseus’s story is called The Odyssey. It’s all about his journey home from the Trojan War.” Remus furrowed his brow, trying to remember. It was Homer - he'd read that in his second year, either before or after The Epic of Gilgamesh, he couldn't remember. He hadn't really liked The Odyssey - he'd preferred The Illiad, because that had all the good war stuff in it. Maybe he'd feel different now, as an adult.
“奥德修斯的故事叫《奥德赛》。它讲的是他从特洛伊战争回家的旅程。”雷穆斯皱起眉头，试图回忆。这是荷马的作品——他在二年级时读过，不记得是在《吉尔伽美什史诗》之前还是之后读的。他当时并不太喜欢《奥德赛》——他更喜欢《伊利亚特》，因为里面有很多精彩的战争内容。也许现在作为成年人会有不同的感觉。

“The Trojans... are they the ones with the wooden horse?” Grant asked, still trying to follow the thread.
“特洛伊人……他们是用木马的那群人吗？”Grant问，仍在努力跟上话题。

“Yeah, that’s right. Odysseus gets into all sorts of trouble as he tries to get home to his wife, Penelope. But the sea god gets angry with him about something - can't remember what, but he destroys Odysseus’s ship, and he washes up on this island, where Calypso lives. She falls in love with him and holds him hostage for seven years.”

“对，就是他们。奥德修斯在试图回家见妻子佩内洛普的途中遇到了各种麻烦。但海神因为某些事情生气了——我不记得是什么了，但他摧毁了奥德修斯的船，奥德修斯被冲上了卡吕普索居住的岛上。她爱上了他，并把他囚禁了七年。”

“What does she do to him?”

“Oh, I dunno. Feeds him, heals his wounds and stuff. I think she dances a lot.”

“She doesn’t sound too bad. She sounds kind.”

“Maybe. But she wants to make him immortal, and Odysseus wants to get back to Penelope. Calypso isn’t his true love.”

“Sort of sad.” Grant huffed, sounding put out.

“It’s just a story.” Remus shrugged.

Chapter 181: 1990 And then she turns to me with her hand extended

Her palm is split with a flower with a flame

 

And she says "I've come to set a twisted thing straight."

And she says "l've come to lighten this dark heart."

And she takes my wrist, I feel her imprint of fear

And I say "I've never thought of finding you here."

 

Mary had her first child that year - a little girl she called Rachel, after her mother. Rachel Marlene.
Mary 那年生了她的第一个孩子——一个小女孩，她以母亲的名字叫她 Rachel。Rachel Marlene。
“Not gonna lie,” she told Remus over the phone, “I’m praying she’s a squib. Can’t be doing with all that nonsense.”
“说实话，”她在电话里对雷穆斯说，“我希望她是个哑炮。我可不想再管那些胡闹的事。”
She invited him to the Christening, and he went out of obligation. It had been decades since he’d set foot in a church, and this was a huge catholic one in Croydon. Grant didn’t come, said he was too scared he’d burst into flames when he crossed the threshold.
她邀请他参加洗礼，他是出于义务去的。他已经有几十年没有踏入教堂了，而这次是在克罗伊登的一座大天主教堂。Grant 没有来，他说他害怕一跨过门槛就会被烧成灰烬。
“That’s ridiculous,” Remus sighed, tired and humourless, “Mary is literally a witch. If she’s safe in a church...”
“那太荒谬了，”雷穆斯叹了口气，疲倦而毫无幽默感地说，“Mary 还是个巫婆呢。如果她在教堂里没事……”
“My grandad was a bible-basher,” Grant shuddered, “They can all do one, far as I’m concerned.”
“我爷爷是个狂热的宗教信徒，”Grant 战栗道，“在我看来，他们全都一样。”
Grant was rarely so stubborn, so Remus went alone, and tried not to think about funerals.
Grant 很少这么固执，所以雷穆斯一个人去了，尽量不去想葬礼的事。
After the ceremony, there was a bit of a party in the hall next door, and Mary showed off the baby. She was gorgeous; chubby with huge brown eyes and huge brown curls and a gummy smile sure to be as dazzling as her mothers’ one day. Remus waved at the giggling cherub nervously, and patted her soft baby hand.
仪式结束后，隔壁大厅里有一个小聚会，Mary 带着宝宝四处炫耀。她非常漂亮；胖乎乎的，有着大大的棕色眼睛和大大的棕色卷发，还有一个没有牙齿的笑容，肯定有一天会像她母亲一样耀眼。雷穆斯紧张地向咯咯笑的小天使挥手，并轻拍她柔软的小手。
“I’m completely obsessed with her.” Mary gushed, holding her up, “Want to hold her?” Mary grinned, then laughed that girlish cackle which took him back years, “I’m teasing, Remus darling. Here, I’ll give her to Darren’s mum for a bit, let’s you and me have a catch up…”
“我完全迷上她了。”Mary 说着，抱起她，“想抱抱她吗？”Mary 咧嘴一笑，然后笑出那种让他回到多年以前的少女般的咯咯笑声，“我逗你的，雷穆斯亲爱的。来，我把她交给 Darren 的妈妈一会儿，我们聊聊天……”
They sat on red plastic chairs in a quiet corner of the church hall, clutching paper cups of watered down orange squash. It was a small space, filled with the noise of family celebration, and children playing. Mary’s family was huge, and as brash and loveable as she was. Remus felt very out of place, but what else was new.
他们坐在教堂大厅一个安静角落的红色塑料椅子上，手里拿着装满稀释橙汁的纸杯。那是一个小空间，充满了家庭庆祝的喧闹声和孩子们的嬉戏声。Mary 的家族庞大，像她一样粗犷可爱。雷穆斯觉得自己很格格不入，但这有什么新奇的呢。
“You’re not getting married, then?” Remus asked, “You and Darren?”
“你不结婚吗？”雷穆斯问道，“你和 Darren？”
“Shh, Mum’ll hear you,” Mary giggled, “She’s furious, of course, she’s pretending we had a small ceremony in Jamaica before Rachel was conceived. Nah, I don’t fancy it - and we’ve barely got the time what with the garage and the new house…”
“嘘，妈妈会听到的，”Mary 咯咯笑道，“她当然很生气，她假装我们在 Rachel 怀上之前在牙买加举行了一个小仪式。不，我不想结婚——而且我们几乎没有时间，因为有车库和新房子要忙……”
Remus nodded along, smiling. It felt so good to be sitting next to Mary again; to have her chattering away, full of energy and joy.
雷穆斯微笑着点头。再次坐在 Mary 旁边感觉真好；听她喋喋不休，充满了活力和快乐。
“How about you, still up Soho?” Mary asked, giving him an appraising look. He’d come dressed in a suit he had bought the day before from a charity shop. It was ok; a bit seventies, and too big on him, but that was the style these days anyway.
“你呢，还在 Soho 吗？”Mary 问道，打量着他。他穿着前一天从慈善商店买的一套西装。还不错；有点七十年代的风格，对他来说太大了，但这正是现在的流行款式。
“Yeah.” He nodded, “Don’t think I’ll ever move, to be honest, the flat’s paid for.”
“是的。”他点头说，“说实话，我想我永远不会搬家，房子已经付清了。”
“Got a boyfriend?”
“有男朋友了吗？”
“Mm, sort of…”
“嗯，算是吧……”
“I know you have, why are you being so mysterious? Is he a muggle?”
“我知道你有，为什么这么神秘？他是麻瓜吗？”
“Yeah.”
“是的。”
“Oh, I wish you’d come and see me more often, Remus. I worry about you.”
“哦，我希望你能经常来看我，雷穆斯。我很担心你。”
He smiled at her, “You’re such a mum.”
他对她微笑，“你真像个妈妈。”
That made her laugh. “Guilty!”
这让她笑了起来。“没错！”
She was still beautiful, and looked the same at thirty as she had at eighteen, in his mind. She wore a loud, hot pink dress suit with razor sharp power shoulders and a gleaming gold fascinator perched atop her head. She’d cut her hair short, making her face look more angular, like a Nefertiti bust.
她依然很美，在他眼中三十岁的她和十八岁时一样。她穿着一套鲜艳的热粉色连衣裙，肩部带有锋利的力量感，头上戴着一顶闪亮的金色礼帽。她把头发剪短了，使她的脸看起来更加棱角分明，像是尼费尔提蒂的半身像。
“Mum keeps calling me ‘Grace Jones’,” Mary touched her bare neck self-consciously, “I like it, though. Can’t waste time fussing in front of the mirror when I’ve got the little monkey keeping me on my toes. Are you working somewhere?”
“妈妈一直叫我‘Grace Jones’，”Mary 不自觉地摸了摸自己裸露的脖子，“不过我喜欢。当我有了这个小猴子让我时刻警觉时，不能在镜子前浪费时间。你在工作吗？”
“Oh… here and there,” Remus shrugged, noncommittally. “You know what it’s like.”
“哦……这儿那儿的，”雷穆斯耸耸肩，不置可否。“你知道的。”
“You know Dumbledore gave Snape a job,” Mary leaned in and whispered. Remus didn’t know why - he was the only other person there who knew who Dumbledore or Snape were. “He’s a teacher at Hogwarts, now. Can you believe that?!”
“你知道邓布利多给了斯内普一个工作，”Mary 靠过来低声说。雷穆斯不知道为什么——那里只有他知道邓布利多或斯内普是谁。“他现在是霍格沃茨的老师。你能相信吗？！”
Remus shrugged. Mary continued, furious. This had obviously been on her mind for some time, “When I think of all the suffering that snivelling coward caused! When I think about all the friends I’ve lost… Lily and James, Peter... Marlene.”
雷穆斯耸耸肩。Mary 继续说，愤怒不已。这显然在她心中存了很久，“当我想到那个哭鼻子的懦夫造成的所有痛苦！当我想到我失去

“Snape wasn’t responsible for their deaths.”

“How are we to know? So what, he turned spy for two bloody weeks at the end - and that guarantees him a cushy job for life, does it? What was he doing while we were hiding in cellars like rats? Where was he when we were disappearing by the day?!”
“我们怎么知道呢？就算他最后当了两周的间谍——那也能保证他一辈子有个舒服的职位吗？当我们像老鼠一样躲在地窖里时，他在干什么？我们一天一个消失，他在哪里？！”

“Mary…”
“Mary……”

“I just can’t believe Dumbledore. Has he offered you any help? He hasn’t me. Not worth his time, I suppose. They all stuck together in the end; the old families.”
“我简直不敢相信邓布利多。他有给你什么帮助吗？他没给过我。也许是觉得我不值得他的时间。最终他们都团结在一起；那些老家族。”

“I don’t want anything from him.” Remus said, “Being in Dumbledore’s debt is too dangerous. Anyway. Snape has to live with what he did; just like we all do.”
“我不想要他的任何东西。”雷穆斯说，“欠邓布利多的人情太危险了。总之，斯内普必须面对他所做的事；就像我们都得面对一样。”

She lowered her eyes, then, and Remus knew they were both thinking about Sirius.
她低下了眼睛，雷穆斯知道他们俩都在想天狼星。

“I tell you what, Remus my love,” She said, finally, “I don’t care if she’s magic or not, my baby girl won’t be cannon fodder for that old bastard. Next time that lot want a war, you and me are going to be smart enough to keep well out of it, eh?”
“告诉你吧，我亲爱的雷穆斯，”她最后说道，“我不在乎她是否有魔法，我的宝贝女儿绝不会成为那个老混蛋的炮灰。下次他们想打仗时，你我一定要足够聪明，远离那些事，好吗？”

“Too right.” Remus replied. They could agree on that, at least. He’d join the werewolves again before he ever re-joined the Order.
“说得对。”雷穆斯回答道。至少在这一点上，他们可以达成一致。他宁愿重新加入狼人，也不愿再加入凤凰社。

“You know, having Rachel makes me think about Harry.” Mary said, wistfully. “Now I’ve got a child of my own, just don’t know how Lily and James did it. Remember? We were all just kids, playing mummies and daddies, weren’t we?”
“你知道，有了 Rachel 我会想起 Harry。”Mary 感慨地说道，“现在我自己也有了孩子，真不知道 Lily 和 James 是怎么做到的。记得吗？我们当时都是孩子，只是在玩‘爸爸妈妈’的游戏，不是吗？”

“I s’pose, yeah.”
“是啊，我想是的。”

“He’ll be starting Hogwarts next year, Harry.”
“他明年就要开始霍格沃茨了，Harry。”

“What?! No, that’s not right, he must only be…” Remus struggled to do the maths in his head. “Shit.” He said. “I didn’t even think.”
“什么？！不，这不对，他应该只有……”雷穆斯努力在脑海中计算。“糟糕。”他说，“我没想到。”

“Poor little love, going to school with no parents to see him off.”
“可怜的小家伙，没有父母送他去上学。”

“Mm…”
“嗯……”

“Oh gosh, sorry, Remus! I wasn’t thinking…”
“哦天哪，对不起，雷穆斯！我没想到……”

“It’s fine,” he chuckled, “I’ve got over being an orphan by now.”
“没关系，”他笑了，“我现在已经不再为自己是孤儿而伤感了。”

He stayed for about an hour before heading off to catch his bus in the cold dark of an early winter evening. He clutched two slices of cake wrapped in pink paper napkins - one for you, one for your ‘sort of’ boyfriend, Mary winked as she’d handed them over.
他待了大约一个小时，然后在寒冷黑暗的初冬傍晚离开，去赶公交车。他紧握着两片裹在粉色纸巾里的蛋糕——一片给你，一片给你那“有点”男朋友，Mary 在递给他时眨了眨眼。

He kissed her cheek, and she stretched up on her tiptoes to hug him. She smelled the same, and it made him want to cry.
他亲吻了她的脸颊，她踮起脚尖抱住他。她的味道还是一样，这让他想哭。

“Love you, sweetheart,” she whispered, “I’m so pleased to see you getting back to yourself.”
“爱你，亲爱的，”她低声说，“我很高兴看到你重新回到自己。”

He gave her a half-smile, congratulated her again, and left.
他给了她一个半笑，祝贺她一遍，然后离开了。

She was right. He was getting back to himself - or if not that, becoming somebody else; somebody who was coping. He’d kicked fags and booze, he rarely spent afternoons staring at his bedroom ceiling, unable to get dressed. Sometimes weird things made him anxious, like the smell of motor oil, or when they played old Bowie songs on the radio. Once he’d seen a teenage girl with ginger hair get off a bus in Finsbury Park and almost followed her home. But he was doing better.
她说得对。他正在找回自己——或者说，变成了另一个人；一个能够应对的人。他戒了烟和酒，几乎不会再花时间盯着卧室的天花板，无力起床。有时，一些奇怪的事会让他焦虑，比如机油的味道，或是收音机里播放老鲍伊的歌曲。一次，他看到一个有红发的少女在芬斯伯里公园下了公交车，差点跟着她回家。但他在好转。

Sometimes he could even think about Sirius. Sometimes he could talk about him - only to Grant, and only if he asked. Funny things, like pranks they’d done at school, or stupid in-jokes. He didn’t think about them being together - he turned Sirius into a different person in his mind, just another character from his school days. That made things much easier.
有时他甚至能想到天狼星。有时他可以谈论他——只对 Grant，只有在 Grant 问起的时候。他会说一些有趣的事，比如他们在学校时做的恶作剧，或者那些愚蠢的笑话。他不再想着他们在一起的样子——他在脑海中把天狼星变成了另一个人，只是他学校时代的另一个角色。这让事情容易多了。

After the Christening, on the way home, Remus thought about Harry. He hoped the kid was happy, or at least that he wasn’t angry. Remus tried to picture himself, aged 11, crossing through the barrier at King’s Cross for the first time. It had been nerve-wracking and exhilarating, and he hadn’t known how to act, how to relate to anyone else. And then he’d met James, the first friendly face on the train that day. It was too cruel that Harry wouldn’t ever know him.
洗礼后，在回家的路上，雷穆斯想到 Harry。他希望那个孩子快乐，或者至少希望他不生气。雷穆斯试着想象自己11岁时第一次穿过国王十字车站的屏障。那时既紧张又兴奋，他不知道该怎么表现，怎么与别人相处。然后他遇到了 James，那天火车上的第一个友善面孔。太残酷了，Harry 永远不会认识他。

Remus was in danger of getting nostalgic now, and weepy, so he got off the bus to walk the rest of the way home. He was tired by the time he got in, and his hip hurt, but that was ok; he felt good about having left the house.
雷穆斯现在有点容易感伤和伤感了，于是他下了公交车，步行回家。回到家时他很累，臀部也很疼，但没关系；他对自己离开家感到满意。

“All right, sunshine?” Grant called from the kitchen as Remus shut the front door.
“怎么样，阳光？”Grant 在厨房里喊道，雷穆斯关上前门时。

“Hiya,”
“嗨，”

“How was it?”
“怎么样？”

“Church bit was boring. Seeing Mary was nice.”
“教堂的部分很无聊。见到 Mary 很好。”

“Oh good,” Grant came through to lean in the door frame. He was drying a dish they’d used last night.
“哦，好。”Grant 走过来倚在门框上。他正在擦干他们昨晚用过的碗盘。

“Leave that, I’ll do it.” Remus said, collapsing into the couch.
“别管那个，我来做。”雷穆斯说，瘫倒在沙发上。

“Nah, it's done.”
“别，已经做完了。”

“Mary invited us for dinner. They live out in Hounslow though, bit of a trek… but if you fancied it...”
“Mary 邀请我们去吃饭。她们住在 Hounslow，那儿有点远……但如果你愿意的话……”

“Oh she knows who I am now?” Grant smirked.
“哦，她现在知道我是谁了？”Grant 露出得意的笑容。

“Sort of.” Remus blushed. “she knows I’m seeing someone, just…”
“算是吧。”雷穆斯脸红了。“她知道我在交往，只是……”

“For almost nine years, Remus…”
“快九年了，雷穆斯……”

“Sorry, it's just weird because… Mary knew me back then, you know.”
“对不起，只是有点奇怪，因为……Mary 当时认识我，你知道的。”

“She knew you when you were with Sirius.” Grant said flatly, turning back into the kitchen to put the plate away.
“她认识你那会儿你和天狼星在一起。”Grant 平淡地说，转回厨房放好盘子。

“Don’t be like that!” Remus said, getting up stiffly.
“别这样！”雷穆斯说，僵硬地站起来。

“I’m not being like anything.” Grant’s face was hidden by the cupboard door.
“我什么也没表现出来。”Grant 的脸被橱柜门遮住了。

“I invited you to the Christening, you didn’t want to come.”
“我邀请你去参加洗礼，你却不愿意来。”

“You know bloody well why, too.”
“你也知道原因。”

“You hate churches, I know.”
“我知道你讨厌教堂。”

“Well, then.”
“那就这样吧。”

“Why are we fighting?!” Remus frowned, confused.
“我们为什么要争吵？！”雷穆斯皱眉，感到困惑。

“This isn’t fighting.” Grant closed the door to the cupboard, sighing.
“这不是争吵。”Grant 关上橱柜门，叹了口气。

“What is it, then?”
“那是什么？”

“It was ten years ago, that's all. You’re still acting like I don’t matter as much as he did.”
“那是十年前的事。你还像以前一样表现得我不如他重要。”

“What?! No, that's mad, that's--"
“什么？！不，那太荒唐了，那是——”

“That's all I want to say.” Grant raises a hand to stop him. “Like I said, this isn’t a fight.”
“这就是我想说的。”Grant 举起手制止他。“就像我说的，这不是争吵。”

“But Grant, I don’t… you’re wrong, I swear! I want you to meet Mary, I do!”
“但 Grant，我不……我发誓你错了！我真的想让你见见 Mary！”

“I’m going for a walk, ok? I need some air.” Grant pushed past him to the door. He took his coat off the hook - the coat Remus had bought him last Christmas. “I’ll be back in an hour or so. Take a paracetamol for your hip, will you? You’re limping again.”
“我去散步，好吗？我需要透透气。”Grant 推开他，走向门口。他从钩子上拿下外套——那是雷穆斯去年圣诞节给他买的。“我会在一个小时左右回来。吃片扑热息痛吧，你的臀部又在跛行了。”

Saturday 9th March 1991

“Have you seen my wand?!”

“Nope.”

“Bugger!”

“Where did you last have it?”

“If I knew that I wouldn’t be looking, would I?!”

 

“All right, all right, keep your hair on,” Grant emerged from the bathroom smelling of toothpaste and pantene. Remus had almost turned the living room upside down in his search. He stood in the middle of the mess, running his fingers anxiously through his hair.
“好啦，好啦，别急，”Grant 从浴室里出来，身上有牙膏和潘婷的味道。雷穆斯在找东西时几乎把客厅翻了个底朝天。他站在一片狼藉中，焦虑地把手指穿过头发。

“I’ve got a million exam sheets to mark today, I really need it…”
“我今天有一大堆考试卷要批改，我真的需要它……”

“Just do it without magic, like the rest of us mortals,” Grant shrugged, lifting the couch cushions to help him look.
“就像我们这些凡人一样，别用魔法做，”Grant 摆了摆肩膀，掀起沙发垫子帮忙找。

“I can’t, I really need my wand…” Remus huffed, looking under the TV table.

“Bloody charmer,” he said, bashfully. “Come on, I’ve got a chocolate cake waiting in the fridge at home, you can blow out the candles and we’ll kiss in the dark.”
“该死的魅力者，”他害羞地说道。“走吧，我家冰箱里有一块巧克力蛋糕等着你，你可以吹灭蜡烛，我们在黑暗中亲吻。”

Remus grinned back, “Sounds perfect.”
雷穆斯笑着回应，“听起来很完美。”

He nipped to the loo before leaving. He could have waited until he got home, they were only around the corner, but he felt that this was his last test of bravery.
他在离开前去了一趟洗手间。他本可以等到回家再去的，他们就在拐角处，但他觉得这是他最后一次勇气测试。

The toilets were unisex, which Remus supposed was fair enough, if a bit embarrassing - there weren’t any girls about at least. He went and used a urinal, as quickly as possible, trying to ignore the sound and scent of sex emanating from the cubicles. He was just washing his hands when the door swung open, and somebody closed in behind him. He spun around, surprised, and faced the stranger.
洗手间是中性的，雷穆斯认为这还算公平，尽管有点尴尬——至少没有女孩。他迅速地去使用小便池，试图忽视从隔间里传来的声音和气味。他刚洗手时，门猛地打开了，有人靠近了他。他转过身，惊讶地面对着陌生人。

“What--”
“什么——”

The man grinned wide, showing his teeth. He licked his lips and sniffed the air, and then it hit Remus - the familiar scent, the instant connection - the lack of respect for personal space. A werewolf.
那人咧开嘴笑，露出牙齿。他舔了舔嘴唇，嗅了嗅空气，然后雷穆斯感到——那熟悉的气味，瞬间的联系——对个人空间的无视。一个狼人。

“I smelled your magic,” the man said, his voice low, “Delicious. Haven't seen you before…”
“我闻到了你的魔法，”那人低声说道，“美味。以前没见过你……”

He wasn't as tall as Remus, and he was quite thin, in a skin tight white shirt. He had long flame red hair, straight as a poker, and glacier blue eyes. The scent of earthy natural magic radiated off him in waves that made Remus giddy, blood rushing through his veins and arteries like an elixir.
他没有雷穆斯高，身材也很瘦，穿着一件紧身白衬衫。他有着长长的火焰红发，直得像个铁棍，和冰川蓝色的眼睛。那股自然魔法的气味以波浪般的形式从他身上散发出来，让雷穆斯感到头晕目眩，血液在他的血管中奔流如同灵药。

“Hi…”
“你好……”

The stranger sniffed again, “Which pack are you? You smell like Greyback…”
那人再次嗅了嗅，“你属于哪个狼群？你闻起来像 Greyback……”

Remus balked a bit at the idea he had anything of Greyback in him, but he shook his head, “No pack.”
雷穆斯对自己身上有任何 Greyback 的东西感到有些厌恶，但他摇了摇头，“没有狼群。”

“Brave of you… Not worried you’ll get rounded up by the Ministry?”
“真勇敢……不担心你会被魔法部抓起来吗？”

“What about you? Who are you with?” For a moment Remus hoped he was one of Castor’s - he desperately wanted to know how they were all doing, but the stranger just shrugged.
“那你呢？你和谁在一起？”雷穆斯希望他是 Castor 的一员——他迫切想知道他们的近况，但那人只是耸了耸肩。

“Oh, we drift here and there. You won’t have heard of us.”
“哦，我们在这里那里漂流。你不会听说过我们。”

“But you know Greyback.”
“但你知道 Greyback。”

“Oh yes.” He pulled his shirt down at the collar, revealing an enormous bite mark which was all too familiar to Remus, “We go back a long way, he and I…”
“哦，是的。”他拉了拉领口，露出一个雷穆斯再熟悉不过的巨大咬痕，“他和我认识很久了……”

“The war, were you--”
“战争，你是——”

“Ha, I was barely a pup, back then,” the werewolf raised an eyebrow. His skin was so fair that his scars were like streaks of silver, pearlescent as moonbeams. “But the next war… the next war, we shall be ready for.”
“哈哈，我那时还只是个小狼崽，”狼人扬起一只眉毛。他的皮肤非常白皙，伤疤像银色的条纹，像月光一样闪烁。“但下一次战争……下一次战争，我们会准备好的。”

“There won’t be another war.” Remus said. He was backed against the porcelain sink, the werewolf had placed a hand either side of him. He was trapped, but he’d made no move to escape, not yet. “Voldemort’s dead.”
“不会有下一次战争。”雷穆斯说道。他背靠在瓷盆上，狼人双手放在他身旁。他被困住了，但他还没有动身逃脱。“伏地魔死了。”

“Mmm, some say…” the werewolf smirked. He leaned in and licked behind Remus’s earlobe. It made him shudder all over, he had to hold in a whimper. The other man pressed in on him, and whispered, “But I have heard that part of him lives still. The forests speak of ancient magic, of cursed blood… the dark lord gathers his strength…”
“嗯，有些人这么说……”狼人冷笑。他靠近，舔了舔雷穆斯耳垂的后面。这让雷穆斯全身颤抖，他不得不抑制住呻吟。那个男人靠近他，低声说道：“但我听说他的一部分仍然存在。森林里传说着古老的魔法，诅咒的血液……黑暗领主在聚集力量……”

“No…” Remus shook his head. He tried to push back, but only succeeded in grinding their bodies together. He knew it was all lies, and he knew this man was trouble, but oh god, the scent was so heady, his body wouldn’t listen to him; it only wanted one thing.
“不……”雷穆斯摇了摇头。他试图推开，但只成功地让他们的身体紧贴在一起。他知道这全是谎言，他知道这个人是麻烦，但天啊，那气味如此醉人，他的身体不听使唤，只想要一个东西。

“Come,” the werewolf kept whispering, his breath hot on Remus's neck, “No more talk of war, it’s not our concern just yet… I want to enjoy you. Do you live nearby? We can go anywhere you like - this is going to be so good, the moon’s waxing…”
“过来，”狼人不断低语，他的呼吸在雷穆斯的脖子上热热的，“别再谈战争了，这还不是我们的事……我想享受你。你住得近吗？我们可以去你喜欢的地方——这会很棒，月亮在渐盈……”

Remus shook his head again, as if he could rid himself of the fog of pheromones flooding his system, “I'm here with someone.” He rasped.
雷穆斯再次摇头，好像能将那充斥在他体内的荷尔蒙雾气驱散，“我和别人一起来的。”他嘶哑地说道。

“Bring them, if you like…” the wolf chuckled, “I’m all for sharing.”
“如果你愿意，可以带他们来……”狼人笑了，“我乐于分享。”

“N-no, I have to go…” Remus used his last shred of willpower to extricate himself from the stranger and hurry back into the bar, feeling the wolf's eyes blazing at his back.
“不，我必须走……”雷穆斯用尽最后一点意志力摆脱那个陌生人，急忙回到酒吧，感受到狼人的目光在背后炽热地盯着他。

He found Grant and grabbed his shirt sleeve, hissing, “We have to go home.”
他找到 Grant，抓住他的衬衫袖子，低声说道：“我们必须回家。”

“Eh? You all right, something happen?”
“嗯？你还好吗，发生了什么事？”

“No… um… I just want to go home. I want to take you home.” He met Grant's eyes, still holding his arm, and he wondered if Grant could feel it too, feel the burning, the need. Sirius always could, but perhaps you had to be sensitive to magic? Remus focussed the intensity, projecting it outwards. Grant's eyes flickered and his pupils dilated, a warm blush creeping up his neck.
“没有……嗯……我只想回家。我想带你回家。”他看着 Grant 的眼睛，仍然抓着他的手臂，他想知道 Grant 是否也能感受到那种炽热和需求。Sirius 总是能，但也许你必须对魔法敏感？雷穆斯集中注意力，向外投射那种强度。Grant 的眼睛闪烁，他的瞳孔放大，脖子上爬上了温暖的红晕。

“All right, then.” He knocked back the last of his drink, and they left, running out onto the busy street together, hand in hand.
“好吧。”他一口气喝完了最后一口饮料，他们离开了，一起跑到繁忙的街道上，手牵着手。
