August 1994

For the first week or so after Remus returned from Hogwarts, he didn’t know how to feel. For the first time in a very long time, Remus was lost; untethered, drifting. He wandered around the flat like a ghost, going through the movements of everyday life, but feeling nothing.
在雷穆斯从霍格沃茨回来后的前一两周，他不知道自己该如何感受。很久以来，雷穆斯第一次感到迷茫；没有束缚，漂浮不定。他像鬼魂一样在公寓里徘徊，做着日常生活的动作，却什么也感觉不到。

It wasn’t depression. He knew what depression felt like.
这不是抑郁。他知道抑郁是什么感觉。

“It’s shock,” said Grant.
“这是震惊，” Grant 说。

“Oh.” said Remus, staring blankly at the TV.
“哦。”雷穆斯说道，呆呆地盯着电视。

Obviously he’d expected Hogwarts to stir up old memories. He’d known from the start that re-visiting the place could easily ruin him, but he'd done it anyway. Maybe he was a masochist. Maybe just stupid.
显然，他预期霍格沃茨会唤起旧日的记忆。他从一开始就知道重访这个地方很可能会毁了他，但他还是去了。也许他是个受虐狂，也许只是愚蠢。

The castle was filled with ghosts from Remus’s past, which was a deeply unsettling experience after spending the better part of a decade trying to forget all of it. The moment he arrived at King’s Cross it all came flooding back - the pokey little train carriages with the worn-out upholstery; the trolley witch, chocolate frogs, the bustle and noise of students embarking on a new term. With the full moon ahead of him, he’d squirrelled away in a compartment and promptly fallen asleep.
城堡里充满了雷穆斯过去的幽灵，这是一种令人极为不安的经历，因为他花了大部分十年时间试图忘记这些。一到国王十字车站，一切都涌上心头——那些破旧的火车车厢；推车女巫、巧克力蛙、学生们开始新学期的喧嚣和噪音。在满月的映衬下，他在一个车厢里藏了起来，很快就睡着了。

Until the carriage turned cold, and the dementors...
直到车厢变冷，出现了摄魂怪……

No. Anyway; ghosts. McGonagall was perhaps the strangest. She must have known he would be coming, but their first meeting had hit Remus harder than expected, and she’d seemed just as surprised as him. They weren’t quite sure how to relate to each other, now.
不。总之；幽灵。麦格教授也许是最奇怪的。她一定知道他会来的，但他们的第一次见面比预期的更打击了雷穆斯，她似乎也和他一样惊讶。他们现在不太确定如何相处。

“Mr Lupin! Oh - I’m sorry, Professor Lupin.”
“卢平先生！哦——对不起，卢平教授。”

“Hello Prof-- I mean… er…”
“您好，教授——我意思是……呃……”

“Minerva, please,” she smiled gracefully.
“麦格，请，”她优雅地微笑。

She reached out and squeezed his arm. She was every bit as formidable as she had been twenty years ago, only a little greyer at the temples. But then, so was he. “It’s wonderful to see you, Remus.” She said, earnestly.
她伸出手握住他的手臂。她依旧像二十年前一样威严，只是太阳穴有些灰白。不过，他也是如此。“看到你真是太好了，雷穆斯。”她真诚地说道。

“It’s good to be back,” he lied.
“回到这里很好，”他撒了谎。

Her eyes were soft and kind, as if she could see right through him.
她的眼睛柔和而亲切，好像能看透他一样。

“My office is always open, if you need anything. As ever.”
“我的办公室随时为你开放，如果你需要什么。像往常一样。”

He appreciated the gesture, but didn’t prevail upon her very often, largely because he wanted to keep to himself. He also wanted to stay away from Gryffindor tower, if he could.
他感激这个表示，但他并不常去找她，主要是因为他想保持独处。如果可以的话，他也想远离格兰芬多塔楼。

The rest of the school was familiar; the lush expansive grounds, the secretive forest, the food, the portraits, the staircases he had mapped so carefully. But Gryffindor Tower - the most intimate and happy space of his adolescence; that would be almost too much to recover from. He was put in mind of Homer, once again - the word ‘nostalgia’, which meant a painful homecoming. That was exactly how it felt.
学校的其他部分很熟悉；那片郁郁葱葱的广阔土地，神秘的森林，食物，画像，那些他曾经仔细绘制过的楼梯。但是格兰芬多塔楼——他青春时期最亲密和幸福的地方；那几乎让他难以恢复。他再次想起了荷马——“怀旧”这个词，意味着痛苦的归乡。这正是他的感受。

He didn’t socialise much with his peers. The staff knew, by and large, about his lycanthropy, but he still prefered to avoid any unpleasant conversations, if he could. Were they tutting, behind his back? Were they wondering about him? No one’s seen him for years, he was Black and Potter’s closest friend - what does he know? What did he do?
他很少和同龄人交往。工作人员大致知道他的狼人症，但他仍然更愿意避免任何不愉快的谈话，如果可能的话。他们背后是否在嘲讽？他们是否在猜测他？没人见过他很多年，他是布莱克和波特最亲密的朋友——他知道什么？他做了什么？

Funnily enough, Professor Binns had forgotten Remus, but at least Flitwick hadn’t. He was very kind, inviting Remus him to stop by the Charms classroom for tea and toast a few times. Remus did, to be polite, but found it difficult to forget all the times he and Sirius had locked themselves inside the kindly professor’s classroom. He generally found it very hard to reconcile his adult self, responsible for lesson plans and marking essays and the welfare of students - with his reckless teenage self, wild and arrogant and madly in love.
有趣的是，宾斯教授忘记了雷穆斯，但至少弗里维克教授没有。他非常友善，邀请雷穆斯到魔咒教室喝茶吃吐司几次。雷穆斯出于礼貌去了，但发现很难忘记他和小天狼星曾几次把自己锁在这位和蔼教授的教室里。他通常很难将自己作为成年人——负责课程计划、批改论文和学生福利——与他那个鲁莽的青少年自己——狂野、傲慢、疯狂地恋爱——和解。

There were entire wings of the castle he actively avoided, for this very reason. He barely left his classroom and chambers except for meals in the Great Hall, and he never went to Hogsmeade, except to quickly pass through on the way to the old phone box just outside the village. And thank god that was still there.
由于这个原因，他主动避开了城堡的整个翼楼。他几乎不离开教室和宿舍，除了在大礼堂用餐外，他从不去霍格斯梅德，除了在经过村子外面的旧电话亭时匆匆经过。谢天谢地，那还在那儿。

“How is it?” Grant asked, the first time Remus called.
“怎么样？” Grant 问道，雷穆斯第一次打电话时。

“Awful. Bearable. I s’pose like teaching, the kids are ok. Actually the kids are great.”
“糟糕。可以忍受。我想就像教学一样，孩子们还不错。实际上，孩子们很好。”

“Well. Just focus on that. First time I went into a remand home after St Edmund’s I thought I was gonna have to quit. I swear those places all smell the same. Anyway, you can get past it, if you remember it's about the kids, not you. Be the teacher you wish you’d had.”
“嗯。只要专注于这一点就好。第一次去 St Edmund’s 后的拘留所时，我以为我要辞职了。我发誓那些地方都闻起来一样。无论如何，你可以克服它，只要记住这是关于孩子们，而不是你。成为你希望自己曾经有的老师。”

This was good advice, and Remus did his very best. He hadn’t had much experience with young people, but he very clearly remembered being a young person himself. He tried to organise lessons he would have found interesting, bringing in magical creatures whenever he could, like Ferox had, and giving extra tips and pointers wherever students were struggling. Really it wasn’t too different from the study sessions he’d held back when he was at school.
这是很好的建议，雷穆斯尽了最大的努力。他对年轻人没有太多经验，但他清楚地记得自己曾经年轻过。他试图组织他自己会觉得有趣的课程，尽可能地带来魔法生物，就像 Ferox 所做的，并在学生遇到困难时提供额外的建议和提示。实际上，这与他在学校时举办的学习小组没有太大区别。

Equally, Remus tried to pay attention to all of his students, and learn their characters, their individual needs. That was incredibly weird at first - he found he had no less than five Weasleys to teach, one in almost every year. Then there was poor little Neville Longbottom, awkward and nervous and twitchy. Narcissa’s son was in another class, the spitting image of Lucius, and then, of course, there was…
同样，雷穆斯尝试关注所有的学生，了解他们的性格和个人需求。一开始这非常奇怪——他发现自己要教不下于五个韦斯莱，几乎每年都有一个。然后是可怜的小奈威·隆巴顿，笨拙、紧张和焦躁。纳西莎的儿子在另一个班级里，简直就是卢修斯的翻版，然后，当然，还有……

Anyway. Aside from Flitwick and McGonagall, the rest of the staff were virtual strangers to Remus - except, of course, for the Potions master.
总之。除了弗里维克和麦格教授之外，其他教职员工对雷穆斯来说几乎都是陌生人——当然，除了药剂学教授。

Remus had really wanted to stay out of Snape’s way, but from the very first day it was clear that would not be easy. It was a full moon, and of course Snape was the only one who knew how to brew Wolfsbane Potion, the prick. He probably learnt how to do it just to torment Remus. It was bad enough they had to share a castle again, but Snape was hellbent on making sure Remus felt his displeasure at the arrangement.
雷穆斯真的想避开斯内普，但从第一天起就显然这不容易。那天是满月，当然斯内普是唯一一个知道如何酿制狼毒药水的混蛋。他可能是为了折磨雷穆斯才学会的。我们再次不得不共享一座城堡已经够糟糕的了，但斯内普却誓言要让雷穆斯感受到他对这种安排的不满。

“Lupin.” He said, haughtily, at their first meeting, just before the welcome feast. “I was surprised to hear you survived the war.” His lips curled, “When it seems so many of your friends did not.”
“卢平。”他在第一次见面时傲慢地说道，就在欢迎宴会前。“我很惊讶你活过了战争。”他的嘴唇翘起，“当许多你的朋友却没有活过来。”

As foul as Snape was, it did bring out something Remus hadn’t properly felt in years. Mischief.
尽管斯内普很恶劣，但这确实激发了雷穆斯多年未曾真正感受的东西。顽皮。

“Severus,” he smiled, warmly, “And I was surprised to hear you survived the trials. When so many of your friends did not.”
“西弗勒斯，”他温暖地微笑，“我也很惊讶你活过了考验。当许多你的朋友却没有。”

Snape sneered, and that set the tone for the year.
斯内普冷笑，这为整年定下了基调。

Severus had clearly not forgotten the events of their fifth year. He was as despicable as Remus remembered him, and had not aged well. His hair still hung lank and greasy, perhaps a little further back than before, his black eyes were more sunken, and his nose more beak-like. He made Remus’s skin crawl, but there was nothing to be done about it; they had to meet privately each month for the potion.
西弗勒斯显然没有忘记他们第五年的事件。他仍然像雷穆斯记忆中的那样卑鄙，且没有变得更好。他的头发仍然油腻地垂着，也许比以前后退了一些，他的黑眼睛更深陷，鼻子更像鸟喙。他让雷穆斯的皮肤发麻，但无可奈何；他们每个月都必须私下见面以便调制药水。

The potion itself was utterly vile, and Remus resented it bitterly. It tasted awful, but worse than that was the effect it had.
药水本身极其恶心，雷穆斯对此感到极度愤恨。它的味道很糟糕，但更糟糕的是它的效果。

He still transformed, still suffered the agonies as his skull elongated and his back split open and his tendons creaked - but he fully retained his human mind afterwards. This was utterly horrible. Remus had come to see the monthly retreat into his animal brain as something of a catharsis. But having an animal body and human thoughts turned out to be very unpleasant indeed; he felt neither here nor there, trapped in the wrong form and unable to escape. He curled up to sleep locked inside his office every month full of self-loathing.
他仍然变形，仍然承受着骨骼延长、背部裂开和肌腱吱嘎作响的痛苦——但之后他完全保留了自己的人的思想。这实在是可怕的。雷穆斯已经将每月的动物脑退隐视为一种宣泄。但拥有一个动物的身体和人的思想证明确实非常不愉快；他感到既不在这里也不在那里，被困在错误的形态中，无法逃脱。他每个月都在充满自我厌恶的办公室里蜷缩着睡觉。

In the mornings after he would limp to Madam Pomfrey’s office to ask for murtlap essence. Of everyone from Remus’s childhood, Madam Pomfrey seemed the most pleased to see him again. She had aged, like everyone else, but had retained her gentle touch, her sweet face and her no-nonsense attitude to Remus’s wellbeing.
早晨过后，他会跛脚地去找庞弗雷夫人的办公室，请求海星精华。在雷穆斯的童年中，庞弗雷夫人似乎是最高兴再次见到他的人。她像其他人一样衰老了，但保留了她温柔的触感、甜美的脸庞和对雷穆斯健康的严肃态度。

“Remus!” She reached up to hug him the very first moment she saw him. “Just look at you, you giant of a man!”
“雷穆斯！”她在看到他的一刻就伸手抱住了他。“瞧你，真是个巨人！”

“Hello, Madam-- er… Poppy.”
“您好，夫人——呃……波比。”

“As polite as ever,” she smiled, “Come on, come and tell me what you’ve been doing with yourself.”
“仍然那么有礼貌，”她微笑着，“来吧，告诉我你最近在做什么。”

They had a few very pleasant catch ups in her office, by the fireplace. She wanted to know everything about his transformations since Hogwarts, and he told her as much as he could. She was very interested to hear about the pack, and how they were able to heal each other by sharing group magic.
他们在她办公室的壁炉旁有几次非常愉快的交谈。她想了解自霍格沃茨以来他变形的所有情况，他尽可能多地告诉了她。她对听到关于狼群的事情非常感兴趣，如何通过共享群体魔法互相治愈。

“I tried to get in touch with you, after the Potters died.” She said, sadly, “But no one could tell me where you were living, and I didn’t dare ask too much in case…”
“在波特夫妇去世后，我试图与你取得联系。”她悲伤地说道，“但没人能告诉我你住在哪里，我也不敢问太多，以免……”

Remus looked away, embarrassed. “I’m sorry.” He said, “I wanted to be left alone.”
雷穆斯转过脸去，感到尴尬。“对不起。”他说，“我想被独自留在一旁。”

“Yes, well you were the same as a boy, stubborn!” she smiled fondly. He smiled back, realising how much he had missed her.
“是的，你小时候也是一样的，固执！”她亲切地微笑。他回以微笑，意识到自己有多么想念她。

For the first month or so, Remus’s nerves were raw, he hesitated as he turned every corner, worried that he might see something painful. But, as pain often does, this lessened over time.
在最初的一个月左右，雷穆斯的神经非常紧绷，他每转过一个角落都会犹豫，担心自己可能会看到痛苦的事物。但正如痛苦常常会逐渐减轻一样，这种感觉随着时间的推移减轻了。

He slipped into a new character - not the teenage Remus who took risks without thinking, who was desperate to prove himself, and not the half muggle, half broken man he had been in London. Somewhere between these warring halves, he became Professor Lupin; restrained and serious, offering encouragement wherever he could.
他逐渐融入了一个新的角色——不是那个不顾一切冒险的少年雷穆斯，不是那个在伦敦时半巫师半破碎的男人。在这两个对立的自我之间，他成为了卢平教授；克制而严肃，尽可能提供鼓励。

And this was all just as well, because that was exactly who he needed to be, for Harry.
这正是最好的，因为他需要成为的正是这样的人，为哈利。

God, Harry.
天哪，哈利。

Harry Potter was James and Lily seamlessly combined; all charm and cheek and strength and goodness. Remus had been worried - knowing that the kid’s childhood had been far from ideal - that Harry would be difficult. Remus well remembered his own spiky temperament at thirteen; cruel adults make bitter children. But no. Harry was as kind-hearted and open minded as his parents - full of love and so, so generous with it. Getting to know him had been painful and joyful all at once.
哈利·波特是詹姆斯和莉莉无缝结合的产物；充满魅力、无畏、力量和善良。雷穆斯曾担心——知道那个孩子的童年远非理想——哈利会很难相处。雷穆斯清楚地记得自己十三岁的脾气；残酷的成年人会让孩子变得苦涩。但不。哈利和他的父母一样，心地善良、开明——充满爱，并且如此慷慨。了解他既痛苦又充满喜悦。

The first time they met, Remus had thought he was still dreaming. He woke up on the train, clawed awake by dementors - those fucking abominations. He cleared the threat, and staring around at the faces of the frightened kids, found Harry, passed out on the floor. Until he opened his eyes he was James; nothing could convince Remus otherwise. A bit skinnier, maybe shorter than Prongs had been at thirteen, but otherwise the spitting image.
他们第一次见面时，雷穆斯曾以为自己还在做梦。他在火车上醒来，被摄魂怪唤醒——那些该死的畸形怪物。他解决了威胁，环顾四周看着那些惊恐的孩子们，发现哈利晕倒在地板上。直到他睁开眼睛，他还是詹姆斯；没有什么能说服雷穆斯这点。也许比詹姆斯在十三岁时更瘦一点，可能也矮一些，但其他方面完全一样。

Of course, Harry had no idea who Remus was, and for as long as possible, it stayed that way. How would he explain? Even after a few conversations with the boy, Remus was completely at sea. So he let Harry lead the way, and answered the questions which had suitable answers. When Harry came to him asking for patronus lessons so that he could keep playing quidditch, Remus couldn’t say no. It was exactly what James would do, too.
当然，哈利不知道雷穆斯是谁，并且尽可能地保持了这种状态。他怎么解释？即使在与这个男孩交谈了几次之后，雷穆斯也完全迷茫了。所以他让哈利主导，回答那些有适当答案的问题。当哈利找他请教护神咒的课程，以便他可以继续打魁地奇时，雷穆斯无法拒绝。这正是詹姆斯会做的事。

And when Sirius came up, he sidestepped it. Harry already knew that Black and James had been friends, and Remus wasn’t sure what more he could say without losing the kid’s trust. “Yes, Harry, your dad was my best friend, but Sirius Black was my everything…”
当提到小天狼星时，他绕开了这个话题。哈利已经知道布莱克和詹姆斯是朋友，而雷穆斯不确定他还能说什么而不会失去孩子的信任。“是的，哈利，你的爸爸是我最好的朋友，但小天狼星·布莱克是我的一切……”

No, it wouldn’t do. What was more, Remus wasn’t sure whether the wizarding world had its own version of Section 28 - if he started confessing to stuff like that, could he get in trouble for corrupting young minds? It was bad enough he was a werewolf.
不，这样不行。而且，雷穆斯也不确定魔法界是否有类似于第28条的规定——如果他开始承认这些事情，会不会因为腐蚀年轻人的思想而惹上麻烦？他已经是狼人了，已经够糟糕了。

By that time it was already clear that Sirius was nearby. When the convict broke into the castle on Halloween night, Remus almost walked straight off the grounds and apparated back to London. Maybe he would have, if the perimeter wasn’t swarming with dementors - and of course the fact that Black was definitely after Harry.
那时已经很明显，小天狼星就在附近。当那个罪犯在万圣节之夜闯入城堡时，雷穆斯差点直接离开校园，瞬间移动回伦敦。如果周边没有被摄魂怪包围的话，也许他会这样做——当然还有布莱克显然是盯上了哈利的事实。

That made Remus furious; hadn’t Sirius done enough damage? He must have really lost his mind, he must have strayed so far from the young man who had cradled baby Harry in his arms with tenderness and awe. Remus used this as a reminder, to steel himself: it was no use mourning Sirius. His Sirius had died many years ago.
这让雷穆斯非常愤怒；小天狼星难道没有造成足够的伤害吗？他一定是彻底疯了，一定已经远离了那个曾经满怀温柔和敬畏地抱着婴儿哈利的年轻人。雷穆斯把这当作一种提醒，来激励自己：悼念小天狼星是没有用的。他的小天狼星已经死了很多年。

And then that night happened. In a matter of hours everything changed...
然后那一夜发生了。一夜之间一切都发生了改变……

 

Fuck.
该死。

Maybe Grant was right, maybe it was shock. After being given his marching orders from Hogwarts (thank god; another year might have killed him), Remus took the Knight Bus back to London, his mind churning over everything he had learnt.
也许格兰特说得对，也许是震惊。在被霍格沃茨解雇后（谢天谢地；再待一年可能会杀了他），雷穆斯乘坐骑士巴士回到伦敦，他的脑海里不断回想着自己学到的一切。

Events kept shifting and re-ordering themselves. Some things became clearer, others muddied by various versions of the truth. The things Sirius had said, the excuses Wormtail had snivelled, and everything Remus had thought he’d known - none of these accounts lined up quite right.
事情不断地变化和重新排列。一些事情变得更清晰了，另一些则被各种版本的真相弄得混乱不堪。小天狼星说的话，咕噜的借口，以及雷穆斯认为自己知道的一切——这些说法都不完全对。

The only thing Remus was certain of, was that for twelve years he had hated the wrong person.
雷穆斯唯一确定的是，十二年来他憎恨的是错的人。

“Please come back,” he wailed down the phone to Grant, once he was home. “Please, please…”
“请回来，”他在家后对格兰特哭诉道，“拜托，拜托……”

“On my way.” Grant said, and hung up immediately.
“马上就来。”格兰特说，然后立即挂断了电话。

It still took hours. Remus changed into his muggle clothes, throwing Professor Lupin’s shabby robes in a corner of the bathroom, and paced the flat while he waited, cursing the slowness of muggle transport. He didn’t drink. He wanted a clear head; he wanted to understand.
这还是花了几个小时。雷穆斯换上了麻瓜的衣服，把卢平教授那件破旧的长袍扔在浴室的一个角落里，来回踱步，诅咒麻瓜交通的缓慢。他没有喝酒。他想要清醒的头脑；他想要理解。

“Remus?!” Grant burst into the living room, tired and dishevelled. He’d had a hair cut in the past year; it was so short it barely curled any more. Remus hated it, but said nothing, just ran to hug him. “What happened?” Grant asked, huffing as Remus knocked the air out of him, but squeezing him back reassuringly.
“雷穆斯？！”格兰特闯入客厅，疲惫不堪。他在过去一年里剪了头发；现在的头发短到几乎没有卷曲。雷穆斯讨厌这个发型，但没有说什么，只是跑去抱他。“发生了什么事？”格兰特问道，喘着气，被雷穆斯抱得没法呼吸，但还是安慰地回抱了他。

He didn’t look the same, but he smelled the same, and that helped; that was very grounding.
他看起来不一样了，但他闻起来一样，这让人感到安慰；这很有安定感。

“He was innocent!” Remus babbled, still clinging on, “It was Peter all along! It was never him! I was such an idiot!”
“他是无辜的！”雷穆斯喋喋不休地说，仍然紧紧抱着，“一直是彼得！从来不是他！我真是个傻瓜！”

“Remus, I don’t know what you’re talking about, please… let’s sit down, shall we? Christ, you’re skinny, don’t they feed you at that school?!”
“雷穆斯，我不知道你在说什么，拜托……我们坐下来谈谈，好吗？天哪，你真瘦，他们在那所学校不喂你吗？！”

Remus allowed Grant to take over. He sat obediently on the couch, accepted a glass of water, and a cigarette, because apparently Grant was smoking again, and the temptation was too much. The flat felt bare and stuffy, having sat empty for most of the year, and Grant opened the living room window, letting in the everyday sounds of foot traffic and pigeons.
雷穆斯让格兰特接管。他乖乖地坐在沙发上，接过一杯水和一支香烟，因为显然格兰特又开始抽烟了，这让他很难抗拒。公寓感觉空荡荡的，闷热不堪，已经空置了大部分时间，格兰特打开了客厅的窗户，让街上的行人声和鸽子的声音进来。

“Ok,” Grant said, sitting opposite Remus, clasping his hands together in a very teacher-ly sort of way, “Let’s start at the beginning, shall we?”
“好吧，”格兰特说，坐在雷穆斯对面，用一种非常老师般的方式双手交叉，“我们从头开始，好吗？”

Remus nodded. He was determined to speak. If anyone could sort all of this out, it was Grant. He was sure of that. “Sirius.” He said. “I saw Sirius. And Peter.”
雷穆斯点了点头。他决心要说出来。如果有人能理清这一切，那就是格兰特。他对此很有信心。“小天狼星。”他说，“我见过小天狼星。还有彼得。”

“Wait,” Grant frowned, “Peter? I thought he…”
“等等，”格兰特皱起眉头，“彼得？我以为他……”

“No.” Remus said, darkly, his insides turning hot with rage, “He’s alive. He’s been hiding, all these years.”
“不是。”雷穆斯阴沉地说，内心充满愤怒，“他还活着。他这些年一直在躲藏。”

“From Sirius?”
“从小天狼星那里？”

“From everyone. He did it. He betrayed James and Lily; it was never Sirius.”
“从所有人那里。他做了这件事。他背叛了詹姆斯和莉莉；从来不是小天狼星。”

“How... “ Grant shook his head, clearly confused, “So he was in prison all this time for something Peter did? Jesus. Ok. You’re sure? He’s the one who told you?”
“怎么……“格兰特摇了摇头，显然很困惑，“所以他一直因为彼得做的事情而入狱？天哪。好的。你确定吗？是他告诉你的？”

“Yes, but I… I know for sure. I saw Peter, and I…” Remus faltered. “I just believe Sirius, ok?”
“是的，但我……我确定。我见过彼得，而且我……”雷穆斯犹豫了。“我只是相信小天狼星，好吗？”

The fact was that he had read Sirius’s mind, and he was still trying to get his head around that. He tried to piece the events of the night together, for Grant’s benefit and his own. “It was all Harry - James’s son. He left the school one night, and I knew why, so I followed him - I was worried Sirius would try to… but then Peter was there, I saw Peter, and I didn’t know what to think.”
事实上，他读取了小天狼星的思想，他仍在试图理清这一点。他试图将那晚的事件拼凑起来，为了格兰特的利益，也为了他自己。“一切都是哈利——詹姆斯的儿子。他某晚离开了学校，我知道原因，所以我跟着他——我担心小天狼星会尝试……但然后彼得在那里，我见到了彼得，我不知道该怎么想。”

Something deep inside him had known at once; the second he saw Wormtail’s name appear on the map. But he’d had to find out, had to know for sure. And then he’d got to the shack, and there was Sirius, skin and bones and rags and madness, cackling on the floor, Harry standing over him, poised with his wand.
他内心深处立即知道了；当他在地图上看到咕噜的名字出现的那一刻。但是他必须查明，必须确认。然后他到达了小屋，那里是小天狼星，骨瘦如柴，破布包裹着，疯狂地在地板上咯咯笑，哈利站在他身上，手握魔杖。

The wolf part of Remus took over, recognising that Padfoot was in danger, and he disarmed everyone at once. “Where is he, Sirius?!”
雷穆斯的狼性占了上风，意识到小天狼星处于危险中，他立刻解除所有人的武装。“他在哪里，小天狼星？！”

Then he saw the rat, and it all fell into place. His mind went rushing back to 1981; all the secrecy, the mistrust, the lies. He looked at Sirius properly, he widened his eyes, and - almost without trying - he entered Sirius’s thoughts. Show me he commanded, using the same magic the werewolves used - Sirius’s brain was half-canine by that point, and maybe that’s why it worked. Black resisted for a moment, no doubt recalling Walpurga’s forced intrusions, but he nodded, and he let Remus in.
然后他看到了那只老鼠，一切都理顺了。他的思绪迅速回到了1981年；所有的秘密，所有的不信任，所有的谎言。他仔细看着小天狼星，睁大了眼睛，几乎不费吹灰之力地进入了小天狼星的思想。展示给我，他命令道，使用了狼人使用的魔法——到那时，小天狼星的大脑已经半是犬类的，也许这就是为什么有效的原因。布莱克抵抗了一下，无疑回忆起了沃尔普尔加的强行侵入，但他点了点头，让雷穆斯进入了他的思维。

“But Padfoot,” James’s voice, echoing from a distant past, “I thought we were agreed?”
“但小天狼星，”詹姆斯的声音，从遥远的过去回响，“我以为我们达成了协议？”

“I know, but this is better, can’t you see?! No one will ever suspect Wormy!”
“我知道，但这更好，不是吗？没有人会怀疑咕噜！”

“Like a double bluff!” Lily chimed in. “It’s brilliant!”
“就像双重虚张声势！”莉莉插话道。“太棒了！”

Remus didn’t need to hear any more. He lowered the wands, and helped Sirius up, and embraced him tightly. I’m sorry, he communicated wordlessly, I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I’m sorry…
雷穆斯不需要再听更多。他放下了魔杖，扶起小天狼星，紧紧拥抱他。他无声地传达着对不起，对不起，对不起，对不起……

Back in the flat, tears pricked in Remus’s eyes, and Grant pulled out a hanky, handing it to him. “So is he free, now? Sirius?”
回到公寓，雷穆斯的眼睛里涌出了泪水，格兰特拿出一块手帕递给他。“那么他现在自由了吗？小天狼星？”

“No,” Remus shook his head, collecting himself, “It all got so complicated, and I… it was a full moon. I only saw him for twenty minutes, maybe, and then I turned, and… so much happened without me. Peter ran away, they didn’t catch him. I should have killed him when I had the chance! I wanted to, I was going to, but Harry stopped me.”
“不，”雷穆斯摇了摇头，整理自己，“一切变得如此复杂，而我……那时是满月。我只见到他二十分钟，也许，然后我变身了……很多事发生在我身上。他跑了，他们没有抓到他。我应该在有机会时杀了他！我想的，我打算的，但哈利阻止了我。”

Grant paled, his mouth a grim line. He didn’t say anything, though.
格兰特脸色苍白，嘴巴紧绷。他没有说话。

“By the time it was morning, Sirius had escaped again too.” Remus continued. “He’s in hiding, and I don’t know…” I don’t know if I’ll ever see him again.
“到早晨时，小天狼星也再次逃脱了。”雷穆斯继续说道。“他在躲藏，我不知道……”我不知道我是否还能再见到他。

He wiped his eyes, and ran his fingers through his hair. “Fuck! All this time! All this time and I believed it! How could I have been so stupid?!”
他擦了擦眼睛，手指穿过头发。“该死！这么长时间！这么长时间我都相信了！我怎么会这么愚蠢？！”

“Hey, stop it.” Grant frowned, reaching out. Remus stood up abruptly, ignoring Grant and pacing the room once more, muttering to himself,
“喂，别这样。”格兰特皱起眉头，伸手去抓他。雷穆斯突然站起身，忽视了格兰特，再次在房间里踱步，自言自语，

“I should have known he would never hurt James! I shouldn’t have been so bloody gullible! So weak! I should have tried to see him, I could have got him out of there, I could have tracked down Peter, I could have…”
“我应该知道他不会伤害詹姆斯的！我不应该这么愚蠢！这么软弱！我应该尝试去见他，我本可以把他从那里救出来，我本可以追踪彼得，我本可以……”

“Remus!” Grant raised his voice, “Stop it.”
“雷穆斯！”格兰特提高了声音，“停下。”

Remus looked at him. “I don’t know what to do.” He said.
雷穆斯看着他。“我不知道该怎么办。”他说。

Grant sighed. “Me neither, mate.” He rubbed a hand over his face, and Remus saw the rings under his eyes. Grant stood up. “But there’s nothing you can do right this second, so. I’m going to have a shower, right? Then we’ll get dinner. Then we’ll talk a bit more.”
格兰特叹了口气。“我也不知道，伙计。”他用手擦了擦脸，雷穆斯看到了他眼下的黑眼圈。格兰特站起来。“但现在你不能做什么。所以。我去洗个澡，好吗？然后我们去吃晚饭。然后我们再聊聊。”

Remus nodded, eagerly. Yes, this was what he needed; a plan. Clear, defined next steps. Grant left the room, wearily. Remus waited, listening to the water running, trying once again to get his thoughts in order. He did something he hadn’t done since he was a teenager. He made a list.
雷穆斯急切地点了点头。是的，这正是他需要的；一个计划。明确的下一步。格兰特疲惫地离开了房间。雷穆斯等待着，听着水声，再次尝试理清思绪。他做了一件自从青少年时期以来就没做过的事。他列了一个清单。

So, Moony, he said to himself, what are the facts?
那么，月亮狼，他对自己说，事实是什么？

Sirius Black did not murder James and Lily Potter.
小天狼星布莱克没有谋杀詹姆斯和莉莉·波特。

Peter Pettigrew was alive.
彼得·佩提格鲁还活着。

Peter Pettigrew had been a spy.
彼得·佩提格鲁曾是间谍。

Peter Pettigrew murdered James and Lily Potter.
彼得·佩提格鲁谋杀了詹姆斯和莉莉·波特。

Sirius Black had been in prison for twelve years for a crime he was innocent of.
小天狼星布莱克因一项他无罪的罪行而入狱十二年。

A surge of anger washed over him once more. He had believed it! He was as guilty as Dumbledore, as anyone else who had simply assumed Sirius was the spy, because Sirius was a Black. In fact, Remus was even more at fault, because he ought to have known! No one was closer to Sirius than he was.
一阵愤怒再次涌上心头。他曾经相信过这一点！他和邓布利多一样有罪，与其他任何简单认为小天狼星是间谍的人一样，因为小天狼星是布莱克家族的人。实际上，雷穆斯的罪责更大，因为他本该知道！没有人比他更接近小天狼星了。

Those last few months of the war were such a blur. Hadn’t there been something wrong? Hadn’t Sirius been distant, cold with him? In the years since, Remus had taken that as proof of Padfoot’s betrayal, but now… now with a sick feeling, he saw it for what it was.
战争的最后几个月真是一片模糊。难道没有什么不对劲吗？难道小天狼星对他不是冷漠而且疏远吗？这些年来，雷穆斯把这当作小天狼星背叛的证据，但现在……现在他带着恶心的感觉看清了事情的真相。

“He thought I was the spy!” He said to Grant, the second he was out of the bathroom.
“他以为我是间谍！”他对格兰特说，当他刚走出浴室时。

“Eh?” Grant frowned, trying to get past Remus, wrapped in a towel. “Spy? What? Oi, let me get dressed, come on…”
“嗯？”格兰特皱起眉头，试图绕过裹着毛巾的雷穆斯。“间谍？什么？喂，让我穿好衣服，快点……”

Remus followed him into the bedroom and sat on the bed, talking fast as Grant dried himself and put on clean clothes.
雷穆斯跟着他进了卧室，坐在床上，格兰特擦干身体、换上干净的衣服时快速地讲述着。

“During the war, we knew there was a spy, we knew someone was passing information to the other side, but no one knew who. Afterwards, we thought it was Sirius - it all made sense, he was caught blowing up a street full of muggles, and--”
“在战争期间，我们知道有个间谍，我们知道有人在向对方传递情报，但没有人知道是谁。之后，我们认为是小天狼星——一切都有了解释，他被抓到炸毁了一条满是麻瓜的街道，和——”

“Do you have to call normal people that?”
“你必须这样称呼普通人吗？”

“Sorry. Anyway - Sirius was the secret keeper for James and Lily - err… that means he had this spell on him, so only he knew where they were. To keep them safe. But he switched with Peter, at the last minute, and now we know that Peter was the spy. And they didn’t tell me about the switch, Sirius didn’t tell me, because he must have thought…”
“对不起。无论如何——小天狼星是詹姆斯和莉莉的秘密守护者——呃……这意味着他身上有一个魔咒，只有他知道他们在哪里。为了保护他们。但他在最后时刻和彼得交换了位置，现在我们知道彼得是间谍。他们没有告诉我这个交换，小天狼星没有告诉我，因为他肯定认为……”

“He didn't trust you.” Grant said, bluntly. Dressed, he sat down on the bed too, at a distance from Remus.
“他不信任你。”格兰特直言不讳地说。穿好衣服后，他也坐在床上，和雷穆斯保持距离。

“I suppose I can’t blame him…”
“我想我不能怪他……”

“Had you broken his trust before?” Grant raised an eyebrow.
“你以前破坏过他的信任吗？”格兰特挑了挑眉。

“...No.”
“……没有。”

“Did you think he was the spy? Before James and Lily died?”
“在詹姆斯和莉莉死之前，你认为他是间谍吗？”

“No, never!”
“不，从来没有！”

“Well then.” Grant stood up. “I’m going to nip to the shop - we need milk and bread… toothpaste…”
“那好吧。”格兰特站起身。“我要去商店——我们需要牛奶和面包……牙膏……”

“Wait, no, what do you mean ‘well then’?!”
“等等，你什么意思‘那好吧’？！”

“Nothing. Look, come on, come to the shop with me. Then I promise we can talk about it. I’ll listen to you all night long if you want, I swear. I just want to get some food in you first.”
“没什么。听着，来吧，跟我去商店。然后我保证我们可以再聊。我会听你讲整晚，如果你愿意的话，我发誓。我只是想先让你吃点东西。”

Remus went along with that. He watched Grant cook, and he swallowed every mouthful, and then he talked and he talked and he talked. But it was no good. It came to nothing in the end.
雷穆斯同意了。他看着格兰特做饭，吞下了每一口，然后他讲述个不停。但结果并不好。最后什么也没有改变。

“If Sirius is in hiding, and Peter’s on the run…” Grant said, yawning.
“如果小天狼星在躲藏，彼得在逃亡……”格兰特打了个哈欠。

“He’ll go straight to Voldemort, the rat.” Remus growled.
“他会直接去找伏地魔，那只老鼠。”雷穆斯低声咆哮。

“Right, ok,” Grant waved a hand, “If Sirius is in hiding, then you can’t do anything. It sounds like it’s out of your hands.”
“对，好吧，”格兰特挥了挥手，“如果小天狼星在躲藏，那么你什么也做不了。听起来这已经超出了你的能力范围。”

“Maybe I could send an owl… only that might give away his location…”
“也许我可以发一只猫头鹰……不过那可能会暴露他的藏身之处……”

“And then you’ll get arrested and sent to Alcatraz, or whatever it is, for colluding with a criminal.” Grant said, with an air of finality.
“然后你会被逮捕，送到阿尔卡特拉兹，或者其他什么地方，因为你与罪犯勾结。”格兰特带着一种最终的语气说。

“I just want to help him.” Remus said.
“我只是想帮他。”雷穆斯说。

“Of course you do. But I don’t see how.”
“当然了。但我看不到办法。”

They sat in silence for a while, thinking. It was dark outside, Remus didn’t know what time it was, but it had to be pretty late. Grant looked exhausted, and Remus felt a small twinge of guilt, on top of everything else.
他们沉默地坐了一会儿，思考着。外面已经黑了，雷穆斯不知道现在是什么时间，但一定很晚了。格兰特看起来很疲惫，雷穆斯在所有其他感受之上还感到一丝内疚。

“Sorry to put you through this.” He said, quietly, reaching for Grant’s hand. “It’s not really fair of me.”
“对不起让你经历这些。”他说，轻声说道，伸手去握格兰特的手。“我这样做对你不公平。”

“It’s fine,” Grant gave him a small smile, stroking Remus’s knuckles with his thumb, “I do understand. It’s just… a lot.”
“没关系，”格兰特给了他一个小小的微笑，用拇指抚摸雷穆斯的指关节，“我理解。这只是……太多了。”

“I know.”
“我知道。”

“How… how was it, seeing him? I mean, how did it make you feel?”
“你见到他时感觉如何？我的意思是，那让你感觉怎么样？”

Remus shifted, awkwardly. There it was. The thought he’d been avoiding. Because if Sirius was innocent, if he’d never betrayed James, then he’d never betrayed Remus, either. And Remus didn’t know what that meant to him, now, after so much time.
雷穆斯尴尬地移动了一下。那里就是了。那是他一直在回避的想法。因为如果小天狼星是无辜的，如果他从未背叛过詹姆斯，那么他也从未背叛过雷穆斯。而雷穆斯不知道这对他意味着什么，现在，经过这么长时间。

“We’re both so different, now.” He said, aware Grant was holding his breath while he waited for the response. “I barely recognised him, really, I just felt sorry for him.” The flutter in his stomach told him he was lying.
“我们现在都变得如此不同。”他说，意识到格兰特在等待回应时屏住了呼吸。“我几乎认不出他了，我只是为他感到遗憾。”他胃中的悸动告诉他他在撒谎。

Grant leaned over and kissed him. “Everything will be all right, in the end.” He said.
格兰特俯身吻了他。“一切都会好的。”他说。

 

Chapter 185: Early Summer 1995We passed upon the stair

We spoke of was and when

Although I wasn't there

He said I was his friend

Which came as some surprise

I spoke into his eyes;

I thought you died alone

A long long time ago.

 

Saturday 24th June 1995

That fucking phoenix arrived, first, and Remus knew at once.

“What the bloody hell is that?!” Grant leapt up, startled by the silvery bird which burst into their living room. They’d been watching telly, with all the windows open to counteract the summer heat. Remus had just been about to put the kettle on.
“这到底是什么鬼东西？！”格兰特吓得跳了起来，看到一只银色的鸟闯进了他们的客厅。他们一直在看电视，所有的窗户都开着，以抵消夏天的热量。雷穆斯刚准备去烧水壶。

The bird sat on top of their boxy little TV and opened its beak, speaking in Dumbledore’s voice;
那只鸟停在他们那台方方正正的小电视上，张开了嘴，用邓布利多的声音说：

“Padfoot is on his way.”
“天狼星正在路上。”

Remus nearly dropped the empty mugs he was holding.
雷穆斯差点儿掉了手里的空杯子。

“Fuck.”
“该死。”

“What?” Grant said, watching the bird vanish into thin air. “Who’s Padfoot?”
“什么？”格兰特问，看到那只鸟消失在空气中。“谁是天狼星？”

“Fuck.” Remus said again, setting down the mugs. He had begun to shake uncontrollably. He felt cold all over. “I don’t think I can. I don’t think I can…” he mumbled to himself, covering his mouth.
“该死。”雷穆斯再次说着，把杯子放下。他开始 uncontrollably地颤抖，全身感到冰冷。“我不觉得我能做到。我不觉得我能……”他自言自语地说，捂住了自己的嘴巴。

“Remus?” Grant stood up and touched his shoulder. “You’re scaring me.”
“雷穆斯？”格兰特站起身，触摸他的肩膀。“你吓到我了。”

“Sirius.” He spluttered. “Sirius is Padfoot.”
“小天狼星。”他结结巴巴地说。“小天狼星是天狼星。”

“Bloody hell. The murderer?”
“天哪。那个杀人犯？”

“Not a murderer, I told you.”
“不是杀人犯，我告诉过你。”

“Right, right, sorry. Coming here ?!”
“对，对，抱歉。要来这里？！”

“It’s his flat, after all.”
“毕竟这是他的公寓。”

“Oh, I forgot.” Grant said, flatly. He bit his lip, “Should I... go?”
“哦，我忘了。”格兰特平淡地说。他咬了咬嘴唇，“我应该……离开吗？”

“No!” Remus clung to Grant, suddenly, “No, please, please don’t. I can’t be alone, don’t leave me alone with--”
“不要！”雷穆斯突然抓住格兰特，“不，请，不要。我不能一个人，别让我一个人和——”

“Ok, ok!” Grant soothed him, hugging him back, “Calm down, all right? I won’t go anywhere if you don’t want. Just… just try to get yourself together.”
“好，好！”格兰特安抚他说，回抱住他，“冷静下来，好吗？如果你不想，我不会离开的。只是……尽量让自己振作起来。”

“I’m sorry.” Remus took a deep breath.
“对不起。”雷穆斯深吸了一口气。

He knew he was acting childishly. This was no time to fall apart. He’d had years and years of that. If Dumbledore was sending Sirius to him, then something had happened. Something important. Now was the time for strength and action. He gazed around blindly for something to do.
他知道自己表现得很幼稚。现在不是崩溃的时候。他已经经历了多年的痛苦。如果邓布利多派小天狼星来找他，那么一定发生了什么事。重要的事。现在是需要力量和行动的时候。他盲目地环顾四周，寻找能做的事情。

“This place is a mess! I should start cleaning. He won’t be long.”
“这个地方一团糟！我应该开始打扫。他不会太久的。”

Grant was helpless to do anything but watch as Remus ran around the flat like a headless chicken, using every cleaning charm he could remember, combined with some actual manual labour when he mucked up the spells. He couldn’t stop moving, he couldn’t bear to sit still for a moment, because then he might have to think.
格兰特无能为力，只能看着雷穆斯在公寓里像无头苍蝇一样跑来跑去，使用他能记得的每一个清洁魔咒，并在咒语失败时进行一些实际的体力劳动。他无法停止移动，无法忍受片刻的静止，因为那样他可能不得不思考。

Within the hour, there was a scratching noise at the door, and a low, gruff bark. Remus froze. A scent he had not known in many years reared something in his subconscious.
一个小时内，门口传来抓挠声和低沉粗哑的吠声。雷穆斯僵住了。他多年来未曾闻过的气味在他的潜意识中唤起了一些东西。

“Was that a dog?” Grant said, nervously, from the kitchen. “You know I hate dogs…”
“那是一只狗吗？”格兰特在厨房里紧张地问。“你知道我讨厌狗……”

“It’s him.” Remus breathed. He walked shakily to the door, and pulled it open. There was Padfoot - scrawny, mangy, fur slightly greying in places. But it was him.
“是他。”雷穆斯喘息着说。他颤颤巍巍地走到门前，拉开了门。那是天狼星——瘦弱、满身脏毛，毛发有些地方变灰了。但那是他。

“Come in,” Remus said, hoarsely.
“进来，”雷穆斯沙哑地说。

The dog huffed, bobbing its head, and entered. Remus clicked the door shut, and leaned against it, watching as Sirius transformed back into himself.
那只狗喘了口气，点了点头，然后进去了。雷穆斯关上门，靠在门上，看着小天狼星变回了他自己。

Scrawny, mangy; greying in places. His eyes, those dark blue eyes that had broken Remus’s heart a thousand times as a teenager, had turned dull gunmetal grey. He was a bag of bones, unsettled all over. It was to be expected.
瘦弱、满身脏毛；毛发有些地方变灰了。他的眼睛，那些在青少年时期让雷穆斯心碎的深蓝色眼睛，已经变成了暗淡的铅灰色。他瘦骨嶙峋，全身不安。这是可以预料的。

“I’ve come straight from Hogwarts.” He said. His voice was as hard and rasping as it had been last summer.
“我刚从霍格沃茨过来。”他说。他的声音像去年夏天一样坚硬和沙哑。

“Yes,” Remus said, rubbing the back of his head. “Dumbledore sent a message ahead.”
“是的，”雷穆斯说，搓了搓自己的后脑勺。“邓布利多提前发了消息。”

Sirius twitched, slightly, and nodded. “Something happened at the tournament. Harry was kidnapped.”
小天狼星稍微有些颤动，点了点头。“比赛中发生了什么事。哈利被绑架了。”

“What?! Is he--”
“什么？！他——”

“He came back, he’s fine - fine as can be expected. Voldemort’s back, too.”
“他回来了，他没事——能有的也就是那样的没事。伏地魔也回来了。”

“What?!”
“什么？！”

“It’s true. Harry faced him.”
“是真的。哈利面对了他。”

“No.” Remus felt sick.
“不。”雷穆斯感到恶心。

“The Order’s reforming. Dumbledore told me to come here, lie low.”
“凤凰社正在重组。邓布利多让我来这里，藏身。”

“Right.” Remus nodded, still taking in the shock.
“对。”雷穆斯点点头，仍在消化震惊。

“If that's…” Sirius’s face softened, he looked younger - more like the real Sirius, “If you don’t mind? I just followed orders without thinking, but I could go somewhere else if…”
“如果那是……”小天狼星的脸变得柔和，看起来年轻了——更像真正的小天狼星，“如果你不介意的话？我只是没有思考地执行命令，但如果……”

“No!” Remus said, very firmly, snapping out of the confusion that had gripped him ever since Dumbledore’s patronus appeared. He put a hand on Sirius’s shoulder. Oh, he was so thin. “Of course you should stay here, it's your home.”
“不要！”雷穆斯非常坚定地说，摆脱了自从邓布利多的护法出现后一直笼罩在他身上的困惑。他拍了拍小天狼星的肩膀。哦，他瘦得可怜。“当然你应该留在这里，这是你的家。”

Sirius looked so relieved that Remus wanted to pull him close and wrap his arms around him. But he didn't. He looked at Grant, who was watching warily from the kitchen doorway.
小天狼星显得如此放松，以至于雷穆斯想要把他拉近，拥抱住他。但他没有这样做。他看着格兰特，格兰特正从厨房门口警惕地看着他们。

Sirius followed his eye line and gave a start. “You’re here.”
小天狼星顺着他的视线看去，吃了一惊。“你在这里。”

It wasn’t a question; just a statement of fact.
这不是一个问题；只是一个事实陈述。

Grant, god love him, gave his breeziest smile, “Alright, mate? Tell you what, you look like you could do with a Chinese. I’ll pop out, shall I, Remus?”
格兰特，上天保佑他，露出他最轻松的笑容，“怎么样，伙计？跟你说，你看起来需要点中餐。我出去一趟，怎么样，雷穆斯？”

“You don’t have to-”
“你不必……”

“I think I do.” Grant smiled.
“我觉得我必须去。”格兰特笑了。

He grabbed his wallet from the coffee table on his way out. He didn’t kiss Remus on the cheek, as he usually might, but gave him a pat on the shoulder and said, “I’ll be half an hour.” He closed the door softly behind himself.
他在离开时从咖啡桌上拿起了钱包。他没有像往常一样亲吻雷穆斯的脸颊，而是拍了拍他的肩膀，说：“我半小时就回来。”他轻轻地关上了门。

Sirius and Remus stood in silence for what felt like minutes.
小天狼星和雷穆斯沉默地站着，感觉过了几分钟。

Sirius frowned, making deep lines appear in his face.
小天狼星皱起了眉头，脸上出现了深深的皱纹。

“That was rude of me. I didn’t mean to be rude.” He began to scratch the back of his hand, anxiously, his fingernails long and black with grime. Remus felt a sorrowful tug deep in his stomach, and reached out to still him.
“我刚才很无礼。我不是故意的。”他开始焦虑地抓挠手背，指甲长而黑，沾满污垢。雷穆斯感到胃里一阵悲伤的抽搐，伸手去安抚他。

“How about a shower? Then a sit down. Everything's ok.”
“怎么了？先洗个澡，然后坐下来。一切都没问题。”

Sirius looked up at him. Remus had forgotten how much smaller he was.
小天狼星抬头看着他。雷穆斯已经忘记了他曾经多么瘦小。

“Sounds good.” Sirius nodded, weakly.
“听起来不错。”小天狼星虚弱地点了点头。

Remus showed him to the bathroom, which was silly, because obviously he knew where the bathroom was; nothing had changed in thirteen years. While Sirius was washing, Remus went to the bedroom to find some clean clothes.
雷穆斯带他去了浴室，这很傻，因为他显然知道浴室在哪里；十三年来没什么变化。当小天狼星在洗澡时，雷穆斯去卧室找干净的衣服。

He pulled a few shirts out of the dresser - he wanted to give Sirius his things to wear, not Grant’s, but after all this time Remus honestly didn’t know which belonged to who. He settled on an oversized knitted jumper, which was definitely his. It would swamp Sirius, but it would be comfortable. Digging out a pair of tartan pyjama bottoms to go with it, he lay them carefully on the bed.
他从衣柜里拿出几件衬衫——他想给小天狼星他的衣服，而不是格兰特的，但这么久以来雷穆斯实际上不知道哪些是属于谁的。他选择了一件超大的针织毛衣，那肯定是他的。虽然会把小天狼星淹没，但会很舒适。他挖出一条格子睡裤，放在床上。

There was only one bed in the flat - there had only ever been one bed and they had only ever needed one bed. The problem of where to put Sirius was unanswerable. Remus was still staring down at the clothes when he heard the water go off (the boiler stuttered and clunked a few times, he’d been meaning to look at it for ages) and the bathroom door click unlocked.
公寓里只有一张床——一直只有一张床，他们只需要一张床。如何安置小天狼星的问题无解。雷穆斯仍在盯着这些衣物时，听到水声停止（锅炉发出几声咔嗒声，他一直打算查看一下）和浴室门的锁扣声。

“Remus?!” Sirius called out, a note of panic in his voice.
“雷穆斯？！”小天狼星焦急地叫道。

“Bedroom.” Remus replied.
“卧室。”雷穆斯回答道。

Sirius entered, his hair dripping on the carpet. He’d wrapped the biggest bath sheet around himself like a shawl, covering his whole body from neck to skinny ankles. Remus looked away, embarrassed, and gestured at the clothes laid out.
小天狼星走了进来，头发滴落在地毯上。他用最大的浴巾裹住自己，像披肩一样，从脖子到瘦弱的脚踝全都包裹住了。雷穆斯不好意思地转过脸去，示意床上的衣物。

“Here.” He said, “I’ll let you change.”
“这里。”他说，“我让你换衣服。”

He made to leave, but Sirius’s hand darted out and grabbed his arm. He had that wild look in his eye again,
他正要离开，但小天狼星的手猛地伸出抓住了他的胳膊。他眼中又有了那种狂野的神情，

“Don’t go.” He said, “Could you stay in the room?”
“不要走。”他说，“你能留在房间里吗？”

“Ok…” Remus nodded, patting Sirius’s claw-like hand. He’d been scratching it again, it was red raw.
“好的……”雷穆斯点了点头，拍了拍小天狼星像爪子一样的手。他又抓挠了它，现在已经红肿了。

Remus turned and looked at the curtains while Sirius dressed himself. His movements sounded slow, like an old man, or an invalid - not like elegant, energetic Sirius Black. Fury seared through Remus. They took everything from him, he thought, fiercely, everything that made him who he was.
雷穆斯转过身看着窗帘，当小天狼星穿衣服时。他的动作缓慢，像个老人，或无用的人——完全不像优雅、充满活力的小天狼星·布莱克。雷穆斯心中充满了愤怒。他们从他身上夺走了一切，他激烈地想着，一切让他成为他自己的东西。

When he turned around, Sirius was staring at the bed. Remus looked too, trying to see it through Sirius’s eyes. The neatly made bedspread; the matching bedside tables; one with a book on top, the other with a packet of cigarettes.
当他转身时，小天狼星正盯着床。雷穆斯也看了看，试图从小天狼星的视角看它。整齐的床单；配套的床头柜；一个上面有一本书，另一个上面有一包香烟。

“I’ll sleep on the couch.” Sirius said. “I don’t want to muck anything up between you and… and… sorry, his name’s gone.”
“小天狼星说。“我会睡在沙发上。我不想打扰你和……和……抱歉，他的名字忘了。”

“Grant.”
“格兰特。”

“Grant.” Sirius looked away again. His eyes never rested long, he was always searching the corners of the room for something. “I’ve forgotten a lot, I think.”
“格兰特。”小天狼星又一次转过头。他的眼睛从不长时间停留，总是四处搜寻房间的角落。“我觉得我忘了很多。”

“That’s ok.”
“没关系。”

Remus had never felt a pain like this. And Remus had been feeling pain most of his life. “Come and sit down. Cup of tea?”
雷穆斯从未感受过这样的痛苦。雷穆斯一生中大多数时间都在感受痛苦。“来坐下。喝杯茶？”

“Cup of tea.” Sirius parroted back.
“小茶杯。”小天狼星复述道。

Remus nodded, slowly, then led him into the kitchen.
雷穆斯慢慢点了点头，然后带他进了厨房。

“Thank you.” Sirius said, after a little while, “Sorry, I… I keep forgetting things.”
“小天狼星过了一会儿说：“谢谢你。”对不起，我……我一直在忘记东西。”

Remus touched his arm, gently,
雷穆斯轻轻地碰了碰他的胳膊，

“It’s ok. Go and sit. I’ll be a minute, you can hear me from the living room.”
“没关系。去坐着。我会很快的，你可以从客厅听到我。”

Sirius left, silently. Remus breathed a sigh of relief - the atmosphere was still thick with memory, and hurt, and Azkaban, but at least it was bearable when Sirius wasn’t standing right there.
小天狼星静静地离开了。雷穆斯松了一口气——气氛依旧充满记忆、痛苦和阿兹卡班，但至少当小天狼星不站在那儿时，这种感觉是可以忍受的。

Last year, in the shack, Remus hadn’t had time to feel anything other than terror and joy. And, typically, he had spent the rest of his time since trying to pretend none of it had happened at all. Not because he’d wanted to, but because it was the only thing he could do. He should have known better; should have known that Sirius always demanded confrontation.
去年，在那间小屋里，雷穆斯没有时间感受其他任何东西，只有恐惧和喜悦。通常，他在那之后花了剩下的时间试图假装这一切都没有发生。不是因为他想这样做，而是因为这是他能做的唯一事。他应该知道得更好；应该知道小天狼星总是要求面对。

He took a long time over the tea, brewing it in a pot, rather than the electric kettle. How did Sirius take his tea? He couldn’t remember. Maybe he had never known - Sirius usually made it, back then. In the end, Remus simply put out everything, setting up a tray with immaculate attention and care, as if he was serving the queen. Slice of lemon. Little jug of milk. Bowl of brown sugar lumps. There weren’t any biscuits left, Grant had had the last of the digestives.
他花了很长时间泡茶，用茶壶而不是电热水壶。他怎么泡茶，小天狼星的茶喝什么？他记不得了。也许他从未知道——当时通常是小天狼星泡茶。最后，雷穆斯只是把一切都准备好，精心地摆放在托盘上，就像他在为女王服务一样。切片柠檬。小 jug的牛奶。装有红糖块的碗。没有饼干了，格兰特吃了最后的消化饼。

When it was all ready, he still hadn’t the nerve to carry it through. He panicked for a moment, before hearing the door click open. Had it been half an hour already?
一切准备好后，他仍然没有勇气把它端出去。他瞬间感到惊慌，随后听到门被打开了。已经过了半小时了吗？

“‘Orright?!” Grant’s brash, overloud cockney accent filled the flat, warming it instantly. He acted as if there was nothing at all out of the ordinary as he bustled into the living room, laden with food.
“‘Orright?!” 格兰特那粗鲁而响亮的伦敦口音充满了公寓，瞬间让它温暖起来。他像没发生什么特别的事一样，忙乎着把食物带进客厅。

Remus could hear him setting it all out on the coffee table, unwrapping cartons of egg fried rice, sweet and sour chicken, chow mein, pork balls, chinese ribs, spring rolls; all the while chatting away to Sirius,
雷穆斯能听到他把所有食物摆放在咖啡桌上，拆开蛋炒饭、糖醋鸡、炒面、猪肉丸、猪肋骨、春卷的包装；同时和小天狼星聊天，

“Blimey, don’t you look better after a wash, eh? Still got that nice thick hair. Jealous, I’ll be bald by the time I’m forty, reckon. Seen how grey Remus is? Looks distinguished, I tell ‘im, but ‘e don’t listen…”
“哎呀，你洗完澡看起来好多了，哈？头发还那么浓密。我真羡慕，我到四十岁时肯定会秃头的。看看雷穆斯多么灰白？我告诉他看起来很有气质，但他不听……”

Fortified, Remus lifted the tray and carried it into the living room. Sirius was sitting primly on the edge of the couch, staring at Grant the way an animal stares at a potential predator.
感到鼓舞，雷穆斯提起托盘，把它带到客厅。小天狼星端坐在沙发边缘，像动物盯着潜在的掠食者一样盯着格兰特。

“I’ll grab plates…” Grant said, passing Remus on his way back to the kitchen. He didn’t make eye contact. Remus didn’t blame him. The situation wasn’t fair on anyone; least of all Grant.
“我去拿盘子……”格兰特边说边从雷穆斯身边走回厨房。他没有与雷穆斯对视。雷穆斯不怪他。这种情况对任何人都不公平；尤其是对格兰特。

Remus tried to smile at Sirius, offering the tea tray. “Here we are.” He murmured.
雷穆斯尝试对小天狼星微笑，递上茶托盘。“来，这里。”他低声说道。

Sirius looked at the tea, the lemon, the sugar, then down at his hands.
小天狼星看着茶、柠檬、糖，然后看向自己的手。

“Are you hungry?” Remus asked, “Is this all right?”
“你饿吗？”雷穆斯问，“这样还好吗？”

Sirius nodded. “Lovely, thanks. You shouldn’t go to all this trouble.”
小天狼星点了点头。“很好，谢谢你。你不必费这么大的劲。”

 

“Nonsense.”
“别说了。”

Grant brought in the plates. They sat around the coffee table, Sirius on the sofa, Remus in the armchair, and Grant on the floor. Sirius put food on his plate and picked at it like a bird. He didn’t use the forks they’d put out, or the chopsticks that came with the meal, he used his hands to eat, tearing everything into small pieces and feeding them into his mouth. Remus and Grant politely ignored it, making light conversation.
格兰特拿来了盘子。他们围坐在咖啡桌周围，小天狼星坐在沙发上，雷穆斯坐在扶手椅里，格兰特则坐在地板上。小天狼星把食物放在自己的盘子里，用手撕成小块，然后送进嘴里，就像只小鸟。他没有使用他们准备的叉子，或者餐食附带的筷子。雷穆斯和格兰特礼貌地忽略了这一点，轻松地聊天。

“I’ll have to do a proper shop, on my way back from work tomorrow.” Grant said. “Get you a toothbrush, some things like that.”
“我明天下班回来的路上得去好好买东西。”格兰特说，“给你买个牙刷，还有一些其他的东西。”

“I can do that.” Remus said. He was keen to take care of Sirius himself; as if he’d brought home a stray he ought to be responsible for. He looked at Sirius, “Your clothes and books are boxed up in the garage. I’ll go and have a look tomorrow.”
“我可以做的。”雷穆斯说。他想亲自照顾小天狼星，就像他带回家了一只流浪狗，应该对它负责。他看着小天狼星，“你的衣服和书都在车库里打包好了。我明天去看看。”

“You kept them?” Sirius looked up, almost hopefully, “You kept my things?”
“你留着它们了吗？”小天狼星抬头看着，几乎带着希望，“你留着我的东西了吗？”

“Er. Well, after everything, Mary showed up and did it for me. I wasn’t… I wasn’t very well, for a while. I’m not sure what state they’re in, I haven’t been there since.”
“呃，嗯，经过一切之后，玛丽来了，帮我处理了。我当时……我当时身体不太好。有段时间我不太清楚它们的状况，自那以后我没去过。”

“I didn’t expect you to keep anything.”
“我没想到你会留着任何东西。”

Remus didn’t know what to say, so he shrugged. It hadn’t really been a case of wanting to hang onto Sirius’s stuff; more that he’d just hidden it away so he didn’t have to think about it. He was glad now, obviously, but he didn’t want any more credit than he was due.
雷穆斯不知道该说什么，于是他耸了耸肩。他并不是想留着小天狼星的东西；更多的是他只是把它们藏起来，好让自己不必去想它们。他现在显然感到很高兴，但他不想获得超出应有的赞誉。

They finished eating, and Sirius wiped his greasy hands on the legs of his pyjama bottoms, and Remus tried not to wince. Sirius used to be so fastidious about cleanliness - Remus’s disorganisation had always irritated him. Another change.
他们吃完了，小天狼星用睡裤的裤腿擦拭油腻的手，雷穆斯尽量不去皱眉。小天狼星以前对清洁是如此讲究——雷穆斯的无序总是让他感到恼火。这是另一个变化。

Grant got up to collect the plates and cutlery for washing up. Sirius sat up, “I can do that, let me,” he withdrew a wand from his baggy sleeve.
格兰特站起来去收拾盘子和餐具。小天狼星坐起身来，“我可以做的，让我来。”他从松垮的袖子里拿出一根魔杖。

“Where did you get that?” Remus asked, frowning.
“你从哪里弄来的？”雷穆斯皱着眉头问。

“Stole it,” Sirius looked down, turning it in his hand, “Took a while to get used to, but I can handle it ok now. Here, let me...”
“偷来的，”小天狼星低下头，转动着手里的魔杖，“花了一段时间才习惯，但我现在可以应付得很好。来，让我……”

“It’s fine.” Grant said. He was smiling, but you couldn’t hear it in his voice. “I’d prefer to do it normally.” He turned, carrying the pile of plates into the kitchen.
“没关系。”格兰特说。他在笑，但声音里听不出笑意。“我更愿意用正常的方式做。”他转身把一堆盘子拿进了厨房。

“ Muffliato .” Sirius muttered. Remus blinked, surprised. He hadn’t heard that spell in a very long time, and he had never, ever used something like that with Grant present. It felt disloyal, sneaky. “Is the floo connection working?” Sirius asked, urgently.
“小声音术。”小天狼星喃喃道。雷穆斯眨了眨眼睛，感到惊讶。他已经很久没听到过这个咒语了，而且他从未在格兰特在场时使用过类似的东西。这感觉不忠诚，阴险。“火焰通道连接正常吗？”小天狼星急切地问。

“No.” Remus said. “I never re-connected. I don’t actually do very much magic at home, because--”
“没有。”雷穆斯说。“我没有重新连接。我在家里实际上不怎么使用魔法，因为——”

“Yeah, because of the muggle,” Sirius finished, and Remus could have sworn he rolled his eyes. “He’s made a lot of changes, I see.” He gave the TV a very pointed look.
“是的，因为麻瓜，”小天狼星接过话茬，雷穆斯可以发誓他翻了个白眼。“他做了很多改变，我看到了。”他非常明显地看了一眼电视。

“It’s his home too,” Remus said, defensively.
“这也是他的家。”雷穆斯辩解道。

“Whatever, I don’t care. Right, we’ll need to re-connect it. If I’m staying here, that is. We’ll need to be able to communicate with the rest of the Order.”
“随便，我不在乎。好吧，我们需要重新连接。如果我要留在这里的话。我们需要能够与其他成员保持联系。”

“The rest of the--”
“其他的——”

“--have you got an owl?” Sirius glanced around.
“——你有猫头鹰吗？”小天狼星环顾四周。

“No,” Remus said. He chewed his lip, “I’ve got a phone.” He offered, trying to lighten the mood.
“没有，”雷穆斯说。他咬着嘴唇，“我有个电话。”他提议道，试图缓解气氛。

“For merlin’s sake, Moony!” Sirius barked, his rough voice crackling with urgency, “What have you been doing all these years, moping about?!”
“天啊，月亮！”小天狼星吼道，他粗糙的声音中带着紧迫感，“这些年你都在做什么，发愁吗？！”

Remus flinched - both at being called Moony, which nobody ever did, and at the cruel accusation.
雷穆斯感到一阵颤抖——既因为被称为月亮，这没人会这样称呼，也因为那个残酷的指责。

“I’ve been surviving.” He said, trying to stay calm, “How easy do you think it is for me to hold down a job? And it’s not as if I’ve had anyone I need to keep in touch with.”
“我一直在生存。”他说，试图保持冷静，“你觉得我维持一份工作有多容易？而且我也没有需要联系的人。”

Sirius didn’t say anything, but pursed his lips and scowled, staring at the carpet. Remus sighed, closing his eyes. “Look,” he said, gently, “I can imagine how you must feel. I know you want to do everything at once, now you’re free, but let’s just take things slowly tonight, ok? Get a proper night’s sleep and we’ll work on a plan tomorrow.”
小天狼星没有说话，只是抿着嘴唇，皱着眉头盯着地毯。雷穆斯叹了口气，闭上了眼睛。“看，”他说，温柔地，“我可以想象你一定是什么感受。我知道你现在自由了，想要一次性做所有的事情，但今晚我们还是慢慢来，好吗？好好睡一晚，明天我们再制定计划。”

Sirius nodded, mollified. Remus felt proud of himself. He hadn't cried, or shouted, and that was pretty good progress, at least as far as Sirius Black was concerned. Grant re-entered the room, and Remus quickly undid the muffliato charm.
小天狼星点了点头，显得平静了下来。雷穆斯感到很自豪。他没有哭泣，也没有大喊大叫，这在小天狼星·布莱克看来已经是很大的进步了。格兰特重新进入房间，雷穆斯迅速解除了小声音术的咒语。

“Shall I stick the telly on?” He asked the silent room. Remus nodded. Sirius returned to scowling.
“我把电视打开吗？”他问着寂静的房间。雷穆斯点了点头。小天狼星又开始皱眉。

The news was on, and then the weather. Then some American hospital drama, which made Grant tut and switch over. There was a documentary on about Fleetwood Mac, which they all vaguely watched. No one really spoke, except Grant every now and then.
新闻开始播放，然后是天气预报。接着是一部美国医院剧，格兰特发出了不满的声音并换台了。之后有一部关于Fleetwood Mac的纪录片，他们都模糊地看着。除了格兰特偶尔发言，大家没有人真正交谈。

Remus was in turmoil, his brain whirring into overdrive as too many conflicting thoughts and feeling flashed past. It had been so long since he’d been in the same room as Sirius, and now they couldn’t even talk to each other without hitting some immeasurable barrier, whether it was the war, or lost friends, or their mutual betrayal. And now the order was reforming, and it looked like everyone expected Remus to sign himself up, once again, without hesitation. But he wasn’t the boy he’d been last time. He was old, and he was tired. He had other responsibilities - he had Grant.
雷穆斯心乱如麻，他的大脑高速运转，冲突的思想和情感闪过。自从他和小天狼星在同一个房间里已经很久了，现在他们甚至无法相互交谈而不遇到某种无法测量的障碍，无论是战争，还是失去的朋友，还是彼此的背叛。现在，凤凰社正在重组，看起来每个人都希望雷穆斯再次毫不犹豫地加入。但他已不再是上次那个少年。他老了，也累了。他还有其他责任——他有格兰特。

At about ten o’clock, Sirius yawned.
大约十点钟，小天狼星打了个哈欠。

“Yeah, me too.” Grant commented, yawning back. “Got work in the morning, maybe it’s time for bed.” He looked at Remus, obviously hoping for some sort of direction.
“嗯，我也是。”格兰特回应道，也打了个哈欠。“明天早上要上班，也许是时候上床睡觉了。”他看向雷穆斯，显然希望得到一些指示。

“Yeah,” Remus said, uncertain. He placed his hands on the arms of his chair to push himself up, stiff from sitting so rigidly all evening. “Um. Sirius, are you ok here? I’ll get you a cushion and a duvet.”
“嗯，”雷穆斯说，语气不确定。他把手放在扶手椅的扶手上，试图站起身来，身体因整晚坐得过于僵硬而感到僵硬。“呃。小天狼星，你在这里还好吗？我去给你拿个靠垫和一条被子。”

“No need.” Sirius said. He stretched again, and transformed into Padfoot. Grant breathed in, sharply, at the surprise, but said nothing. The big black dog curled up on the couch and closed its eyes.
“没必要。”小天狼星说。他再次伸展了一下，然后变成了帕德弗特。格兰特对这一惊讶深吸了一口气，但没有说话。那只大黑狗在沙发上蜷缩起来，闭上了眼睛。

“Can you do that?” Grant whispered, half an hour later, once he and Remus were both in bed. “Turn into a wolf whenever you like?”
“你能这样做吗？”格兰特在半小时后，雷穆斯和他都躺在床上时，低声问道。“你可以随时变成狼吗？”

“No.” Remus said. “He’s an animagus. He learnt how to do it. I’m a werewolf, I got bitten, I don’t get a choice.”
“不能。”雷穆斯说。“他是个变形人。他学会了怎么做。我是狼人，我被咬了，我没有选择。”

“Bad luck.” Grant said, “Mind you, don’t think I’d like it much, if you could.”
“真是不走运。”格兰特说，“不过，你别以为我会喜欢，如果你能变的话。”

“He won’t hurt you, he’s still got his normal mind when he’s a dog.” Though Remus wasn’t sure what Sirius’s ‘normal mind’ was like, anymore. Everything else about him was rumpled and damaged in some way.
“他不会伤害你，他作为狗的时候，头脑还是正常的。”虽然雷穆斯不确定小天狼星的“正常头脑”现在是什么样的。他身上的其他一切都以某种方式变得皱巴巴和受损。

“Are you ok?” Grant said, turning his head to watch Remus’s face.
“你还好吗？”格兰特说，转头看着雷穆斯的脸。

“I think so.” Remus said, honestly, “But it’s weird. It’s going to be difficult, I think.”
“我想是的。”雷穆斯诚实地说，“但这很奇怪。我觉得这会很困难。”

“How long will he be here?”
“他会待多久？”

“Oh. I don’t know. A while, maybe. He’s talking about… about another war. I might need to help.”
“哦。我不知道。也许有一段时间。他在谈论……另一场战争。我可能需要帮忙。”

“Remus…”
“雷穆斯……”

“I know, I know,” Remus screwed up his face. “I’m sorry, the whole situation is… it’s a fucking nightmare, really. I need some time to think.”
“我知道，我知道，”雷穆斯皱起了脸。“对不起，整个情况……这真是一场恶梦。我需要一些时间来思考。”

“I wish I could help.” Grant said. “I wish I understood.”
“我希望我能帮忙。”格兰特说。“我希望我能理解。”

“You’re so good with Sirius.” Remus offered, “I don’t know what to say to him, he’s so… I dunno, prickly. I’m scared I’ll say something wrong and he’ll bite my head off.”
“你对小天狼星很好。”雷穆斯说，“我不知道对他说什么，他现在很……我不知道，难对付。我担心我会说错话，他会把我的头咬掉。”

“Hmm, well I have a bit of experience with those types.” Grant said, his lips curling, “Anyway, he’s obviously been through the mill. Just gotta be patient. Kind. You can’t force him to get better, I’m afraid.”
“嗯，我对这些类型有一点经验。”格兰特说，嘴角微微翘起，“不管怎样，他显然经历了很多磨难。只需要耐心。友善。恐怕你不能强迫他变好。”

* * *

Sirius slept for a very long time. Long after Grant had left for work, and Remus had eaten breakfast and marked a few exam papers. He stayed in the kitchen, but he could see the living room couch through the door, just in case.
小天狼星睡了很长时间。格兰特离开去上班后，雷穆斯吃了早餐，还批改了一些试卷。他待在厨房里，但可以透过门看到客厅的沙发，以防万一。

It was almost half past eleven when Padfoot jerked awake, and began barking loudly, leaping off the couch.
快到十一点半时，帕德弗特突然惊醒，开始大声吠叫，跳下了沙发。

“Shh!” Remus ran into the living room anxiously, “Sirius, it’s me! You’re here, you’re with me!”
“嘘！”雷穆斯焦急地跑进客厅，“小天狼星，是我！你在这里，你和我在一起！”

The dog stopped, cocked its head, then transformed back into Sirius. His eyes were wide and his jaw shadowy with stubble. He looked like a mad person. Remus tried to be patient, and kind, like Grant said. “Sorry,” he said, steadying his voice, “It’s just that we’re not allowed pets, here, and if the neighbours hear you…”
那只狗停了下来，歪着头，然后变回了小天狼星。他的眼睛睁得很大，脸颊上有胡茬，看起来像个疯子。雷穆斯试图耐心和友善，就像格兰特说的那样。“对不起，”他稳住声音说，“只是这里不允许宠物，如果邻居听见了……”

“Sorry.” Sirius looked down, embarrassed. “You’d think I’d be used to it now. Been out for a year.”
“对不起。”小天狼星低下头，显得很尴尬。“你会觉得我现在应该习惯了。我已经离开一年了。”

“It’s fine.” Remus shook his head, “Sorry I shouted.”
“没关系。”雷穆斯摇头说，“对不起，我吼了。”

Things stayed that awkward for most of the day. They went out to the garage after Sirius had eaten breakfast.
整个上午都是那种尴尬的气氛。在小天狼星吃过早餐后，他们去了车库。

The door took a few goes to heave open, and Sirius had to stay in dog form while they were out of the flat, so it fell to Remus. Still, they got in eventually, and everything was very much as they remembered. No motorbike, of course, though all the tools were still there. Sirius’s clothes and books were neatly stacked in labelled boxes, without so much as a layer of dust on them.
门好几次才被推开，而小天狼星在他们离开公寓时必须保持狗的形态，所以这份任务落在了雷穆斯身上。不过，他们最终还是进去了，一切和他们记忆中的样子一样。当然没有摩托车，不过所有工具还在。小天狼星的衣服和书籍整齐地叠放在标记好的箱子里，连一层灰尘都没有。

“Mary must have done some sort of preserving spell,” Remus commented.
“玛丽一定做了什么保养咒语，”雷穆斯评论道。

Sirius nodded vaguely, walking through the piles of relics like an ancient monk. He selected a few things to take back to the flat - or rather, for Remus to carry back. Sirius chose robes and wizard clothes, none of his muggle stuff, not even his old leather jacket, which Remus found stuffed inside a box under some records. He had to resist the urge to bury his face in it and inhale the gorgeous scent; as if the jacket had more of Sirius in it than the man standing next to him.
小天狼星含糊地点了点头，像古老的僧侣一样穿过一堆堆遗物。他挑选了一些东西带回公寓——更准确地说，是让雷穆斯带回去。小天狼星选择了长袍和巫师服，没有他的麻瓜用品，连他旧的皮夹克都没有。雷穆斯在一些唱片下的箱子里发现了它。他不得不抑制住想把脸埋在上面，吸入那迷人气味的冲动；仿佛这件夹克里包含了比他身边站着的那个男人更多的小天狼星的气息。

Back at the flat, Sirius changed into the robes at once. Remus could see why - he looked much better already, in his own things, having had a few good meals and a proper wash. His hair was a bit straggly, and still had knots in it despite the fact that he’d clearly used half a bottle of shampoo on it.
回到公寓后，小天狼星立刻换上了长袍。雷穆斯明白为什么——他穿上自己的衣服，吃过几顿好饭，洗了个彻底的澡，看起来好多了。他的头发有些蓬乱，尽管显然用了半瓶洗发水，仍然有结。

He slept again, after lunch. Remus didn’t see how, he’d only been awake a few hours. Still, despite Sirius’s inability to stay still, he exhausted easily. He curled up on the couch again, in the nest of blankets he’d created, and Remus sat beside him with the TV on very low. At least when Sirius slept he was a dog, and therefore easier to share a room with.
午餐后，他又睡着了。雷穆斯不明白怎么回事，他才醒了几个小时。不过，尽管小天狼星无法安静地待着，他很容易疲惫。他再次蜷缩在他创造的毯子窝里，而雷穆斯坐在他身边，电视声音调得很低。至少当小天狼星睡觉时，他是只狗，因此和他共处一室更容易一些。

He was grumpy, when he woke up. He squinted at the TV, then at Remus.
他醒来时很脾气不好。他眯着眼睛看着电视，然后看向雷穆斯。

“Don’t you read any more?”
“你不再读书了吗？”

“Of course I do.” Remus gestured at the bookcases either side of the fireplace, which were sagging under the weight. “TV is just background noise.”
“当然读。”雷穆斯指着壁炉两侧的书架，那些书架都因书的重量而下垂。“电视只是背景噪音。”

Sirius grunted, sitting up and straightening his clothes. He ran his fingers through his hair, and they got caught. He winced.
小天狼星发出一声闷哼，坐起身来，整理衣服。他用手指梳理头发，但卡住了。他皱起了眉头。

“Do you want to try washing it again?” Remus asked, “If you put loads of conditioner on, then comb it through, that might help?”
“你想再试着洗一次吗？”雷穆斯问道，“如果你多涂一些护发素，然后梳理一下，可能会有帮助。”

He remembered Grant telling him that about two brothers who’d come to the remand centre. They’d been neglected, and had never had their hair cut or brushed, and they were frightened of the clippers. Grant remembered Matron’s brutal buzz cuts, and he immediately promised them he wouldn’t cut their hair. He’d spent hours gently combing it through, instead, and his hands were wet and cold for so long his eczema flared up and his palms were rough and chapped for weeks.
他记得格兰特告诉他关于两个来到拘留中心的兄弟的事情。他们被忽视，从未剪过头发或梳过头发，害怕剪发器。格兰特记得护士长那残酷的剃发，他立即答应他们不会剪他们的头发。他花了几个小时轻柔地梳理他们的头发，结果手在湿冷中呆了很久，湿疹发作，手掌粗糙干裂了好几周。

Sirius seemed to appreciate the suggestion, so Remus went to run the bath. Sirius followed him. He didn’t seem to want to be left alone at all, even if he didn’t want to talk.
小天狼星似乎很感激这个建议，于是雷穆斯去准备浴缸。小天狼星跟着他。他似乎不想被留下一个人，即使他不想说话。

Remus rooted around in the medicine cabinet for a good strong comb, and some scissors, just in case. He set them on the edge of the bathtub, and stepped back. “Er… shall I leave you to it?” He asked, as the bathwater steamed gently. Sirius rubbed his arm, looking around.
雷穆斯在药柜里翻找了一把好的结实的梳子和一些剪刀，以备不时之需。他把它们放在浴缸边缘，然后退后一步。“呃……我还是让你自己来吧？”他说，浴水轻轻冒着蒸汽。小天狼星揉了揉手臂，四处张望。

“No I think I’d rather… if you don’t mind?”
“不，我想……如果你不介意的话？”

“Anything you like,” Remus said. Let him lead the way, Grant had suggested. Go with the flow. He thought about turning around as Sirius undressed, but that seemed redundant if he was staying in the room, and anyway, Sirius had no scruples about stripping off in front of him. There was nothing sensual about it; he did it in the same way he now ate with his hands, or wiped his mouth with his sleeve, or curled up tightly on the sofa; he did it because he had forgotten how to act around other people.
“随你喜欢，”雷穆斯说。让他来主导，格兰特建议过。顺其自然。他考虑了一下是否应该转身，小天狼星脱衣服时，但如果他还在房间里，这似乎没什么必要，而且小天狼星在他面前脱衣服毫无顾忌。没有任何情色的意味；他这样做就像现在用手吃东西，或者用袖子擦嘴，或者在沙发上紧紧蜷缩；他这样做是因为他忘记了如何在其他人面前表现自己。

He was so thin, so frail, his elbows jutted out like knives and his hollow ribs moved under his paper white skin. His once warm, slender wrists, which Remus had adored, were now so narrow they looked like they'd snap as he lowered himself into the bath.
他太瘦了，太虚弱了，肘部突出得像刀子一样，空洞的肋骨在他苍白的皮肤下移动。他曾经温暖而纤细的手腕，雷穆斯曾经钟爱，现在却如此狭窄，看起来像是他在低下身体时会断裂一样。

Remus pretended to be tidying the bathroom, and started folding up the flannel hanging off the side of the sink, straightening the towels slung over the radiator. He was embarrassed, he didn't want to stare. Though, to be honest, Sirius probably wouldn't notice, either way.
雷穆斯假装整理浴室，开始折叠挂在水槽边上的毛巾，整理挂在暖气上的毛巾。他感到尴尬，不想盯着看。不过，说实话，小天狼星可能也不会注意到。

Eventually, Remus sat on the closed toilet lid, crossing his legs in an effort to look nonchalant - and because the bathroom was much too small for his annoying gangly body. Sirius leaned back into the hot water, making small slow waves slop gently against the plastic sides of the tub. He closed his eyes, and tilted his head back into the water, exposing his throat, his adam’s apple protruding.
最后，雷穆斯坐在盖上的马桶盖上，交叉双腿以显得若无其事——而且因为浴室太小，不适合他那烦人的长腿。小天狼星靠在热水里，轻轻搅动水面，慢慢地在塑料浴缸的侧面溅起水波。他闭上眼睛，仰头靠在水中，露出喉咙，喉结突出。

Remus had to remember to close his mouth as Sirius resurfaced, opening his eyes and sweeping his hair back. Now it was wet, the grey had vanished, and he became suddenly younger, more recognisable.
小天狼星浮出水面时，雷穆斯不得不记得合上嘴巴，他睁开眼睛，将头发往后梳。现在头发湿了，灰色消失了，他突然变得年轻了，更加容易识别。

He started lathering his hair with the shampoo, sitting up, leaning forward. Remus watched his bony white fingers clawing through the foam, and remembered how graceful Sirius had been as a young man, how every movement was perfectly weighted, how he used to treat his own body with such tenderness. The steam from the hot water stung Remus’s eyes, and he had to blink away tears.
他开始用洗发水给头发起泡，坐起身，向前倾。雷穆斯看着他那骨瘦如柴的白色手指在泡沫中抓挠，想起了小天狼星年轻时的优雅，每一个动作都恰到好处，他曾经如此温柔地对待自己的身体。热水的蒸汽刺痛了雷穆斯的眼睛，他不得不眨眼以拭去泪水。

Sirius rinsed out the shampoo, then started on the conditioner, using loads of it, Remus would have to buy more.
小天狼星冲洗掉洗发水，然后开始使用护发素，涂了很多，雷穆斯需要去再买一些。

“We ought to make a list.” Sirius said, abruptly.
“我们应该列个清单。”小天狼星突然说。

“What?” Remus frowned.
“什么？”雷穆斯皱眉。

“A list.” Sirius said, picking up the comb. “We ought to make one. People to get in contact with, for Dumbledore.”
“清单。”小天狼星说，拿起梳子。“我们应该做一个。要联系的人，为邓布利多。”

“For Dumbledore.” Remus repeated. He suddenly felt very tired.
“为邓布利多。”雷穆斯重复道。他突然感到非常疲惫。

“Yeah, he said get in touch with the old crowd. Only my memory’s shot, so you'll have to help. The names, you know.” He tugged the comb through his knots, hard.
“是的，他说要联系老朋友。只是我的记忆力糟糕，所以你得帮忙。那些名字，你知道的。”他用力地拉梳子，梳理结。

“You really want to go right back to war, don’t you?” Remus said.
“你真的想立刻回到战争中去，对吧？”雷穆斯说。

Sirius turned and gave him a look of disbelief, and with a horrible sinking feeling Remus realised that in Sirius’s mind the war had never ended.
小天狼星转过身，用不敢置信的目光看着他，雷穆斯突然有种可怕的沮丧感，意识到在小天狼星的心目中，战争从未结束。

“Look,” Remus tried to explain, “It’s not that I don’t believe in the cause, it’s just… I remember how it went last time.”
“看，”雷穆斯试图解释，“这不是我不相信这个事业，只是……我记得上一次的经过。”

“As if I don’t!” Sirius hissed, yanking at the comb in his hair, “I haven’t been on holiday for twelve years!”
“就像我不记得一样！”小天狼星嘶嘶地说，一边用力梳理头发，“我已经十二年没休假了！”

“No, I know, but…” Remus wished he’d stop saying it like that. Twelve years . What forgiveness could there ever be, for that?
“是的，我知道，不过……”雷穆斯希望他别再那样说。十二年 。对于这点，能有什么宽恕呢？

“It's all we can do.” Sirius said, fiercely, “It's the only thing that matters.” He raised the comb again, looking as if he was about to stab himself with it, rather than groom himself. Remus couldn't stand it.
“这是我们能做的唯一事情。”小天狼星激烈地说，“这是唯一重要的事。”他再次举起梳子，看起来像是要用它刺自己，而不是梳理头发。雷穆斯无法忍受。

“Stop that,” he said, getting up. “You'll rip all your bloody hair out, come on. Let me do it.”
“别那样，”他说，站起来。“你会把自己的头发都撕掉的，来吧。让我来。”

He rolled up a towel and put it on the floor to kneel on, grabbing the comb out of Sirius's hand. Sirius looked at him warily for a moment, and Remus realised that they had not been this close yet - they had hugged, in the Shack a year ago, but that had been pure adrenaline. It had not been intimate. This was.
他卷起一条毛巾放在地上跪着，拿过小天狼星手里的梳子。小天狼星警惕地看了他一眼，雷穆斯意识到他们还没有如此亲密过——他们曾在一年前在狼屋里拥抱过，但那是纯粹的肾上腺素，并不亲密。这才是。

“May I?” Remus asked, softening his voice.
“我可以吗？”雷穆斯问，语气变得柔和。

Sirius nodded, slowly, then turned his head, so that Remus could reach. Leaning in, not too much, Remus began to work, sliding his fingers carefully through the slick black locks, gently easing the comb through in sections from the bottom up. Slowly, slowly, the knots began to loosen, giving way to that familiar old silken texture.
小天狼星缓慢地点头，然后转过头，让雷穆斯能够触及。雷穆斯轻轻靠近，开始工作，小心翼翼地用手指穿过湿漉漉的黑发，从下往上逐段梳理。渐渐地，结开始松开，露出那熟悉的光滑质感。

It was difficult work, and took a lot of patience, and the rest of the bottle of conditioner, but Remus finally felt like he was helping; he was in control and he was doing something positive. Sirius was so quiet and still the whole time; tense at first, but gradually relaxing, bit by bit - Remus could practically see his tendons slackening.
这是一项艰难的工作，需要很大的耐心，以及用完了剩下的护发素，但雷穆斯终于感觉到自己在帮忙；他掌握了控制，并做了一些积极的事情。小天狼星一直非常安静，最初有些紧张，但逐渐放松，一点一点地——雷穆斯几乎能看到他的肌腱在放松。

Once he was finished, Remus leaned back to survey his work, the muscles in his back ached like they were on fire, but it was worth it. He stood up, shakily, a hand on the sink. Sirius raised his hands, moved them gingerly over his head, fingers skimming the smooth surface.
完成后，雷穆斯靠后坐下，检查自己的工作，背部的肌肉像着火一样疼痛，但这是值得的。他颤抖着站起来，一只手撑在水槽上。小天狼星抬起双手，轻柔地移动在头顶，手指滑过光滑的表面。

“Thanks.”
“谢谢。”

“Any time.” Remus smiled, sitting back on the loo seat.
“随时可以。”雷穆斯笑着，坐回马桶盖上。

Sirius rinsed his hair a few more times, then climbed out and dried himself, getting dressed again. Remus expected him to look at himself in the mirror, but he didn't, he purposefully avoided it, keeping his eyes down.
小天狼星再冲洗了几次头发，然后爬出浴缸，擦干身体，再次穿上衣服。雷穆斯期待他会看镜子里的自己，但他没有，他故意避免了这一点，眼睛低垂。

Back in the living room, Remus made them tea and some cheese on toast, because he wanted Sirius to eat as often as possible. He expected Sirius to fall asleep again, but he didn't. He took some paper from Remus’s pile of exams, and flipped it over, picking up a biro too.
回到客厅，雷穆斯为他们准备了茶和奶酪吐司，因为他希望小天狼星能尽可能多吃点东西。他原以为小天狼星会再睡一觉，但他没有。他从雷穆斯的试卷堆里拿出一张纸，把它翻过来，还拿了一支圆珠笔。

“Ok,” he said, “Moody, obviously, top of the list - after he's recovered of course, wait til you hear what happened to him at Hogwarts! Then the Weasley's, and Mary…”
“好了，”他说，“摩地，显然，排在首位——当然是在他康复之后，等着听听他在霍格沃茨发生了什么！然后是韦斯莱一家，还有玛丽……”

“No, not Mary.” Remus said. “She won't… she's settled down, she's got kids. And the Weasley's, they've got seven kids, Sirius, you can't ask that of people…”
“不，玛丽不行。”雷穆斯说。“她不会……她已经安顿下来，有了孩子。还有韦斯莱一家，他们有七个孩子，小天狼星，你不能这样要求他们……”

“I don't need to.” Sirius said, sharply. “They'll do what's right.”
“我不需要。”小天狼星尖锐地说。“他们会做正确的事。”

“I can't see it that way.” Remus said, “All I can see is the cost of another war…”
“我看不到这样。”雷穆斯说，“我只看到另一场战争的代价……”

“We don't have a choice!”
“我们没有选择！”

“I know, I know, I just want us to think , before we--”
“我知道，我知道，只是希望我们在——之前考虑清楚。”

What’s happened to you, Remus?! This isn’t like you. You’re supposed to be a Gryffindor!”
你怎么了，雷穆斯？！这不像你。你应该是个格兰芬多！”

That struck a nerve. How dare he!?
这戳中了痛点。他怎么敢！？

“Quite a bit has happened to me, actually.” Remus said, acidly. “I lost everyone I ever cared about in the last war, so forgive me if I’m not thrilled about marching straight into battle again. I’m not twenty-one any more.”
“其实发生了不少事。”雷穆斯酸涩地说。“我在上一场战争中失去了我关心的所有人，所以请原谅我如果我对再次直接投入战斗不感到兴奋。我已经不再二十一岁了。”

Sirius shook his head, still unable to comprehend. “We owe it to them! To Lily and James!”
小天狼星摇了摇头，仍然无法理解。“我们欠他们的！给莉莉和詹姆斯！”

“I don’t owe them anything!” Remus shouted, his face burning with anger, “Maybe you feel like you do, ‘secret keeper’, but if you recall, I wasn’t fucking consulted on that one!”
“我什么都不欠他们！”雷穆斯大声喊道，脸上充满了愤怒，“也许你觉得你欠他们，‘秘密守护者’，但如果你还记得，我他妈的没有被咨询过！”

He didn't know why he said it; it just all came tumbling out before he could stop himself. He hasn't realised how angry he really was, until that moment. Clearly Sirius hadn't, either,
他不知道自己为什么这么说；这些话在他能阻止自己之前全都涌了出来。他直到那一刻才意识到自己有多生气。显然，小天狼星也没有意识到。

“Moony--”
“小天狼星——”

“Don’t you dare call me ‘Moony’! Don’t act like we’re still… like nothing’s changed! Like everything’s fine, and I'm just going to do everything you say!”
“别你敢叫我‘小天狼星’！别装作我们仍然……像什么都没变一样！像一切都没问题，我就会照你说的做！”

He stood up, he needed to get out, he needed a break. He turned on his heel, heading for the door.
他站起来，需要离开一下，他需要休息一下。他转过身，朝门口走去。
